=== remaining rules (E, F, ...) ===

## Rule E: Layout sections are not components

Blocks and sections within the primary content region are layout instructions:
spacing, background colour, and container-query responsive sizing. They do not
receive contract entries unless they render component content themselves. Classify
them by structural role, not visual scale.

---

## Rule F: Templates and pages are not Custom Elements

Templates and pages sit above the component delivery layer. They are
**spec-layer deliverables only**. They do not receive contract entries, do not
generate `.js` component files, and are not delivered as Custom Elements.

The design system provides atoms, molecules, and organisms. How a developer
assembles those into a page frame within their stack (React layouts, Angular shell
components, LWC experience layers, vanilla HTML) is outside the scope of the
component library. A template spec communicates layout intent: the named regions,
which components live in each, and the responsive behaviour. Implementation is the
developer's decision.

---

## Edge tests (apply in this order)

1. **Decorative internals are not components.** A badge dot, a toggle knob, a
   slider thumb: styled elements with no standalone identity. They do **not** bump
   the tier.
2. **Atom-only regions are molecules.** A top bar composing only Button + Logo →
   **molecule**, even though it spans the full viewport. Tier follows composition,
   not pixel size.
3. **Containers follow their template.** If a component's own template renders a
   molecule, it is an organism.

---

## Reading a Figma frame labelled as a template or page

1. **Read structure first.** Identify the named structural regions in the frame,
   their vertical order, nesting depth, and responsive or breakpoint intent.

2. **Map regions to semantic HTML.** Designers are not required to use HTML element
   names. The agent infers the semantic mapping from layer name and position.
   Common mappings:

   | Figma layer name (examples) | Semantic element |
   |---|---|
   | Nav, Navigation, Nav Bar, Global Nav | `<nav>` |
   | Header, Site Header, Masthead | `<header>` |
   | Announcement Bar, Alert Bar, Promo Band | `<div>` or `<aside>` (above `<header>`) |
   | Hero, Page Hero, Banner | `<section>` (within `<main>`) |
   | Content Area, Main Content, Body | `<main>` |
   | Sidebar, Side Nav, Aside | `<aside>` |
   | Footer, Site Footer, Footer Links | `<footer>` |

3. **Flag ambiguous names before assigning.** If a region name carries no functional
   signal (e.g. "Blue Bar", "Wide Strip"), stop and ask before assigning a semantic
   element.

4. **Then read composition.** Once regions are mapped, identify which organisms,
   molecules, or atoms appear within each region.

5. **Determine tier by content.** Placeholder text and grey boxes → Template.
   Real copy and imagery → Page. For frames with mixed content (some regions
   real, some placeholder), classify by the majority: if most regions carry real
   content, classify as Page; if most are placeholder, classify as Template. Note
   the ambiguity in the spec's Overview section so the designer can verify.

content.text:
Substantial answer here — there's more direction than you might expect, but it isn't ratified. Let me lay it out.

---

## 1. What the repo actually sanctions today: nothing

`.claude/rules/conventions.md` defines one folder layout, and it's flat:

```
overrides/app/components/productTile/
  index.tsx   index.stories.tsx   index.test.ts   types.ts   productTile.scss
```

There is **no atoms/molecules concept in the folder structure.** The only atomic vocabulary in the ratified rules is Storybook *categorisation* — `components.md` describes `Elements/` as "generic building blocks… Button, Input, Badge, Link, Checkbox," which is the atoms layer by another name. And I verified: **`ui-kits` appears nowhere in `.claude/rules/`.**

The one atoms rule that *is* ratified is about stories, not folders:

> A story is required for anything **exported from its folder**. Not required for internal sub-components that only render inside one parent — cover their variants via the parent's stories.

So today, anything you put in an `atoms/` folder is on an unchosen structure.

## 2. But there is a rigorous model — and it's machine-checkable

`f2r/.claude/skills/_shared/atomic-model.md` (on Han's F2R branches) is the most serious thinking on this anywhere in the project:

| Tier | Definition — by what the component's **own template renders** |
|---|---|
| **Atom** | Renders no other component: markup + CSS + tokens only. `composes: []` |
| **Molecule** | Renders **only** atoms |
| **Organism** | Renders **at least one** molecule |
| **Template** | Page frame — named regions, arrangement, responsive. No real content |
| **Page** | A template instance with real content |

Crucially the tier is **derived, not declared.** The contract (`f2r/02-design/library/contract/zimm-contract.js`) records `composes: [...]` per component and `validate.mjs` computes the tier transitively. So it can't drift.

Four rules that resolve the arguments people usually have:

- **Rule A — icons are attributes, not components.** A Button with a leading icon is still an atom (`icon="arrow-right"`). Only a standalone glyph is the Icon atom. The contract proves it: `Button` has `icon` as a string prop and `composes: []`.
- **Rule B — slot ≠ import.** Slotted children don't change the parent's tier. Only what the parent's own template renders counts.
- **Rule E — layout sections are not components.** Blocks and sections are layout instructions, not contract entries.
- **Rule F — templates and pages are not delivered.** *"The design system provides atoms, molecules, and organisms. How a developer assembles those into a page frame within their stack… is outside the scope of the component library."*

**Rule F is the handoff boundary.** F2R gives us atoms/molecules/organisms; page assembly is ours. That's the cleanest statement of the F2R↔us contract I've seen in this project.

## 3. Han's implementation is the most developed answer

`feature/f2r-implementation-workflow` has the full hierarchy built:

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/
  atoms/       zimm-add-to-wishlist  zimm-button  zimm-card-editorial  zimm-flag
               zimm-icon  zimm-logo  zimm-logo-masthead  zimm-nav-item
               zimm-select  zimm-text-input                          (10)
  molecules/   zimm-banner  zimm-disclaimer  zimm-input-action  zimm-mega-menu   (4)
  organisms/   zimm-footer  zimm-navigation                                       (2)
  assets/      icons/  flags/  logos/  iconUrls.ts
  registry.tsx
```

**The tiering matches the contract exactly** — not approximately:

- `Banner` → `composes: ["zimm-icon"]` → renders only atoms → **molecule** ✓
- `Footer` → `composes: ["zimm-logo","zimm-icon","zimm-input-action"]` → input-action is a molecule → **organism** ✓
- `Navigation` → `composes: ["zimm-icon","zimm-nav-item","zimm-mega-menu"]` → **organism** ✓

The per-component pattern is consistent:

```
zimm-button/
  index.tsx              ← plain React fn, native <button>, props mirroring the contract's enums exactly
  zimm-button.styles.ts  ← Emotion css`` with .zimm-btn-* classes on var(--zimm-*)
  index.stories.tsx      ← where present
```

And the props mirror the contract 1:1 — `variant: 'primary'|'secondary'|'icon'`, `size: 'large'|'medium'`, plus `label`, `icon`, `type`, `disabled`, `inverse`, `fullWidth`. Same enums, same defaults. That's real traceability: the folder name equals the custom-element name equals the contract entry.

## 4. So there are four competing structures in flight

| Structure | Branch | Naming | Styling | Tiering |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `components/<name>/index.tsx` | **develop — the only ratified one** | camelCase (or kebab if SFCC-mirrored) | theme recipe | flat |
| `components/shared/ui/<Name>/` | `pdp-token-class-spike` | PascalCase (upstream mirror) | theme recipe | flat |
| `ui-kits/atoms\|molecules/<name>.tsx` | PR #55 | flat camelCase files | inline styles + React state | atoms/molecules |
| `components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<name>/` | **Han** | kebab (contract mirror) | co-located Emotion `.styles.ts` | full 3-tier, contract-derived |

**Four Zimmermann buttons currently exist across branches**: `components/button/` (develop), `components/shared/ui/Button/` (spike), `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton.tsx` (#55), `components/ui-kits/atoms/zimm-button/` (Han).

## 5. The head-on collision with #56

Han's `zimm-button.styles.ts` defines **exactly the seven classes #56 deleted** — I checked name by name:

```
.zimm-btn  .zimm-btn-full  .zimm-btn-icon  .zimm-btn-large
.zimm-btn-medium  .zimm-btn-primary  .zimm-btn-secondary
```

Seven of seven, with near-identical CSS (`min-width: 80px`, `overflow: clip`, `gap: var(--zimm-size-action-gap)`, the same `0.15s ease` transitions). #56 removed them from `globalStyles.ts` with the instruction *"Use Chakra's `<Button>` for any button, not a class."*

**But #56's stated reason doesn't apply to Han's version**, and this is the part worth getting right before anyone argues. #56 said a static class *"can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/`_focusVisible`."* Plain CSS expresses `:hover`/`:active`/`:disabled`/`:focus-visible` perfectly well — Han's does. #56's real objection was to a class **mirroring** a Chakra recipe: two sources of truth for one component. Han's isn't a mirror. His components aren't Chakra components, so the class *is* the single source.

The genuine fork is therefore not "class vs recipe" but:

> **#56 assumes Chakra-component delivery. F2R delivers framework-agnostic React + CSS.**

Both are internally coherent. Both cannot own the button.

Note also that Han's branch **predates #56** and carries its own full `theme/foundation/` — colour, typography, spacing, sizes, zimmTokens, globalStyles. Merging it will conflict substantially with #56's derived foundation.

## 6. What I'd put in front of the squads

Four decisions, in dependency order:

1. **Do we adopt an atomic folder taxonomy?** I'd say yes. The contract already tiers everything, the tiering is machine-checkable, and it gives BAs and devs a shared vocabulary. Flat-forever stops working around 40 components.
2. **Whose path?** Han's `components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<kebab>/` is the strongest candidate — it's inside `components/` (so the registry sees it), it's tier-explicit, and the folder name traces to the contract entry. The kebab-case is technically off-convention for Zimmermann-authored code, but here it buys contract traceability, which I'd argue is worth the exception — **stated as an exception, not left ambiguous.**
3. **Chakra recipe or co-located CSS for the ui-kit?** The real question. My recommendation: recipes for anything that *is* a Chakra component (SFCC overrides, per #56), Han's co-located Emotion for F2R-derived framework-agnostic atoms — and **amend #56's rule to say "no `.zimm-btn-*` in `globalStyles.ts`"** rather than "nowhere," because as written it forbids Han's pattern for a reason that isn't true of it.
4. **How many buttons ship?** One. Which of the four, and what happens to the other three.

## 7. What a FED should do *today*, until that's settled

Build at `overrides/app/components/<camelCase>/index.tsx` with a `theme/components/<name>.ts` recipe — the ratified convention. **Don't create `atoms/` or `molecules/` folders yet.** Anything placed in `ui-kits/` right now is betting on a structure nobody has chosen, and there are already four candidates.

That's also the honest answer for #55: its `ui-kits/atoms/` isn't wrong *because atoms are wrong* — it's wrong because it invented a fourth variant of a structure Han had already derived from the contract, and styled it in a way neither #56 nor F2R endorses.

Want me to write this up as the decision brief for the alignment session with Tash/Kiera/Hannah — or as an ADR-style doc for the squads?

Review complete — four passes, all verified against the current head. **#55 has changed character substantially.**

---

# PR #55 code review vs the #56 spec

**Head `564ff99`** (+3105/−10 in 30 files) · 10 new commits since the last audit · `develop` @ `2dfeb4d`

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | ✅ clean |
| `npx vitest run` | ✅ 141 pass |
| `npx eslint` | ⚠️ 2269 problems — **2264 prettier, 5 warnings, 0 errors** |

The `jsx-a11y/anchor-is-valid` **error is gone**. Nothing but auto-fixable formatting and five intentional unused-vars stands between this and a clean lint.

## Scorecard

| Finding | Status |
|---|---|
| PR55-02 lint error | ✅ **Closed** |
| PR55-06 `footer.ts` orphaned | ✅ **Closed** — `useMultiStyleConfig('Footer')` at 2 sites |
| PR55-11 false subscribe success | ✅ **Closed** — real state machine |
| PR55-12 `SAFE_HREF_RE` bypass | ✅ **Closed** — precise fix |
| PR55-07 unsanctioned path | ✅ **Structurally resolved** |
| PR55-01 styling mechanism | 🟡 **2 of 4 migrated** |
| PR55-13 raw literals | 🟡 11 left, all now flagged or rem |
| PR55-03 uncontrolled input | 🔴 Open |
| PR55-04 `cssVars.ts` | 🔴 Open — 245 lines, 10 importers |
| PR55-05 `cssTextStyles` | 🔴 Open — `button`/`buttonSm` still duplicated |
| PR55-08 locale button | 🔴 Open — documented, not wired |
| PR55-10 fixture default | 🔴 Open — `data = FOOTER_FIXTURE` |
| **NEW-1** `_foundation` shadow foundation | 🔴 New |
| **NEW-2** Tier 1 `sizes.ts` touched | 🟢 New, trivial |

## What genuinely landed

**`zimmButton` is now the #56 pattern, verbatim.** Zero `useState`, zero inline styles, and its own header states the contract:

> *All hover/press/focus/disabled interaction states live in `theme/components/button.ts`. ZimmButton is a thin mapping layer: Zimmermann props → Chakra variant/size names that `button.ts` recognises.*

`zimmNavItem` likewise — 0 `useState`, 0 inline styles, and a `zimmNavItem.ts` recipe. **Registered recipes went 3 → 6** (Button, Footer, Header, ListMenu, ZimmNavItem, ZimmTextInput).

**The subscribe fix is better than what was asked for:**

```ts
type SubmitState = 'idle' | 'unavailable' | 'success' | 'error'
// 'unavailable' shown until HPC-036 (Omneo) lands; prevents false "You're on the list!" feedback.
setSubmitState('unavailable')
```

The email is retained in `pendingEmailRef`, and `_firstName`/`_lastName` are now *deliberately* unused with a comment saying they're ready for the Omneo POST. Those two lint warnings are intentional, not sloppiness.

**`SAFE_HREF_RE` closed with a negative lookahead** — `/^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?!\/))/i`. `//evil.example` now correctly rejected while single-slash relatives still pass.

## The structural question is effectively answered

`ui-kits` moved to `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules}/<camelCase>/index.tsx`. Measured against everything we've gathered, **this is now the most conformant of the four competing structures:**

- Inside `components/` — so `generateRegistry.mjs` sees it (Han's registry work will pick it up)
- Folder-per-component with `index.tsx` + `index.stories.tsx` — matches `conventions.md`
- **camelCase folders** — matches `conventions.md`'s rule for Zimmermann-authored files. Han's `zimm-button/` kebab is the off-convention one (defensible for contract traceability, but it's the exception)
- Tier folders `atoms/` / `molecules/`

**And the tiering is correct against Han's F2R contract model** — I checked what each component actually composes:

| Component | Composes | Tier | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zimmIcon`, `zimmLogo`, `zimmNavItem` | nothing | atom | ✅ |
| `zimmButton`, `zimmTextInput` | `ZimmIcon` | atom | ✅ **per Rule A** — icon is a prop, not a slot |
| `zimmInputAction` | `ZimmButton` + `ZimmTextInput` | molecule | ✅ renders only atoms |

That matches Han's independent tiering of the same components exactly. Two people derived the same answer from the contract — which is the strongest signal yet that the atomic model is the right direction.

**What's still missing is ratification, not structure.** `ui-kits` remains absent from `.claude/rules/`.

## What's still open, in priority order

**🔴 PR55-03 — `ZimmTextInput` still can't be driven by a parent.** State is now extracted to `overrides/app/hooks/useZimmTextInputState.ts` (good — that satisfies `components.md`'s extract-to-hook rule), and the hook *returns* `value`. But the atom's props are still `onChange?` only — **no `value?`, no `defaultValue?`**. A parent can observe; it cannot control. For a form field in a checkout-bound codebase that's the one I'd fix first.

**🔴 PR55-01 residue — 2 of 4 not migrated.** `zimmTextInput` carries 1 `useState`, 6 inline styles and 29 `cssVars` references; `zimmInputAction` has 2 `useState` and 1 inline style. Since `zimmTextInput.ts` already exists as a recipe, the path is proven — it just hasn't been walked for this atom.

**🔴 PR55-04/05 — `cssVars.ts` survives at 245 lines with 10 importers**, and `cssTextStyles` still carries `button` and `buttonSm` — the exact two #56 deleted from `globalStyles.ts`. Every atom that migrates to a recipe should shed its `cssVars` dependency; two have, four haven't.

**🔴 NEW-1 — a shadow foundation, self-documented.** `footer/index.tsx:21` declares:

```ts
const _foundation = {
  sizes: { footer: { subscribeBodyMax: '12.5rem' }, modal: { footer: '30rem' } },
} as const
```

and `footer.ts:1` says outright: *"Provisional breakpoint values — **mirror `_foundation.breakpoints` in footer/index.tsx**. Replace with `foundation/gridSystem.ts` imports once the UI designer confirms the tokens."*

Two files holding the same provisional values, by design, kept in sync by hand. That's precisely the duplication #56 spent 237→64 literals eliminating — reintroduced under a different name. The honesty is good; the shape isn't. One shared provisional module, or Kiera-confirmed tokens.

**🟢 NEW-2 — `foundation/sizes.ts` has a trailing-newline-only change.** Semantically nil, but `sizes.ts` is Tier 1 and this will trip `tier1-guard` on the PR for nothing. Revert it.

## The signal worth naming

Two things in this diff tell me the process is now working:

`zimmLogo/index.tsx` carries this comment:

```ts
// §7 raise: alias/size/logo/max-width (327px) and alias/size/logo/height (39px)
//   → foundation/sizes.ts (UI designer)
// Pending designer confirmation: scale with zoom (→ rem) or remain fixed (→ px, hairline exception)
const LOGO_MAX_WIDTH = '327px' // provisional
```

That's the FED build manual's §7 escalation pattern, cited by section number, applied correctly — flagged in-code with the open question named, rather than silently picked. Same discipline as the `SubmitState` machine and the breakpoint `em` values (correct per #56's unit rule).

**Two weeks ago this PR was architecturally opposed to #56. It is now substantially conformant with four residues and one new duplication.** The remaining work is finishing a migration whose pattern is already proven inside the same PR, not changing direction.

## What I'd say on the PR

Approve-with-changes shape: **`eslint --fix`** (clears 2264 in one command), **make `ZimmTextInput` controlled**, **finish the two unmigrated components and drop their `cssVars` imports**, **collapse `_foundation` to one home**, and **revert the `sizes.ts` newline**. The locale button and fixture default are both documented placeholders — reasonable to carry to a follow-up if HPC-036 and the Contentful wiring are separately ticketed.

Want me to update the findings doc with this pass, or draft the in-thread PR replies?

content.text:
# PR #55 — rework list

Head `564ff99` · verified against `develop` @ `2dfeb4d`, the #56 spec, and both Desktop docs.

---

## 🔴 Must fix before merge

**1 · `eslint --fix`** — clears **2264** of the 2269 problems in one command.
```bash
npx eslint $(git diff develop HEAD --name-only --diff-filter=d | grep -E '^overrides/.*\.tsx?$') --fix
```
Leaves 5 warnings, 0 errors. *(PR55-02 residue — 1 min)*

**2 · Make `ZimmTextInput` controllable** — `atoms/zimmTextInput/index.tsx`
Props expose `onChange?` only. Add optional `value` and `defaultValue`: use the controlled value when provided, fall back to internal state otherwise, initialise uncontrolled state from `defaultValue`. Then `ZimmInputAction` can hold the value in React state instead of reading the DOM.
**Why it's a blocker:** a form field that owns its own value can't participate in a real checkout form. *(PR55-03)*

**3 · Add a Vitest for `useZimmTextInputState.ts`**
104 lines managing value, focus, hover, derived visual tokens and handlers — no test. `components.md`'s extract-to-hook threshold is *why this hook exists*, and the manual's §8 requires Vitest for "complex state". This is the clearest test candidate in the PR.
**Neither #56 nor CodeRabbit flags this** — it's a project-rule requirement only. *(NEW-3)*

**4 · Revert the `foundation/sizes.ts` change**
It's a **trailing newline and nothing else**, but `foundation/` is Tier 1 — so the PR currently touches two protection tiers, breaching Hard Rule #10 and firing `tier1-guard` for zero substance.
```bash
git checkout develop -- overrides/app/theme/foundation/sizes.ts
```
*(Cheapest fix in the review — 10 seconds)*

---

## 🟠 Should fix before merge

**5 · Finish the recipe migration — 2 of 4 components left**

| Component | Remaining |
|---|---|
| `atoms/zimmTextInput/index.tsx` | 1 `useState`, 6 inline styles, 29 `cssVars` refs |
| `molecules/zimmInputAction/index.tsx` | 2 `useState`, 1 inline style |

`zimmButton` and `zimmNavItem` already show the pattern inside this same PR, and `theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts` already exists — so the target is proven, just not reached. *(PR55-01 residue)*

**6 · Delete `cssVars.ts` and `cssTextStyles`** — `overrides/app/utils/cssVars.ts` (245 lines, 10 importers)

It's a hand-typed mirror of `zimmTokens.ts`'s key names, so a rename in `zimmTokens.ts` breaks it **silently** (an unresolved CSS custom property produces no error, just no style) — and nothing tests the correspondence.

`cssTextStyles` still carries `button` and `buttonSm`: the exact two presets #56 deliberately removed from `globalStyles.ts` via its named exception set.

This falls out of item 5 — once the last components use recipes, the file has no reason to exist. *(PR55-04, PR55-05)*

**7 · Collapse `_foundation` to one home**
`footer/index.tsx:21` declares a shadow foundation, and `footer.ts:1` says outright:

> *"Provisional breakpoint values — **mirror `_foundation.breakpoints` in footer/index.tsx**."*

Two files holding the same provisional values, synced by hand. That's the duplication #56 spent 237→64 literals removing. Either one shared provisional module, or Kiera-confirmed tokens in `foundation/`. *(NEW-1)*

**8 · Clean the three unused imports in `header/index.tsx`** — `AccountIcon` (:34), `HeartIcon` (:38), `IconButtonWithRegistration` (:55). Left behind by the `BrandLogo` → `ZimmLogo` swap. Note this file is **Tier 2 shared shell** — coordinate with the other squad.

---

## 🟡 Resolve or ticket explicitly

**9 · `FOOTER_FIXTURE` still defaults into the production path** — `footer/index.tsx:509`
```ts
data = FOOTER_FIXTURE,
```
`Footer` renders with no props from `_app`, so production renders placeholder copy. AGENTS.md forbids hardcoded fixtures in production paths. Keep the fixture for stories/tests; render an explicit unavailable state when live config is absent. *(PR55-10)*

**10 · Locale button has no handler** — `footer/index.tsx:458-461`
`<button aria-label="Change locale">` with `// PLACEHOLDER` and no `onClick`. Screen readers announce it as actionable. Either wire it, or make it non-interactive text and drop the button semantics + ARIA. *(PR55-08)*

**11 · The 11 remaining literals** — all currently flagged as provisional, which is the sanctioned pattern, so this is a **design escalation not a code fix**:

| File | Values |
|---|---|
| `atoms/zimmLogo/index.tsx:12-13` | `'327px'`, `'39px'` — already carries a `// §7 raise → foundation/sizes.ts (UI designer)` note |
| `atoms/zimmTextInput/index.tsx:30` | `'36px'` |
| `theme/components/footer.ts:12-15` | `'3rem'`, `'8.75rem'`, `'20rem'`, `'37.5rem'` |
| `footer/index.tsx:25,29` | `'12.5rem'`, `'30rem'` |

Take them to Kiera as one batch. *(PR55-13)*

**12 · `_firstName` / `_lastName` unused** — `footer/index.tsx:355`. Now *intentional* (comment says they're ready for the Omneo POST). Prefix-underscore already signals intent; either add an eslint-disable with the HPC-036 reference or accept the two warnings.

---

## ⏳ The one thing I can't verify for you

**13 · Preview environment vs Figma at the defined breakpoints** — Play 5, question 8.

The MRT preview comment is on the PR, so the URL exists. Per the playbook this is non-optional against a 10-defect / no-Sev3 budget, and it's the only review surface still outstanding. Worth the hour.

---

## ✅ Already correct — don't re-open these

So nobody spends effort re-litigating verified-clean items:

- `tsc` clean · 141 tests pass · **0 lint errors**
- **0** raw hex · **0** `fontSize` in components · **0** `console.log` · **0** data-fetching hooks in `components/`
- **0** Chakra `<Image>` without `alt` — the manual's named blind spot
- Story for all 7 exported components, `Default` in each, categorisation matching `components.md`'s table exactly (`Layout/Footer`, `Elements/Zimm*` ×5, `Forms/ZimmInputAction`)
- State coverage well beyond the bar — 23 exports on `zimmButton` including two `play` stories, plus `KeyboardFocus` and `SubmitInteraction`
- Target size **24px** via `cssVars.spacing.xl` (SC 2.5.8) with `_focusVisible`
- JSDoc + `@returns` on the exported hook · props types match component names · discriminated union on the button (the `typescript.md` idiom)
- Australian spelling correct (`hoverBorderColour`) · named constants throughout, no magic numbers
- `SAFE_HREF_RE` protocol-relative bypass closed with `\/(?!\/)`
- Subscribe false-success replaced by a real `'idle' | 'unavailable' | 'success' | 'error'` state machine
- `footer.ts` consumed via `useMultiStyleConfig('Footer')` at both call sites
- **Atomic tiering correct against Han's F2R contract** — all 5 atoms compose nothing (or only an icon, per Rule A), `zimmInputAction` composes only atoms → molecule

---

**Effort read:** items 1, 4 and 8 are minutes. Items 2, 3, 5, 6 are the real work — half a day, and 6 falls out of 5 for free. Items 9–12 are decisions more than code.

The direction is settled now; this is finishing a migration whose pattern already exists inside the same PR. Want me to draft the in-thread PR replies, or open this as a task list on the PR itself?

     2	import type React from 'react'
     3	import {cssVars} from 'app/utils/cssVars'
     4	
     5	// Figma Textfield flush variant (node 40000265:374): field/border/* tokens.
     6	// hover and filled (has value, unfocused) both darken to focus colour per Figma spec.
     7	const BORDER = {
     8	    default: cssVars.color.border.forms,  // #707070 — Figma field/border/default
     9	    hover:   cssVars.color.border.focus,  // #191919 — Figma field/border/hover
    10	    filled:  cssVars.color.border.focus,  // #191919 — Figma field/border/filled
    11	    focus:   cssVars.color.border.focus,  // #191919 — Figma field/border/focus
    12	    error:   cssVars.color.border.error,  // #9c0000 — Figma field/border/error
    13	} as const
    14	
    15	// Figma field/border/inverse/default = white (opaque), inverse/error = #f98f8c (coral).
    16	// Figma does not spec inverse/hover or inverse/focus separately — use same white.
    17	const BORDER_INVERSE = {
    18	    default: cssVars.color.text.inverse,           // white  — Figma field/border/inverse/default
    19	    hover:   cssVars.color.text.inverse,           // white  — Figma (not separately spec'd, same as default)
    20	    filled:  cssVars.color.text.inverse,           // white  — Figma (not separately spec'd)
    21	    focus:   cssVars.color.text.inverse,           // white  — Figma field/border/inverse/focus
    22	    error:   cssVars.color.status.errorBackground, // #f98f8c — Figma field/border/inverse/error
    23	} as const
    24	
    25	type UseZimmTextInputStateParams = {
    26	    inverse:   boolean
    27	    disabled:  boolean
    28	    hasError:  boolean
    29	    onChange?: (value: string) => void
    30	}
    31	
    32	type UseZimmTextInputStateReturn = {
    33	    value:        string
    34	    focused:      boolean
    35	    floated:      boolean
    36	    borderColour: string
    37	    /** hover border colour — used by the component to apply :hover via CSS (chakra sx) */
    38	    hoverBorderColour: string
    39	    labelColour:  string
    40	    inputRef:     React.RefObject<HTMLInputElement>
    41	    handleChange: (e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void
    42	    handleClear:  () => void
    43	    setFocused:   React.Dispatch<React.SetStateAction<boolean>>
    44	}
    45	
    46	/**
    47	 * Manages interaction state for ZimmTextInput — value, focus, and derived
    48	 * border/label colours aligned to Figma Textfield flush tokens (node 40000265:374).
    49	 * Hover border is no longer managed as JS state — the component applies it via
    50	 * CSS pseudo-class (chakra sx `_hover`) to avoid a useState round-trip per mouse event.
    51	 * @returns value, focus flag, derived visual tokens, inputRef, and event handlers
    52	 */
    53	export const useZimmTextInputState = ({
    54	    inverse,
    55	    disabled,
    56	    hasError,
    57	    onChange,
    58	}: UseZimmTextInputStateParams): UseZimmTextInputStateReturn => {
    59	    const [value,   setValue]   = useState('')
    60	    const [focused, setFocused] = useState(false)
    61	    const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)
    62	
    63	    const floated = focused || value.length > 0
    64	    const palette = inverse ? BORDER_INVERSE : BORDER
    65	
    66	    const borderColour = (() => {
    67	        if (disabled)         return palette.default
    68	        if (hasError)         return palette.error
    69	        if (focused)          return palette.focus
    70	        if (value.length > 0) return palette.filled
    71	        return palette.default
    72	    })()
    73	
    74	    // When in error state, hover keeps the error colour (error > hover in priority).
    75	    // In all other states, hover darkens to focus colour — same value as focus itself.
    76	    const hoverBorderColour = hasError ? borderColour : palette.hover
    77	
    78	    // Figma text/subtle = #666 (colors.text.secondary) for floated/disabled label in light mode.
    79	    // Figma text/inverse/subtle = #969696 (colors.text.inverseGrey) for floated/disabled label in inverse mode.
    80	    const labelColour = (() => {
    81	        if (disabled) return inverse ? cssVars.color.text.inverseGrey : cssVars.color.text.secondary
    82	        if (inverse)  return floated ? cssVars.color.text.inverseGrey : cssVars.color.text.inverse
    83	        return floated ? cssVars.color.text.secondary : cssVars.color.text.default
    84	    })()
    85	
    86	    const handleChange = (e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
    87	        setValue(e.target.value)
    88	        onChange?.(e.target.value)
    89	    }
    90	
    91	    const handleClear = () => {
    92	        setValue('')
    93	        onChange?.('')
    94	        inputRef.current?.focus()
    95	    }
    96	
    97	    return {
    98	        value, focused, floated,
    99	        borderColour, hoverBorderColour, labelColour,
   100	        inputRef,
   101	        handleChange, handleClear,
   102	        setFocused,
   103	    }
   104	}

content.text:
Two of my own items were wrong. Correcting both, and there's bigger news first.

---

# Your working tree already contains items 2, 3 and 4

```
 M overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmTextInput/index.tsx   ← item 2
 M overrides/app/hooks/useZimmTextInputState.ts                     ← item 2
 M overrides/app/theme/foundation/sizes.ts                          ← item 4 (newline reverted)
?? overrides/app/hooks/useZimmTextInputState.test.ts                ← item 3
```

Uncommitted, and I verified it: **`tsc` clean, 160 tests pass** (up from 141). Three of the six "must fix" items are done and just need committing.

---

## Item 2 — controllable `ZimmTextInput` ✅ done, and done well

**Why it mattered:** a field that owns its own value can't be driven by a parent form. In checkout, a parent needs to reset, prefill, or validate-and-revert — none of which is possible if the only channel is an outbound `onChange`.

**What the implementation does** — the standard React idiom, correctly:

```ts
const isControlled = controlledValue !== undefined
const [internalValue, setInternalValue] = useState(defaultValue ?? '')
const value = isControlled ? controlledValue : internalValue
```

Three things it gets right that are easy to get wrong:

- **Single read path.** Every derived token (`floated`, `borderColour`, `labelColour`) reads `value`, so both modes behave identically without duplicated branches.
- **`onChange` fires in both modes**, but internal state is only touched when uncontrolled: `if (!isControlled) setInternalValue(...)`.
- **`handleClear` follows the same rule** — a controlled parent stays authoritative even on clear.

The 19-case test covers both modes plus every derived-token branch (`controlled: defaultValue is ignored`, `controlled: a new prop value is reflected on re-render`). That's thorough.

**Optional nicety, not required:** React normally warns when a component flips controlled↔uncontrolled mid-life. Worth a dev-only guard if you want it, but the tests cover the behaviour.

---

## Item 5 — finish the recipe migration (2 components)

Current state with your uncommitted work applied:

| File | `useState` | inline `style={{}}` | `cssVars` refs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `atoms/zimmTextInput/index.tsx` | 1 | 6 | **29** |
| `molecules/zimmInputAction/index.tsx` | 2 | 1 | 0 |

**Why:** these are the last two components still styling themselves rather than being styled by the theme. Everything in that inline block is unreachable by `theme/components/*`, so a designer token change can't reach them — the exact problem #56 exists to prevent. `zimmButton` and `zimmNavItem` already prove the pattern inside this same PR.

**What changes:**

`theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts` is currently a stub:

```ts
// Placeholder recipe — full theming of ZimmTextInput is deferred.
export const ZimmTextInput = defineStyleConfig({ baseStyle: {} })
```

Fill it in. Specifically, the colour derivation currently living in `useZimmTextInputState` — `borderColour`, `hoverBorderColour`, `labelColour` — moves into the recipe as pseudo-props:

```ts
_hover:        { borderBottomColor: '…' },
_focusWithin:  { borderBottomColor: '…' },
_disabled:     { opacity: 0.4 },
_invalid:      { borderBottomColor: '…' },
```

The hook then keeps only what's genuinely React state: `value`, `focused`, `floated`, `inputRef`, and the handlers. **`floated` has to stay in JS** — it's `value !== '' || focused`, which CSS can't express — so the hook doesn't disappear, it gets smaller and its tests stay valid.

`zimmInputAction`'s 2 `useState` are validation state (`validationError`), not styling — **those stay.** Only its 1 inline style moves.

---

## Item 6 — deleting `cssVars.ts`: what actually replaces it

This is the one you asked about most directly, so here's the honest answer: **nothing new needs to be written.**

`cssVars.ts` is a second set of names for values that already have names. Every entry maps to something already registered in the theme:

| `cssVars` expression | Replacement | Already registered? |
|---|---|---|
| `cssVars.color.text.default` | `color="text.default"` | ✅ `theme.colors` |
| `cssVars.color.background['05']` | `bg="background.05"` | ✅ `theme.colors` |
| `cssVars.spacing.xl` | `p="xl"` / `mb="xl"` | ✅ `theme.space` |
| `cssVars.border.width` | `borderWidth="default"` | ✅ `theme.borderWidths` |
| `cssTextStyles.caption` | `textStyle="caption"` | ✅ `theme.textStyles` |
| `cssVars.font.size['2xs']` | — **never**; use `textStyle` | (deliberately unregistered) |
| `cssVars.focusRingOffset.default` | `import {focusRingOffsets}` from `foundation` | constant |
| `cssVars.motion.duration.fast` | `import {motion}` from `foundation` | constant |

**Why delete it at all:** it's a hand-typed mirror of `zimmTokens.ts`'s *key names*. Rename a key there and this file breaks **silently** — an unresolved CSS custom property produces no error, just no style. Nothing tests the correspondence, and `theme/index.test.tsx`'s 125 guards know nothing about it. That's the same failure mode #56 removed by cutting 237 literals to 64.

**The deletion is a dependency chain, not one commit.** Ten importers, and the order matters:

| Step | Files | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5 story files | `cssVars.color.*` → Chakra props (`bg="background.05"`). Stories render inside `ChakraProvider`, so this just works |
| 2 | `zimmLogo/index.tsx` | 1 ref for the SVG `fill` → `currentColor` or a Chakra token |
| 3 | `zimmNavItem/index.tsx` | 1 remaining `cssVars.font` ref → move into `zimmNavItem.ts` |
| 4 | `zimmTextInput` + hook + test | **This is item 5.** Colours to the recipe, hook keeps real state |
| 5 | `footer/index.tsx` | 5 `cssTextStyles.*` refs → `textStyle="…"`; remaining `cssVars` → `footer.ts` |
| 6 | — | `rm overrides/app/utils/cssVars.ts` |

**Steps 4 and 5 are the work; 1–3 and 6 are minutes.** And note `cssTextStyles` still carries `button` and `buttonSm` — the two presets #56 explicitly deleted from `globalStyles.ts` — so step 5 also closes that.

---

## Item 7 — I mischaracterised this. Correcting it.

I said `footer.ts` mirrors `_foundation.breakpoints`, making them a synced duplicate. **That's wrong.** `_foundation` contains **only `sizes`** — there is no `breakpoints` key:

```ts
const _foundation = {
  sizes: {
    footer: { subscribeBodyMax: '12.5rem' },   // 200px
    modal:  { footer: '30rem' },               // 480px
  },
} as const
```

Meanwhile `footer.ts` holds an entirely **different** set: `BP` (3 breakpoints in `em`) plus `SPACE_SECTION`, `SIZE_COL_NAV`, `SIZE_COL_SUB`, `SIZE_COL_MAP`, `COLOUR_HALF_INV`.

So they don't duplicate each other. **The real finding is smaller and different:**

1. **`footer.ts:1` carries a false comment** — *"mirror `_foundation.breakpoints` in footer/index.tsx"* points at a key that doesn't exist. Same class of problem as `overrideStyling.md`'s dangling references.
2. **Provisional values are split across two files** with no rule for which goes where — `subscribeBodyMax` sits in the component while `SIZE_COL_NAV` sits in the theme, both for the same reason.

**What changes:** fix or delete the false comment, and move `_foundation.sizes` into `footer.ts` alongside the other provisional consts so one file holds all of them pending Kiera. Then escalate the whole set as one batch. Lower severity than I originally gave it — this is tidiness plus a wrong comment, not drift.

content.text:
Now it's clear — and item 7 is **not what I originally called it.** It isn't a duplicate. It's the visible residue of a half-finished migration. ## What's actually going on Commit `00fb6ab` — *"migrate layout to footer.ts theme config"* — moved the footer onto a Chakra recipe. But it only migrated **2 of the 5 components** in that file: | Component | Line | Styling source | |---|---|---| | `SubscribeModal` | 139 | ❌ inline `style={{}}` | | `SubscribeSection` | 334 | ❌ inline `style={{}}` | | `ContactIconRow` | 416 | ❌ inline | | `BottomBar` | 451 | ✅ `useMultiStyleConfig('Footer')` | | `Footer` | 523 | ✅ `useMultiStyleConfig('Footer')` | `_foundation` exists **only** to feed the two that were left behind. It has exactly two values and exactly two consumers: ```ts // footer/index.tsx:21 const _foundation = { sizes: { footer: { subscribeBodyMax: '12.5rem' }, // 200px → used once, line 367 modal: { footer: '30rem' }, // 480px → used once, line 239 }, } as const ``` Meanwhile `footer.ts` already holds the same *kind* of value, correctly, as named constants — `SPACE_SECTION`, `SIZE_COL_NAV`, `SIZE_COL_SUB`, `SIZE_COL_MAP`, `COLOUR_HALF_INV` — heavily used by the recipe (`BP` alone has 17 uses). **So the same category of value lives in two files for no reason other than which components got migrated.** ## Three specific defects **1 · The comment on `footer.ts:1` is false.** ```ts // Provisional breakpoint values — mirror _foundation.breakpoints in footer/index.tsx. ``` `_foundation` has **no `breakpoints` key.** It has `sizes` and nothing else. A developer told to keep these "in sync" will go looking and find nothing — the same dangling-reference problem we found in `overrideStyling.md`. **2 · `_foundation` is a dangerous name.** `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` is a real, Tier 1, designer-owned directory. Naming a local const `_foundation` inside a component means a `grep foundation` returns a false hit, and a reader may reasonably assume it's an approved token source. The underscore says "private"; the noun says the opposite. **3 · The values contradict the file's own stated ownership.** `footer.ts` declares, in its own header: > *footer.ts owns: … **All responsive layout styles for each named part** — consumed via `__css` in footer/index.tsx* `maxWidth` on the modal panel and on the subscribe body copy are layout for named parts. They're in the wrong file by the file's own rule. ## The fix **Step 1 — move the two values into `footer.ts`,** following the pattern already established three lines above them: ```ts const SPACE_SECTION = '3rem' // alias/space/section (48px) const SIZE_COL_NAV = '8.75rem' // alias/size/footer/col-width-nav (140px) const SIZE_COL_SUB = '20rem' // alias/size/footer/col-width-subscribe (320px) const SIZE_COL_MAP = '37.5rem' // alias/size/footer/col-width-sitemap (600px) const COLOUR_HALF_INV = 'rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.5)' // alias/color/opacity-50-inverse + const SIZE_MODAL_SUB = '30rem' // alias/size/modal/footer (480px) + const SIZE_SUB_BODY_MAX = '12.5rem' // alias/size/footer/subscribe-body-max (200px) ``` **Step 2 — expose them as recipe parts**, so the components consume them the way `BottomBar` already does: ```ts subscribeModalPanel: { background: 'background.07', width: '100%', maxWidth: SIZE_MODAL_SUB, padding: '3xl', }, subscribeBody: { maxWidth: SIZE_SUB_BODY_MAX, marginBottom: '3xl', }, ``` **Step 3 — migrate the two call sites.** Both components need the one line `BottomBar` already has: ```tsx const styles = useMultiStyleConfig('Footer', {}) ``` then: ```tsx // line 239 — SubscribeModal -
+ // line 367 — SubscribeSection -

+ ``` **Step 4 — delete `_foundation` entirely** (lines 21–32) and **fix the comment on `footer.ts:1`**: ```ts - // Provisional breakpoint values — mirror _foundation.breakpoints in footer/index.tsx. + // Provisional breakpoint values — no confirmed token yet. // Replace with foundation/gridSystem.ts imports once the UI designer confirms the tokens. ``` ## Why it's worth doing now rather than later Three things fall out of the same change: - **All provisional values end up in one file.** When Kiera confirms the tokens, it's one file to edit and one PR — instead of hunting a shadow object in a component. - **It closes part of item 5.** `SubscribeModal` and `SubscribeSection` are two of the components still styling themselves inline; migrating them removes several of the footer's remaining `cssVars` references, which feeds item 6. - **It removes a name that will mislead someone.** `_foundation` next to a real Tier 1 `foundation/` is the kind of thing that costs a confused half-hour once and then keeps costing it. While you're in there, `MODAL_OVERLAY_BG`, `MODAL_BG`, `MODAL_TEXT_MUTED` and `MODAL_Z_INDEX` (lines 117–123) are the same category — presentational constants living in the component because the component wasn't on the recipe. Same treatment, same commit. **Effort: an hour or so.** Mostly mechanical, and the pattern is already proven twice in the same file. Want me to make this change?

content.text:
Now I have the full picture — and it's a cleaner story than I first told you.

## What item 8 is

Three symbols ESLint flags as unused in `header/index.tsx`:

```
34:3  warning  'AccountIcon' is defined but never used
38:3  warning  'HeartIcon' is defined but never used
55:7  warning  'IconButtonWithRegistration' is assigned a value but never used
```

They aren't orphans. All three exist solely to serve a commented-out JSX block at lines 359–380 — the base SFCC Account and Wishlist **icon buttons**:

```jsx
{/* <IconButtonWithRegistration
      icon={<AccountIcon />}
      aria-label={… 'My Account' …}
      onClick={onMyAccountClick}
    />
    <IconButtonWithRegistration
      icon={<HeartIcon />}
      aria-label={… 'Wishlist' …}
      onClick={onWishlistClick}
    /> */}
```

## What's actually wrong

**My first read was wrong on two counts.** I said they were "left behind by the `BrandLogo` → `ZimmLogo` swap" and that the fix was to delete the imports. Neither holds — they predate that swap, and deleting the imports while leaving the block would strand it.

Here's what the evidence actually says:

**1 · The block is *superseded*, not *pending*.** Line 230 of the same file:

```jsx
{/* Desktop right: Account | Saved | Bag as text */}
```

and at line 245:

```jsx
<ButtonWithRegistration onClick={onMyAccountClick}>
```

The Zimmermann header design replaced base SFCC's **icon** buttons with **text** buttons. `ButtonWithRegistration` supersedes `IconButtonWithRegistration`; text labels supersede `AccountIcon`/`HeartIcon`.

**2 · The requirement is satisfied.** `.docs/prd/homepage.md:18` — HPC-018, Confirmed:

> The confirmed header icon set is: **Search, Account, and Bag**.

Account is present — as text. So commenting out the icon version isn't a regression against a confirmed requirement. Same for Wishlist, which the header renders as "Saved".

**3 · It's been dead since day one.** `git log -L` traces the commenting to `cd60b7a Initial commit during Detailed Design phase` — i.e. it was disabled the moment the file was copied into `overrides/`. That's the **copy-first rule working as designed**: copy the base file verbatim, comment out what you're replacing. It was a deliberate reference marker, not an accident.

**4 · And the rule collision is real.** AGENTS.md:

> **Comments:** Do not remove existing commented-out code or comments (except when removing the corresponding code) — leave for the user to delete manually.

So this is a decision for you, not a cleanup a reviewer performs.

## How to fix it — three options

**Option A · Leave it, document why** *(zero risk, 3 warnings remain)*
Add a line above the import block:
```tsx
// AccountIcon / HeartIcon / IconButtonWithRegistration support the commented-out base
// SFCC icon-button block below (~L359). Superseded by the Account | Saved | Bag text
// buttons per the Zimmermann header design; kept as a reference to the base implementation.
```

**Option B · Delete block and imports together** *(my recommendation)*
AGENTS.md explicitly permits removing commented code *"when removing the corresponding code"* — and here the block **is** the corresponding code. Removes ~25 lines and all 3 warnings.

Justified because: the block is superseded by a shipped alternative rather than awaiting a decision; it's been dead since the initial commit; git history preserves it if anyone ever wants it back; and the file gets a Tier 2 review regardless.

**Option C · `eslint-disable` with a reason**
Keeps the block, silences the warnings, states the reason at the point of use. Middle ground, but it adds a suppression to carry forever for code nobody intends to restore.

## What I'd do

**Option B.** The usual reason to preserve commented-out code is "we might need this back" — that doesn't apply when a working replacement is already shipping in the same file and the PRD confirms the replacement satisfies the requirement.

One caveat worth your judgement: `header/index.tsx` is **Tier 2 shared shell**, owned by both squads. Deleting 25 lines of base-template reference from it is the kind of thing the other squad might reasonably want to know about, even though it's inert.

Want me to make the Option B change? It's a small, contained edit — and I'd leave it uncommitted alongside the item 7 work for you to review.

Item 8 done — **+9 lines, no deletions.**

## What I added

Two notes at the two places ESLint points at. The main one, above the icons import:

```tsx
// AccountIcon and HeartIcon are imported but not rendered. They serve the commented-out
// base SFCC icon-button block further down this file (search: IconButtonWithRegistration).
// That block was disabled when this file was first copied into overrides/ per the copy-first
// rule, and is superseded by the Account | Saved | Bag *text* buttons the Zimmermann header
// design uses instead — see the "Desktop right" block below. HPC-018 (Confirmed) requires
// Search / Account / Bag in the header; Account is present as text, so nothing is missing.
// Kept as a reference to the base implementation, per AGENTS.md's rule on commented-out code.
```

and a one-line cross-reference at `IconButtonWithRegistration`.

It answers the four questions a reader would have: *why unused*, *what they serve*, *why it's disabled*, and *why keeping it is deliberate rather than neglect* — with the HPC-018 reference so nobody has to re-derive that Account isn't missing.

## Gates

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | ✅ 0 errors |
| `npx vitest run` | ✅ **160 passed** (4 files) |
| New non-prettier problems from my edits | **0** across all three files |

## A correction to my item 7 report

I told you eslint showed **"0 problems"** on the footer files after item 7. **That was wrong** — my grep pattern was being defeated by ESLint's ANSI colour codes, so it counted nothing and I read that as clean. Re-checked with `--format json`:

| File | prettier | non-prettier |
|---|---|---|
| `header/index.tsx` | 2 | **3 warnings** — exactly the Option A ones ✓ |
| `footer/index.tsx` | 392 | 2 warnings (`_firstName`/`_lastName`, pre-existing) |
| `theme/components/footer.ts` | 230 | **0** |

The substantive conclusion holds — **I introduced zero non-prettier problems** — but the prettier numbers are not zero, and I shouldn't have said they were.

On `footer.ts` specifically: it had **199** prettier errors before my edit and has **230** after. My 38 added lines contributed 31, because I matched the file's existing aligned-colon house style, which prettier itself disagrees with. That's the same reason the file already had 199.

**I deliberately haven't run `eslint --fix` on these files.** Doing it now would reformat all 199 pre-existing errors in `footer.ts` alongside my 31, burying the item 7 diff in mass reformatting. Item 1 does it across the whole branch in one deliberate pass, which keeps the history readable.

## Where things stand

Six items now sit uncommitted in your tree:


content.text:
Now I have the full diagnosis. (Correction: `zimmInputAction` has **one** `useState`, not two — my earlier count included the import line.)

---

# Item 5 — what it is

Two components still style themselves at the call site instead of being styled by the theme.

| Component | `useState` | inline `style={{}}` | recipe refs | `cssVars` refs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `atoms/zimmTextInput` | 1 | **6** | **0** | **29** |
| `molecules/zimmInputAction` | 1 *(validation — legitimate)* | 1 | 0 | 0 |

For comparison, the ones already migrated: `zimmButton` 0/0, `zimmNavItem` 0/0 with 4 recipe refs.

## What's wrong

**1 · The recipe exists and nothing uses it.** `theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts` is registered in `theme/components/index.ts` — and is this:

```ts
// Placeholder recipe — full theming of ZimmTextInput is deferred.
// Register here so the theme object doesn't throw on runtime access.
export const ZimmTextInput = defineStyleConfig({
    baseStyle: {},
})
```

**0 references** from the component. It's the same orphaned-artifact pattern `footer.ts` had before item 7 — registered, empty, looks like compliance.

**2 · Six inline `style={{}}` blocks** at lines 69, 87, 90, 119, 172, 177 — the root div, content div, label, input, and both helper/error paragraphs. Inline styles carry the highest specificity short of `!important`, so **the theme cannot reach any of them.** A designer token change stops at the door.

**3 · The colour logic lives in a hook, not the theme.** `useZimmTextInputState` computes and returns `borderColour`, `hoverBorderColour`, `labelColour` — a five-input decision table (inverse × disabled × hasError × focused × filled). Under #56 that's exactly what `_hover` / `_focusWithin` / `_disabled` / `_invalid` express, and it belongs in `theme/components/`.

**4 · It's the single biggest blocker on item 6.** 29 of the branch's `cssVars` references are in this one file. Nothing else comes close.

**5 · The mixed idiom is confusing.** Two elements already use `chakra.div sx={{}}` with a proper `_hover` and a WCAG-correct `_focusVisible` — so the component *half* knows the pattern. The other six elements are raw inline styles.

## The one thing that legitimately stays

`floated = value !== '' || focused` drives the label position and input opacity. CSS can express `:focus-within`, but "has a value" isn't reliably expressible without a `:placeholder-shown` trick that changes the markup contract.

**So `floated` stays in JS** — it just gets passed *into* the recipe rather than used to pick colours in the component.

## How to fix it

Convert to a Chakra **multipart recipe with a prop-driven `baseStyle`**. Chakra 2.7.0 supports this — `baseStyle` can be a function receiving props.

**`theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts`:**

```ts
export const ZimmTextInput = {
  parts: ['root', 'row', 'content', 'label', 'input', 'clearButton', 'helper', 'error'],
  baseStyle: ({ inverse, disabled, hasError, floated }) => ({
    root:  { display: 'block', width: '100%', opacity: disabled ? 0.4 : 1 },
    row:   {
      display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 'xs',
      borderBottom: '…',                       // the borderColour table moves here
      _hover: disabled ? undefined : { borderBottomColor: '…' },
    },
    label: { /* the floated ? … : … branches */ },
    input: { /* … */ },
    clearButton: { /* keeps the existing _focusVisible */ },
    helper: { /* inverse branch */ },
    error:  { /* inverse branch */ },
  }),
}
```

**In the component:**

```tsx
const styles = useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmTextInput', { inverse, disabled, hasError, floated })

<chakra.div __css={styles.root}>
  <chakra.div __css={styles.row}>
    <chakra.label __css={styles.label} htmlFor={inputId}>{label}</chakra.label>
    <chakra.input __css={styles.input} … />
```

**The hook slims to what it should own** — `value`, `focused`, `floated`, `inputRef`, `handleChange`, `handleClear`, `setFocused`. The three `*Colour` returns disappear.

`zimmInputAction` is trivial by comparison: one `<form style={{display:'block', width:'100%'}}>` → `<chakra.form>`. Its `useState` is `validationError` — real validation state, which stays.

## The trade-off worth knowing about

**7 of the 19 tests you just wrote cover colour derivation** (`inverse mode uses the inverse palette`, `hover keeps the error colour when in error`, `disabled uses the subtle colour for the mode`, etc.). If the colour table moves to the recipe, those tests no longer describe the hook.

**But they don't die — they get simpler.** A recipe `baseStyle` is a plain function, so testing it needs no `renderHook`:

```ts
expect(ZimmTextInput.baseStyle({ inverse: true, hasError: true }).row.borderBottom)
  .toContain('…')
```

That's a cheaper test than the hook version, and it tests the thing the designer actually edits. So the migration relocates the coverage rather than losing it — worth doing the test move in the same commit so nothing is uncovered in between.

## Why it's worth it

- Kills **29 of the branch's `cssVars` references** in one file — the single biggest step toward deleting `cssVars.ts` (item 6)
- Makes the last non-conformant atom themeable, so a designer token change actually reaches it
- Removes the orphaned-stub smell — the registered recipe finally does something
- Leaves `zimmButton`, `zimmNavItem`, `zimmTextInput` all on the same pattern, which is what a reviewer will look for

**Effort: this is the largest remaining item — roughly half a day**, most of it in getting the label/input `floated` branches right and moving the 7 tests. Everything else in the list is minutes to an hour.

Want me to do it? I'd suggest committing items 2/3/4/7/8 first so this lands as its own reviewable diff rather than merging into the pile.

Item 5 done and green.

## What changed

| File | Before → After |
|---|---|
| `theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts` | 8-line empty stub → **173-line multipart recipe** |
| `atoms/zimmTextInput/index.tsx` | 191 → **115 lines** |
| `hooks/useZimmTextInputState.ts` | 118 → **63 lines** |
| `molecules/zimmInputAction/index.tsx` | `<form style={{}}>` → `<chakra.form __css>` |
| `theme/components/zimmTextInput.test.ts` | **new**, 13 tests |
| `hooks/useZimmTextInputState.test.ts` | 19 → 10 tests (colour coverage relocated) |

## The mechanism table now

| Component | `useState` | inline style | recipe | `cssVars` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `zimmButton` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `zimmIcon` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| **`zimmTextInput`** | **0** *(was 1)* | **0** *(was 6)* | **10** *(was 0)* | **0** *(was 29)* |
| `zimmNavItem` | 0 | 0 | 4 | 2 |
| `zimmInputAction` | 1 *(validation)* | **0** *(was 1)* | 1 | 0 |
| `zimmLogo` | 0 | 1 | 0 | 2 |

**29 `cssVars` references eliminated from one file** — that was the branch's single largest consumer, and the main thing standing between you and deleting `cssVars.ts`.

## How it's structured

The recipe takes the state the theme can't observe and resolves the Figma cascade itself:

```ts
baseStyle: ({inverse, disabled, focused, filled}) => ({
  root, row, content, label, input, clearButton, helper, error
})
```

with three exported resolvers — `resolveBorderColour`, `resolveHoverBorderColour`, `resolveLabelColour` — carrying the precedence rules and their Figma comments.

The component feeds it back:

```tsx
const styles = useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmTextInput', {
  inverse, disabled, hasError, focused, filled: value.length > 0,
})
```

The hook now owns only what React must: value, focus, `floated`, the ref and the handlers. **Both the controlled/uncontrolled logic from item 2 and the WCAG 2.5.8 24px target and 2.4.7 focus ring survived intact** — the latter two now live in the `clearButton` part.

## On the test trade-off

I flagged that 9 colour tests would be invalidated. They weren't lost — they moved and got cheaper. No `renderHook`, just direct function calls:

```ts
expect(resolveBorderColour({...base, hasError: true, filled: true}))
  .toBe('var(--zimm-color-status-error)')
```

Plus 4 new wiring tests the hook version couldn't express — every declared part is produced, the row border reflects the resolved colour, `_hover` is suppressed when disabled, and the floated label switches size and position.

**Net: 160 → 164 tests.** All 5 files pass, `tsc` clean, **0 non-prettier lint problems** on everything I touched.

## Two things worth knowing

**I hit one type error and fixed it** — `_hover` isn't on `SystemStyleObject`'s plain-CSS surface, so that assertion needed a `Record<string, unknown>` cast with a comment explaining why.

**Prettier counts went up** (recipe 138, component 93) for the same reason as item 7 — I matched the files' aligned-colon house style, which prettier disagrees with. Item 1 normalises all of it in one pass; doing it now would bury this diff.

## Remaining after this

`zimmLogo` is the last holdout — 1 inline style and 2 `cssVars` refs, both for the SVG `fill` and the provisional `327px`/`39px` already flagged for Kiera. Small.

For **item 6**, the `cssVars.ts` importers are now: `footer/index.tsx` (35), `zimmNavItem` (2), `zimmLogo` (2), the hook's test — gone — and 5 story files. The heavy one left is the footer.

Working tree now has seven modified files and two untracked tests across items 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 — all green. Want me to run item 1 (`eslint --fix`) now to normalise the lot?

content.text:
Now I have the accurate picture. Two corrections to my own earlier reporting first.

## Corrections

**`cssTextStyles` has 7 presets, not 5.** `body2` and `heading3` exist — my earlier count used a regex that couldn't match keys containing digits. The findings doc's *"PR55-05 Partially — 7 → 5 presets"* is wrong and needs fixing; the count never dropped.

**And I nearly reported a bug that isn't one.** I thought the footer referenced two removed presets. It doesn't — they resolve fine.

---

# Item 6 — what it is

`overrides/app/utils/cssVars.ts` — **245 lines**, exporting two objects:

- **`cssVars`** — 91 unique `var(--zimm-*)` strings, hand-typed to mirror `zimmTokens.ts`'s key names
- **`cssTextStyles`** — 7 presets (`navigation`, `caption`, `footer`, `body2`, `heading3`, `button`, `buttonSm`) reimplementing registered `textStyles`

**8 importers, 53 references.** Item 5 removed 29 of them, so what's left is one real job and seven small ones:

| Importer | Refs | What it uses |
|---|---|---|
| `components/footer/index.tsx` | **35** | `color.text` ×9, `spacing.*` ×15, `color.opacity[50]` ×2, 5 `cssTextStyles` |
| 5 story files | 15 | `color.background['05']`, `color.text`, `spacing.xl` |
| `atoms/zimmNavItem` | 1 | `font.family.body` |
| `atoms/zimmLogo` | 2 | `color.text.inverse` / `.default` for the SVG `fill` |

## What's wrong

**Being straight: it isn't broken.** I checked all 91 var names against `zimmTokens.ts` — **0 drifted.** So this is a maintenance-risk argument, not a live-defect one.

**1 · It's a second set of names for values that already have names.** Every entry maps to something already registered in the theme. `cssVars.color.text.default` and `color="text.default"` resolve to the same value; one is registered and type-checked, the other is a hand-typed string.

**2 · The sync is hand-maintained and nothing tests it.** `theme/index.test.tsx`'s 125 guards know nothing about this file. Rename a key in `zimmTokens.ts` and the failure is **silent** — an unresolved CSS custom property produces no error, just no style. Currently clean; nothing keeps it that way.

**3 · The type makes a typo compile.**

```ts
export const cssTextStyles: Record<string, Record<string, string>> = {
```

Any string key typechecks. `cssTextStyles.captionn` returns `undefined`, spreads nothing, and renders an unstyled element with no warning at build or runtime. That's a real latent hazard — I went looking for exactly this and only didn't find it because nobody's typo'd yet.

**4 · `button` and `buttonSm` duplicate what `button.ts` owns.** #56 deliberately removed `.zimm-text-btn-lg/-sm` from `globalStyles.ts` and made `button.ts` the single source for button styling. These two presets reintroduce that duplication one layer up.

## How to fix it

Nothing new needs writing — every value already has a registered equivalent:

| `cssVars` expression | Replacement | Registered as |
|---|---|---|
| `cssVars.color.text.default` | `color="text.default"` | `theme.colors` |
| `cssVars.color.background['05']` | `bg="background.05"` | `theme.colors` |
| `cssVars.spacing.xl` | `p="xl"` / `mb="xl"` | `theme.space` |
| `cssTextStyles.caption` | `textStyle="caption"` | `theme.textStyles` |
| `cssVars.font.family.body` | `fontFamily="body"` | `theme.fonts` |
| `cssVars.color.opacity[50]` | `var(--zimm-color-opacity-50)` in a recipe | — |

**Order of operations** — deliberate, because each step shrinks the next:

| Step | Files | Work |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5 stories | `cssVars.color.background['05']` → `bg="background.05"`. They render inside `ChakraProvider`, so this just works |
| 2 | `zimmLogo` | 2 refs → `currentColor` or a `useToken` lookup for the SVG `fill` |
| 3 | `zimmNavItem` | 1 ref → move `fontFamily` into `zimmNavItem.ts` |
| 4 | **`footer/index.tsx`** | **The job.** 35 refs → `footer.ts` parts, following the pattern item 7 established for three elements |
| 5 | — | `rm overrides/app/utils/cssVars.ts` |

Steps 1–3 and 5 are minutes. **Step 4 is the work** — and it's the same migration item 7 did for `SubscribeModal` and `SubscribeSection`, applied to the remaining elements. `ContactIconRow` is the last footer sub-component still fully inline.

## My honest read on whether to do it now

The strongest argument isn't the drift risk — it's that **the footer is the last place in the PR still styling itself at the call site**, and finishing it closes items 5 and 6 together. Deleting `cssVars.ts` then becomes a consequence rather than a task.

The weakest argument is urgency: 0/91 drifted, so nothing is broken today.

If you want it done, I'd do steps 1–3 now (15 minutes, low risk) and treat step 4 as its own change — it's the larger half of what's left in the footer, and it deserves a reviewable diff of its own rather than being bundled.

Want me to take steps 1–3, the whole thing, or leave it for the branch owner?

Steps 1–3 done. **`footer/index.tsx` is now the only remaining `cssVars` importer** — down from 8.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | ✅ 0 errors |
| `npx vitest run` | ✅ 164 passed |
| Non-prettier lint, all 10 touched files | ✅ **0** |

## What changed

**Step 1 — five story files.** All `cssVars` imports removed:

```tsx
<Box bg={cssVars.color.background['05']} …>   →  <Box bg="background.05" …>
<Text style={{color: cssVars.color.text.secondary}}>  →  <Text color="text.secondary">
<div style={{backgroundColor: …, padding: …}}>  →  <Box bg="background.05" p="xl">
```

The two `<div>` cases became `<Box>` (imported from Chakra), which also removed four inline styles from the stories.

**Step 2 — `zimmLogo`.** An SVG `fill` attribute needs a concrete colour, not a `var()` reference, so `useToken` is the right tool rather than a Chakra prop:

```tsx
const [inverseColour, defaultColour] = useToken('colors', ['text.inverse', 'text.default'])
const fill = variant === 'inverse' ? inverseColour : defaultColour
```

Behaviour is identical — it now resolves through the registered theme instead of a hand-typed mirror. All 10 `<path fill={fill}>` untouched.

**Step 3 — `zimmNavItem`.** This one had a subtlety worth flagging.

The `fontFamily` override was applied via `sx` specifically because **`sx` outranks the `textStyle` prop, and `__css` doesn't.** Moving `fontFamily` into the recipe alone would have let `textStyle="navigation"` win and silently restore the heading font.

So I moved **both** into the recipe, ordered so `fontFamily` overrides the expanded `textStyle`:

```ts
const baseStyle = {
    textStyle: 'navigation',
    fontFamily: 'var(--zimm-font-family-body)',   // deliberately overrides the spread
    …
}
```

and dropped `textStyle="navigation"`, `sx={{fontFamily}}` and the `fontOverride` const from both JSX branches. Net effect: the component carries no styling at all now — just `__css={styles}`.

## Where item 6 stands

```
cssVars.ts:  245 lines, 91 vars, 7 text presets
importers:   1  (was 8)
             └─ components/footer/index.tsx — 35 refs
```

Step 4 is the whole remaining job: migrating the footer's 35 references into `footer.ts` parts, following the pattern item 7 established for `SubscribeModal` and `SubscribeSection`. `ContactIconRow` is the last sub-component still fully inline.

Once that's done, step 5 is `rm overrides/app/utils/cssVars.ts` — and items 5 and 6 close together.

- **Modal** — `modalOverlay`, `modalTitle`, `modalField`, `modalFieldLast`, `modalConsent`, `modalConsentLink`, `modalDisclaimer`, `modalActions`

## Three judgement calls worth flagging

**1 · I added an `sx` prop to `ZimmNavItem`.** The footer passes styles *into* that component, and its only channel was `style?: CSSProperties` — which takes raw CSS, so Chakra token keys like `'xs'` wouldn't resolve. A three-line `sx?: SystemStyleObject` pass-through lets the footer send `sx={styles.legalLink}` properly. Small API addition to an atom we own, and it's the idiomatic Chakra escape hatch.

**2 · The contact icons now inherit their colour.** `ZimmIcon` already defaults to `color='currentColor'`, so instead of passing `color={cssVars.color.text.inverse}` at three call sites, `contactIconLink` sets `color` once and the glyphs inherit. Same for the locale chevron.

## Final gates

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | ✅ 0 errors |
| `npx vitest run` | ✅ **164 passed** (5 files) |
| Non-prettier lint, 18 changed files | ✅ **5** — all pre-existing and intentional |
| Prettier | 1702 — item 1's job |

The 5 remaining warnings are the ones we deliberately kept: `_firstName`/`_lastName` (HPC-036 placeholders) and the three header imports documented under item 8.

## Item status

| # | Item | |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `eslint --fix` | **OPEN** |
| 2 | `ZimmTextInput` controllable | ✅ |
| 3 | Tests — 10 hook + 13 recipe | ✅ |
| 4 | `sizes.ts` Tier 1 revert | ✅ |
| 5 | Recipe migration | ✅ |
| 6 | `cssVars.ts` deleted | ✅ |
| 7 | `_foundation` collapsed | ✅ |
| 8 | Header imports documented | ✅ |

## What step 5 involved beyond the delete

**A safety sweep first** — 0 importers under `overrides/`, and no references in `e2e/`, `scripts/` or `.storybook/` either.

**Regenerated the registry.** `.claude/registry/utils.md` still listed `cssVars` as a Custom util. `node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` cleared it — utils.md is now 30 entries, Custom: 1. The pre-commit hook would have caught this, but leaving a stale generated file in the tree isn't tidy.

**Backups kept.** `scratchpad/cssVars.ts.DELETED-BACKUP`, and it's recoverable from git regardless since the file is tracked.

## The arc, end to end

`cssVars.ts` was **245 lines with 8 importers and 53 references**. It's gone, and nothing needed writing to replace it — every value already had a registered name in the theme. The work was moving 53 call sites onto names that already existed.

Along the way the footer went **555 → 463 lines** with inline styles from **15 → 1**, and `zimmTextInput` from **6 inline styles and 29 `cssVars` refs → 0 and 0**.

## Two notes for the branch owner

**One tooling issue found and fixed mid-flight:** `ZimmNavItem` only accepted `style?: CSSProperties`, so it couldn't receive theme-resolved styles. I added an `sx?: SystemStyleObject` pass-through — three lines, and it's the idiomatic Chakra escape hatch.

**The Storybook `play` tests haven't been exercised.** `vitest` doesn't run them, and this work changed element types across the footer modal, the text input and the nav item. A `npm run storybook` pass — or the CI storybook job — should run before merge.

Working tree: **19 modified, 1 deleted, 2 new test files**, nothing committed. Item 1 is all that's left, and it'll touch most of these files again — so it's cleanest as its own commit after you've reviewed the substantive diffs.

Item 1 done. **All 8 items complete.**

## Result

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| prettier problems | **2126** | **0** |
| non-prettier | 5 | **5** (unchanged, all intentional) |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | — | ✅ 0 errors |
| `npx vitest run` | — | ✅ **164 passed** |

27 files formatted. The 5 surviving warnings are exactly the ones we deliberately kept: `_firstName`/`_lastName` (HPC-036 placeholders) and the three header imports documented under item 8.

## Confirming it was formatting-only

Three ways, because a 2126-change auto-fix on an uncommitted tree deserves it:

**1 · By construction.** I audited before running: of everything ESLint offered to fix, **2126 of 2126 were `prettier/prettier`** — no other rule provided a fix, so `--fix` had nothing else it could apply.

**2 · By inspection.** The changes are quote spacing, semicolons, indentation (4→2 spaces), and line reflowing:

```diff
- import {useRef, useState} from 'react'
+ import { useRef, useState } from 'react';

-     value?:        string
+   value?: string;
```

My first normalisation check flagged 22 files, which was my test being wrong, not the fix — prettier also changes quotes, semicolons and trailing commas, none of which are whitespace. After normalising those too, only 3 files differed, and inspecting them showed line **re-wrapping** (prettier joining a 3-line `renderHook(...)` call onto one line, reflowing a multi-line import list) — my normaliser couldn't account for that, but the tokens are identical.

**3 · By behaviour.** `tsc` clean and all 164 tests still pass.

## Final state — all 8 items

| # | Item | |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `eslint --fix` | ✅ |
| 2 | `ZimmTextInput` controllable | ✅ |
| 3 | Tests — 10 hook + 13 recipe | ✅ |
| 4 | `sizes.ts` Tier 1 revert | ✅ |
| 5 | Recipe migration | ✅ |
| 6 | `cssVars.ts` deleted | ✅ |
| 7 | `_foundation` collapsed | ✅ |
| 8 | Header imports documented | ✅ |

**Working tree:** 19 modified, 1 deleted, 2 new test files, plus 3 regenerated registry files. Nothing committed — that's still your call.

## Two things before this merges

**The `--fix` reformatted 27 files, including 5 I never otherwise touched** (`contentfulFixture.ts`, `contentfulSchema.placeholder.ts`, `footer/index.stories.tsx`, `zimmIcon/index.tsx` and its story). That's the intended scope — it makes CI clean — but it means the formatting commit is large and mechanical. **Strongly worth committing it separately** from the substantive work, or the real changes become unreviewable.

**Storybook `play` tests still haven't been run.** `vitest` doesn't execute them, and this work changed element types across the footer modal, text input and nav item. `npm run storybook` or the CI storybook job should pass before merge — it's the one gate none of my verification covered.
