# Styling an Override Component

How to style a component under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/theme/`.
Cross-references [overrides.md](./overrides.md) (module-replacement correctness — a
different concern: that file is about not breaking SFCC's own imports, this one is
about what values to reach for once the component compiles). Day-to-day CSS/token
rules live in [css.md](./css.md); this file is the practical "what do I actually type"
companion.

---

## The hierarchy — reach for these in order

1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
   All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
2. **Semantic colour/spacing token strings** — `color="text.default"`, `bg="background.02"`,
   `spacing="m"`, `padding={{ base: 'm', md: 'xl' }}`. These resolve through
   `theme.colors`/`theme.space` (both registered — see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment
   for which foundation scales are and aren't registered, and why).
3. **A component's own theme config** (`theme/components/<name>.ts`) for anything that
   needs to vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop — see
   "Component-local tokens" below. For an interactive component with existing Chakra
   support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme config is the single source of truth —
   see "One canonical styling surface per component type" below.
4. **`sx` prop** for a one-off Chakra-prop-system gap, per [css.md](./css.md).
5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors,
   keyframes) — same file, same rules as [css.md](./css.md) already documents.

**Never**: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token
instead. The one standing exception is `button.ts`'s provisional height/padding
constants (`BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`), pending UI-designer
sign-off — see Units below. Run `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` before opening
a PR that touches `overrides/app/components/**` or `overrides/app/theme/components/**`
— it greps for exactly this. It is not wired into CI yet — that's a reasonable next
step once someone owns triaging its false positives (hairline px is expected and
not a bug; see below).

## Units

- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with the user's root font-size / browser zoom
  (WCAG 1.4.4): type (`fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`) and spacing
  (`spacing.ts`'s named scale). Letter-spacing values that were specified as sub-pixel px
  in the source don't round to clean rem numbers, so those keep a trailing `// -0.12px`
  comment for traceability.
- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should _not_ scale: border widths, focus-ring
  offsets, and (for now) the provisional button-height constants in `button.ts` that are
  still pending UI-designer sign-off against Handover.
- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts` — deliberate, so `.zimm-grid`'s media
  queries shift with zoom the same way Chakra's responsive props do) and other
  genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.

## The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy

`theme/foundation/colour.ts`'s primitive tier (`grey`, `ivory`, ...) is defined first as
plain `const`s, and the semantic/alias tier below it (`text`, `background`, `border`,
...) reads from those consts (`text.default: grey[900]`) instead of retyping the hex
value. Do the same for any new primitive/alias pair you add — two values can't disagree
if only one of them is ever typed.

`zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry for `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*`
classes) is fully derived the same way — it imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/
`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid`
from their owning files rather than retyping values. The only literals left are the 7
numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with no named-scale equivalent (`025`, `700`, `1100`,
`1200`, `1300`, `3500`, `4500`) — not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to
derive them from. `theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision-guard tests still exist as a
regression net; treat a failure there as a real drift signal, not test noise.

## One canonical styling surface per component type

Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its
`theme/components/<name>.ts` config, consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
`<Link>` variant, etc.). Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in
`globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class "mirror" is
structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing
with the real theme config over time. `button.ts` is the single source of truth for
button styling; `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*` classes — use Chakra's `<Button>`
for any button, not a class.

`.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool for genuinely static, non-interactive,
massively-reused treatments (typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout) where
there's no interactive state to lose.

## Importing an already-overridden component from a new component

If component A (e.g. `productDetailOptions`) uses component B, and B already has an
override (e.g. `swatch-group`), **import B via a relative path
(`'../swatch-group'`), not the SFCC base path
(`'@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group'`)** — even though the
base path is exactly what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) requires _inside_ an override
that's itself shadowing an SFCC module (see `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
import, which is correct for that file).

The reason the two cases differ: the resolver that redirects
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` (`ccExtensibility` in
`package.json`, read by a webpack plugin) only runs in the **real app build** — dev
server and production. `.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to
`node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it at all, so neither loads the
resolver. A base-path import of an already-overridden component will build and run
correctly in the shipped app, but silently render/test the **unstyled base SFCC
version** in Storybook and Vitest — the story or test looks like it's exercising your
override and isn't.

**Known instance of this, not yet fixed:** `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
import uses the base path. Currently dormant only because its Storybook story exercises
the `CardBaseline` named export (which takes `price` as a pre-rendered node and never
calls `DisplayPrice`), not the default `ProductTile` bridge that actually renders it —
worth fixing before anything writes a story/test against the default export.

An override component's own base-path imports (of modules it is _not_ also
overriding) are unaffected by this — `RecommendedProducts`, `Seo`, `QuantityPicker`
etc. have no local override to miss, so the base path is simply correct for them.

## Component-local tokens

When a component needs a spacing/sizing value that already has a `spacing.ts` /
`iconSizes` / etc. entry, reference it **by name** in the theme config
(`marginBottom: 'xs'`, not `marginBottom: 2` or `marginBottom: '0.5rem'`) — Chakra
resolves named scale keys against the registered `theme.space` automatically. See
`theme/components/imageGallery.ts` / `swatchGroup.ts` for the pattern: both re-express
values the base SFCC theme already had as anonymous Chakra numerics (`marginBottom: 2`)
using our named scale instead, at the same responsive steps (`['2xs', '2xs', 'xs',
'xs']` instead of `[1, 1, 2, 2]`) — same computed output, now traceable to a brand
token.

When a component needs a dimension with **no existing foundation entry** (and you don't
have a confirmed Figma value for it), leave it inherited from the base SFCC theme rather
than inventing a number — don't guess at design values. Follow the precedent already in
`header.ts`/`button.ts`: if you do have to ship a placeholder value pending designer
sign-off, say so in a comment next to it, the same way those files already do.

## The SFCC bridge pattern (shared components only)

If the component is used internally by SFCC's own base components (check with `grep -r
"from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'"
node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`), its **default export must stay a
faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour,
matching what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) already requires for correctness. Put
Zimmermann-only styling behind a **named export** that wraps the default and adds
brand-specific defaults, the same split `product-tile/index.tsx` (`CardBaseline`
name + default) and `link/index.tsx` already use. `image-gallery`, `display-price`, and
`swatch-group` are all shared internal SFCC dependencies — their default exports are
kept API-compatible; brand styling for them lives in their `theme/components/*.ts`
config instead of a named-export split, since token-driven theming doesn't require a
second export the way `CardBaseline`'s prop-narrowing did.

---

## Known gaps (not silently dropped — logged here)

- The f2r `zimm-product-detail-options` prototype spec includes a size-as-dropdown
  picker, a wishlist button, a "find in boutique" link, and description/shipping
  accordions. None of those exist as overrides yet, so `ProductDetailOptions` ships
  without them — it's colour/size swatches, quantity, and add-to-bag only.
- `swatch-group`'s `square`/`circle` variant functions (selected/disabled colour logic,
  the diagonal disabled-state gradient) are still inherited from the base SFCC theme —
  real visual design decisions with no Zimmermann Figma spec behind them yet.
- `button.ts`'s `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM` (50px/41px) disagree with the
  Handover-sourced `actionSizes.height.lg`/`.md` (52px/40px) — flagged in `button.ts`,
  pending UI-designer sign-off. `BTN_PADDING_Y` (5px) has no Handover token at all —
  a gap to fill, not a conflict to resolve.
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` is claimed by `.claude/rules/squadA.md`
  (draft, scope still settling) — flagged for awareness, not treated as a hard block.

## Follow-up work (separate initiatives)

- **Per-component CSS loading.** `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*` class registry is
  registered as one `theme.styles.global` block and ships on every page regardless of
  which classes a given page's components actually use. If component overrides start
  applying `.zimm-*` classNames directly for the non-interactive cases described above,
  only the classes a page's components actually reference should load, not the whole
  registry. Needs its own investigation, not scoped or estimated yet.
- **`globalStyles.ts` adoption is currently near zero.** Of the classes still defined
  there, none have a real consumer anywhere in the app today except one Storybook demo
  (`spacing.stories.tsx`'s `.zimm-grid` example). They're Handover-ported 1:1 and
  presumably _intended_ to be reused, just not adopted by any component yet — worth
  revisiting once component overrides actually start applying them.

# Tier 1 — Frozen Files

These files must not be modified by Claude Code without the developer explicitly naming the file
in the prompt AND confirming they have spoken to the listed owner. No exceptions.

> **Note:** this is a slim overrides project on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 — paths
> below reference `overrides/app/...` (the customisation surface) rather than the upstream
> monorepo `packages/template-retail-react-app/app/...` path.

## Design System (Owner: UI Designer — #design-system)

The whole `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` folder is Tier 1. Currently present:

```text
overrides/app/theme/index.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/index.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/fonts.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/spacing.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/motion.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/sizes.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts
```

**No font binaries in this repo.** Futura Round ships under a Monotype *"Font Software For
Desktop End User License Agreement"* which forbids "further distribute the Font Software, or
any copy thereof" and "Install the Font Software on any server or in any digital asset
management system" — so `.woff2`/`.otf` must not be committed here or served from the MRT CDN.
Licence: Zimmermann-Handover repo, `02-design/library/assets/Font Futura WOFF2/Licenses/2275/`.
Type renders from the fallback stack in `foundation/fonts.ts`. Self-hosting needs Zimmermann's
own Monotype Web Page Content entitlement (2 fonts: Regular 400, Medium 500).

Per-component theme overrides live in `overrides/app/theme/components/` and are
**Tier 2** — see [protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md). `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`
is also **Tier 2** — it composes the `.zimm-*` global class registry from the `--zimm-*`
variables defined in `foundation/zimmTokens.ts`, so it is derived styling rather than a
brand token source, but it emits CSS on every page and therefore needs a named owner.

## Commerce SDK Hooks (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text

overrides/app/hooks/use-current-customer.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-einstein.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-datacloud.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-refresh-token.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-navigation.ts
```

Note: `commerce-sdk-react` is consumed from `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/` —
it is not in this repo and cannot be modified here. The hooks above are the overrides surface.

## Runtime & Integration Config (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
config/                              ← entire directory (default.js, sites.js, sit.js, dev.js, utils.js)
overrides/app/ssr.js
overrides/app/ssr/                   ← SSR helper modules split from ssr.js in refactor 610020e:
                                         connectionPools.ts  — undici pool isolation (blast-radius mitigation)
                                         contentSecurityPolicy.ts  — CSP headers; wrong change = security hole on every page
                                         slasTokens.ts  — SLAS auth token handling; wrong change = broken auth site-wide
                                         paymentMetadata.ts  — payment method metadata SSR (checkout pages)
                                         marketingCloud.ts  — MC client-credentials token exchange
worker/main.js
package.json (root)
mobify.config.js
overrides/app/config/countries.ts
overrides/app/config/contentful.ts   ← gates preview/draft content; removing the server-side check exposes drafts on production
```

**`overrides/app/request-processor.js` — add here when populated.**
Currently the Salesforce example stub. Once Zimmermann's geo-redirect and storefront-routing logic lands here it runs on every single request — it will be one of the highest-blast-radius files in the repo. Add it to this section before that work begins.

## Build Pipeline (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

Path aliases are configured in four places that must stay in sync (see architecture.md §Path Aliases).
Breaking either file silently breaks every `app/` and `~` import across the codebase.

```text

```

```text
Didomi / consent configuration (paths TBD — add when introduced)
```

## Test & Tooling Config (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

Mirrors AGENTS.md hard rule 8 — test config drift breaks every contributor's harness.

```text
vitest.config.*
vitest.setup.ts       ← test environment setup; complements vitest.config.*
playwright.config.*
```


## Governance (Owner: Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead — #dev-team)

```text
CLAUDE.md
CODEOWNERS
```

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)

content.text: Verified this against the actual tooling rather than reasoning about it — and it turned up something that changes my earlier answer. ## What leaving it as-is actually produces **Visually:** nothing changes. Correct per Figma on every storefront. **Mouse:** hover shows a pointer cursor, click does nothing. No error, no feedback — just a dead control. **Keyboard:** it's a tab stop in the footer. Focus ring appears, Enter/Space do nothing. One wasted stop per page. **Screen reader:** announced as *"Change locale, button."* Not as the text on screen. **Voice control** (Dragon / macOS Voice Control): a user reads the screen and says *"click United States"* — no match, because the accessible name is "Change locale". The control is unreachable by voice. ## The one thing I got wrong earlier I told you no automated check would catch this. That was right about the missing handler, but I missed the `aria-label`. ```html ``` Visible text is *"United States (USD) / ENG"*. Accessible name is *"Change locale"*. The name doesn't contain the visible text — that's **WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name, Level A**. Not AA. Level A, and the project targets 2.2 AA. I ran axe-core 4.11.4 against that exact markup: ``` rule: label-content-name-mismatch → incomplete tags: wcag21a, wcag253, EN-301-549, EN-9.2.5.3 enabled by default: true ``` **Result: `incomplete`, not `violation`.** And I checked the addon's failure condition — `violations.length > 0`. So: | Gate | Outcome | |---|---| | `storybook-test` job runs on this PR? | ✅ yes — `overrides/app/components/**` and `theme/**` are in its path filter | | `test-storybook --ci` with `a11y: {test: 'error'}` | ✅ **passes** — incomplete doesn't fail | | Storybook a11y panel | ⚠️ appears under **"Inconclusive"** | | Manual audit / VPAT | ❌ callable as a **Level A** finding | So CI won't stop you. But it's now a *named, citable* conformance issue with a rule ID attached — not the soft "false affordance" judgement call I framed it as last message. That's a different kind of risk: it survives into an accessibility audit, and it's Level A, which is the tier nobody negotiates on. ## And the AC doesn't cover it Your AC declaration handles *"the label is wrong"* and *"it doesn't do anything"* — both content/scope. It doesn't cover *"the accessible name contradicts the visible name."* An a11y auditor isn't reading SFCC-55's AC. ## The precedent cost This is the part I'd weigh heaviest as lead. content.text:
Found it — and it's bigger and more actionable than the "8 provisional literals" I originally logged.

# Fix #11 — Provisional literals with no foundation token

## First, the count is wrong

It's **13, not 8**. Partly because I only looked at `footer.ts` originally, partly because *our own rework* added three (`SIZE_MODAL_SUB`, `SIZE_SUB_BODY_MAX` in item 7; `MODAL_Z_INDEX` migrated in from `index.tsx` in item 6).

And they're not all the same kind of problem:

| # | Constant | Value | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `MODAL_Z_INDEX` | `1000` | 🔴 **live bug** |
| 2 | `BP.tablet` | `48em` | 🟠 **duplicate** of an existing token |
| 3 | `SPACE_SECTION` | `3rem` (48px) | 🟡 value-duplicate, unit conflict |
| 4 | `SIZE_COL_NAV` | `8.75rem` (140px) | 🟡 value-duplicate, unit conflict |
| 5–13 | 9 others | — | ⚪ genuine gaps → Kiera |

---

## 🔴 The bug: the header renders on top of the subscribe modal

```ts
// footer.ts:19
const MODAL_Z_INDEX = 1000;
// footer.ts:138-146 — modalOverlay
position: 'fixed', inset: 0, zIndex: MODAL_Z_INDEX,
```

```ts
// header.ts:28-30 — container
position: 'sticky', top: 0, zIndex: 'sticky',
```

Chakra's `zIndices.sticky` is **1100**. The overlay is **1000**.

I checked whether a stacking context saves you — it doesn't. `footer.ts` has no `transform`, `opacity`, `filter`, `isolation`, or `zIndex` anywhere except the overlay itself; the root container is just `backgroundColor` + `width`. So the overlay competes with the header directly in the root stacking context, and **loses**.

**Result:** open the footer subscribe modal → the sticky header stays painted above the dimmed backdrop, fully visible and clickable. Focus can also land on header links behind the modal.

That's a Sev3-class defect against your ≤10 / no-Sev3 SOW bar, and it's the kind QA finds in the first five minutes.

There's a second signal that `1000` was a guess: it's *exactly* Chakra's `dropdown` token. The comment says "above all page content; below toasts/notifications" — but 1000 is below sticky, banner, overlay, modal, popover, skipLink, tooltip. Seven of the thirteen.

**Fix — no designer needed, the tokens already exist:**

```diff
- const MODAL_Z_INDEX = 1000; // above all page content; below toasts/notifications
```
```diff
  modalOverlay: {
    position: 'fixed',
    inset: 0,
-   zIndex: MODAL_Z_INDEX,
+   zIndex: 'overlay',   // 1300 — above sticky header (1100) and banner (1200)
  },
  subscribeModalPanel: {
+   zIndex: 'modal',     // 1400 — panel above its own overlay
```

Chakra's `overlay`/`modal` are semantic tokens registered in the theme. Using them is rung 2 of the hierarchy, not a literal — this actually *removes* a provisional rather than parking it.

---

## 🟠 `BP.tablet` is a straight duplicate

```ts
const BP = { tablet: '48em' }               // footer.ts:5
breakpoints = { md: '48em' }                // foundation/gridSystem.ts:11
```

Same value, typed twice. Its own comment even says `(= Chakra theme.breakpoints.md)` — so this was known and shipped anyway. Exactly the failure mode `overrideStyling.md` warns about: *"two values can't disagree if only one of them is ever typed."*

**Fix — import it. Reading a Tier 1 file isn't modifying it, and it's the same pattern `zimmTokens.ts` already uses:**

```diff
+ import { breakpoints } from '../foundation/gridSystem';

  const BP = {
-   tablet: '48em',
+   tablet: breakpoints.md,
    tabletWide: '53.75em',
    desktop: '64em',
  } as const;
```

---

## 🟡 Two value-duplicates where *footer.ts is the more correct one*

| footer.ts | zimmTokens.ts | Same value? |
|---|---|---|
| `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` | `--zimm-scale-1200: '48px'` | yes — 48px |
| `SIZE_COL_NAV = '8.75rem'` | `--zimm-scale-3500: '140px'` | yes — 140px |

Both pairs are physically identical at default root size, but they **diverge under browser zoom / user font-size** — `rem` scales, `px` doesn't. Per `overrideStyling.md`'s Units rule, spacing must be `rem` for WCAG 1.4.4. So `footer.ts` has it right and the foundation token has it wrong.

I'd **not** collapse these into the existing vars — that would be swapping correct behaviour for incorrect. The fix is to document the relationship and push the unit correction upstream:

```diff
- const SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'; // alias/space/section (48px)
+ // alias/space/section (48px). Same value as --zimm-scale-1200, which is '48px'
+ // — kept as rem here for WCAG 1.4.4 zoom scaling. Collapse to the var once
+ // zimmTokens.ts's numeric aliases move to rem (Kiera / Tier 1).
+ const SPACE_SECTION = '3rem';
```

Note this also contradicts `overrideStyling.md`, which claims the 7 numeric aliases are *"not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to derive them from."* Two of them now have exact twins. That doc line needs updating — but it's Tier 1 governance, so it's a flag, not an edit.

---

## ⚪ The 9 genuine gaps — the actual Kiera ask

| Constant | Value | Figma alias claimed | What's missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BP.tabletWide` | 860px | `alias/breakpoint/tablet-wide` | no equivalent in `gridSystem` |
| `BP.desktop` | 1024px | `alias/breakpoint/desktop` | **conflicts** — Chakra `lg`=992px, `xl`=1280px |
| `SIZE_COL_SUB` | 320px | `alias/size/footer/col-width-subscribe` | no width scale exists at all |
| `SIZE_COL_MAP` | 600px | `alias/size/footer/col-width-sitemap` | ″ |
| `SIZE_MODAL_SUB` | 480px | `alias/size/modal/footer` | ″ |
| `SIZE_SUB_BODY_MAX` | 200px | `alias/size/footer/subscribe-body-max` | ″ |
| `COLOUR_HALF_INV` | `rgba(255,255,255,.5)` | `alias/color/opacity-50-inverse` | `colour.opacity` exists but **grey-900 only** — no white twin |
| `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT` | 36px | `alias/size/field/height` | no field-height token |
| `OPACITY_DISABLED` | `0.4` | — | no numeric opacity scale |

Two of these are cheap wins worth calling out to her specifically:

- **`COLOUR_HALF_INV`** — `colour.ts:32-36` already has `opacity: {50, 40, 30, 15}` in grey-900. The ask is just *"add the inverse twin"*, mirroring existing structure rather than inventing one.
- **`BP.desktop`** — this is a **conflict, not a gap**. Figma says desktop = 1024px; Chakra's `lg` is 992px and `xl` is 1280px. Someone has to decide whether Figma's 1024 maps onto `lg`, or whether the foundation gains a real 1024 breakpoint. Every footer `@media (min-width: 64em)` is currently unreachable via Chakra responsive props, which is why the file uses raw `@media` throughout.

---

## One more thing

`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` tells you to run this before any PR touching `theme/components/**`:

```
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
```

**It doesn't exist.** `scripts/` has no such file. So the documented pre-PR check for exactly this class of problem has never run — which is a fair part of why 13 literals accumulated without anyone noticing.

---

## Proposed split

| | Action | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| **Now, this PR** | z-index → `overlay`/`modal`; `BP.tablet` → import; comment the 2 unit-conflicts | nothing |
| **Raise to Kiera** | the 9-row table above | design decision |
| **Backlog** | write `auditTokenUsage.mjs`; correct the `overrideStyling.md` "not duplicates" line | Tier 1 governance |

Want me to execute the "Now" column? The z-index one I'd do regardless — it's a real defect, and the fix uses tokens that already exist.

content.text:
Pulled the real state. Item #12 is three things, and one of them is drift **we** introduced during the last fix.

# Fix #12 — Dead placeholder plumbing in `SubscribeSection`

## 12a · The underscore convention isn't wired up — 2 live warnings

```
footer/index.tsx:218  warn  @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars  '_firstName' is defined but never used.
footer/index.tsx:218  warn  @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars  '_lastName' is defined but never used.
```

```tsx
const handleModalSubmit = (_firstName: string, _lastName: string) => {
```

The `_` prefix is the standard signal for "intentionally unused" — but it only works if `argsIgnorePattern: '^_'` is configured. I checked `.eslintrc.js`: it sets exactly five rules, none of them `no-unused-vars`. So the convention is being *used* but not *honoured*, and these two warnings are permanent noise.

Two ways out:

**Add `argsIgnorePattern` to `.eslintrc.js`** — fixes it repo-wide and makes `_` mean what everyone assumes it means. It's not Tier 1 (not in `frozenFiles.md`, not in Hard Rule 8's list), so it's *allowed*. But changing repo-wide lint config from a footer PR is a wide blast radius for a narrow problem, and it's a team convention decision. I'd raise it separately, not smuggle it in here.

**Drop the parameters.** TypeScript lets a handler take fewer params than its prop type declares, so this satisfies `onSubmit: (firstName: string, lastName: string) => void` unchanged:

```diff
- const handleModalSubmit = (_firstName: string, _lastName: string) => {
+ const handleModalSubmit = () => {
    // PLACEHOLDER until HPC-036 (Omneo integration) lands.
-   // pendingEmailRef.current, _firstName, _lastName are available here for the Omneo POST.
+   // The Omneo POST needs pendingEmailRef.current plus the modal's firstName/lastName —
+   // re-add them as parameters here (SubscribeModal already passes both) when wiring it up.
    setModalOpen(false);
    setSubmitState('unavailable');
  };
```

Zero config change, zero behaviour change, both warnings gone, and the comment still tells the next dev exactly what to do.

## 12b · `pendingEmailRef` is write-only — but keep it

```tsx
const pendingEmailRef = useRef('');          // 209
pendingEmailRef.current = email;             // 214  ← only assignment
// pendingEmailRef.current, ... available here  // 220  ← a comment, not a read
```

Never read anywhere in the file. CodeRabbit will flag it as dead state, and on the surface it looks like the same problem as 12a.

**It isn't, and I'd keep it.** The email lives inside `ZimmInputAction`'s own state. Once `submitState` flips to `'unavailable'`, that component unmounts and the value is gone. The ref is the only thing capturing it at the one moment it's available. Delete it and whoever wires HPC-036 has to rediscover *why* the email vanished before their POST.

That's the principled split between the two:

| | Data lost if removed? | Cost to re-add |
|---|---|---|
| `pendingEmailRef` | ✅ yes — input unmounts | rediscover the capture point |
| `_firstName` / `_lastName` | ❌ no — caller hands them over | one keystroke |

## 12c · A comment now contradicts the code — from our own last fix

`index.tsx:262-264`, the block header above `ContactIconRow`:

> *all hrefs are undefined and each icon renders as an inert `<span aria-hidden>` — visible in the layout but **excluded from the tab order and from assistive tech announcements**.*

Twenty-five lines below, the code we changed last session does the opposite:

```tsx
// - labelled, not aria-hidden: ZimmIcon emits role="img" + aria-label, so screen
//   reader users learn the channel exists instead of getting silence
<chakra.span key={icon} __css={styles.contactIconLink}>
  <ZimmIcon type={icon} size="md" aria-label={label} />
```

So the file now carries both the old rationale and the new one, and they disagree. Worse, the stale one is the *header* comment — the thing someone skims first. This is the exact failure mode that makes people stop trusting comments.

```diff
  // hrefs sourced from Contentful FooterConfigEntry (HPC-034). Until that integration lands,
- // all hrefs are undefined and each icon renders as an inert <span aria-hidden> — visible
- // in the layout but excluded from the tab order and from assistive tech announcements.
+ // all hrefs are undefined and each icon renders as a non-interactive but labelled <span>
+ // — visible in the layout and announced by screen readers, but absent from the tab order.
+ // See the inline note on the fallback branch below for the full a11y reasoning.
  // When a href arrives it switches to a live <a>, no other changes needed.
```

This one I'd fix regardless of what you decide on 12a/12b — it's a factual error about behaviour, introduced by us, in a Tier 2 shared component.

---

## Proposed

| | Change | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| **12a** | drop the two unused params, expand the comment | none — TS-safe, kills 2 warnings |
| **12b** | keep `pendingEmailRef`, no change | none |
| **12c** | correct the stale header comment | none |
| *separate* | raise `argsIgnorePattern: '^_'` for `.eslintrc.js` as a team convention decision | out of scope here |

That takes the PR's warning count from 5 to 3. Want me to execute 12a and 12c?

(HMAC appears in Omneo's docs only for Shopify app-proxy request signing, a separate Shopify-only concern.)

Per the updated CRM-174, the iFrame contains Communication Preferences, region/country selection, and clickable images that open the respective PLP within the iFrame (the PLP-in-iFrame behaviour is logged as an enhancement and is not in scope at launch). However, Omneo's documented embed is a **Shopify theme app extension** that authenticates the logged-in customer via the Omneo CX Shopify app proxy (a token fetched from the Shopify storefront session) — auth plumbing that does not exist in a PWA. Confirm, for the non-Shopify embed on Zimmermann's plan: (a) the Profile Portal embed URL and how the Communication Preferences and region/country selection views are scoped within it; and (b) the auth handshake outside Shopify — whether it is the customer-scoped signed-URL / HMAC approach this document assumes, or a server-minted customer-scoped Omneo token. If neither embed path is available on the plan, the fallback is a redirect to the hosted Profile Portal or a native rebuild against Omneo's API.

content.text:
They're real customer data — not scaffolding. Here's the full chain:

## The flow

**1 · Footer email field** (HPC-034) — user types their email, hits Subscribe:

```tsx
const handleEmailSubmit = (email: string) => {
  pendingEmailRef.current = email;   // captured
  setModalOpen(true);                // modal opens
};
```

**2 · Modal collects the names** (HPC-035) — two working `ZimmTextInput` fields:

```tsx
<ZimmTextInput label="First Name" name="firstName" />
<ZimmTextInput label="Last Name"  name="lastName" />
```

I verified `name` is forwarded to the real `<input>` (`zimmTextInput/index.tsx:78`), so these are genuine named form controls, not decorative.

**3 · Form submit reads them out of the DOM:**

```tsx
const handleFormSubmit = (e) => {
  e.preventDefault();
  const firstName = (form.elements.namedItem('firstName') as HTMLInputElement)?.value ?? '';
  const lastName  = (form.elements.namedItem('lastName')  as HTMLInputElement)?.value ?? '';
  onSubmit(firstName.trim(), lastName.trim());   // ← trimmed, real values
};
```

**4 · And then they're dropped:**

```tsx
const handleModalSubmit = (_firstName: string, _lastName: string) => {
  setModalOpen(false);
  setSubmitState('unavailable');   // params never touched
};
```

## What they're *for*

`.docs/prd/homepage.md` §6, both **confirmed** requirements:

> - On clicking the Continue CTA, a **modal** collects the customer's **first name and last name** (HPC-035, confirmed)
> - Sign-up data passed to **Omneo**, which then forwards to **Emarsys** (HPC-036, confirmed)

So `_firstName` + `_lastName` + `pendingEmailRef.current` are the **three fields of the HPC-036 sign-up payload**. That's the whole newsletter registration record. The plumbing is complete — capture, modal, validation, trim, handoff — right up to the final step, where there's no Omneo client to hand them to.

## Why the naming is the actual problem

The `_` prefix conventionally means *"this parameter exists only to satisfy a signature; ignore it."* That's what it's saying here. But it's false:

| | What `_` implies | What's true |
|---|---|---|
| Origin | signature filler | user-typed PII |
| Requirement | none | HPC-035, confirmed |
| Future | may never be used | required by HPC-036 |
| Value | irrelevant | the entire payload |

Someone skimming this reads two throwaway args. It's actually the most important data in the component.

Worth noting the discard itself is **correct**: nothing is logged, nothing is persisted, and `submitState` goes to `'unavailable'` rather than `'success'` — so the user is told plainly it didn't go through. No false promise, no orphaned PII. That part of the state machine is doing exactly the right thing.

The only issue is that the signature lies about what these are.

---

So the question for 12a becomes narrower than I framed it: not *"how do we silence a lint warning"* but **"how do we stop this reading as disposable?"** Dropping the params is one answer. Naming them properly and configuring `argsIgnorePattern` is the other — it keeps the payload shape visible at the signature.

Want me to lay out those two against each other before you pick?

message.content: how do we address this concern? what are our options for it?

content.text:
Four real options. The concern is *"the signature says disposable, the data is required"* — so the test for each is whether it makes the payload more visible, not just quieter.

## Option 1 — Drop the params

```tsx
const handleModalSubmit = () => {
```

Kills both warnings, no config change. But it makes the payload shape **invisible** at the call site — the opposite of what you're worried about. Cheapest, and wrong for this concern.

## Option 2 — Keep `_`, configure `argsIgnorePattern`

```js
// .eslintrc.js
'@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars': ['warn', {argsIgnorePattern: '^_'}]
```

Warnings gone, shape stays visible. But `_` *is* the "ignore me" signal — you'd be keeping the exact thing that misreads, and changing repo-wide lint config to do it. Worth doing eventually as a team convention; doesn't solve this.

## Option 3 — Assemble the actual payload ⭐

`pendingEmailRef` is already a staging area holding one third of the record. Widen it to hold all three:

```diff
+ // The HPC-036 sign-up payload: footer email (HPC-034) + modal names (HPC-035).
+ // Assembled across two steps, POSTed to Omneo → Emarsys when the integration lands.
+ type PendingSignup = { email: string; firstName: string; lastName: string };

- // Retained for the HPC-036 Omneo POST: ref avoids a re-render on capture and is
- // available synchronously in handleModalSubmit when the integration lands.
- const pendingEmailRef = useRef('');
+ // Ref, not state: nothing renders from it, so a re-render on capture would be wasted.
+ // The footer input unmounts once submitState leaves 'idle', so the email must be
+ // captured here at step 1 or it is unrecoverable at step 2.
+ const pendingSignupRef = useRef<PendingSignup>({ email: '', firstName: '', lastName: '' });

  const handleEmailSubmit = (email: string) => {
-   pendingEmailRef.current = email;
+   pendingSignupRef.current.email = email;
    setModalOpen(true);
  };

- const handleModalSubmit = (_firstName: string, _lastName: string) => {
-   // PLACEHOLDER until HPC-036 (Omneo integration) lands.
-   // pendingEmailRef.current, _firstName, _lastName are available here for the Omneo POST.
-   // On confirmed response → setSubmitState('success'). On failure → setSubmitState('error').
-   // 'unavailable' is shown until the integration is live; never show false success.
+ const handleModalSubmit = (firstName: string, lastName: string) => {
+   pendingSignupRef.current = { ...pendingSignupRef.current, firstName, lastName };
+   // PLACEHOLDER until HPC-036 (Omneo integration) lands: POST pendingSignupRef.current.
+   // On confirmed response → setSubmitState('success'). On failure → setSubmitState('error').
+   // 'unavailable' is shown until the integration is live; never show false success.
    setModalOpen(false);
    setSubmitState('unavailable');
  };
```

What this buys, in one change:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Lint warnings | 2 | **0** |
| Config change needed | — | **none** |
| Payload shape documented | scattered across 3 identifiers | one named `type` |
| Reads as disposable | yes (`_` prefix) | no |
| Write-only ref (12b) | yes, email only | still unread, but now a coherent typed record |
| Work for HPC-036 | gather 3 values, build payload | POST one object |

It also resolves 12b as a side effect — the ref stops being "a string somebody set once" and becomes the named thing the integration consumes.

## Option 4 — Extract a placeholder `submitNewsletterSignup()` util

Makes the integration seam explicit and unit-testable. But `04-omneo.md` §9 still has open items on the auth handshake, so you'd be inventing a contract — and AGENTS.md is explicit about not filling gaps with assumptions. **Right move once HPC-036 is actually being built, premature now.**

---

## Recommendation

**Option 3.** It's the only one that answers the concern you raised rather than muting it: the data stops looking optional because it's now assembled into a named payload type that cites its own requirement IDs.

It costs nothing extra — same file, no config, no new module, no invented API — and leaves HPC-036 as a genuine one-liner.

One thing it does *not* fix: the payload is still never sent. That's correct and intentional (no integration, no false success), but a reviewer may still flag the ref as unread. The `PendingSignup` type plus the HPC-036 comment is the defence, and it's a better one than the current three loose identifiers.

Want me to execute Option 3?

Before the code — precisely what happens to those two params:

## What Option 3 does to them

**1 · The underscore comes off.** `_firstName` → `firstName`. That single character is what currently reads as "ignore me," so it's the main thing being fixed.

**2 · They get consumed.** One statement stores both:

```tsx
pendingSignupRef.current = { ...pendingSignupRef.current, firstName, lastName };
```

That's what turns off the two lint warnings — they stop being "defined but never used" because they now have a destination.

**3 · Their category changes:**

| | Now | After |
|---|---|---|
| Role | satisfy a type signature | supply two thirds of a payload |
| Destination | none | `pendingSignupRef.current` |
| Traceability | a comment mentions them | typed member of `PendingSignup`, which cites HPC-035/036 |
| Lifetime | evaporate at function exit | held until footer unmount |

## What it does *not* do

They still aren't **sent**. Option 3 moves the dead end one step later — from the function boundary to the network boundary. The data is now captured, in the right shape, in the right place; it just has nowhere to go until HPC-036.

Worth naming the fair criticism: *writing to a ref nobody reads is technically enough to satisfy `no-unused-vars`*, so a cynic could call this silencing the linter with a dead store. My defence is that the store isn't arbitrary — it's the exact record the integration needs, in the same place the email already had to live for real reasons. But you should hear the objection from me rather than from CodeRabbit.

## One genuine consequence

Today the names hit the handler and vanish. After this, they sit in memory for the life of the mounted footer — i.e. the page session.

That's net-new PII retention. It's small and it's within the rules (`conventions.md`'s hard rule covers *payment* credentials — PANs, CVVs, gift card PINs — not names; and this is React memory only, never storage, never logged). But it's real, so I'll add a note telling whoever wires HPC-036 to clear the ref after a confirmed response rather than leave it hanging.

# Text Input

**Source:** Zimmermann_Design_System_2026: TextfieldV2 (https://www.figma.com/design/wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm/Zimmermann_Design_System_2026?node-id=40000265-374)
**Extracted:** 2026-07-16
**Stack:** web
**Status:** draft

---

<!-- design-layer: designer-owned. Do not edit below this line if you are a developer -->
## Design layer

### Overview

`<zimm-text-input>` is a floating-label text input. The label animates between a large placeholder position (14px, vertically centred) when the field is empty and an unfocused small label position (10px, top-pinned) when the field has a value or is focused. Two border styles via `variant`: `flush` (bottom border only, default) and `outline` (full border, light-only). Supports helper text, error state, and an optional trailing icon.

Atomic tier: atom.

### Screenshot

![Text input component screenshot](../../library/elements/text-input/assets/2026-07-16-screenshot.png)

### Tokens used

| Token | CSS variable | Value | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Border forms | `--zimm-color-border-forms` | #707070 | Default border (light) |
| Text default | `--zimm-color-text-default` | #191919 | Hover/focus border (light), input text |
| Grey white | `--zimm-color-grey-white` | white | Border and text (inverse) |
| Grey 300 | `--zimm-color-grey-300` | #969696 | Disabled border, inverse label |
| Text secondary | `--zimm-color-text-secondary` | #666 | Floating label (light) |
| Status error | `--zimm-color-status-error` | #9c0000 | Error border, error text, label (light) |
| Status error bg | `--zimm-color-status-error-bg` | #f98f8c | Error border, error text, label (inverse) |
| Font family body | `--zimm-font-family-body` | Futura Round | All text |
| Font weight regular | `--zimm-font-weight-regular` | 400 | Input text, label (unfloated) |
| Font weight medium | `--zimm-font-weight-medium` | 500 | Label (floated) |
| Font size 2xs | `--zimm-font-size-2xs` | 14px | Input text, label unfloated |
| Font size 4xs | `--zimm-font-size-4xs` | 10px | Label floated |
| Font size 3xs | `--zimm-font-size-3xs` | 12px | Helper/error text |
| Line height 2xs | `--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs` | 18px | All text |
| Scale 2xs | `--zimm-scale-2xs` | 4px | Border row vertical padding |
| Scale xs | `--zimm-scale-xs` | 8px | Gap between content and trailing icon |
| Motion duration fast | `--zimm-motion-duration-fast` | 200ms | Label float transition |
| Motion easing standard | `--zimm-motion-easing-standard` | ease | Label float transition |

- Content area height: 36px (Figma `h-[36px]` on `.content`)
- Input container height: 20px (Figma `h-[20px]` on `.inputContainer`)
- Border row min-height: 44px (36px + 2x4px padding)

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | string | "" | Floating label text. Acts as visual placeholder when empty/unfocused. |
| `placeholder` | string | "" | HTML placeholder on the native input. Shown when focused and empty (optional). |
| `value` | string | "" | Initial value. Pre-populates the input and sets the label to floated state. |
| `variant` | enum: flush, outline | "flush" | Border style. flush = bottom border only. outline = full border, light-only (no inverse). |
| `type` | string | "text" | HTML input type: text, email, tel, search, password. |
| `helper-text` | string | "" | Supplementary copy below the field. Shown alongside error-text when both are set. |
| `error-text` | string | "" | Error message. Presence triggers error state (red border + label colour). |
| `disabled` | boolean | false | Disables the native input. |
| `inverse` | boolean | false | Dark background mode (white border, white text, coral error). |
| `trailing-icon` | string | "" | Icon type string passed to `zimm-icon` size 16. Omit to hide the icon slot. |

### Floating label behaviour

| Field state | Label position | Label size | Label weight |
|---|---|---|---|
| Empty, unfocused | Vertically centred in content area | 14px | Regular 400 |
| Focused (empty or value) | Pinned to top of content area (4px from top) | 10px | Medium 500 |
| Has value, unfocused | Pinned to top | 10px | Medium 500 |

### States

| State | Border (light) | Border (inverse) | Label colour | Triggered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Default | #707070 | white | `--zimm-color-text-secondary` | no attributes |
| Hover | #191919 | white | unchanged | CSS :hover |

content.text:
Ran the check. **Verdict: feasible — and about three-quarters of it already exists in the repo, unnamed.** But the idea needs one refinement or it will over-promise on the "stories can close and pass testing" part.

---

# What already exists

| Piece | Where | State |
|---|---|---|
| Local tokens live in the right tier already | `theme/components/*.ts` is **Tier 2**; `foundation/` is Tier 1 | ✅ no Tier 1 change needed to adopt |
| The practice is already sanctioned | `overrideStyling.md`: *"if you do have to ship a placeholder value pending designer sign-off, say so in a comment next to it"* | ✅ blessed, just unstructured |
| Working "scan code → emit markdown → auto-stage" precedent | `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` + `.claude/registry/*.md` + `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` | ✅ directly reusable |
| Design-side vocabulary for the same concept | Han's `f2r/02-design/specs/components/text-input.md` | ✅ **already lists our exact gap** |
| One canonical token naming convention | PR #56's `foundation/` → `zimmTokens.ts` → `var(--zimm-*)` chain | ✅ makes a local token shaped like its replacement |
| The audit hook | `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` — referenced by `overrideStyling.md` as the pre-PR check | ❌ **does not exist** |

## Han's work is more than half the design side

His `text-input.md` spec has two distinct sections:

> **Tokens used** — Token | CSS variable | Value | Used by *(18 rows, all real `--zimm-*`)*
>
> **Structural measurements (not in named token scale):**
> - Content area height: **36px** (Figma `h-[36px]` on `.content`)
> - Input container height: 20px
> - Border row min-height: 44px

That 36px **is** our `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT = '36px'` in `zimmTextInput.ts`. The designer has already identified it as a non-token and published the confirmed value. We just have no link between his line and our line.

His `annotation-template.md` even writes the fallback rule you're proposing:

> **Duration:** [use token name if in library, **otherwise value in ms**]

⚠️ **But `f2r/` is not on develop.** His branch is 360 files / 31k insertions, unmerged. So the design half is real but not yet a shared dependency — worth knowing before you design around it.

---

# The refinement: three gaps are being conflated

I classified all 21 module-level constants in `theme/components/`. They are not one problem:

| Category | Meaning | Local token works? | Count |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A — Missing token, value confirmed** | Figma/Handover gives the value; only the token name is absent | ✅ **yes** | ~9 |
| **B — Value conflict** | A token exists and *disagrees* with the prototype | ❌ **no** | 3 |
| **C — Value invented** | Nobody has specified it | ❌ **no** | 2 |
| **D — Not a design gap at all** | A framework token already covers it | ❌ n/a | 1 |

**Category A** — `SIZE_COL_NAV` 140px, `SIZE_COL_SUB` 320px, `SIZE_COL_MAP` 600px, `SIZE_MODAL_SUB` 480px, `SIZE_SUB_BODY_MAX` 200px, `SPACE_SECTION` 48px, `COLOUR_HALF_INV`, `BP.tabletWide` 860px, `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT` 36px. These are your idea working perfectly: value is right, pixel is right, QA passes, story closes, and the eventual token swap is cosmetic.

**Category B** — `BTN_HEIGHT_LG` 50px vs Handover's `actionSizes.height.lg` **52px**; `BTN_HEIGHT_SM` 41px vs **40px**; `BP.desktop` 1024px vs Chakra `lg` 992px / `xl` 1280px. A local token here **enshrines a value we already know is contested**. The story would close on a wrong pixel and the defect surfaces later, further from its cause.

**Category C** — `OPACITY_DISABLED = 0.4`, and `BTN_PADDING_Y = 5px` (which `overrideStyling.md` admits *"has no Handover token at all"*). A guess wearing a token's clothes.

**Category D** — `MODAL_Z_INDEX = 1000`, which isn't a designer dependency: Chakra ships `overlay: 1300` / `modal: 1400`. It's just wrong (that's the header-over-modal defect from earlier).

**So the honest version of the claim** is: *local tokens unblock stories where the value is confirmed and only the token is missing.* That's ~60% of the current backlog — genuinely worth building. The other 40% still needs a designer decision, and the system's real value there is **making that visible instead of invisible**.

---

# The mechanism that makes closing cheap

Right now, replacing a local token means find-and-replace across every consuming line. That's why nobody does it.

Declare the local as the CSS custom property it will eventually become, scoped to the component root:

```ts
// theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts
root: {
  // LOCAL TOKEN — value confirmed (f2r text-input.md "Structural measurements",
  // Figma h-[36px]); awaiting alias/size/field/height in foundation/sizes.ts.
  '--zimm-size-field-height': '36px',
},
content: {
  height: 'var(--zimm-size-field-height)',   // ← never changes
}
```

When Kiera lands the real token in `foundation/`, `ZimmTokensGlobal` publishes it at `:root` — and closing the local is **deleting one line**. Every consuming line already reads the final name.

⚠️ **The risk this creates, and why the audit script becomes mandatory:** a component-scoped custom property *overrides* the inherited `:root` value. So a local left behind after the real token lands would **silently shadow it** — the component keeps the placeholder while the rest of the app moves on. That's a worse failure than today's, and it's invisible. It's only safe with a mechanical leftover check.

Also note: **no Tier 2 file declares a `--zimm-*` var today.** This would be a new pattern — worth a deliberate decision with Tim, not something to slide in.

---

# What you'd actually build

| # | Piece | Effort | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Structured marker replacing free-text comments — `@local-token` JSDoc with `figma:`, `value:`, `owner:`, `raised:`, `category:` | S | comments aren't queryable; this is the whole unlock |
| 2 | `.claude/registry/tokens.md` generated by extending `generateRegistry.mjs` | **S** | generator + pre-commit auto-stage already work |
| 3 | `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` — fails on unmarked literals **and** locals shadowing a now-real token | M | already referenced by the rules; writing it closes a documented gap |
| 4 | Join key to Han's specs via the Figma alias path (`alias/size/footer/col-width-nav`) | S | `footer.ts` is *already writing these* in comments |

Item 4 is the sleeper. Those alias paths were written speculatively — they're the foreign key that makes a code-side registry joinable to a designer-side spec with no new vocabulary invented by either side.

---

# Blockers to name up front

1. **Closing a token is a two-tier change** — add to `foundation/` (Tier 1) *and* remove the local (Tier 2). AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 requires confirming scope for exactly this. Not fatal, but every close needs a Tier 1 approver, so batch them rather than doing one at a time.
2. **Silent shadowing** (above) — the audit script is a prerequisite, not a follow-up.
3. **Category B/C can't be laundered into "closed."** If a story ships on a contested value, the AC must say so — same discipline as the locale-button declaration.
4. **`f2r/` is unmerged**, so the code↔design join is speculative until Han's branch lands.
5. **`auditTokenUsage.mjs` isn't wired to CI** and `overrideStyling.md` already flags why (false positives on hairline px). Someone has to own triage or it gets ignored like the existing prose tracking in `projectState.md` — which *does* already list the button-height conflicts, buried in a 3,000-word paragraph nobody reads.

---

# Recommendation

**Build it, scoped to Category A only, and keep B/C/D visibly separate.**

The strongest argument for it isn't the unblocking — it's that you currently have ~15 provisional values whose only marker is prose, and **no mechanical way to distinguish `const MOTION = 'var(--zimm-...)'` (fine) from `const FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT = '36px'` (a designer dependency).** They're syntactically identical. That's the actual defect in today's setup, and it's what makes these leak into `develop` unnoticed.

Two things I'd settle with Tim before writing code:

1. **Is the CSS-var shadow pattern acceptable as a new Tier 2 convention?** It's what makes closure a one-line delete, but it's novel here and carries the shadowing risk.
2. **Does a Category B value block the story, or ship with a declared deviation?** That's a delivery call, not a technical one — and it's the question that decides whether this system speeds you up or just documents the slowdown.

Want me to draft the `@local-token` marker format and a worked example against `footer.ts`'s nine, so you and Tim have something concrete to react to?

content.text:
Poorly worded row on my part — it reads as "the system already exists," which isn't what I meant. The claim was about **tier placement**, not about the system.

## What I meant

The values that would *become* local tokens are already sitting in `theme/components/*.ts`, which is **Tier 2** — developer-editable with peer review. They are not in `foundation/`, which is **Tier 1** — UI-designer-owned, frozen.

That matters for one reason: **you don't need permission to start.**

If the natural home for a local token were `foundation/`, every local token would need a Tier 1 approver to *create* and another to *delete*. Fifteen placeholders × two approvals each — the system would cost more than the problem. Because they live in Tier 2, a FED can create one in their own feature PR, and closing it is the only step that touches Tier 1.

## The concrete version

Here's `zimmTextInput.ts` today:

```ts
// Figma: content div h-[36px] — pending alias/size/field/height token from the designer.
const FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT = '36px';
```

That is already a local token in every respect except the ones that matter:

| | Today | Under the proposal |
|---|---|---|
| Named constant, not a scattered literal | ✅ | ✅ |
| Value confirmed from Figma | ✅ | ✅ |
| Names the token it's waiting for | ✅ (`alias/size/field/height`) | ✅ |
| In a tier a FED can edit | ✅ | ✅ |
| **Queryable** | ❌ prose comment | ✅ structured marker |
| **Has an owner** | ❌ "the designer" | ✅ named |
| **Has a raised date** | ❌ | ✅ |
| **Appears in a list anyone reads** | ❌ | ✅ generated registry |
| **Anything fails if it's forgotten** | ❌ | ✅ audit script |

So the practice exists — 15 instances of it across three files, plus more on `develop` in `button.ts`, `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`, `motion.ts`. What doesn't exist is any structure around it.

## Why that reframes the proposal

You and Tim aren't introducing a new pattern. You're **formalising one the team is already doing informally** — which is a much easier sell and a much lower-risk change. The work is:

1. Replace the prose comment with a parseable marker
2. Generate a list from those markers
3. Fail the build when one is stale

Not "invent local tokens." They're already here — currently invisible, with no owner and no exit condition. That's the actual gap.

content.text:
# Provisional Token Audit — full sweep

Scanned `overrides/app/theme/**`, `overrides/app/components/**`, `overrides/app/pages/**` for raw hex / px / rem / em / rgba outside comments, cross-referenced against `foundation/` and `develop`.

**20 values are genuinely pending designer work**, plus one whole Tier 1 file marked provisional. A further 6 are *not* designer dependencies — they're duplicates or bugs that can be closed today.

---

## 🟢 Category A — Missing token, value confirmed *(14)*
**Your "local token" idea works perfectly here.** Value is Figma/Handover-sourced, only the token name is absent. Story can close, QA passes on pixel.

| # | Constant | Value | File | Tier | Target token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `BP.tabletWide` | 53.75em (860px) | `footer.ts` | 2 | `alias/breakpoint/tablet-wide` |
| 2 | `SPACE_SECTION` | 3rem (48px) | `footer.ts` | 2 | `alias/space/section` |
| 3 | `SIZE_COL_NAV` | 8.75rem (140px) | `footer.ts` | 2 | `alias/size/footer/col-width-nav` |
| 4 | `SIZE_COL_SUB` | 20rem (320px) | `footer.ts` | 2 | `alias/size/footer/col-width-subscribe` |
| 5 | `SIZE_COL_MAP` | 37.5rem (600px) | `footer.ts` | 2 | `alias/size/footer/col-width-sitemap` |
| 6 | `SIZE_MODAL_SUB` | 30rem (480px) | `footer.ts` | 2 | `alias/size/modal/footer` |
| 7 | `SIZE_SUB_BODY_MAX` | 12.5rem (200px) | `footer.ts` | 2 | `alias/size/footer/subscribe-body-max` |
| 8 | `COLOUR_HALF_INV` | `rgba(255,255,255,.5)` | `footer.ts` | 2 | `alias/color/opacity-50-inverse` |
| 9 | `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT` | 36px | `zimmTextInput.ts` | 2 | `alias/size/field/height` |
| 10 | `FOCUS_RING_INVERSE` | composed | `button.ts` | 2 | `--zimm-focus-ring-inverse` |
| 11 | `LOGO_MAX_WIDTH` | 327px | `zimmLogo/index.tsx` | 4 | `alias/size/logo/max-width` |
| 12 | `LOGO_HEIGHT` | 39px | `zimmLogo/index.tsx` | 4 | `alias/size/logo/height` |
| 13 | logo `width` | `min(597px, 60vw)` | `header.ts` | 2 | — |
| 14 | logo `height` | `min(70px, 7.04vw)` | `header.ts` | 2 | — |

**#9 is already solved on the design side** — Han's `f2r/02-design/specs/components/text-input.md` lists it under *"Structural measurements (not in named token scale): Content area height: 36px (Figma h-[36px])"*. The value is confirmed and published; only the token is missing.

**#11–12** carry an explicit `// §7 raise:` marker — but there is no §7 anywhere in the repo. It referenced a PR description. That's the tracking gap in miniature.

**#13–14** are also **duplicated inline** at `header/index.tsx:436` — same two values typed twice, theme and call site.

---

## 🟠 Category B — Value conflict, not a gap *(4)*
**A local token would enshrine a value we already know is contested.** Needs a decision, not a placeholder.

| # | Constant | Prototype | Conflicts with | File |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15 | `BTN_HEIGHT_LG` | 50px | `actionSizes.height.lg` = **52px** | `button.ts` |
| 16 | `BTN_HEIGHT_SM` | 41px | `actionSizes.height.md` = **40px** | `button.ts` |
| 17 | `BP.desktop` | 64em (1024px) | Chakra `lg`=992px / `xl`=1280px | `footer.ts` |
| 18 | `NAV_LETTER_SPACING` | 0.02em | `textStyles.navigation` = **0** | `navConstants.ts` |

#18's own comment says it best: *"unresolved with the UI designer, so this prototype value is kept rather than silently switched."*

---

## 🔴 Category C — Value invented *(2)*
No Figma source, no Handover token. A guess wearing a token's clothes.

| # | Constant | Value | File | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 19 | `OPACITY_DISABLED` | 0.4 | `zimmTextInput.ts` | no opacity scale exists |
| 20 | `BTN_PADDING_Y` | 5px | `button.ts` | `overrideStyling.md`: *"has no Handover token at all"* |

---

## ⚫ Tier 1 — whole file provisional
`foundation/motion.ts` carries a file-level warning: *"PROVISIONAL: Motion design is pending formal sign-off… Do not treat as final."* Six values (`fast/default/slow` 200/300/500ms; `standard/slides/fades` easings), consumed by `zimmTextInput.ts`'s label transition and `globalStyles.ts`. **Tier 1 — closing it needs a designer + Tier 1 approver.**

---

## ✅ Not designer dependencies — closeable now *(6)*

| Item | File | Reality |
|---|---|---|
| `BP.tablet` = 48em | `footer.ts` | identical to `gridSystem.breakpoints.md` — import it |
| `MODAL_Z_INDEX` = 1000 | `footer.ts` | Chakra has `overlay`/`modal`; **and it's the live header-over-modal bug** |
| `minHeight: '36px'` | `globalStyles.ts:233` | third copy of #9 |
| `outlineOffset: '2px'` ×2 | `globalStyles.ts:78,292` | duplicates `spacing.focusRingOffsets.default` |
| logo `min(597px…)` inline | `header/index.tsx:436` | duplicates #13–14 |

Plus two **value-duplicates in different units** — `SPACE_SECTION` 3rem vs `--zimm-scale-1200` **48px**, and `SIZE_COL_NAV` 8.75rem vs `--zimm-scale-3500` **140px**. Same number, different scaling behaviour under zoom. `overrideStyling.md` currently asserts those numeric aliases are *"not duplicates"* — no longer true for those two.

---

## Excluded from the count
`contentful/**` (7 literals), `pages/home` (2), `pages/my-new-route` (1), `header/index.tsx:229` — Salesforce demo scaffolding and CMS placeholders, not Zimmermann design-system surface. Worth a separate cleanup pass, not a Kiera raise.

---

## Where they came from

| Source | Count |
|---|---|
| **New in this PR** (`footer.ts`, `zimmTextInput.ts`, `zimmLogo`) | 15 |
| **Pre-existing on `develop`** (`button.ts`, `header.ts`, `navConstants.ts`, `globalStyles.ts`, `motion.ts`) | 11 |

So roughly half predate SFCC-55. This isn't a footer problem — it's accumulating at ~15 per feature branch with nothing catching it.

**One Tier 1 note:** `foundation/sizes.ts` is modified on this branch, but the diff is a single trailing newline. Harmless, though it will trip `tier1-guard` on the PR and pull in a code-owner review. Worth reverting before you raise it.

---

Want me to write this to `.docs/` (or Desktop) as the raise document for Kiera, split by category with the Figma alias paths as the join key? That's the artifact the tracking system would generate automatically once built.

content.text:
# Provisional Token Audit — full inventory

Method: bundled `foundation/index.ts` via esbuild to get **real** token values (not regex-guessed), normalised every value to a common unit (px-equivalent, canonical rgba), then cross-referenced all 29 raw design literals against 76 distinct official token values, with semantic-scale compatibility checking so a width matching a breakpoint doesn't count as a hit.

**29 raw design values across 10 files.** They are not one problem.

---

## A · Already have an official token — delete the provisional

| # | Provisional | Official token | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `BP.tablet = '48em'` `footer.ts:5` | **`breakpoints.md = '48em'`** | 🟢 **exact, same unit** |
| 2 | `MARKER_SIZE = '16px'` `hotspotMarker.tsx:25` | **`iconSizes.md = '16px'`** | 🟢 exact + semantically identical (it's an icon) |
| 3 | `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` `footer.ts:12` | `--zimm-scale-1200 = '48px'` | 🟡 same value, **unit differs** |
| 4 | `SIZE_COL_NAV = '8.75rem'` `footer.ts:13` | `--zimm-scale-3500 = '140px'` | 🟡 same value, **unit differs** |
| 5 | `w = '180px'` `hotspotPopup.tsx:23` | `--zimm-scale-4500 = '180px'` | 🔴 numeric only — spacing scale used for a width |

**#1 and #2 are free deletions.** `BP.tablet` is a byte-for-byte retype of `breakpoints.md`, and its own comment already admits it (`= Chakra theme.breakpoints.md`).

**#3 and #4 need care** — the values match but `footer.ts` uses `rem` where the foundation token uses `px`. Under browser zoom these diverge, and per `overrideStyling.md`'s Units rule **`footer.ts` is the correct one**. Don't collapse these downward; raise the foundation token to `rem` instead.

---

## B · Not gaps — *conflicts*. A token exists and disagrees

These are the ones a local-token system would silently enshrine as correct. They need a decision, not a placeholder.

| Provisional | Official token | Delta |
|---|---|---|
| `BTN_HEIGHT_LG = 50px` | `actionSizes.height.lg = 52px` | −2px |
| `BTN_HEIGHT_SM = 41px` | `actionSizes.height.md = 40px` | +1px |
| `NAV_LETTER_SPACING = 0.02em` | `textStyles.navigation` → `letterSpacings.sm = '0'` | +0.24px |
| `BP.desktop = 64em` (1024px) | `breakpoints.lg = 62em` (992px) / `xl = 80em` (1280px) | no clean mapping |

`navConstants.ts` states its own conflict outright:

> *"The design system's `.zimm-text-nav` / `textStyles.navigation` both specify 0px — unresolved with the UI designer, so this prototype value is kept rather than silently switched."*

It also uses `em`, which `overrideStyling.md` restricts to breakpoints only — so it breaks the unit rule on top of the value conflict.

---

## C · Duplicates among the provisionals themselves

**One true duplicate:**

```tsx
// productHero.tsx:40  — the loaded branch
boxSize={{ base: '240px', md: '320px' }}
// productHero.tsx:46  — the skeleton branch
boxSize={{ base: '240px', md: '320px' }}
```

Identical pair, one file, two branches that must stay in sync and nothing keeping them there. Should be one constant regardless of any token work.

**Two cross-domain coincidences — *not* duplicates:** `240px` appears 4× (heroBanner height, productHero boxSize ×2, header minW) and `320px` 3× (footer column width, productHero boxSize ×2). Different domains that happen to share a number. Candidates for a future width scale; **not** evidence of a missing shared token today.

---

## D · Genuine gaps — the real designer backlog

**Value confirmed from Figma, only the token missing** — these are the ones your local-token idea handles cleanly:

| Provisional | Value | Figma alias already written in-code |
|---|---|---|
| `SIZE_COL_SUB` | 320px | `alias/size/footer/col-width-subscribe` |
| `SIZE_COL_MAP` | 600px | `alias/size/footer/col-width-sitemap` |
| `SIZE_MODAL_SUB` | 480px | `alias/size/modal/footer` |
| `SIZE_SUB_BODY_MAX` | 200px | `alias/size/footer/subscribe-body-max` |
| `BP.tabletWide` | 860px | `alias/breakpoint/tablet-wide` |
| `COLOUR_HALF_INV` | `rgba(255,255,255,.5)` | `alias/color/opacity-50-inverse` |
| `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT` | 36px | `alias/size/field/height` |

Two of these have existing structure to extend rather than invent:
- **`COLOUR_HALF_INV`** — `colors.opacity{15,30,40,50}` exists but is grey-900-based only. The ask is the white twin, not a new concept.
- **`OPACITY_DISABLED = 0.4`** — the number already lives inside `colors.opacity[40]` as the alpha channel. Missing form is a *scalar*, not a value.

**No Figma alias, no confirmed value** — these are guesses and shouldn't become local tokens: `BTN_PADDING_Y` (5px), `LOGO_MAX_WIDTH` (327px), `LOGO_HEIGHT` (39px), plus the Contentful scaffolding literals (`400px`, `120px`, `240px`).

**Not a design gap at all:** `MODAL_Z_INDEX = 1000` — Chakra already ships `overlay: 1300` / `modal: 1400`. This is the header-over-modal defect, not a token request.

---

## Scope split — what's yours vs inherited

| | Count | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **New in PR #55** | ~15 | all `footer.ts` constants, `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT`, `OPACITY_DISABLED`, `LOGO_*` |
| **Pre-existing on develop** | ~14 | `BTN_HEIGHT_*`, `BTN_PADDING_Y`, `NAV_LETTER_SPACING`, all Contentful/header literals |

Roughly half this backlog predates your PR — worth knowing before the whole inventory gets attached to SFCC-55.

---

## What this tells you about the local-token proposal

The audit changes the sizing from my earlier estimate:

| Bucket | Count | Local token appropriate? |
|---|---|---|
| Already tokenised (A) | 5 | ❌ **just delete** — 2 are free today |
| Conflicts (B) | 4 | ❌ needs a decision |
| Confirmed value, missing token (D-upper) | 7 | ✅ **exactly the target** |
| Guessed value (D-lower) | ~8 | ❌ guess wearing a token's clothes |
| Not a design gap | 1 | ❌ framework token exists |
| Intra-file duplicate | 1 pair | ❌ plain DRY fix |

**So ~7 of 29 are true local-token candidates** — about a quarter, not the "~60%" I estimated before running this. The system is still worth building, but its main value is clearer now: **the audit itself is the product.** Two-thirds of what looks like "waiting on the designer" turns out to be duplicates, conflicts, guesses, or already-solved — and none of that was visible while the only marker was a prose comment.

---

Want me to (a) write this to `/Desktop/provisional-token-audit.md` in the same format as the PR52/55 findings doc, (b) execute the two free deletions (`BP.tablet` → `breakpoints.md`, `MARKER_SIZE` → `iconSizes.md`), or (c) draft the Kiera-facing ask from bucket D-upper?
