content.content: 1 # FED Lead Playbook 2 3 **Derived from:** the two "Contentful v PWA Kit Components and User Story Alignment" sessions 4 **Owner:** Marcel Navarro · **Started:** August 2026 5 **Companions:** [fedBuild-manual.md](./fedBuild-manual.md) (the developer-facing half — how to build) · [componentStories-BA-guide.md](./componentStories-BA-guide.md) (the BA-facing version) · [pr52-pr55-findings.md](./pr52-pr55-findings.md) (worked example of Play 5 applied to two live PRs) · `.docs/temp/{componentStoryReview,meeting2Prep,meeting2Analysis}.md` (the underlying analysis) 6 **Authority on styling:** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` in-repo — if this playbook and that file disagree, it wins. 7 8 Purpose: the two sessions put sixteen things on your desk without saying when or how any of them get done. This turns that into a rhythm, a set of repeatable plays, and the specific mechanics for each. 9 10 --- 11 12 ## 1. The mandate, consolidated 13 14 What the sessions actually assigned you: 15 16 | # | Responsibility | From | 17 |---|---|---| 18 | 1 | Own dependency discovery during refinement | M1 — the strongest expectation raised | 19 | 2 | Protect Salesforce / PWA Kit reuse; challenge "let's build this" | M1 | 20 | 3 | Own component governance — prevent duplicate Buttons, Links, utilities | M1 | 21 | 4 | Strengthen FE PR review criteria | M1 | 22 | 5 | Improve estimation accuracy — surface hidden work before planning | M1 (Jasmijn, repeatedly) | 23 | 6 | Embed accessibility in component stories, not as follow-up | M1 + M2 | 24 | 7 | Follow up design-system gaps with Kiera / design owners | M1 | 25 | 8 | Define the atoms governance model + a refinement checklist | M1 (strategic) | 26 | 9 | Component completeness — all variants designed upfront | M2 | 27 | 10 | Define a standard renderer contract between Contentful models and React components | M2 | 28 | 11 | Ensure components gracefully handle optional fields | M2 | 29 | 12 | Document accessibility expectations component-by-component | M2 | 30 | 13 | Own page-level validation — visual, responsive, integration, design parity | M2 | 31 | 14 | Push back where requirements are unclear before sizing | M2 | 32 | 15 | Support incremental assembly (build → drop in → verify) | M2 | 33 | 16 | Separate component-build effort from page-composition effort in estimates | M2 | 34 35 **The through-line, in Tim's words:** *"FED leadership needs to identify what already exists before the team commits to building something new."* 36 37 **The one to resist as stated.** #1 makes you a serial gate across both squads' refinement sessions. It won't scale and it will slip. Play 1 handles this by moving the lookup to where the story is drafted and keeping only the judgement calls for yourself. 38 39 ### The quality bar this all serves 40 41 Everything below is calibrated to one number. **The SOW allows no more than 10 defects, and no Sev3.** 42 43 Zimmermann is a luxury brand and is exceptionally particular about UI. That combination means the usual 44 trade — ship it, fix it in QA — is not available here. A visual defect that would be a shrug on another 45 project consumes part of a very small budget. 46 47 Three consequences to plan around rather than discover: 48 49 - **Vigilance is the job, not an overhead on the job.** Be as vigilant as possible, on every PR. 50 - **Budget real time for checking.** A proper pass over a UI PR — preview environment, Figma, tokens, 51 states, responsive — is **an hour or more**. Treat that as the cost of the review, not as slippage. 52 - **Do as much as we can and flag the rest.** Where design is missing, ambiguous or contradictory, the 53 answer is to raise it, not to invent a value. An invented value becomes a defect *and* a design-system 54 divergence. 55 56 --- 57 58 ## 2. Your operating rhythm 59 60 Sixteen responsibilities, four moments. Everything below hangs off this. 61 62 | When | Plays | Time | 63 |---|---|---| 64 | **Story drafting** (BA-initiated, async) | 1 — reuse & dependency check | Async, minutes per story | 65 | **Refinement** (per story) | 1, 3, 9, 14 — dependencies, variants, push-back | In the session | 66 | **Pre-sprint-planning** (weekly) | 2 — estimation validation | ~30 min | 67 | **PR review** (continuous) | 5 — the human-only checks | Per PR | 68 | **Design review** (weekly, with Kiera) | 6 — design-system gaps | Standing slot | 69 70 Two standing items that don't fit a cadence: the **renderer contract** (Play 4, once per Contentful component) and **page-level validation** (Play 7, once per page assembly). 71 72 --- 73 74 ## Play 1 — The reuse & dependency check 75 76 *Covers responsibilities 1, 2, 3, 8* 77 78 ### The ladder (agreed in M1) 79 80 ``` 81 Salesforce / PWA Kit capability 82 ↓ (nothing fits) 83 Existing shared component in overrides/ 84 ↓ (nothing fits) 85 Existing pattern 86 ↓ (nothing fits) 87 New implementation ← justify this out loud 88 ``` 89 90 ### Where to actually look 91 92 | Question | Source | 93 |---|---| 94 | Does a Base, Override or Custom component already exist? | `.claude/registry/components.md` — columns: **Origin · Path · Props · Tier · Squad · Consumers**. Regenerated automatically by the pre-commit hook on any `overrides/app/**` change | 95 | Same for hooks / utils / pages / routes | `.claude/registry/{hooks,utils,pages,routes}.md` | 96 | What's in the base package? | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` and `/app/hooks/` | 97 | Is it already claimed by a squad? | Registry `Squad` column · `.claude/rules/squadA.md` | 98 | What tier am I about to touch? | Registry `Tier` column, or `/audit-tier` | 99 100 The `Origin` column is doing most of the work: **`Base` means it exists but isn't scaffolded into `overrides/` yet** — which is a cost, not a free win (see below). 101 102 ### Worked examples, already verified 103 104 | Ask | What already exists | 105 |---|---| 106 | Size selector | Base `swatch-group/` — index, swatch, plus an existing test | 107 | Add to bag | Base `product-view/index.jsx` — already does `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the button and label, the add-to-cart modal, bundle handling, and an `updateCart` variant | 108 | Max purchase quantity | Base `quantity-picker/` | 109 | Variant resolution | `use-controlled-variations`, `use-derived-product`, `use-add-to-cart-modal` | 110 111 Worth knowing before SFCC-650 is sized: its description says *"Cart API integration is in scope"*, but the base already performs the cart call. That story should read as **extend `product-view`**, not build cart integration. 112 113 ### Override-first — why the second rung is where the value is 114 115 The ladder says "reuse before build". The stronger version, and the one to hold the line on: 116 **default to overriding the base component, not writing a new one.** 117 118 The reason is not tidiness — it's that an override **inherits the wiring for free**. Override 119 `product-view` and you get `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the add-to-cart modal, bundle 120 handling and `updateCart` already connected. Build a bespoke equivalent and every one of those has to be 121 re-derived, re-tested and re-reviewed, and none of it is visible in the story points. 122 123 There's a second-order effect worth naming in refinement. PWA Kit's resolver rewires imports 124 transparently, so **overriding a component SFCC's own base components already import means the whole base 125 template inherits your version** — no call sites touched. A bespoke component in a new folder reaches only 126 the pages someone remembers to wire it into. Same visual result on the page you're building; very 127 different coverage across the site. 128 129 ⚠️ **One documented exception: `shared/ui/`.** That directory is consumed through a barrel 130 (`shared/ui/index.jsx`), and the barrel's own re-exports are **relative** (`export {Button} from 131 './Button'`). The `ccExtensibility` resolver only rewrites `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` 132 specifiers, so a relative import inside `node_modules` is never redirected. **208 base files import 133 that barrel; none import `shared/ui/Button` directly — so overriding `shared/ui//` intercepts 134 nothing.** It is a place to put raw Zimmermann primitives for *our own* code to import explicitly, not 135 an interception point. See "Two component families" below. 136 137 So the question in review isn't only "did you reuse?" but **"is this an override, and if not, why not?"** 138 139 **In flight, and relevant:** Han is extending the registry generator to account for the `shared/` folder 140 as well, and is building the override-first approach into the F2R workflow — so the default lands in the 141 tooling rather than depending on everyone remembering it. Worth tracking; it removes work from Play 1. 142 143 ### The hidden cost to name every time 144 145 If `Origin = Base`, the component isn't in `overrides/` yet, and AGENTS.md's **Copy-first rule** applies before any functional work: 146 147 1. Copy base file → mirrored path in `overrides/` 148 2. Convert to TypeScript, fix imports 149 3. `npx tsc --noEmit` 150 4. Add a temporary `console.log` marker 151 5. **Stop — a human confirms the override renders instead of the base** 152 6. Then build; remove markers 153 154 It's serialised and human-gated. **The first story against a given base component pays it; later ones don't.** This is the single most common reason a story looks small and isn't — exactly Jasmijn's concern. Either split it into an enabler story or size the first story accordingly. 155 156 ### Making this scale (the fix for #1) 157 158 Add one line to the BA prompt template in Confluence 274137093: 159 160 > *"Check `.claude/registry/components.md` — does a Base, Override or Custom component already cover this? Report Origin, Tier, Squad and Consumer count."* 161 162 That makes four of the six refinement questions self-service. You keep the two that need judgement: 163 164 - **Is extending the base the right call, or is a Zimmermann-specific build justified?** 165 - **Is the design-system prerequisite real, or can we proceed?** 166 167 ### Preventing duplicate atoms (#3, #8) 168 169 The atoms question — *"when does an atom deserve its own story?"* — is largely already answered by existing convention rather than needing a new model: 170 171 - A story is required for anything **exported from its folder** under `overrides/app/components/` or `/pages/`. 172 - **Not** required for internal sub-components that only render inside one parent — cover their variants via the parent's stories. 173 - The Storybook categorisation (`Foundation / Elements / Layout / Commerce / Forms / Pages / Contentful`) gives you the vocabulary: `Elements/` *is* the atoms layer. 174 175 Applied to 04.7's `↳ Sub-component` rows: Pause/Play, Footer Item, Footer Textfield, Icons don't each need a story unless independently reusable. Without that rule the Footer alone generates four. 176 177 --- 178 179 ## Play 2 — Estimation validation 180 181 *Covers responsibilities 5, 16* 182 183 Run this before sprint planning, not in it. 184 185 ### The re-baseline to communicate once 186 187 M2 concluded pages become assemblies. The honest consequence: 188 189 - **Homepage / page estimates should go down.** Composition genuinely is cheaper. 190 - **Component estimates should go up by more than the pages save.** 191 192 Because a component story now carries: all variants upfront + accessibility AC + a mandatory Storybook story + a test where logic-heavy + Copy-first scaffolding on first touch. 193 194 If only the first half of that lands, the programme will look like it got faster and won't have. Say this out loud in planning — once, clearly. 195 196 ### Split the two kinds of effort (#16) 197 198 | Component build | Page composition | 199 |---|---| 200 | Real frontend development | Assembly and configuration | 201 | Variants, states, accessibility | Integration testing | 202 | Storybook + tests | Visual validation | 203 | Sized as build work | Sized as validation work | 204 205 Don't let them be estimated with the same scale. 206 207 ### Challenge list 208 209 For each story before it's sized: 210 211 - [ ] `Origin = Base`? → Copy-first cost is in, or split out 212 - [ ] All variants captured, or only the ones on the first page? 213 - [ ] Accessibility written as AC, or assumed? 214 - [ ] Storybook story accounted for? 215 - [ ] Designs confirmed, or still in progress? (04.7 status column) 216 - [ ] Does it depend on anything in Play 8's open list? 217 - [ ] Composition variant hiding as a configuration variant? (Play 3) 218 219 --- 220 221 ## Play 3 — Component completeness & variant review 222 223 *Covers responsibilities 9, 11* 224 225 M2's rule: a component isn't complete until it covers all supported variants, and the page just configures it. One Editorial Card, not a Homepage one and a PLP one. 226 227 ### The distinction to hold 228 229 | Kind | Examples | How it's built | 230 |---|---|---| 231 | **Configuration variant** | text alignment, CTA on/off, title on/off, body copy present/absent | Props on one component ✅ Tim's rule applies directly | 232 | **Composition variant** | 1 vs 2 column, 3-up vs 4-up grids | A **container/slot component** — structurally a second component | 233 234 This matters because a composition variant priced as a prop will be under-estimated. On the Studio Experiences path especially, a repeating structure can't be a prop — the composition primitive is `children`. So "one Editorial Card with all variants" often resolves to *two* components: the card, plus a container holding one or two. 235 236 Better outcome — the container is reusable anywhere — but it changes the count. Catch it at refinement. 237 238 ### Why "upfront" is a hard requirement here, not a preference 239 240 The Contentful sync is **additive-only — it cannot delete a field from a published content type**. Getting the variant model wrong isn't rework, it's semi-permanent. This is the strongest argument you have for holding the line on variant completeness, and it supports Tim's position rather than fighting it. 241 242 ### Optional-field handling (#11) 243 244 M2: don't assume CMS fields are populated. Every Contentful-backed component needs AC for the absent case — no empty space, no placeholder, no layout break. Make it a standing question in refinement rather than a per-story discovery. 245 246 --- 247 248 ## Play 4 — The renderer contract 249 250 *Covers responsibility 10* 251 252 M2 asked for "a standard renderer contract between Contentful models and React components." This is the artifact that makes the Contentful story and the PWA Kit story independently workable — without it they drift, and additive-only sync makes drift expensive. 253 254 **The requirement it satisfies:** `02-contentful.md` §2 — *"TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time."* 255 256 **The artifact:** one table, identical in both stories of every Contentful pair. 257 258 | Field ID | Display name | Type / control | Required | Localised | Notes | 259 |---|---|---|---|---|---| 260 | `image` | Image | Media | Yes | No | | 261 | `imageAlt` | Image Alt Text | shortText | No | Yes | behaviour when empty — see Play 6 | 262 | `bodyCopy` | Body Copy | longText | No | Yes | | 263 | `ctaLabel` | CTA Label | shortText | No | Yes | CTA renders only if label **and** URL set | 264 | `ctaUrl` | CTA URL | shortText | No | No | internal → same tab; external → new tab + `rel="noopener noreferrer"` | 265 266 **Field IDs, not display names.** "Body copy" in prose is where drift starts. 267 268 **You own the template; the BA fills it; you sign off the field IDs before the Contentful story is built.** That signature is the cheapest possible insurance against an undeletable wrong field. 269 270 **Note for the ordering question:** for Studio Experiences components the contract is generated from the React props rather than authored first — so the review point moves to the component's prop type. Which pattern a given component uses is still unresolved (Play 8). 271 272 --- 273 274 ## Play 5 — PR review 275 276 *Covers responsibility 4* 277 278 The useful move here is knowing what the tooling already catches, so your attention goes where it's actually needed. 279 280 ### Already mechanical — don't spend review time on it 281 282 | Check | Enforced by | 283 |---|---| 284 | Missing `alt` on `` | ast-grep `img-missing-alt` | 285 | `IconButton` without `aria-label` | ast-grep `icon-button-missing-aria-label` | 286 | `onClick` on non-interactive element without `role` | ast-grep `clickable-non-interactive-element` | 287 | Payment credentials logged | semgrep `payment-credential-logged` | 288 | Unsanitised `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` | semgrep `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` | 289 | Type errors, lint, conventional commits | `tsc --noEmit`, lint, commit-msg hook | 290 | Registry freshness | pre-commit hook | 291 292 ### Not enforced — this is your list 293 294 | Gap | Why it matters | 295 |---|---| 296 | **Hardcoded hex / px values** in Chakra props and `.scss` | `css.md` states plainly it isn't mechanically enforced. Highest-frequency design-system violation | 297 | **Component complexity / size** | No `complexity` or `max-lines-per-function` in `.eslintrc.js` — confirmed | 298 | **Chakra `` without alt** | The ast-grep rule matches lowercase `` only. Every Contentful component here uses `` — so the guard doesn't cover the component family under discussion | 299 | **Duplication / reuse** | No tool detects "this is a second Button". This is the core of responsibility #3 and it is entirely human | 300 | **Salesforce alignment** | Whether base capability was leveraged — judgement only | 301 302 Two of these are cheap to close, and the repo's own rules files already recommend the fix: an ast-grep rule for hardcoded design values, and the two ESLint core rules. **Both touch Tier 1 files** — raise as a decision, don't land quietly. See §Guardrails. 303 304 ### Gate zero — does it actually build? 305 306 **Check this before spending review attention on anything else.** A PR has already been opened on this 307 project with a failing typecheck — missing type declarations that the branch itself had previously 308 supplied and lost in a merge. Reviewing the design of code that doesn't compile wastes the expensive part 309 of your day. 310 311 ```bash 312 npx tsc --noEmit # must be clean 313 npm run lint # separate real errors from auto-fixable prettier noise 314 npx vitest run 315 ``` 316 317 Two things worth knowing about this failure mode, because it will recur: 318 319 - **A merge can silently delete a declaration.** When a branch merges `develop` and both sides touched the 320 same ambient-types file, the merge can resolve to develop's version and drop what the branch added. It 321 typechecks on neither side's intent and nobody notices until CI or a local build. 322 - **It isn't always the author's mistake.** In that instance a second error came from following a repo 323 rules file that named a package which doesn't exist on the installed Storybook major. Check whether the 324 rule or the code is wrong before raising it as a code finding. 325 326 Make "green locally before opening" the expectation, and say so once to the whole team rather than 327 per-PR. It isn't about blame — it's that the review budget is an hour per PR and this spends it on nothing. 328 329 ### Review across three surfaces, not one 330 331 Reading the diff is the smallest part. For any UI PR, look at all three: 332 333 | Surface | What only it will tell you | 334 |---|---| 335 | **The diff** | Tokens vs literals, reuse vs reimplementation, abstractions respected | 336 | **The preview environment** | What it actually renders — states, responsive behaviour, whether hover/focus work at all | 337 | **Figma** | Whether the rendered output matches the design, and which gaps are design gaps rather than build gaps | 338 339 Every `feature/*` and `fix/*` branch now auto-deploys to its own MRT environment and posts the URL on the 340 PR. There is no longer a reason to review a UI change from the diff alone — **open the environment and put 341 it beside Figma.** If no URL comment appeared, the branch had no open PR when it was pushed; a further 342 push once the PR exists will post it. 343 344 Evaluate the rendered output against Figma deliberately, at the breakpoints the design defines. Anything 345 that doesn't line up is either a build finding or a design gap — and separating those two is your call, 346 not the developer's. 347 348 ### Tokens and CSS — the highest-yield thing you check 349 350 This is where divergence starts, it is not mechanically enforced, and both PRs currently in flight have 351 drifted in different directions. Be deliberately vigilant here. 352 353 `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` is the authority. The hierarchy, in order: 354 355 1. `textStyle` for anything textual — **never** a raw `fontSize` 356 2. Semantic token strings — `color="text.default"`, `padding="m"` 357 3. The component's own `theme/components/.ts` for variant / size / state 358 4. `sx` only for a genuine prop-system gap 359 5. Scoped `.scss` only when `sx` truly can't express it 360 361 What to actively look for: 362 363 - **The correct token, not just a token.** A value that resolves to the right pixels via the wrong token 364 passes a casual glance and breaks the moment the design system moves. Two `sx` blocks recently 365 hand-rebuilt what `textStyle="heading3"` and `textStyle="body2"` already provide, property for property. 366 - **`var(--zimm-*)` in the right layer.** It is the convention *inside* `theme/components/*.ts`. In 367 component JSX it is not — that's rungs 1 and 2. Seeing `var()` in a `.tsx` is a signal to look closer. 368 - **`--zimm-scale-NNN` numeric aliases in JSX.** They exist only for the `.zimm-*` global classes. The 369 named scale (`m`, `l`, `xl`) is the Chakra-facing surface. 370 - **A theme recipe that nothing consumes.** A `theme/components/.ts` file that is written and 371 registered but never read via `useStyleConfig` looks like compliance and is dead code. 372 - **A second copy of the token registry.** Any new utility that re-types token names as strings 373 reintroduces exactly the drift the derived-token work removed. 374 - **Interaction states in JavaScript.** `useState` for hover / press / focus instead of 375 `_hover` / `_active` / `_focusVisible` means those states are dead until hydration, sticky on touch, 376 and unreachable by the theme. 377 378 ### Tests and stories — the minimum, while UI is the focus 379 380 The build focus is UI, and that's fine — but don't let coverage reach zero on the way through: 381 382 - **Unit tests where they earn their place** — data mapping, transforms, non-obvious logic. Not for 383 re-exports or passthroughs. 384 - **At minimum, scaffold the Storybook story.** Every component exported from its folder needs one. A 385 scaffolded story with a `Default` export and the meaningful states is the floor, even if the `play` 386 function comes later. It's also the surface your own review depends on. 387 388 ### Review questions, in order 389 390 0. **Does it build?** `tsc`, lint, tests — gate zero above 391 1. Was an existing component / hook / utility reused, or is this a second implementation? 392 2. **Is it an override, or a bespoke build — and if bespoke, why?** 393 3. Are all design values tokens — and the *correct* tokens, in the correct layer? 394 4. Does it respect existing abstractions, or work around them? 395 5. Was base Salesforce capability leveraged where it exists? 396 6. Accessibility: keyboard, focus order, states — beyond what ast-grep catches 397 7. Storybook story present? Test where logic-heavy? 398 8. **Does the preview environment match Figma at the defined breakpoints?** 399 400 --- 401 402 ## Play 6 — Accessibility 403 404 *Covers responsibilities 6, 12* 405 406 M1 and M2 both landed on accessibility living **inside** component stories, as AC, not as a follow-up task. 407 408 ### The per-component AC set (#12) 409 410 Standing list to apply to every component story: 411 412 - Keyboard operability and reachability 413 - Focus order and visible focus states 414 - Interaction states (hover, active, disabled, focused) 415 - Screen-reader behaviour for images and icon-only controls 416 - Behaviour when optional content is absent 417 418 **Baseline is WCAG 2.2 AA**, falling back to 2.1 only where 2.2 is technically infeasible *and* the reason is documented. Worth correcting on SFCC-648, which currently commits to 2.1 AA — and setting 2.2 as the story-template default so it doesn't propagate. 419 420 ### The one open item 421 422 M2 landed on: *if alt text exists render it; if not, don't render the attribute.* There's a real technical problem with that — omitting the attribute makes assistive tech treat the image as meaningful-but-undescribed, and it commonly reads out the filename; `alt=""` removes it from the accessibility tree entirely. The existing draft AC on the render story already says the latter. 423 424 **Your action:** get it confirmed with Tim before it propagates into every image-bearing component. Frame it as the content-model question it really is — *how do we distinguish "intentionally decorative" from "someone forgot"?* — which is a Contentful field decision (required alt, or an explicit decorative toggle), not a renderer decision. The BA guide flags it as pending rather than settled. 425 426 --- 427 428 ## Play 7 — Page-level validation 429 430 *Covers responsibilities 13, 15* 431 432 M2 kept page validation with FED even though pages stop being development units: spacing, layout, design fidelity, responsive behaviour, assembled UX. 433 434 ### Where each part lands today 435 436 | Ask | Home | 437 |---|---| 438 | Assembled UX / integration | ⚠️ Playwright E2E — the `@area` **vocabulary** is `homepage, checkout, search, account, pdp, plp, integrations`, but only `@homepage` and `@checkout` are applied to any spec today. Five of the seven areas have no coverage at all | 439 | Performance | ✅ `lighthouserc.js` | 440 | Responsive behaviour | ⚠️ Partial — Playwright runs desktop + mobile Chrome, but asserts behaviour, not appearance | 441 | **Spacing / design fidelity / design parity** | ❌ **No automated home.** `testing.md` explicitly excludes visual snapshots from the Vitest budget | 442 443 **Name this rather than absorbing it.** Design-parity validation is currently manual visual QA. Either it's accepted as manual and the time is resourced, or it's a visual-regression tooling decision (Chromatic / Loki / Percy) — a new dependency and budget, which needs approval before anything is installed. An unresourced ask that quietly becomes yours is the failure mode here. 444 445 Operational note: only `e2e_homepage` is currently mapped in the change-scoping config. Each new area's first spec needs its own allow-list group, or it silently falls back to the full suite. 446 447 ### Incremental assembly (#15) 448 449 Tim's build → drop-in → verify loop is well supported and costs nothing to adopt: 450 451 | Step | Support | 452 |---|---| 453 | Build in isolation | Storybook — mandatory story; `Contentful/` category explicitly allows mock CMS data | 454 | Make available to authors | `npm run generate:contentful` regenerates definitions; pre-commit keeps it in sync | 455 | Author drops it on a page | Studio Experiences — appears once annotated | 456 | Verify | `pages/experience/` and `pages/contentfulPreview/` routes exist | 457 458 **Caveat worth stating:** this loop only works for Studio Experiences components. Entry-driven ones are wired in code and aren't drag-and-droppable. Another reason the pattern question in Play 8 matters. 459 460 --- 461 462 ## Play 8 — Pushing back before sizing 463 464 *Covers responsibility 14* 465 466 These were explicitly left unresolved. Your job is to keep them from being sized on assumption. 467 468 | Open item | Position to hold | 469 |---|---| 470 | **Alt text** | Confirm with Tim before it lands in AC — Play 6 | 471 | **External links** | Already answered in draft AC (internal → same tab; external → new tab + `rel="noopener noreferrer"`). Adopt it, bake it into the Link component when built. Doesn't need another meeting | 472 | **Recommendations** | Not actually unknown — `SFCC-7` already holds eight decomposed, requirement-traced tickets (112, 118, 119, 313, 314, 642, 647, plus 301 under Cart). **SFCC-647 is already `Ready for Development`** and is the one that answers the data-source question. All are Priority `Low`, which is why they surfaced as unknowns. Raise 647; don't create tickets | 473 | **Shop the Look naming** | Four names in circulation for possibly two things: "Shop the Look" (M2 + SFCC-90), "Shop the Edit" (SFCC-313), "Product Cards with Lookbook" (04.7, marked Done), and `shoppableImage` (which already exists in code and delivers exactly the manual curation Bianca described). Resolve to one name per capability before estimating | 474 | **Preview & publishing** | Documented: the preview token is set on dev/test/sit/uat only, never staging or prod; both preview paths 404 without it and are `noindex`. **Authors preview on `uat`.** Settle it now — "can we preview on prod?" is a likely later ask, and it needs a Tier 1 change against a documented security rationale | 475 | **Contentful pattern per component** | Still unresolved after two sessions, and it decides story order, whether the incremental-assembly loop is available, and whether a component is buildable as specified. **Highest-value item to close** | 476 | **`regions` content-model field** | Unconfirmed, and it affects every Contentful component's variant model across 8 storefronts. Prerequisite to "design variants upfront" | 477 | **Composed-page ownership** | Tim's *"not product/category → Contentful"* rule is a good default but doesn't settle PDP/PLP editorial blocks, category landing pages, or promotional tiles in navigation. Category landing pages are the sharp edge, and PLP work is already in flight | 478 479 ### The Figma link on the card is an input — treat it as one 480 481 The devs work from the Figma links on the Jira card via the Figma MCP. That makes the link a **build 482 input**, not a reference: whatever it points at is what gets coded, near-literally. 483 484 So a wrong or stale link doesn't produce a question — it produces a component built to the wrong design, 485 which then propagates: 486 487 - the **dev** builds the wrong thing, 488 - the **BA** signs off AC written against a different frame, 489 - **QA** tests against a third source, 490 491 and nobody discovers it until page assembly, by which point it's a defect against a 10-defect budget. 492 493 **Action:** where a card's Figma links are wrong, stale, or point at the wrong frame, go back to **Jas** and 494 ask for the card to be reworked with correct links rather than clarifying it verbally to one developer. 495 A verbal fix repairs one person's understanding and leaves the card — the thing BA and QA both read — 496 still wrong. 497 498 Worth adding to the refinement checklist: **does the card carry a Figma link, and does it point at the 499 frame this story is actually about?** It's a ten-second check that removes a whole class of misalignment. 500 501 **A process note worth acting on.** The Size Selector / Add To Bag split was argued and settled in a Jira comment thread two weeks before M1 re-derived it. Decisions made in refinement need somewhere findable to live, or they get re-litigated. Cheapest fix: when a decision lands, it goes on the story *and* into the relevant Confluence page — not just the thread. 502 503 --- 504 505 ## Play 9 — Design-system escalation 506 507 *Covers responsibility 7* 508 509 Standing agenda for the design review with Kiera. Two concrete items rather than a general "validate button states": 510 511 1. **Button** — 04.7 lists *"Style: Primary, Secondary · Size: Large, Small · Colour: Normal, Inverse"* and marks it Done. The implemented component exposes `variant: 'primary'|'secondary'` and `size: 'lg'|'sm'` — **no Colour axis.** Worth noting the *states* are fine (hover, active, disabled, focus-visible are all defined for both variants), so "disabled variants" isn't the gap; the Colour axis is. **The registry reports 10 consumers** (`.claude/registry/components.md`, verified against `develop` 512 @ `2dfeb4d`), so adding the axis later touches ten call sites, not a handful. Re-check the number before 513 quoting it — the registry is regenerated on every `overrides/app/**` change. 514 2. **Icon Button** — same Inventory spec, also marked Done, **no implementation at all.** 515 516 ### Missing tokens and misaligned designs — the standing route 517 518 **Anything the design system doesn't answer goes to Kiera. Nothing gets invented locally.** 519 520 Two categories, same destination: 521 522 | What you hit | Why it can't be solved in code | 523 |---|---| 524 | **A Figma value with no token** | `theme/foundation/` is Tier 1 and designer-owned. Adding a token locally forks the design system silently | 525 | **A design that contradicts the implemented tokens** | Someone has to decide which is right. A developer picking one is an undocumented decision that later reads as a bug | 526 527 Live examples to carry into the next design review, all currently flagged in-code rather than resolved: 528 529 - **Primary button hover is 2.96:1** — white on `#969696`, failing WCAG AA (needs 4.5:1). Known, logged, 530 still open. 531 - **No inverse focus-ring token**, so focus on a dark surface is invisible. 532 - **Button heights** — `50/41px` in `button.ts` vs `52/40px` from Handover, and `BTN_PADDING_Y` (`5px`) 533 has no Handover token at all. 534 - **`textStyles.navigation`** is the only one of 22 text styles hardcoding `lineHeight: 'normal'` instead 535 of referencing the scale; Figma reportedly specifies 100%. Until it's decided, nav line-height renders 536 off-spec. 537 - **Spacing gaps** — 28px and 44px are in use with no named scale entry between `xl` (24) and `2xl` (32), 538 or `3xl` (40) and `4xl` (64). 539 540 The pattern to reinforce with the team: **flag it in-code with a comment naming the open question, and 541 raise it — don't silently pick a number.** That's already the convention; it's working, and it's worth 542 praising when you see it, because the alternative is invisible. 543 544 More broadly: 04.7's status column marks components Done on *design* confirmation, which doesn't imply the implemented API matches. Worth agreeing what "Done" means in that column, since story writers are reading it as readiness. 545 546 --- 547 548 ## Who owns what — and the session to settle it 549 550 The plays above assume a clear escalation route for each kind of problem. In practice the ownership 551 boundaries between FED, design and BA are not agreed, which is why the same question reaches different 552 people and gets different answers. 553 554 **Action: run an alignment session with Tash, Kiera and Hannah to establish who owns what.** Not a status 555 meeting — a boundary-setting one. The output is a single line per category naming the owner. 556 557 Working view going in, to be confirmed or corrected in the session: 558 559 | Category | Working owner | Route | 560 |---|---|---| 561 | Design system, tokens, missing values | **Kiera** | Standing design review — Play 9 | 562 | Design intent, misaligned or missing frames | **Kiera** | Same slot | 563 | Story content, AC, Figma links on the card | **Jas** | Rework the card, don't patch it verbally — Play 8 | 564 | Registry tooling, `shared/` coverage, override-first in F2R | **Han** | In flight — Play 1 | 565 | Component reuse, override-vs-build calls, PR quality | **You** | Plays 1 and 5 | 566 | Design-parity validation (who actually does the visual pass) | **Unassigned** | The sharp edge — Play 7 | 567 568 That last row is the one to force a decision on. Play 7 already notes design-parity validation has no 569 automated home and no named owner; combined with a 10-defect budget, "it quietly becomes the FED lead's 570 job" is the default outcome unless the session says otherwise. 571 572 Two dependencies worth tracking out of the same conversation: 573 574 - **Han's registry work** extends the generator to cover the `shared/` folder and bakes override-first 575 into the F2R workflow. Both reduce Play 1's manual load — worth knowing when they land so the playbook 576 can stop asking you to do it by hand. 577 - **The Figma-link quality issue** (Play 8) needs Jas to own card correctness, not just card creation. 578 579 --- 580 581 ## Guardrails 582 583 Things to respect while moving fast on all of the above. 584 585 **Tier 1 files.** You hold tier-1-approver / admin, so the verified-session exception applies — you can proceed after naming the file and the reason. Relevant to Play 5's two proposed rules (`.coderabbit/`, `.eslintrc.js`) and to `.github/workflows/`. 586 587 **Four files are absolute** — the exception does *not* apply regardless of approver status: `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js`. 588 589 **Branches.** Never work on `develop` or `main`. `release/*` is supervised — plan-first, confirm every edit, and code fixes go through a `fix/release-*` sub-branch. 590 591 **Squad boundaries.** `header/`, `footer/`, `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/` are shared shell — coordinate with the other squad before touching. `order-summary/` is Tier 2 and Squad B-notified. 592 593 **Commits and PRs** only on explicit request — not as a "natural next step" after finishing work. 594 595 **Scope.** Fixing a bug in a component doesn't license touching the hook it calls. Propose upward refactors; don't do them silently. 596 597 --- 598 599 ## Standing artifacts you own 600 601 | Artifact | Cadence | 602 |---|---| 603 | Refinement checklist (Play 2's challenge list) | Keep current as patterns emerge | 604 | Renderer contract template (Play 4) | Once; sign off per Contentful component | 605 | Per-component accessibility AC set (Play 6) | Once; applied per story | 606 | PR review question list (Play 5) | Review quarterly against what tooling now catches | 607 | Open-items register (Play 8) | Update as items close | 608 | Design-system gap list (Play 9) | Standing design-review agenda | 609 610 --- 611 612 ## First two weeks 613 614 Sequenced by leverage — the first three unblock everything else. 615 616 **Week 1** 617 1. Close the alt-text question with Tim before it propagates into AC 618 2. Get the Contentful pattern decision made (entry-driven vs Studio Experiences per component) — it blocks story order and buildability 619 3. Add the registry line to the BA prompt template — makes Play 1 self-service instead of making you a gate 620 4. Adopt the external-link standard from existing draft AC and close the item 621 622 **Week 2** 623 5. Publish the renderer-contract template and use it on the next Contentful pair 624 6. Communicate the estimation re-baseline once, clearly, in planning 625 7. Take the two Button / Icon Button items to design review — plus the token gaps in Play 9 626 8. Raise SFCC-647 so the recommendations question resolves itself 627 9. Put the two enforcement rules up as a decision 628 629 **Also, and not optional given the defect budget** 630 631 10. **Run the ownership alignment session** with Tash, Kiera and Hannah — and force a decision on who owns 632 design-parity validation. Everything else in this playbook has a named owner; that one doesn't. 633 11. **Ask Jas to rework any card whose Figma links are wrong or stale.** It's the cheapest defect 634 prevention available — the links are a build input, not a reference. 635 12. **Set the "green locally before opening a PR" expectation once, to the whole team.** `tsc`, lint, 636 tests. Said once as a standard, it costs nothing; enforced per-PR, it costs an hour each time. 637 13. **Say the override-first default out loud in refinement**, with the reason — overrides inherit the 638 hooks and wiring, bespoke builds re-derive them invisibly. 639 640 --- 641 642 *Working document. The plays are grounded in what the two sessions actually asked for; the mechanics come from how this repo works today, so both will need updating as the tooling and the backlog move.* 643 644 *Verified against `develop` @ `2dfeb4d` on 18 August 2026. Confirmed accurate: every asserted repo path, 645 the base-capability claims (`product-view`'s `addToCart`/`updateCart`, `swatch-group`'s index/swatch/test, 646 `quantity-picker`, all three variant hooks), the ast-grep and semgrep rule ids, the absent ESLint 647 complexity rules, the bundlesize budgets, the four absolute files, and `shoppableImage` / 648 `pages/experience` / `pages/contentfulPreview`. Two figures were corrected in this pass — Button's 649 consumer count and the E2E area coverage. See the companion findings doc for the full V&V trail.* 650 651 *Updated 18 August 2026 with the UI-build additions: the 10-defect quality bar (§1), override-first as the 652 default (Play 1), gate-zero plus three-surface review and the token checklist (Play 5), Figma-link 653 correctness as a build input (Play 8), the design-system escalation route and live token gaps (Play 9), and 654 the ownership alignment session (new section). The token specifics reflect `develop` after PR #56 — check 655 `overrideStyling.md` before quoting them.* 656

file.content: # FED Lead Playbook **Derived from:** the two "Contentful v PWA Kit Components and User Story Alignment" sessions **Owner:** Marcel Navarro · **Started:** August 2026 **Companions:** [fedBuild-manual.md](./fedBuild-manual.md) (the developer-facing half — how to build) · [componentStories-BA-guide.md](./componentStories-BA-guide.md) (the BA-facing version) · [pr52-pr55-findings.md](./pr52-pr55-findings.md) (worked example of Play 5 applied to two live PRs) · `.docs/temp/{componentStoryReview,meeting2Prep,meeting2Analysis}.md` (the underlying analysis) **Authority on styling:** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` in-repo — if this playbook and that file disagree, it wins. Purpose: the two sessions put sixteen things on your desk without saying when or how any of them get done. This turns that into a rhythm, a set of repeatable plays, and the specific mechanics for each. --- ## 1. Regenerated automatically by the pre-commit hook on any `overrides/app/**` change | | Same for hooks / utils / pages / routes | `.claude/registry/{hooks,utils,pages,routes}.md` | | What's in the base package? | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` and `/app/hooks/` | | Is it already claimed by a squad? | Registry `Squad` column · `.claude/rules/squadA.md` | | What tier am I about to touch? | Registry `Tier` column, or `/audit-tier` | The `Origin` column is doing most of the work: **`Base` means it exists but isn't scaffolded into `overrides/` yet** — which is a cost, not a free win (see below). ### Worked examples, already verified | Ask | What already exists | |---|---| | Size selector | Base `swatch-group/` — index, swatch, plus an existing test | | Add to bag | Base `product-view/index.jsx` — already does `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the button and label, the add-to-cart modal, bundle handling, and an `updateCart` variant | | Max purchase quantity | Base `quantity-picker/` | | Variant resolution | `use-controlled-variations`, `use-derived-product`, `use-add-to-cart-modal` | Worth knowing before SFCC-650 is sized: its description says *"Cart API integration is in scope"*, but the base already performs the cart call. That story should read as **extend `product-view`**, not build cart integration. ### Override-first — why the second rung is where the value is The ladder says "reuse before build". The stronger version, and the one to hold the line on: **default to overriding the base component, not writing a new one.** The reason is not tidiness — it's that an override **inherits the wiring for free**. Override `product-view` and you get `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the add-to-cart modal, bundle handling and `updateCart` already connected. Build a bespoke equivalent and every one of those has to be re-derived, re-tested and re-reviewed, and none of it is visible in the story points. There's a second-order effect worth naming in refinement. PWA Kit's resolver rewires imports transparently, so **overriding a component SFCC's own base components already import means the whole base template inherits your version** — no call sites touched. A bespoke component in a new folder reaches only the pages someone remembers to wire it into. Same visual result on the page you're building; very different coverage across the site. ⚠️ **One documented exception: `shared/ui/`.** That directory is consumed through a barrel (`shared/ui/index.jsx`), and the barrel's own re-exports are **relative** (`export {Button} from './Button'`). The `ccExtensibility` resolver only rewrites `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` specifiers, so a relative import inside `node_modules` is never redirected. **208 base files import that barrel; none import `shared/ui/Button` directly — so overriding `shared/ui//` intercepts nothing.** It is a place to put raw Zimmermann primitives for *our own* code to import explicitly, not an interception point. See "Two component families" below. So the question in review isn't only "did you reuse?" but **"is this an override, and if not, why not?"** **In flight, and relevant:** Han is extending the registry generator to account for the `shared/` folder as well, and is building the override-first approach into the F2R workflow — so the default lands in the tooling rather than depending on everyone remembering it. Worth tracking; it removes work from Play 1. ### The hidden cost to name every time If `Origin = Base`, the component isn't in `overrides/` yet, and AGENTS.md's **Copy-first rule** applies before any functional work: 1. Copy base file → mirrored path in `overrides/` 2. Convert to TypeScript, fix imports 3. `npx tsc --noEmit` 4. Add a temporary `console.log` marker 5. **Stop — a human confirms the override renders instead of the base** 6. Then build; remove markers It's serialised and human-gated. **The first story against a given base component pays it; later ones don't.** This is the single most common reason a story looks small and isn't — exactly Jasmijn's concern. Either split it into an enabler story or size the first story accordingly. ### Making this scale (the fix for #1) Add one line to the BA prompt template in Confluence 274137093: > *"Check `.claude/registry/components.md` — does a Base, Override or Custom component already cover this? Report Origin, Tier, Squad and Consumer count."* That makes four of the six refinement questions self-service. You keep the two that need judgement: - **Is extending the base the right call, or is a Zimmermann-specific build justified?** - **Is the design-system prerequisite real, or can we proceed?** ### Preventing duplicate atoms (#3, #8) The atoms question — *"when does an atom deserve its own story?"* — is largely already answered by existing convention rather than needing a new model: - A story is required for anything **exported from its folder** under `overrides/app/components/` or `/pages/`. - **Not** required for internal sub-components that only render inside one parent — cover their variants via the parent's stories. - The Storybook categorisation (`Foundation / Elements / Layout / Commerce / Forms / Pages / Contentful`) gives you the vocabulary: `Elements/` *is* the atoms layer. Applied to 04.7's `↳ Sub-component` rows: Pause/Play, Footer Item, Footer Textfield, Icons don't each need a story unless independently reusable. Without that rule the Footer alone generates four. --- ## Play 2 — Estimation validation *Covers responsibilities 5, 16* Run this before sprint planning, not in it. ### The re-baseline to communicate once M2 concluded pages become assemblies. One Editorial Card, not a Homepage one and a PLP one. ### The distinction to hold | Kind | Examples | How it's built | |---|---|---| | **Configuration variant** | text alignment, CTA on/off, title on/off, body copy present/absent | Props on one component ✅ Tim's rule applies directly | | **Composition variant** | 1 vs 2 column, 3-up vs 4-up grids | A **container/slot component** — structurally a second component | This matters because a composition variant priced as a prop will be under-estimated. On the Studio Experiences path especially, a repeating structure can't be a prop — the composition primitive is `children`. So "one Editorial Card with all variants" often resolves to *two* components: the card, plus a container holding one or two. Better outcome — the container is reusable anywhere — but it changes the count. Catch it at refinement. ### Why "upfront" is a hard requirement here, not a preference The Contentful sync is **additive-only — it cannot delete a field from a published content type**. Getting the variant model wrong isn't rework, it's semi-permanent. This is the strongest argument you have for holding the line on variant completeness, and it supports Tim's position rather than fighting it. ### Optional-field handling (#11) M2: don't assume CMS fields are populated. Every Contentful-backed component needs AC for the absent case — no empty space, no placeholder, no layout break. Make it a standing question in refinement rather than a per-story discovery. --- ## Play 4 — The renderer contract *Covers responsibility 10* M2 asked for "a standard renderer contract between Contentful models and React components." This is the artifact that makes the Contentful story and the PWA Kit story independently workable — without it they drift, and additive-only sync makes drift expensive. **The requirement it satisfies:** `02-contentful.md` §2 — *"TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time."* **The artifact:** one table, identical in both stories of every Contentful pair. | Field ID | Display name | Type / control | Required | Localised | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `image` | Image | Media | Yes | No | | | `imageAlt` | Image Alt Text | shortText | No | Yes | behaviour when empty — see Play 6 | | `bodyCopy` | Body Copy | longText | No | Yes | | | `ctaLabel` | CTA Label | shortText | No | Yes | CTA renders only if label **and** URL set | | `ctaUrl` | CTA URL | shortText | No | No | internal → same tab; external → new tab + `rel="noopener noreferrer"` | **Field IDs, not display names.** "Body copy" in prose is where drift starts. **You own the template; the BA fills it; you sign off the field IDs before the Contentful story is built.** That signature is the cheapest possible insurance against an undeletable wrong field. **Note for the ordering question:** for Studio Experiences components the contract is generated from the React props rather than authored first — so the review point moves to the component's prop type. Highest-frequency design-system violation | | **Component complexity / size** | No `complexity` or `max-lines-per-function` in `.eslintrc.js` — confirmed | | **Chakra `` without alt** | The ast-grep rule matches lowercase `` only. Every Contentful component here uses `` — so the guard doesn't cover the component family under discussion | | **Duplication / reuse** | No tool detects "this is a second Button". This is the core of responsibility #3 and it is entirely human | | **Salesforce alignment** | Whether base capability was leveraged — judgement only | Two of these are cheap to close, and the repo's own rules files already recommend the fix: an ast-grep rule for hardcoded design values, and the two ESLint core rules. **Both touch Tier 1 files** — raise as a decision, don't land quietly. See §Guardrails. ### Gate zero — does it actually build? **Check this before spending review attention on anything else.** A PR has already been opened on this project with a failing typecheck — missing type declarations that the branch itself had previously supplied and lost in a merge. Reviewing the design of code that doesn't compile wastes the expensive part of your day. ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # must be clean npm run lint # separate real errors from auto-fixable prettier noise npx vitest run ``` Two things worth knowing about this failure mode, because it will recur: - **A merge can silently delete a declaration.** When a branch merges `develop` and both sides touched the same ambient-types file, the merge can resolve to develop's version and drop what the branch added. It typechecks on neither side's intent and nobody notices until CI or a local build. - **It isn't always the author's mistake.** In that instance a second error came from following a repo rules file that named a package which doesn't exist on the installed Storybook major. Check whether the rule or the code is wrong before raising it as a code finding. Make "green locally before opening" the expectation, and say so once to the whole team rather than per-PR. It isn't about blame — it's that the review budget is an hour per PR and this spends it on nothing. ### Review across three surfaces, not one Reading the diff is the smallest part. For any UI PR, look at all three: | Surface | What only it will tell you | |---|---| | **The diff** | Tokens vs literals, reuse vs reimplementation, abstractions respected | | **The preview environment** | What it actually renders — states, responsive behaviour, whether hover/focus work at all | | **Figma** | Whether the rendered output matches the design, and which gaps are design gaps rather than build gaps | Every `feature/*` and `fix/*` branch now auto-deploys to its own MRT environment and posts the URL on the PR. There is no longer a reason to review a UI change from the diff alone — **open the environment and put it beside Figma.** If no URL comment appeared, the branch had no open PR when it was pushed; a further push once the PR exists will post it. Evaluate the rendered output against Figma deliberately, at the breakpoints the design defines. Anything that doesn't line up is either a build finding or a design gap — and separating those two is your call, not the developer's. ### Tokens and CSS — the highest-yield thing you check This is where divergence starts, it is not mechanically enforced, and both PRs currently in flight have drifted in different directions. Be deliberately vigilant here. `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` is the authority. The hierarchy, in order: 1. `textStyle` for anything textual — **never** a raw `fontSize` 2. Semantic token strings — `color="text.default"`, `padding="m"` 3. The component's own `theme/components/.ts` for variant / size / state 4. `sx` only for a genuine prop-system gap 5. Scoped `.scss` only when `sx` truly can't express it What to actively look for: - **The correct token, not just a token.** A value that resolves to the right pixels via the wrong token passes a casual glance and breaks the moment the design system moves. Two `sx` blocks recently hand-rebuilt what `textStyle="heading3"` and `textStyle="body2"` already provide, property for property. - **`var(--zimm-*)` in the right layer.** It is the convention *inside* `theme/components/*.ts`. In component JSX it is not — that's rungs 1 and 2. Seeing `var()` in a `.tsx` is a signal to look closer. - **`--zimm-scale-NNN` numeric aliases in JSX.** They exist only for the `.zimm-*` global classes. The named scale (`m`, `l`, `xl`) is the Chakra-facing surface. - **A theme recipe that nothing consumes.** A `theme/components/.ts` file that is written and registered but never read via `useStyleConfig` looks like compliance and is dead code. - **A second copy of the token registry.** Any new utility that re-types token names as strings reintroduces exactly the drift the derived-token work removed. - **Interaction states in JavaScript.** `useState` for hover / press / focus instead of `_hover` / `_active` / `_focusVisible` means those states are dead until hydration, sticky on touch, and unreachable by the theme. ### Tests and stories — the minimum, while UI is the focus The build focus is UI, and that's fine — but don't let coverage reach zero on the way through: - **Unit tests where they earn their place** — data mapping, transforms, non-obvious logic. Not for re-exports or passthroughs. - **At minimum, scaffold the Storybook story.** Every component exported from its folder needs one. A scaffolded story with a `Default` export and the meaningful states is the floor, even if the `play` function comes later. It's also the surface your own review depends on. ### Review questions, in order 0. **Does it build?** `tsc`, lint, tests — gate zero above 1. Was an existing component / hook / utility reused, or is this a second implementation? 2. **Is it an override, or a bespoke build — and if bespoke, why?** 3. Are all design values tokens — and the *correct* tokens, in the correct layer? 4. Does it respect existing abstractions, or work around them? 5. Was base Salesforce capability leveraged where it exists? 6. Accessibility: keyboard, focus order, states — beyond what ast-grep catches 7. Storybook story present? Test where logic-heavy? 8. **Does the preview environment match Figma at the defined breakpoints?** --- ## Play 6 — Accessibility *Covers responsibilities 6, 12* M1 and M2 both landed on accessibility living **inside** component stories, as AC, not as a follow-up task. ### The per-component AC set (#12) Standing list to apply to every component story: - Keyboard operability and reachability - Focus order and visible focus states - Interaction states (hover, active, disabled, focused) - Screen-reader behaviour for images and icon-only controls - Behaviour when optional content is absent **Baseline is WCAG 2.2 AA**, falling back to 2.1 only where 2.2 is technically infeasible *and* the reason is documented. Worth correcting on SFCC-648, which currently commits to 2.1 AA — and setting 2.2 as the story-template default so it doesn't propagate. ### The one open item M2 landed on: *if alt text exists render it; if not, don't render the attribute.* There's a real technical problem with that — omitting the attribute makes assistive tech treat the image as meaningful-but-undescribed, and it commonly reads out the filename; `alt=""` removes it from the accessibility tree entirely. The existing draft AC on the render story already says the latter. **Your action:** get it confirmed with Tim before it propagates into every image-bearing component. Frame it as the content-model question it really is — *how do we distinguish "intentionally decorative" from "someone forgot"?* — which is a Contentful field decision (required alt, or an explicit decorative toggle), not a renderer decision.
