1	# FED Build Manual — Manual UI Build & Delivery
2	
3	**Owner:** Marcel Angelo Navarro · **Started:** August 2026
4	
5	This is the guide to building the UI manually — not via a Figma-to-React generator. F2R outputs are an
6	input we leverage where they exist; they are not the delivery mechanism. You are writing the component.
7	
8	Read §3 (Design Foundations) before your first component. It contains traps that will cost you time
9	each if you meet them by surprise.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## 1. The Operating Principles
14	
15	Four things were agreed that change how you build. They apply to every story.
16	
17	### Static-first
18	
19	Where an integration isn't available yet, **build against static data and move on.** Do not block, and
20	do not stub out a fake integration layer.
21	
22	- Props in, markup out. The component takes the data it renders as props.
23	- Static/mock data lives in the **story**, not in the component.
24	- No data-fetching hooks inside `overrides/app/components/` — that's the container/presentational rule
25	  in `.claude/rules/components.md`, and it's what makes the later wiring a one-file change instead of
26	  a rewrite.
27	
28	When Contentful (or SFCC, or Omneo) comes online, the component doesn't change — the page or container
29	that feeds it does. If you find yourself writing "temporary" fetch logic inside a component, stop:
30	that's the thing static-first exists to prevent.
31	
32	### Leverage what exists before building
33	
34	In priority order — this is the ladder, and you should be able to say which rung you landed on:
35	
36	```
37	Salesforce / PWA Kit base capability
38	        ↓  nothing fits
39	Existing shared component in overrides/
40	        ↓  nothing fits
41	Existing pattern in the codebase
42	        ↓  nothing fits
43	New implementation  ← justify this in the PR description
44	```
45	
46	F2R outputs count as "existing": the onshore design team's outputs, Jersey's work (currently mostly
47	primitive/foundation-level), and the design foundations now in the codebase. Use them where they fit
48	rather than starting clean.
49	
50	**The default is override, not build.** Not for tidiness — because an override **inherits the wiring for
51	free.** Override `product-view` and you get `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the add-to-cart
52	modal, bundle handling and `updateCart` already connected. Build a bespoke equivalent and every one of
53	those has to be re-derived, re-tested and re-reviewed — none of which is visible in the story points, and
54	all of which lands on you.
55	
56	There's a second effect worth understanding, because it changes where your work shows up. PWA Kit's
57	resolver rewires imports transparently, so **overriding a component that SFCC's own base components
58	already import means the entire base template inherits your version** — zero call sites touched. A
59	bespoke component in a new folder only reaches the pages someone remembers to wire it into. Same result
60	on the page you're building; very different coverage across the site.
61	
62	⚠️ **One documented exception: `shared/ui/`.** That directory is consumed through a barrel
63	(`shared/ui/index.jsx`), and the barrel's own re-exports are **relative** (`export {Button} from
64	'./Button'`). The `ccExtensibility` resolver only rewrites `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...`
65	specifiers, so a relative import inside `node_modules` is never redirected. **208 base files import
66	that barrel; none import `shared/ui/Button` directly — so overriding `shared/ui/<Name>/` intercepts
67	nothing.** It is a place to put raw Zimmermann primitives for *our own* code to import explicitly, not
68	an interception point. See "Two component families" below.
69	
70	If you do land on "build custom", expect to justify it in the PR — that's not a formality, it's the one
71	question review will always ask.
72	
73	### Figma stays open the whole time
74	
75	Figma is not a one-time handoff you read and close. Keep it open and use it to actively find problems:
76	
77	- Validate the build against the design as you go, not at the end.
78	- Spot **missing tokens** — a value in Figma with no counterpart in `theme/foundation/`.
79	- Spot **missing design definitions** — a state (hover, disabled, error, empty) with no design.
80	- Catch discrepancies between design and implementation.
81	
82	When you find a gap, **raise it** — §7 covers where it goes. Silently inventing a value is the failure
83	mode; a hardcoded hex that "looked right" is how a design system dies.
84	
85	**Check the Figma link on the card actually points at your story's frame.** Because we work through the
86	Figma MCP, that link isn't a reference — it's effectively the spec, and whatever it points at is what
87	gets built.
88	
89	A wrong or stale link doesn't announce itself. It produces a component built to the wrong design, AC
90	signed off against a different frame, and QA testing a third source — none of which surfaces until page
91	assembly. If the link looks wrong, **ask the BA (Jas) to fix the card**, don't just work it out in a DM.
92	A verbal fix repairs one person's understanding and leaves the card — which the BA and QA both read —
93	still wrong.
94	
95	### Ask in the group chat
96	
97	Work it out together rather than solo. If you've been stuck more than ~30 minutes, or you're about to
98	make a decision that affects more than your own component, post it. These threads are how the team
99	learns as a group — a question you think is basic is usually three people's question.
100	
101	Claude is part of the workflow where it fits. Treat its output the way you'd treat a colleague's
102	first draft: useful, and checked before it ships.
103	
104	### The bar you're building to
105	
106	Worth knowing, because it explains why review here is stricter than you may be used to:
107	**the SOW allows no more than 10 defects across the build, and no Sev3.**
108	
109	Zimmermann is a luxury brand and is exceptionally particular about UI. That combination removes the usual
110	"ship it, fix it in QA" option — a visual defect that would be a shrug elsewhere consumes part of a very
111	small budget. Practically, for you:
112	
113	- Expect UI PRs to be reviewed against the preview environment **and** Figma, not just the diff.
114	- Self-review the same way before you open it (§8). It's faster than a review round-trip.
115	- Where design is missing or contradictory, **flag it** rather than picking something plausible. An
116	  invented value becomes a defect *and* a design-system divergence — two problems instead of none.
117	
118	---
119	
120	## 2. Before you write any code
121	
122	Five minutes here saves a day later.
123	
124	### Run the session start
125	
126	```bash
127	/session-start
128	```
129	
130	Reads the tracking docs, checks your branch, states where the project is. Do it once per session.
131	
132	### Confirm your branch
133	
134	```bash
135	git branch --show-current
136	```
137	
138	`feature/*` or `fix/*`, branched from `develop`. **If it says `develop` or `main`, stop.** No exceptions.
139	
140	### Check what already exists
141	
142	| Question | Where to look |
143	|---|---|
144	| Does a Base / Override / Custom component already cover this? | `.claude/registry/components.md` |
145	| Same for hooks, utils, pages, routes | `.claude/registry/{hooks,utils,pages,routes}.md` |
146	| What's in the base package? | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` |
147	| Which tier am I about to touch? | Registry `Tier` column, or `/audit-tier <path>` |
148	| Is another squad the owner? | Registry `Squad` column · `.claude/rules/squad{A,B}.md` |
149	
150	The registry's **`Origin`** column is the one that matters most:
151	
152	- **`Custom`** — a Zimmermann component already in `overrides/`. Extend it.
153	- **`Override`** — a base component already scaffolded into `overrides/`. Edit it directly.
154	- **`Base`** — it exists upstream but is **not** in `overrides/` yet. **This has a cost.** See below.
155	
156	### Two component families — and they do different jobs
157	
158	`overrides/app/components/` holds two kinds of thing. Knowing which you're writing decides the path, the
159	naming, and whether it affects anything but your own page.
160	
161	| | `components/<kebab-name>/` | `components/shared/ui/<PascalName>/` |
162	|---|---|---|
163	| **What it is** | An override of an SFCC component | A raw Zimmermann primitive — Link, Text, Image, Button |
164	| **Naming** | Keep SFCC's kebab-case exactly (`product-tile/`) | Mirror upstream's PascalCase (`Button/`) |
165	| **Does it intercept SFCC?** | **Yes** — base files import these by full package path, so your version replaces theirs everywhere | **No** — see the barrel exception above |
166	| **Who consumes it** | Every base page that already used it, plus you | Only code that imports it explicitly — chiefly Contentful renderers |
167	| **Why you'd reach for it** | You want to change how an SFCC component looks or behaves | You want a plain branded primitive with no commerce semantics attached |
168	
169	The `shared/ui` family exists because **Contentful renderers need primitives, not commerce components.**
170	Every Contentful component on `develop` already pulls them in — `duplexSection` (`Box`, `Text`),
171	`collectionHero` (`Box`, `Button`, `Heading`, `Text`), `hotspotPopup` (`Box`, `Image`, `Link`, `Skeleton`,
172	`Text`), `imageText`, `heroBanner`, `shoppableImage`. Upstream those resolve to bare Chakra
173	(`shared/ui/Button/index.jsx` is literally `export {Button} from '@chakra-ui/react'`). A CMS rich-text
174	renderer mapping a `hyperlink` node to a `Link` wants exactly that — predictable and unopinionated — not a
175	component carrying SFCC's locale-routing and commerce behaviour.
176	
177	**Status: the intent is agreed, the wiring is not built.** A `shared/ui/Button` exists on
178	`feature/pdp-token-class-spike`, its only consumer is the `/dev/components` catalogue page, there is no
179	`overrides/app/components/shared/ui/index.tsx` barrel, and `collectionHero` still imports `Button` from
180	the SFCC barrel — so it still gets raw Chakra. Don't build against this family until the barrel question
181	is settled (see the playbook).
182	
183	### What's actually overridden today
184	
185	Worth knowing before you estimate anything: **`overrides/app/components/` currently contains seven
186	directories.** As of `develop` @ `2dfeb4d`:
187	
188	```
189	_app-config   button   contentful   foundation   header   icons   pageContainer
190	```
191	
192	That's it. `product-tile`, `display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `footer`,
193	`list-menu`, `drawer-menu` and `seo` are all still **`Origin = Base`** — they exist upstream and are
194	referenced throughout `.claude/rules/` and the protected-file lists, but they have **not** been scaffolded
195	into `overrides/` yet.
196	
197	Two consequences:
198	
199	- **Most stories you pick up will pay copy-first** (below). Assume it until the registry says otherwise.
200	- **When a rules file points at one of those as an example, the file won't be there.** The convention is
201	  real; the worked example often isn't yet. Check before you go looking.
202	
203	### If `Origin = Base`, the copy-first rule applies
204	
205	Before any functional work, AGENTS.md requires:
206	
207	1. Copy the base file → mirrored path in `overrides/` (keep the kebab-case filename exactly)
208	2. Convert to TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`), fix imports
209	3. `npx tsc --noEmit`
210	4. Add a temporary `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')` marker
211	5. **Stop.** A human confirms the override is rendering instead of the base
212	6. Then build; remove the markers
213	
214	It's serialised and human-gated, and **the first story against a given base component pays it — later
215	ones don't.** This is the single most common reason a story looks small and isn't. Flag it at refinement,
216	not on day three of the sprint.
217	
218	### Sanity-check the scope
219	
220	```bash
221	/scope-check
222	```
223	
224	Classifies everything you're about to touch by tier and tells you if the change is safe, risky, or
225	blocked. Worth it any time you're not certain.
226	
227	---
228	
229	## 3. Design Foundations — read this before your first component
230	
231	**Canonical reference: `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`.** That file is the authority on styling an
232	override; this section is the orientation for it. If the two ever disagree, the rules file wins — and
233	this section needs a fix, so raise it.
234	
235	The design system lives in `overrides/app/theme/`. It has **one** source of truth and derives outward:
236	
237	```
238	foundation/  colour.ts · typography.ts · spacing.ts · sizes.ts · motion.ts · gridSystem.ts
239	        |  imported and derived from — never retyped
240	foundation/zimmTokens.ts          -> the --zimm-* CSS custom properties
241	        |  consumed by
242	theme/components/*.ts (recipes)   ·   globalStyles.ts (.zimm-* classes)
243	```
244	
245	`zimmTokens.ts` is **derived**, not a second copy — it imports `colors.grey[900]` rather than retyping
246	`#191919`. That is why you never edit it directly, and why two values cannot drift apart.
247	`theme/index.test.tsx` guards the arrangement with 125 tests; a failure there is a real drift signal,
248	not test noise.
249	
250	### The styling hierarchy — reach for these in order
251	
252	This is the load-bearing rule of the whole section.
253	
254	1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual — `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`
255	2. **Semantic token strings** — `color="text.default"`, `bg="background.02"`,
256	   `padding={{ base: 'm', md: 'xl' }}`
257	3. **The component's own `theme/components/<name>.ts`** for anything that varies by variant / size /
258	   state. For an interactive component with Chakra support (buttons, inputs, links) that file is the
259	   **single source of truth**
260	4. **`sx` prop** for a genuine one-off gap in the Chakra prop system
261	5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` truly cannot express it (complex pseudo-selectors, keyframes)
262	
263	**Never** a raw hex / px / rem / em literal in a component file. The one standing exception is
264	`button.ts`'s provisional constants — trap 2 below.
265	
266	Registered component recipes today: `Button`, `Header`, `ListMenu` (`theme/components/index.ts`).
267	Adding a new one is yours to do — one file per Chakra component, registered in that index.
268	
269	### Setting type — always `textStyle`, never `fontSize`
270	
271	```tsx
272	<Text textStyle="body1">…</Text>          // ✅
273	<Heading textStyle="heading3">…</Heading>  // ✅
274	<Text fontSize="md">…</Text>               // ❌ never
275	```
276	
277	**Why this is a hard rule, not a preference.** Four Zimmermann font-size keys collide with Chakra
278	defaults, and the base retail-react-app uses those names at ~199 call sites:
279	
280	| Key | Zimmermann | Chakra |
281	|---|---|---|
282	| `md` | 24px | 16px |
283	| `xs` | 16px | 12px |
284	| `2xs` | 14px | 10px |
285	| `3xs` | 12px | 7.2px |
286	
287	The Zimmermann font scale is **deliberately not registered** as `theme.fontSizes` for exactly this
288	reason. If you write `fontSize="md"` expecting 24px you get 16px. If you "fix" that by registering the
289	scale, you silently restyle every base component on the site. There's a test guarding against it —
290	don't fight it, use `textStyle`.
291	
292	**The 22 available text styles:**
293	
294	`heading1Strong` `heading1` `heading2` `heading3` · `body1Strong` `body1` `body2Strong` `body2` ·
295	`mobileBody1Strong` `mobileBody1` `mobileBody2` · `label` `caption` · `linkLg` `linkSm` ·
296	`button` `buttonSm` · `productNames` `price` · `navigation` · `footer` · `serif`
297	
298	Browse them rendered in Storybook under **Foundation → Typography**.
299	
300	### Colour — use the semantic aliases
301	
302	```tsx
303	<Box bg="background.01" color="text.default" borderColor="border.default" />   // ✅
304	<Box bg="#f9f8f6" color="#191919" />                                          // ❌
305	```
306	
307	Two layers exist. Reach for the **semantic** layer; the primitives are what the semantics are built from.
308	
309	| Group | Keys |
310	|---|---|
311	| `text.*` | `default` `inverse` `inverseGrey` `secondary` `muted` |
312	| `background.*` | `01`–`07` (`01`–`04` light/ivory, `05`–`06` dark, `07` white) |
313	| `border.*` | `default` `secondary` `focus` `forms` `error` |
314	| `status.*` | `success` `error` `errorBackground` `storeClosed` |
315	| `link.*` · `icon.*` | `default` `hover` · `default` |
316	| `action.primary.*` | `bgDefault` `bgHover` `bgPressed` `bgDisabled` `bgFocused` `text` `textDisabled` |
317	| `action.secondary.*` | `border` `bgHover` `text` `textInverse` `textDisabled` |
318	| Primitives | `grey.{black,900,800,700,600,500,300,200,100,white}` `ivory.{100..400}` `coral/green/orange/red.500` `opacity.{15,30,40,50}` |
319	
320	Browse under **Foundation → Colour**.
321	
322	### Spacing
323	
324	Both scales work — Chakra's numerics are preserved and the Zimmermann named scale is added on top.
325	**Prefer the named scale**, since it's what the design system speaks:
326	
327	```tsx
328	<Box padding="m" marginBottom="xl" />   // ✅ 1rem, 1.5rem
329	<Box padding={4} />                      // works, but not the design vocabulary
330	```
331	
332	`3xs` 0.125 · `2xs` 0.25 · `xs` 0.5 · `s` 0.75 · `m` 1 · `l` 1.25 · `xl` 1.5 · `2xl` 2 · `3xl` 2.5 ·
333	`4xl` 4 · `5xl` 5 · `6xl` 8 · `7xl` 10 — **in `rem`**, i.e. 2/4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40/64/80/128/160px at
334	the default 16px root font-size.
335	
336	**The scale is `rem`, not `px`** — spacing and type scale with the user's root font-size and browser
337	zoom (WCAG 1.4.4). Hairline geometry deliberately does not:
338	
339	- `borderWidth="default"` → `1px`, registered as a Chakra scale
340	- `focusRingOffsets.{default, secondary}` → `2px` / `3px`, imported as a constant from
341	  `app/theme/foundation` (`secondary` exists to clear the secondary button's 1px border)
342	
343	**Unit rule:** `rem` for anything that should scale (type, spacing) · `px` only for hairline geometry
344	(border widths, focus-ring offsets) · `em` only for breakpoints. Never a raw literal of any unit in a
345	component file.
346	
347	⚠️ **Don't use the `--zimm-scale-NNN` numeric aliases in JSX.** You'll see them in `zimmTokens.ts`
348	(`--zimm-scale-500`, `--zimm-scale-1100`, …). They exist **only** so the `.zimm-*` global classes have
349	something to reference. The named scale is the Chakra-facing surface:
350	
351	```tsx
352	<Box mb="var(--zimm-scale-500)" />   // ❌ 20px, but bypasses the scale
353	<Box mb="l" />                        // ✅ same 20px, traceable to the token
354	```
355	
356	If the value you need has no named entry — 28px and 44px are both in use with nothing between `xl` (24)
357	and `2xl` (32), or `3xl` (40) and `4xl` (64) — that's a **token gap to raise** (§7), not a reason to reach
358	for the numeric alias.
359	
360	### Icon sizes, action sizes and motion are NOT theme tokens
361	
362	These collide with Chakra scales too (`theme.sizes.lg` is 32rem and backs `w`/`h`/`boxSize` everywhere),
363	so they're **imported as constants** instead:
364	
365	```tsx
366	import { iconSizes, actionSizes, motion } from 'app/theme/foundation';
367	
368	<Icon boxSize={iconSizes.lg} />                                    // 20px
369	<Button height={actionSizes.height.lg} />                          // 52px
370	transition: `opacity ${motion.duration.fast} ${motion.easing.standard}`
371	```
372	
373	`iconSizes` — `lg` 20 · `md` 16 · `sm` 12
374	`actionSizes` — `height.{lg:52, md:40}` · `paddingX.{lg:32, md:20}` · `gap:16`
375	`motion` — `duration.{fast:200ms, default:300ms, slow:500ms}` · `easing.{standard, slides, fades}`
376	
377	⚠️ **Motion values are PROVISIONAL** and pending designer sign-off. Use them, but expect them to move.
378	
379	### The `.zimm-*` global classes — and the one rule about them
380	
381	**27** global classes exist: `.zimm-text-*` (typography), `.zimm-form-*` (form-field layout),
382	`.zimm-grid`, `.zimm-focus-visible`. They mirror the design system as static CSS so handover markup can
383	be pasted and look right. They are **not** the preferred authoring route for new Zimmermann components —
384	default to the hierarchy above.
385	
386	**There are no `.zimm-btn-*` classes, and there must never be.** The whole family was deleted
387	deliberately, and the reason generalises:
388	
389	> **One canonical styling surface per component type.** If a component has interactive state, its
390	> `theme/components/<name>.ts` recipe is the only place its look is defined. A static CSS class cannot
391	> express `_hover` / `_active` / `_disabled` / `_focusVisible`, so a class "mirror" of a recipe is
392	> structurally incomplete from birth — and nothing stops the two drifting apart afterwards.
393	
394	So: **every button is Chakra's `<Button>` styled by `theme/components/button.ts`.** Never a class, never
395	a hand-rolled `<button>` with its own styles. `.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool only for genuinely
396	static, non-interactive, heavily-reused treatments — typography, the grid, form-field layout.
397	
398	⚠️ Worth knowing: `globalStyles.ts` has almost no consumers today (one Storybook demo uses `.zimm-grid`)
399	and it ships on every page. Don't reach for a class where a prop or a recipe will do.
400	
401	### Interaction state goes in CSS, never in React state
402	
403	This is the rule most likely to cost you a rewrite, so it's worth being blunt about.
404	
405	Hover, press, focus and disabled belong in the component's theme recipe as Chakra's pseudo-props. They do
406	**not** belong in `useState`.
407	
408	```tsx
409	// ❌ never — interaction state in React
410	const [hovered, setHovered] = useState(false)
411	<button onMouseEnter={() => setHovered(true)} style={{background: hovered ? a : b}}>
412	
413	// ✅ theme/components/myThing.ts — the browser does the work
414	_hover:        { bg: 'var(--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-hover)' },
415	_active:       { bg: 'var(--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-pressed)' },
416	_disabled:     { bg: 'var(--zimm-color-border-secondary)', cursor: 'not-allowed' },
417	_focusVisible: { outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)', outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)' },
418	```
419	
420	It looks identical in a screenshot. It behaves differently in five ways that all matter here:
421	
422	| JS state | CSS pseudo-class |
423	|---|---|
424	| Dead until hydration — the button renders but doesn't respond | Works on first paint, no JS needed |
425	| No way to express `@media (hover: hover)` → sticky hover on touch after a tap | Opts out on touch devices properly |
426	| Inline styles win every specificity fight — the theme **cannot** override them | Overridable by variant, later |
427	| The keyboard focus ring built for WCAG 2.4.7 lives in the recipe, so it never applies | Inherited automatically |
428	| Every hover re-renders the component | No React work at all |
429	
430	With a ≤2s p75 mobile LCP budget and a WCAG 2.2 AA target, the first and fourth rows are the ones that
431	turn into defects.
432	
433	**Corollary — a theme recipe nothing consumes is dead code.** If you write
434	`theme/components/myThing.ts` and register it, the component has to actually read it — Chakra's
435	`<Button>`/`<Link>` etc. do so automatically; a custom multipart component needs
436	`useStyleConfig('MyThing')`. A registered-but-unread recipe looks like compliance and changes nothing.
437	
438	### Adding a new token
439	
440	**You don't.** `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` is Tier 1 and designer-owned (Hard Rule #3). If Figma
441	has a value with no token, that's a §7 escalation, not a local addition. Same for
442	`theme/globalStyles.ts` (Tier 2, needs a named owner's nod).
443	
444	Per-component theme overrides in `theme/components/` **are** yours to add — one file per Chakra
445	component, registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.
446	
447	---
448	
449	## 4. The build sequence
450	
451	Four steps, in order. This is the agreed approach.
452	
453	### Step 1 — Does it already exist?
454	
455	§2. Check the registry and the base package. Report what you found in the PR description, even when the
456	answer is "nothing" — that's the evidence the ladder was walked.
457	
458	### Step 2 — Use as-is, override/extend, or build custom?
459	
460	| Verdict | When | What you do |
461	|---|---|---|
462	| **Use as-is** | Base behaviour and markup are right; only styling differs | Style it via `theme/components/<name>.ts`. No component file at all |
463	| **Override / extend** | Base structure is right, behaviour or markup needs changing | Copy-first (§2), then modify. **Minimal changes** — don't remove base functionality you weren't asked to touch |
464	| **Build custom** | Nothing upstream is close | `/new-component` scaffolds it. Justify the call in the PR |
465	
466	Most work should land in the first two columns. If you're reaching for "custom" often, raise it — either
467	the ladder isn't being walked or there's a real gap worth naming.
468	
469	**If SFCC's own components import the thing you're overriding, use the bridge pattern.** Check first:
470	
471	```bash
472	grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" \
473	  node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/
474	```
475	
476	Any hits mean base components depend on it, so its **default export must stay a faithful, undecorated
477	port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour. Put Zimmermann-only styling behind a
478	**named export** that wraps the default. Get this wrong and you restyle or break base cart / checkout /
479	account screens you never opened.
480	
481	Where the brand difference is purely token-driven you don't need the split at all — put it in
482	`theme/components/<name>.ts` instead, and leave the default export untouched.
483	
484	⚠️ **No worked precedent exists in the repo yet.** `overrideStyling.md` describes this pattern using
485	`product-tile` (`CardBaseline` + faithful default), `link`, `image-gallery`, `display-price` and
486	`swatch-group` — **none of which are overrides on `develop` today.** The pattern is the agreed approach;
487	you may well be the one who establishes the first example of it. If you are, say so in the PR so the rule
488	file can be updated to point at something real.
489	
490	### Step 3 — Execute the swap / override / build
491	
492	Component folder layout (`.claude/rules/conventions.md`):
493	
494	```
495	overrides/app/components/productTile/
496	  index.tsx            ← the component (named export matching the folder)
497	  index.stories.tsx    ← mandatory
498	  index.test.ts        ← only if logic-heavy
499	  types.ts             ← only if props are shared with siblings
500	  productTile.scss     ← only if Chakra props genuinely can't express it
501	```
502	
503	- **Zimmermann-authored files:** `camelCase` (`productTile.tsx`)
504	- **Override files mirroring a base file:** keep the original kebab-case exactly (`product-tile.tsx`)
505	- **TypeScript only inside `overrides/`.** No `.js`/`.jsx`, including stories and config
506	- Named export matches the folder; props type is `<ComponentName>Props`
507	- Callbacks are `onEventName`; required props non-optional, optional props use `?`
508	- Australian spelling in Zimmermann-authored code (`colour`, `centre`) — override files keep upstream
509	  spelling verbatim
510	- No magic numbers or strings — name the constant
511	- JSDoc required on anything with ≥2 callers and on every exported hook
512	
513	**Split it up when:** the component passes ~150 lines, branches heavily, or accumulates ≥2 related
514	`useState` calls (→ extract a hook in `overrides/app/hooks/use<Component><Feature>.ts`).
515	
516	### Step 4 — Apply the design styles
517	
518	§3. Chakra props first, tokens always, `textStyle` for type. Then check it against Figma at the
519	breakpoints the design defines, and raise what doesn't line up.
520	
521	---
522	
523	## 5. Storybook — non-negotiable, and your build surface
524	
525	Every component exported from its folder needs a `*.stories.tsx`. Internal sub-components that only
526	render inside one parent don't — cover their variants through the parent.
527	
528	Build **in** Storybook rather than building and then adding a story. It's the fastest loop you have,
529	and it's the only place a reviewer can see every state at once.
530	
531	```bash
532	npm run storybook
533	```
534	
535	**Categorisation** (drives the sidebar; pick the first that matches):
536	
537	| Category | What goes here |
538	|---|---|
539	| `Foundation/` | Design tokens — Colour, Typography, Spacing, Icons |
540	| `Elements/` | Generic building blocks — Button, Input, Badge, Link, Checkbox. *Tiebreaker: usable outside a form?* → `Elements/` |
541	| `Layout/` | Global chrome and structure — Header, Footer, DrawerMenu, Breadcrumb, Pagination |
542	| `Commerce/` | Commerce-specific shared — ProductTile, OrderSummary, PromoCode, DisplayPrice |
543	| `Forms/` | Composed form assemblies — AddressForm, NewsletterSignup |
544	| `Pages/` | Full page assemblies |
545	| `Contentful/` | CMS-driven — use mock Contentful data so variants are visible without a live CMS |
546	
547	```ts
548	export default { title: 'Commerce/ProductTile' };   // ✅
549	export default { title: 'Elements/DisplayPrice' };  // ❌ commerce-specific → Commerce/
550	```
551	
552	**Content:** every file has a `Default` export. Add named exports for meaningful states (`Loading`,
553	`OutOfStock`, `WithDiscount`, `Empty`) — not for every prop permutation. This is where your static-first
554	data lives.
555	
556	**`play` functions** only where there's interactive behaviour worth asserting — validation on blur,
557	disclosure open/close, focus movement. Query through `within(canvasElement)`, prefer `getByRole` with
558	an accessible name, and import `userEvent` from `@storybook/test` (not `@testing-library/user-event`).
559	
560	⚠️ **If a component looks wrong in Storybook but right in the app, suspect your imports before your
561	CSS.** `--zimm-*` variables now resolve correctly in Storybook (§3 trap 1). The likely cause is §3 trap
562	1b: a base-path import of an already-overridden component renders the *base* SFCC version in Storybook
563	and Vitest while working fine in the app. Switch it to a relative import.
564	
565	### Your branch gets a live URL, automatically
566	
567	Separate from Storybook, and new: every push to a `feature/*` or `fix/*` branch now builds and deploys
568	itself to its own dedicated MRT environment, then posts the URL as a comment on the PR.
569	
570	- Created on first push and **reused** on later pushes — one environment per branch, not per commit. The
571	  comment updates in place rather than piling up.
572	- **Torn down automatically** when the PR closes or the branch is deleted.
573	- A real Sydney-hosted (`ap-southeast-2`) storefront with real dev environment variables — not a mock.
574	- Excluded: `fix/release-*` sub-branches and `hotfix/*`.
575	
576	Use it for design review, QA sign-off, and anything cross-device. Nobody needs your branch checked out
577	locally to look at your work, and it's why you should never have to fight over the shared dev target
578	again.
579	
580	Storybook is still where you **build** — fastest loop, every state visible at once. The preview
581	environment is where other people **review**.
582	
583	---
584	
585	## 6. Accessibility — written as AC, not added later
586	
587	Baseline is **WCAG 2.2 AA**. Fall back to 2.1 AA only where 2.2 is technically infeasible, and document
588	why in the story.
589	
590	### The standing set — apply to every component
591	
592	- Keyboard operability and reachability
593	- Focus order, and a **visible** focus state
594	- All interaction states: hover, active, disabled, focused
595	- Screen-reader behaviour for images and icon-only controls
596	- Behaviour when optional content is absent (no empty box, no layout break)
597	- Target size ≥ 24×24 CSS px for interactive controls (SC 2.5.8)
598	
599	### Already mechanically enforced — you'll be caught anyway
600	
601	| Check | By |
602	|---|---|
603	| `<img>` without `alt` (`alt=""` is fine when decorative) | ast-grep |
604	| `IconButton` / `IconButtonWithRegistration` without `aria-label` | ast-grep |
605	| `onClick` on a non-interactive element without `role` | ast-grep |
606	| Unsanitised `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` | semgrep |
607	| Storybook a11y violations | `@storybook/addon-a11y`, `test: 'error'` — **fails CI** |
608	
609	⚠️ **The `<img>` rule matches lowercase `<img>` only.** Chakra's `<Image>` is *not* covered. Most
610	components here use `<Image>` — that one is on you.
611	
612	### Not enforced anywhere — genuinely your responsibility
613	
614	Keyboard flow, focus order, colour-contrast in states, screen-reader semantics beyond the above, and
615	whether the disabled state is actually communicated rather than just faded.
616	
617	---
618	
619	## 7. When you find a gap
620	
621	You will find them. Figma will be missing a state, a token won't exist, a requirement will contradict
622	itself. **Raise, don't invent.**
623	
624	| What you found | Where it goes |
625	|---|---|
626	| Value in Figma with no token | Design review (Kiera) via the lead — never add to `foundation/` yourself |
627	| Missing design for a state (hover/disabled/error/empty) | Design review, and flag on the story before it's sized |
628	| Design contradicts a signed-off PRD in `.docs/prd/` | **Stop.** Cite doc + section + requirement ID, ask which wins. Don't proceed silently either way |
629	| Requirement unclear, ambiguous, or unconfirmed | Ask in the group chat first; if it changes scope, it goes back to refinement |
630	| Contrast/a11y failure in the tokens themselves | Raise with the lead — several are already known (§3) |
631	| Needs a new npm package | **Stop.** Integration team approval required. Check `package.json` first — something installed may already do it |
632	| Needs a shared hook's signature changed | **Stop.** Team RFC |
633	| Touches a Tier 1 file | **Stop.** See `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` |
634	
635	Ask **one question at a time** and wait for the answer — batching them gets them half-answered.
636	
637	---
638	
639	## 8. Before you open a PR
640	
641	**Green locally before you open it.** Not a nicety — a PR that doesn't compile spends a reviewer's whole
642	budget on nothing, and review here runs an hour or more per UI PR.
643	
644	```bash
645	npx tsc --noEmit          # must be clean
646	npm run lint              # must not add new errors
647	npm test                  # Vitest
648	/code-quality             # naming, imports, structure, missing stories/tests
649	```
650	
651	Two failure modes specific to this repo, both seen already:
652	
653	- **A `develop` merge can silently delete a type declaration.** If your branch added something to
654	  `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts` and `develop` also changed that file, the merge can resolve to
655	  develop's version and drop yours. Re-run `tsc` **after** every merge from `develop`, not just before.
656	- **Sometimes the rule is wrong, not your code.** One recent failure came from following a repo rules file
657	  that named a package which doesn't exist on the installed Storybook major. If a documented import
658	  doesn't resolve, check the package actually exists before assuming you mistyped it — then flag the rule.
659	
660	### Self-review across the same three surfaces the reviewer will use
661	
662	Cheaper to catch it yourself than in a review round-trip:
663	
664	| Surface | What you're checking |
665	|---|---|
666	| **The diff** | Correct tokens in the correct layer, reuse over reimplementation, no raw literals |
667	| **The preview environment** | What it actually renders — every state, every breakpoint, hover and focus genuinely working |
668	| **Figma, side by side** | Parity at the breakpoints the design defines |
669	
670	Your branch's preview URL is posted on the PR automatically (§5). If a difference from Figma is a *design*
671	gap rather than a build gap, say so in the PR description — don't quietly resolve it.
672	
673	Then a local CodeRabbit review — **required, not optional**:
674	
675	```bash
676	coderabbit auth status && cr review --light --base develop
677	```
678	
679	If the CLI isn't installed or authenticated, install it (coderabbit.ai/cli) and run
680	`npm run env -- init` for the shared key rather than committing without a review. The GitHub PR review
681	is still the real gate; this one catches things earlier.
682	
683	### Self-check
684	
685	- [ ] Ladder walked — reuse checked and reported, "custom" justified
686	- [ ] Copy-first done and confirmed if `Origin = Base`; `console.log` markers removed
687	- [ ] All design values are tokens — **no hardcoded hex, no raw px/rem/em** (still not mechanically
688	      enforced: `overrideStyling.md` points at `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`, which does not exist yet —
689	      so this stays the highest-frequency violation in review)
690	- [ ] Type set with `textStyle`, never `fontSize`
691	- [ ] Storybook story exists, categorised correctly, `Default` plus meaningful states
692	- [ ] Vitest where logic is non-obvious — data mapping, transforms, complex state
693	- [ ] Accessibility AC met, including the parts no tool checks
694	- [ ] Optional/absent content handled — no empty space, no layout break
695	- [ ] No data-fetching hooks inside a `components/` file
696	- [ ] No `console.log`/`console.error` left behind
697	- [ ] Existing comments and commented-out code left alone (only remove alongside the code they describe)
698	- [ ] One protection tier touched, not several
699	- [ ] `/pr-checklist` run to generate the description
700	
701	**Commits, pushes and PRs happen only when explicitly asked.** Finishing the work is not the trigger.
702	
703	---
704	
705	## 9. Hard stops
706	
707	Non-negotiable. From AGENTS.md.
708	
709	- **Never work on `develop` or `main`.**
710	- **Never modify `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`** — designer-owned.
711	- **Never modify** `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js` —
712	  absolute, no approver exception.
713	- **Never modify test config** — `vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, `.storybook/`, `lighthouserc.js`.
714	- **Never add or remove packages** without integration-team approval. Use `npm install`, don't hand-edit
715	  `package.json`.
716	- **Never delete files** unless explicitly asked. Propose it and let a human confirm.
717	- **Never refactor upward** — fixing a component doesn't license changing the hook it calls.
718	- **Never rename or move a shared hook or component.**
719	- **Never reference a later sprint's code** — check `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`.
720	- **Never run `npm start`** — ask; the dev server is shared.
721	- **Never load a third-party script outside a Didomi consent callback.** Fail closed: unknown consent
722	  state means load nothing.
723	
724	### Shared-shell coordination
725	
726	`header/` `footer/` `drawer-menu/` `list-menu/` `seo/` `_app/` `_app-config/` `routes.tsx` are Tier 2
727	shared shell — **coordinate with the other squad before touching.** Same for
728	`product-tile/` `product-item/` `display-price/` `image-gallery/` `swatch-group/` (Squad B owns) and
729	`order-summary/` `promo-code/` `pickup-or-delivery/` (Squad A owns).
730	
731	---
732	
733	## 10. Performance — it's a requirement, not a polish pass
734	
735	Mobile page speed is a top project priority. **LCP budget ≤ 2s at p75 mobile.**
736	
737	- **Images:** always lazy-load, always serve correctly sized. Never render a full-res image at thumbnail size.
738	- **Code splitting:** dynamic `import()` for heavy components not needed on first render.
739	- **Data fetching:** request only the fields you need. No waterfalls — parallelise.
740	- **Third-party scripts:** must not block LCP. `defer`/`async`/post-hydration only, and always behind Didomi.
741	- **Bundle size:** gated at `main.js` ≤ 180 kB, `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB. Don't introduce a large dependency
742	  without asking. *(Note: there is currently no CSS budget in CI — that doesn't mean CSS is free.)*
743	
744	---
745	
746	## 11. Quick reference
747	
748	### Commands
749	
750	```bash
751	/session-start                    # start-of-session ritual
752	/audit-tier <path>                # tier, owner, blast radius
753	/scope-check                      # is this prompt safe to run
754	/new-component                     # scaffold component + story
755	/code-quality                     # audit before PR
756	/pr-checklist                     # generate PR description
757	npx tsc --noEmit                  # type check
758	npm run lint                      # ESLint
759	npm test                          # Vitest
760	npm run storybook                 # Storybook at :6006
761	cr review --light --base develop  # local CodeRabbit
762	```
763	
764	### Paths
765	
766	| What | Where |
767	|---|---|
768	| Components | `overrides/app/components/` |
769	| Hooks | `overrides/app/hooks/` |
770	| Pages | `overrides/app/pages/` |
771	| Shared types | `overrides/app/types/{commerce,components,hooks}.ts` |
772	| Design tokens (Tier 1, read-only) | `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` |
773	| Component theme overrides (yours) | `overrides/app/theme/components/` |
774	| **Styling rules — canonical, read this** | `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` |
775	| `--zimm-*` injection (app + Storybook) | `overrides/app/theme/zimmTokensGlobal.tsx` |
776	| Icons — **single source of truth** | `overrides/app/components/icons/` |
777	| Registries | `.claude/registry/*.md` |
778	| Rules | `.claude/rules/*.md` |
779	| Requirements | `.docs/prd/` · integrations `.docs/integration/NN-*.md` |
780	
781	**Icons:** import only from `overrides/app/components/icons`. Never from
782	`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons`. If an icon is missing, **ask** — don't substitute
783	a visually different one.
784	
785	### The six things people get wrong most
786	
787	1. **Interaction state in `useState` instead of the recipe's `_hover` / `_active` / `_focusVisible`** →
788	   identical in a screenshot; dead until hydration, sticky on touch, and unstylable by the theme (§3)
789	2. `fontSize="md"` instead of `textStyle` → wrong size, silently
790	3. Importing an already-overridden component by its `@salesforce/...` base path → your story or test
791	   silently exercises the unstyled **base** component while the app renders fine (§3 trap 1b)
792	4. A hardcoded hex or px that "matched the design" → no tool catches it; review will. Reaching for a
793	   `--zimm-scale-NNN` alias instead of the named scale counts as the same mistake
794	5. Data-fetching inside a `components/` file → makes the later integration a rewrite
795	6. Skipping copy-first on an `Origin = Base` component → the override never renders and you debug the
796	   wrong file
797	
798	---
799	
800	*Verified against `develop` @ `2dfeb4d` on 18 August 2026. Confirmed exact: the 22 text styles, the 27
801	`.zimm-*` classes, the 125 theme guard tests, the three registered recipes, every colour group and key,
802	`iconSizes` / `actionSizes` / `motion`, `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`, `NAV_LETTER_SPACING`,
803	`FONT_SERIF`, `--zimm-scale-500 = spacing.l`, the bundlesize budgets, and all six npm scripts. Corrected in
804	this pass: several components the rules files describe as existing overrides are still base — see "What's
805	actually overridden today" in §2.*
806	
807	*Working document, aligned to `develop` as of 18 August 2026 — PRs #53 (token foundation), #54 (preview
808	environments) and #56 (token architecture hardening + the styling rules file).
809	
810	*§3 is the part that moves. Its canonical source is `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` — if that file and
811	this section disagree, the rules file wins and this one needs correcting. Raise anything here that's gone
812	stale rather than working around it.*

# FED Build Manual — Manual UI Build & Delivery

**Owner:** Marcel Angelo Navarro · **Started:** August 2026

This is the guide to building the UI manually — not via a Figma-to-React generator. F2R outputs are an
input we leverage where they exist; they are not the delivery mechanism. You are writing the component.

Read §3 (Design Foundations) before your first component. It contains traps that will cost you time
each if you meet them by surprise.

---

## 1. The Operating Principles

Four things were agreed that change how you build. They apply to every story.

### Static-first

Where an integration isn't available yet, **build against static data and move on.** Do not block, and
do not stub out a fake integration layer.

- Props in, markup out. The component takes the data it renders as props.
- Static/mock data lives in the **story**, not in the component.
- No data-fetching hooks inside `overrides/app/components/` — that's the container/presentational rule
  in `.claude/rules/components.md`, and it's what makes the later wiring a one-file change instead of
  a rewrite.

When Contentful (or SFCC, or Omneo) comes online, the component doesn't change — the page or container
that feeds it does. If you find yourself writing "temporary" fetch logic inside a component, stop:
that's the thing static-first exists to prevent.

### Leverage what exists before building

In priority order — this is the ladder, and you should be able to say which rung you landed on:

```
Salesforce / PWA Kit base capability
        ↓  nothing fits
Existing shared component in overrides/
        ↓  nothing fits
Existing pattern in the codebase
        ↓  nothing fits
New implementation  ← justify this in the PR description
```

F2R outputs count as "existing": the onshore design team's outputs, Jersey's work (currently mostly
primitive/foundation-level), and the design foundations now in the codebase. Use them where they fit
rather than starting clean.

**The default is override, not build.** Not for tidiness — because an override **inherits the wiring for
free.** Override `product-view` and you get `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the add-to-cart
modal, bundle handling and `updateCart` already connected. Build a bespoke equivalent and every one of
those has to be re-derived, re-tested and re-reviewed — none of which is visible in the story points, and
all of which lands on you.

There's a second effect worth understanding, because it changes where your work shows up. PWA Kit's
resolver rewires imports transparently, so **overriding a component that SFCC's own base components
already import means the entire base template inherits your version** — zero call sites touched. A
bespoke component in a new folder only reaches the pages someone remembers to wire it into. Same result
on the page you're building; very different coverage across the site.

⚠️ **One documented exception: `shared/ui/`.** That directory is consumed through a barrel
(`shared/ui/index.jsx`), and the barrel's own re-exports are **relative** (`export {Button} from
'./Button'`). The `ccExtensibility` resolver only rewrites `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...`
specifiers, so a relative import inside `node_modules` is never redirected. **208 base files import
that barrel; none import `shared/ui/Button` directly — so overriding `shared/ui/<Name>/` intercepts
nothing.** It is a place to put raw Zimmermann primitives for *our own* code to import explicitly, not
an interception point. See "Two component families" below.

If you do land on "build custom", expect to justify it in the PR — that's not a formality, it's the one
question review will always ask.

### Figma stays open the whole time

Figma is not a one-time handoff you read and close. Keep it open and use it to actively find problems:

- Validate the build against the design as you go, not at the end.
- Spot **missing tokens** — a value in Figma with no counterpart in `theme/foundation/`.
- Spot **missing design definitions** — a state (hover, disabled, error, empty) with no design.
- Catch discrepancies between design and implementation.

When you find a gap, **raise it** — §7 covers where it goes. Silently inventing a value is the failure
mode; a hardcoded hex that "looked right" is how a design system dies.

**Check the Figma link on the card actually points at your story's frame.** Because we work through the
Figma MCP, that link isn't a reference — it's effectively the spec, and whatever it points at is what
gets built.

A wrong or stale link doesn't announce itself. It produces a component built to the wrong design, AC
signed off against a different frame, and QA testing a third source — none of which surfaces until page
assembly. If the link looks wrong, **ask the BA (Jas) to fix the card**, don't just work it out in a DM.
A verbal fix repairs one person's understanding and leaves the card — which the BA and QA both read —
still wrong.

### Ask in the group chat

Work it out together rather than solo. If you've been stuck more than ~30 minutes, or you're about to
make a decision that affects more than your own component, post it. These threads are how the team
learns as a group — a question you think is basic is usually three people's question.

Claude is part of the workflow where it fits. Treat its output the way you'd treat a colleague's
first draft: useful, and checked before it ships.

### The bar you're building to

Worth knowing, because it explains why review here is stricter than you may be used to:
**the SOW allows no more than 10 defects across the build, and no Sev3.**

Zimmermann is a luxury brand and is exceptionally particular about UI. That combination removes the usual
"ship it, fix it in QA" option — a visual defect that would be a shrug elsewhere consumes part of a very
small budget. Practically, for you:

- Expect UI PRs to be reviewed against the preview environment **and** Figma, not just the diff.
- Self-review the same way before you open it (§8). It's faster than a review round-trip.
- Where design is missing or contradictory, **flag it** rather than picking something plausible. An
  invented value becomes a defect *and* a design-system divergence — two problems instead of none.

## 2. Before you write any code

Five minutes here saves a day later.

### Run the session start

```bash
/session-start
```

Reads the tracking docs, checks your branch, states where the project is. Do it once per session.

### Confirm your branch

```bash
git branch --show-current
```

`feature/*` or `fix/*`, branched from `develop`. **If it says `develop` or `main`, stop.** No exceptions.

### Check what already exists

| Question | Where to look |
|---|---|
| Does a Base / Override / Custom component already cover this? | `.claude/registry/components.md` |
| Same for hooks, utils, pages, routes | `.claude/registry/{hooks,utils,pages,routes}.md` |
| What's in the base package? | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` |
| Which tier am I about to touch? | Registry `Tier` column, or `/audit-tier <path>` |
| Is another squad the owner? | Registry `Squad` column · `.claude/rules/squad{A,B}.md` |

The registry's **`Origin`** column is the one that matters most:

- **`Custom`** — a Zimmermann component already in `overrides/`. Extend it.
- **`Override`** — a base component already scaffolded into `overrides/`. Edit it directly.
- **`Base`** — it exists upstream but is **not** in `overrides/` yet. **This has a cost.** See below.

### Two component families — and they do different jobs

`overrides/app/components/` holds two kinds of thing. Knowing which you're writing decides the path, the
naming, and whether it affects anything but your own page.

| | `components/<kebab-name>/` | `components/shared/ui/<PascalName>/` |
|---|---|---|
| **What it is** | An override of an SFCC component | A raw Zimmermann primitive — Link, Text, Image, Button |
| **Naming** | Keep SFCC's kebab-case exactly (`product-tile/`) | Mirror upstream's PascalCase (`Button/`) |
| **Does it intercept SFCC?** | **Yes** — base files import these by full package path, so your version replaces theirs everywhere | **No** — see the barrel exception above |
| **Who consumes it** | Every base page that already used it, plus you | Only code that imports it explicitly — chiefly Contentful renderers |
| **Why you'd reach for it** | You want to change how an SFCC component looks or behaves | You want a plain branded primitive with no commerce semantics attached |

The `shared/ui` family exists because **Contentful renderers need primitives, not commerce components.**
Every Contentful component on `develop` already pulls them in — `duplexSection` (`Box`, `Text`),
`collectionHero` (`Box`, `Button`, `Heading`, `Text`), `hotspotPopup` (`Box`, `Image`, `Link`, `Skeleton`,
`Text`), `imageText`, `heroBanner`, `shoppableImage`. Upstream those resolve to bare Chakra
(`shared/ui/Button/index.jsx` is literally `export {Button} from '@chakra-ui/react'`). A CMS rich-text
renderer mapping a `hyperlink` node to a `Link` wants exactly that — predictable and unopinionated — not a
component carrying SFCC's locale-routing and commerce behaviour.

**Status: the intent is agreed, the wiring is not built.** A `shared/ui/Button` exists on
`feature/pdp-token-class-spike`, its only consumer is the `/dev/components` catalogue page, there is no
`overrides/app/components/shared/ui/index.tsx` barrel, and `collectionHero` still imports `Button` from
the SFCC barrel — so it still gets raw Chakra. Don't build against this family until the barrel question
is settled (see the playbook).

### What's actually overridden today

Worth knowing before you estimate anything: **`overrides/app/components/` currently contains seven
directories.** As of `develop` @ `2dfeb4d`:

```
_app-config   button   contentful   foundation   header   icons   pageContainer
```

That's it. `product-tile`, `display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `footer`,
`list-menu`, `drawer-menu` and `seo` are all still **`Origin = Base`** — they exist upstream and are
referenced throughout `.claude/rules/` and the protected-file lists, but they have **not** been scaffolded
into `overrides/` yet.

Two consequences:

- **Most stories you pick up will pay copy-first** (below). Assume it until the registry says otherwise.
- **When a rules file points at one of those as an example, the file won't be there.** The convention is
  real; the worked example often isn't yet. Check before you go looking.

### If `Origin = Base`, the copy-first rule applies

Before any functional work, AGENTS.md requires:

1. Copy the base file → mirrored path in `overrides/` (keep the kebab-case filename exactly)
2. Convert to TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`), fix imports
3. `npx tsc --noEmit`
4. Add a temporary `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')` marker
5. **Stop.** A human confirms the override is rendering instead of the base
6. Then build; remove the markers

It's serialised and human-gated, and **the first story against a given base component pays it — later
ones don't.** This is the single most common reason a story looks small and isn't. Flag it at refinement,
not on day three of the sprint.

### Sanity-check the scope

```bash
/scope-check
```

Classifies everything you're about to touch by tier and tells you if the change is safe, risky, or
blocked. Worth it any time you're not certain.

## 3. Design Foundations — read this before your first component

**Canonical reference: `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`.** That file is the authority on styling an
override; this section is the orientation for it. If the two ever disagree, the rules file wins — and
this section needs a fix, so raise it.

The design system lives in `overrides/app/theme/`. It has **one** source of truth and derives outward:

```
foundation/  colour.ts · typography.ts · spacing.ts · sizes.ts · motion.ts · gridSystem.ts
        |  imported and derived from — never retyped
foundation/zimmTokens.ts          -> the --zimm-* CSS custom properties
        |  consumed by
theme/components/*.ts (recipes)   ·   globalStyles.ts (.zimm-* classes)
```

`zimmTokens.ts` is **derived**, not a second copy — it imports `colors.grey[900]` rather than retyping
`#191919`. That is why you never edit it directly, and why two values cannot drift apart.
`theme/index.test.tsx` guards the arrangement with 125 tests; a failure there is a real drift signal,
not test noise.

### The styling hierarchy — reach for these in order

This is the load-bearing rule of the whole section.

1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual — `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`
2. **Semantic token strings** — `color="text.default"`, `bg="background.02"`,
   `padding={{ base: 'm', md: 'xl' }}`
3. **The component's own `theme/components/<name>.ts`** for anything that varies by variant / size /
   state. For an interactive component with Chakra support (buttons, inputs, links) that file is the
   **single source of truth**
4. **`sx` prop** for a genuine one-off gap in the Chakra prop system
5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` truly cannot express it (complex pseudo-selectors, keyframes)

**Never** a raw hex / px / rem / em literal in a component file. The one standing exception is
`button.ts`'s provisional constants — trap 2 below.

Registered component recipes today: `Button`, `Header`, `ListMenu` (`theme/components/index.ts`).
Adding a new one is yours to do — one file per Chakra component, registered in that index.

### Setting type — always `textStyle`, never `fontSize`

```tsx
<Text textStyle="body1">…</Text>          // ✅
<Heading textStyle="heading3">…</Heading>  // ✅
<Text fontSize="md">…</Text>               // ❌ never
```

**Why this is a hard rule, not a preference.** Four Zimmermann font-size keys collide with Chakra
defaults, and the base retail-react-app uses those names at ~199 call sites:

| Key | Zimmermann | Chakra |
|---|---|---|
| `md` | 24px | 16px |
| `xs` | 16px | 12px |
| `2xs` | 14px | 10px |
| `3xs` | 12px | 7.2px |

The Zimmermann font scale is **deliberately not registered** as `theme.fontSizes` for exactly this
reason. If you write `fontSize="md"` expecting 24px you get 16px. If you "fix" that by registering the
scale, you silently restyle every base component on the site. There's a test guarding against it —
don't fight it, use `textStyle`.

**The 22 available text styles:**

`heading1Strong` `heading1` `heading2` `heading3` · `body1Strong` `body1` `body2Strong` `body2` ·
`mobileBody1Strong` `mobileBody1` `mobileBody2` · `label` `caption` · `linkLg` `linkSm` ·
`button` `buttonSm` · `productNames` `price` · `navigation` · `footer` · `serif`

Browse them rendered in Storybook under **Foundation → Typography**.

### Colour — use the semantic aliases

```tsx
<Box bg="background.01" color="text.default" borderColor="border.default" />   // ✅
<Box bg="#f9f8f6" color="#191919" />                                          // ❌
```

Two layers exist. Reach for the **semantic** layer; the primitives are what the semantics are built from.

| Group | Keys |
|---|---|
| `text.*` | `default` `inverse` `inverseGrey` `secondary` `muted` |
| `background.*` | `01`–`07` (`01`–`04` light/ivory, `05`–`06` dark, `07` white) |
| `border.*` | `default` `secondary` `focus` `forms` `error` |
| `status.*` | `success` `error` `errorBackground` `storeClosed` |
| `link.*` · `icon.*` | `default` `hover` · `default` |
| `action.primary.*` | `bgDefault` `bgHover` `bgPressed` `bgDisabled` `bgFocused` `text` `textDisabled` |
| `action.secondary.*` | `border` `bgHover` `text` `textInverse` `textDisabled` |
| Primitives | `grey.{black,900,800,700,600,500,300,200,100,white}` `ivory.{100..400}` `coral/green/orange/red.500` `opacity.{15,30,40,50}` |

Browse under **Foundation → Colour**.

### Spacing

Both scales work — Chakra's numerics are preserved and the Zimmermann named scale is added on top.
**Prefer the named scale**, since it's what the design system speaks:

```tsx
<Box padding="m" marginBottom="xl" />   // ✅ 1rem, 1.5rem
<Box padding={4} />                      // works, but not the design vocabulary
```

`3xs` 0.125 · `2xs` 0.25 · `xs` 0.5 · `s` 0.75 · `m` 1 · `l` 1.25 · `xl` 1.5 · `2xl` 2 · `3xl` 2.5 ·
`4xl` 4 · `5xl` 5 · `6xl` 8 · `7xl` 10 — **in `rem`**, i.e. 2/4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40/64/80/128/160px at
the default 16px root font-size.

**The scale is `rem`, not `px`** — spacing and type scale with the user's root font-size and browser
zoom (WCAG 1.4.4). Hairline geometry deliberately does not:

- `borderWidth="default"` → `1px`, registered as a Chakra scale
- `focusRingOffsets.{default, secondary}` → `2px` / `3px`, imported as a constant from
  `app/theme/foundation` (`secondary` exists to clear the secondary button's 1px border)

**Unit rule:** `rem` for anything that should scale (type, spacing) · `px` only for hairline geometry
(border widths, focus-ring offsets) · `em` only for breakpoints. Never a raw literal of any unit in a
component file.

⚠️ **Don't use the `--zimm-scale-NNN` numeric aliases in JSX.** You'll see them in `zimmTokens.ts`
(`--zimm-scale-500`, `--zimm-scale-1100`, …). They exist **only** so the `.zimm-*` global classes have
something to reference. The named scale is the Chakra-facing surface:

```tsx
<Box mb="var(--zimm-scale-500)" />   // ❌ 20px, but bypasses the scale
<Box mb="l" />                        // ✅ same 20px, traceable to the token
```

If the value you need has no named entry — 28px and 44px are both in use with nothing between `xl` (24)
and `2xl` (32), or `3xl` (40) and `4xl` (64) — that's a **token gap to raise** (§7), not a reason to reach
for the numeric alias.

### Icon sizes, action sizes and motion are NOT theme tokens

These collide with Chakra scales too (`theme.sizes.lg` is 32rem and backs `w`/`h`/`boxSize` everywhere),
so they're **imported as constants** instead:

```tsx
import { iconSizes, actionSizes, motion } from 'app/theme/foundation';

<Icon boxSize={iconSizes.lg} />                                    // 20px
<Button height={actionSizes.height.lg} />                          // 52px
transition: `opacity ${motion.duration.fast} ${motion.easing.standard}`
```

`iconSizes` — `lg` 20 · `md` 16 · `sm` 12
`actionSizes` — `height.{lg:52, md:40}` · `paddingX.{lg:32, md:20}` · `gap:16`
`motion` — `duration.{fast:200ms, default:300ms, slow:500ms}` · `easing.{standard, slides, fades}`

⚠️ **Motion values are PROVISIONAL** and pending designer sign-off. Use them, but expect them to move.

### The `.zimm-*` global classes — and the one rule about them

**27** global classes exist: `.zimm-text-*` (typography), `.zimm-form-*` (form-field layout),
`.zimm-grid`, `.zimm-focus-visible`. They mirror the design system as static CSS so handover markup can
be pasted and look right. They are **not** the preferred authoring route for new Zimmermann components —
default to the hierarchy above.

**There are no `.zimm-btn-*` classes, and there must never be.** The whole family was deleted
deliberately, and the reason generalises:

> **One canonical styling surface per component type.** If a component has interactive state, its
> `theme/components/<name>.ts` recipe is the only place its look is defined. A static CSS class cannot
> express `_hover` / `_active` / `_disabled` / `_focusVisible`, so a class "mirror" of a recipe is
> structurally incomplete from birth — and nothing stops the two drifting apart afterwards.

So: **every button is Chakra's `<Button>` styled by `theme/components/button.ts`.** Never a class, never
a hand-rolled `<button>` with its own styles. `.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool only for genuinely
static, non-interactive, heavily-reused treatments — typography, the grid, form-field layout.

⚠️ Worth knowing: `globalStyles.ts` has almost no consumers today (one Storybook demo uses `.zimm-grid`)
and it ships on every page. Don't reach for a class where a prop or a recipe will do.

### Interaction state goes in CSS, never in React state

This is the rule most likely to cost you a rewrite, so it's worth being blunt about.

Hover, press, focus and disabled belong in the component's theme recipe as Chakra's pseudo-props. They do
**not** belong in `useState`.

```tsx
// ❌ never — interaction state in React
const [hovered, setHovered] = useState(false)
<button onMouseEnter={() => setHovered(true)} style={{background: hovered ? a : b}}>

// ✅ theme/components/myThing.ts — the browser does the work
_hover:        { bg: 'var(--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-hover)' },
_active:       { bg: 'var(--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-pressed)' },
_disabled:     { bg: 'var(--zimm-color-border-secondary)', cursor: 'not-allowed' },
_focusVisible: { outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)', outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)' },
```

It looks identical in a screenshot. It behaves differently in five ways that all matter here:

| JS state | CSS pseudo-class |
|---|---|
| Dead until hydration — the button renders but doesn't respond | Works on first paint, no JS needed |
| No way to express `@media (hover: hover)` → sticky hover on touch after a tap | Opts out on touch devices properly |
| Inline styles win every specificity fight — the theme **cannot** override them | Overridable by variant, later |
| The keyboard focus ring built for WCAG 2.4.7 lives in the recipe, so it never applies | Inherited automatically |
| Every hover re-renders the component | No React work at all |

With a ≤2s p75 mobile LCP budget and a WCAG 2.2 AA target, the first and fourth rows are the ones that
turn into defects.

**Corollary — a theme recipe nothing consumes is dead code.** If you write
`theme/components/myThing.ts` and register it, the component has to actually read it — Chakra's
`<Button>`/`<Link>` etc. do so automatically; a custom multipart component needs
`useStyleConfig('MyThing')`. A registered-but-unread recipe looks like compliance and changes nothing.

### Adding a new token

**You don't.** `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` is Tier 1 and designer-owned (Hard Rule #3). If Figma
has a value with no token, that's a §7 escalation, not a local addition. Same for
`theme/globalStyles.ts` (Tier 2, needs a named owner's nod).

Per-component theme overrides in `theme/components/` **are** yours to add — one file per Chakra
component, registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.

## 4. The build sequence

Four steps, in order. This is the agreed approach.

### Step 1 — Does it already exist?

§2. Check the registry and the base package. Report what you found in the PR description, even when the
answer is "nothing" — that's the evidence the ladder was walked.

### Step 2 — Use as-is, override/extend, or build custom?

| Verdict | When | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| **Use as-is** | Base behaviour and markup are right; only styling differs | Style it via `theme/components/<name>.ts`. No component file at all |
| **Override / extend** | Base structure is right, behaviour or markup needs changing | Copy-first (§2), then modify. **Minimal changes** — don't remove base functionality you weren't asked to touch |
| **Build custom** | Nothing upstream is close | `/new-component` scaffolds it. Justify the call in the PR |

Most work should land in the first two columns. If you're reaching for "custom" often, raise it — either
the ladder isn't being walked or there's a real gap worth naming.

**If SFCC's own components import the thing you're overriding, use the bridge pattern.** Check first:

```bash
grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" \
  node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/
```

Any hits mean base components depend on it, so its **default export must stay a faithful, undecorated
port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour. Put Zimmermann-only styling behind a
**named export** that wraps the default. Get this wrong and you restyle or break base cart / checkout /
account screens you never opened.

Where the brand difference is purely token-driven you don't need the split at all — put it in
`theme/components/<name>.ts` instead, and leave the default export untouched.

⚠️ **No worked precedent exists in the repo yet.** `overrideStyling.md` describes this pattern using
`product-tile` (`CardBaseline` + faithful default), `link`, `image-gallery`, `display-price` and
`swatch-group` — **none of which are overrides on `develop` today.** The pattern is the agreed approach;
you may well be the one who establishes the first example of it. If you are, say so in the PR so the rule
file can be updated to point at something real.

### Step 3 — Execute the swap / override / build

Component folder layout (`.claude/rules/conventions.md`):

```
overrides/app/components/productTile/
  index.tsx            ← the component (named export matching the folder)
  index.stories.tsx    ← mandatory
  index.test.ts        ← only if logic-heavy
  types.ts             ← only if props are shared with siblings
  productTile.scss     ← only if Chakra props genuinely can't express it
```

- **Zimmermann-authored files:** `camelCase` (`productTile.tsx`)
- **Override files mirroring a base file:** keep the original kebab-case exactly (`product-tile.tsx`)
- **TypeScript only inside `overrides/`.** No `.js`/`.jsx`, including stories and config
- Named export matches the folder; props type is `<ComponentName>Props`
- Callbacks are `onEventName`; required props non-optional, optional props use `?`
- Australian spelling in Zimmermann-authored code (`colour`, `centre`) — override files keep upstream
  spelling verbatim
- No magic numbers or strings — name the constant
- JSDoc required on anything with ≥2 callers and on every exported hook

**Split it up when:** the component passes ~150 lines, branches heavily, or accumulates ≥2 related
`useState` calls (→ extract a hook in `overrides/app/hooks/use<Component><Feature>.ts`).

### Step 4 — Apply the design styles

§3. Chakra props first, tokens always, `textStyle` for type. Then check it against Figma at the
breakpoints the design defines, and raise what doesn't line up.

## 5. Storybook — non-negotiable, and your build surface

Every component exported from its folder needs a `*.stories.tsx`. Internal sub-components that only
render inside one parent don't — cover their variants through the parent.

Build **in** Storybook rather than building and then adding a story. It's the fastest loop you have,
and it's the only place a reviewer can see every state at once.

```bash
npm run storybook
```

**Categorisation** (drives the sidebar; pick the first that matches):

| Category | What goes here |
|---|---|
| `Foundation/` | Design tokens — Colour, Typography, Spacing, Icons |
| `Elements/` | Generic building blocks — Button, Input, Badge, Link, Checkbox. *Tiebreaker: usable outside a form?* → `Elements/` |
| `Layout/` | Global chrome and structure — Header, Footer, DrawerMenu, Breadcrumb, Pagination |
| `Commerce/` | Commerce-specific shared — ProductTile, OrderSummary, PromoCode, DisplayPrice |
| `Forms/` | Composed form assemblies — AddressForm, NewsletterSignup |
| `Pages/` | Full page assemblies |
| `Contentful/` | CMS-driven — use mock Contentful data so variants are visible without a live CMS |

```ts
export default { title: 'Commerce/ProductTile' };   // ✅
export default { title: 'Elements/DisplayPrice' };  // ❌ commerce-specific → Commerce/
```

**Content:** every file has a `Default` export. Add named exports for meaningful states (`Loading`,
`OutOfStock`, `WithDiscount`, `Empty`) — not for every prop permutation. This is where your static-first
data lives.

**`play` functions** only where there's interactive behaviour worth asserting — validation on blur,
disclosure open/close, focus movement. Query through `within(canvasElement)`, prefer `getByRole` with
an accessible name, and import `userEvent` from `@storybook/test` (not `@testing-library/user-event`).

⚠️ **If a component looks wrong in Storybook but right in the app, suspect your imports before your
CSS.** `--zimm-*` variables now resolve correctly in Storybook (§3 trap 1). The likely cause is §3 trap
1b: a base-path import of an already-overridden component renders the *base* SFCC version in Storybook
and Vitest while working fine in the app. Switch it to a relative import.

### Your branch gets a live URL, automatically

Separate from Storybook, and new: every push to a `feature/*` or `fix/*` branch now builds and deploys
itself to its own dedicated MRT environment, then posts the URL as a comment on the PR.

- Created on first push and **reused** on later pushes — one environment per branch, not per commit. The
  comment updates in place rather than piling up.
- **Torn down automatically** when the PR closes or the branch is deleted.
- A real Sydney-hosted (`ap-southeast-2`) storefront with real dev environment variables — not a mock.
- Excluded: `fix/release-*` sub-branches and `hotfix/*`.

Use it for design review, QA sign-off, and anything cross-device. Nobody needs your branch checked out
locally to look at your work, and it's why you should never have to fight over the shared dev target
again.

Storybook is still where you **build** — fastest loop, every state visible at once. The preview
environment is where other people **review**.
