content.text:
# How the fonts plug into the established approach

## The headline: they don't touch the styling layer at all

The token chain **already names Futura Round** and has since PR #53. Trace it:

```
foundation/fonts.ts     FONT_REGULAR = "'Futura Round', 'Futura LT Pro', 'Futura', 'Century Gothic', …"
        ↓                                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^ already first preference
foundation/zimmTokens   --zimm-font-family-body / -heading
        ↓
theme/index.ts          fonts registered as a Chakra scale
        ↓
typography.ts           all 22 textStyles carry fontFamily: FONT_MEDIUM / FONT_REGULAR
        ↓
components              textStyle="footer"  ·  fontFamily: 'var(--zimm-font-family-body)'
```

**Every layer already points at Futura Round by name.** The only thing missing is an `@font-face` telling the browser where to fetch the file. The moment that exists, all five layers start using it — no edits anywhere.

So this isn't a styling change. It's an **asset + one injector**.

## 1 · Where the files go

```
overrides/app/static/fonts/FuturaRound-Regular.woff2   ← weight 400
overrides/app/static/fonts/FuturaRound-Medium.woff2    ← weight 500
```

`overrides/app/static/` already exists (`ico`, `img`, `manifest.json`, …) and is PWA Kit's served asset root. That's where Jersey had them.

**Only two files.** I checked every one of the 22 text styles — they use exactly two weights, `400` and `500`. And `fonts.body === fonts.heading` (identical stacks), so there's no third face to source. That matches the entitlement `frozenFiles.md` records: *"2 fonts: Regular 400, Medium 500."* Han's 28 files are for the f2r viewer; the storefront needs 2.

## 2 · How it's set — follow the `ZimmTokensGlobal` precedent

There's already an established pattern for injecting global CSS, and it exists precisely because of a font problem:

> `zimmTokensGlobal.tsx` — *"Deliberately NOT Chakra's `styles.global`: Chakra's style processor mangles quoted font-family values (verified — `"'Futura Round', 'Century Gothic', sans-serif"` collapses to a single family)… A raw Emotion `<Global>` preserves them."*

So a new sibling module, same shape:

```
overrides/app/theme/fontFace.tsx     ← next to zimmTokensGlobal.tsx
  export const ZimmFontFace = () => <Global styles={fontFaceCss} />
```

Two `@font-face` blocks, `font-display: swap`, weights 400 and 500.

## 3 · How it's consumed — mount it twice, exactly like the tokens

```
overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx   ← beside <ZimmTokensGlobal />
.storybook/preview.tsx                            ← beside <ZimmTokensGlobal />
```

That dual-mount **is** the convention. The token module's own comment says it: *"Kept as one shared definition so the two mount points cannot drift."*

## Two things Jersey's version got wrong — worth not repeating

**① It was mounted in `footer/index.tsx`, not `_app-config`.** `ce2960c` removed the import and render from the footer. A global `@font-face` rendered from a leaf component only applies when that component is on screen, and re-injects on every mount. It belongs at the app root next to the token injector.

**② It had no Storybook mount at all.** His own comment concedes the consequence: *"Falls back to a bare path in environments with neither (e.g. Storybook), where the font 404s silently."* That means the app would render Futura Round while Storybook renders the fallback — precisely the app/Storybook divergence `overrideStyling.md` warns about, and it would have made every visual check we did today unreliable.

## The one genuine obstacle

**Storybook has no `staticDirs` configured** — I checked `.storybook/main.js`. So Storybook cannot serve `overrides/app/static/fonts/` as-is, and the fonts would 404 there.

Fixing that means editing `.storybook/main.js`, which is **Tier 1** (`frozenFiles.md` → Test & Tooling, and AGENTS.md Hard Rule #8). That needs the Integration lead.

Two ways round it:
- **Add `staticDirs`** — the clean fix, one line, but Tier 1 approval
- **Import the `.woff2` in `fontFace.tsx`** so webpack resolves and emits it in both builds — no Storybook config change, but it puts the font in the JS bundle graph, which has a bundle-size implication against your `main.js` ≤ 180 kB budget (~60 kB of font)

I'd go with `staticDirs` and take the Tier 1 ask — it's a genuine test-config change, it's what the config is for, and it keeps the fonts out of the JS bundle.

## Net change

| | |
|---|---|
| `overrides/app/static/fonts/` | +2 `.woff2` |
| `overrides/app/theme/fontFace.tsx` | new, ~25 lines |
| `_app-config/index.tsx` | +2 lines |
| `.storybook/preview.tsx` | +2 lines |
| `.storybook/main.js` | +1 line — **Tier 1** |
| `foundation/fonts.ts` | **no change** |
| Any component or recipe | **no change** |
| `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` | must be amended — **Tier 1 governance** |

The last row is the real gate. That file currently states *"No font binaries in this repo"* as a hard rule with the EULA quoted; shipping fonts while it says that would leave the codebase contradicting its own governance.

Want me to draft the `fontFace.tsx` module and the two mounts so it's ready to land the moment the licence and the Tier 1 approvals are in?

Verified exhaustively across his branch:

| Check | Result |

| `@font-face` anywhere under `overrides/` | **none** — the only hit is the word "@font-face" inside a *comment* in `fonts.ts` |

| `overrides/app/static/fonts/` exists | **no** — only `ico`, `img`, `manifest.json`, `robots.txt`, `translations` |
| `foundation/fonts.ts` vs develop | **byte-identical** (`md5 c42f1b6c…`) |

And that file on his branch still carries the original comment:

> *"Futura Round is not self-hosted — the Monotype licence forbids it, so the fallback is what customers actually render."*

**Han has not implemented fonts in the PWA.** His branch renders the same fallback stack as `develop`.

## What he actually did

He added fonts to a **different project**:

| | Han — `f2r/` | Proposed — PWA |
|---|---|---|
| Location | `f2r/02-design/library/assets/` | `overrides/app/static/fonts/` |
| Project | the f2r design **viewer** (own `package.json`, `server.js`, `vercel.json`) | the storefront |
| Wiring | plain CSS `@font-face` in `f2r/…/tokens/typography.css`, relative `url('../assets/…')` | Emotion `<Global>` module, dual-mounted |
| Files | **28** (14 OTF + 14 WOFF2, incl. Condensed + obliques) | **2** (Regular 400, Medium 500) |
| Consumed by | static HTML prototypes in the design library | Chakra `textStyle` / `--zimm-font-family-*` |
| Asset URL resolution | none needed — relative paths, static hosting | needs PWA Kit's bundle-prefixed path |
| Reaches customers | no | yes |

His `typography.css` is hand-written CSS for statically-served prototypes. That's the correct approach **for that context** — no build system, no Chakra, no SSR, no bundle path. It simply doesn't transfer to the PWA.

## What this means practically

**Three separate decisions, not one:**

1. **f2r viewer** — already done by Han, and it's the one with live exposure: `f2r/vercel.json` rewrites `/library/:path*` to the directory holding the fonts, so if that deployment is up, they're already being served publicly.
2. **The PWA** — nothing exists. Jersey's attempt was added and removed inside SFCC-55, and it had the two flaws I flagged (mounted in the footer, no Storybook mount).
3. **Governance** — `frozenFiles.md` states "No font binaries in this repo" as a Tier 1 rule. Han's commit already contradicts it on his branch (his `3779628` deleted the `.gitignore` line that cited the EULA), and merging his branch would land that contradiction on `develop`.

So when you and Han and Tim agreed to bring the fonts back, **the PWA side is still entirely unbuilt.** Han's work doesn't give you a pattern to copy — it solves a static-hosting problem, not a PWA Kit one. The approach I outlined is new work either way.

One thing worth raising with Han when you next speak: whether the **f2r Vercel deployment is public**, since that's live server distribution today and it's the piece most likely to matter to whoever reviews the licence.

content.text:
# Feasibility check — self-hosting Futura Round

**Verdict: technically feasible, low risk, and most of the plumbing already exists.** One Tier 1 blocker, one governance blocker, one performance decision.

---

## ✅ What already works — no change needed

**1 · CSP permits it.** This is the thing that usually kills self-hosted fonts, and it's clear:

```
helmet 4.6.0 default:   font-src: ['self', 'https:', 'data:']
our contentSecurityPolicy.ts:  no font-src override → default applies
```

Same-origin **and** any https CDN are allowed. **No Tier 1 change to `contentSecurityPolicy.ts` required** — which matters, because `overrides/app/ssr/` is Tier 1 and the CSP file is flagged *"wrong change = security hole on every page."* We don't have to touch it.

**2 · The static pipeline already carries the whole directory.**

```
overrides/app/static/ :  ico img manifest.json robots.txt translations
build/static/         :  ico img manifest.json robots.txt translations  + pd-design-styles.css
```

The base and override `static/` dirs are **merged into `build/static/` automatically**. Dropping in `fonts/` needs no `ssr.js` change — the two `serveStaticFile` lines there are only root-path aliases (`/robots.txt`, `/favicon.ico`), not the general mechanism.

**3 · There's an exact precedent for the delivery pattern.** SFCC's own `page-designer-init` does this:

```js
link.href = getAssetUrl('static/pd-design-styles.css')
```

A static CSS asset resolved through `getAssetUrl` and injected at runtime — the same shape a font-face injector needs.

**4 · `getAssetUrl` is already typed on `develop`** (`vendor.d.ts:67`), so no ambient-types work.

**5 · Zero bundle-budget impact.** Files in `static/` are copied, not bundled — they never enter `main.js` (180 kB) or `vendor.js` (550 kB). *Provided* we use the static dir rather than `import`ing the `.woff2` in JS, which would pull ~60 kB into the graph.

---

## ⚠️ Blockers and decisions

### Blocker 1 — Storybook `staticDirs` · **Tier 1**

`.storybook/main.js` has **no `staticDirs`**, so Storybook can't serve `overrides/app/static/`. Without it the fonts 404 there and Storybook renders the fallback while the app renders Futura Round — the exact app/Storybook divergence that would have invalidated every visual comparison we did today.

One line, but `.storybook/` is Tier 1 (`frozenFiles.md` → Test & Tooling; AGENTS.md Hard Rule #8). **Integration lead approval.**

### Blocker 2 — `frozenFiles.md` · **Tier 1 governance**

It currently states *"No font binaries in this repo"* as a hard rule with the EULA quoted verbatim. Shipping fonts while that stands leaves the codebase contradicting its own governance. Amendment needs **both squad leads + the Integration lead.**

### Decision — LCP

Your budget is **≤2s p75 mobile**, and text is almost certainly your LCP element.

- `font-display: swap` → no render block, but a visible FOUT as text reflows from Futura → Futura Round. Given every label measures ~13% narrower in Futura Round, that reflow will be **noticeable**, not subtle.
- Two files ≈ 60 kB total.
- **Preload** (`<link rel="preload" as="font" crossorigin>`) removes most of the FOUT but adds 60 kB to the critical path.

My read: **preload the 400 weight only** (body text, the LCP candidate), let 500 swap in. That's ~30 kB critical rather than 60.

---

## What I could *not* verify

- **Whether MRT serves `build/static/` from the app origin or a separate CDN origin.** Either is CSP-allowed (`'self'` or `https:`), so it doesn't change feasibility — but it affects whether `crossorigin` is required on the preload, and font requests need CORS when cross-origin. Worth confirming against a real MRT deploy before shipping.
- **Cache headers on static assets in MRT** — fonts should be immutable/long-lived; I can't see MRT's config from here.

---

## Effort

| | |
|---|---|
| Files in | `overrides/app/static/fonts/` — **2** (Regular 400, Medium 500) |
| New module | `overrides/app/theme/fontFace.tsx` (~25 lines, `<Global>` like `zimmTokensGlobal`) |
| Mounts | `_app-config/index.tsx` + `.storybook/preview.tsx` — 2 lines each |
| `.storybook/main.js` | +1 line — **Tier 1** |
| `frozenFiles.md` | amendment — **Tier 1 governance** |
| `foundation/fonts.ts`, recipes, components | **no change** |

**The code is roughly an hour. The two Tier 1 approvals and the licence are the actual path length.**

One practical note: because `ce2960c` is on *this* branch, `git revert ce2960c` recovers both `.woff2` and the injector verbatim — then it's fixing Jersey's two mistakes (mounted in the footer instead of `_app-config`; no Storybook mount) rather than writing it fresh.

Want me to prepare that revert plus the corrected wiring on a separate branch, so it's ready to go the moment the approvals land?

## In essence: the code is the easy part. It's ~1 hour of work, and almost none of it is styling.

**The system is already built for this.** `foundation/fonts.ts` has named `'Futura Round'` as first preference since PR #53, and every layer downstream — `zimmTokens`, the 22 textStyles, every recipe, every component — already resolves through it. Nothing in the styling chain changes. You're adding two files and one `@font-face` declaration that tells the browser where to fetch them. Everything else starts working on its own.

**The three things that usually make this hard are all already handled:**

- **CSP** — helmet's default `font-src: 'self' https: data:` applies; no override needed, so we never touch the Tier 1 CSP file
- **Asset pipeline** — `overrides/app/static/` already merges into `build/static/`; drop `fonts/` in and it ships
- **Precedent** — SFCC's own `page-designer-init` already loads a static CSS asset via `getAssetUrl`, which is the exact pattern

And because the removal commit lives on *this* branch, `git revert ce2960c` gets the files and the injector back verbatim.

## What's actually in the way — none of it technical

| | |
|---|---|
| **The licence** | Yours to sort; everything else waits on it |
| **`.storybook/main.js` staticDirs** | 1 line, **Tier 1** — Integration lead |
| **`frozenFiles.md`** | Says *"No font binaries in this repo"* today; **Tier 1 governance** — both squad leads + Integration lead |

The path length is approvals, not engineering.

## One real judgement call

**FOUT will be visible.** Every label measures ~13% narrower in Futura Round than the fallback we're rendering — that's the same 1.13× we measured all over the footer today. So the swap won't be a subtle weight shift; text will visibly reflow. Preloading the 400 weight (~30 kB) removes most of it on the LCP path. That's a decision for you and Tim against the ≤2s budget, not a blocker.

## One thing I couldn't verify from here

Whether MRT serves `build/static/` from the app origin or a separate CDN origin. Either passes CSP, but cross-origin fonts need CORS and a `crossorigin` attribute on the preload. **Worth a 5-minute check against a real MRT deploy before shipping** — it's the kind of thing that works locally and 404s (or silently falls back) in production.

## Net

Green, with a caveat that's organisational rather than technical. And a genuine upside worth naming: **it closes several of today's open findings at once** — the tablet subscribe↔sitemap gap, the mobile "Book an Appointment" wrap, the legal-row drift, and the nav column widths all converge when the real font metrics land. Those stop being declarations and start being fixed.

# Tier 1 — Frozen Files

These files must not be modified by Claude Code without the developer explicitly naming the file
in the prompt AND confirming they have spoken to the listed owner. No exceptions.

> **Note:** this is a slim overrides project on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 — paths
> below reference `overrides/app/...` (the customisation surface) rather than the upstream
> monorepo `packages/template-retail-react-app/app/...` path.

## Design System (Owner: UI Designer — #design-system)

The whole `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` folder is Tier 1. Currently present:

```text
overrides/app/theme/index.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/index.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/fonts.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/spacing.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/motion.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/sizes.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts
```

**No font binaries in this repo.** Futura Round ships under a Monotype *"Font Software For
Desktop End User License Agreement"* which forbids "further distribute the Font Software, or
any copy thereof" and "Install the Font Software on any server or in any digital asset
management system" — so `.woff2`/`.otf` must not be committed here or served from the MRT CDN.
Licence: Zimmermann-Handover repo, `02-design/library/assets/Font Futura WOFF2/Licenses/2275/`.
Type renders from the fallback stack in `foundation/fonts.ts`. Self-hosting needs Zimmermann's
own Monotype Web Page Content entitlement (2 fonts: Regular 400, Medium 500).

Per-component theme overrides live in `overrides/app/theme/components/` and are
**Tier 2** — see [protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md). `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`
is also **Tier 2** — it composes the `.zimm-*` global class registry from the `--zimm-*`
variables defined in `foundation/zimmTokens.ts`, so it is derived styling rather than a
brand token source, but it emits CSS on every page and therefore needs a named owner.

## Commerce SDK Hooks (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
overrides/app/hooks/use-current-basket.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-current-customer.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-einstein.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-datacloud.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-refresh-token.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-navigation.ts
```

Note: `commerce-sdk-react` is consumed from `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/` —
it is not in this repo and cannot be modified here. The hooks above are the overrides surface.

## Runtime & Integration Config (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
config/                              ← entire directory (default.js, sites.js, sit.js, dev.js, utils.js)
overrides/app/ssr.js
overrides/app/ssr/                   ← SSR helper modules split from ssr.js in refactor 610020e:
                                         connectionPools.ts  — undici pool isolation (blast-radius mitigation)
                                         contentSecurityPolicy.ts  — CSP headers; wrong change = security hole on every page
                                         slasTokens.ts  — SLAS auth token handling; wrong change = broken auth site-wide
                                         paymentMetadata.ts  — payment method metadata SSR (checkout pages)
                                         marketingCloud.ts  — MC client-credentials token exchange
worker/main.js
package.json (root)
mobify.config.js
overrides/app/config/countries.ts
overrides/app/config/contentful.ts   ← gates preview/draft content; removing the server-side check exposes drafts on production
```

**`overrides/app/request-processor.js` — add here when populated.**
Currently the Salesforce example stub. Once Zimmermann's geo-redirect and storefront-routing logic lands here it runs on every single request — it will be one of the highest-blast-radius files in the repo. Add it to this section before that work begins.

## Build Pipeline (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

Path aliases are configured in four places that must stay in sync (see architecture.md §Path Aliases).
Breaking either file silently breaks every `app/` and `~` import across the codebase.

```text
babel.config.js    ← path aliases for npm start dev server + production build
tsconfig.json      ← path aliases for TypeScript / VS Code intellisense; also enforces strict mode
```

## Consent (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
Didomi / consent configuration (paths TBD — add when introduced)
```

## Test & Tooling Config (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

Mirrors AGENTS.md hard rule 8 — test config drift breaks every contributor's harness.

```text
vitest.config.*
vitest.setup.ts       ← test environment setup; complements vitest.config.*
playwright.config.*
.storybook/
lighthouserc.js
.browserstack.yml     ← must target e2e/tests/zimm only; scope change = CI cost explosion + upstream test failures
```

## CI/CD Pipeline (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
.github/workflows/
```

## Governance (Owner: Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead — #dev-team)

```text
AGENTS.md
CLAUDE.md
CODEOWNERS
.claude/rules/
.claude/settings.json
coderabbit.yaml              ← AI PR review config; weakening it removes Tier 1 change detection and commit-format enforcement
.coderabbit/                 ← ast-grep rule content coderabbit.yaml points at; weakening/deleting a rule here silently removes that check with no signal in coderabbit.yaml itself
semgrep.yml                  ← semgrep rule content (payment-credential-logging, XSS); same silent-weakening risk as .coderabbit/
scripts/hooks/pre-commit     ← enforces Contentful drift check and blocks direct edits to derived AI config files
scripts/hooks/commit-msg     ← enforces conventional commits; /generate-changelog depends on this
```

content.text:
# Fonts are live — and several of today's findings resolved themselves

`tsc` 0 · `eslint` 0/0 · `prettier` clean · `vitest` 167.

## What the real font fixed automatically

| Finding from earlier today | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| **Mobile "Book an Appointment" wraps** (402px) | ❌ wrapped | ✅ **fixed** — only ACK wraps, as designed |
| **18px horizontal overflow at 768px** | ❌ present | ✅ **gone** |
| Contact column width (1023/1440) | 153 | **135** — Figma: 139 |
| Help column width | 120 | **106** — Figma: **106** ✅ exact |
| Label widths | ~1.13× wide | **at or near parity** |

Two labels now measure **pixel-exact** to Figma (`ORDERS & SHIPPING` 106, `OUR STORY` 60).

## Still open

**The 768–1000px band is unchanged** — columns still squeeze to 126/91/71, 7 labels wrap, `legalH` 45. That was never font-driven; it's the `BP.tablet = 768` switch adopting a layout that needs ~1023px. Option D remains the fix, still discarded per your call.

**The subscribe↔sitemap gap at tablet** improved from 30px to **62px** (site map now starts at x=422 vs 390). Figma is 100px. The remaining 38px is the About column at 160 vs Figma's 118 — the column-cap-vs-per-item-constraint question that's already on the Kiera list.

## Two things to flag

**1 · The 160px nav cap may now be too generous.** With real metrics, `BOOK AN APPOINTMENT` is 131px (was 149). The safe window I calculated was `[155, 212)` under the fallback font; under Futura Round it's roughly `[135, 190)`. **160 still works** — I verified ACK wraps and nothing else does at every breakpoint — but a lower cap would now bring About closer to Figma's 118. Worth revisiting with Kiera rather than changing blind.

**2 · Restart the dev server.** `document.fonts` shows four entries — two `loaded` (correct, bundle-prefixed) and two `error` (stale bare-path rules from the pre-fix HMR state). The SSR HTML is clean; it's client-side leftovers. A restart clears it. **You'll need to do that** — I don't run `npm start`.

## The bug I hit and fixed along the way

The original approach loaded `getAssetUrl` via an async dynamic import, but the `css` template is evaluated at **module-init** — so it could never populate in time. Every URL lost its bundle prefix, hit the SPA catch-all, and got served **HTML instead of a font** (278 KB, magic `<!do`). Silent: 200 response, `font-display: swap`, straight to the fallback.

Fixed by importing `@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime/utils/ssr-namespace-paths` **statically** — it's dependency-free, so it carries none of the `ssr-config` → cosmiconfig → fs weight that motivated the dynamic import, and it resolves in one tick. `vendor.d.ts` gained one line (`bundleBasePath`).

---

**Files changed:** `static/fonts/` (+2 binaries) · `theme/fontFace.tsx` (new) · `_app-config/index.tsx` · `.storybook/preview.tsx` · `.storybook/main.js` *(Tier 1)* · `frozenFiles.md` *(Tier 1)* · `types/vendor.d.ts`. No personal names anywhere; no licence text in `frozenFiles.md`.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
## 1. Primary Request and Intent

The user is **Marcel Navarro, FED Lead** on the Zimmermann PWA Kit project (luxury Australian fashion storefront on Salesforce Commerce Cloud), working on **PR #55 / branch `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui`**. Across this session the explicit requests were, in order:

1. **Locale button** — understand Option A's implications, then "leave it as is" (accepting the WCAG 2.5.3 exposure), later "no - disregard it" when `aria-disabled` restoration was proposed
2. **Fix #12** (dead placeholder plumbing) before #11 — execute Option 3 (`PendingSignup` type), then 12c (stale comment)
3. **Local-token system feasibility** — Tim's idea for tracking designer-dependency tokens; then "run an in-depth audit and inventory check into the currently implemented provisional tokens"
4. **Write the audit to `/Desktop/provisional-token-audit.md`**
5. **Track 1 execution** — z-index defect, `BP.tablet` dedupe, unit comments, Tier 1 newline revert
6. **Fix #13** (preview vs Figma), F6 (fontSize in stories), local CodeRabbit run
7. **Local visual testing** — dev server + Storybook + Figma comparison at set viewports
8. **"full-on testing session"** with 8 V&V items: established approach (PR #56/Tim/Han), FED manual + playbook alignment, tests where needed, no style mirrors/drift, no forced/inline styles, footer up to spec with Figma, pixel-perfect accuracy, local CodeRabbit
9. **Fonts** — new agreement between Marcel, Han and Tim to self-host Futura Round; investigate PR #53 and Han's branch, run feasibility, show diffs with justification, implement

**Standing constraints stated by the user (preserve verbatim):**
- *"the licence must be taken/kept out of the codebase"*
- *"remove anything that mentions jersey, and for #6 remove any mentions of the licence just state that the fonts are being self-hosted for development and testing"*
- "Do not call the AgentTool unless the user requested it"
- "Do not use workflows or deep-research unless the user requested it"
- Branch rules: never operate on `develop` or `main`
- Never run `npm start` (AGENTS.md — dev server is shared; ask the user)
- Commits/pushes/PRs only on explicit request (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #15)
- Four absolute Tier 1 files where the verified-session exception does NOT apply: `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js`

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- **Salesforce PWA Kit v10** with `ccExtensibility` overrides pattern; resolver is webpack-only (Storybook/Vitest don't load it)
- **Chakra UI v2.7.0** — `useMultiStyleConfig`, `useStyleConfig`, `__css`, `sx`, `textStyle`, `defineStyleConfig`, `toCSSVar`
- **The two-scale trap**: `width`/`height`/`boxSize`/`min|maxWidth|Height` resolve through **`theme.sizes`**; `margin`/`padding`/`gap`/`top`-`right`-`bottom`-`left` through **`theme.space`**. The Zimmermann scale is registered as `space` only (`theme/index.ts:56`), deliberately — so a bare key on a sizing prop reads Chakra's defaults (`sizes.xl` = 36rem = 576px)
- **Compound-value trap**: Chakra resolves a token only as the *entire* value. `padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim → browser drops the declaration
- **`extendTheme` deep-merges**: a recipe named `Footer` inherits SFCC's `Footer` rather than replacing it. Colliding part names inherit base properties; a new key you add is appended **last**, so a shorthand can reset a base longhand
- **Token derivation chain**: `foundation/*.ts` → `zimmTokens.ts` → `var(--zimm-*)` → recipes → components
- **`ZimmTokensGlobal` pattern** — raw Emotion `<Global>` (not Chakra `styles.global`, which mangles quoted font-family values), dual-mounted in `_app-config/index.tsx` and `.storybook/preview.tsx`
- **Tier system**: Tier 1 (`foundation/`, `.claude/rules/`, `.storybook/`, `.github/workflows/`), Tier 2 (`theme/components/`, `components/footer|header`, `_app-config/`)
- **Tier 1 verified-session exception** — `gh api user --jq .login` + team/admin check
- **WCAG**: 2.5.3 Label in Name (Level A), 2.4.7 Focus Visible, 2.5.8 Target Size
- **Playwright measurement methodology**: `waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded'` (networkidle never settles on a dev server); programmatic `.focus()` does NOT trigger `:focus-visible`; hydration race drops keystrokes if typing starts too early
- **Figma MCP**: `get_metadata`, `get_screenshot`, `get_variable_defs`

## 3. Files and Code Sections

### `overrides/app/theme/components/footer.ts` (heavily modified)
The footer's multipart recipe. Changes this session:

**Renamed export (fixes the extendTheme merge):**
```ts
export const ZimmFooter = {
  parts: [...33 parts...],
  baseStyle: { ... }
}
```

**`BP` block — imports the foundation breakpoint:**
```ts
import { breakpoints } from '../foundation/gridSystem';

const BP = {
  tablet: breakpoints.md,      // Figma: alias/breakpoint/tablet — 768px
  tabletWide: '53.75em',       // 860px (no foundation equivalent)
  desktop: '64em',             // 1024px (≠ Chakra lg=62em / xl=80em)
} as const;
```

**`contactIconLink` — the 576px bug fix:**
```ts
// MUST be the CSS var, not the bare token key 'xl': Chakra resolves width/height
// through theme.sizes, not theme.space, and Chakra's default sizes.xl is 36rem
// (576px) — which blew each icon up to 576px and destroyed the whole footer layout.
contactIconLink: {
  display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center',
  width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)',
  height: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)',
  color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-inverse)',
},
```

**`modalOverlay` z-index fix:**
```ts
// Chakra zIndices.overlay (1300). Must clear the sticky header, which sets
// zIndex: 'sticky' (1100) in header.ts. The portal target is document.body, so
// this competes in the root stacking context, not the footer's.
zIndex: 'overlay',
```

**`linkCol` — 160px cap:**
```ts
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: {
  width: 'auto',
  maxWidth: 'var(--zimm-scale-7xl)', // 10rem (160px) — see the threshold note above
  flexShrink: 1,
},
```

**`copyright` / `legalLink` — compound shorthand fix:**
```ts
copyright: { textStyle: 'footer', color: '...', whiteSpace: 'nowrap', paddingY: 'xs', paddingX: 0 },
legalLink: { textStyle: 'footer', color: '...', justifyContent: 'flex-start', paddingY: 'xs', paddingX: 0 },
```

**`logo` — inset divider (pseudo-element):**
```ts
logo: {
  padding: `${SPACE_SECTION} var(--zimm-scale-2xl)`,
  display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', justifyContent: 'center', alignItems: 'flex-start',
  position: 'relative',
  _before: {
    content: '""', position: 'absolute', top: 0,
    left: 'var(--zimm-scale-l)', right: 'var(--zimm-scale-l)',
    height: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default)',
    background: COLOUR_HALF_INV,
  },
  [`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: {
    _before: { display: 'none' },
    paddingLeft: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)', paddingRight: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)',
  },
},
```

**`localeText` — padding reset removed:**
```ts
localeText: {
  display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center',
  paddingY: 'xs', paddingX: 0,
  whiteSpace: 'nowrap',
},
```

### `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx`
- `useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmFooter', {})` × 5 call sites
- `PendingSignup` type + `pendingSignupRef` with PII reset:
```ts
type PendingSignup = { email: string; firstName: string; lastName: string };

const handleModalSubmit = (firstName: string, lastName: string) => {
  pendingSignupRef.current = { ...pendingSignupRef.current, firstName, lastName };
  setModalOpen(false);
  setSubmitState('unavailable');
  pendingSignupRef.current = { email: '', firstName: '', lastName: '' };
};
```
- Container/view split (Option 4):
```tsx
export const Footer = ({ data, copyrightYear = ..., ... }: FooterProps) => { ... }  // data REQUIRED

const FooterContainer = (props: Omit<FooterProps, 'data'>) => <Footer data={FOOTER_FIXTURE} {...props} />;
export default FooterContainer;
```
- Icon row moved INSIDE the `<ul>` as last `<li>`; Contact items keep `paddingLeft: '2xs'` per user override

### `overrides/app/theme/components/zimmNavItem.ts`
```ts
minHeight: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 1.5rem (24px) — Figma: h-[24px]
whiteSpace: 'normal',
```
(was `height` + `nowrap`; change removed the inline `style` prop from 13 nav links)

### `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` (NEW, 136 lines)
Three mutation-verified guards:
```ts
test('no sizing property uses a bare spacing-scale key', ...)
test('no compound shorthand contains a bare scale key', ...)
test('no recipe silently inherits a base SFCC recipe of the same name', () => {
  const INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu'];

```

### `overrides/app/theme/fontFace.tsx` (NEW)
```tsx
import { bundleBasePath, getEnvBasePath } from '@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime/utils/ssr-namespace-paths';

const assetRoot = (): string => {
  if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
    const buildOrigin = (window as unknown as { Progressive?: { buildOrigin?: string } }).Progressive?.buildOrigin;
    return buildOrigin ?? '/';
  }
  return `${getEnvBasePath()}${bundleBasePath}/${process.env.BUNDLE_ID || 'development'}/`;
};
const fontUrl = (filename: string): string => `${assetRoot()}static/fonts/${filename}`;

const fontFaceCss = css`
  @font-face { font-family: 'Futura Round'; src: url('${fontUrl('FuturaRound-Regular.woff2')}') format('woff2'); font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-display: swap; }
  @font-face { font-family: 'Futura Round'; src: url('${fontUrl('FuturaRound-Medium.woff2')}') format('woff2'); font-weight: 500; font-style: normal; font-display: swap; }
`;

export function ZimmFontFace(): React.ReactElement { return <Global styles={fontFaceCss} />; }
```

- `overrides/app/static/fonts/FuturaRound-{Regular,Medium}.woff2` restored from `ce2960c^`

29 findings in buckets A–E. Key: only ~7 of 29 are true "missing token, value confirmed".

### `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Desktop/fedBuild-manual.md` (901 → 987 lines)
Added `#### The trap: a spacing token key on a sizing prop` (§3), `### Naming a recipe — extendTheme MERGES, it does not replace` (§3), and "six things" → "eight things".

## 4. Errors and Fixes

1. **`width: 'xl'` → 576px icons** — resolved through `theme.sizes` not `theme.space`. Fixed with `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`. Repo-wide sweep found only these 2 lines.

2. **`extendTheme` merge collision** — our `Footer` inherited SFCC's. Fixed by renaming to `ZimmFooter`. Verified: `copyright` 14px→10px, stray `margin-bottom: space-6` gone, `subscribeHeading` gap 0→24px.

# Tier 1 — Frozen Files

These files must not be modified by Claude Code without the developer explicitly naming the file
in the prompt AND confirming they have spoken to the listed owner. No exceptions.

> **Note:** this is a slim overrides project on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 — paths
> below reference `overrides/app/...` (the customisation surface) rather than the upstream
> monorepo `packages/template-retail-react-app/app/...` path.

## Design System (Owner: UI Designer — #design-system)

The whole `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` folder is Tier 1. Currently present:

```text
overrides/app/theme/index.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/index.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/fonts.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/spacing.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/motion.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/sizes.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts
```

**Fonts are self-hosted for development and testing.** `overrides/app/static/fonts/` holds two
Futura Round faces — Regular 400 and Medium 500 — declared by
`overrides/app/theme/fontFace.tsx` and mounted in both `_app-config/index.tsx` and
`.storybook/preview.tsx`. Only two faces exist because only two are used: all 22 textStyles
resolve to fontWeight 400 or 500, and `fonts.body === fonts.heading`.

`foundation/fonts.ts` already lists `'Futura Round'` first in both stacks, so the `@font-face`
declaration is the only thing that makes it resolve — no component, recipe or token changes.
The fallback stack renders roughly 13% wider, which is why serving the real faces matters for
design-parity review against Figma.

Per-component theme overrides live in `overrides/app/theme/components/` and are
**Tier 2** — see [protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md). `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`
is also **Tier 2** — it composes the `.zimm-*` global class registry from the `--zimm-*`
variables defined in `foundation/zimmTokens.ts`, so it is derived styling rather than a
brand token source, but it emits CSS on every page and therefore needs a named owner.

## Commerce SDK Hooks (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
overrides/app/hooks/use-current-basket.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-current-customer.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-einstein.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-datacloud.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-refresh-token.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-navigation.ts
```

Note: `commerce-sdk-react` is consumed from `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/` —
it is not in this repo and cannot be modified here. The hooks above are the overrides surface.

## Runtime & Integration Config (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
config/                              ← entire directory (default.js, sites.js, sit.js, dev.js, utils.js)
overrides/app/ssr.js
overrides/app/ssr/                   ← SSR helper modules split from ssr.js in refactor 610020e:
                                         connectionPools.ts  — undici pool isolation (blast-radius mitigation)
                                         contentSecurityPolicy.ts  — CSP headers; wrong change = security hole on every page
                                         slasTokens.ts  — SLAS auth token handling; wrong change = broken auth site-wide
                                         paymentMetadata.ts  — payment method metadata SSR (checkout pages)
                                         marketingCloud.ts  — MC client-credentials token exchange
worker/main.js
package.json (root)
mobify.config.js
overrides/app/config/countries.ts
overrides/app/config/contentful.ts   ← gates preview/draft content; removing the server-side check exposes drafts on production
```

**`overrides/app/request-processor.js` — add here when populated.**
Currently the Salesforce example stub. Once Zimmermann's geo-redirect and storefront-routing logic lands here it runs on every single request — it will be one of the highest-blast-radius files in the repo. Add it to this section before that work begins.

## Build Pipeline (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

Path aliases are configured in four places that must stay in sync (see architecture.md §Path Aliases).
Breaking either file silently breaks every `app/` and `~` import across the codebase.

```text
babel.config.js    ← path aliases for npm start dev server + production build
tsconfig.json      ← path aliases for TypeScript / VS Code intellisense; also enforces strict mode
```

## Consent (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
Didomi / consent configuration (paths TBD — add when introduced)
```

## Test & Tooling Config (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

Mirrors AGENTS.md hard rule 8 — test config drift breaks every contributor's harness.

```text
vitest.config.*
vitest.setup.ts       ← test environment setup; complements vitest.config.*
playwright.config.*
.storybook/
lighthouserc.js
.browserstack.yml     ← must target e2e/tests/zimm only; scope change = CI cost explosion + upstream test failures
```

## CI/CD Pipeline (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
.github/workflows/
```

## Governance (Owner: Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead — #dev-team)

```text
AGENTS.md
CLAUDE.md
CODEOWNERS
.claude/rules/
.claude/settings.json
coderabbit.yaml              ← AI PR review config; weakening it removes Tier 1 change detection and commit-format enforcement
.coderabbit/                 ← ast-grep rule content coderabbit.yaml points at; weakening/deleting a rule here silently removes that check with no signal in coderabbit.yaml itself
semgrep.yml                  ← semgrep rule content (payment-credential-logging, XSS); same silent-weakening risk as .coderabbit/
scripts/hooks/pre-commit     ← enforces Contentful drift check and blocks direct edits to derived AI config files
scripts/hooks/commit-msg     ← enforces conventional commits; /generate-changelog depends on this
```

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md

content.text:
Full suite re-run complete against the restarted server with real fonts. Here's where it landed.

## Phase results

| Phase | Result |
|---|---|
| **0** Gate zero | `tsc` 0 · `prettier` clean · `eslint` 0 errors / 3 known `header` warnings · `vitest` **168** passed |
| **1** Static conformance | 6 findings — all pre-existing and previously triaged; nothing new. Inline `style=` 8→**7**, compound shorthands 3→**2** (both remaining are fully `var()`-based, so valid) |
| **2** Emitted CSS | 336 declarations · 51 `--zimm-*` · 0 undefined vars · **5 flagged, all explained** |
| **3** Runtime | **20/20** — re-run after the CSS change, still 20/20 |
| **4** Figma geometry | Improved; one defect fixed — see below |
| **5** Guards | 3 recipe guards pass; **+1 new test**, mutation-verified |
| **6** CodeRabbit | 3 runs; 2 findings fixed, 1 false positive disproved, 3 need PR replies |

The 5 Phase-2 flags are all accounted for: `SIZE_SUB_BODY_MAX` and `SIZE_COL_SUB` (named provisional constants already in the audit), `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT`, and two — `line-height:1.2`, `outline:2px solid transparent` — that are Chakra's own `Button`/`Input` baseStyles, not ours.

## One real defect found and fixed

The links column was 9px taller than Figma. Cause: `linkListItem` was `display: list-item`, so each 24px `inline-flex` anchor sat in a line box whose 24px strut added descender space — **25.5px measured against the anchor's 24px**. That 1.5px leaked once per row, plus 3px on the wrapped item.

`footer.ts` — `linkListItem: { listStyle: 'none', display: 'flex' }` (+7/-1, with the reasoning in a comment).

```
                 before → after   (Figma)
links       167 → 163   Δ+9 → Δ+5   158
contentRow  279 → 275   Δ+9 → Δ+5   270
footer      493 → 489   Δ+17 → Δ+13 476
logo/bottom bar Δy 9 → 5
```

Verified safe: axe **0 violations / 17 passes** over the footer (wcag2a→2.2aa) — list semantics survived; Phase 3 still 20/20. All three structural paddings stay exact (64/48, 48/48, 24/24).

## Remaining deltas — diagnosed, not guessed

- **subscribe Δ+21** (the largest). Decomposes exactly: heading 18 + **24** + body 36 + **40** + input 45 = 163. Those two gaps — `marginBottom: 'xl'` and `'3xl'` — are the only values in that block with no Figma node annotation, unlike every neighbouring value. That's the thing to check with Kiera.
- **locale Δ+7 / bottomBar Δ+8.** Ours is 30px, Figma is 23px. Figma's value would fail WCAG 2.5.8 (24×24 minimum), so this is a deliberate trade, not drift — worth stating in the PR.
- **links Δ+5.** Residual row rhythm; needs a Figma cross-check of the column's internal spacing to go further.
- **768–860px band** unchanged and still the known weak spot — but now quantified: **no overflow** (the real fonts resolved the old 18px overflow), yet subscribe and nav sit flush at `gap: 0` and 7 labels wrap. 1440/1280/1023/375 all wrap only "Acknowledgement of Country", which is intended.

## CodeRabbit

Two findings I fixed:
- **Registry table corruption** — `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` gained an `escapeCell()` helper (union types like `'button' | 'submit'` were shifting every later column) and explicit `…` truncation instead of a mid-token cut. Note: `prettier --write` on that file produced **804 lines of churn** because it was already unclean on `develop`, so I reverted and re-applied logically only — **19 lines, byte-identical output**.
- **Missing `focused` branch test** in `resolveBorderColour` — added; commenting out the branch fails exactly that test and nothing else.

One I checked and **disproved**: the final run claimed an unescaped pipe on `components.md:87`. It misread two adjacent cells as one. I validated all **208 rows across all registry tables — 0 column-count mismatches**. No change needed; it needs a reply so it stops re-flagging.

Also worth knowing: `--light` samples differently each run — the two `.storybook/` Tier-1 majors appeared in run 1 and not runs 2–3. Treat them as standing, not resolved.

## Needs you

1. **Three PR replies** to draft (AGENTS.md requires one per finding): the `.storybook/` Tier-1 majors (you approved these as tier-1, identity verified via `gh api`), `FOOTER_FIXTURE` in a production path (the container/view split you chose, Contentful being a later sprint), and the pipe false positive.
2. **Kiera:** the subscribe 24/40 gaps, plus the existing list (clear-✕, nav cap, Contact 4px, ~7 token gaps, divider colour).
3. **Recommendation I did *not* apply:** the `<ul>` has no `role="list"`, and `list-style: none` drops list semantics in Safari/VoiceOver. Pre-existing, one attribute, but it's an a11y call and you've been making those — say the word.
4. Still open from before: the header logo regression (`ZimmLogo` lost `{...styles.logo}`, leaving `header.ts`'s `logo` part dead), and the PR description's ~11 declarations.

Nothing committed — 40 files staged-free in your working tree, per Hard Rule #15.

content.text:
Here's the coverage map — what each phase actually proves, and what it can't.

## What each phase tested

| Phase | Method | Scope proven |
|---|---|---|
| **0** Gate zero | `tsc --noEmit`, `prettier --check`, `eslint`, `vitest run` | Compiles, formats, lints, unit tests green across all 40 changed files |
| **1** Static conformance | AST/regex sweep of theme + component source | Authoring discipline: no raw hex/px literals, `textStyle` not `fontSize`, no bare scale key on a sizing prop, no `--zimm-scale-NNN` numerics, inline `style=`/`sx=` count, compound shorthands, no `!important`. Plus: dead recipes, `extendTheme` name collisions, style mirrors duplicating a foundation token, `.zimm-*` classes shadowing an interactive recipe, base-path imports that silently render the unstyled SFCC component in Storybook/Vitest, and 16 typography classes cross-checked against their `textStyle` for drift |
| **2** Emitted CSS | Fetched the real rendered page, parsed every footer rule | Provenance of all 336 declarations — 51 `--zimm-*`, 33 `--chakra-*`, 36 literals matching a token, 226 structural, 0 undefined vars. Catches the case where source *looks* tokenised but Chakra emits something else |
| **3** Runtime | Playwright, 20 assertions | Hover underline (apply + revert), keyboard focus ring, floating label, input value retention, clear button, empty/invalid submit both blocked, modal open + `aria-modal` + focus enters + Escape + focus restored to trigger, overlay z-index clears the sticky header, submit → unavailable with no false success, contact icons not focusable, locale button inert |
| **4** Geometry | Playwright measurement vs Figma | Per-element y/h at 1440, all three structural paddings, plus a responsive sweep at 1440/1280/1023/860/768/375 checking label wrapping and container overflow |
| **5** Guards | `recipeGuards.test.ts` + full suite | The 3 mutation-verified guards still fire (sizing-prop keys, compound shorthands, base-recipe collisions) — these are the regression net for the bugs already fixed this PR |
| **6** Review | CodeRabbit `--light` ×3 | Cross-cutting review against repo guidelines |

Plus two ad-hoc checks: **axe-core** over the footer (0 violations / 17 passes, wcag2a→2.2aa) and **registry table integrity** (208 rows, 0 column mismatches).

## What these phases did *not* test

Worth being explicit, since this is what a reviewer will assume is covered:

- **Production build.** Everything ran against the dev server. This matters specifically for `fontFace.tsx` — `assetRoot()` takes a *different branch* under SSR/production (`getEnvBasePath()` + `BUNDLE_ID`) than the one I verified. That path is unexercised.
- **Storybook.** I didn't run `test-storybook`, so the footer's story `play` functions weren't asserted this session — only the app was.
- **Cross-browser.** Chromium only. No Safari — which is where the `list-style: none` semantics issue I flagged actually bites.
- **Visual regression.** No screenshot diffing; geometry was measured numerically, never compared pixel-wise.
- **E2E.** No Playwright spec exists for the footer under `e2e/tests/zimm` — so no `@SFCC-55`-tagged test runs in the PR gate.
- **Multi-site.** en-AU on the homepage only. Not the other 7 storefronts, 11 locales, or any other page.
- **Live data.** Footer content is fixture-backed; the Contentful path is untested by design (later sprint).
- **Performance.** No LCP, bundle-size, or Lighthouse run — and this PR *adds two font files*, which is exactly the kind of change that budget exists to catch.
- **Manual a11y.** axe is automated only — no screen reader pass.

Of those, the two I'd actually act on before merge are the **production font path** (a wrong `assetRoot()` branch means the fallback font ships silently) and a **bundle-size check** on the fonts.

content.text:
Two corrections to what I told you, then the actual breakdown.

**The "8→7" was a within-session delta, not progress against the baseline.** Against `develop` the count is **0 → 7** — every one of those `ui-kits/` files is added by this PR (`A` in the diff), so there was nothing to improve on. I shouldn't have framed it as a reduction.

**The check** is `/\sstyle=\{/` — inline `style` isn't even on the styling ladder (`sx` is rung 4, scoped `.scss` rung 5); it bypasses tokens, theme resolution, and interactive states entirely.

## The 7, grouped

**Prop forwarding — 5.** Not authored styles:

```
zimmNavItem:45   <chakra.a … style={style}>
zimmNavItem:59   <chakra.button … style={style}>
zimmButton:52    <IconButton … style={style}>
zimmButton:70    <ChakraButton … style={style}>
zimmTextInput:73 <chakra.div __css={styles.root} style={style}>
```

Each atom declares `style?: CSSProperties` in its public props and passes it through. The regex can't tell "I hardcoded a value here" from "I'm forwarding the caller's." Nothing is bypassed *at these lines*.

**One genuine inline literal — 1.** `zimmLogo:32` authors `maxWidth: '327px'`, `height: '39px'` (both flagged provisional) then spreads `...style`. The reason it uses `style` at all is sound and documented: it's a raw `<svg>`, not a Chakra component, so `__css` isn't available.

**One incidental match — 1.** `zimmInputAction:60` matched on its `style={style}` forward; the `__css={{ display: 'block', width: '100%' }}` next to it is two structural properties with no design tokens involved.

## The part the number hides

`layer1.cjs` scans a **hardcoded 8-file list** — footer, the ui-kits atoms/molecules, and the theme files. It does **not** scan `header/index.tsx`. And that's where the one real abuse lives:

```
header/index.tsx:441
  <ZimmLogo style={{ width: 'min(597px, 60vw)', height: 'min(70px, 7.04vw)' }} />
```

Raw values, no tokens — and it's exactly the header logo regression already on your open list. `header/index.tsx` *is* modified in this PR, so the honest figure is **8**, and the 8th is the one that matters.

So the finding isn't really "7 inline styles." It's:

1. **5 forwards + 1 provisional literal** — benign as written.
2. **The `style?: CSSProperties` prop being public API on every atom** is what makes bypass possible. That's the `ui-kits/` design question you deferred as F1.
3. **One caller actually taking that escape hatch**, in `header`, with hardcoded `min()` values — the live defect.

If you want the count to mean something in review, the fix is to widen the scanned file list so `header/` is covered — otherwise the check reports clean on the only place it's currently being violated.

content.text:
Good — all three claims check out. Here's the actual picture.

## What the rule is watching for

`style={...}` writes CSS straight onto the DOM node. That's flagged because it defeats three things at once:

1. **Provenance** — a value in `style` never passes through the theme, so nothing can tell you whether `39px` is a token or someone's guess.
2. **Cascade** — inline styles beat every class. A recipe, a variant, a `_hover` — none of them can override it.
3. **Expressiveness** — `style` has no `:hover`, no `:focus-visible`, no media queries. It's a single static snapshot.

That's why the ladder in `overrideStyling.md` puts `style` off the end entirely: recipe → token → `sx` → `.scss`.

## The 7 remaining split into two very different things

**Six are prop pass-through, not styles at all:**

```tsx
// zimmNavItem ×2, zimmButton ×2, zimmTextInput ×1, zimmInputAction ×1
<chakra.a __css={styles} sx={sx} style={style}>
```

There's no design value on those lines. The atom declares `style?: CSSProperties` in its props and forwards it. The regex matches the string `style=`; the *content* is whatever a caller passed — and right now, **nothing passes anything**. Zero call sites in the footer.

So the real question isn't "is line 45 bad," it's **should these atoms expose a `style` prop at all?** My read: no. `ZimmNavItem` already accepts `sx`, which is strictly better — it resolves through the theme, supports pseudo-states and responsive arrays. Keeping `style` alongside it is a second, weaker escape hatch whose only distinguishing feature is that it's un-overridable. It's an open door for exactly the drift the rule exists to stop. Low urgency (nothing uses it), worth closing.

**One is the genuine violation — `zimmLogo/index.tsx:32`:**

```tsx
<svg
  style={{
    display: 'block',
    width: '100%',
    maxWidth: LOGO_MAX_WIDTH,  // '327px'  ← provisional
    height: LOGO_HEIGHT,       // '39px'   ← provisional
    overflow: 'clip',
    ...style,
  }}
>
```

This one hardcodes two provisional pixel values into the DOM. And the cause is structural: `ZimmLogo` imports only `useToken` from Chakra — it's a **raw `<svg>`, not `chakra.svg`**, so it has no `__css` or `sx` surface. `style` is its *only* styling channel.

That's the same root cause as the header logo regression already on your open list: `header.ts` defines a `logo` part, but nothing can consume it, so it sits there as dead code. Converting to `chakra.svg` fixes both at once — the recipe becomes reachable and the two provisional constants move into the theme where the audit can see them.

## What the 8th was

The footer used to pass an inline `style` to `ZimmNavItem` to force `minHeight` and `whiteSpace` — the latter being what let "ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF COUNTRY" wrap. That's the "apply via tokenisation and remove inline" change you approved. Those two values now live in `zimmNavItem.ts:13,16` as `minHeight: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'` and `whiteSpace: 'normal'`, and the footer passes no `style` at all.

Which is why the wrap still works today with nothing inline: it's the recipe doing it, not an override.

## Verdict

| | Count | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Pass-through `style={style}` | 6 | Unused. Drop the prop from the ui-kit atoms — separate cleanup, not this PR |
| `ZimmLogo` inline object | 1 | Real. Fix with `chakra.svg`; also revives `header.ts`'s dead `logo` part |

Neither blocks this PR. The `ZimmLogo` one is already sitting on your open list as the header logo regression — this just confirms it's one defect showing up in two places, not two.

Verified — and this is worse than a hygiene issue.

## When it was flagged

| When | What |
|---|---|
| **18 Aug, 06:45** | I first flagged it — the header hand-copies `header.ts:70-74`'s two values into an inline style instead of consuming `{...styles.logo}` |
| **18 Aug, 07:04** | CodeRabbit sharpened it — spotted the *consequence*: `ZimmLogo` has its own internal `maxWidth: '327px'` |
| **18 Aug, 09:04** | I noted it had got **worse** — a commit added `height: '39px'` to the atom |

27 messages across the session touch it. It was raised three times and never decided — that's on me for leaving it as a bullet on an open list instead of forcing the call.

## The live bug

```
viewport 1440px
  rendered  : 327.0 x 70.0
  max-width : 327px
  asked for : min(597px, 60vw) = 597px
```

**The header logo renders 45% narrower than designed.** The atom sets `maxWidth: '327px'` *before* spreading `...style`. The header only passes `width` and `height` — never `maxWidth` — so the atom's cap survives, and `max-width` beats `width`. Same at 1024px.

And because the SVG keeps its default `preserveAspectRatio`, the artwork letterboxes: ~327×38.6 of actual wordmark centred in a 327×70 box, with ~15px of dead space above and below. On `develop`, `<BrandLogo {...styles.logo} />` had no such cap.

So this isn't "an inline style that offends the linter." It's a visibly wrong header logo on every page, introduced by this PR.

## On scope — you're right, and it changes the answer

I framed this as "should we fix the header here," which was the wrong framing. The real position:

**This PR already changes the header.** The `BrandLogo` → `ZimmLogo` swap *is* this PR's diff — `header/index.tsx`, +18/-2, Tier 2 Global Shell, both-squad ownership. I'm not proposing to newly touch the header; I'm pointing at something SFCC-55 already did.

So the question is actually: **should SFCC-55 be changing the header at all?** If your answer is no — which is what your instinct is saying — then the cleanest resolution isn't the `chakra.svg` refactor I proposed. It's to **revert that hunk**: restore `<BrandLogo {...styles.logo} />`, drop the `ZimmLogo` import from the header, and let ZimmLogo adoption happen in its own header ticket with the sizing designed properly.

That would: fix the rendering bug by removing its cause, revive `header.ts`'s part, clear the Phase 1 inline-style flag, drop the header out of the Tier 2 coordination surface, and make SFCC-55 genuinely footer-only. The footer keeps using `ZimmLogo` — only the header reverts.

The one thing I can't judge for you: whether the header swap was *deliberate* SFCC-55 content (standardising both header and footer onto the new atom) or drift that crept in. If deliberate, it stays and gets fixed properly. If drift, revert.

content.text:
Mapped it. Short answer: **no, it doesn't have to touch the footer** — but there's a catch worth knowing.

## Why the footer is entangled at all

The atom's "defaults" are actually **the footer's dimensions**:

```tsx
const LOGO_MAX_WIDTH = '327px';   // provisional
const LOGO_HEIGHT    = '39px';    // provisional
```

The footer passes nothing — `<ZimmLogo variant="inverse" />` — so it relies entirely on those. Measured just now: footer renders **327 × 39**, and Phase 4 confirmed 39px height is Figma-exact. So `ZimmLogo` was written footer-first, and the header is the one fighting values that were never meant to be universal.

Only two consumers exist: footer:462 and header:441.

## The fix — three hunks, footer untouched

**1. `zimmLogo/index.tsx`** — give it a style channel. Same five properties, same computed output.

```diff
-import { useToken } from '@chakra-ui/react';
+import { chakra, useToken, type SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';

 type ZimmLogoProps = {
   variant?: 'inverse' | 'default';
-  style?: CSSProperties;
+  sx?: SystemStyleObject;
 };

-    <svg
-      style={{
-        display: 'block',
-        width: '100%',
-        maxWidth: LOGO_MAX_WIDTH,
-        height: LOGO_HEIGHT,
-        overflow: 'clip',
-        ...style,
-      }}
+    <chakra.svg
+      __css={{
+        display: 'block',
+        width: '100%',
+        maxWidth: LOGO_MAX_WIDTH,
+        height: LOGO_HEIGHT,
+        overflow: 'clip',
+      }}
+      sx={sx}
```

**2. `header.ts`** — the `logo` part gains `maxWidth`. **This is the line that actually fixes the bug.**

```diff
     logo: {
       width: 'min(597px, 60vw)',
       height: 'min(70px, 7.04vw)',
+      // Displaces ZimmLogo's own 327px cap, which is the footer's width, not the header's.
+      maxWidth: 'min(597px, 60vw)',
     },
```

**3. `header/index.tsx`** — consume the part instead of duplicating it.

```diff
-<ZimmLogo style={{ width: 'min(597px, 60vw)', height: 'min(70px, 7.04vw)' }} />
+<ZimmLogo sx={styles.logo} />
```

Footer: **zero lines changed.** It keeps hitting the atom's `__css` defaults and renders 327 × 39 exactly as it does now.

## The catch

Hunk 2 is non-negotiable, and it's the one that widens scope. `sx` beats `__css` in Chakra's cascade — but only for properties it actually sets. `header.ts`'s `logo` part currently sets `width` and `height` and *not* `maxWidth`, so without that line the atom's 327px cap survives and the bug persists even after the refactor.

And `header.ts` is **not currently in this PR** — it's Tier 2 theme, UI Designer owner, notify-before-changing.

So the real trade is:

- **Touch `header.ts`** (+3 lines) → footer untouched, header fixed, one new Tier 2 file in the PR.
- **Don't touch `header.ts`** → the only other way to clear the cap is removing `maxWidth` from the atom, and that *does* hit the footer: the footer's svg is `width: 100%` inside its wrapper, so without the cap it would blow out to the full footer width. You'd then have to re-add 327px in `footer.ts`.

There's no version that touches neither. My recommendation is `header.ts` — one line, and header logo sizing belongs there anyway, next to the two values already living in that part.

Want me to apply it, or does the `header.ts` involvement push you back toward reverting the header hunk and making this its own ticket?

content.text:
Traced both. The second question turns out to be the important one.

## Where the values came from

Two different provenance stories, and only one of them is sound:

| Value | Where | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `327px` / `39px` (atom) | `zimmLogo/index.tsx:12-13` | **Figma nodes 1892:50472 / 1892:50474**, cited in the comment |
| `597px` / `70px` (header) | `header.ts:73-74` | **Nothing.** No Figma node, no `.docs/` reference, no ticket |

I grepped `overrides/` and `.docs/` for `597` and `7.04vw`. They appear in exactly three places: the `header.ts` definition, its own explanatory comment, and the duplicate in `header/index.tsx`. That comment explains the *arithmetic* — `597 = 70 × 631/74` — but never says where **70** came from. It was derived from an unsourced number.

For context, base SFCC had `logo: { width: [8, 8, 8, 12], height: [6, 6, 6, 8] }` — 32–48px wide. Ours replaced that wholesale in `cd60b7a "Initial commit during Detailed Design phase"`, and the values haven't been touched since.

**So this changes the fix calculus.** Clearing the 327px cap makes the header logo 597px — nearly double — on the authority of a number nobody sourced. That's not obviously a fix; it risks trading *quietly* wrong for *confidently* wrong.

Meanwhile the value it currently renders at, 327px, is the one with Figma backing — but that Figma node is the logo component's own viewport, which is very likely the **footer's** instance, not the header's. Nobody has established what the header logo should measure.

I can't settle that from the repo. It needs the header frame from Figma — say the word and I'll pull it.

## How the two files should be

Independent of which number wins, the shape is wrong, and the principle is simple: **the component says *which* logo and *where*; the theme says *how big*.** Right now the component says how big, in numbers hand-copied from the theme, and the theme's copy is unreachable.

```ts
// header.ts — sole owner of header logo geometry
logo: {
  width: 'min(597px, 60vw)',
  height: 'min(70px, 7.04vw)',
  maxWidth: 'min(597px, 60vw)',   // must be here, or the atom's 327px cap wins
}
```

```tsx
// header/index.tsx — consumes, never redefines
<ZimmLogo sx={styles.logo} />
```

That's the same relationship `header/index.tsx` already has with `styles.logoBar` and `styles.logoButton` two lines above — the logo is the one that broke the pattern.

The deeper smell is the atom itself. `LOGO_MAX_WIDTH`/`LOGO_HEIGHT` are **one consumer's dimensions installed as universal defaults**, which is precisely why the header can't override them cleanly. The clean end state is an atom that carries only `display: block; width: 100%; height: auto` and lets each consumer size it from its own theme file — footer from `footer.ts`, header from `header.ts`. But that requires declaring 327×39 in `footer.ts`, which is the footer-touching path you were trying to avoid.

## What I'd do

Given 597/70 has no design source, I'd **not** ship the cap fix in this PR. Reverting the header hunk is now the stronger option: it restores `<BrandLogo {...styles.logo} />`, which rendered correctly on `develop`, removes the regression, keeps SFCC-55 footer-only, and leaves the header logo sizing question to a ticket where someone can get the Figma number first.

Then the header ticket does it properly: confirm the dimensions with Kiera, raise 327/39 into `foundation/sizes.ts` as real tokens (the audit already lists both as pending that), strip the atom's hardcoded defaults, and have both consumers size from their own theme files.

Which way do you want to go — revert the hunk, or should I pull the header frame from Figma first so you're deciding with the real number in hand?

content.text:
Broadly yes, but two refinements matter.

**Footer — correct values, provisional *home*.**

"Provisional" here doesn't mean guessed. `327px`/`39px` cite Figma nodes 1892:50472 / 1892:50474 in the comment, and Phase 4 measured the footer logo at **39px against Figma's 39px — exact**. They're provisional only in that they live as `const`s in a component file instead of `foundation/sizes.ts`, which is Tier 1 and the UI Designer's to populate. That's tokenisation debt — already logged in your audit — not a correctness problem.

**Header — wrong on two independent levels.**

1. *Mechanically broken.* It duplicates `header.ts:73-74` into an inline style, orphaning the theme part, and the override silently fails because it never passes `maxWidth`. Result: 327 × 70 instead of 597 × 70. Definite defect, introduced by this PR.
2. *Unsourced target.* Even the number it's trying to reach — 597/70 — has no Figma node, no `.docs/` entry, nothing. Grep finds it only in its own definition and its duplicate.

So the header isn't just implemented wrongly; it's aiming at a value nobody has verified. Fixing (1) without settling (2) would make it confidently wrong at 597px rather than quietly wrong at 327px.

**And one thing worth flagging: the footer is only *accidentally* correct.**

It renders right because it passes nothing and the atom's defaults happen to be the footer's dimensions. There's no guard on that. If anyone edits `LOGO_MAX_WIDTH`/`LOGO_HEIGHT` to serve the header — which is exactly what a well-meaning fix to the header would tempt someone into — the footer silently changes size, with no test or type error to catch it.

That's the real structural issue: **a shared atom carrying one consumer's dimensions as universal defaults.** The header exposed it; it didn't cause it.

Net: footer is fine to ship as-is. The header change is the part that doesn't belong — which is why reverting that hunk still looks like the cleanest move for SFCC-55.

content.text:
Partial revert applied and verified.

## What changed

`overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx` — **+14, −0. Every added line is a comment.** Zero functional change against `develop`.

Reverted: `BrandLogo` restored to the icons import, `ZimmLogo` import removed, and `<BrandLogo {...styles.logo} />` back in place of the inline-styled `<ZimmLogo>`.

Kept: all three documentation blocks — the `AccountIcon`/`HeartIcon` rationale, the `IconButtonWithRegistration` note, and the commented-out icon-block explanation with the HPC-018 reference. Those were the genuinely useful part of the hunk and they're unrelated to the logo.

## Verified

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Header logo | **597 × 70** — was 327 × 70, now consuming `{...styles.logo}` with `max-width: none` |
| Footer logo | **327 × 39** — byte-identical, untouched |
| `header.ts` `logo` part | Live again at `header/index.tsx:439`, no longer orphaned |
| `tsc` / `prettier` / `vitest` | 0 errors · clean · 168 passed |
| `eslint` | 0 errors, 3 warnings (pre-date this PR, 7 occurrences on `develop`) |
| Phase 3 runtime | 20/20 |
| `header.ts` | Not touched — stayed out of the PR entirely |

## One thing that got better than expected

`ZimmLogo` now has exactly **one consumer — the footer**. That collapses the problem: what was a two-consumer conflict over a shared atom's defaults is now just "the footer's logo dimensions live in a component file instead of `foundation/sizes.ts`" — which is already item `LOGO_MAX_WIDTH`/`LOGO_HEIGHT` on your provisional-token audit. Nothing new to track.

The atom's `style={{...}}` still shows in Phase 1's inline-style count (7, unchanged — the header's instance was never in that scan's scope), but it's now a single-consumer tokenisation item rather than a structural conflict.

## For the follow-up ticket

- Header logo dimensions `597`/`70` have **no Figma source** — confirm with Kiera before anyone acts on them
- `327`/`39` are Figma-backed (nodes 1892:50472 / 1892:50474); raise into `foundation/sizes.ts`
- Then: strip the atom's hardcoded defaults, convert to `chakra.svg`, header consumes `styles.logo`, footer declares its size in `footer.ts`
- Sequencing matters — token raise before atom cleanup, or the footer breaks

Worth noting the original swap wasn't a bad idea: `BrandLogo` renders via SFCC's sprite (`<use xlink:href="#b...">`), which is the timing dependency `ZimmLogo` was built to avoid. The motivation was sound; it just wasn't scoped or sized correctly. That belongs in the header ticket, not here.

Nothing committed — 40 files still unstaged.

content.text:
Good question — the bucket is doing more than its label suggests. Here's what's actually in it.

## What the classifier does

Each emitted declaration falls through a chain: `var(--zimm-*)` → `var(--chakra-*)` → CSS keyword → structural property → **then** the value is normalised and looked up in the foundation token index. Match → this bucket. No match → `NO TOKEN` flag.

So it means: **the CSS shipped a hard value instead of a `var()` reference, but that value exactly equals something in our token set.** Value right, provenance unproven.

**36 is occurrences; there are 14 distinct declarations.** They split into two very different groups.

## Group 1 — `textStyle` and theme expansion (12 of 14). No action.

```
font-size: 0.625rem      ← textStyles.footer.fontSize
line-height: 0.875rem    ← textStyles.footer.lineHeight
letter-spacing: 0.025rem ← textStyles.footer.letterSpacing
font-weight: 500         ← fontWeights.medium
font-family: 'Futura Round', …  ← fonts.body
width/height: 16px       ← iconSizes.md
width/height: 12px       ← iconSizes.sm
```

When a recipe says `textStyle: 'footer'`, Chakra expands it at build time into individual properties and emits the **resolved literal**, not a var. That's just how `textStyle` works — and `textStyle` is rung 1 of the styling ladder, the thing `overrideStyling.md` tells you to reach for first.

So these aren't findings. They're the audit observing correct code and being unable to prove it's correct from the CSS alone.

The `←` attribution reads noisy — `16px` maps back to 19 tokens — because the reverse lookup is one-to-many. Many tokens legitimately share a value. It doesn't mean ambiguity in the source.

## Group 2 — the two that actually matter

```
gap: 3rem       ← zimmTokens[--zimm-scale-1200]
width: 8.75rem  ← zimmTokens[--zimm-scale-3500]
```

These are `SPACE_SECTION` and `SIZE_COL_NAV` in `footer.ts` — **hand-typed constants that duplicate an existing token.** They're the same two Phase 1's mirror check flags:

```
footer.ts  SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'    ≡  zimmTokens[--zimm-scale-1200]
footer.ts  SIZE_COL_NAV  = '8.75rem' ≡  zimmTokens[--zimm-scale-3500]
```

Phase 1 catches them at the source, Phase 2 catches them in the output — same defect, two angles. They should be `var(--zimm-scale-1200)` and `var(--zimm-scale-3500)`.

Phase 1 lists a third — `SIZE_MODAL_SUB = '30rem' ≡ breakpoints.sm` — which doesn't appear here because the subscribe modal isn't in the DOM on initial load. That's a useful reminder that Phase 2 only sees what actually rendered.

## The takeaway

The bucket is **not** a defect count. It's "the value is right but the CSS doesn't say which token it came from," and ~85% of it is `textStyle` doing exactly what it's supposed to. Its real use is as a cross-check: anything in here that *isn't* explained by theme expansion is a hand-typed duplicate, and Phase 1's source-level mirror check is what pins those down.

Two are actionable, both already on your list. Worth fixing in this PR — it's a two-line change in `footer.ts` and it would clear a Phase 1 finding too. Want me to?

content.text:
Verified — and the answer is architectural, not a lapse.

## The rule governs authoring, not emission

Nobody typed `0.625rem`. Here's the actual source:

```ts
// typography.ts:221
footer: {
  fontFamily: FONT_MEDIUM,
  fontSize: fontSizes['4xs'],        // ← named reference
  fontWeight: fontWeights.medium,
  lineHeight: lineHeights['4xs'],
  letterSpacing: letterSpacings.footer,
}
```

Every value is a named token reference. The literal in the CSS is what those references *resolve to* at build time. The rule "no raw hex/px in a component file" is about what you write; the stylesheet is a build artifact.

## Why a `textStyle` *can't* emit a `--zimm-*` var

This is the part that makes it unavoidable rather than merely acceptable:

```
typography.ts   fontSizes['4xs'] = '0.625rem'      ← the source of truth
      ↓ imported by
zimmTokens.ts   --zimm-font-size-4xs: '0.625rem'   ← derived mirror
```

`zimmTokens.ts:8` imports **from** `typography.ts`. The CSS variables are downstream of the values, not upstream. So `typography.ts` physically cannot write `fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-4xs)'` — that's a circular import.

When a recipe says `textStyle: 'footer'`, Chakra walks to `theme.textStyles.footer` → `fontSizes['4xs']` → `'0.625rem'` and emits it. The var was never in that path.

And that's the right way round. The `--zimm-*` registry exists to serve the `.zimm-*` global classes in `globalStyles.ts` — it's a **delivery mechanism**, not the design system. Inverting the dependency to make vars survive to the output would promote the CSS-var mirror to source of truth. Worse architecture for a cosmetic win.

## The three emission paths

That's why the footer's CSS has all three shapes:

| You write | You get | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `zIndex: 'overlay'`, `padding: 'xs'` | `var(--chakra-*)` — 33 | Chakra recognises a registered scale key and varifies it |
| `width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'` | `var(--zimm-*)` — 51 | An opaque string; Chakra passes it through verbatim |
| `textStyle: 'footer'` | literal — 36 | Composite; resolved at build time |

Path 2 is deliberate, not preference — it's the workaround for the sizes-vs-space trap, where a bare `'xl'` on `width` would resolve through `theme.sizes` and give you Chakra's 36rem instead of our 24px.

## So what makes a literal valid?

**Single-sourcing — not `var()` syntax.** One place the value is typed. Change `fontSizes['4xs']` and every consumer moves with it.

The test isn't "is this a literal," it's **"is this value typed more than once?"**

By that test:

- ✅ `font-size: 0.625rem` — typed once, in `typography.ts`. Valid.
- ✅ `width: 16px` — typed once, in `sizes.ts` as `iconSizes.md`. Valid.
- ❌ `gap: 3rem` — `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` hand-typed in `footer.ts` while `--zimm-scale-1200` already holds 3rem. **Two copies, free to drift. Invalid.**
- ❌ `width: 8.75rem` — same, `SIZE_COL_NAV`.

That's precisely why Phase 1 has a separate *mirror* check: it doesn't care whether a value is a literal, it cares whether it duplicates one that already exists.

## And it's guarded

`drift.cjs` cross-checks all 16 typography classes against their `textStyles` on every run — **0 drift**. So the derived literals aren't taken on trust; if `typography.ts` and the emitted CSS ever disagreed, that fails.

Net: 12 of the 14 distinct literals are correct by construction and mechanically verified. Two are genuine duplicates, both already flagged from the source side. The `var()`-vs-literal distinction is a red herring — single-sourcing is the actual invariant.
