content.text:
Checked before writing the diff, and it's a good thing I did. **Don't fix these — I was wrong to call them actionable.** Here's the diff I would have applied and why each line is a regression.

## The "fix" that shouldn't ship

```diff
  const SPACE_SECTION = '3rem';      // alias/space/section (48px)
  const SIZE_COL_NAV  = '8.75rem';   // alias/size/footer/col-width-nav (140px)

- padding: `${SPACE_SECTION} var(--zimm-scale-2xl)`,
+ padding: 'var(--zimm-scale-1200) var(--zimm-scale-2xl)',

-   width: SIZE_COL_NAV,
+   width: 'var(--zimm-scale-3500)',
```

Three things break.

**1. It's a WCAG 1.4.4 regression.** The tokens aren't what I assumed:

```
--zimm-scale-1200: '48px'     ← px, not rem
--zimm-scale-3500: '140px'    ← px, not rem
```

`3rem` scales with browser zoom and root font-size. `48px` does not. `overrideStyling.md` is explicit that spacing must be `rem` for exactly this reason. The current code is **more correct** than the replacement.

The audit matched them because it normalises units before comparing — 3rem and 48px are numerically equal, so it reported equivalence. They are not interchangeable.

**2. It violates rule 1d.** Phase 1 forbids `zimm-scale-[0-9]` — consuming the numeric Handover aliases directly, because "1200" carries no semantic meaning. That check currently sits at **0 violations**. The fix would introduce two.

**3. There's no legitimate token to point at.** I checked the named scale programmatically:

```
3rem      — NO named equivalent
8.75rem   — NO named equivalent
30rem     — NO named equivalent
```

The named scale jumps 2.5rem (`3xl`) → 4rem (`4xl`), straight past 3rem; and 8rem (`6xl`) → 10rem (`7xl`), past 8.75rem.

## So all three "style mirrors" are false positives

Including the third, `SIZE_MODAL_SUB = '30rem' ≡ breakpoints.sm` — that's a **coincidental value collision**. A subscribe-modal max-width has no semantic relationship to a breakpoint; they just both happen to be 480px. Pointing a modal width at `breakpoints.sm` would be wrong even though the value matches.

The check matches on normalised value alone. It's blind to unit semantics, to semantic role, and to whether the token it matched is one you're permitted to use.

## What's actually correct

The current code is right as written:

```ts
const SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'; // alias/space/section (48px)
const SIZE_COL_NAV  = '8.75rem'; // alias/size/footer/col-width-nav (140px)
```

Named locally, `rem` units, annotated with the Figma alias, pending a real foundation entry. That's exactly the pattern `overrideStyling.md` prescribes for a value with no foundation home.

**The real gap is upstream:** `alias/space/section` (48px) and `alias/size/footer/col-width-nav` (140px) need named entries in `foundation/spacing.ts` / `sizes.ts`. Tier 1, UI Designer's call — and both are already on your provisional-token audit.

## One thing worth surfacing to Kiera

The named scale is authored in `rem`; the numeric Handover aliases are authored in `px`. Two units for the same conceptual scale, in the same file. That inconsistency is what made this look like a fix in the first place, and it'll mislead the next person too.

## Optional

I could tighten the mirror check so it stops flagging a match when the matched token is a rule-1d numeric alias, is in a different unit, or lives in a semantically unrelated scale like `breakpoints`. Right now it produces three false positives on every run, which is the fastest way to train people to ignore it. Say the word.

content.text:
Honest answer: **no — not by the phases as I originally ran them. I've now closed that gap, and here's where it actually stands.**

## The hole in what I ran

Phase 1's literal/inline checks used a **hand-curated list of 13 files**, not a directory walk. `overrides/` has 71. **Seven of the 20 files this PR changed were outside that list** — including `header/index.tsx`, which is exactly why the `<ZimmLogo style={{...}} />` inline style never appeared in the count I reported to you.

I've now re-run the full check set over all 19 PR files and repo-wide.

## PR scope — complete, all findings accounted for

| Check | Count | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 1a raw literal | 16 | **All 16 accounted for.** 3 `button.ts` (the standing documented exception), 2 `zimmLogo` (Figma-sourced, provisional), 9 `footer.ts` (2 breakpoints with no foundation equivalent + 7 named constants, each annotated with its Figma alias), 1 `zimmTextInput`, 1 `header` — **pre-dates this PR** (`develop:220`) |
| 1b `fontSize=` | 1 | `header:302` — pre-dates (`develop:293`). `"l"` isn't a valid fontSize token; separate pre-existing bug |
| 1c sizing key | 0 | ✅ |
| 1d numeric alias | 0 | ✅ |
| 1e inline `style=` | 7 | 6 unused pass-through props + `zimmLogo`'s object (now single-consumer) |
| 1f `sx=` | 3 | `footer:361` deliberate rung-4 + 2 pass-through |
| 1g compound shorthand | 2 | Both fully `var()`-based — valid |
| 1h `!important` | 0 | ✅ |

**Nothing unexplained, and nothing introduced by this PR that isn't annotated.** Every provisional constant is already inventoried in your audit.

## What the wider sweep turned up (pre-existing, not yours)

- **Rule 1d is genuinely violated outside this PR** — `listMenu.ts` ×4 uses `var(--zimm-scale-700)`, and `header.ts:59` uses `var(--zimm-scale-1200)`. Real numeric-alias consumption, 5 sites. My earlier "1d: 0 ✅" was true only for the 13-file list.
- **`pages/my-new-route/index.tsx`** — a scaffold page with `style={{ textAlign: 'center', fontSize: '4rem' }}`.
- Repo-wide: 103 raw literals, 11 `fontSize=`. Mostly Contentful scaffolding and untouched base ports.

Also worth knowing: the rem-vs-px reasoning we just worked through is **already documented** at `footer.ts:20-24`, citing WCAG 1.4.4 — so a reviewer hitting those two constants will find the justification in place.

## What still isn't proven, even now

Be clear-eyed about this before you treat it as a clean bill:

- **Regex-based.** Blind to computed values, template literals built from variables, styles assembled at runtime, and values passed down as props from a parent.
- **Phase 2 saw only the `<footer>` subtree, on the homepage, in its initial rendered state.** The subscribe modal isn't in the DOM until submit — **its CSS has never been audited at all.**
- **The mirror check has confirmed false positives** (all three of them). Nothing measures its false *negatives*.
- No coverage of Storybook, other pages, other locales, or a production build.

## My recommendation

The PR's own surface is clean and fully explained — I'd ship on that basis. But the 13-file hand-list is a trap that already bit us once here; if these audits are going to keep being the gate, the file list should become a walk over changed files. That's a small change to the tooling and I can fold it in whenever you want.

**Yes — the latest run reports `No new findings ✔`.** But that answer needs one caveat, and the run surfaced a real bug I'd introduced.

## What happened on this pass

The run before last flagged three things on my own generator change. I checked each rather than accepting them:

**1. Base cache not invalidated — real, mine, now fixed.** My extractor change altered what gets stored in `baseScan.components`, but `loadBaseCache()` accepts any cache matching `BASE_CACHE_SCHEMA`. There *was* a `.baseCache.json` on disk **dated 31 Jul**, actively serving stale merged props. Bumped 2 → 3; regeneration then rewrote 36 lines of `components.md` instead of 16 — those extra 20 were the stale rows. CodeRabbit was right and I'd have shipped it.

**2 & 3. Extractor can't resolve unions/intersections — pre-existing, not mine.** Verified against `develop`: `Button` and `PageContainer` show `—` there and `—` now, identical. The regex only matches `type X Props = {`, so `ZimmButtonProps = A | B` and `X = Base & {...}` are invisible. Fixing properly needs a TS parser — genuine scope creep, and I've already made four changes to that file.

## Full arc across six runs

| Run | Findings | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4 | 2 registry minors **fixed** · 2 `.storybook/` majors — your approved Tier 1 exception |
| 2 | 4 | 2 registry **fixed** · `FOOTER_FIXTURE` major — your container-split decision · missing test **fixed** |
| 3 | 1 | Registry pipe — **false positive**, disproved (208 rows, 0 mismatches) |
| 4 | 1 | Footer prop contract wrong — **fixed** |
| 5 | 3 | Cache — **fixed** · 2 pre-existing extractor limits |
| 6 | **0 new** | — |

Net: **5 fixed** (registry escaping, truncation, prop scoping, cache invalidation, plus a mutation-verified test), **3 decided** and needing PR replies, **1 disproved**, **2 open** pre-existing tooling limitations.

## The caveat

`--light` **samples differently every run.** The two `.storybook/` Tier-1 majors appeared only in run 1 and never again — they weren't resolved, just not re-sampled. So "no new findings" means *this pass found nothing new*, not *the tree is clean*. Don't read run 6 as a clean bill on runs 1–5's content.


## Still on you

Three in-thread PR replies once it's up, per AGENTS.md — silence teaches CodeRabbit nothing:

1. **`.storybook/main.js` + `preview.tsx`** — Tier 1, you approved as tier-1-approver, identity verified via `gh api`. Cite the exception.

3. **The pipe false positive** — explain the two-adjacent-cells misread so it stops re-flagging.

And optionally worth a line in the PR body: the extractor's union/intersection blind spot is pre-existing and knowingly left, so a reviewer seeing `—` in a props cell knows it's a tooling limit, not a component without props.

content.text:
Verdict: **yes, they're worth taking — most of it is additive, and three pieces are strictly better than what I did.** Here's the breakdown.

## Clean wins — no conflict with our work at all

**`theme/components/button.ts`** — replaces magic numbers and a raw literal with named constants and a token:

```diff
- transition: 'opacity 0.15s ease',
+ const ICON_TRANSITION = 'opacity var(--zimm-motion-duration-fast) var(--zimm-motion-easing-standard)'
- opacity: 0.6,   →  OPACITY_ICON_HOVER
- opacity: 0.4,   →  OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED
```

Genuine value: kills two `conventions.md` magic-number violations and moves `0.15s` onto a motion token. My Phase 2 audit *saw* `transition: opacity 0.15s ease` in the emitted CSS and classified it as structural — Jersey fixed the source. **We don't touch this file. Pure gain.**

**`types/contentful.ts`** — adds `phoneHref`, `whatsAppHref`, `emailHref`. Backs the ContactIconRow href work. **No conflict. Pure gain.**

## Strictly superior to mine

**`generateRegistry.mjs` — three changes, all better than my equivalents:**

1. **`preferredTypeName` scoping** — the same fix I made, but better documented. **Take theirs, drop mine.**
2. **Truncation removed entirely** (`m[3].trim()`, no slice) rather than my 29-char + `…`. Cleaner call — the registry should carry the real type.
3. **`([^\n;,]+)` → `(.+?)`** — this one neither I nor CodeRabbit caught. The old regex stops at a comma, so `Record<string, string>` silently became `Record<string` — and because that's under 30 chars, **my ellipsis fix wouldn't even have flagged it**. No component hits it today, so it's latent, but it's a real bug my change couldn't have caught.

The one thing to carry forward from mine: the **`BASE_CACHE_SCHEMA` 2→3 bump**. Jersey changed extraction without invalidating the cache, and I confirmed a stale `.baseCache.json` from 31 Jul was actively serving wrong props. Their change needs it as much as mine did.

## Test coverage we genuinely lack

**`zimmNavItem` — unsafe-href play test.** Asserts `SAFE_HREF_RE` rejects `javascript:`, `data:`, and protocol-relative `//` hrefs, each falling back to `<button>` with no `href`.

This is a **security regression test for an XSS guard**, and I checked: `SAFE_HREF_RE` appears in exactly one file locally — the component — with **zero tests anywhere**. Our 8 existing zimmNavItem stories cover visual states and keyboard focus; none covers this. Our Phase 3 suite doesn't either.

Highest-value item in the three commits.

**`zimmInputAction` — `EmptySubmitValidation` / `InvalidEmailValidation` play tests.** Partially overlaps our `SubmitInteraction`, but adds the `expect(args.onSubmit).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` assertion. Modest gain.

## The conflict I flagged earlier — resolved, and it's not one

`cssVars.ts`. I called this a hard delete-vs-modify needing a human call. Having read it: **Jersey removed every consumer of `cssVars`/`cssTextStyles` and left the file orphaned.** We removed every consumer *and* deleted the file.

Same conclusion, reached independently — we just finished the job. Git will still flag the conflict mechanically, but the resolution is unambiguous: **keep the deletion.**

## ⚠️ One change that contradicts a decision you made

`af5861f` alters the locale button:

```diff
- onClick={undefined}
+ disabled
- // PLACEHOLDER: wire to locale selector once available.
+ // PLACEHOLDER: remove disabled and wire onClick to the locale selector once available.
```

You explicitly said *"leave it as is"* and later *"no — disregard it"* when I proposed restoring `aria-disabled`. Jersey has now made it genuinely `disabled`, which removes it from tab order — a real a11y behaviour change, not a comment tweak. Our Phase 3 assertion ("locale button present but inert") would still pass, so **the test suite won't catch this reverting your call.** Decide deliberately rather than letting the merge decide.

## Net answer

| | |
|---|---|
| **Worth taking** | `button.ts`, `types/contentful.ts`, all three `generateRegistry` fixes, both sets of play tests |
| **Superseded by ours** | `cssVars.ts` — keep our deletion |
| **Carry forward from ours** | `BASE_CACHE_SCHEMA` 2→3 |
| **Needs your decision** | locale button `disabled` |
| **Wasted effort** | my `preferredTypeName` + ellipsis work — drop it, theirs is better |

Their 14 other file-level overlaps are small (their +121/−65 vs our +429/−538 on `footer/index.tsx`, +2/−1 vs our +453/−215 on `footer.ts`), so your work dominates the merge; theirs slots in around it.

Worth telling Jersey you both fixed the same CodeRabbit findings and the same generator bug in parallel — that's the second time this branch has cost duplicate effort.

content.text:
I have everything. Here's the complete take-list with the actual code and where each lands.

---

## 1. `theme/components/button.ts` — **pure add, zero conflict**

We don't touch this file. Jersey's version drops in whole.

```diff
+// Icon-variant opacity levels. No foundation opacity token covers element-level opacity
+// (colors.opacity holds RGBA overlays, not multipliers), so named constants are the
+// correct pattern per conventions.md > "No magic numbers or strings."
+const OPACITY_ICON_HOVER    = 0.6;
+const OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED = 0.4;
+const ICON_TRANSITION = 'opacity var(--zimm-motion-duration-fast) var(--zimm-motion-easing-standard)';

 icon: {
-  transition: 'opacity 0.15s ease',
+  transition: ICON_TRANSITION,
-  _hover: { opacity: 0.6 },
+  _hover: { opacity: OPACITY_ICON_HOVER },
-  _disabled: { opacity: 0.4 },
+  _disabled: { opacity: OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED },
 }
```

**Why:** `0.6` and `0.4` are magic numbers, and `0.15s ease` is a raw literal — both violate rules we're enforcing everywhere else. My Phase 2 audit actually *saw* `transition: opacity 0.15s ease` in the emitted CSS and waved it through as "structural." Jersey went after the source. Applied twice (icon + iconInverse variants).

---

## 2. `types/contentful.ts` + the ContactIconRow wiring — **fills a real gap of ours**

```diff
 export type FooterConfigEntry = {
   fields: {
     copyrightOwner?: string;
+    phoneHref?: string;
+    whatsAppHref?: string;
+    emailHref?: string;
   };
 };
```

```diff
- <ContactIconRow />
+ <ContactIconRow phoneHref={phoneHref} whatsAppHref={whatsAppHref} emailHref={emailHref} />
```

**Why this matters more than it looks.** Our `ContactIconRow` *accepts* those three props (line 285) — but our call site at line 451 passes **none of them**. The component is wired to receive hrefs that nothing supplies. Our type doesn't even declare the fields, so there was no way to pass them.

The uncomfortable part: Phase 3's `✅ contact icons are not focusable` passes because **there are no hrefs to focus**, not because the design says they're decorative. A green test masking missing plumbing.

**Honest caveat:** neither fixture carries values, so this changes nothing visible today. It's correct plumbing waiting on Contentful — but without it, someone adding the CMS fields later would find the wire still cut.

---

## 3. `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` — **replace mine wholesale**

Take Jersey's `extractTsProps` verbatim. Three things it does better:

```diff
-function extractTsProps(content) {
+function extractTsProps(content, preferredTypeName = null) {
```

**(a) Per-block collection instead of one shared bucket.** Jersey collects each `*Props` block separately with its own dedupe set, *then* picks. Mine deduped globally while collecting, so ordering could leak a prop from the wrong block. Same outcome on today's files, more robust design.

**(b) Truncation removed entirely** — `const type = m[3].trim()`, no slice. Better than my 29-char + `…`. The registry should carry the real type.

**(c) The one neither I nor CodeRabbit caught:**

```diff
- const lineRe = /^\s{2,}(\w+)(\??):\s*([^\n;,]+)[;,]?\s*$/gm
+ const lineRe = /^\s{2,}(\w+)(\??):\s*(.+?)\s*[;,]?\s*$/gm
```

`[^\n;,]+` stops at a comma. So `Record<string, string>` silently became `Record<string` — and since that's under 30 characters, **my ellipsis fix wouldn't have marked it**. A wrong value presenting as a complete one. No component hits it today, so it's latent, but my change couldn't have caught it.

**Keep one thing of mine on top:**

```diff
-const BASE_CACHE_SCHEMA = 2
+const BASE_CACHE_SCHEMA = 3
```

Jersey changed extraction without invalidating the cache. I found a `.baseCache.json` dated **31 Jul** actively serving stale merged props — bumping it rewrote 20 more registry lines. Their change needs this as much as mine did.

---

## 4. Story tests — **coverage we genuinely don't have**

**`zimmNavItem` — the highest-value item in all three commits:**

```tsx
export const PlaceholderButton: Story = {
    name: 'Placeholder — No href (or unsafe href) renders as button',
    render: () => (
        <Box display="flex" flexDirection="column" gap={2} alignItems="flex-start">
            <ZimmNavItem label="Omitted href" />
            <ZimmNavItem label="javascript: href" href="javascript:void(0)" />
            <ZimmNavItem label="data: href" href="data:text/html,xss" />
            <ZimmNavItem label="Protocol-relative href" href="//example.com" />
        </Box>
    ),
    play: async ({canvasElement}) => {
        const canvas = within(canvasElement)
        const cases = ['Omitted href', 'javascript: href', 'data: href', 'Protocol-relative href']
        for (const label of cases) {
            const el = canvas.getByRole('button', {name: label})
            await expect(el).toBeInTheDocument()
            await expect(el).not.toHaveAttribute('href')
        }
    },
}
```

**Why this is the one to take:** it's a **security regression test for an XSS guard**. I grepped — `SAFE_HREF_RE` appears in exactly one file (the component) with **zero tests anywhere in the repo**. Our 8 existing zimmNavItem stories cover visual states and keyboard focus; none touches this. Commit `e9c2180` closed a protocol-relative bypass and shipped no test to keep it closed. This is that test.

**`zimmInputAction` — two validation stories:**

```tsx
export const EmptySubmitValidation: Story = {
    args: {label: 'Email address', type: 'email', onSubmit: fn()},
    play: async ({canvasElement, args}) => {
        const canvas = within(canvasElement)
        await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('button', {name: /submit/i}))
        await expect(canvas.getByRole('alert')).toHaveTextContent(/please enter a value/i)
        await expect(args.onSubmit).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
    },
}
```

(plus `InvalidEmailValidation`, same shape with `'not-an-email'`)

**Why:** we have `SubmitInteraction`, which covers the happy path. These add the *negative* cases and — the bit that matters — `expect(args.onSubmit).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`. Proving the handler *didn't* fire is what stops a future refactor silently submitting invalid input.

---

## 5. `cssVars.ts` — **take nothing, keep our deletion**

I flagged this as a hard conflict earlier. Having read it: Jersey removed every consumer and left the file orphaned. We removed every consumer **and deleted the file**. Same conclusion, independently.

Git will still raise delete-vs-modify. Resolve as **keep our deletion** — Jersey left 245 lines of dead code; we finished the job.

---

## 6. ⚠️ Locale button — **take nothing without your say-so**

```diff
- onClick={undefined}
+ disabled
- // PLACEHOLDER: wire to locale selector once available.
+ // PLACEHOLDER: remove disabled and wire onClick to the locale selector once available.
```

You said *"leave it as is"* and later *"no — disregard it"*. `disabled` removes the button from tab order — a real a11y behaviour change, not a comment tweak.

**And our test won't catch it.** Phase 3 asserts "locale button present but inert," which stays green either way. If you let the merge take this, your decision gets reverted silently.

---

## Summary

| From Jersey | Action | Conflict? |
|---|---|---|
| `button.ts` constants + motion token | Take whole | None |
| `contentful.ts` href fields + wiring | Take | None |
| `extractTsProps` (all 3 fixes) | **Replace mine** | Drop my version |
| `zimmNavItem` unsafe-href play | Take | Additive |
| `zimmInputAction` validation plays | Take | Additive |
| `cssVars.ts` refactor | **Reject** — keep our delete | Mechanical only |
| Locale button `disabled` | **Your call** | Contradicts your decision |
| `BASE_CACHE_SCHEMA` 2→3 | **Keep mine** on top | — |

The work I'd bin: my `preferredTypeName` implementation and the ellipsis truncation. Both superseded.

Want me to stage this as a concrete merge plan — or hold until you've spoken to Jersey? Given you're both live on the branch and have now duplicated effort twice, I'd talk first.
Same scrutiny as the 597/70 question — good. Let me verify Jersey's claims rather than repeat them.

content.text:
Found something that changes my earlier advice. **Take half of this, not all of it.**

## Where the values came from

| Value | Origin | Design source |
|---|---|---|
| `0.6` / `0.4` | Written new in `9bd13bf` (ZimmButton → Chakra migration) | **None.** Not in base SFCC, not migrated from anywhere, no Figma reference anywhere in `.docs/` or the theme |
| `0.15s ease` | Same commit | **None** |
| `--zimm-motion-duration-fast` = 200ms | Real token in `motion.ts` | Exists — but the file header says **"PROVISIONAL: Motion design is pending formal sign-off. Values are functional placeholders... Do not treat as final."** |

Jersey's claim about `colors.opacity` is correct, by the way — I checked, it holds `rgba(25, 25, 25, 0.40)` overlays, not multipliers. You genuinely can't write `opacity: colors.opacity[40]`; it would emit an rgba string into a numeric CSS property. So "no token covers this" is true.

## Why named constants are the right pattern

For the **opacity values**, four concrete reasons:

1. **The name carries intent.** A bare `0.4` could be anything; `OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED` says what it's for.
2. **Single-sourcing.** Both are used twice — `icon` and `iconInverse` variants. Two typed copies can drift; one can't. Same invariant as the `textStyle` discussion earlier: the rule isn't "no literals," it's "no value typed twice."
3. **One line to change** when the designer confirms.
4. **It's the documented escape hatch.** `overrideStyling.md` prescribes exactly this for a value with no foundation home — a named constant with a comment saying why. Identical pattern to `SPACE_SECTION` in `footer.ts`.

None of that makes `0.6` *correct* — it makes it **findable, singular, and honest about being unconfirmed.**

## But the transition change contradicts a decision already recorded in that file

`button.ts:13-14`, 130 lines above what Jersey edited:

```ts
// 0.15s matches no motion token (fast 200ms / default 300ms) — left as-is
// pending the UI designer's confirmation rather than retimed silently.
transition: 'background-color 0.15s ease, border-color 0.15s ease, color 0.15s ease',
```

Somebody already considered mapping `0.15s` onto the 200ms token and **explicitly decided not to**, because it would retime the component without designer sign-off.

Jersey's `ICON_TRANSITION` does precisely that — **150ms → 200ms, 33% slower** — for the icon variants only. Two consequences:

- **`button.ts` ends up with two timings.** `baseStyle` at 150ms, icon variants at 200ms, in the same component, with the rationale for 150ms still sitting at line 13.
- **Jersey's comment misreads the precedent.** It says "same provisional caveat as baseStyle's transition comment above" — but that comment isn't *"this is provisional, so use the token."* It's *"the token doesn't match, so don't use it yet."* Opposite conclusion.

So this is trading one unsourced number for another unsourced number, against a written decision, and creating an inconsistency in the process.

## Revised recommendation

**Take the opacity constants as-is:**

```diff
+const OPACITY_ICON_HOVER    = 0.6;
+const OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED = 0.4;
```

Pure hygiene, zero behaviour change, correct pattern.

**Modify the transition constant** — keep the DRY win, drop the retiming:

```diff
-const ICON_TRANSITION = 'opacity var(--zimm-motion-duration-fast) var(--zimm-motion-easing-standard)';
+// 0.15s, matching baseStyle. Deliberately NOT var(--zimm-motion-duration-fast) (200ms):
+// see baseStyle's transition comment above — retiming needs UI-designer sign-off, and
+// motion.ts is itself marked provisional. One constant so icon/iconInverse can't drift.
+const ICON_TRANSITION = 'opacity 0.15s ease';
```

That still removes the duplicated literal across both icon variants, keeps the file internally consistent at 150ms, and leaves one line to change when motion design is signed off.

I said "pure gain, take whole" earlier — that was right for the opacity half and wrong for the transition. This is the third time this session that tracing provenance flipped a conclusion (597/70, the `3rem` "mirrors", now this) — worth making it a standing habit on this codebase, since a lot of values look tokenised and aren't.

One for Kiera's list either way: **icon-button hover/disabled opacity has no design source at all**, and the 150-vs-200ms question is now formally open in two places.

Confirmed the constraint that decides this. **A pull fails right now** — exactly as expected:

```
error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge:
```

## The constraint that shapes everything

**We have 0 commits ahead.** Jersey's 3 are already published on a shared branch. So this is *not* a "cherry-pick what we like" problem — dropping any of them would mean force-pushing, which breaks Jersey's local checkout.

That reframes the take/reject list from earlier. It becomes two separate things:

1. **Conflict resolutions** — where our work and theirs touch the same lines
2. **A deliberate follow-up commit** — for the two things we're consciously reversing (locale button, transition constant)

Reversals must be their *own commit*. Burying them inside a conflict resolution makes them invisible to Jersey and to review.

## Recommended: commit → rebase → resolve → follow-up

**Step 1 — commit the 40 staged files first.** Non-negotiable. Right now the only copy of a full day's work is the git index. Any operation that touches the working tree can lose it, and the index has no reflog. Committing gives it a SHA and makes everything after it recoverable.

**Step 2 — `git pull --rebase`.** We'd have exactly one commit replaying onto their three. Linear history, one conflict pass, no merge commit noise on a feature branch.

**Step 3 — resolve with a pre-decided policy** (below).

**Step 4 — separate commit** for the transition constant and the locale-button decision.

**Not stash.** With 40 files, `stash pop` conflicts are materially worse — no per-file staging, no rebase tooling, and a failed pop can strand work in a dangling stash.

## Per-file resolution policy for the 16 conflicts

| File | Resolve as |
|---|---|
| `.claude/registry/components.md` · `hooks.md` | **Don't hand-merge.** Generated. Take either side, then `npm run generate:registry` |
| `utils/cssVars.ts` | `git rm` — our deletion completes their orphaning |
| `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` | **Theirs**, then re-apply our `BASE_CACHE_SCHEMA` 2→3 |
| `theme/components/footer.ts` | Ours (+453/−215 vs their +2/−1 comment) |
| `footer/index.tsx` | Ours, then re-apply their `ContactIconRow` href wiring |
| `zimmNavItem/index.stories.tsx` | Ours, then re-apply their unsafe-href `play` |
| `zimmInputAction/index.stories.tsx` | Ours, then re-apply their 2 validation `play`s |
| `footer/index.stories.tsx` | Ours, review their 2 added stories |
| `zimmButton` · `zimmLogo` · `zimmTextInput` stories | Ours — theirs are 1–5 line touches |
| `zimmLogo/index.tsx` · `zimmNavItem/index.tsx` | Ours |
| **`zimmTextInput/index.tsx`** · **`useZimmTextInputState.ts`** | ⚠️ **Read both properly.** Their +57/+27 is real cssVars-removal work, not a trivial touch |

Those last two are the only ones I'd not pre-decide. Everything else has a clear winner.

Two files arrive conflict-free as pure gain: `theme/components/button.ts` and `types/contentful.ts`.

## Things that will bite

- **`pre-commit` hook** blocks direct edits to derived AI config files. We regenerated the registry via the generator, so it should pass — but if it complains, that's why.
- **`commit-msg` enforces conventional commits.** The 40-file commit needs a proper `feat(footer): …` subject.
- **`rerere` is off.** Worth `git config rerere.enabled true` before starting — if the rebase goes wrong and you redo it, you won't re-resolve everything by hand.

## One judgement call for you

That 40-file, +3794 commit is a big blob to resolve conflicts against. Splitting it into 2–3 logical commits first — footer / ui-kit / tooling — would make the rebase surface conflicts in smaller, meaningful chunks. It costs an hour of selective staging. With 16 overlapping files I'd lean toward doing it, but it's your time budget.

## Before any of this

Message Jersey. You're both live on this branch, you've now duplicated effort twice, and two of the resolutions above **reverse decisions they made and pushed** — the locale button and the transition retiming. Those land better as a conversation than as a surprise commit.

══ commit-msg hook — the actual rules ══
  #!/bin/bash
  # commit-msg: enforces conventional commits format on every commit.
  #
  # Install: cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg
  #          chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
  commit_msg=$(cat "$1")
  # Pass through merge commits, reverts, fixups, and WIP
  if echo "$commit_msg" | grep -qE '^(Merge|Revert|fixup!|squash!|WIP)'; then
    exit 0
  fi
  # Conventional commits pattern
  # type(optional-scope): description
  # upstream-sync is a Zimmermann-specific type for PWA Kit sync changes
  pattern='^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|upstream-sync)(\([a-z0-9/._-]+\))?: .{1,100}$'
  if ! echo "$commit_msg" | grep -qE "$pattern"; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Commit rejected — message does not follow conventional commits format."
    echo ""
    echo "  Required:  type(scope): short description"
    echo ""
    echo "  Types:"
    echo "    feat           new feature"
    echo "    fix            bug fix"
    echo "    docs           documentation only"
    echo "    style          formatting, no logic change"
    echo "    refactor       neither fix nor feat"
    echo "    perf           performance improvement"
    echo "    test           adding or updating tests"
    echo "    build          build system or dependency changes"
    echo "    ci             CI/CD configuration"
    echo "    chore          maintenance tasks"
    echo "    upstream-sync  upstream Salesforce PWA Kit sync"
    echo ""
    echo "  Scope examples (optional but encouraged):"
    echo "    product-tile  checkout  auth  header  search"
    echo "    global-e  adyen  contentful  searchspring"
    echo "    pwa-kit-runtime  commerce-sdk-react"
    echo ""
    echo "  Examples:"
    echo "    feat(product-tile): add sale badge for discounted variants"
    echo "    fix(checkout): resolve shipping method not persisting on refresh"
    echo "    upstream-sync(pwa-kit-runtime): apply v3.18.0 SSR cache fix"
    echo "    chore(deps): update @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react to 5.3.0"
    echo "    test(use-current-basket): add guest basket merge coverage"
    echo ""
    exit 1
  fi
  exit 0

content.text:
Now I can show you why the earlier fix broke. The arithmetic:

| Requirement | Constraint |
|---|---|
| `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT` fits line 1 | cap ≥ **115px** |
| `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF` must NOT fit | cap < **132.9px** |
| `Book an Appointment` must not wrap | cap ≥ **131px** |

**Combined window: [131, 132.9) — 1.9 pixels.** That's not a tolerance, it's a coincidence. The 160px cap I set earlier was calibrated against *fallback-font* metrics; with Futura Round loaded, `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF` shrank to 132.9px and now fits, so it wraps after "OF".

No single column cap can satisfy both robustly. The fix belongs on the phrase, not the column.

content.text:
Fixed and verified.

## What was wrong

The 160px cap I set earlier was calibrated against **fallback-font** metrics. Once Futura Round loaded, every label got ~12% narrower — and `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF` dropped to 132.9px, which now fits inside 160. So it wrapped after "OF" instead of after "ACKNOWLEDGEMENT".

The arithmetic shows why no cap value can fix it:

| Requirement | Constraint |
|---|---|
| `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT` fits line 1 | cap ≥ **115px** |
| `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF` must **not** fit | cap < **132.9px** |
| `Book an Appointment` must stay one line | cap ≥ **131px** |

**Viable window: [131, 132.9) — 1.9 pixels.** That's a coincidence, not a tolerance. Any browser, any hinting difference, any one-character copy edit breaks it. The constraint belongs on the phrase, not the column.

## The fix

`contentfulFixture.ts` — a non-breaking space binding "of Country":

```diff
+ // \u00A0 (non-breaking space) between "of" and "Country" is deliberate. Figma wraps
+ // this label as ACKNOWLEDGEMENT / OF COUNTRY. Under Futura Round "ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF"
+ // measures 132.9px and "Book an Appointment" 131px, so no shared linkCol max-width can
+ // both wrap this after the first word and keep BOOK on one line — the window is 1.9px.
+ // Binding "of Country" leaves one break opportunity, so the wrap is correct at any cap
+ // from 115px to 186px. Production content must carry the same NBSP from Contentful.
- fields: { label: 'Acknowledgement of Country', href: '#' },
+ fields: { label: 'Acknowledgement of\u00A0Country', href: '#' },
```

With one break opportunity left, the full string (187px) can't fit any cap, so it *must* break there. **Safe window goes from 1.9px to 71px.**

I used the `\u00A0` escape rather than a literal character — an invisible byte in source is a trap for the next reader.

## Verified

Measured text-line rects, not just element height:

```
1440px   lines = [115, 69]     ← ACKNOWLEDGEMENT / OF COUNTRY ✅
1280px   lines = [115, 69]  ✅
1023px   lines = [115, 69]  ✅
 768px   lines = [115, 69]  ✅
 375px   lines = [115, 69]  ✅
```

115px and 69px match the measured widths of `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT` and `OF COUNTRY` exactly. Phase 4 geometry is byte-identical to before (footer Δ13, links Δ5, all paddings exact), `tsc` clean, **168 tests pass**, eslint clean. No cap change needed — 160px still works, and the item now renders its natural 115px line.

## Two things to carry forward

**Content dependency.** In production this label comes from Contentful, so an editor has to author the NBSP there too. A plain space reverts the wrap. Worth telling the content team — it's a standard editorial practice, but it needs to be *known*.

**The 768–860px band is unchanged** and still wraps 7 labels — pre-existing, unrelated to this, still on the open list.

Nothing committed. This is now part of the 40 staged files awaiting the merge strategy decision.

══ commit-msg hook: the enforced pattern ══
  #!/bin/bash
  # commit-msg: enforces conventional commits format on every commit.
  #
  # Install: cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg
  #          chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
  commit_msg=$(cat "$1")
  # Pass through merge commits, reverts, fixups, and WIP
  if echo "$commit_msg" | grep -qE '^(Merge|Revert|fixup!|squash!|WIP)'; then
    exit 0
  fi
  # Conventional commits pattern
  # type(optional-scope): description
  # upstream-sync is a Zimmermann-specific type for PWA Kit sync changes
  pattern='^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|upstream-sync)(\([a-z0-9/._-]+\))?: .{1,100}$'
  if ! echo "$commit_msg" | grep -qE "$pattern"; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Commit rejected — message does not follow conventional commits format."
    echo ""
    echo "  Required:  type(scope): short description"
    echo ""
    echo "  Types:"
    echo "    feat           new feature"
    echo "    fix            bug fix"
    echo "    docs           documentation only"
    echo "    style          formatting, no logic change"
    echo "    refactor       neither fix nor feat"
    echo "    perf           performance improvement"
    echo "    test           adding or updating tests"
    echo "    build          build system or dependency changes"
    echo "    ci             CI/CD configuration"
    echo "    chore          maintenance tasks"
    echo "    upstream-sync  upstream Salesforce PWA Kit sync"
    echo ""
    echo "  Scope examples (optional but encouraged):"
    echo "    product-tile  checkout  auth  header  search"
    echo "    global-e  adyen  contentful  searchspring"
    echo "    pwa-kit-runtime  commerce-sdk-react"
    echo ""
    echo "  Examples:"
    echo "    feat(product-tile): add sale badge for discounted variants"

content.text:
Two things the hooks force, which change the ordering:

- **The `pre-commit` hook auto-regenerates `.claude/registry/` and `git add`s it** on any `overrides/app/{components,hooks,utils,pages}/` change. So the generator fix **must land first**, or the next commit bakes in output from the buggy extractor.
- **Staging `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` triggers `syncCursorRules --fix`**, which auto-adds `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (already stale — "source is 1 day newer").

## Pre-flight: drop one file

`overrides/app/theme/foundation/sizes.ts` — the entire change is **removing one trailing blank line**. It's **Tier 1**. Committing it triggers the CODEOWNERS review requirement and the `tier1-guard` PR warning for zero benefit.

```bash
git restore --staged --worktree overrides/app/theme/foundation/sizes.ts
```

That takes 40 files → 39.

## The plan — 8 commits

**1 · `fix(registry): scope prop extraction and escape Markdown table cells`** — 4 files
`scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` · `.claude/registry/{components,hooks,utils}.md`
**Must be first.** Stages nothing under `overrides/app/`, so the hook won't re-trigger — and every later commit's auto-regen then uses the fixed extractor.

**2 · `feat(theme): self-host Futura Round for development and testing`** — 8 files
`static/fonts/FuturaRound-{Regular,Medium}.woff2` · `theme/fontFace.tsx` · `_app-config/index.tsx` · `types/vendor.d.ts` · `.storybook/preview.tsx` · `.storybook/main.js` · `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`
⚠️ **Three Tier 1 files** — name them and the approval in the body. Will also auto-add `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.
Second because font metrics change every measurement downstream; landing it early makes the later visual decisions reproducible.

**3 · `refactor(ui-kit): replace cssVars/cssTextStyles with raw var(--zimm-*) strings`** — 10 files
`utils/cssVars.ts` (deleted) · zimmIcon ×2 · zimmLogo ×2 · zimmNavItem ×2 · zimmButton ×2 · `theme/components/zimmNavItem.ts`

**4 · `refactor(zimm-text-input): move colour derivation from the hook into the theme recipe`** — 6 files
`theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts` · zimmTextInput ×2 · zimmInputAction ×2 · `hooks/useZimmTextInputState.ts`

**5 · `feat(footer): global footer UI with ZimmFooter recipe and Contentful-shaped data`** — 6 files
`theme/components/footer.ts` · `theme/components/index.ts` · `footer/index.tsx` · `footer/index.stories.tsx` · `contentfulFixture.ts` · `contentfulSchema.placeholder.ts`

**6 · `test(theme): add recipe guards and text-input colour coverage`** — 3 files
`recipeGuards.test.ts` · `zimmTextInput.test.ts` · `useZimmTextInputState.test.ts`

**7 · `style(icons): apply Prettier formatting to zimm icon paths`** — 1 file
`components/icons/zimm.tsx` — verified pure reformat; every added line is `<path`, an attribute, or `/>`. Isolated so it doesn't pollute review.

**8 · `docs(header): explain the disabled base SFCC icon-button block`** — 1 file
`components/header/index.tsx` — comment-only after the revert (+14/−0).

**39 files. All types valid against the hook's pattern** (`feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|upstream-sync`), all scopes lowercase-safe, all subjects under 100 chars.

## Why this order

Dependencies run downhill: tooling → fonts → atoms → composite → assembly → tests. Commits 3–5 each build on the one before, so any of them can be reviewed against a working tree that actually compiles. Commits 7 and 8 are independent and parked at the end deliberately — pure noise, zero review cost.

## Bodies worth writing

Three commits need more than a subject:

- **#2** — name the three Tier 1 files, state that you approved them as a tier-1-approver (identity verified via `gh api`), and note the licence is deliberately excluded.
- **#5** — the declarations: provisional constants pending Kiera, the NBSP in the ACK label, the 768–860px band, `FOOTER_FIXTURE` being static-first pending Contentful.
- **#3** — that `cssVars.ts` is deleted rather than orphaned.

All get `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.

## One thing to expect

Commits 3–6 each stage files under `overrides/app/`, so the hook will regenerate and re-add `.claude/registry/` into each. That's correct — the registry tracks the components — but it means those commits will show registry churn you didn't stage. Not a problem, just don't be surprised.

Want me to execute this as-is, adjust the groupings, or draft the three full commit bodies for review first?

content.text:
Here's every item in diff form. One of them changed my recommendation.

---

## 1 · `theme/components/button.ts` — take the constants, **modify** the transition

```diff
+// Icon-variant opacity levels. No foundation opacity token covers element-level opacity
+// (colors.opacity holds RGBA overlays, not multipliers), so named constants are the
+// correct pattern per conventions.md > "No magic numbers or strings."
+const OPACITY_ICON_HOVER    = 0.6;
+const OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED = 0.4;

 icon: {
-  transition: 'opacity 0.15s ease',
+  transition: ICON_TRANSITION,
-  _hover:    { opacity: 0.6 },
+  _hover:    { opacity: OPACITY_ICON_HOVER },
-  _disabled: { opacity: 0.4 },
+  _disabled: { opacity: OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED },
 }
 iconInverse: {  … same four lines again … }
```

Applied twice — `icon` and `iconInverse`. That's the DRY case for the constants.

**But not their `ICON_TRANSITION` verbatim:**

```diff
  // theirs — retimes 150ms → 200ms
- const ICON_TRANSITION = 'opacity var(--zimm-motion-duration-fast) var(--zimm-motion-easing-standard)';

  // ours — keeps the DRY win, drops the retiming
+ // 0.15s, matching baseStyle. Deliberately NOT var(--zimm-motion-duration-fast) (200ms):
+ // see baseStyle's transition comment above — retiming needs UI-designer sign-off, and
+ // motion.ts is itself marked provisional. One constant so icon/iconInverse can't drift.
+ const ICON_TRANSITION = 'opacity 0.15s ease';
```

`button.ts:13` already records the opposite decision: *"0.15s matches no motion token (fast 200ms / default 300ms) — left as-is pending the UI designer's confirmation rather than retimed silently."*

---

## 2 · `types/contentful.ts` + `footer/index.tsx` — take as-is

```diff
 export type FooterConfigEntry = {
   fields: {
     copyrightOwner?: string;
```

```
        :857  ${r.exports}  ${r.desc}            ← utils   NOT escaped

Ours   :696  ${escapeCell(r.props)} … ${escapeCell(r.desc)}
        :799  ${escapeCell(r.desc)}
        :862  ${escapeCell(r.exports)} … ${escapeCell(r.desc)}
```

content.text:
Audit complete. Tree fully reverted to your 8 commits, `tsc` 0, 168 tests passing. Every claim below was **executed**, not read.

---

## Verdict per item

| # | Item | Verdict | Proof |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1a | `button.ts` opacity constants | **Take** — zero-risk | Theme output byte-identical (`0.6`/`0.4`) |
| 1b | `ICON_TRANSITION` token | **Reject as written** | Browser: **0.15s → 0.2s** |
| 2 | `contentful` hrefs + wiring | **Take** — safe today | Turns 3 dead icons into 3 working links |
| 3 | `generateRegistry` | **Hybrid required** | Ours drops **2 of 6** props; theirs breaks 2 tables |
| 4 | Unsafe-href play test | **Take** — highest value | 2/2 mutations caught |
| 5 | Validation play tests | **Take** | 3/3 mutations caught |

---

## 1 · button.ts — the split is empirically justified

Extracted the theme object through esbuild, then measured computed CSS in-browser:

```
ours      → duration: 0.15s
Jersey's  → duration: 0.2s        ← 33% slower, real behaviour change
proposed  → duration: 0.15s       ← constants kept, timing preserved
```

Opacity values resolve **identically** (`0.6`/`0.4`) — pure hygiene, take freely. The transition genuinely retimes, contradicting `button.ts:13`'s written decision. My proposed variant was measured and confirmed to restore 0.15s while keeping the DRY win.

## 2 · Contentful wiring — works, and exposes a bad test

Applied the type + wiring with real fixture values:

```json
{"tag":"A","href":"tel:+61280808080","label":"Call us","focusable":true}
{"tag":"A","href":"https://wa.me/61280808080","label":"WhatsApp","focusable":true}
{"tag":"A","href":"mailto:care@zimmermann.com","label":"Email us","focusable":true}
```

Then ran Phase 3 — **19/20**, failing on `contact icons are not focusable`.

**Our test encodes the broken state as correct.** When Contentful supplies hrefs, it fails, and the obvious "fix" is to weaken the test rather than notice it was asserting a bug. With the wiring but an empty fixture (the real adoption state) it's back to **20/20** — so adoption is zero-risk today.

## 3 · Generator — neither version is correct alone

Built a probe with six props covering every edge case:

```
OURS    → 4 of 6 captured.  withComma: Record<string, string>  and
                            commaAndPipe?: Map<string, 'x'|'y'>  SILENTLY DROPPED
JERSEY  → 6 of 6 captured, full types, no truncation
HYBRID  → 6 of 6 + escaping on all tables
```

The comma bug is worse than truncation — `[^\n;,]+` stops at the comma, so the line never matches `$` and **the prop vanishes entirely**.

But Jersey's escapes only the components table. Proven with a util whose JSDoc contains a pipe:

```
ours    → 'alpha' \| 'beta'    ✅
Jersey  → 'alpha' | 'beta'     ❌ breaks the column
```

Hybrid validated: **210 rows, 0 column mismatches**, Footer row correct, cache bumped to 3. Real-world delta is 3 rows — `ZimmNavItem`'s `React.MouseEvent<HTMLAnch…` becomes the full `React.MouseEvent<HTMLAnchorElement \| HTMLButtonElement>`.

**Saved at** `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/KEEP-generateRegistry-hybrid.mjs` (37,266 bytes).

## 4 & 5 · Play tests — mutation-proven

All assertions ran verbatim against **our** components: **5/5 pass**, including two CONTROL tests proving they aren't vacuously passing. Then five mutations:

| Mutation | Caught |
|---|---|
| Drop `(?!\/)` — the exact bypass `e9c2180` closed | ✅ |
| Allow `javascript:` | ✅ |
| Drop empty-value guard | ✅ |
| Drop email-format guard | ✅ |
| Guards fire but `onSubmit` still called | ✅ |

That last one is the dangerous silent-submit bug, caught only by `expect(onSubmit).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`.

**And these have real gate value:** `qa.yml`'s `storybook-test` job runs play functions via `@storybook/test-runner`, triggered on `overrides/app/components/**` — which this PR touches.

---

## Two findings that only surfaced by running things

**The play tests cannot run under vitest.** The icons barrel re-exports SFCC icons needing webpack's `svg-sprite-loader`; vitest dies on `Cannot create property 'viewBox' on string`. They're **Storybook-only**. Fine — that's where CI runs them — but don't expect `npm run test` to cover them.

**At `c8248c5` those stories still import the deleted `cssVars`.** Only at the tip (`af5861f`) are they clean. Cherry-picking the intermediate commit would break the build.

content.text:
**Yes — all five align, with one caveat and one honest tension.** Verified against the rules, not asserted.

## Conformance results

| Check | Before | After | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1a raw colour/length literal | 25 | 25 | **no change** (identical per-file) |
| 1b `fontSize=` | 1 | 1 | unchanged |
| 1c bare key on sizing prop | 0 | 0 | ✅ |
| 1d `--zimm-scale-NNN` alias | 0 | 0 | ✅ |
| 1e inline `style=` | 7 | 7 | unchanged |
| 1f `sx=` | 3 | 3 | unchanged |
| 1g compound shorthand | 2 | 2 | unchanged |
| 1h `!important` | 0 | 0 | ✅ |
| Dead recipes / collisions / mirrors / base-path imports | — | — | identical |
| Typography drift | 0 | 0 | ✅ 16 classes |

**Zero new violations.** (The "16 → 24" I flagged mid-audit was a display artefact — one sweep truncated its list. Per-file comparison confirmed identical.)

## Per item

**`button.ts`** — sits in `theme/components/`, rung 3 of the hierarchy and the canonical surface for buttons. Named constants satisfy `conventions.md`'s no-magic-numbers rule. The only `button.ts` flags are the pre-existing `BTN_HEIGHT_*` constants that `overrideStyling.md` explicitly names as its standing exception.

**`contentful.ts` + wiring** — Footer still receives data as props and fetches nothing, exactly what `components.md`'s container/presentational rule requires. Additive optional fields on the Contentful-shaped type.

**Generator** — build tooling, outside the UI rules entirely.

**Both story files** — clean against `components.md` and `testing.md`:

```
Elements/ZimmNavItem     ← generic building block, correct bucket
Forms/ZimmInputAction    ← composed form assembly, correct bucket
Default export           ✅ both
play only where there's interactive behaviour   ✅
selectors: 10 × getByRole, 0 × getByText, 0 × data-testid
```

That last line is worth noting — **every selector is rung 1** of testing.md's priority order. No test-ids at all.

## The caveat: Jersey's code needs prettier on adoption

```
button.ts:10:26  error  Delete `···`  prettier/prettier
```

Their aligned-assignment style breaks our config:

```diff
- const OPACITY_ICON_HOVER    = 0.6;
+ const OPACITY_ICON_HOVER = 0.6;
```

`prettier --write` fixes it; eslint then reports **0 errors**. Their tree appears to use different formatting settings, so **run prettier over anything adopted** rather than pasting verbatim.

## The honest tension

On paper, **Jersey's `ICON_TRANSITION` is *more* token-aligned than mine.** Theirs references `var(--zimm-motion-duration-fast)`; mine keeps a raw `0.15s`.

Neither trips a rule — the 1a regex only covers hex/px/rem/em, not `s` — so this is judgement, not enforcement. I chose the less token-pure option because `button.ts:13` records an explicit decision *not* to retime without designer sign-off, and taking theirs would leave the file running two different timings.

That's a deliberate trade of token-purity for not silently changing behaviour. It should be a conscious call, and it belongs on Kiera's list: **confirm whether icon transitions should move to the 200ms token**, at which point `baseStyle` and the icon variants move together and my constant becomes the token version.

Everything reverted — tree clean at `f79a52a`, 168 tests passing.

## Verdict: adopt all five, with two modifications

Both V&V passes support it. Nothing found that argues against adoption; three items proved worth **more** than face value.

| Item | Value verdict | Conformance |
|---|---|---|
| `button.ts` opacity constants | Zero-risk hygiene — output byte-identical | ✅ clean |
| `ICON_TRANSITION` | **Modify** — theirs retimes 0.15s → 0.2s | ✅ either way |
| `contentful` hrefs + wiring | Real fix — 3 dead icons → 3 working links | ✅ clean |
| Generator | **Hybrid** — ours dropped 2 of 6 props; theirs broke 2 tables | n/a (tooling) |
| Unsafe-href play test | Highest value — 2/2 mutations caught | ✅ clean |
| Validation play tests | 3/3 mutations caught | ✅ clean |

**Conformance: zero new violations.** Every static check identical before and after — 1a, 1e, 1f, 1g unchanged; 1c/1d/1h still zero; no new dead recipes, collisions, or mirrors; typography drift zero across 16 classes. Storybook categorisation correct (`Elements/`, `Forms/`), `Default` exports present, and all 10 selectors are `getByRole` — rung 1, no test-ids.

## Two conditions

**1. Keep `0.15s` in `ICON_TRANSITION`.** Measured in-browser: theirs is 0.2s, ours 0.15s. `button.ts:13` already records the decision not to retime without designer sign-off; taking theirs leaves one component running two timings.

**2. Run `prettier --write` on anything adopted.** Their aligned-assignment style is an eslint error under our config (`Delete ···`). Fixes cleanly, 0 errors after.

## One downstream consequence

Adopting the contentful wiring is safe **today** — Phase 3 stays 20/20 with our empty fixture. But once Contentful supplies real hrefs it drops to **19/20**, because our `contact icons are not focusable` assertion encodes the broken state as correct. Rewrite that test when the CMS data lands, rather than letting someone weaken it.

## Two things for Kiera

- **Icon-button hover/disabled opacity has no design source** — `0.6`/`0.4` were invented during the ZimmButton migration.
- **Should icon transitions move to the 200ms token?** If yes, `baseStyle` and the icon variants move together and my constant becomes the token version. Right now it's the one place where I chose less token-purity over a silent behaviour change.

## What this changes for the merge plan

Nothing structural — the per-file resolution policy stands. It just makes three resolutions concrete rather than judgement calls:

- **`generateRegistry.mjs`** — not "take theirs" as I first said. Take their `extractTsProps` + call sites, keep our `escapeCell` (4 sites, all three tables) and `BASE_CACHE_SCHEMA = 3`. Validated file sitting at `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/KEEP-generateRegistry-hybrid.mjs`.
- **`cssVars.ts`** — resolve as `git rm`. Same conclusion reached independently; we just finished it.
- **Locale button** — still yours. Phase 3 stays green either way, so the suite won't flag it reverting your decision.

Tree is clean at `f79a52a`, 168 tests passing, nothing staged. Ready for `git config rerere.enabled true` → talk to Jersey → `git pull --rebase`.

Here's the closing comment, ready to paste:

---

## Closing to re-open with a clean history

This branch has been rebased, so the commit history that reviewers see here no longer matches what's on the branch. Rather than force-push over an existing review thread, I'm closing this and re-opening so the new PR starts from an accurate, reviewable history.

**Nothing is lost** — every commit below is on the branch, and Jersey's three commits are preserved in the lineage.

### What changed structurally

The work was previously one large uncommitted change set. It's now **11 logical commits** on top of Jersey's three, each independently reviewable:

```
fix(registry)          scope prop extraction and escape Markdown table cells
feat(theme)            self-host Futura Round for development and testing
refactor(ui-kit)       replace cssVars/cssTextStyles with raw var(--zimm-*) strings
refactor(zimm-text-input)  move colour derivation from the hook into the theme recipe
feat(footer)           global footer UI with ZimmFooter recipe and Contentful-shaped data
test(theme)            add recipe guards and text-input colour coverage
style(icons)           apply Prettier formatting to zimm icon paths
docs(header)           explain the disabled base SFCC icon-button block
fix(button)            keep the icon transition at 0.15s instead of the 200ms motion token
feat(footer)           wire Contentful contact hrefs through to ContactIconRow
test(ui-kit)           cover unsafe-href fallback and input-action validation
```

44 files · +3898 / −71 vs `develop` · `tsc` 0 · 168 tests passing.

### Defects found and fixed during verification

Several were silent — correct-looking code producing wrong output:

- **`extendTheme` merge collision.** The recipe was named `Footer`, which deep-merges with SFCC's base `Footer` rather than replacing it. Copyright rendered at 14px instead of 10px and the subscribe heading lost its 24px gap. Renamed to `ZimmFooter`.
- **`width: 'xl'` rendered contact icons at 576px.** `width`/`height` resolve through `theme.sizes`, not `theme.space`, and Chakra's default `sizes.xl` is 36rem. Fixed with the CSS var; a regression guard now covers it.
- **Four compound-shorthand bugs.** Chakra only resolves a token as the *entire* value, so `padding: 'xs 0'` was emitted verbatim and dropped by the browser.
- **1.5px descender leak per nav row.** `<li>` was `display: list-item` wrapping a 24px `inline-flex` anchor, making the links column 9px taller than Figma. Now `display: flex`.
- **Registry generator dropped props silently.** `[^\n;,]+` stopped at a comma, so `Record<string, string>` never matched and the prop vanished. Also unescaped `|` in union types shifted table columns.

### Decisions worth recording

- **Header reverted to `BrandLogo`.** This PR had swapped it for `ZimmLogo`, which orphaned `header.ts`'s `logo` part and rendered the header logo at **327×70 instead of 597×70** — the atom's own `maxWidth: 327px` (a footer dimension) capped it. Out of scope for a footer ticket; raised separately. The header now carries comment-only changes.
- **`utils/cssVars.ts` deleted.** Jersey removed every consumer; this removes the orphaned file.
- **Icon transition kept at 0.15s.** The upstream change routed it through `--zimm-motion-duration-fast`, measured at 0.2s. `button.ts` already records the decision not to retime without designer sign-off, and changing only the icon variants would leave two durations in one file.
- **`foundation/sizes.ts` excluded.** Its only change was a trailing blank line — not worth a Tier 1 review gate.
- **Fonts self-hosted** for development and testing. Touches three Tier 1 files (`.storybook/main.js`, `.storybook/preview.tsx`, `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`), approved by a tier-1-approver. No licence files in the repo.

### Open items for the new PR

- Subscribe column is **21px taller than Figma** — the two inter-element gaps are the only values in that block without a Figma annotation. Needs designer confirmation.
- **768–860px band**: subscribe and nav sit flush and seven labels wrap. Known, unresolved.
- Contact icon hover/disabled opacity (`0.6`/`0.4`) and the header logo's `597×70` have **no design source**.
- Should icon transitions move to the 200ms motion token? If yes, `baseStyle` and the icon variants move together.

content.text:
```
Closing this in favour of a fresh PR — I've taken over the branch from Jersey and
rewrote the history, so the commits and review threads here no longer match what's
on the branch.

What changed materially while working through it:

- The footer recipe was named `Footer`, which extendTheme merged with SFCC's base
  recipe instead of replacing it. Renamed to `ZimmFooter` — that alone fixed the
  copyright rendering at 14px instead of 10px and a missing 24px heading gap.
- Contact icons were sized `xl`, which resolves through theme.sizes (36rem), not
  theme.space. They were rendering at 576px.
- Futura Round is now self-hosted, so local and Storybook match Figma metrics.
  Several sizing decisions made against the fallback font were wrong and got redone.
- `utils/cssVars.ts` is gone; everything reads the `--zimm-*` vars directly.
- The registry generator was silently dropping props with commas in their types and
  breaking table columns on union types. Fixed.
- Added recipe guards and a regression test for `SAFE_HREF_RE`, which had none
  despite a bypass being patched in it earlier.

The work is all preserved — same branch, split into logical commits instead of one
block. New PR to follow.
```

Two things worth knowing before you post it:

- It names the two bugs that were actually shipping wrong pixels, since those are what justify the redo to anyone skimming.
- It doesn't mention the CodeRabbit threads. If you'd rather flag that the unanswered ones carry over, say so and I'll add a line — otherwise they'll just be lost with the closed PR.

Visual check done across both surfaces. **Everything we fixed this session is holding, and the two environments agree.**

## Dev server (localhost:3000)

| Viewport | Result |
|---|---|
| **1440** | Clean. ACK wraps `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT` / `OF COUNTRY`, contact icons indented under CONNECT WITH US, logo and bottom bar correct |
| **768** | The **known band problem**, now visible: 7 labels wrap (`BOUTIQUE LOCATOR`, `BOOK AN APPOINTMENT`, `CONNECT WITH US`, `ORDERS & SHIPPING`, `RETURN POLICY`, `SUBMIT A RETURN`) with subscribe crowding the nav flush against it |
| **375** | Clean stack. Subscribe block, ACK wrap, contact icons, **inset divider above the logo** (this session's fix), stacked bottom bar |

Futura Round confirmed rendering at all three.

## Storybook (localhost:6006)

74 stories, all three adopted ones registered and rendering with **zero page errors**:

- `Layout/Footer / Default` — **matches the dev server exactly**. That's the parity the dual-mounted `ZimmFontFace` was for, now confirmed visually.
- `Elements/ZimmNavItem / Placeholder — No href (or unsafe href)…` — all four rejection cases render, play ran clean.
- `Forms/ZimmInputAction / Submit Validation — empty value` — play executed and produced the real error state: red underline + "Please enter a value."

## One finding — Storybook-only, pre-existing

The submit button renders as an **empty outlined box** in Storybook where the app shows a `>` chevron.

Cause: `chevron-right` maps to `ChevronRightIcon`, which is **re-exported from SFCC**, and `.storybook/main.js` applies `ignore-loader` to SFCC SVGs. Deliberate config with its own comment ("SFCC SVGs are sprite-loaded server-side only") — not a regression, and not caused by our work.

Scope of the gap:

```
ZimmIcon mapped icons : 15
  from our zimm.tsx   :  8  render in Storybook ✅
  from SFCC base      :  7  blank in Storybook ⚠
    chevron-down, chevron-left, chevron-right, chevron-up,
    wishlist-selected, aria-hidden, aria-label
```

**Practical consequence:** any component using one of those 7 can't be visually reviewed in Storybook — including the subscribe field. The `>` renders correctly in the app, so it's a review-tooling gap, not a product bug. Worth a ticket if Storybook is meant to be the design-review surface.

*(The flower graphic overlapping the logo in the dev shots is the third-party consent widget, not our markup.)*

## Two cosmetic notes, both third-party or known

- The consent modal blocks the mobile footer until dismissed — expected, Didomi placeholder.
- Subscribe→sitemap vertical gap still reads large at desktop; that's the Δ21 from the two unannotated `marginBottom` values already on Kiera's list.

Nothing changed on disk — 11 commits ahead, tree clean.

content.text:
Good catch — it was real, and now measurable.

## What was wrong

| Column | Box | Longest line | Slack |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ABOUT** | **160** | **115** | **45px** |
| CONTACT | 135 | 131 | 4 |
| HELP | 105.6 | 105.6 | 0 |

Contact and Help already hugged their content. About sat pinned at `linkCol`'s 160px cap with 45px of dead space, pushing Contact right — exactly the disproportion you spotted against Figma's auto-gap layout.

**Cause:** a wrapped element takes the width *available* to it, not the width of its longest line. The Acknowledgement item wraps, so it filled the 160px cap even though its longest line is 115px.

## The fix

`width: min-content` on that item — it resolves to the widest *unbreakable run*, which the non-breaking space makes exactly `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT` (115px), with the two-line wrap intact.

Applied per instance, gated on the NBSP, because I tested that it's only correct for a deliberately-wrapped label:

```
ACK + min-content       160 → 115   ✅  lines still [115, 69]
Book an Appointment     131 → 76    ✗  collapses to longest word, wraps
```

Keying it off the NBSP ties the sizing to the same signal that already marks the break as intentional.

## Result

```
About  160 → 115px   slack 45 → 0
gaps   99.7 → 122.2px  (evenly redistributed)
```

All three columns now hug their content with the gaps absorbing the remainder — Figma's model. Verified visually, and the wrap holds at 1440/1280/1023/768/375.

`vitest` **168** · Phase 3 **20/20** · Phase 4 geometry unchanged · prettier/eslint clean.

**Committed:** `fcaba93` — now **12 commits ahead**, tree clean.

## Two notes

- This takes the `sx` (rung 4) count from 3 → 4. Justified in the commit body: it's per-instance behaviour the shared recipe can't express, which is exactly what rung 4 is for.
- At 768px the wrap count went 7 → 6, with `Brand Protection` newly wrapping and two others no longer doing so. That band is still the known unresolved one — this shifted it slightly, didn't fix it.

content.text:
Full box-model sweep done — **112 elements, every viewport**. Your concern was justified: it found a real misalignment.

## The clean result

**Zero off-token values.** Every padding, margin, gap and border across all 112 footer elements at 1440/1280/1023/860/768/375 resolves to the spacing scale (2/4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40/52/64/80/128/160) or a documented provisional constant. Borders are all 1px.

**One asymmetry, and it's correct:** `contentRow` padding-Y 64/48 — matches Figma exactly.

The structural tree:

```
footer                          1440 × 489
  contentRow    pad 64/40/48/40   1440 × 275
    subscribe                      320 × 163    heading mb 24 · body mb 40 · field 45
    links                          600 × 163    columns 115 / 135 / 105.6, gap 16
  logoArea      pad 48/40/48/40   1440 × 135    logo 327 × 39
  bottomInner   pad 24/40/24/40   1440 × 79     locale py 8 · legal py 8, gap 32
```

## The bug it found

`contentRow` and `logoArea` step their gutter 32→40px at **BP.tablet (768)**. `bottomInner` held 32px until **BP.desktop (1024)**.

So across the entire **768–1023px band** the bottom bar was inset 8px less than the content above it — on **both** edges. The locale control and legal links sat left of the subscribe column and the logo.

```
         subscribe / locale
1440        40 / 40   aligned
1023        40 / 32   -8   ⚠
 900        40 / 32   -8   ⚠
 768        40 / 32   -8   ⚠
 375        32 / 32   aligned
```

They already agreed at desktop *and* mobile, so alignment was clearly the intent — the breakpoint was just the odd one out. This is almost certainly the residue of the copyright/legal-row misalignment you flagged earlier in the session: fixed at desktop, never harmonised at tablet.

**Fixed** — moved the gutter step to `BP.tablet`. Now 0px delta at every width.

## Verification

`vitest` **168** · Phase 3 **20/20** · Phase 4 paddings all ✅ · prettier clean · box audit re-run: **0 off-token at all six viewports**.

**Committed:** `b88a9e4` — **13 commits ahead**, tree clean.

## What the sweep did *not* find

No stray borders, no unintended asymmetries, no off-scale gaps. The three known deltas are unchanged and all previously documented: subscribe Δ+21 (the two unannotated `marginBottom`s pending Kiera), locale Δ+7 (the WCAG 2.5.8 target-size trade), links Δ+5.

The 768–860px wrapping band remains the one genuinely unresolved layout issue — separate from this, and still open.

content.text:
You're right, and it's a rule violation rather than a styling slip.

## What's happening

`zimm.tsx` defines **no chevrons at all**. All four, plus `wishlist-selected`, are substituted from Salesforce's base set:

```
OURS — stroked line art (8)          SUBSTITUTED FROM SFCC (5)
  arrow-down                           chevron-down
  arrow-link                           chevron-left
  arrow-up                             chevron-right      ← the one you spotted
  bag-selected                         chevron-up
  carousel-selected                    wishlist-selected
  external-link
  info-selected
  share-2
```

The visual mismatch is systematic:

```
SFCC chevron-right   viewBox 0 0 24 24   fill="currentColor"        solid filled wedge
Zimmermann icons     viewBox 0 0 20 20   stroke="currentColor"      thin line art
                                          fill="none"
```

So it's not a slightly-different chevron — it's a **filled Material-style glyph sitting among stroked Zimmermann line art**. Different weight, different construction, different viewBox.

## This is explicitly against the project rule

AGENTS.md:

> **Icons:** … If a required icon is missing from the overrides set, **ask the user — do not substitute a visually different one.**

Five icons were substituted rather than flagged. Pre-existing — it dates from whenever `zimmIcon` was scaffolded, not from this PR.

## Where it shows

`chevron-right` renders in three live places:
- `footer/index.tsx:249` — the subscribe field's submit button (the `>` you see)
- `footer/index.tsx:346` — the locale control's trailing chevron
- `zimmInputAction` default `icon` prop — so any future input-action inherits it

It's also why the Storybook check earlier showed an **empty box** there: `.storybook/main.js` `ignore-loader`s SFCC SVGs, so substituted icons don't render in Storybook at all.

## What I'd do — and what I won't

I'm **not** going to swap in a different icon or hand-draw one. The rule says ask, and picking a substitute is exactly what created this.

What's needed is the real asset. For Kiera:

> The footer submit and locale controls render Salesforce's filled `chevron-right`, not a Zimmermann one — `zimm.tsx` has no chevron. Same for chevron-up/down/left and `wishlist-selected`. Can we get these five exported from the design system as stroked line art matching `arrow-link` (20×20, `stroke="currentColor"`, `fill="none"`)?

Once the assets land, the change is small: add them to `zimm.tsx`, and the barrel's five SFCC re-exports drop out. That also fixes the Storybook blank-icon gap for free, since our own icons aren't `ignore-loader`ed.

Want me to check whether Figma exposes those chevrons as components I can pull the geometry from — or leave it entirely with Kiera?

Use this skill to turn a Figma design into code in a target codebase. This is the **read-FROM-Figma** direction: pull design context out of Figma with `get_design_context`, then adapt it into the project's real stack. This skill owns the **workflow** for design-to-code. Parameter mechanics (nodeId / fileKey / branchKey extraction, URL parsing, `format`/`query` options, response shape) live on the `get_design_context` tool description itself — follow them there.

- You MUST NOT write code until G1 and G2-G4 pass. You MUST NOT finish until G5 passes.
- Gates are self-checks. You MUST NOT change the implementation solely to produce gate evidence.

### 1. Call get_design_context first

- If the response is sparse metadata, request only the visible child regions needed to implement the target, preferably in one parallel batch.

### 3. Reuse what the project already has

- Before writing new code, You MUST check likely project-owned paths for existing components, layout patterns, and design tokens that match the design intent.
- You MUST reuse the project's existing components and tokens instead of generating new equivalents from scratch.

### 4. Honor the response hints by priority

You MUST apply only hint sources that are present and relevant, in this order — earlier sources override later ones:

1. **Code Connect snippets** → use the mapped codebase component directly.
2. **Component documentation links** → follow them for usage and guidelines.
3. **Design annotations** → follow any designer notes or constraints.
4. **Design tokens (CSS variables)** → map them to the project's token system.

G2-G4 PASS - `<stack/path; reuse search/result; present hints/application>`

### 5. Reproduce images and icons faithfully

Images and icons come back as exported assets. Apply these rules as you write the code:

- **Render every icon/image from its exported asset.** Never author, redraw, omit, or replace it with a placeholder or screenshot.
- **Sourcing:** remote asset URLs expire in ~7 days. For committed code, download the exact bytes or use the project's data source.
- **Reuse a project icon component only if its glyph clearly matches**; otherwise use the exported asset.
- **Preserve designed geometry:** You MUST preserve the outer asset box and inner leaf separately, including both dimensions, padding, and aspect ratio.
- Relative fill sizing is allowed only if you verified the container constrains the leaf; otherwise set both leaf dimensions explicitly. You MUST NOT use `auto` for a fixed-size leaf.
- You MUST NOT apply one global size to unlike assets or stretch assets through broad descendant rules.

#### G5 - Asset Fidelity

To pass G5:
- You MUST use the correct source for every asset.
- You MUST verify one representative of each shared sizing rule and every exception preserves intended outer and leaf dimensions.
- You MUST NOT pass on source evidence alone when geometry is unverified.

G5 PASS - `<sources; sizing rules and exceptions; rendered or explicit-dimension evidence>`

Otherwise G5 is `FAIL`. You MUST fix it before finishing.

- On a `get_design_context` error, STOP and read the message before retrying.
- If the design URL has no `node-id` (a file-only URL), ask the user for a node-specific URL — You MUST NOT guess or pass an empty `nodeId`.
- On a timeout, retry against a smaller node or selection.
- You MUST NOT silently fall back to hand-writing the screen from the screenshot alone when `get_design_context` can still provide context.

Got it — and it confirms your observation with hard numbers.

## Figma's chevron

```svg
<path d="M0.312348 0.390434L7.81235 6.39044L15.3123 0.390434" stroke="#191919"/>
```

A **stroked two-segment polyline**. No fill. Stroke-width 1 (the 15.62 × 7.03 export box against a 15 × 6 path is exactly the 0.5px bleed each side). `#191919` = `grey[900]` in `colour.ts:8`, i.e. `text.default`.

Node metadata: **6 × 15 at (9, 4.5)** — centred in a 24×24 frame, exported unrotated so it reads as a `v`.

Normalised to a right-pointing 24×24 icon:

```
M 9 4.5  L 15 12  L 9 19.5
```

Steep and narrow: 6px wide, 15px tall.

## Against what we ship

| | Figma | SFCC (ours) |
|---|---|---|
| Render | `stroke`, `fill="none"` | **`fill="currentColor"`** |
| Weight | 1px line | solid wedge |
| Geometry | 6 × 15, two segments | ~7 × 12 filled mass in 24×24 |
| Caps/joins | default (butt / miter) | n/a — it's a filled outline |

So it's not a near-miss. We're rendering a **solid filled glyph where the design is a hairline stroke** — which is why it reads heavier and blunter than the frame next to it, and why it clashes with `arrow-link` and the contact icons, which are all stroked.

## What I'd add — pending your go-ahead

This slots straight into `zimm.tsx` alongside the existing stroked icons:

```tsx
export const ChevronRightIcon = createIcon({
  displayName: 'ChevronRightIcon',
  viewBox: '0 0 24 24',
  // Figma node 40002182:52552 — stroked polyline, 6x15 centred in 24x24.
  path: <path d="M9 4.5L15 12L9 19.5" stroke="currentColor" fill="none" />,
});
```

`currentColor` rather than `#191919`, so it inherits — same as every other icon in that file, and it needs to render inverse in the footer.

Then `icons/index.tsx` drops `ChevronRightIcon` from the SFCC re-export list, and it starts rendering in Storybook too (our icons aren't `ignore-loader`ed).

## Two things before I touch anything

**The other three chevrons.** This node is right-only. `chevron-left`, `chevron-up` and `chevron-down` are still SFCC-sourced. They're presumably the same vector rotated, and I could derive them — but deriving isn't the same as taking the designer's asset, and AGENTS.md is explicit about not substituting. Do you want me to pull their nodes from Figma too? If you have the node IDs or the icon-set frame ID, I'll fetch all four properly.

**Stroke-width.** Figma's is 1 at 24×24. Our `ZimmIcon` renders at `sm` (12px) and `md` (16px) — at 12px a 1px stroke scales to 0.5px and will look thin/blurry. Worth checking whether Figma specs a different weight at smaller sizes, or whether the icon is only ever used at 24.

Say the word and I'll add it — nothing committed.

  ---
  
  ## Play 3 — Component completeness & variant review
  
  *Covers responsibilities 9, 11*
  
  M2's rule: a component isn't complete until it covers all supported variants, and the page just configures it. One Editorial Card, not a Homepage one and a PLP one.
  
  ### The distinction to hold
  
  | Kind | Examples | How it's built |
  |---|---|---|
  | **Configuration variant** | text alignment, CTA on/off, title on/off, body copy present/absent | Props on one component ✅ Tim's rule applies directly |
  | **Composition variant** | 1 vs 2 column, 3-up vs 4-up grids | A **container/slot component** — structurally a second component |
  
  This matters because a composition variant priced as a prop will be under-estimated. On the Studio Experiences path especially, a repeating structure can't be a prop — the composition primitive is `children`.
