Yes — and it's your own rule, Play 3 of the playbook:

> *"a component isn't complete until it covers all supported variants, and the page just configures it."*

Whether it binds the chevrons is a real question, so let me give you both sides honestly.

**The rule's stated rationale doesn't apply.** Play 3 justifies "upfront" specifically on Contentful: *"the sync is additive-only — it cannot delete a field from a published content type. Getting the variant model wrong isn't rework, it's semi-permanent."* Icons aren't Contentful-backed. Adding `chevron-left` next month costs nothing irreversible.

**But the rule's text does apply, and something stronger does too.** Play 3's own table puts this squarely in the **configuration variant** column — "props on one component". `ZimmIcon`'s `type` prop *is* that axis, and it already declares all four chevrons in its union, with all four listed in its stories. So the atom's public API already claims to support them.

That's the real point: this isn't *"three variants not yet built."* It's **four variants built wrong** — all four currently render Salesforce's filled glyph against a stroked design language. Fixing only `chevron-right` would leave one atom rendering two different icon languages depending on the prop value, which is worse than the status quo's consistent wrongness.

Add AGENTS.md's icon rule — *"do not substitute a visually different one"* — which all four violate equally, and I'd say: **yes, do all four, but not because of Play 3.** Because a half-corrected atom is incoherent.

## Answer to your question

**Yes, the rule applies — but not for the reason Play 3 gives.**

Play 3's "upfront is a hard requirement" argument is explicitly Contentful-based: additive-only sync, can't delete a published field, so a wrong variant model is semi-permanent. **None of that is true for icons.**

What does bind here is simpler and stronger: `ZimmIcon` already declares all four chevrons in its `type` union and lists all four in its stories. The atom's API *claims* to support them. So this isn't three unbuilt variants — it's **four variants built wrong**, all rendering Salesforce's filled glyph in a stroked design language.

Fix only `chevron-right` and one atom renders two different icon languages depending on the prop value. That's worse than the current consistent wrongness. Play 3's table also puts these squarely in the **configuration variant** column — "props on one component" — which is exactly what it says must be complete.

So: do all four. Plus `wishlist-selected`, which is the fifth SFCC substitution and has the same problem.

## What I need

I have `chevron-right` confirmed from Figma:

```
M 9 4.5 L 15 12 L 9 19.5    stroke, fill:none, 1px, 6×15 centred in 24×24
```

For the rest, either:

**A — send me the node URLs** (or the `Icons` component-set URL and I'll enumerate). Cleanest: every icon comes from the designer's asset, exactly per AGENTS.md.

**B — I derive the other three by rotating this one.** A chevron is symmetric, so rotation is mathematically exact — `left` is `M 15 4.5 L 9 12 L 15 19.5`, and up/down are the 90° cases. Fast, and arguably not "substituting a visually different icon" since it's the same confirmed vector. But it's still me generating an asset rather than taking one, and `wishlist-selected` can't be derived at all — that needs a real export.

I'd go with A if Kiera's reachable, B only if you want it unblocked today with a note on the PR that three were derived and need sign-off.

Also still open regardless of which: **stroke-width at small sizes.** Figma's is 1px at 24×24, but `ZimmIcon` renders `sm` at 12px and `md` at 16px — a 1px stroke scales to 0.5px at `sm` and will look thin or blur on non-retina. Can't walk up the tree — `get_metadata` returns only the queried node, and there's one page with no navigable index from a leaf.

## On the rule — yes, it applies

Play 3: *"a component isn't complete until it covers all supported variants, and the page just configures it."*

But the playbook's stated justification — Contentful being additive-only, so a wrong variant model is semi-permanent — **doesn't apply here.** `ZimmIcon`'s `type` is a TypeScript union we can extend any time. Nothing is semi-permanent.

The argument that does apply is stronger:

```ts
type ZimmIconType = … | 'chevron-down' | 'chevron-left' | 'chevron-right' | 'chevron-up' | …
```

**The atom already declares all four.** Three currently render Salesforce's filled glyph. So this isn't "should we build variants we don't need yet" — the component is publicly advertising a surface it doesn't correctly fulfil. Shipping only `chevron-right` would leave that worse: one correct chevron and three wrong ones in the same union, which is harder to spot than four consistently wrong ones.

By the same logic `wishlist-selected` is in scope too — same substitution, same union.

## What the Figma node tells us

The exported path is **15 × 6**, but the node sits in-frame at **6 × 15**. Figma is rendering it *rotated*. So the design system itself builds the chevron set by rotating one base glyph — which means deriving left/up/down is reproducing the designer's own construction, not substituting a different icon. That distinction matters against the AGENTS.md rule.

Derived from the confirmed geometry, in a 24×24 box:

```
right   M 9 4.5   L 15 12   L 9 19.5     ← confirmed from Figma
left    M 15 4.5  L 9 12    L 15 19.5
up      M 4.5 15  L 12 9    L 19.5 15
down    M 4.5 9   L 12 15   L 19.5 9
```

## Two open questions I can't resolve from here

**1. I'd rather confirm than derive.** Send me the `Icons` component-set node URL (or the four chevron nodes) and I'll pull each one properly instead of rotating. If you'd rather not chase it, deriving is defensible here — but confirming is cheap and it's the designer's asset either way.

**2. Stroke weight at small sizes.** Figma's stroke is 1px at 24×24. `ZimmIcon` renders at `sm` 12px and `md` 16px — at 12px that scales to a 0.5px line, which will look washed out. Does the design system spec a heavier weight at smaller sizes, or is the chevron only used at 24? Worth asking Kiera alongside `wishlist-selected`.

Tell me which way you want to go — confirm all four from Figma, or derive the three — and whether to include `wishlist-selected` in the same pass. I won't commit anything without your go.

content.text:
I verified this myself rather than relying on the earlier report. Here's what I found.

## Atoms and molecules — all built, all used

Six components exist in the ui-kit, and `footer/index.tsx` imports and renders **all six**:

| Component | Footer render sites |
|---|---|
| `ZimmLogo` | 1 — line 487 |
| `ZimmIcon` | 3 — 300, 313, 346 |
| `ZimmNavItem` | 2 — 357, 461 |
| `ZimmButton` | 2 — 184, 185 |
| `ZimmTextInput` | 2 — 162, 167 (modal name fields) |
| `ZimmInputAction` | 1 — 245 (subscribe field) |

No missing atom, no missing molecule, nothing built-but-unused. Confirms the correction — `ZimmInputAction` *is* used.

Four sub-components live inside `footer/index.tsx` — `SubscribeModal`, `SubscribeSection`, `ContactIconRow`, `BottomBar`. `components.md` permits internal sub-components without their own stories, so that's conformant, but they sit outside ui-kit governance.

## Variants and states — six gaps, one that matters

| Component | Stories | Uncovered props |
|---|---|---|
| `ZimmButton` | 23 | — (all covered; `fullWidth` only on `primary`) |
| `ZimmIcon` | 5 | `color` |
| `ZimmLogo` | 4 | — complete |
| `ZimmNavItem` | 8 | `onClick` |
| `ZimmTextInput` | 7 | **`trailing`**, `value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange` |
| `ZimmInputAction` | 8 | `disabled` |

**The one that matters is `ZimmTextInput.trailing`.** It has zero story coverage and **one production usage** — `zimmInputAction/index.tsx:69`, which is how the submit button gets into the subscribe field. So the mechanism behind the footer's entire subscribe control is only ever exercised indirectly, through the molecule's stories. If `trailing` broke, `ZimmTextInput`'s own stories would all still pass.

`onChange` is the same shape — one production usage, no direct coverage.

**The rest are weaker:** `value`/`defaultValue` have **zero** production usages (the component is uncontrolled; the `Filled` story types into it via `play` instead), `ZimmInputAction.disabled` isn't used in the footer, `ZimmIcon.color` and `ZimmNavItem.onClick` are unused API surface.

One correction to the earlier report: it claimed `secondary × fullWidth` was untested. `fullWidth` is genuinely only exercised on `primary` — but its extractor missed `zimmButton`'s intersection types entirely, so it under-reported that component's surface. Same regex limitation we hit in the registry generator.

## Against Play 3

*"A component isn't complete until it covers all supported variants."* By that bar, `ZimmTextInput` is the one genuinely incomplete atom in the footer build — a load-bearing prop with no direct test.

The honest counter: `value`/`defaultValue`/`color`/`onClick` are declared-but-unused API. Story coverage for props nothing calls is lower value than `trailing`, and arguably the better fix for some is to drop the prop rather than test it.

## Suggestion

One story on `ZimmTextInput` covering `trailing` + `onChange` closes the real gap. The other five are worth logging but not worth holding this PR for.

Want me to add that story?

content.text:
Confirmed live. Here's what `trailing` is and why the story matters.

## What `trailing` is

It's a **slot** — nothing more:

```tsx
trailing?: React.ReactNode;
...
{trailing}          // line 110, rendered after the clear button
```

`ZimmTextInput` has no idea what goes in it. `ZimmInputAction` passes the submit button in:

```tsx
<ZimmTextInput
  trailing={<ZimmButton variant="icon" icon="chevron-right" type="submit" … />}
/>
```

So `trailing` is **the entire mechanism that connects the atom to the molecule.** It's how the `>` gets inside the email field. Break it and the footer's subscribe control loses its submit button — and every `ZimmTextInput` story would still pass, because none of them use it.

## Why it's more than a coverage gap

The code comments document a known collision, and I verified it's live:

```
empty field  → ["Subscribe"]
with value   → ["Clear input", "Subscribe"]
```

Type into the footer field and you get **✕ and >** side by side (screenshot above). Figma shows one control.

The comment explains why: the clear-✕ was added on the belief that Figma's trailing glyph was an ✕. Kiera confirmed on 20 Aug it's the chevron — which now lives in `trailing`. So the field renders two trailing controls where the design has one. It was kept rather than deleted, pending her answer on whether the field should have a clear affordance at all.

Right now that entire situation is recorded **only in a code comment.** Nothing tests it, nothing fails if someone "tidies up" either control.

## So what would the story actually be

Three assertions, on `ZimmTextInput` directly:

1. **`trailing` renders at all** — pass a node, assert it's in the document. Currently unproven.
2. **Ordering** — it renders *after* the clear button, not before. That's the designed stacking and nothing pins it.
3. **The collision** — with a value present, both the clear-✕ and the trailing node appear.

Assertion 3 is the valuable one. It doesn't declare the collision correct — it **pins the current behaviour so Kiera's decision has something to flip.** If she says drop the clear-✕, that test fails loudly and tells you exactly what changed. If she says keep both, the test documents that it's deliberate.

Without it, the collision lives in a comment that a future refactor will quietly delete.

## Scope

One story, maybe 25 lines, in `zimmTextInput/index.stories.tsx`. It also closes `onChange` if I assert the value round-trip in the same play.

Want me to write it?

The ✕ is a **separate, hardcoded element** on its own condition, sitting just above it:

content.text:
## The mental model

`trailing` is **an empty slot** at the right-hand end of the input. Not an icon. Not the ✕. Just a hole you can put any element into.

```tsx
trailing?: React.ReactNode      // "put whatever you want here"
```

`ZimmInputAction` puts **the chevron** in that hole. That's the whole job.

The ✕ is a **completely different thing** — hardcoded inside the input, with its own rule: *"if the field has text, show me."* It doesn't know `trailing` exists, and `trailing` doesn't know it exists.

Two separate things that happen to sit next to each other:

```
[ Email: someone@example.com          ✕    >  ]
                                      ↑     ↑
                              hardcoded    the slot
                              (not spec'd) (spec'd)
```

## Where the mix-up came from

The original belief was: *Figma's glyph is an ✕* → so someone built the ✕.

Kiera then said: *it's a chevron* → so the chevron went into the `trailing` slot.

But **nobody removed the ✕.** So now you get both.

## The bit that inverts your conclusion

You said "now we know it's a chevron, there's no more trailing."

I overstated it. You're right to push — here's the corrected position.

## `trailing` is already covered

Three of `ZimmInputAction`'s play functions do this:

```tsx
canvas.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i })
```

That button **only exists because `trailing` works.** If `trailing` stopped rendering, those three plays fail immediately — `getByRole` throws. So a regression *would* be caught, just one level up.

My earlier framing — "if `trailing` broke, every `ZimmTextInput` story would still pass" — was true but misleading. The molecule's tests are the ones that matter here, and they cover it.

**So a dedicated `trailing` story adds close to nothing.** Scratch that recommendation.

## What's genuinely untested

The **collision**. Phase 3 asserts:

```
✅ clear button appears on value
✅ clear button empties the field
```

Both about the ✕ alone. Nothing anywhere asserts that when you type, **two** controls appear side by side. Not in the atom's stories, not the molecule's, not Phase 3.

So the real gap is one assertion, not a story:

> with a value present, the input row contains exactly two buttons — `Clear input` and `Subscribe`

## But even that's arguably the wrong move

That test would pin behaviour we already believe is **wrong** — Figma shows one control, we render two. Writing a test to lock in a known defect, so it can be deleted next week when Kiera answers, is busywork.

The better sequence:

1. **Ask Kiera** — should the footer email field have a clear affordance at all?
2. **If no** (likely — it's not in the spec): delete the ✕ block, 5 lines. Phase 3's two clear-button assertions go with it. No new test needed.
3. **If yes**: *then* it's a real designed behaviour, and it's worth a story showing both controls together.

## Net answer to your question

Nothing is missing on `trailing`. It works, and it's covered transitively by three play functions.

The only untested thing is a two-control state that's probably a bug, and the fix for a bug is to remove it, not to test it. I'd leave both alone until Kiera answers — and that question is already on her list.

## Fact — these hold up

- **One production usage** — `zimmInputAction/index.tsx:69`. True.
- **"Only ever exercised indirectly, through the molecule's stories."** Also literally true.

## Overstated — the framing around those facts

I presented "exercised indirectly" as a *deficiency*. It isn't. `trailing` is a **slot prop** — its whole purpose is to receive something from a consumer. Testing it through the consumer that fills it is the *correct* level, not a lesser substitute.

And I said: *"If `trailing` broke, `ZimmTextInput`'s own stories would all still pass."* True in isolation, but I used it to imply a regression would slip through. It wouldn't — three `getByRole('button', {name: /submit/i})` calls in `ZimmInputAction`'s plays would throw immediately.

That's a wrong call. It's complete in the sense that matters, and I recommended a story that would have added close to nothing.

## Why it happened

I ran a mechanical audit: *for each declared prop, count references in that component's story file.* That's a smoke detector, and a reasonable one — but it can't distinguish:

- a prop with no coverage anywhere,
- from a prop covered by its consumer,
- from a prop nothing uses at all.

## Genuinely missing: nothing

Every prop and state that's actually used in the footer is covered — directly or by the consumer that fills it.

**States** are the part I hadn't checked properly. |---|---|

content.text:
## The bug

**`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmTextInput/index.tsx`, lines 105–110**

```tsx
105  {!disabled && value.length > 0 && (
106    <chakra.button type="button" aria-label="Clear input" onClick={handleClear} __css={styles.clearButton}>
107      <ZimmIcon type="close" size="sm" aria-hidden={true} />
108    </chakra.button>
109  )}
110  {trailing}
```

Two trailing controls render back to back. Line 105–109 is the ✕; line 110 is the slot holding the chevron.

## What it looks like

```
empty field  → ["Subscribe"]
with value   → ["Clear input", "Subscribe"]
```

Measured live. On screen you get **✕ followed by >** inside the field once you type — the screenshot from earlier.

Figma specs **one** trailing control.

## Where you'll see it

The **footer subscribe field**. Empty state is correct — only the chevron. Type anything and the ✕ appears next to it.

Also anywhere else `ZimmTextInput` gets a `trailing` node, but `ZimmInputAction` is currently the only consumer that passes one.

## Why it exists

The ✕ was built on the belief that Figma's trailing glyph was an ✕. Kiera confirmed on 20 Aug it's the chevron, and the chevron went into `trailing` — but nobody removed the ✕. It's leftover from the wrong reading.

Confirmed against the extracted spec on Han's branch: `trailing-icon` is a documented attribute; there is **no** `clearable` attribute and no clear control anywhere in that spec.

## The fix

Delete lines 105–109. That's it — `trailing` and the chevron are untouched.

Two things go with it: `handleClear` in `useZimmTextInputState` becomes unused, and Phase 3's two assertions (`clear button appears on value`, `clear button empties the field`) would need removing, since they test the deleted control.

## Why it's still there

It's deliberately parked, with a comment explaining why, pending Kiera answering: **should the footer email field have a clear affordance at all?** If she says yes, it's a legitimate design addition and the collision needs resolving in layout instead. If she says no — which the spec implies — it's a straight delete.

That question is already on her list. I'd not touch it until she answers.

content.text:
That settles it — and it corrects me.

```
<!-- managed-by: /extract | do-not-edit -->
**Extracted:** 2026-07-16
**Status:** draft
```

The spec is a **mechanical extraction** from Figma's `TextfieldV2` node, marked **draft**, and over a month old. So the absence of a `clearable` attribute means *the Figma component doesn't have one* — **not** that the design system has ruled one out. That's absence of evidence, not evidence of absence, and I presented it as the latter.

## What we actually know

| | Status |
|---|---|
| Figma `TextfieldV2` (16 Jul) has a `trailing-icon` slot, no clear | ✅ Verified |
| Kiera confirmed the footer field's trailing glyph is the chevron, not an ✕ | ✅ Per the code comment, 20 Aug |
| Whether a clear affordance should exist at all | ❌ **Unanswered** |

Kiera answered **which glyph**. That's a different question from **whether a clear control belongs**. The code comment says so itself — it's parked "pending Kiera's answer on whether the footer email field should have a clear affordance at all."

## What *is* certain

The current state is wrong: two trailing controls where the footer Figma frame shows one. That much holds regardless.

What's **not** certain is the fix.

## And there's a third option I skipped

I framed it as delete-or-keep. But `ZimmTextInput` is an **atom** — a clear affordance is a perfectly reasonable general text-input feature even if the footer doesn't want it. A search field probably does.

So the likely-correct shape isn't "delete" — it's:

```tsx
clearable?: boolean;   // default false
```

Footer's subscribe field doesn't opt in, so it renders one control and matches Figma. A future search field opts in. Nothing is lost, and the atom stops making the decision for its consumers.

That's better than either of the options I gave you, and it's the one I'd put to Kiera.

## Revised question for her

Not *"should we delete the clear button?"* but:

> The text input currently always shows a clear ✕ once it has a value, alongside whatever trailing icon the consumer passes — so the footer email field shows ✕ and > together, where the frame shows one. Two questions: should the footer field have a clear affordance at all, and should clear be an opt-in prop on the atom for fields that do want it (search, say)?

So: **not certain, and my "the spec implies no clear" was overstated.** What's certain is that the footer renders one control too many.

Confirmed live: fill both and the modal shows **2** clear buttons — **3** on the page, counting the subscribe field's.

So the ✕ appears in three places, and the two-control collision only happens on the subscribe field, because that's the only one with a `trailing` node.

## Where it started

```
cf6edcd  Jersey Perez  2026-08-17 14:51
feat(footer): SFCC-55 global footer UI — atoms, molecules, subscribe modal, and Figma token alignment
```

The original footer commit — 17 Aug, on this branch only, never on `develop`. It's been in every version since. `handleClear` in the hook came a day later (`d83d20c`, 18 Aug), and the file moved into `atoms/` on the 19th, which is why a naive search points at the later commits.

So it's Jersey's, from the initial build, and it's never left this branch. Nothing published it to `develop`.

## What I'd do with it

**Not delete it.** I said that earlier and I'd walk it back — a clear affordance on a *text input atom* is reasonable, and the modal's name fields are a plausible place to want one. The problem isn't that it exists; it's that it's **unconditional**.

The atom currently decides for every consumer. Make it opt-in:

```tsx
clearable?: boolean;   // default false
```

Then:
- **Subscribe field** — doesn't opt in. Renders the chevron only. Matches Figma.
- **Modal name fields** — you decide whether they opt in.
- **Future search field** — opts in.

That fixes the collision without discarding working, tested behaviour, and stops the atom imposing a decision its consumers should make.

## But it still needs Kiera

Two questions, and neither is answered:

1. Should the footer email field have a clear affordance at all?
2. Should the modal name fields?

The extracted spec has no `clearable` attribute — but as we established, that spec is a mechanical Figma extraction marked **draft** from 16 July, so it describes what `TextfieldV2` contains, not what's been decided.

My recommendation: propose `clearable` opt-in as the shape, and let her answer which fields opt in. That way the code change doesn't block on the design answer — only the per-field defaults do.

content.text:
It settles the question — not by ruling the ✕ out, but by removing the last reason to think it was ever asked for.

## What the AC actually specifies

> *"the Stay in Touch section is displayed with **an email input field and submit button** as a placeholder component."*

Two elements. Input, submit. The ✕ is a **third element nobody requested.**

Three things reinforce that:

- **"Figma is leading."** Stated explicitly, and Figma shows one trailing glyph — the chevron Kiera confirmed.
- **Scope is "the footer shell, layout, and component structure only."** A clear affordance is interaction behaviour, not structure.
- **"as a placeholder component"** — the whole section is a placeholder pending Omneo.

So: the ticket, the design, and the extracted spec all describe input + submit. The ✕ came from the wrong reading of the Figma glyph and nothing else.

## What it doesn't do

It doesn't *forbid* a clear. Kiera could still say the atom should have one. But the question shifts from *"is this required?"* — clearly not — to *"do we want it?"*, which supports the `clearable` opt-in shape: default off, so the footer matches the AC and Figma, available if a future field wants it.

**On current evidence I'd default it off and ship matching the AC.**

## Two adjacent things the ticket raises

**1. The subscribe modal may be out of scope.** The AC says input + submit. It says nothing about a modal capturing First Name and Last Name — and *"email sign-up Omneo integration [is] covered in separate stories."* Yet we've built `SubscribeModal` with two name fields, consent copy, and Cancel/Continue.

Jasmijn's 7 July note says they *"signed off with Dani & Vicky: ... seeing the behavior of email sign up,"* so it may well have been agreed verbally. But it isn't in the written AC, and **SFCC-T120 ("Stay in Touch section renders") won't test it** — QA writing from that AC will check for a field and a button.

Worth confirming before QA drafts those seven test cases, all still Draft.

**2. The hover AC is met.** Jasmijn added it specifically on 7 July because it was an open item rather than an AC:

> *"the rollover state will be that that word or those words are underlined"*

Phase 3 covers it — `nav hover underline appears` and `nav hover underline reverts`, both passing.

## Suggested line for Kiera

> The AC specifies the Stay in Touch section as an email field plus submit button, and Figma shows a single trailing chevron. We currently also render a clear ✕ whenever the field has a value, so the subscribe field shows two controls. Proposal: make clear an opt-in prop on the text input, default off — footer matches the AC and Figma, and the option stays available for fields that want it. Do the modal's name fields want it?

History is in good shape. Here's the assessment.

## Clean

**All 16 conform** to the conventional-commits pattern the `commit-msg` hook enforces — types, scopes, subject lengths.

**No churn.** Nothing added by one of our commits is deleted by another. No file appears then disappears.

**No broken intermediate states.** I checked the riskiest case — commit 3 deletes `utils/cssVars.ts` — and no commit at any point in the range imports it after deletion. Each commit stands on its own.

**Commit 1 is honest.** Its message describes the registry fix, and after the rebase conflict resolution its *content* is the validated hybrid — `preferredTypeName`, `escapeCell`, `BASE_CACHE_SCHEMA = 3`. It doesn't carry my superseded implementation.

**The header revert reads correctly.** The `<ZimmLogo style=` swap was introduced in `cf6edcd` — **below our range**, in the original footer commit — and reverted in our commit 8. So the history shows a change made earlier and undone later, which is exactly what happened. We're not undoing our own work.

## The one blemish

```
9 commits touch .claude/registry/components.md
3 commits touch .claude/registry/hooks.md
```

That's the `pre-commit` hook auto-regenerating the registry on any `components/`, `hooks/` or `utils/` change, then `git add`-ing it. So 9 of 16 commits carry registry noise a reviewer has to scroll past.

It's the hook working as designed, not something we did — and squashing wouldn't fix it, since the hook would just regenerate on the squashed commit. I'd leave it and mention it in the PR description so reviewers know to skip those hunks.

`footer/index.tsx` at 3 commits is legitimate: the build, the ContactIconRow wiring, the About column fix. Three distinct concerns.

## Shape

Dependencies run downhill — tooling → fonts → atoms → composite → assembly → tests → adoptions → fixes. Commits 9–11 (the adoptions from Jersey's work) sit after the rebase rather than being folded into the conflict resolution, which was deliberate: it keeps "what we took from upstream and why" visible instead of buried in a merge.

## Before you push

`git push --force-with-lease` — history was rewritten by the rebase. The `--force-with-lease` matters: if Jersey has pushed anything since, it aborts rather than clobbering.

content.text:
I have the pattern. All four use the same 8 sections, plain conventional title with no SFCC key, and `Linked` carries a ticket line (with epic + Confluence reference) plus a sprint line.

## Proposed title

```
feat(footer): global footer UI — shell, layout, and ui-kit component structure
```

Matches your convention: conventional prefix, descriptive, no ticket key.

## Proposed body

````markdown
# Description

Builds the global footer per SFCC-55 — shell, layout, and component structure across
all eight storefronts and both breakpoints. Content is Contentful-shaped but
fixture-backed: the CMS integration, link destinations, and Omneo sign-up are
separate stories, so `FooterContainer` supplies `FOOTER_FIXTURE` and `Footer` itself
takes its content as a required prop and fetches nothing.

Six ui-kit atoms/molecules were built or completed alongside it — logo, icon,
nav-item, button, text-input, and the input-action molecule — all six consumed by
the footer.

Three points worth surfacing before review:

- **Fonts are now self-hosted**, reversing the position stated in #53. Futura Round
  renders in-app and in Storybook from one shared `@font-face` module. The fallback
  stack measures ~13% wider, so several sizing decisions made against it were wrong
  and were redone once real metrics were in play. Licence files are deliberately
  excluded from the repository.
- **This branch was taken over from Jersey.** Their three CodeRabbit-fix commits are
  in the history; the parts worth keeping were adopted deliberately as separate
  commits (`fix(button)`, `feat(footer)`, `test(ui-kit)`) rather than folded into
  conflict resolution, so what came from upstream and why stays visible.
- **9 of the 16 new commits carry `.claude/registry/` churn.** The `pre-commit` hook
  regenerates it on any `components/`/`hooks/`/`utils/` change and `git add`s it.
  Mechanical — skip those hunks.

# Linked

- Ticket: **SFCC-55** (Global Footer UI) under epic **SFCC-1**. Design: Figma
  *Zimmermann_Design_System_2026*; footer frames signed off with Dani & Vicky
  (2026-07-07). Test cases SFCC-T116 – SFCC-T122
- Sprint: SFCC — Sprint 3

# Squad ownership

- [x] Squad A

# Types of Changes

- [x] **New feature** (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

# Changes

- `components/footer/` — footer assembly, subscribe section + modal, contact icon row,
  bottom bar; Contentful-shaped fixture and schema placeholder
- `theme/components/footer.ts` — the `ZimmFooter` multipart recipe. Named `ZimmFooter`,
  not `Footer`: `extendTheme` deep-merges, so a recipe sharing a base SFCC recipe's name
  inherits it rather than replacing it
- `components/ui-kits/` — six atoms/molecules; `cssVars` indirection removed in favour of
  the `--zimm-*` custom properties directly, and `utils/cssVars.ts` deleted
- `theme/fontFace.tsx` + `static/fonts/` — self-hosted Futura Round, mounted in both the
  app and Storybook from one module so the two cannot drift
- `components/icons/` — the four Zimmermann chevrons, replacing base-template
  substitutions that rendered a filled glyph where the design is a 1px stroke
- `theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts` — colour derivation moved out of the hook into the
  recipe, so the recipe is the single styling surface
- `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` — prop extraction scoped to `<ComponentName>Props`,
  Markdown table cells escaped, comma-containing types no longer silently dropped

# How to test-drive this PR

- `npm run env -- dev && npm start` → `/`, scroll to the footer. Nav columns hug their
  content with even gaps; hovering a link underlines it
- Resize through **1030px → 760px** — the bottom bar stays aligned with the content above
  it at every width
- Type a valid email → `>` opens the Join Us modal; empty or malformed is blocked inline
  with no modal
- `npm run storybook` → `Layout/Footer` (4 states incl. modal-open), `Elements/ZimmNavItem`
  (unsafe-href fallback), `Forms/ZimmInputAction` (validation)

# Protection-tier check

> ⚠️ **Tier 1** — `.storybook/{main.js,preview.tsx}` (test config, **Integration-owned**)
> for serving and mounting the self-hosted fonts; `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`
> (governance, **both squad leads + Integration lead**) to record them;
> `theme/foundation/sizes.ts` (design system, **UI-Designer-owned**) — whitespace only,
> and it now diffs to **zero** against `develop`.
> Authenticated as `marcelannavarro`, a member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`.
>
> ⚠️ **Tier 2** — `components/footer/`, `components/header/` (comments only),
> `theme/components/` (**UI-Designer — notified**).

# Testing

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npm run lint` — 0 errors (3 pre-existing `header` unused-import warnings, documented in-file)
- [x] `npm run test` (Vitest) — 168/168
- [x] Storybook interaction — 15 `play` functions across 7 stories
- [x] Runtime behaviour — 20/20 (hover, focus-visible, validation, modal focus trap + Escape + focus restore, overlay z-index above the sticky header)
- [x] Figma geometry — structural paddings exact at 64/48, 48/48, 24/24
- [x] Box model — 112 footer elements × 6 viewports, 0 off-token paddings/margins/gaps/borders
- [x] Accessibility — axe 0 violations / 17 passes (wcag2a → 2.2aa)
- [x] Local CodeRabbit — no new findings

# Known gaps

- **768–860px** — subscribe and nav columns sit flush and seven labels wrap. Unresolved
- **Subscribe column is 21px taller than Figma** — the two inter-element gaps are the only
  values in that block with no Figma annotation. Pending the designer
- **Locale control is 30px vs Figma's 23px** — deliberate; 23px fails WCAG 2.5.8 target size
- **12 icons still resolve to base-template glyphs** (`bag`, `search`, `menu`, `profile`
  among them). Raised separately
- **The subscribe modal is not in SFCC-55's AC**, which specifies "an email input field and
  submit button". It was demoed and signed off verbally on 2026-07-07 — worth confirming
  before SFCC-T120 is drafted
- **The locale control is inert** pending the locale selector
````

## Two things to decide

1. **Squad ownership** — I've put Squad A, since `.claude/rules/squadA.md` claims the PDP path and this is footer/global-shell work. Your call if it should be both squads.
2. **The "Known gaps" section is new** — none of your four reference PRs has one. I'd argue it earns its place given how many open design questions this carries, but it's a departure from your established shape. Happy to fold them into `# Description` instead.

Want me to adjust anything before you push and create it?

When done: open a PR targeting develop. qa.yml unit tests run automatically. One approval required before merge — develop is a shared integration point and your PR must not break it for anyone else.

Before every session:git branch --show-current (confirm branch) and git pull origin develop (merges happen frequently, even if you pulled this morning).

Hotfix branches — production emergencies only
When: a defect in production needs an immediate fix outside the sprint cycle.

Create from main — not develop:



git checkout main
git pull origin main
git checkout -b hotfix/SFCC-999_critical-fix-description
Why from main not develop:develop has unreleased sprint work in progress. A hotfix branched from develop would accidentally include unreleased features. Branching from main keeps the fix clean and scoped to production state only.

Tier 1 rules still apply — even under deadline pressure, do not modify Tier 1 files without owner approval.

When done: PR into main. After merge, the fix must also be back-merged to develop to prevent the regression re-appearing next sprint. (Merge commit vs. cherry-pick mechanism — confirm with the Integration Lead.)

Release branches — deployment targets, not working branches
When: a sprint is complete and a release is being promoted.

Release branches are created by squad leads or CI from a tagged develop state — developers do not create these. They exist as deployment targets for the SIT gate and cross-browser tests.

Pattern:release/v0.1.0, release/digital/v1.0.0.

What happens here: the full Digital SIT gate runs on every PR targeting release/**; BrowserStack cross-browser tests run on every PR targeting release/**; no new feature work goes here — only emergency release fixes after squad lead approval.

Making a code fix on a release branch
Do not edit the release branch directly for code changes. Branch off it instead so the CI gate runs against the fix before it lands.



# Step 1 — branch from the release branch, not develop
git checkout release/v0.1.0
git pull origin release/v0.1.0
git checkout -b fix/release-v0.1.0_short-description
# Step 2 — make the fix
# Step 3 — PR back into the release branch (not develop)
gh pr create --base release/v0.1.0 --title "fix(checkout): SFCC-999 payment error on SIT"
Once merged, squad leads apply the same fix to develop via a second PR to prevent the regression re-appearing next sprint.

When direct commits to a release branch are acceptable: only for changes with no logic — copy corrections, version number bumps, a boolean flag toggle. These require explicit squad lead approval before committing.

Claude Code on release/**: supervised mode — plan first, blast-radius check, confirm before every edit. Code logic changes must go through a fix/release-* sub-branch as described above.

develop — the integration branch
No direct commits. All changes arrive via PR from a feature/* branch. develop receives a deployment to Digital Dev and SIT on every push — a bad push breaks the integration environment for both squads simultaneously, which is why the PR review gate exists.

main — production state
No direct commits. All changes arrive via a release promotion or a hotfix/* PR. main always reflects the current production code. Tagging main with a semver tag (v0.1.0) is done by the release tooling at scripts/tagRelease.sh.

Stage

Example

Go-live

v1.0.0

v1.0.{patch}

v1.0.1, v1.0.2

Post-go-live features

v1.{minor}.0

v1.1.0

Tags are created by running scripts/tagRelease.sh v{version} from main after the release PR is merged — this creates both v{version} and release/digital/v{version} tags.

Sprint boundary tags (sprint/{N}/{date}) are created automatically by CI when scripts/sprint.txt is updated. Update the file to the new sprint number when a sprint begins — increment it in a commit on develop.

When done: open a PR targeting develop. qa.yml unit tests run automatically. One approval required before merge — develop is a shared integration point and your PR must not break it for anyone else.

Before every session:git branch --show-current (confirm branch) and git pull origin develop (merges happen frequently, even if you pulled this morning).

Hotfix branches — production emergencies only
When: a defect in production needs an immediate fix outside the sprint cycle.

Create from main — not develop:



git checkout main
git pull origin main
git checkout -b hotfix/SFCC-999_critical-fix-description
Why from main not develop:develop has unreleased sprint work in progress. A hotfix branched from develop would accidentally include unreleased features. Branching from main keeps the fix clean and scoped to production state only.

Tier 1 rules still apply — even under deadline pressure, do not modify Tier 1 files without owner approval.

When done: PR into main. After merge, the fix must also be back-merged to develop to prevent the regression re-appearing next sprint. (Merge commit vs. cherry-pick mechanism — confirm with the Integration Lead.)

Release branches — deployment targets, not working branches
When: a sprint is complete and a release is being promoted.

Release branches are created by squad leads or CI from a tagged develop state — developers do not create these. They exist as deployment targets for the SIT gate and cross-browser tests.

Pattern:release/v0.1.0, release/digital/v1.0.0.

What happens here: the full Digital SIT gate runs on every PR targeting release/**; BrowserStack cross-browser tests run on every PR targeting release/**; no new feature work goes here — only emergency release fixes after squad lead approval.

Making a code fix on a release branch
Do not edit the release branch directly for code changes. Branch off it instead so the CI gate runs against the fix before it lands.



# Step 1 — branch from the release branch, not develop
git checkout release/v0.1.0
git pull origin release/v0.1.0
git checkout -b fix/release-v0.1.0_short-description
# Step 2 — make the fix
# Step 3 — PR back into the release branch (not develop)
gh pr create --base release/v0.1.0 --title "fix(checkout): SFCC-999 payment error on SIT"
Once merged, squad leads apply the same fix to develop via a second PR to prevent the regression re-appearing next sprint.

When direct commits to a release branch are acceptable: only for changes with no logic — copy corrections, version number bumps, a boolean flag toggle. These require explicit squad lead approval before committing.

Claude Code on release/**: supervised mode — plan first, blast-radius check, confirm before every edit. Code logic changes must go through a fix/release-* sub-branch as described above.

develop — the integration branch
No direct commits. All changes arrive via PR from a feature/* branch. develop receives a deployment to Digital Dev and SIT on every push — a bad push breaks the integration environment for both squads simultaneously, which is why the PR review gate exists.

main — production state
No direct commits. All changes arrive via a release promotion or a hotfix/* PR. main always reflects the current production code. Tagging main with a semver tag (v0.1.0) is done by the release tooling at scripts/tagRelease.sh.

Tagging and versioning
Stage

Version format

Example

Pre-go-live sprints

v0.{sprint}.0

v0.1.0, v0.2.0

Go-live

v1.0.0

v1.0.0

Post-go-live patches

v1.0.{patch}

v1.0.1, v1.0.2

Post-go-live features

v1.{minor}.0

v1.1.0

Tags are created by running scripts/tagRelease.sh v{version} from main after the release PR is merged — this creates both v{version} and release/digital/v{version} tags.

Sprint boundary tags (sprint/{N}/{date}) are created automatically by CI when scripts/sprint.txt is updated. Update the file to the new sprint number when a sprint begins — increment it in a commit on develop.

content.content:
══ manual §8 — Before you open a PR ══
  ## 8. Before you open a PR
  
  **Green locally before you open it.** Not a nicety — a PR that doesn't compile spends a reviewer's whole
  budget on nothing, and review here runs an hour or more per UI PR.
  
  ```bash
  npx tsc --noEmit          # must be clean
  npm run lint              # must not add new errors
  npm test                  # Vitest
  /code-quality             # naming, imports, structure, missing stories/tests
  ```
  
  Two failure modes specific to this repo, both seen already:
  
  - **A `develop` merge can silently delete a type declaration.** If your branch added something to
    `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts` and `develop` also changed that file, the merge can resolve to
    develop's version and drop yours. Re-run `tsc` **after** every merge from `develop`, not just before.
  - **Sometimes the rule is wrong, not your code.** One recent failure came from following a repo rules file
    that named a package which doesn't exist on the installed Storybook major. If a documented import
    doesn't resolve, check the package actually exists before assuming you mistyped it — then flag the rule.
  
  ### Self-review across the same three surfaces the reviewer will use
  
  Cheaper to catch it yourself than in a review round-trip:
  
  | Surface | What you're checking |
  |---|---|
  | **The diff** | Correct tokens in the correct layer, reuse over reimplementation, no raw literals |
  | **The preview environment** | What it actually renders — every state, every breakpoint, hover and focus genuinely working |
  | **Figma, side by side** | Parity at the breakpoints the design defines |
  
  Your branch's preview URL is posted on the PR automatically (§5). If a difference from Figma is a *design*
  gap rather than a build gap, say so in the PR description — don't quietly resolve it.
  
  Then a local CodeRabbit review — **required, not optional**:
  
  ```bash
  coderabbit auth status && cr review --light --base develop
  ```
  
  If the CLI isn't installed or authenticated, install it (coderabbit.ai/cli) and run
  `npm run env -- init` for the shared key rather than committing without a review. The GitHub PR review
  is still the real gate; this one catches things earlier.
  
  ### Self-check
  
  - [ ] Ladder walked — reuse checked and reported, "custom" justified
  - [ ] Copy-first done and confirmed if `Origin = Base`; `console.log` markers removed
  - [ ] All design values are tokens — **no hardcoded hex, no raw px/rem/em** (still not mechanically
        enforced: `overrideStyling.md` points at `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`, which does not exist yet —
        so this stays the highest-frequency violation in review)
  - [ ] Type set with `textStyle`, never `fontSize`
  - [ ] Storybook story exists, categorised correctly, `Default` plus meaningful states
  - [ ] Vitest where logic is non-obvious — data mapping, transforms, complex state
  - [ ] Accessibility AC met, including the parts no tool checks
  - [ ] Optional/absent content handled — no empty space, no layout break

Verdict below. I checked every item on the manual's §8 self-check and the playbook's completeness rule.

## ✅ Clean

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | 0 errors |

| Optional/absent content | `ContactIconRow` degrades when hrefs are absent; `legalLinks = []` defaults |
| Existing comments preserved | ✅ — the header revert deliberately kept all documentation |

## ✅ No duplication

All five atoms **wrap** rather than reimplement — `ZimmButton` renders Chakra's `ChakraButton`/`IconButton`, the rest build on `chakra.*` primitives, `ZimmIcon` uses `createIcon`. Nothing hand-rolls a button, link, or input. Playbook #3 satisfied.

The one genuine duplication we found — `utils/cssVars.ts` shadowing the `--zimm-*` vars — was **deleted**.

## ✅ Completeness (playbook #9)

Six atoms/molecules, all six consumed by the footer, all declared props covered directly or by their consumer. The five uncovered props are **unused API** (`value`, `defaultValue`, `ZimmInputAction.disabled`, `ZimmIcon.color`, `ZimmNavItem.onClick`) — a trim-or-keep decision, not a build gap. Every declared recipe state (`_hover`, `_active`, `_focusVisible`, `_disabled`) is exercised.

## ⚠️ Three things to know before you push

**1. `fontSize="l"` at `header/index.tsx:302`** — violates "always `textStyle`, never `fontSize`", and `l` isn't even a valid fontSize token. **Pre-existing**, inside the block we only added comments to (+16/−4, comments only). Not introduced here, but it *is* in a file this PR touches, so a reviewer may flag it.

**2. `useCurrentBasket` in `header/index.tsx`** — technically violates "no data-fetching hooks inside a `components/` file". It's a **copy-first SFCC base component**, so the hook came with it; our diff there is comments only. Same status: pre-existing, visible in this PR.

**3. Multiple protection tiers touched** — Hard Rule #10 says don't, "without stopping to confirm scope with the developer." We touched **Tier 1** (`.storybook/` ×2, `frozenFiles.md`, `sizes.ts`) and **Tier 2** (footer, header, `theme/components/`). Each Tier 1 file was individually approved by you in-session and your `tier-1-approvers` membership verified, so the rule's condition is met — but the PR body needs to make that explicit, which it does.

- The manual points at `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` for token enforcement — **it doesn't exist**. The manual already flags this; confirming it's still true, so "no raw px/rem/em" remains manually verified only. Our sweep did it by hand: every literal is an annotated provisional constant.
- The Confluence branching page references `scripts/tagRelease.sh`, **retired in your own PR #49**.

---

## Verdict

**Ready to push.** No build gaps, no duplication, no inline-style or mirrored-style violations introduced, complete variant/state coverage on everything in use, and full token/CSS-structure conformance.

The three ⚠️ items are all **pre-existing conditions in files this PR touches**, not defects it introduces. My recommendation: add one line to the PR description noting that `header/index.tsx` carries a pre-existing `fontSize="l"` and an SDK hook from the copy-first import, so a reviewer doesn't spend time on them.

Still processing. Here's the prep — anticipated findings and drafted replies, based on six local runs.

## CI so far

```
✅ Unit tests (Vitest)              ✅ Tier 1 — Frozen Files Check
✅ Detect relevant changes          ✅ Tier 2 — Protected Files Warning
✅ Branch Target Check              ✅ Cross-Squad Boundary Check
⏳ Storybook interaction & a11y     ⏳ Playwright E2E (localhost)
⏳ Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack) ⏳ CodeRabbit  ⏳ Deploy Preview
```

All four guard jobs passed. Note **BrowserStack is running** — `detect-changes` found `SFCC-55` in the title, so it's `--grep`-scoped to `@SFCC-55`. No spec carries that tag, so it should report "no tests found" and cost nothing. If it *fails* rather than no-ops, that's a scoping bug worth reporting, not a real failure.

## Almost certain to recur — reply, don't change

**1 · `.storybook/main.js` and `preview.tsx` — "revert the Storybook config change"** (2 findings, major)

Appeared in run 1 of 6. `--light` sampled it out afterwards; the full PR review will likely surface it again.

> These two changes are the self-hosted-font enablement and were made deliberately under AGENTS.md's Tier 1 Approval process, not in spite of it. `main.js` gains a `staticDirs` mapping so `overrides/app/static` is served in Storybook; `preview.tsx` mounts `ZimmFontFace` alongside the existing `ZimmTokensGlobal`. Without both, Storybook renders the fallback stack while the app renders Futura Round — the fallback measures ~13% wider, so no visual comparison made in Storybook could be trusted. Approved and committed by `marcelannavarro`, a verified member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`; CODEOWNERS still routes the files for review. Recorded in the PR's Protection-tier section.

**2 · `FOOTER_FIXTURE` in a production path** (major)

Appeared in runs 2 and 6, anchored variously at `contentfulFixture.ts`, `footer/index.tsx`, and `types/contentful.ts`.

> Deliberate, and the reason the container/view split exists. `Footer` takes `data` as a **required** prop and fetches nothing; only `FooterContainer` supplies the fixture. SFCC-55 explicitly scopes Contentful integration to a separate story — "This story covers the footer shell, layout, and component structure only" — so there is no live source to read from yet. The fixture is already the shape the CMS will deliver, so wiring it up later is a swap at one call site. Rendering nothing instead would leave the component unreviewable for the static-first build this story asks for.

**3 · `extractTsProps` can't resolve unions/intersections** (minor)

> Pre-existing and knowingly left — verified identical on `develop`, where `Button` and `PageContainer` show the same empty props cell. Resolving `extends`, intersections and union aliases needs a real TypeScript parser rather than the current regex; that's a larger change than this PR should carry. This PR fixed the three tractable defects in the same function: props leaking between sibling `*Props` blocks, unescaped `|` breaking table columns, and comma-containing types being silently dropped entirely.

## Likely new, and worth taking seriously

Untested surface from the last few commits — I'd expect at least one of:

- **`sx={{ width: 'min-content' }}`** in `footer/index.tsx` — rung 4 of the styling ladder. Justified in an eight-line comment; if flagged, the reply is that per-instance sizing can't live in a shared recipe, which is exactly rung 4's purpose.
- **`clearable` default `false`** — may be read as a breaking API change. It isn't: no consumer passed it, and it restores AC-specified behaviour.
- **The chevron `viewBox: '0 0 24 24'`** against the file's usual 20 — the comment covers it, citing `Icon_chevron_down` as a 24×24 symbol.
- **NBSP in the fixture label** — an invisible character. Documented with a six-line comment explaining the 1.9px window.

## What I'd actually change if raised

- A genuine a11y finding — e.g. `role="list"` on the footer `<ul>`, which I flagged earlier and you haven't ruled on. If CodeRabbit raises it, that's a cheap fix and probably right.
- Anything on the `min-content` approach that identifies a case I didn't test.

## The rule

Every finding needs an in-thread reply, fixed or not — a fix commit alone doesn't count. Silence teaches CodeRabbit nothing; an explanation teaches it to stop flagging a non-issue.

Want me to poll until the review lands and draft replies against the actual findings?

content.text:
Both diagnosed. **Only one is mine.**

## 1 · Storybook interaction — my regression, fixed

`zimmTextInput/index.stories.tsx` → `Filled` story:

```tsx
const clearBtn = canvas.getByRole('button', { name: /clear input/i });
await expect(clearBtn).toBeInTheDocument();
```

My `clearable` change removed that button, so the story had nothing to click. **1 failed of 73.**

**I told you no story referenced the clear button. That was wrong.** I grepped for the literal `"Clear input"` — the aria-label casing — and the story uses the lowercase regex `/clear input/i`, so a case-sensitive grep found nothing. I then reported "no story updates needed" on the strength of it.

Fixed by splitting the two behaviours, which is what should have happened anyway:

- **`Filled`** — now asserts the *default*: a value present, and `queryByRole(...)` **not** in the document
- **`Clearable`** — new story with `clearable: true`, carrying the original type/click/focus/empty assertions

`tsc` clean. That covers both sides of the new prop rather than just restoring the old test.

## 2 · BrowserStack — not ours, and not a real failure

```
Error: Config file does not exist at any parent directory of:
       /home/runner/work/zimmermann-pwa/zimmer…
```

`browserstack-node-sdk` can't find its config. But **`.browserstack.yml` is committed** — since `cd60b7a`, the initial commit. So the file exists; the SDK is looking in the wrong place, or the job's working directory is wrong.

This is infrastructure, not code. It's also the job I predicted would no-op: `detect-changes` found `SFCC-55` in the title and scoped it to `@SFCC-55`, but **no spec carries that tag** — there's no footer E2E spec. Per `testing.md` that should report "no tests found" for free. Instead the SDK dies before it gets that far.

Worth raising with Integration — it'll fail identically on any PR whose title carries a Jira key, which is now every PR following the documented title convention. Which is likely *why* it's surfacing now: your previous PRs omitted the key, so this job never ran.

## Local `test-storybook` is unreliable as I ran it

74/74 failed locally against the live HMR'ing dev server, where CI had 72 passing. It needs a built Storybook (`build-storybook` + `http-server`), which is what CI does. My run proved nothing — CI is the authority here, and I should have built rather than pointed at :6006.

## Next

The fix is uncommitted. Want me to commit and push so CI re-runs? BrowserStack will still fail — that one needs Integration.

Confirmed, and the cause is structural:

| Item | box | leading above text |
|---|---|---|
| Our Story | 24 | **4.5** |
| Sustainability | 24 | **4.5** |
| Careers | 24 | **4.5** |
| Brand Protection | 24 | **4.5** |
| **Acknowledgement** | 29 | **0** ← |

Spacing comes from `minHeight: 24px` + `alignItems: center`. A single 14.5px line centres in 24px giving 4.5px leading; two lines are 29px, overflow the 24px floor, so the leading collapses to zero. Let me check the spec before choosing a fix.

content.text:
The spec is decisive, and it reveals a conflict worth surfacing:

```
Anchor: display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 20px; white-space: nowrap
Padding bottom: 2px (aligns text above border indicator)
```

**The nav-item atom is specified as `white-space: nowrap`, fixed 20px — it never wraps.** Our recipe already diverges (`whiteSpace: normal`, `minHeight: 24px`) because the *footer frame* shows ACK on two lines at `h-[24px]`. So the wrap is a footer-level override of the atom spec, and the atom spec has nothing to say about two-line leading.

content.text:
Diagnosed, but I want the node before I pick a fix — deriving design values has cost us twice today.

## What's happening

`zimmNavItem.ts` treats `h-[24px]` as a floor with `alignItems: center`. That works for one line — 14.5px of text centres in 24px, giving 4.5px leading. Two lines are 29px, which overflows the floor, so centring has nothing to distribute and the leading goes to **zero**. Hence the tight top you're seeing.

## The three fixes, and why I don't want to guess

Our links column is already **163px against Figma's 158**. Every option grows it further:

| Fix | Wrapped item | Column | vs Figma 158 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** `lineHeight: 24px` — rhythm from the line box | 29 → **48** | 182 | +24 ✗ |
| **B** uniform `gap` on the list, items content-height | 29 | ~163 | +5, but touches every item |
| **C** `paddingTop` on wrapped items only | 29 → **33.5** | 167.5 | +9.5 |

**A** is the typographically correct answer and the one I'd normally reach for — rhythm belongs in line-height, not in min-height plus centring. But it nearly doubles the wrapped item and pushes us 24px past Figma.

There's a fourth possibility I can't rule out: the **single-line items may be the wrong ones.** The atom spec says `height: 20px`, not 24. If Figma's footer items are 20px, four of them at 20 plus a 29px wrapped item lands at 147 — *under* 158, which suggests Figma's wrapped item is taller than 29 and its leading is deliberate.

I can't tell which without the frame.

## What I need

The **ABOUT column** node, or just the **ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF COUNTRY** item — same as you sent for the chevrons. `footer.ts` has node refs for the subscribe heading and body but none for the links column, so there's nothing recorded to read.

With it I can read the item heights and spacing directly and pick the fix that lands on the spec rather than near it.

## If you'd rather not chase it

**C** is the safe interim: it restores the 4.5px leading on the wrapped item only, leaves all four single-line items untouched, and costs 4.5px of column height. Visually it fixes exactly what you flagged. It's conditional in the same way the `min-content` fix is — keyed off the same NBSP signal — so it's one line next to code that already does this.

Say which, or send the node.

content.text:
**Exact match to Figma on every item, and the column total lands on 134 — Figma's `Links` frame height precisely.**

```
ITEM                     box   leading   Figma
Our Story                24    4.5       24  ✅
Sustainability           24    4.5       24  ✅
Careers                  24    4.5       24  ✅
Brand Protection         24    4.5       24  ✅
Acknowledgement…         38    4.5       38  ✅

column items total: 134   Figma Links frame: 134
```

## What was wrong

Spacing came from `minHeight: 24px` + `alignItems: center`. Centring only distributes whatever a single line leaves over — a wrapped label overflows the 24px floor, so the leading collapsed to zero and the second line sat flush against the item above.

## The fix

Height now derives from line-height plus padding, so it holds at any line count:

```ts
lineHeight: 'var(--zimm-font-lineheight-4xs)',  // 14px
paddingBlock: NAV_ITEM_PAD_Y,                    // 4.5px
```

Figma's own text boxes are cap-height (8px one line, 22px two) where a browser line box isn't, so I took the *rule* — equal leading, height follows the text — rather than the numbers. The inner span reserves 1px for the underline indicator, so a line box measures 15px and two measure 29px; 4.5px each side gives 24 and 38.

`4.5px` isn't in `spacing.ts`. Documented as provisional with the same treatment as `button.ts`'s `BTN_PADDING_Y`, which `overrideStyling.md` already names as the standing exception. One for Kiera's list.

## A second bug found on the way

My first attempt didn't apply at all — `padding: 0` sat *after* `paddingBlock` in the recipe object and silently reset it. Shorthand-after-longhand, which is precisely the class of defect `recipeGuards.test.ts` was written for. Changed to `paddingInline: 0` with a comment so nobody reintroduces it.

Worth noting the guard didn't catch this one — it checks for bare scale keys in compound shorthands, not a shorthand resetting a longhand declared above it. Possible follow-up for that test.

## State

Uncommitted, alongside the Storybook story fix from earlier. `tsc` clean.

Two things pending your call: commit both, and whether to re-run the full phase suite first given this changes the links column height (Phase 4's `links` was 163 — it'll now be ~172, further from Figma's 158, because the *heading* gap is a separate discrepancy I haven't touched).

## Phase results

| Phase | Result |
|---|---|
| **0** Gate zero | `tsc` 0 · `vitest` **168** · prettier clean · eslint **0 errors** / 3 known warnings |
| **1** Static | 1a **25 → 17** (the `sizes.ts` fix removed 8) · 1f `sx=` 3 → 4 (the justified `min-content`) · rest unchanged · **drift 0/16** |
| **2** Emitted CSS | 5 → 8 flags, all three new ones ours: `padding-block: 4.5px` and two vendor-prefixed `min-content` variants of the same declaration |
| **3** Runtime | **20/20** |
| **4** Geometry | Items now **exact** |
| **5** Guards | 3/3 |

## The geometry result

```
ours : 24 / 24 / 24 / 24 / 38 = 134
figma: 24 / 24 / 24 / 24 / 38 = 134   ✅
```

Every item matches, and the column total lands on Figma's `Links` frame height exactly. `links` moved 163 → 164, so the residual **Δ6 relocated from the items to the heading gap** — Figma measures its column-heading text box at 8px where ours renders 14px. That's a separate discrepancy, now isolated and identified rather than smeared across the column.

## CodeRabbit's two findings

**1 · Registry records a future date** — `2026-08-21` against a generation timestamp of `2026-08-20T17:47Z`. That's the date rolling over mid-session; local is 21 Aug, UTC still 20 Aug. Timezone artifact, not a defect. Needs a reply, not a fix.

**2 · Four icons' viewBox disagrees with their documented frame** — `ShareIcon`/`ShareTwoIcon` comment "Size=20" but use `0 0 14 14`; `BagSelectedIcon` "Size=20" with `15 15`; `InfoSelectedIcon` "Size=12" with `8 8`.

The concern is legitimate — if those viewBoxes are glyph bounding boxes rather than frames, `ZimmIcon` scales them to full size and strips the intended padding, rendering them proportionally larger than designed. But **"Size=20" is the Figma variant name, not the frame**, so the comments aren't necessarily wrong.

All four are pre-existing from `8c25f11`, unrelated to the footer, and each needs its own Figma check. Our chevrons are unaffected — `0 0 24 24` was verified against `Icon_chevron_down` being a 24×24 symbol. **Goes on the icon-audit ticket** with the 12 substitutions.

## Ready to push

Two commits ahead of the remote. Push and CI re-runs — the Storybook job should go green now; BrowserStack will still fail on its missing config, which is Integration's.

distributes what a single line leaves over. A two-line label overflows the floor, so the leading
collapses to zero and the item sits flush against the one above. Derive height from `lineHeight` plus
padding instead — it holds at any line count.

**A block `<li>` wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` leaks ~1.5px per row.** The line box's strut adds
descender space below the baseline. Five rows cost 9px against Figma. `display: flex` on the list item
removes the line box entirely; axe confirmed list semantics survive.

#### Figma's text boxes are cap-height. Browser line boxes are not.

Figma reports a single-line footer item as 8px of text and two lines as 22px; the same text in a browser
measures ~14.5px and ~29px. **Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** For the nav item the rule was "equal
space above and below, height follows the line count" — expressed in our units as `lineHeight: 14px` plus
4.5px block padding, which lands on Figma's 24px and 38px exactly. Copying 8/22 would have produced
nonsense.

#### Type metrics change layout decisions — get the real font in first

Before the real faces were served, the fallback stack rendered roughly **13% wider**. Several sizing
decisions taken against it were simply wrong and had to be redone: a nav-column cap chosen to make one
label wrap stopped working once labels shrank, and a 768px overflow disappeared on its own. If a build
depends on measured text, self-host the font before you start measuring.

#### When no single value satisfies two constraints, constrain the text instead

The ACK label needed to wrap after the first word while "BOOK AN APPOINTMENT" stayed on one line. The
viable column cap was **[131, 132.9) — 1.9px**, a coincidence rather than a tolerance. A non-breaking
space between the words that must stay together widened the safe window to 71px. Content-level fixes are
sometimes the robust ones — but note the dependency: production copy has to carry the same character.

### The `.zimm-*` global classes — and the one rule about them"""

in `zimm.tsx` are unaffected — so an icon that appears blank in Storybook is usually a sourcing signal,
not a broken glyph.

content.text:
Both updated. **Manual 987 → 1056, playbook 729 → 800.** Structure intact in both.

## Build manual — technical discoveries

**§3, after the existing sizing-prop trap** — *"Four more layout traps, all found by rendering rather than by any tool"*:

- **A shorthand resets a longhand you declared above it.** The manual already warns about shorthands wiping the *base's* longhands; this is the sibling case inside your own object. `padding: 0` twelve lines below `paddingBlock` made the first nav-item fix a complete no-op. Noted that `recipeGuards` doesn't catch it.
- **A wrapped element takes available width, not its longest line** — the 45px of dead space in the ABOUT column, and why `min-content` has to be gated.
- **`minHeight` + centring breaks when content wraps** — leading collapses to zero; derive height from line-height plus padding.
- **A block `<li>` around an `inline-flex` `<a>` leaks ~1.5px per row** — the strut's descender space, 9px across five rows.

Then three new subsections:

- **Figma's text boxes are cap-height, browser line boxes aren't** — 8/22 vs 14.5/29 for the same text. Transfer the *rule*, not the numbers. This is the one I'd most want the next person to read.
- **Type metrics change layout decisions** — the fallback rendered ~13% wider, so several sizing calls made against it were simply wrong.
- **When no single value satisfies two constraints, constrain the text** — the 1.9px cap window, and the NBSP, with its production-copy dependency called out.

**§5** — the two things Storybook won't show truthfully: base-template SVGs are `ignore-loader`ed so those icons render as empty boxes, and `test-storybook` needs a *built* Storybook.

**§8** — `build-storybook && test-storybook` added to the pre-PR commands, with the reason: **Vitest doesn't run `play` functions.** Cited the actual miss — green locally, 1 of 73 in CI.

## Playbook — Play 5b, "Verifying a design claim before you act on it"

Placed between PR review and Accessibility, since it's a review-adjacent discipline. Six rules, each from a reversal that would otherwise have shipped:

- **Absence in an extracted spec is not a decision** — `managed-by: /extract`, `Status: draft`. Nearly deleted a control instead of making it opt-in.
- **A value in the codebase is not a spec until you find its source** — the 597px with no Figma node anywhere, contrasted with the icon geometry that does cite one.
- **Ask for the node** — four times it took one message and replaced a derivation. With the distinction between deriving *from* the source and deriving from resemblance.
- **An audit matching on value alone produces confident nonsense** — the three false mirrors, with a table showing two of the three "fixes" were WCAG regressions.
- **A grep count is not a coverage verdict** — both my proxy errors, and their common shape.
- **A passing test can be encoding the bug** — the contact-icons assertion that had frozen a defect.

## Not added

I left out anything already covered — `extendTheme` merging and the sizing-prop trap are both already in §3, so I anchored the new material around them rather than restating.

Both files are on your Desktop, outside the repo, so nothing to commit.

sidetask: look into PR #57 - and draft a code review to identify what needs to be changed/revised/improved/refactored from it according to the work/approach/way of working we did for this footer PR particularly with the approach for the build: components, tokens, css structure, etc. -> full coverage and to strengthen the findings, run the full phase 0-6 test suite we have on it as support to the audit, also review alignment with the fed lead playbook and fed build manual, here's some information for this ticket/US: PDP UI — Static Product Information




Key details
Templates ➤


Story
Description

As a Shopper,
I want to see clear product information when I land on a product detail page,
so that I can quickly understand what the product is before deciding to buy.

This story covers the rendering of static product information on the PDP — fields sourced directly from the SFCC product record. It has no dependency on the Contentful integration, the colour/variation model, or inventory data. It is the most foundational PDP story and should be built first. In Scope:

 

Product name

Full price in the currency of the active storefront (single/full price only)

Product description

"Model is…" copy — model height and size worn

Style Code

Breadcrumb navigation reflecting the product's category path (bottom of PDP)

Out of scope (separate stories):

Badges

Was/Now sale price display

Wishlist icon (CTAs story)

Colour swatches and variation selection

Size selector and availability states

Add to Bag, Find in Boutique CTAs

Image gallery

Accordion content (Details & Care, Size & Fit, Shipping & Returns)

Contentful-sourced content

Rollout Scope

AU
ME
EU - Domestic
EU - International
HK
UK
US - Domestic
US - International
Acceptance Criteria


Mandatory inputs for a Product to show on the website:

Product name

Given a shopper lands on a PDP, when the page loads, then the product name is displayed prominently at the top of the product information panel, sourced from the SFCC product record.

Price

Given a shopper lands on a PDP and the product has a single full price, when the page loads, then the full price is displayed beneath the product name in the currency of the active storefront.

Product description

Given a shopper lands on a PDP, when the page loads, then the product description is displayed.

Product style code

Given a shopper lands on a PDP, when the page loads, then the product style code is displayed.

Optional input:

Model copy

Given a product has "Model is…" copy populated in the relevant SFCC attribute, when the page loads, then the model height and size worn are displayed on the page.

Given a product does not have "Model is…" copy populated, when the page loads, then no model copy is displayed and no empty placeholder is shown.

Breadcrumb navigation

Given a shopper is on a PDP, when the page loads, then a breadcrumb trail is displayed underneath the product pictures reflecting the product's category path (e.g. HOME / NEW / DRESSES / [PRODUCT NAME]).

Given a shopper clicks a breadcrumb node, when the click is registered, then the shopper is navigated to the corresponding category page.Dependency


 

On the product attribute that contains the "Model is wearing size S…" copy - this is enriched in Magento - would be the same in SFCC, same with true to size copy → Informed Dani that this copy is part of an existing field that contains more data than just the  model size copy - it would need to be a separate field then in SFCC if we want to split this text out and display on PDP
