Without it + // only the bare `Props {` form matches, and an extended or intersected type resolves + // to nothing, which sends the preferredTypeName lookup into the merge-everything + // fallback it exists to prevent. + const re = /(?:type|interface)\s+(\w*Props)\s*(?:=\s*)?[^{\n]*\{([\s\S]*?)\n\}/g ``` ## Why it's flagged The regex reads a props type by looking for the name, then **immediately** the `{`. It allows only whitespace or an `=` in between: ```ts type FooProps = { // name, =, { → matches interface FooProps { // name, { → matches type FooProps = BoxProps & { // name, =, BoxProps, &, { → nothing matches interface FooProps extends BoxProps { → nothing matches ``` That last pair is the normal way to say "my props, plus Chakra's." Three of our own types do it, and the regex is blind to all three. **The damage isn't a missing row — it's a silently wrong one.** `extractTsProps` takes a `preferredTypeName` so `PageContainer`'s row shows `PageContainerProps`, not some sub-component's internal props type. When the regex can't see the preferred type, the function falls through to *"collect every `*Props` block in the file and merge them."* So: - **`PageContainer`** — the only Props type in the file is an intersection, so nothing matches and the row reads `—`. Its props vanished. - **`ZimmButton`** — the base type matches but the two variant types don't, so the row is built from `ZimmButtonBaseProps` alone and quietly omits the label/icon variants. The registry is what AI tooling reads to know a component's shape. A blank cell is obvious. A cell that looks complete but is missing two variants is the one that costs someone an afternoon. **Worth being precise about one thing:** CodeRabbit justified this by saying base-package components commonly extend Chakra prop types. That's wrong — there are **zero** in the base package, because those are `.jsx` with PropTypes, not TypeScript. The reasoning was wrong; the bug is real, in our own code. I checked rather than inherit the claim. --- # Finding E — `escapeCell` and angle brackets ```diff function escapeCell(value) { // (? are escaped for the same reason the pipe is: the cell is rendered as Markdown, + // and GitHub treats an unescaped angle-bracket run as raw HTML and drops it. Type + // expressions (Array, React.Ref) and any prose naming an element + // (``, ``) otherwise lose everything between the brackets. + return String(value) + .replace(/(?/g, '>') } ``` ## Why it's flagged `escapeCell` has one job: make a value safe to drop inside a Markdown table cell. A raw `|` would be read as a column separator and split the row, so it gets escaped. Angle brackets are the same category of problem and were missed. Markdown allows inline HTML. So when GitHub renders `React.Ref`, it sees `` as an opening tag for an unknown element and **swallows it**. The cell displays `React.Ref` — no error, no warning, just a type that lost its argument. This is live in `components.md` right now, across both columns `escapeCell` guards: ``` props onClick?: (e: React.MouseEvent) => void props searchInputRef?: React.Ref desc ...easy to create a `` element with related theme-aware `` elements desc `locale` format for OCAPI and Commerce API: - ``` Note the first line — that cell has the pipe correctly escaped as `\|` **and** angle brackets left raw. Same function, same cell, one hazard handled and its twin missed. That's what makes this mine: I added the pipe half in commit 6 and stopped there. ## The one real judgement call Entity-escaping means the raw file now reads `Array<Foo>` instead of `Array`, and `.claude/registry/` is read raw as AI context, not only rendered on GitHub. So this trades a little raw-text noise for correct rendering. CodeRabbit's alternative was wrapping the props value in backticks. That reads better raw — but it only fixes the props column, and the descriptions have the same problem (``, ``, `` are disappearing today). Since `escapeCell` guards **three** columns across all five registry files, fixing it at the function is the fix that covers everything. `<` is still perfectly legible to a raw reader; a silently truncated type isn't. --- Both diffs are validated against plain / `extends` / intersection / generic forms, and against already-escaped pipes so the fix I made in commit 6 doesn't regress. Say go and I'll apply them as one `fix(registry):` commit on top of `706e47d`.

<result>I read both documents in full. Below is the extracted checklist — no code audited.

Convention: **PB-nn** = fedLead-playbook.md, **BM-nn** = fedBuild-manual.md. Items stated in both docs appear once, under the ID of the doc that states them most concretely, with both sources cited. MANDATORY = stated as must/never/required/gate/non-negotiable. ADVISORY = should/prefer/judgement/expect.

---

# 1. Component/atom completeness

| ID | Requirement | Source | Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| PB-01 | A component is not complete until it covers **all supported variants**; the page merely configures it. "One Editorial Card, not a Homepage one and a PLP one." | Playbook, Play 3 | MANDATORY |
| PB-02 | Distinguish **configuration variants** (text alignment, CTA on/off, title on/off, body copy present/absent → props on one component) from **composition variants** (1 vs 2 column, 3-up vs 4-up grids → a separate container/slot component). A composition variant must not be built as a prop; on the Studio Experiences path "a repeating structure can't be a prop — the composition primitive is `children`". | Playbook, Play 3 | MANDATORY |
| PB-03 | Variant completeness must be settled **upfront** because "the Contentful sync is **additive-only** — it cannot delete a field from a published content type." Getting the variant model wrong is "semi-permanent", not rework. | Playbook, Play 3 | MANDATORY |
| PB-04 | Every Contentful-backed component needs AC for the **absent optional field** case — "no empty space, no placeholder, no layout break." Standing refinement question, not per-story discovery. | Playbook, Play 3 (#11) | MANDATORY |
| BM-01 | Optional / absent content is handled at build time — "no empty space, no layout break." | Manual, §8 Self-check; §6 standing set | MANDATORY |
| PB-05 | A complete component story carries all five: **all variants upfront + accessibility AC + a mandatory Storybook story + a test where logic-heavy + copy-first scaffolding on first touch.** | Playbook, Play 2 (re-baseline) | MANDATORY |
| PB-06 | "One Editorial Card with all variants" often resolves to **two** components (the card + a container holding one or two) — expect and catch the extra component at refinement. | Playbook, Play 3 | ADVISORY |

---

# 2. Testing requirements

| ID | Requirement | Source | Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| BM-02 | `npm test` (Vitest) passes locally before the PR is opened. | Manual, §8 | MANDATORY |
| BM-03 | Vitest **only where logic is non-obvious** — "data mapping, transforms, complex state". `index.test.ts` in the component folder "only if logic-heavy". | Manual, §8 Self-check; §4 Step 3 | MANDATORY (conditional) |
| PB-07 | "Unit tests where they earn their place — data mapping, transforms, non-obvious logic. **Not** for re-exports or passthroughs." Coverage must not reach zero while the build focus is UI. | Playbook, Play 5 | MANDATORY (conditional) |
| BM-04 | `npm run build-storybook && npx test-storybook` must be run before the PR — it is the only thing that runs `play` functions and the a11y checks. **"Vitest does not run `play` functions."** Worked precedent: the footer PR was green on `tsc`/`lint`/`vitest` and CI caught it at "1 failure in 73". | Manual, §8 | MANDATORY |
| BM-05 | `test-storybook` requires a **built** Storybook (`build-storybook` + static server). Pointing it at a running dev server "produces wholesale failures that mean nothing." | Manual, §5 | MANDATORY |
| BM-06 | Storybook a11y violations **fail CI** (`@storybook/addon-a11y`, `test: 'error'`). | Manual, §6 | MANDATORY |
| PB-08 | Reviewer gate zero includes `npx vitest run` alongside `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run lint`. | Playbook, Play 5 (Gate zero) | MANDATORY |
| PB-09 | Coverage for a **slot prop** belongs at the level of the molecule that fills the slot (e.g. three `play` functions in that molecule), not at the atom exposing the slot. | Playbook, Play 5b | ADVISORY |
| PB-10 | Do **not** put visual/design-parity snapshots in the Vitest budget — `testing.md` explicitly excludes them; spacing/design fidelity has "**No automated home**". | Playbook, Play 7 | MANDATORY |
| PB-11 | E2E: the `@area` vocabulary is exactly `homepage, checkout, search, account, pdp, plp, integrations`. Only `@homepage` and `@checkout` are applied to any spec today. Each new area's first spec **needs its own allow-list group in the change-scoping config**, or it silently falls back to the full suite (only `e2e_homepage` is mapped today). | Playbook, Play 7 | MANDATORY |

---

# 3. Storybook requirements

| ID | Requirement | Source | Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| BM-07 | **Every component exported from its folder** under `overrides/app/components/` or `/pages/` needs a `*.stories.tsx`. `index.stories.tsx` is marked "← mandatory" in the folder layout. | Manual, §5, §4 Step 3; Playbook, Play 1, Play 5 | MANDATORY |
| BM-08 | Internal sub-components that only render inside one parent do **not** need their own story — "cover their variants through the parent." (Applied to 04.7's `↳ Sub-component` rows: Pause/Play, Footer Item, Footer Textfield, Icons don't each need a story unless independently reusable.) | Manual, §5; Playbook, Play 1 | MANDATORY |
| BM-09 | Every story file has a **`Default`** export, plus named exports for meaningful states (`Loading`, `OutOfStock`, `WithDiscount`, `Empty`) — "not for every prop permutation." | Manual, §5 | MANDATORY |
| BM-10 | Story `title` uses the **first matching** category of exactly: `Foundation/` `Elements/` `Layout/` `Commerce/` `Forms/` `Pages/` `Contentful/`. `Elements/` tiebreaker: "usable outside a form?" Worked examples: `title: 'Commerce/ProductTile'` ✅ · `title: 'Elements/DisplayPrice'` ❌ (commerce-specific → `Commerce/`). | Manual, §5; Playbook, Play 1 | MANDATORY |
| BM-11 | `Contentful/` stories use **mock Contentful data** so variants are visible without a live CMS connection. | Manual, §5; Playbook, Play 7 | MANDATORY |
| BM-12 | Static/mock data lives **in the story, not in the component**. | Manual, §1 (Static-first), §5 | MANDATORY |
| BM-13 | `play` functions only where there is interactive behaviour worth asserting — "validation on blur, disclosure open/close, focus movement". When written: query through `within(canvasElement)`, prefer `getByRole` with an accessible name, and import `userEvent` from **`@storybook/test`**, not `@testing-library/user-event`. | Manual, §5 | MANDATORY (when a `play` is written) |
| PB-12 | The **floor** is a scaffolded story with a `Default` export and the meaningful states — even if the `play` function comes later. | Playbook, Play 5 | MANDATORY |
| BM-14 | Build **in** Storybook rather than building and then adding a story. | Manual, §5 | ADVISORY |
| BM-15 | Base-template SVGs are `ignore-loader`ed in `.storybook/main.js`, so any icon sourced from `@salesforce/retail-react-app` renders as an **empty box** in Storybook while rendering correctly in the app (12 of `ZimmIcon`'s types today). A blank icon is a sourcing signal, not a broken glyph. | Manual, §5 | ADVISORY |
| BM-16 | If a component looks wrong in Storybook but right in the app, **suspect the imports before the CSS** — a base-path import of an already-overridden component renders the base SFCC version in Storybook and Vitest. Switch it to a relative import. | Manual, §5, §11 (#5) | ADVISORY |
| BM-17 | Storybook is where you **build**; the branch preview environment is where others **review**. | Manual, §5 | ADVISORY |

---

# 4. Tokens / styling / CSS structure

| ID | Requirement | Source | Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| BM-18 | The styling hierarchy, in order: **1** `textStyle` for anything textual · **2** semantic token strings (`color="text.default"`, `bg="background.02"`, `padding={{ base: 'm', md: 'xl' }}`) · **3** the component's own `theme/components/<name>.ts` for variant/size/state · **4** `sx` for a genuine one-off prop-system gap · **5** scoped `.scss` only when `sx` truly cannot express it. | Manual, §3; Playbook, Play 5 | MANDATORY |
| BM-19 | **Never a raw hex / px / rem / em literal in a component file.** The one standing exception is `button.ts`'s provisional constants. | Manual, §3, §8 Self-check | MANDATORY |
| BM-20 | Type is always set with `textStyle`, **never** `fontSize`. Four keys collide (Zimmermann vs Chakra): `md` **24px/16px**, `xs` **16px/12px**, `2xs` **14px/10px**, `3xs` **12px/7.2px**; the base app uses those names at ~199 call sites. The Zimmermann font scale is **deliberately not registered** as `theme.fontSizes`; do not "fix" it by registering it (a test guards this). | Manual, §3; Playbook, Play 5 | MANDATORY |
| BM-21 | Type must resolve to one of the **22 registered text styles**: `heading1Strong` `heading1` `heading2` `heading3` · `body1Strong` `body1` `body2Strong` `body2` · `mobileBody1Strong` `mobileBody1` `mobileBody2` · `label` `caption` · `linkLg` `linkSm` · `button` `buttonSm` · `productNames` `price` · `navigation` · `footer` · `serif`. | Manual, §3 | MANDATORY |
| BM-22 | Colour comes from the **semantic** aliases, never a hex: `text.{default,inverse,inverseGrey,secondary,muted}` · `background.01`–`07` · `border.{default,secondary,focus,forms,error}` · `status.{success,error,errorBackground,storeClosed}` · `link.{default,hover}` · `icon.default` · `action.primary.{bgDefault,bgHover,bgPressed,bgDisabled,bgFocused,text,textDisabled}` · `action.secondary.{border,bgHover,text,textInverse,textDisabled}`. Primitives (`grey.*`, `ivory.*`, `coral/green/orange/red.500`, `opacity.*`) are what the semantics are built from, not what you reach for. | Manual, §3 | MANDATORY |
| BM-23 | Prefer the **named spacing scale** over Chakra numerics: `3xs` 0.125 · `2xs` 0.25 · `xs` 0.5 · `s` 0.75 · `m` 1 · `l` 1.25 · `xl` 1.5 · `2xl` 2 · `3xl` 2.5 · `4xl` 4 · `5xl` 5 · `6xl` 8 · `7xl` 10 — **in `rem`** (2/4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40/64/80/128/160px at a 16px root). | Manual, §3 | MANDATORY |
| BM-24 | Unit rule: **`rem`** for anything that should scale (type, spacing — WCAG 1.4.4) · **`px`** only for hairline geometry (border widths, focus-ring offsets) · **`em`** only for breakpoints. `borderWidth="default"` → `1px`; `focusRingOffsets.{default, secondary}` → `2px`/`3px`, imported as a constant from `app/theme/foundation`. | Manual, §3 | MANDATORY |
| BM-25 | **Never use the `--zimm-scale-NNN` numeric aliases in JSX** — they exist only so the `.zimm-*` global classes have something to reference. `<Box mb="var(--zimm-scale-500)" />` ❌ vs `<Box mb="l" />` ✅ (same 20px, traceable). Reaching for a numeric alias instead of the named scale counts as the same mistake as a hardcoded hex. | Manual, §3, §11 (#6); Playbook, Play 5 | MANDATORY |
| BM-26 | A value with **no named scale entry** is a token gap to raise, not a reason to reach for a numeric alias. Named gaps: **28px** and **44px** are in use with nothing between `xl` (24) and `2xl` (32), or `3xl` (40) and `4xl` (64). | Manual, §3; Playbook, Play 9 | MANDATORY |
| BM-27 | `iconSizes`, `actionSizes` and `motion` are **not theme tokens** — import them as constants from `app/theme/foundation`. `iconSizes` `lg` 20 · `md` 16 · `sm` 12. `actionSizes` `height.{lg:52, md:40}` · `paddingX.{lg:32, md:20}` · `gap:16`. `motion` `duration.{fast:200ms, default:300ms, slow:500ms}` · `easing.{standard, slides, fades}` — **motion values are PROVISIONAL**, pending designer sign-off. | Manual, §3 | MANDATORY |
| BM-28 | **The sizing-vs-spacing trap.** `width` / `height` / `boxSize` / `min\|maxWidth` / `min\|maxHeight` resolve through `theme.sizes`; `margin` / `padding` / `gap` / `top`-`right`-`bottom`-`left` resolve through `theme.space`. The Zimmermann named scale is registered as **`space` only**, so a bare scale key on a sizing prop falls through to Chakra's `sizes` (`xs` 20rem · `sm` 24rem · `md` 28rem · `lg` 32rem · `xl` 36rem) — `width: 'xl'` = **576px**, a silent 20–30× (24×) blow-up. **On a sizing property use `var(--zimm-scale-*)`, an imported constant, or an explicit unit — never a bare scale key.** Nothing catches it: it passed `tsc`, `eslint`, `vitest`, CodeRabbit (local and PR) and the Storybook a11y run. | Manual, §3, §11 (#3) | MANDATORY |
| BM-29 | Inside your own recipe, **a shorthand declared after a longhand silently wipes it** (`paddingBlock: '4.5px'` … then `padding: 0`). Use `paddingInline: 0` when you mean "no horizontal padding". `recipeGuards.test.ts` catches a bare scale key inside a shorthand; it does **not** catch this. | Manual, §3 | MANDATORY |
| BM-30 | `extendTheme` **deep-merges** — a recipe key matching an SFCC base key **inherits** it, it does not replace it. Base SFCC ships `Footer`, `Header`, `ListMenu`, `Button`, `CheckoutFooter` and more. Rules: **full rewrite → namespace the key** (`ZimmFooter`, consumed as `useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmFooter')`); **genuine partial override → keep the base key but never introduce a CSS shorthand on a part where the base sets longhands** (yours is appended last and wipes them); **always declare your own `parts` array**. | Manual, §3, §11 (#4) | MANDATORY |
| BM-31 | **Interaction state lives in CSS pseudo-props, never in React state.** `_hover` / `_active` / `_disabled` / `_focusVisible` in the recipe — not `useState` + `onMouseEnter` + inline style. Five stated consequences of getting it wrong: dead until hydration; no `@media (hover: hover)` so sticky hover on touch; inline styles win specificity so the theme cannot override; the WCAG 2.4.7 focus ring in the recipe never applies; every hover re-renders. | Manual, §3, §11 (#1); Playbook, Play 5 | MANDATORY |
| BM-32 | **A registered-but-unread recipe is dead code.** A custom multipart component must actually read it (`useStyleConfig` / `useMultiStyleConfig`); Chakra's `<Button>`/`<Link>` do so automatically. "A registered-but-unread recipe looks like compliance and changes nothing." | Manual, §3; Playbook, Play 5 | MANDATORY |
| BM-33 | **One canonical styling surface per component type.** There are **no `.zimm-btn-*` classes and there must never be**. Every button is Chakra's `<Button>` styled by `theme/components/button.ts` — "never a class, never a hand-rolled `<button>` with its own styles." | Manual, §3 | MANDATORY |
| BM-34 | **27** `.zimm-*` global classes exist (`.zimm-text-*`, `.zimm-form-*`, `.zimm-grid`, `.zimm-focus-visible`). They are **not** the preferred authoring route for new components — only for "genuinely static, non-interactive, heavily-reused treatments — typography, the grid, form-field layout". `globalStyles.ts` ships on every page and has almost no consumers (one Storybook `.zimm-grid` demo). | Manual, §3 | MANDATORY |
| BM-35 | **A ui-kit component's styling surface is a theme recipe, always** — not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` class, not a co-located CSS file. Four cases: *is* a Chakra component → recipe at `theme/components/<name>.ts` (component becomes a thin prop-mapping layer) · **bespoke multipart** → recipe + register + `useMultiStyleConfig` + the `chakra()` factory · genuinely static/non-interactive/heavily reused → `.zimm-*` class · nothing fits → `sx`, then co-located `.scss` as last resort. A `.styles.ts`, a `cssVars`-style helper, a new `.zimm-*` class, or inline styles all mean the same conversation. | Manual, §3; Playbook, Play 1, Play 5 (Q9) | MANDATORY |
| BM-36 | The **theme key is PascalCase** (`ZimmTextInput`) while the **file is camelCase** (`zimmTextInput.ts`) — same split as `listMenu.ts` → `ListMenu`. A new recipe must be **registered in `theme/components/index.ts`** "or destructuring throws at runtime". Only `Button`, `Header`, `ListMenu` are registered today. | Manual, §3 | MANDATORY |
| BM-37 | **You do not add tokens.** `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` is Tier 1 and designer-owned (Hard Rule #3); a Figma value with no token is an escalation. `theme/globalStyles.ts` is Tier 2 (needs a named owner's nod). `theme/components/` **is** yours — one file per Chakra component, registered in that index. | Manual, §3, §7, §9 | MANDATORY |
| PB-13 | Check for **the correct token, not just a token.** "A value that resolves to the right pixels via the wrong token passes a casual glance and breaks the moment the design system moves." Named instance: two `sx` blocks hand-rebuilt what `textStyle="heading3"` and `textStyle="body2"` already provide, property for property. | Playbook, Play 5 | MANDATORY |
| PB-14 | `var(--zimm-*)` is the convention **inside** `theme/components/*.ts`. In component JSX it is not — that's rungs 1 and 2. "Seeing `var()` in a `.tsx` is a signal to look closer." | Playbook, Play 5 | MANDATORY |
| PB-15 | **No second copy of the token registry** — "any new utility that re-types token names as strings reintroduces exactly the drift the derived-token work removed." | Playbook, Play 5 | MANDATORY |
| BM-38 | `zimmTokens.ts` is **derived, not a second copy** (it imports `colors.grey[900]` rather than retyping `#191919`) — never edit it directly. `theme/index.test.tsx` guards the arrangement with **125 tests**; a failure there is a real drift signal, not test noise. | Manual, §3 | MANDATORY |
| BM-39 | Do not author in co-located CSS: a stylesheet can only see `var(--zimm-*)`, which is **derived output** — authoring there forfeits `textStyle`, the named `theme.space` scale, semantic colour tokens, responsive arrays, and the 125 drift-guard tests. "It isn't bad CSS; it's the wrong end of the pipeline." | Manual, §3; Playbook, Play 1 | MANDATORY |
| BM-40 | Layout traps that only rendering finds: (a) `width: min-content` resolves to the widest unbreakable run — correct only for a label whose break is deliberate, so **gate it on a signal meaning "this break is intentional"**; (b) **derive height from `lineHeight` + padding**, not `minHeight` + `align-items: center`, which collapses leading the moment content wraps; (c) a block `<li>` wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` **leaks ~1.5px per row** (5 rows = 9px against Figma) — use `display: flex` on the list item (axe confirmed list semantics survive). | Manual, §3 | MANDATORY |
| BM-41 | When no single value satisfies two constraints, a content-level fix can be the robust one (a non-breaking space widened a **1.9px** safe window — `[131, 132.9)` — to 71px) — **but note the dependency: production copy has to carry the same character.** | Manual, §3 | ADVISORY |

---

# 5. Accessibility

| ID | Requirement | Source | Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| BM-42 | Baseline is **WCAG 2.2 AA**. Fall back to 2.1 AA **only** where 2.2 is technically infeasible **and document why in the story**. | Manual, §6; Playbook, Play 6 | MANDATORY |
| BM-43 | The standing per-component AC set, applied to **every** component: keyboard operability and reachability · focus order and a **visible** focus state · all interaction states (hover, active, disabled, focused) · screen-reader behaviour for images and icon-only controls · behaviour when optional content is absent (no empty box, no layout break) · **target size ≥ 24×24 CSS px for interactive controls (SC 2.5.8)**. *(The playbook lists the first five; the manual adds the 24×24 item — see CONFLICTS.)* | Manual, §6; Playbook, Play 6 | MANDATORY |
| PB-16 | Accessibility lives **inside the component story as AC**, not as a follow-up task. | Playbook, Play 6 (#6, #12) | MANDATORY |
| BM-44 | **Chakra's `<Image>` is not covered** by the ast-grep `<img>` rule — that rule matches lowercase `<img>` only. "Most components here use `<Image>` — that one is on you." | Manual, §6; Playbook, Play 5 | MANDATORY |
| BM-45 | Already mechanically enforced (don't spend review time, but you will be caught): `<img>` without `alt` (`img-missing-alt`) · `IconButton`/`IconButtonWithRegistration` without `aria-label` (`icon-button-missing-aria-label`) · `onClick` on a non-interactive element without `role` (`clickable-non-interactive-element`) · unsanitised `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` (semgrep `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized`) · payment credentials logged (semgrep `payment-credential-logged`) · Storybook a11y (`addon-a11y`, `test: 'error'`, **fails CI**). | Manual, §6; Playbook, Play 5 | MANDATORY (mechanical) |
| BM-46 | **Not enforced anywhere — genuinely the author's responsibility:** keyboard flow, focus order, colour-contrast in states, screen-reader semantics beyond the above, and "whether the disabled state is actually communicated rather than just faded." | Manual, §6; Playbook, Play 5 (Q6) | MANDATORY |
| PB-17 | **Alt-text handling is an OPEN item — do not bake it into AC.** M2 landed on "if alt text exists render it; if not, don't render the attribute", which is technically wrong (omitting makes AT treat the image as meaningful-but-undescribed and commonly read the filename; `alt=""` removes it from the accessibility tree). The existing draft AC already says `alt=""`. Must be confirmed with Tim, framed as a **content-model** question (required alt, or an explicit decorative toggle), before it propagates into every image-bearing component. | Playbook, Play 6, Play 8 | MANDATORY (blocker — confirm, don't assume) |

Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills/code-quality

Audit code quality for the specified scope. Do not modify any files — this is a read-only
diagnostic. Produce a prioritised report with actionable fixes.

---

## Input

The user will provide one of:
- A file path or directory to audit
- No argument — default to files changed on the current branch: `git diff --name-only main`

If no argument is given, run: `git diff --name-only main` and audit those files.
Exclude test files (`*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`), stories (`*.stories.tsx`), and any registry files.

---

## Parallel execution

For audits covering more than 5 files, split into four independent checks and run them
as parallel agents simultaneously. Each agent receives only its own checklist — do not
bundle all checks into one agent.

- **Agent A — Naming & structure**
- **Agent B — Import analysis**
- **Agent C — TypeScript coverage**
- **Agent D — Test & story coverage**

For 5 files or fewer, run all checks sequentially in a single pass.

---

## Agent A — Naming & structure

Rules are defined once, split across [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md)
(cross-cutting), [css.md](../../rules/css.md) (Chakra/styling), and
[components.md](../../rules/components.md) (components/hooks/Storybook) — read the relevant
ones first, then apply each rule to the files in scope. Do not re-list the rules here;
that's how the files drift apart.

Walk the file list and audit each file against the relevant section:

- Every file → conventions.md **General** section.
- Every file with JSX/Chakra props → css.md **Tokens** section (no hardcoded hex/px values).
- `.tsx` under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/` → components.md
  **Components** + **Composition** sections, plus conventions.md **File naming and folder
  structure**.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/hooks/` → components.md **Hooks** section.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/utils/` → conventions.md **Utilities** section.

For each violation, record `file:line` and which rule file + bullet failed — the section
anchor is enough (e.g. "components.md → Components → Props type placement").

---

## Agent B — Import analysis

For each file, read the import statements and check:

- No circular imports: if File A imports from File B, File B must not import from File A
  (check by reading the imported file's imports in turn — one level deep is sufficient).
- No imports from a higher tier without justification:
  - A component must not import directly from internal `commerce-sdk-react` source paths.
  - A page must not bypass its own hooks to call raw API functions.
- No imports from a later-sprint feature (reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` when present).
- No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels — flag for path alias review.

---

## Agent C — TypeScript coverage

Check each file against the relevant rule file:

- Every `.ts`/`.tsx` → [typescript.md](../../rules/typescript.md) in full (no `any` without
  justification, `type` vs `interface`, non-null assertions, discriminated unions, utility
  types, `import type`, `satisfies`, `readonly`, generic naming).
- Components → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Components** (props type name,
  placement, optional `?`, callback naming, JSDoc).
- Hooks → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Hooks** (typed params, explicit
  return type, JSDoc with `@returns`).

Then run `npx tsc --noEmit` **once** for the whole branch (not per file) and report any
errors. Cross-reference any new errors against the files in scope.

---

## Agent D — Test & story coverage

For each component file under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/`:
- A paired `*.stories.tsx` exists in the same directory (required by [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) > Testing).
- For logic-heavy components or hooks: a `*.test.ts` exists OR a `play` function exists in the story.
- If a test file exists, verify:
  - At least one test covers the primary render case.
  - At least one test covers a user interaction (click, input) if the component has interactive elements.
  - No tests use `toBeTruthy()` as the sole assertion — check for meaningful assertions.
- If a paired `.stories.tsx` is missing, flag as MISSING STORY (mandatory).
- If a logic-heavy file has neither a `.test.ts` nor a `play` function, flag as MISSING TEST.

For each utility file under `overrides/app/utils/`:
- **`.test.ts` required** when the utility has ≥1 conditional branch or performs ≥1
  transformation (currency, locale, mapping, parsing, etc.). Trivial re-exports and
  one-liners are exempt.
- If a test file exists, verify it covers both the happy path and at least one edge case
  (empty input, null, locale variation — whichever applies).

---

## Output format

Combine all agent results into a single prioritised report:

```
## Code Quality Report
**Scope:** [files audited]
**Branch:** [current branch]
**Date:** [today]

### 🔴 Must fix before PR merge

```

```

But that script lives in the job tmp directory — it isn't in the repo and doesn't run in CI. So `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, which is what stops the storefront URL leaking to WhatsApp, has no regression net. My own verification gave me false confidence that coverage existed.

# Must-fix #1 — a type assertion sitting on the XSS guard

## What the code does now

```ts
// utils/safeHref.ts:15
export const isSafeHref = (href: string | undefined): boolean => (href ? SAFE_HREF_RE.test(href) : false);

// footer/index.tsx
const leavesTheSite = (href: string): boolean => /^https?:/i.test(href);   // takes string, not undefined

isSafeHref(href) ? (
  <chakra.a
    {...(leavesTheSite(href as string) ? { target: '_blank', rel: 'noopener noreferrer' } : {})}
    aria-label={leavesTheSite(href as string) ? `${label}${NEW_TAB_SUFFIX}` : label}
```

## The ELI5

`href` arrives as `string | undefined` — Contentful might not supply a channel. `isSafeHref` proves it's a usable string, and inside the `?` branch we know that. But `isSafeHref` is typed as returning a plain `boolean`, and a boolean carries **no information about `href`**. TypeScript still thinks `href` might be `undefined`. `leavesTheSite` only accepts `string`. So the call doesn't type-check, and someone — me — silenced it with `as string`.

`as` is not a check. It's *"trust me, compiler."* It generates no runtime code and no error. It's a promise.

## Why it's must-fix rather than cosmetic

Two reasons, and the second is the real one.

**First:** `typescript.md` requires an inline comment explaining any `as`, on the same reasoning as `any`. Neither of these has one. The comments nearby explain the *guard's purpose* and *why `rel` is explicit* — not the assertion. So it fails the rule as written.

**Second, and this is why I put it in must-fix:** it's on the line that decides `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. That attribute is what stops the storefront URL leaking to WhatsApp in the `Referer` header. Twelve `as` casts in a layout file are noise. An `as` on the branch that controls a security attribute is the one place where "trust me" costs something — because a future change to `isSafeHref`'s signature will produce a **silent** miscompile there rather than an error.

The specific failure: change `isSafeHref` to accept a richer input type, and `href` stops being narrowable. Every other call site errors. These two don't — `as string` swallows it, and `leavesTheSite` receives something that isn't a string, `/^https?:/i.test()` coerces it, and the new-tab decision goes wrong quietly.

## The fix, and why not the obvious one

Agent C proposed a **type predicate**:

```ts
export const isSafeHref = (href: string | undefined): href is string => ...
```

That compiles and removes both casts — I tested it, `tsc` 0. **But it's unsound, and I'd push back on it.** `href is string` tells TypeScript *"if this returns false, it isn't a string."* That's false:

```
isSafeHref("javascript:void(0)") = false        typeof "javascript:void(0)" = string
```

So in the `else` branch TypeScript narrows `href` to `undefined` when it's actually an unsafe string. Harmless **today** — I checked all three false branches and none reads `href`; they render `<span>`/`<button>`. But it plants a trap: the day someone logs the rejected value, the compiler tells them it's `undefined`. And it does that by changing a **shared util's** contract, so `zimmNavItem` inherits it too.

What I'd ship instead — widen the local helper:

```diff
- const leavesTheSite = (href: string): boolean => /^https?:/i.test(href);
+ const leavesTheSite = (href: string | undefined): boolean => /^https?:/i.test(href ?? '');
```

```
tsc 0 · vitest 187/187 · eslint 0 · both `as string` gone
```

No assertion, no narrowing claim, no soundness hole. `safeHref`'s contract untouched, so `zimmNavItem` is unaffected. Honest about the input it actually receives.

---

# Must-fix #2 — two casts that were never needed

```tsx
onClick?: (e: React.MouseEvent<HTMLAnchorElement | HTMLButtonElement>) => void;   // :22

onClick={onClick as React.MouseEventHandler<HTMLAnchorElement>}   // :40  on <chakra.a>
onClick={onClick as React.MouseEventHandler<HTMLButtonElement>}   // :54  on <chakra.button>
```

## The ELI5

`ZimmNavItem` renders an `<a>` when the href is safe and a `<button>` otherwise. The prop accepts an event from **either**, so it's a union. Someone assumed handing a union-typed handler to an anchor-specific slot would need a cast.

It doesn't. **Function parameters are contravariant.** A handler that copes with "anchor *or* button" is strictly *more* capable than one that only copes with anchors — so it's already assignable, no cast required. Same as offering a mechanic who fixes cars and motorbikes to a job that only needs cars: they're overqualified, not unqualified.

```
removed 2 casts  →  tsc 0 errors
```

## Why it's must-fix and not backlog

A cast that changes nothing isn't harmless — it's a **live suppression** sitting on the prop's only wiring point.

Concretely: change line 22 to `React.MouseEvent<HTMLAnchorElement>` only. That's now genuinely wrong for the `<button>` branch, and the compiler should say so. It won't. `as React.MouseEventHandler<HTMLButtonElement>` asserts the mismatch away, and you get a runtime type error in the branch that renders for every unsafe or absent href — which, given the fixture ships `#` for 19 of 20 links, is most of the footer.

The fix is deleting eleven words. It costs nothing and restores the compiler's ability to fail on the one thing that would actually break.

---

## Both share a shape worth naming

Neither is a bug today. Both are **verified-safe suppressions on branches that matter** — the security attribute in #1, the button path in #2. That's the category the FED playbook's PB-35 is about from the other direction: *"would this still fail if the feature were broken in the obvious way?"* Here the answer is no, and that's the defect.

`#2` is unambiguous — I'd just delete them. `#1` has two candidate fixes and I'd take the widening over the predicate for the soundness reason above, but say the word if you'd rather have the predicate.

## Two things the verification caught that I'd have otherwise missed

**My parts-consistency check was wrong, again.** After moving `logoButton` my static regex reported *4 missing baseStyle keys*. It was my regex — HEAD reports the identical 4, and importing the recipe gives **34/34, missing NONE**. Third time this session I've reported a proxy as a finding; the runtime import is the only check that means anything here.

**The hook extraction had zero CI coverage — proven, not assumed.** After extracting, I mutation-tested it: breaking focus-into-modal **and** breaking Escape-to-close both passed the full Storybook suite 75/75. Only my Phase 3 script caught them, and that script isn't in the repo. So a refactor of focus-trap code had no regression net in CI at all.

That's Agent D's S3, which wasn't in your #3–#12 list — but since I'd just moved that exact code, shipping it uncovered wasn't defensible. I added focus-entry, Escape-dismissal and focus-restore assertions to `SubscribeModalOpen`, then re-ran:

## Four commits

```
712065f  fix(registry): escape angle brackets outside code spans and match extended Props types
2c4ab7a  refactor(footer): replace type assertions with honest signatures on the guard path
0269957  refactor(footer): reattach detached comments, name the recipe key, drop dead state

```

`footer/index.tsx` spans three of the four, so I built each commit's intended tree state forward from `HEAD` and ran `tsc` against it before committing — validating what actually lands, not just the end state:

```
A   tsc 0                        generator only
B   tsc 0 · vitest 187/187       floated tests still present here
C   tsc 0 · vitest 185/185       floated tests removed
D   tsc 0 · vitest 185/185       tree diffed identical to the verified snapshot
```

That last check matters most: after commit D I diffed the working tree against the snapshot I'd run the full phase suite and mutation tests against — **identical**, so the four-way split moved no code.

## Final gate

```
working tree   clean
tsc            0 errors
vitest         185/185
prettier       clean
eslint         3 warnings — all pre-existing in header/index.tsx
```

Those three are the unused `AccountIcon`/`HeartIcon`/`IconButtonWithRegistration` that our 14 added comment lines exist to *explain*. Diff to that file is 14 added, 0 removed.

## Registry landed where the hook put it

As expected, pre-commit regenerated `.claude/registry/` and auto-staged it into B and C rather than following my grouping — it reads the working tree, not the index. Commit B carries the 22-line `components.md` change from the fixed `escapeCell`, which is arguably where it belongs anyway since A is the generator that produced it.

## CI

Checks are running now. Expected green except **BrowserStack**, which will fail again on `Config file does not exist` — pre-existing infrastructure, Integration's to fix. CodeRabbit will re-review this push.

## Still outstanding

Three decisions are yours: **`ui-kits` naming** (Hard Rule #6, and PB-39 records it as unsettled with Han using the same convention), the **header icons import** (Tier 2 Global Shell, dormant), and the **PB-35 locale assertion** that asserts the absence of a feature.

And **eight CodeRabbit replies** are still owed on the PR — the five from before plus the three declines from today's runs, each with cause: the `@storybook/test` import is disproven, the resolver tests already exist with 21 assertions, and adding foundation tokens would breach Hard Rule #3. here's the User Story for this PR: "Global Footer UI




Key details
Templates ➤


Story
Description

As a Shopper, 
I want to see a consistent global footer on every page, 
so that I can access navigation links, contact information, legal content, and newsletter sign-up from anywhere on the site.

Reference image (Figma is leading):

image-20260618-041717.png
The global footer is displayed at the bottom of every page across all storefronts and devices. It is CMS-managed via Contentful, allowing business users to update footer links and copy without a code deployment. The content of the footer (e.g. links) can be configured per storefront. Contentful integration is covered in a separate user story. This story covers the footer shell, layout, and component structure only — footer link destinations, email sign-up Omneo integration, and Cookie Settings behaviour are covered in separate stories.
Links like “ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF COUNTRY” are only relevant on the AU storefront, however, for the purpose of this user story we can include whatever placeholder links we want and can use the design as a first set of links.

Responsive behaviour: There is a footer design for both desktop and mobile.

Rollout Scope

AU
ME
EU - Domestic
EU - International
HK
UK
US - Domestic
US - International
Acceptance Criteria


Shopper

Given a shopper visits any page on the storefront, when the page loads, then the global footer is displayed at the bottom of the page on both desktop and mobile.

Given a shopper views the footer on desktop, when the page loads, then navigation links are displayed in columns (ABOUT, CONTACT, HELP) per the Figma design.

Given a shopper hovers over one of the navigation links, the rollover state will be that that word or those words are underlined.

Given a shopper views the footer on mobile, when the page loads, then navigation columns stack vertically per the Figma design.

Given a shopper views the footer, when the page loads, then the Stay in Touch section is displayed with an email input field and submit button as a placeholder component.

Given a shopper views the footer, when the page loads, then the Zimmermann wordmark, region/currency indicator, copyright text, and legal links are displayed in the bottom bar per the Figma design.

Site Merchandiser

Given a storefront needs particular links to be included in the footer, when the merchandiser is setting up the storefront in SFCC, then they are able to define the links in the footer per storefront.

Assumptions

We will build the footer structure first, without any content behind the different links and buttons.

Design/Technical Notes


Link to Footer: https://www.figma.com/design/wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm/Zimmermann_Design_System_2026?node-id=2083-54022&m=devYour team sees richer Figma previewsConnect

content.text:
You're right to challenge it. Here's what the evidence actually says.

## The modal has a requirement — just not from this story

`.docs/prd/homepage.md` §6, both marked **confirmed**:

```
HPC-035  On clicking the Continue CTA, a modal collects the customer's first name and last name
HPC-037  Sign-up modal displays privacy consent copy, a link to the local Privacy Policy,
         and an accessibility disclaimer
```

So it isn't invented from nothing. But it belongs to the homepage PRD's **"Join Us" email capture** flow, and SFCC-55's AC says something narrower:

> *"…then the Stay in Touch section is displayed with **an email input field and submit button as a placeholder component**."*

Plus two explicit exclusions in the same story: *"email sign-up Omneo integration … covered in separate stories"* and *"We will build the footer structure first, **without any content behind the different links and buttons**."*

A modal that collects names to post to Omneo is content behind a button. HPC-036 — the Omneo POST it exists to feed — is deferred by this story's own text.

## And you're right about the designs — there are none

```
subscribeModalPanel   — no Figma reference
modalOverlay          — no Figma reference
modalTitle            — no Figma reference
modalField            — no Figma reference
modalConsent          — no Figma reference
modalActions          — no Figma reference

for contrast: footer.ts carries 27 Figma refs across nodes
              40000407:11736 · 40000461:10415 · 40000538:24875
```

Every footer part that *has* a design cites its node. **All nine modal parts cite nothing.** So its panel width, overlay treatment, field spacing, and button layout were all decided locally — which is exactly what `overrideStyling.md` and your own playbook forbid: *"Anything the design system doesn't answer goes to Kiera. Nothing gets invented locally."* And BM-75: *"missing design for a state → design review, and flag on the story before it's sized."*

## Scale

```
SubscribeModal        77 lines
useSubscribeModal    106 lines   ← I extracted this today
modal theme parts      9
story states           2
Figma coverage         0
```

I should own part of this: I spent a chunk of today refactoring and adding coverage to un-designed UI, and extracting a hook for it. The code is correct against HPC-035/037 — but correctness against a requirement isn't the same as belonging in this PR.

## Two source-of-truth documents disagree

This is the case AGENTS.md says to stop on — a conflict *within* the docs, not between a doc and an instruction. `homepage.md` §6 requires the modal; SFCC-55's AC scopes the footer to a placeholder input and button. Both are confirmed. Neither references the other.

Worth noting the PR body already declares the modal openly (*"the Join Us modal"*, *"4 states incl. modal-open"*), so it isn't hidden — but declaring it isn't the same as it being in scope, and no decision to build it ahead of HPC-035 is recorded anywhere in `projectState.md`.

## What I'd recommend

**Keep the code, descope it from this PR** — put the modal behind the state machine's `unavailable` path so submit shows the existing "temporarily unavailable" message and the modal never opens. That satisfies the AC exactly (input + button, placeholder), removes un-designed UI from a PR heading for `develop`, and keeps the work intact for HPC-035 once Kiera supplies a design. Roughly a one-line gate plus removing two story states.

The alternative — ship it and flag it — leaves us with un-designed UI live on eight storefronts, and QA writing test cases against a layout the designer never approved. My earlier note that **SFCC-T120 won't test it** is a symptom of the same gap.

Either way this needs Jasmijn and Dani, not just us: Jasmijn added the hover AC specifically so it would be built *and tested*, and the 2 July comment records Dani's design sign-off as still pending. A modal with no Figma node can't have been part of that sign-off.

Want me to draft the message to them, or prepare the descope so you can compare the two options against the AC side by side?

## What changed

`enableNameCapture?: boolean`, defaulting **false**, threaded `Footer` → `SubscribeSection`:

```ts
const handleEmailSubmit = (email: string) => {
  pendingSignupRef.current.email = email;
  if (enableNameCapture) { setModalOpen(true); return; }
  // Descoped path, and the default. SFCC-55's AC scopes this section to "an email input
  // field and submit button as a placeholder component"… HPC-035/HPC-037 are confirmed in
  // .docs/prd/homepage.md §6 but have no Figma node — all nine theme parts are undesigned,
  // unlike the 27 Figma-referenced parts around it.
  setSubmitState('unavailable');
  pendingSignupRef.current = { email: '', firstName: '', lastName: '' };
};
```

The modal is also not mounted at all when off, and the PII ref is cleared on the descoped path — nothing was sent, so nothing needs retaining.

## Verification

```
tsc 0 · vitest 185/185 · eslint 0 · prettier clean
phase 5 (CI parity, built Storybook) 76/76, 12 suites
```

Mutation-tested, and one result is worth being precise about:

| Mutation | Result | |
|---|---|---|
| default `enableNameCapture` back to `true` | **1 failed** | ✅ the descope is genuinely asserted |
| remove the `{enableNameCapture && }` render gate | 76 passed | **correct** — not a gap |

The second one passing is right, not a hole. With the prop still false, `handleEmailSubmit` never sets `modalOpen`, so the modal mounts with `isOpen={false}` and `line 105: if (!mounted || !isOpen) return null` — nothing renders, no user-visible change. The **branch in `handleEmailSubmit` is the load-bearing gate**; the render gate is defensive, stopping an unreachable dialog from mounting at all. I'd rather say that than claim a coverage gap I can't demonstrate.

Subscribe — placeholder path (SFCC-55 default) ← NEW, the shipped behaviour
Subscribe — two-step flow (HPC-035, not shipped)      ← opts in

The two modal stories are renamed so nobody reads them as shipped scope, and they keep the modal exercised — including the focus/Escape assertions that took mutation testing to get right — so HPC-035 inherits working, covered code rather than a rebuild.

Type a valid email → click `>` → **no modal**, the field is replaced by *"Subscription is temporarily unavailable. Please try again later."* Empty and malformed emails still blocked inline. That's the AC: input plus submit button as a placeholder.

content.text:
Measured, not inferred. Here's the arithmetic. ## What actually happens ``` idle
→
45px (input + submit) after
→

68px (message) Δ 23px propagates: contentRow +22px → footer 490 → 512px ``` The `aria-live` wrapper is a bare `

` with **`minHeight: 0px`** — it reserves nothing. It's sized purely by whichever child is currently mounted, and the two children have genuinely different natural heights. ## Why the paragraph is 68px ``` 320px wide · 80 chars · 2 visual lines lineHeight 18px × 2 lines = 36px paddingTop 'm' + paddingBottom 'm' = 16 + 16 = 32px total = 68px ``` So it isn't the text that dominates — it's **32px of vertical padding** on `subscribeSuccess` against 36px of actual text. The recipe sets `paddingTop: 'm'` / `paddingBottom: 'm'`, and there's no `minHeight` anywhere in the chain to absorb the swap. ## Three compounding factors **1. Nothing reserves the space.** `styles.subscribeSuccess` has `margin: 0` and no `minHeight`; the wrapper has none either. The taller state simply wins. **2. The two messages are different lengths, so the shift isn't even consistent.** ``` 80 chars "You're on the list! Be the first to know about new collections…" → 2 lines 64 chars "Subscription is temporarily unavailable. Please try again later." → likely 1 line ``` Both render through the same `subscribeSuccess` part. At 320px the success copy wraps to two lines and the unavailable copy probably doesn't — so today's shipped path (unavailable) and tomorrow's post-HPC-036 path (success) jump by *different* amounts. Any fixed `minHeight` has to cover the longest, and translated copy across eight storefronts will be longer still. **3. Everything below moves.** The subscribe column is in `contentRow`, so the wordmark and the entire bottom bar — locale control, copyright, legal links — all shift down 22px at the moment of submit. ## One thing worth being precise about This is **not** a Lighthouse CLS penalty. Core Web Vitals excludes shifts within 500ms of user input, and this one is click-triggered. So it won't show up in the LCP/CLS budget — it's a UX jank problem and an accessibility one, not a metrics one. Worth knowing before anyone treats it as a perf regression. The accessibility angle is the more interesting half: the region is `aria-live="polite"`, so a screen reader announces the new message — but a sighted keyboard user watching the bottom bar jump 22px under their cursor gets no such courtesy. ## Fix options **Reserve the height on the wrapper** — `minHeight` equal to the tallest state, so the swap is invisible. Simplest, but the value is copy- and locale-dependent, so it's a magic number that rots. **Derive it instead** — the form is 45px and the message is `2 × lineHeight + 2 × padding`. Setting the wrapper's `minHeight` from those tokens rather than a literal keeps it traceable, and matches the approach we took for the nav-item height (derive from `lineHeight` + padding, don't guess). **Or reduce the message's own padding** so the two states are closer — but 32px of padding against 36px of text looks like it may itself be unintentional, and that's a design question for Kiera, not something to tune by eye. I'd want the Figma spec for the post-submit state before picking. Do we have a node for it? If the design only ever shows the idle state — which is what I'd expect, given the modal had no node either — then this is the same class of gap: undesigned UI making its own layout decisions. Want me to check the Figma footer node for a submitted/confirmation state?

Fully decomposed. Here's why it jumps.

## The measurement

```
element        idle h/y        after h/y       Δh     Δy
footer         490/510         512/488          22    -22
contentRow     276/510         298/488          22    -22
subscribeCol   164/574         186/552          22    -22
liveRegion      45/692          68/670          23    -22
inputAction     45/692          —             gone
message          —             68/670           new
linksCol       164/574         186/552          22    -22
logoArea       135/786         135/786           0      0
```

## The cause

```
IDLE    form  45px   (padding 0/0)          column width 320px
AFTER   msg   68px   (padding 16/16)
        text box 36px = 2 lines × 18px (font 14px)
        "Subscription is temporarily unavailable. Please try again later."

Δ = 23px       padding 32px + text 36px = 68   vs   form 45px
```

Two things compound:

**1. `subscribeSuccess` adds 32px of vertical padding the form doesn't have.**

```ts
subscribeSuccess: {
  textStyle: 'body2',
  paddingTop: 'm',      // 16px
  paddingBottom: 'm',   // 16px
}
```

The form it replaces has `padding: 0`. So before a single character is measured, the replacement is already 32px taller than the element's own content box.

**2. The message wraps to two lines.** The subscribe column is capped at `SIZE_COL_SUB` = 20rem = **320px**, and that sentence needs two 18px lines at `body2`. So 36px of text + 32px of padding = 68px against the form's 45px.

`logoArea` is the tell: **Δh 0, Δy 0**. Nothing below the content row moved relative to the footer — the whole 22px came from inside the subscribe column, and because the footer sits at the page bottom, it grows *upward*, which is why every `Δy` is `-22`.

`linksCol` also reports +22 without any content change — it's a flex sibling stretching to the row's new height. So the site-map column visually grows too, which is likely what makes the jump so noticeable.

## One thing worth flagging

The shift is **message-dependent**, so it isn't a fixed 22px. The success string — *"You're on the list! Be the first to know about new collections and new arrivals."* — is much longer and will wrap to three lines at 320px, making the jump larger again. Right now only the `unavailable` path is reachable (the descope), so 22px is what you'll see; the success path becomes reachable with HPC-036 and will be worse.

That makes the message 23px taller than the control it replaces. The body copy's `marginBottom: 40px` doesn't change, so the entire 23px lands as growth. ## What the design says The success node keeps a **`Textfield` instance** in place — it doesn't swap in a paragraph: ```xml Subscribe Section y=64 320 × 141 About Link y=0 h=8 ← "KEEP IN TOUCH" Our Story Link y=32 h=26 ← body copy Textfield y=82 320 × 59 ← the message lives HERE ``` Compare to the idle state: subscribe column **142** vs success **141**, and the `Textfield` slot is **59px in both**. The footer is **476px in both**. The design treats the message as a *state of the field*, occupying the field's box — which is exactly why it can't shift. ## Two separate gaps, and only one is real ``` figma idle submitted control slot 59 45 68 ← REAL: −14 then +9 heading h 8 18 18 ← artefact body h 26 36 36 ← artefact ``` The heading and body `+10`s are **not** errors — that's the cap-height issue your build manual documents (BM-72): Figma's text boxes are cap-height, browser line boxes aren't. The control slot is different. `Textfield` is an **instance**, not a text node, so 59px is a real frame height — and our field renders 45px. That's a genuine idle-state gap, and it's the root of the `subscribe Δ22` I logged during Phase 4 and never traced to a cause. Assertion added and proven. **76/76**, and it catches both regressions.

## Storybook gate

```
BASELINE (built)                          76 passed
MUTATION A  remove minHeight               1 failed  ✅
MUTATION B  restore subscribeSuccess pad   1 failed  ✅
RESTORED                                  76 passed
```

Each run is a **full rebuild + static server** — the CI-parity path.

## The assertion

```ts
// Asserted on the slot as well as the footer: at desktop widths the taller site-map column
// sets the row height, so a footer-only check passes even when the column has shifted.
await expect(rounded(slot.getBoundingClientRect().height)).toBe(rounded(slotBefore));
await expect(rounded(footer.getBoundingClientRect().height)).toBe(rounded(heightBefore));
```

Checking the **slot** as well as the footer is what makes it work. A footer-only assertion would have passed under both mutations at Storybook's viewport, because the site-map column sets the row height there — exactly the false-negative the earlier measurements exposed.

## I have to flag how I nearly got this wrong

My first mutation run reported **1 failed on the baseline**, which made all four results uninterpretable. I'd pointed `test-storybook` at the **dev** server for speed — which BM-05 explicitly says isn't a valid target, and which I'd already been corrected on earlier today. After ~15 rapid file mutations its bundle was unreliable.

Two follow-on misreads while diagnosing it:

- The failure reported `index.stories.tsx:417`. The file is **206 lines** — that's a *bundle* offset, not a source line, and I initially read it as one.
- My probe timed out on `input[type=email]` and I suspected the story was broken. It wasn't: `test-storybook` runs the play, which submits the form, so the input is legitimately gone by the time a later query looks for it.

Neither was a code problem. Both were my instrumentation, and the fix was to stop taking the shortcut.

## State

```
tsc 0 · built Storybook 76/76 · parts 35/35 runtime-verified
shift: footer / contentRow / column / slot all Δ0 across 4 viewports
```

Uncommitted, in two logical pieces:

```
descope         footer/index.tsx · index.stories.tsx    enableNameCapture opt-in, 3 stories
layout shift    theme/components/footer.ts · both above  subscribeControl slot + assertion
```

`SIZE_SUBSCRIBE_SLOT` is still the measured 45px with the Figma 59px discrepancy annotated for Kiera — that stays a design question.

the form is 45px (36px content + 4/4 padding + 1px border) while the message was 68px (36px of

the footer stays 476 in both states: the message is a state of the field, occupying the field's
box, not a paragraph with padding of its own. So the slot is now reserved and the message no
longer supplies vertical padding.

Both halves are load-bearing, which the measurements only showed at mobile. Dropping the padding
alone appears to fix it at desktop and tablet — the message becomes shorter than the field, so the
column shrinks 9px and the taller site-map column keeps the row height unchanged. On mobile the

768, 375 and 320, with no clipping or text overflow.

input.prompt:
Audit repo /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui, 55 commits ahead of develop.

YOUR SCOPE — imports and override/architecture correctness ONLY. Other agents own tokens/CSS, TypeScript, tests, AC conformance.

READ FIRST, in full:
- .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md — especially "Importing an already-overridden component from a new component" and "The SFCC bridge pattern"
- .claude/rules/conventions.md — the "Imports" section
- .claude/rules/components.md — "Composition" (container/presentational separation)
- .docs/memory/sprintScope.md if it exists

AUDIT every .ts/.tsx in `git diff origin/develop --name-only` under overrides/, plus .storybook/preview.tsx.

Check:
1. **THE BIG ONE — base-path import of an already-overridden component.** If file A imports `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/B` and `overrides/app/components/B/` ALSO exists, then the real app build resolves to the override but Storybook (`.storybook/main.js` aliases the package straight to node_modules) and Vitest (no alias at all) resolve to BASE. The story/test then silently exercises the wrong component. For every base-path import, `ls` the corresponding overrides path and report every hit. A base-path import with NO local override is CORRECT — do not flag it.
2. **Circular imports** — one level deep is sufficient; verify mechanically across the overrides/ graph.
3. **No imports from internal node_modules/@salesforce/... source paths** (published entrypoints only).
4. **Container/presentational separation** — nothing under overrides/app/components/ may call data-fetching hooks (@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react, React Query). Note: useMultiSite and useHistory are NOT data-fetching.
5. **No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels.**
6. **No imports from a later-sprint feature** (cross-check .docs/memory/sprintScope.md).
7. **Bridge pattern** — for any component overridden here, grep whether SFCC's own base components import it: `grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`. - overrides/app/utils/safeHref.ts — an allow-list guard whose result gates whether an href reaches an anchor
- overrides/app/hooks/useSubscribeModal.ts — newly extracted, owns focus management and a keyboard trap
- overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx — the largest file; check the SubmitState union, the PendingSignup type, and the new enableNameCapture prop threading

- Do not report a proxy as a finding; verify by compiling rather than by reading, where you can.

input.prompt:
Audit repo /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui, 55 commits ahead of develop.

YOUR SCOPE — test and story coverage ONLY, and whether the tests that exist have real value. Other agents own tokens/CSS, imports, TypeScript, AC conformance.

READ FIRST, in full:
- .claude/rules/testing.md
- .claude/rules/components.md — the "Storybook" section
- AGENTS.md — the "Testing" section

AUDIT every component/hook/util in `git diff origin/develop --name-only`.

Part 1 — COVERAGE PRESENCE:
- Every component exported from its folder under overrides/app/components/ needs a *.stories.tsx. Internal sub-components rendering inside a single parent are EXEMPT — verify by grepping for importers before flagging.
- Logic-heavy components/hooks need a *.test.ts OR a `play`. Utilities need a .test.ts when they have >=1 conditional or perform a transformation.
- Story `title` must be one of: Foundation/ Elements/ Layout/ Commerce/ Forms/ Pages/ Contentful/. Every story file needs a `Default` export.
- Produce an inventory table: component | story? | title | play count | unit test?

Part 2 — DO THE TESTS ACTUALLY HAVE VALUE? This is the more important half.
For each significant assertion, ask testing.md's question and the FED playbook's standing one: **"would this test still pass if the feature were broken in the obvious way?"** Flag any assertion that:
- asserts the ABSENCE of a feature (encoding a placeholder as expected behaviour, so it FAILS when the feature is correctly implemented later)
- is vacuous (iterates an empty collection, asserts a tautology, or `toBeTruthy()` as the sole assertion)
- tests the framework rather than our code
- duplicates coverage that a cheaper layer already provides

Known instance of the first category, confirm and look for others like it: a Playwright/phase script asserts 'locale button present but inert'. The locale control is an annotated placeholder; that assertion will FAIL when the locale selector is wired.

Part 3 — WHAT IS STILL UNCOVERED THAT MATTERS? Specifically assess:
- overrides/app/hooks/useSubscribeModal.ts — newly extracted; owns focus save/restore, body-scroll lock, Escape/Tab trap
- overrides/app/utils/safeHref.ts — the XSS allow-list guard
- the footer's contact-channel target/rel treatment (rel="noopener noreferrer")
- the subscribe state machine and the enableNameCapture gate
- the no-layout-shift assertion in the SubscribePlaceholder story
For each: state where coverage lives, or that it is absent.

ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS:
- `ls` the directory to confirm a file is absent before calling it missing. Do not infer.
- COVERAGE THROUGH A CONSUMER COUNTS. testing.md says pick the cheapest layer that proves the behaviour; a slot prop is correctly covered by the molecule that fills it, not the atom exposing it. Before flagging something untested, check whether a consumer's story or test exercises it, and report where the coverage actually lives. I previously reported `trailing` as uncovered when three `play` functions in ZimmInputAction exercise it.
- A case-sensitive grep miss is not absence — retry case-insensitively. I previously concluded "no story references the clear button" from a case-sensitive grep for "Clear input" while the story matched /clear input/i, and broke CI.
- `storybook/test` is the CORRECT import path on this repo's Storybook 10; `@storybook/test` is NOT installed. Do not flag the former.
- Run `npx vitest run` to confirm the current pass count. Do NOT run test-storybook or build Storybook — I am doing that; a concurrent build would collide.

OUTPUT: the inventory table, then findings classified MUST-FIX / SHOULD-FIX / BACKLOG, plus an explicit "verified adequately covered" section naming where coverage lives. Read-only — do not modify files.

input.description: Jira AC conformance audit
input.prompt:
Audit repo /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui, against its Jira user story. You are checking CODE vs REQUIREMENTS — not code quality. Other agents own tokens/CSS, imports, TypeScript, tests.

=== THE USER STORY: SFCC-55 "Global Footer UI" ===

As a Shopper, I want to see a consistent global footer on every page, so that I can access navigation links, contact information, legal content, and newsletter sign-up from anywhere on the site.

SCOPE STATEMENTS (these bound the work):
- "The global footer is displayed at the bottom of every page across all storefronts and devices. It is CMS-managed via Contentful... Contentful integration is covered in a separate user story."
- "This story covers the footer shell, layout, and component structure only — footer link destinations, email sign-up Omneo integration, and Cookie Settings behaviour are covered in separate stories."
- "Links like ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF COUNTRY are only relevant on the AU storefront, however, for the purpose of this user story we can include whatever placeholder links we want and can use the design as a first set of links."
- Responsive: "There is a footer design for both desktop and mobile."
- Rollout scope: AU, ME, EU-Domestic, EU-International, HK, UK, US-Domestic, US-International
- ASSUMPTION: "We will build the footer structure first, without any content behind the different links and buttons."
- NOTE: "Keep in mind that the minimum size of that email sign up button is taken into consideration for accessibility purposes"

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — Shopper:
AC1. Given a shopper visits any page on the storefront, when the page loads, then the global footer is displayed at the bottom of the page on both desktop and mobile.
AC2. Given a shopper views the footer on desktop, when the page loads, then navigation links are displayed in columns (ABOUT, CONTACT, HELP) per the Figma design.
AC3. Given a shopper hovers over one of the navigation links, the rollover state will be that that word or those words are underlined.
AC4. Given a shopper views the footer on mobile, when the page loads, then navigation columns stack vertically per the Figma design.
AC5. Given a shopper views the footer, when the page loads, then the Stay in Touch section is displayed with an email input field and submit button as a placeholder component.
AC6. Given a shopper views the footer, when the page loads, then the Zimmermann wordmark, region/currency indicator, copyright text, and legal links are displayed in the bottom bar per the Figma design.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — Site Merchandiser:
AC7. Given a storefront needs particular links to be included in the footer, when the merchandiser is setting up the storefront in SFCC, then they are able to define the links in the footer per storefront.

=== YOUR TASK ===

For EACH of AC1-AC7 plus the scope statements and the accessibility note, determine from the code whether it is: SATISFIED / PARTIALLY SATISFIED / NOT SATISFIED / OUT OF SCOPE BY THE STORY'S OWN TEXT. Cite file:line evidence for every verdict. Read overrides/app/components/footer/, overrides/app/theme/components/footer.ts, overrides/app/components/ui-kits/, and the fixture/types.

Then answer these specific questions:
1. **AC7 (merchandiser-defined links per storefront).** The story says Contentful integration is a separate story. Does the code provide the STRUCTURE for per-storefront link definition even though the integration is deferred? Is AC7 satisfiable by this PR, or is it necessarily deferred? Be precise about what exists (types, schema placeholder, fixture) vs what doesn't.
2. **AC5.** Does the Stay in Touch section render exactly "an email input field and submit button as a placeholder component" — no more? Check whether anything beyond that ships ENABLED. Note: a name-capture modal exists in the code behind an `enableNameCapture` prop that defaults false — assess whether that satisfies or violates AC5.
3. **The accessibility note on the email submit button's minimum size.** WCAG 2.5.8 requires a 24x24 CSS px minimum target. Find the button's rendered target size in the theme/component code and state whether it meets it.
4. **Rollout scope — 8 storefronts.** Find anything hardcoded to a single storefront that would be wrong on the other seven (locale labels, currency, region strings, AU-specific content, hardcoded hrefs). This matters: the code contains a LOCALE_LABEL_PLACEHOLDER.
5. **Anything BUILT THAT THE STORY DOES NOT ASK FOR.** Scope creep is as much a finding as a gap. List it.
6. Is there anything in the AC that the code CANNOT satisfy without a separate story, which should be flagged back to the BA?

ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS:

This resolves two things, including correcting myself.

## Pixel comparison — the subscribe column, both states

```
── IDLE ──              figma    ours     Δ
column height           142      163      +21
control slot y           98      118      +20
control slot h           44       45       +1     ✅

column height           141      163      +22
control slot y           82      118      +36
control slot h           59       45      −14     ← real
gap body→control         24       40      +16     ← real
```

**The idle Δ21 is fully explained, and it isn't a defect.** The control slot lands at exactly the right height (44 vs 45) with exactly the right gap above it (40 vs 40). The whole delta is the slot sitting 20px lower, and that decomposes precisely:

```
        figma          ours
heading  8              18      +10  cap-height artefact
gap     24              24        0
body    26              36      +10  cap-height artefact
        ──             ──
        58              78      +20  = the slot's y offset
```

Two text blocks, each measuring 10px taller in a browser than Figma's cap-height boxes — exactly BM-72. That closes the `subscribe Δ22` item I'd logged as unexplained since the first Phase 4 run. Nothing to fix; "correcting" it would produce the nonsense the manual warns about.

## I got the success state wrong earlier

I told you *"the design's slot is 59px in both states."* It isn't. The design-system file documents `footer/textfield` with **two variants**:

```
Subscribed=False   320 × 44
Subscribed=True    308 × 59
```

And the composed frames show how the column stays flat:

```
design   field 44 → message 59  (+15)   gap 40 → 24  (−16)   ⇒ column 142 → 141
ours     slot  45 → 45          ( 0)    gap 40 → 40  (  0)   ⇒ column 163 → 163
```

The design *does* grow the box — by 15 — and pulls it **up** 16px to compensate. It's a repositioning, not a reserved slot. My fix reserved the slot instead, which lands the same outcome (no shift, and ours is flat rather than −1) but by a different mechanism.

**So two real deltas remain in the success state:** our message box is **14px shorter** and sits **16px lower** than the design.

And the useful correction to my earlier advice: the subscribed message is **not undesigned**. It's a documented component variant, narrower too (308 vs 320). So implementing it is a build task, not a Kiera question — which changes what I said when we descoped.

content.text:
Confirmed by measurement. Two blocking findings, and I'm not going to sit on them while the last two agents finish.

## 🔴 Blocker 1 — a font licence prohibition was reversed inside this PR

`.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` is **Tier 1 Governance**. This branch **deleted** this text from it:

> **No font binaries in this repo.** Futura Round ships under a Monotype *"Font Software For Desktop End User License Agreement"* which forbids "further distribute the Font Software, or any copy thereof" and "Install the Font Software on any server or in any digital asset management system" — so `.woff2`/`.otf` must not be committed here or served from the MRT CDN. […] Self-hosting needs Zimmermann's own Monotype **Web Page Content** entitlement.

…replaced it with *"Fonts are self-hosted for development and testing"*, and committed two 32K `.woff2` files. The history shows this was **already decided once and reversed**:

```
34486eb  feat(theme): self-host Futura Round for development and testing     ← re-added
a81a927  fix(footer): remove self-hosted Futura Round font files             ← removed
cac48af  feat(theme): self-host Futura Round for development and testing     ← added
```

A Desktop EULA does not cover serving from a CDN, and this branch deploys to MRT. The prohibition named the licence path and the specific entitlement that would be required.

**This is a legal question decided inside a footer-UI story, and it is not mine to close.** Your `gh` identity *is* in `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`, so the Tier 1 workflow exception technically applies to the file edit — but being a Tier 1 approver doesn't settle whether Zimmermann holds a Web Page Content entitlement. That needs a human answer before this merges.

I should have caught this when the fonts work landed. The whole reason I wanted the real font was to trust my measurements, and I didn't check what the rules file said about it.

## 🔴 Blocker 2 — the one control the AC names fails WCAG 2.5.8

The story says: *"Keep in mind that the minimum size of that email sign up button is taken into consideration for accessibility purposes."*

```
control                              w × h     WCAG 2.5.8
subscribe submit  ← the AC's control  16×16    ❌ FAIL
contact: phone                        24×24    ✅
contact: whatsapp                     24×24    ✅
contact: email                        24×24    ✅
locale button                      129.6×30    ✅
wordmark button                      327×39    ✅
nav link                            59.6×24    ✅
```

Every other control passes. The named one doesn't. Cause: `button.ts` sets `icon: {p: 'xs'}` which *would* give 32×32, but Chakra's `IconButton` hardcodes `padding: "0"` as a **style prop**, and style props are merged after `__css`, so `padding: 0` wins. The agent derived that from Chakra's source; I confirmed it in the browser.

The same file gets it right elsewhere — the opt-in clear-✕ carries `minWidth`/`minHeight: var(--zimm-scale-xl)` with the comment *"WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 — 24px minimum target size"*. Fix is one line on `sizes.icon`, or `sx` on the IconButton (a style prop, so it beats the hardcoded zero).

## Also material

**Bridge pattern is inverted.** `components/footer` *is* a shared SFCC dependency — base `_app/index.jsx:43` imports it. `overrideStyling.md` requires the default export to be the faithful port with brand behaviour behind a named export; ours is the reverse. Runtime impact is nil today (the sole consumer passes no props) and the code documents the reasoning, but base spreads `...otherProps` onto its root and ours drops that passthrough.

**`.storybook/main.js` and `preview.tsx` are Tier 1** (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #8) and modified here. The CI guard watches `.storybook/**` but is explicitly *not* a required check, which is why it passed.

**`@storybook/react` isn't a declared dependency** — one story imports it, 11 use `@storybook/react-webpack5`. Works on hoisting only.

**PRD IDs in comments are wrong**: the Contentful footer story is HPC-030, not HPC-034; Omneo is HPC-036, not HPC-035; HPC-038 is region-specific links, not Cookie Settings.

**Localisation**: zero `react-intl` in the footer, replacing a base component with 14 translated strings. EU-domestic serves fr/it/es. Chrome strings like `Subscribe`, `Email`, `Copyright ©` and the validation messages currently belong to no story.

My phases are green (0–6, detailed earlier). Two agents outstanding — tokens/CSS and the FED playbook. I'll fold those in, but the two blockers above don't need them.

**1. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon/index.tsx:140-143` — `as` casts justified by a factually false comment**
