All four, verified. Nothing applied yet.

---

# 1. `safeHref.ts` — the live bypass 🟠

```diff
+const C0_OR_SPACE = /^[\u0000-\u0020]+|[\u0000-\u0020]+$/g;
+const TAB_LF_CR = /[\u0009\u000a\u000d]/g;
+
+/**
+ * Normalise the way the URL parser will, before testing.
+ *
+ * The WHATWG parser strips leading/trailing C0-and-space and removes tab/LF/CR from anywhere
+ * in the input BEFORE it parses. So `/\t/evil.com` is parsed as `//evil.com`. Testing the raw
+ * string means the allow-list checks a different value than the browser resolves.
+ */
+const normalise = (href: string): string => href.replace(C0_OR_SPACE, '').replace(TAB_LF_CR, '');
+
-const SAFE_HREF_RE = /^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?!\/))/i;
+const SAFE_HREF_RE = /^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?![/\\]))/i;

 /** True when `href` is safe to render on an anchor. Absent or unsafe values return false. */
-export const isSafeHref = (href: string | undefined): boolean => (href ? SAFE_HREF_RE.test(href) : false);
+export const isSafeHref = (href: string | undefined): boolean =>
+  href ? SAFE_HREF_RE.test(normalise(href)) : false;
```

And the docblock, which currently makes a claim that isn't true any more:

```diff
- * execute; a protocol-relative `//host` silently leaves the site. The `(?!\/)` lookahead is
- * what rejects the last case — it was a real bypass, closed in e9c2180.
+ * execute; an authority reference like `//host` silently leaves the site. The `(?![/\\])`
+ * lookahead rejects that — including the backslash form, because a browser treats `/\host`
+ * as `//host`. `e9c2180` closed only the forward-slash half; the backslash and the
+ * control-character forms stayed open until this change.
```

Plus the missing test cases:

```diff
     ['//example.com', false],
+    ['/\\example.com', false],
+    ['/\\/evil.com', false],
+    ['/\u0009/evil.com', false],
+    ['/\u000a/evil.com', false],
+    ['\u0009//evil.com', false],
+    ['/ /evil.com', true],
```

## Why — ELI5

The guard asks "does this start with a slash that isn't followed by another slash?" — because `//host` means "go to a different website."

Two things it didn't know:

**A backslash is also a slash.** Browsers are forgiving about this, so `/\evil.com` is treated exactly like `//evil.com`. The guard saw one forward slash, said "fine, that's a local path," and let it through.

**The browser cleans the string before reading it.** Tabs and newlines get *deleted* first. So `/⇥/evil.com` becomes `//evil.com` at the moment the browser parses it — but the guard tested the version *with* the tab still in, which looked harmless.

That's the real lesson: **we were checking a different string than the browser would.** So the fix isn't just "also reject backslash" — it's clean the string the same way the browser does, *then* check it. Otherwise you're inspecting one thing and shipping another.

The last case, `/ /evil.com`, stays allowed on purpose. A plain space isn't deleted — it's encoded — so it resolves to `zimmermann.com/%20/evil.com`, which never leaves the site. Rejecting it would be over-blocking.

**Verified: 21 cases, 0 mismatches.** `/ /evil.com` is the case that proves it isn't just "reject anything odd."

---

# 2. Locale button — the dead control

```diff
       <chakra.button
         type="button"
         aria-label="Change locale"
+        // Focusable and visible, but announced as unavailable: there is no selector to open
+        // yet. aria-disabled rather than the `disabled` attribute so it keeps its place in the
+        // tab order and its Figma appearance — `disabled` would also drop the pointer cursor
+        // the recipe sets. ContactIconRow makes the same call 60 lines up for the same reason:
+        // never promise an action that cannot be performed (WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4).
+        aria-disabled={true}
         __css={styles.localeButton}
         // PLACEHOLDER: wire to locale selector once available.
         // Label and destination are hardcoded until sourced from active locale/site config.
         onClick={undefined}
       >
```

## Why — ELI5

Right now this is a button that looks like a button, announces itself as a button, can be tabbed to and pressed — and does nothing. For a sighted mouse user that's a shrug. For someone using a screen reader it's worse: the software says "Change locale, button," they activate it, and there's silence. They can't tell whether it's broken or whether they did it wrong.

`aria-disabled` changes the announcement to "unavailable." Still there, still visible, still reachable — but honest about what it can do.

Your own footer already does this. Sixty lines earlier, a contact channel with no destination renders as a labelled `<span>` instead of a dead link, with a comment explaining exactly this reasoning. This just applies the same rule to the one control that missed it.

**Note this is only half of CodeRabbit's comment.** The other half is the hardcoded label, which you've parked — the reply should say so explicitly, or the bot keeps raising both. It's already come up in three runs.

---

# 3. `fontFace.test.tsx` — decline, no diff

No change. The file already solves the problem, better than the suggestion would:

```ts
const hadWindow = 'window' in globalThis;
afterEach(() => {
  if (!hadWindow) delete (globalThis as { window?: unknown }).window;
});
```

## Why — ELI5

The concern is real in general: tests that share global state can poison each other, so test 3 fails only because test 2 ran first.

But here every one of the six tests **sets `globalThis.window` itself** before asserting. None of them inherits anything. You could run them in any order, or run one alone, and get the same result. The `afterEach` above already restores the environment to how it found it.

The suggestion also asks for `vi.clearAllMocks()`. There's nothing to clear — the single `vi.mock` is module-level and hoisted, not a spy that accumulates calls.

So adding `beforeEach` would duplicate work each test already does, and `clearAllMocks` would clear nothing. This is a generic convention being applied where the file already handles the concern a different way — which is exactly the case `AGENTS.md` says to reply to rather than "fix," so the bot learns not to re-flag it.

---

# 4. The magic `10`

```diff
+    // One decimal place. Sub-pixel jitter in getBoundingClientRect would otherwise fail an
+    // equality check on layouts that did not actually move.
+    const LAYOUT_PRECISION_DP = 1;
+    const rounded = (n: number) => Number(n.toFixed(LAYOUT_PRECISION_DP));
-    const rounded = (n: number) => Math.round(n * 10) / 10;
```

## Why — ELI5

`Math.round(n * 10) / 10` is a trick for "round to one decimal place." Anyone reading it has to work backwards from the `10` to figure that out — and if someone later wants two decimals, they have to know to change it to `100`, in two places.

`toFixed(1)` says the thing directly, and the named constant says *why* one decimal: browsers report element sizes with tiny fractional wobble, so comparing raw values would flag a "shift" that never happened.

`conventions.md:50` asks for exactly this — *"any literal value with semantic meaning."* That `10` carries meaning, so it gets a name.

This is my code from yesterday, and the finding is correct.

---

## Summary

```
1  safeHref     regex + normalise + 6 test cases   verified 21/21     ~10 min
2  locale       one attribute + rationale          a11y, not visual   ~5 min
3  fontFace     no change — reply with cause       reply only
4  precision    one named constant                 mine, valid        ~2 min
```

Say which you want and I'll apply them, or all four.

Two of the three need no visual check. One did, and I've now run it.

## Per file

**`safeHref.test.ts`** — test-only. No.

**`index.stories.tsx`** — the change is *inside* a `play` function: it only alters how two numbers are compared, not what renders. No visual check needed, and the Storybook gate already passed 76/76 with all four footer stories rendering.

**`safeHref.ts`** — **yes, and this one mattered.** It's pure logic, but its return value decides whether the footer renders an `<a>` or an inert `<span>`. Making the guard *stricter* can silently swap a working link for a non-interactive span — a rendering change hiding behind a logic change, and exactly the kind of thing a passing unit test wouldn't show.

## What I checked

```
distinct fixture hrefs: 4      rejected by the new guard: 0
  tel:+61280808080              PASS
  https://wa.me/61280808080     PASS
  mailto:care@zimmermann.com    PASS
  #                             PASS
```

And in the rendered DOM at both viewports:

```
@1440   footer=490    anchors=21 (tel=1 wa=1 mail=1 '#'=18)   inert-span-fallbacks=0   buttons=3
@390    footer=1005   anchors=21 (tel=1 wa=1 mail=1 '#'=18)   inert-span-fallbacks=0   buttons=3
```

**21 anchors, zero fallback spans, geometry unchanged.** Nothing downgraded. Worth noting the fixture only has 4 distinct href values across 21 links, so the surface is small — but that's exactly why it's worth confirming rather than reasoning about.

content.text:
That answers it precisely, and it's not a mystery — it's mechanical.

## It can approve, and does

```
PR #51   APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED, COMMENTED
PR #47   APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED, COMMENTED
PR #46   APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED, COMMENTED
PR #42   APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED, COMMENTED, DISMISSED
PR #35   APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED, COMMENTED
```

Five past PRs went `CHANGES_REQUESTED → APPROVED`. So the capability is there and configured — `coderabbit.yaml:32` sets `request_changes_workflow: true`, which is exactly the setting that makes it block and then approve.

## Why this PR hasn't

Look at what triggers each state:

```
08-20 18:38   CHANGES_REQUESTED   ← 14 findings
08-21 06:17   CHANGES_REQUESTED   ← 2 more (incl. safeHref)
08-21 07:47   CHANGES_REQUESTED   ← 1 more
08-21 08:56   CHANGES_REQUESTED   ← 1 more
08-21 15:09+  COMMENTED ×many     ← thread replies and resolutions only
```

Every state-changing review came from a **full review pass on a push**. Everything after 15:09 is reply and resolution traffic, which posts as `COMMENTED`.

The catch is timing. My last push was **15:43 UTC**, and the reviews at **15:45** are two minutes after it — but they're the *empty-bodied* ones tied to thread resolution, not a fresh full pass. CodeRabbit resolved the threads my fixes addressed and stopped there. It hasn't run the incremental review that would produce a new verdict.

So `CHANGES_REQUESTED` is a stale flag from 08:56 sitting on a PR whose findings are all resolved. Nothing is actually outstanding on its side.

## Two things worth knowing

**Approval is per-commit-SHA.** Even if it approves `1bc0a9d` now, the next push invalidates it and it re-reviews. So there's no point chasing the flag until the branch is otherwise final.

**And it isn't the gate anyway.** `mergeState: BLOCKED` with `mergeable: MERGEABLE` means no conflicts — the block is the review requirement, and CODEOWNERS routes that to humans. This branch now touches two Tier 1 files with *different* owner groups:

```
.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md              Governance — Squad Leads + Integration Lead
overrides/app/theme/foundation/fonts.ts   Design System — UI Designer
.storybook/{main.js,preview.tsx}          Test config — Integration
```

Plus Tier 2 footer and shell paths. A bot approval wouldn't satisfy any of those.

## If you want the flag cleared

Comment `@coderabbitai review` on the PR — that forces a fresh pass on the current SHA, and given all 18 threads are resolved and the last two passes found nothing, it should come back `APPROVED`.

Worth noting PRs **#57** and **#55** are the two that never got there — both show `DISMISSED`, which is consistent with them being superseded rather than resolved. #55 is the PR this one replaced.

## #2 PII on abandonment — **valid, fix it**

The claim holds exactly. Four writes to `pendingSignupRef`:

```
198  init            { email:'', firstName:'', lastName:'' }
203  capture email   handleEmailSubmit
216  clear           the descoped path — clears after showing the placeholder
229  clear           handleModalSubmit — clears after the (future) POST
257  onClose={() => setModalOpen(false)}     ← no clear
```

So **both paths that finish a flow clear it, and the path that abandons one doesn't.** A shopper types their email, the modal opens, they hit Escape — and their address stays in memory. That's the case where you'd least want to keep it, and it's the only one missed.

It's also inconsistent with reasoning already in the file. Line 229 carries a comment saying the record holds customer PII and there's no request for it to outlive. That argument applies with more force to a cancellation than to a submit.

## #1 grammar — **valid concern, wrong correction**

CodeRabbit says `composed from` → `composed of`. I'd push back on that specific change, and the repo tells you why:

```
zimmTokens.ts:2   "All --zimm-* variables, derived from the other foundation/* files"
```

The relationship is **derivation** — the `.zimm-*` classes are *generated using* the tokens, not *made up of* them. `composed of` would say the classes consist of tokens, which is the wrong claim. LanguageTool is applying a generic collocation rule without the semantics.

But the phrase *is* awkward, so it's worth changing — just to the word the codebase already uses for this exact relationship:

```diff
- the `.zimm-*` global classes composed from them live in `globalStyles.ts` (Tier 2)
+ the `.zimm-*` global classes derived from them live in `globalStyles.ts` (Tier 2)
```

That's unambiguous, grammatically clean, and consistent with `zimmTokens.ts` and `overrideStyling.md`, which both describe this as derivation. It satisfies the finding without accepting a correction that would make the sentence less accurate.

| # | Verdict | Change |
|---|---|---|
| **2** | **Fix** — real, and the only unclosed PII path | 5 lines, diff as proposed |
| **1** | **Fix, but differently** — `derived from`, not `composed of` | one word |

# Tier 1 — Frozen Files

These files must not be modified by Claude Code without the developer explicitly naming the file
in the prompt AND confirming they have spoken to the listed owner. No exceptions.

> **Note:** this is a slim overrides project on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 — paths
> below reference `overrides/app/...` (the customisation surface) rather than the upstream
> monorepo `packages/template-retail-react-app/app/...` path.

## Design System (Owner: UI Designer — #design-system)

The whole `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` folder is Tier 1. Currently present:

```text
overrides/app/theme/index.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/index.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/fonts.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/spacing.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/motion.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/sizes.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts
```

**Fonts are self-hosted and served on every tier.** `overrides/app/static/fonts/` holds two
Futura Round faces — Regular 400 and Medium 500 — declared by
`overrides/app/theme/fontFace.tsx` and mounted in both `_app-config/index.tsx` and
`.storybook/preview.tsx`. Only two faces exist because only two are used: all 22 textStyles
resolve to fontWeight 400 or 500, and `fonts.body === fonts.heading`.

There is **no environment gate** on this, and it is worth stating plainly because an earlier
revision of this section claimed there was. `ZimmFontFace` mounts unconditionally inside
`_app-config`'s `ChakraProvider`, and `pwa-kit-dev`'s `staticFolderCopyPlugin` copies
`overrides/app/static` in both the client and SSR webpack configs — so the `.woff2` are
published with every bundle and shoppers on every storefront render Futura Round.

`foundation/fonts.ts` already lists `'Futura Round'` first in both stacks, so the `@font-face`
declaration is the only thing that makes it resolve — no component, recipe or token changes.
The fallback stack renders roughly 13% wider, which is why serving the real faces matters for
design-parity review against Figma.

Per-component theme overrides live in `overrides/app/theme/components/` and are
**Tier 2** — see [protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md). `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`
is also **Tier 2** — it composes the `.zimm-*` global class registry from the `--zimm-*`
variables defined in `foundation/zimmTokens.ts`, so it is derived styling rather than a
brand token source, but it emits CSS on every page and therefore needs a named owner.

## Commerce SDK Hooks (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
overrides/app/hooks/use-current-basket.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-current-customer.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-einstein.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-datacloud.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-refresh-token.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-navigation.ts
```

Note: `commerce-sdk-react` is consumed from `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/` —
it is not in this repo and cannot be modified here. The hooks above are the overrides surface.

## Runtime & Integration Config (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
config/                              ← entire directory (default.js, sites.js, sit.js, dev.js, utils.js)
overrides/app/ssr.js
overrides/app/ssr/                   ← SSR helper modules split from ssr.js in refactor 610020e:
                                         connectionPools.ts  — undici pool isolation (blast-radius mitigation)
                                         contentSecurityPolicy.ts  — CSP headers; wrong change = security hole on every page
                                         slasTokens.ts  — SLAS auth token handling; wrong change = broken auth site-wide
                                         paymentMetadata.ts  — payment method metadata SSR (checkout pages)
                                         marketingCloud.ts  — MC client-credentials token exchange
worker/main.js
package.json (root)
mobify.config.js
overrides/app/config/countries.ts
overrides/app/config/contentful.ts   ← gates preview/draft content; removing the server-side check exposes drafts on production
```

**`overrides/app/request-processor.js` — add here when populated.**
Currently the Salesforce example stub. Once Zimmermann's geo-redirect and storefront-routing logic lands here it runs on every single request — it will be one of the highest-blast-radius files in the repo. Add it to this section before that work begins.

## Build Pipeline (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

Path aliases are configured in four places that must stay in sync (see architecture.md §Path Aliases).
Breaking either file silently breaks every `app/` and `~` import across the codebase.

```text
babel.config.js    ← path aliases for npm start dev server + production build
tsconfig.json      ← path aliases for TypeScript / VS Code intellisense; also enforces strict mode
```

## Consent (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
Didomi / consent configuration (paths TBD — add when introduced)
```

## Test & Tooling Config (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

Mirrors AGENTS.md hard rule 8 — test config drift breaks every contributor's harness.

```text
vitest.config.*
vitest.setup.ts       ← test environment setup; complements vitest.config.*
playwright.config.*
.storybook/
lighthouserc.js
.browserstack.yml     ← must target e2e/tests/zimm only; scope change = CI cost explosion + upstream test failures
```

## CI/CD Pipeline (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
.github/workflows/
```

## Governance (Owner: Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead — #dev-team)

```text
AGENTS.md
CLAUDE.md
CODEOWNERS
.claude/rules/
.claude/settings.json
coderabbit.yaml              ← AI PR review config; weakening it removes Tier 1 change detection and commit-format enforcement
.coderabbit/                 ← ast-grep rule content coderabbit.yaml points at; weakening/deleting a rule here silently removes that check with no signal in coderabbit.yaml itself
semgrep.yml                  ← semgrep rule content (payment-credential-logging, XSS); same silent-weakening risk as .coderabbit/
scripts/hooks/pre-commit     ← enforces Contentful drift check and blocks direct edits to derived AI config files
scripts/hooks/commit-msg     ← enforces conventional commits; /generate-changelog depends on this
```

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills/code-quality

Audit code quality for the specified scope. Do not modify any files — this is a read-only
diagnostic. Produce a prioritised report with actionable fixes.

---

## Input

The user will provide one of:
- A file path or directory to audit
- No argument — default to files changed on the current branch: `git diff --name-only main`

If no argument is given, run: `git diff --name-only main` and audit those files.
Exclude test files (`*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`), stories (`*.stories.tsx`), and any registry files.

---

## Parallel execution

For audits covering more than 5 files, split into four independent checks and run them
as parallel agents simultaneously. Each agent receives only its own checklist — do not
bundle all checks into one agent.

- **Agent A — Naming & structure**
- **Agent B — Import analysis**
- **Agent C — TypeScript coverage**
- **Agent D — Test & story coverage**

For 5 files or fewer, run all checks sequentially in a single pass.

---

## Agent A — Naming & structure

Rules are defined once, split across [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md)
(cross-cutting), [css.md](../../rules/css.md) (Chakra/styling), and
[components.md](../../rules/components.md) (components/hooks/Storybook) — read the relevant
ones first, then apply each rule to the files in scope. Do not re-list the rules here;
that's how the files drift apart.

Walk the file list and audit each file against the relevant section:

- Every file → conventions.md **General** section.
- Every file with JSX/Chakra props → css.md **Tokens** section (no hardcoded hex/px values).
- `.tsx` under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/` → components.md
  **Components** + **Composition** sections, plus conventions.md **File naming and folder
  structure**.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/hooks/` → components.md **Hooks** section.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/utils/` → conventions.md **Utilities** section.

For each violation, record `file:line` and which rule file + bullet failed — the section
anchor is enough (e.g. "components.md → Components → Props type placement").

---

## Agent B — Import analysis

For each file, read the import statements and check:

- No circular imports: if File A imports from File B, File B must not import from File A
  (check by reading the imported file's imports in turn — one level deep is sufficient).
- No imports from a higher tier without justification:
  - A component must not import directly from internal `commerce-sdk-react` source paths.
  - A page must not bypass its own hooks to call raw API functions.
- No imports from a later-sprint feature (reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` when present).
- No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels — flag for path alias review.

---

## Agent C — TypeScript coverage

Check each file against the relevant rule file:

- Every `.ts`/`.tsx` → [typescript.md](../../rules/typescript.md) in full (no `any` without
  justification, `type` vs `interface`, non-null assertions, discriminated unions, utility
  types, `import type`, `satisfies`, `readonly`, generic naming).
- Components → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Components** (props type name,
  placement, optional `?`, callback naming, JSDoc).
- Hooks → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Hooks** (typed params, explicit
  return type, JSDoc with `@returns`).

Then run `npx tsc --noEmit` **once** for the whole branch (not per file) and report any
errors. Cross-reference any new errors against the files in scope.

---

## Agent D — Test & story coverage

For each component file under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/`:
- A paired `*.stories.tsx` exists in the same directory (required by [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) > Testing).
- For logic-heavy components or hooks: a `*.test.ts` exists OR a `play` function exists in the story.
- If a test file exists, verify:
  - At least one test covers the primary render case.
  - At least one test covers a user interaction (click, input) if the component has interactive elements.
  - No tests use `toBeTruthy()` as the sole assertion — check for meaningful assertions.
- If a paired `.stories.tsx` is missing, flag as MISSING STORY (mandatory).
- If a logic-heavy file has neither a `.test.ts` nor a `play` function, flag as MISSING TEST.

For each utility file under `overrides/app/utils/`:
- **`.test.ts` required** when the utility has ≥1 conditional branch or performs ≥1
  transformation (currency, locale, mapping, parsing, etc.). Trivial re-exports and
  one-liners are exempt.
- If a test file exists, verify it covers both the happy path and at least one edge case
  (empty input, null, locale variation — whichever applies).

---

## Output format

Combine all agent results into a single prioritised report:

```
## Code Quality Report
**Scope:** [files audited]
**Branch:** [current branch]
**Date:** [today]

### 🔴 Must fix before PR merge
[Issues that would fail review or cause runtime errors — one line per issue with file:line]

### 🟡 Should fix in this PR
[Issues that affect maintainability or violate conventions — one line per issue with file:line]

### 🔵 Backlog (log, don't block)
[Minor style issues, missing test cases for edge cases — one line per issue]

### ✅ No issues found
[List checks that passed cleanly]

### Summary
X must-fix · Y should-fix · Z backlog items
```

Do not suggest refactors beyond the scope of the changed files.
Do not modify any files — report only.


ARGUMENTS: Audit this branch's changes against develop — feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui (global footer, SFCC-55). Includes 2 uncommitted files: scripts/generateRegistry.mjs and .claude/registry/components.md.

content.text:
Both declined, replies posted.

## What I said

**Grammar** — declined on two grounds, and the second is the substantive one: the suggested replacement would make the sentence **less** accurate. `composed of` asserts the `.zimm-*` classes *consist of* the tokens; they're *generated using* them. The repo already has settled language for that relationship — `zimmTokens.ts:2` says *"derived from"*, and `overrideStyling.md` describes it the same way. So I noted that `derived from` would be the correct rewrite if the line were touched, and that `COMPOSE_FROM_OF` is a generic collocation rule with no view of the semantics. That gives the bot something better than "won't fix."

**PII** — deferred, and I opened by saying the finding is correct and the proposed diff is right as written. The deferral rests on it being unreachable: `enableNameCapture` defaults false at both sites, the render is gated, so `SubscribeModal` never mounts and `modalOpen` is never true. Plus the modal is HPC-035's subject, has no Figma design, and will likely be rebuilt on Chakra's own `Modal` — which base SFCC uses in 28 files and which handles dismissal itself. Hardening a close handler that's about to be replaced adds something to undo.

I recorded the requirement explicitly in the thread so it travels with the story: **when `enableNameCapture` is enabled, the close handler must clear `pendingSignupRef`.**

## State

```
20 threads · 18 resolved · 2 unresolved
review: CHANGES_REQUESTED
```

The two new ones stayed **unresolved**, unlike the earlier declines the bot closed. That's actually the better outcome for a deferral — an open thread is a visible marker, and the PII one carries a real follow-up obligation that shouldn't disappear into a closed thread.

`CHANGES_REQUESTED` won't lift while those two are open, so the merge gate now needs a human either way — which it did regardless, given the two Tier 1 owner groups on this branch.

## Where the PR sits

```
64 commits · working tree clean · tsc 0 · vitest 197/197 · Storybook 76/76
CI 10/11 green — BrowserStack config failure is pre-existing infrastructure
19 CodeRabbit replies posted, 20 threads answered
```

Two things now carry forward to HPC-035 with reasoning attached rather than as loose ends: the `pendingSignupRef` clear on close, and `aria-disabled` on the locale control.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

The user is **Marcel Navarro, FED Lead** on the Zimmermann PWA Kit project (luxury Australian fashion storefront on Salesforce Commerce Cloud), working on **SFCC-55 global footer**, branch `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui`, PR #59. Requests in order:

- Answer PR #59 / CodeRabbit status
- Run the full phase 0–6 test suite; ensure lint and prettier are good
- Split changes into logical commits and push (no `Co-Authored-By`)
- Re-run the full suite on the 6 commits, run local CodeRabbit, check alignment with the FED lead playbook and build manual, run Storybook
- Confirm the `code-review` skill is local CodeRabbit; run it
- Explain B and E generator findings in diff form, ELI5-but-FED-Lead
- Execute fixes #3–#12 via feasibility→implement→V&V→test
- Run `/code-quality`
- Launch a multi-agent audit of the entire diff against the Jira ticket, FED docs, Figma, tests, and styling
- Run a 4-stage multi-agent pipeline (validate → implement → regress → commit-check) on the 13 must/should-fix items
- **Step back:** honestly assess whether the work is overengineering, via in-depth recursive multi-agent analysis. "do not decide for me, i'll make the calls based on the findings"
- Decisions: keep fonts (dev-only, drop layers 1 and 2), fix font doc contradictions, apply 24px to the subscribe submit, drop the overengineering fixes
- Remove all Monotype licence open-item text; replace "Han's branch" with the branch name
- Pull all CodeRabbit comments; apply 13 replies
- Fix safeHref, decline locale button, decline fontFace.test.tsx, fix magic 10
- Commit and push, then reply to threads
- Defer/decline the grammar and PII findings
- **Current:** 7 new findings — "see what's actually needed, defer/decline the overengineering stuff - report back with your findings"

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
- `extendTheme` deep-merges — a recipe named `Footer` inherits SFCC's; hence `ZimmFooter`
- **Sizing-vs-spacing trap**: Zimmermann scale registered as `theme.space` ONLY. Bare key on `width`/`height`/`boxSize`/`min|maxWidth|Height` falls through to Chakra's `sizes`. Measured range **8×–112×** (`2xs` = 64×), and `s`/`m`/`l` are ABSENT so declarations are dropped entirely
- **Undocumented typography twin**: `theme.fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings` never registered. `fontSize: '2xs'` → 0.625rem not 0.875rem; `'4xs'` emits nothing. Live instance at `header/index.tsx:302` (`fontSize="l"` emits nothing) — outside recipe-walker scope
- **`extendTheme` does NOT populate `theme.__cssMap`** — only `ChakraProvider` does via `toCSSVar`. Direct `css()(theme)` in tests passes vacuously
- Chakra `IconButton` hard-sets `padding: "0"` as a **style prop**, merged after `__css`, so `p:` in a recipe is silently discarded
- WHATWG URL parser strips leading/trailing C0-or-space and removes tab/LF/CR **before** parsing; a browser treats `/\host` as `//host`
- Figma text boxes are cap-height; browser line boxes aren't (8/22 vs 18/36, +10 each)
- `footer/textfield` has two variants: `Subscribed=False` 320×44, `Subscribed=True` 308×59, with a compensating gap change (40→24)
- `test-storybook` requires a BUILT Storybook; dev-server runs are invalid (BM-05)
- `addon-a11y` is NOT gated in CI — no `.storybook/test-runner.js`
- CodeRabbit `request_changes_workflow: true` at `coderabbit.yaml:32`; a `COMMENTED` review cannot clear `CHANGES_REQUESTED`
- Tier system: Tier 1 = `foundation/`, `.claude/rules/`, `.storybook/`, `config/`; Tier 2 = `theme/components/`, `components/footer|header`, `_app-config/`
- AGENTS.md Hard Rule #4 names four absolutes and grants the exception to `.github/workflows/` — proving Tier 1 membership alone isn't disqualifying

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

- **`overrides/app/utils/safeHref.ts`** — the security guard, fixed in `1ed34ea`:
```ts
/* eslint-disable no-control-regex */
const C0_OR_SPACE = /^[\u0000-\u0020]+|[\u0000-\u0020]+$/g;
const TAB_LF_CR = /[\u0009\u000a\u000d]/g;
/* eslint-enable no-control-regex */
const normalise = (href: string): string => href.replace(C0_OR_SPACE, '').replace(TAB_LF_CR, '');
const SAFE_HREF_RE = /^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?![/\\]))/i;
export const isSafeHref = (href: string | undefined): boolean =>
  href ? SAFE_HREF_RE.test(normalise(href)) : false;
```
Closed `/\example.com`, `/\/evil.com`, `/\t/`, `/\n/`, `/\r/`. `/ /evil.com` correctly still allowed (space is percent-encoded).

- **`overrides/app/theme/components/button.ts`** — 24×24 fix in `c6fda36`:
```ts
icon: { h: 'auto', minW: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', minH: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)' },
```
Removed dead `p: 'xs'`.

- **`overrides/app/theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts`** — `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT = '2.25rem'` (was `'36px'`), commit `31b35fb`. S8 (textStyle body2) was REVERTED.

- **`overrides/app/components/footer/index.stories.tsx`** — `LAYOUT_PRECISION_DP = 1` with `toFixed`, commit `1bc0a9d`.

- **`overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`** — commit `e686bd3`: non-empty precondition, responsive-container walker (`BREAKPOINT_KEYS` derived from `foundation/gridSystem`), TYPOGRAPHY_PROPS. `fontWeight` deliberately excluded.

- **`overrides/app/hooks/useSubscribeModal.test.tsx`** (NEW, 123 lines) — commit `4f4b97f`.

- **Font doc sites corrected then licence text removed** (`af87b5b`, `f8d2f75`): `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` (T1), `overrides/app/theme/foundation/fonts.ts` (T1), `.docs/architecture.md`, `.docs/memory/projectState.md`, `overrides/app/theme/components/footer.ts`, `overrides/app/components/foundation/typography.stories.tsx`.

4. **Errors and fixes:**

- **Said "10 of 14 addressed" when 9 fixed + 5 replies = 14.** Corrected to 9.
- **Phase 2's inventory was hand-maintained**; my regex counted JSX-comment prose and matched `.rem` inside `removeEventListener`. Inflated 19→41 literals. Fixed both filters.
- **Wordmark comment claimed `useNavigation` and `variant="unstyled"`** — neither true. `FooterContainer` deliberately uses `history.push(buildUrl(HOME_HREF))`.
- **Demoting a JSDoc to fix the registry row was whack-a-mole** — the row went to `NEW_TAB_SUFFIX`. Fixed `extractDescription` properly.
- **Stashing pulled the generator fix out of the working tree**, and the pre-commit hook reads the working tree — commit 2 would have reverted commit 1's registry fix. Caught before committing.
- **Parity check false-alarmed 3× on function `baseStyle`.** Real state: ZimmFooter 38/38 (now 35/35), ZimmTextInput 8/8, Header 17/8 (pre-existing).
- **Pointed `test-storybook` at the dev server** — invalid per BM-05, made mutation results uninterpretable (baseline itself failed).
- **Misread a bundle offset as a source line** (`index.stories.tsx:417` in a 206-line file).
- **Cited the FED Lead playbook in a PR reply** — a local Desktop file. User: "it's wrong to mention the fed lead playbook here, because that file is only local to me". Patched to rest on AGENTS.md Hard Rule #4.
- **Said 5 threads unresolved; user said 4.** I'd used "has no reply" as a proxy. GraphQL confirmed 4.
- **Reported `safeHref` as "well covered, 3 layers"** — 13 tests, zero backslashes, live bypass CodeRabbit had already named at 06:17.
- **Reported "Storybook interaction & a11y" as CI-gated** — a11y isn't; no `test-runner.js`.
- **Reported scope as 38% deferred/unmentioned** — actually 17–25%; I'd counted 1,181 lines of mandated stories as discretionary.
- **Claimed the "all variants upfront" mandate** — doesn't exist on this branch; no `f2r/` directory.
- **Said `ZimmButton`/`ZimmTextInput` have zero live render sites** — true only of *direct* sites; both render via `ZimmInputAction`.
- **Passed along "modal test is 48% of suite runtime"** — arithmetically right, meaningless (2.19s suite, parallel).
- **Said 11 `<path fill>` elements; actually 10.** Said modal is 633 lines; actually 371.
- **Said chevron-left/up unused** — mandatory; 16 base SFCC files consume them.
- **Common cause identified:** the verification instrument was built from the same belief as the thing verified, and never made to fail on purpose.

5. **Problem Solving:**

Solved: the descope (`enableNameCapture`, mutation-tested); the 22px layout shift (Δ0 at 1440/768/375/320, `minHeight` load-bearing only on mobile); the 16×16 WCAG failure (now 24×24, all 7 controls pass); the safeHref bypass (21 cases, 0 mismatches, orthogonal mutations); the font documentation contradictions (6 sites, then licence text removed per user); 20 CodeRabbit threads answered with 19 replies.

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills/code-quality

Audit code quality for the specified scope. Do not modify any files — this is a read-only
diagnostic. Produce a prioritised report with actionable fixes.

---

## Input

The user will provide one of:
- A file path or directory to audit
- No argument — default to files changed on the current branch: `git diff --name-only main`

If no argument is given, run: `git diff --name-only main` and audit those files.
Exclude test files (`*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`), stories (`*.stories.tsx`), and any registry files.

---

## Parallel execution

For audits covering more than 5 files, split into four independent checks and run them
as parallel agents simultaneously. Each agent receives only its own checklist — do not
bundle all checks into one agent.

- **Agent A — Naming & structure**
- **Agent B — Import analysis**
- **Agent C — TypeScript coverage**
- **Agent D — Test & story coverage**

For 5 files or fewer, run all checks sequentially in a single pass.

---

## Agent A — Naming & structure

Rules are defined once, split across [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md)
(cross-cutting), [css.md](../../rules/css.md) (Chakra/styling), and
[components.md](../../rules/components.md) (components/hooks/Storybook) — read the relevant
ones first, then apply each rule to the files in scope. Do not re-list the rules here;
that's how the files drift apart.

Walk the file list and audit each file against the relevant section:

- Every file → conventions.md **General** section.
- Every file with JSX/Chakra props → css.md **Tokens** section (no hardcoded hex/px values).
- `.tsx` under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/` → components.md
  **Components** + **Composition** sections, plus conventions.md **File naming and folder
  structure**.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/hooks/` → components.md **Hooks** section.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/utils/` → conventions.md **Utilities** section.

For each violation, record `file:line` and which rule file + bullet failed — the section
anchor is enough (e.g. "components.md → Components → Props type placement").

---

## Agent B — Import analysis

For each file, read the import statements and check:

- No circular imports: if File A imports from File B, File B must not import from File A
  (check by reading the imported file's imports in turn — one level deep is sufficient).
- No imports from a higher tier without justification:
  - A component must not import directly from internal `commerce-sdk-react` source paths.
  - A page must not bypass its own hooks to call raw API functions.
- No imports from a later-sprint feature (reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` when present).
- No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels — flag for path alias review.

---

## Agent C — TypeScript coverage

Check each file against the relevant rule file:

- Every `.ts`/`.tsx` → [typescript.md](../../rules/typescript.md) in full (no `any` without
  justification, `type` vs `interface`, non-null assertions, discriminated unions, utility
  types, `import type`, `satisfies`, `readonly`, generic naming).
- Components → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Components** (props type name,
  placement, optional `?`, callback naming, JSDoc).
- Hooks → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Hooks** (typed params, explicit
  return type, JSDoc with `@returns`).

Then run `npx tsc --noEmit` **once** for the whole branch (not per file) and report any
errors. Cross-reference any new errors against the files in scope.

---

## Agent D — Test & story coverage

For each component file under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/`:
- A paired `*.stories.tsx` exists in the same directory (required by [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) > Testing).
- For logic-heavy components or hooks: a `*.test.ts` exists OR a `play` function exists in the story.
- If a test file exists, verify:
  - At least one test covers the primary render case.
  - At least one test covers a user interaction (click, input) if the component has interactive elements.
  - No tests use `toBeTruthy()` as the sole assertion — check for meaningful assertions.
- If a paired `.stories.tsx` is missing, flag as MISSING STORY (mandatory).
- If a logic-heavy file has neither a `.test.ts` nor a `play` function, flag as MISSING TEST.

For each utility file under `overrides/app/utils/`:
- **`.test.ts` required** when the utility has ≥1 conditional branch or performs ≥1
  transformation (currency, locale, mapping, parsing, etc.). Trivial re-exports and
  one-liners are exempt.
- If a test file exists, verify it covers both the happy path and at least one edge case
  (empty input, null, locale variation — whichever applies).

---

## Output format

Combine all agent results into a single prioritised report:

```
## Code Quality Report
**Scope:** [files audited]
**Branch:** [current branch]
**Date:** [today]

### 🔴 Must fix before PR merge
[Issues that would fail review or cause runtime errors — one line per issue with file:line]

### 🟡 Should fix in this PR
[Issues that affect maintainability or violate conventions — one line per issue with file:line]

### 🔵 Backlog (log, don't block)
[Minor style issues, missing test cases for edge cases — one line per issue]

### ✅ No issues found
[List checks that passed cleanly]

### Summary
X must-fix · Y should-fix · Z backlog items
```

Do not suggest refactors beyond the scope of the changed files.
Do not modify any files — report only.


ARGUMENTS: Audit this branch's changes against develop — feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui (global footer, SFCC-55). Includes 2 uncommitted files: scripts/generateRegistry.mjs and .claude/registry/components.md.

## Findings: 7 new CodeRabbit threads

**2 worth fixing · 1 needs your call · 4 decline.** No files changed, nothing committed.

---

### ✅ Fix — #3 Focus escapes the subscribe dialog (🟠 Major)
`overrides/app/hooks/useSubscribeModal.ts:94`

**This one is real, and I reproduced it.** I built a throwaway probe: click the non-focusable disclaimer prose → `document.activeElement` becomes `<body>` → press Tab → focus lands on a button *outside* the `aria-modal="true"` dialog. The probe asserted the escape and passed:

```
>>> after Tab from body, focus landed on: OUTSIDE_BEHIND_OVERLAY
```

The trap only has two branches — `activeElement === first` and `=== last`. From anywhere else, neither fires, no `preventDefault`, and the browser walks document order into the page behind the overlay. Breaks WCAG 2.1.2 and 2.4.3.

This is a genuine hole in coverage I told you was solid: I mutation-tested both wrap directions but never the "focus arrives from outside the set" entry state. Fix is a 3-line containment branch.

Worth naming the tempting-but-wrong option: `react-focus-lock@2.13.7`, `react-remove-scroll@2.7.2` and `@chakra-ui/modal@2.2.12` are all already installed, and an earlier audit wave argued the hand-rolled trap should be replaced by them. For a component that ships disabled, swapping the implementation is exactly the overengineering we just cut. **Patch the branch, don't replace the hook.**

### ✅ Fix — #7 Registry merges mutually-exclusive variant props (🟡 Minor)
`scripts/generateRegistry.mjs:482`

Confirmed wrong output. `ZimmButtonProps = ZimmLabelButtonProps | ZimmIconButtonProps` is a union, and the regex only matches object-literal bodies, so the fallback merges both variants. The generated row reads:

```
label: string, … , icon: ZimmIconType
```

`label` and a *required* `icon` shown side by side — a combination that cannot exist. Dev tooling, low stakes, but it's actively misleading metadata. Minimal fix is the bot's own second option: detect the union and stop merging, rather than building a full alias resolver.

---

### ⚖️ Your call — #2 Contact placeholders are routable (🟡 Minor)
`overrides/app/components/footer/contentfulFixture.ts:25`

The substance is right and I can't argue it away: `href: '#'` is inert, but `tel:+61280808080` and `https://wa.me/61280808080` **dial**. That's a plausible real Sydney number on the production render path (`index.tsx:557`). A shopper tapping the phone icon reaches a stranger.

I'm flagging rather than fixing because **this reverses your earlier instruction** — you asked for the contacts activated as anchors, and SFCC-55 explicitly grants placeholder latitude ("we can include whatever placeholder links we want"). Two cheap options:

- **Omit the three fields** → `ContactIconRow` falls back to its labelled inert `<span>`. Already built, and already story-covered (`index.stories.tsx:175` sets `phoneHref: undefined`). Loses the live-anchor rendering you asked for.
- **Keep them as anchors, swap to a non-routable number** — preserves what you wanted and removes the third-party risk. I'd want to confirm the exact ACMA fictitious-number range before writing one in rather than guess at it.

Recommend the second.

---

### ❌ Decline — 4 items

**#1 `.storybook/main.js:11` (🟠) — the reviewer already withdrew this.** Original 20 Aug 18:38, my reply 21 Aug 15:10, and at 15:11 it wrote: *"I withdraw this finding. AGENTS.md Hard Rule #2 permits the verified-session exception… my original finding incorrectly treated Hard Rule #8 as an absolute restriction"* — then resolved the thread and re-raised it verbatim at 16:34. Nothing in the file changed between. Declining on its own concession.

**#4 `recipeGuards.test.ts:33` (🟡) — real bug, wrong PR.** This is CodeRabbit reading *my own comment* naming the live `fontSize="l"` instance and handing it back as a task. The bug is genuine — `theme.fontSizes` was never registered, so the declaration emits nothing. But `header/index.tsx:302` is Hardi's from the 12 Jun initial commit, and this branch's only change to that file is **14 lines of comments, zero code**. Fixing it changes the header heading's rendered size — a live visual change, unreviewed against Figma, in a footer PR. My comment already states the correct remedy: an ast-grep rule covering the whole class, not a one-off patch.

**#5 `zimmTextInput.test.ts:11` (🟡) — both hooks would be no-ops.** The file has **zero `vi.*` calls**, so `vi.clearAllMocks()` clears nothing. `base` is a frozen literal that's only ever spread into calls, never mutated, so `beforeEach` re-initialisation guards against nothing. Same class as the `fontFace.test.tsx` item you already declined.

**#6 `foundation/fonts.ts:3` (🟠) — not a re-raise; genuinely new** (I checked — first ever comment on that path). Declining anyway: the edit is comment-only with zero tokens touched, so the rule's stated rationale ("design-token changes must go through the UI designer") isn't engaged. Its proposed alternative — move the text to a doc file — would leave the false claim that *the Monotype licence forbids self-hosting* sitting in a Tier 1 file at the point of use. A wrong comment in a frozen file is worse than a corrected one.

**Signal quality on this pass is poor.** Four of seven are rule-citations against files that are in the diff only for comment or test reasons, and one is a confirmed re-raise of a finding the bot itself retracted in writing. Two actionable out of seven.

All measured. Native style adds 26 prettier-rule errors to a file that already has 369 and that CI never lints — versus a ~370-line reformat. Keeping the small diff. Zero non-prettier errors.

## Done: fix #7

**Visible outcome is one character** — `icon: ZimmIconType` → `icon?: ZimmIconType` in ZimmButton's registry row. That's the whole reported defect: the row claimed `label` and a required `icon` coexist, which the union forbids.

It took ~60 lines to get there honestly, because the two cheap routes both made things worse:
- *Just stop merging* → row loses its props entirely.
- *Naive union resolve* → **dropped `label`**, since both members are `ZimmButtonBaseProps & {…}` and their own literals hold only the variant half. So the fix follows one level of intersection.

```
scripts/generateRegistry.mjs   | 63 +++++++++++++++---  (3 deletions = the regex + 2 touched lines)
.claude/registry/components.md |  2 +-                  (timestamp + icon?)
```

`tsc` 0 · vitest 197/197 · idempotent across runs · no other registry row moved · zero non-prettier eslint errors.

**One trap I hit and backed out of:** I ran `prettier --write` on the generator, which reformatted the entire file — semicolons and brace spacing — because the file predates the config. My "eslint exit 0" a moment later was an artifact of that reformat, not a real pass. HEAD already fails eslint there with 369 prettier errors and CI's lint is scoped to `overrides/**/*.{ts,tsx}`, so I reverted and reapplied in the file's native no-semicolon style. Storybook not re-run — dev tooling, no runtime or story surface.

## Draft replies for your review

**#1 `.storybook/main.js` — decline.** Points at its own withdrawal: *"I withdraw this finding. Hard Rule #4 identifies the files that remain absolute, and `.storybook/` is not in that list"* (#3831370131, 21 Aug), thread resolved, file unchanged since.

**#2 `contentfulFixture.ts` — decline.** Grants the finding is accurate and that `FooterContainer` is the default export base `_app` renders, then rests on SFCC-55's explicit placeholder scope and HPC-034 replacing `FOOTER_FIXTURE` wholesale — exposure knowingly accepted for the placeholder window, recorded so HPC-034 supplies all three channels. **Does not claim dev/test-only.**

**#3 `useSubscribeModal.ts` — defer to HPC-035.** Confirms and reports the reproduction, states the test gap plainly, then defers on unreachability: default `false` at both sites, gated at `index.tsx:254`, only Storybook passes `true`. Paired with the consent finding on the same hook, and notes `react-focus-lock`/`@chakra-ui/modal` are installed so the likely resolution is replacement.

**#4 `recipeGuards.test.ts` — decline.** Agrees the bug is real, then: `header/index.tsx:302` is from cd60b7a (12 Jun), this branch adds only 14 comment lines there, and correcting it changes a header heading's rendered size in Tier 2 shared shell with no Figma review — Hard Rule #5. Repeats the comment's own remedy: an ast-grep rule for the class.

**#5 `zimmTextInput.test.ts` — decline.** Zero `vi.*` calls so `clearAllMocks` clears nothing; `base` is a frozen literal only ever spread. Ceremony without effect.

**#6 `fonts.ts` — decline.** Comment-only, no token touched, so Hard Rule #3's stated rationale isn't engaged; verified tier-1-approver session. On the alternative: it would leave the original claim that the Monotype licence prevents self-hosting, while `fontFace.tsx` serves both faces on every tier — a wrong comment in a frozen file beats a corrected one only if nobody reads it.

**#7 — fixed,** describing the union+intersection resolution and the one-character net effect.

## Open question for you

Only #2's wording. You gave "testing and development, not prod" as the reason, and that premise doesn't survive checking — the fixture ships on every page. My draft declines on SFCC-55 scope + HPC-034 instead, which is both true and defensible. Confirm that wording works, or tell me to swap the reason.

Nothing committed. Two files modified in the working tree. **Say go and I'll commit #7, push, and post all seven replies.**

content.text:
Here's the state and what I'd send. Three of the four need no argument — the bot already conceded them and left them open only as a record.

## The four, and what closes each

**`contentfulFixture.ts` · `useSubscribeModal.ts` — nothing left to say.** Bot's words: *"the temporary exposure is an explicit SFCC-55 scope decision"* and *"Deferring the work to HPC-035 is appropriate."* It even added the HPC-035 acceptance criteria itself (include the focus-recovery test, prefer replacing the trap). **Resolve as-is.**

**`recipeGuards.test.ts` — agreed, but it asked you a direct question:** *"Would you like me to create a GitHub issue for that rule and assign it to you?"* My answer: **no.** This project tracks in Jira (`SFCC-*`/`HPC-*`); a GitHub issue is a parallel tracker nobody watches, and `.coderabbit/` is Tier 1 governance so the ast-grep rule needs its own story and owner regardless. Short reply declining, then resolve.

**`zimmTextInput.test.ts` — the only genuine disagreement.** It argues the rule is unconditional: *"It does not restrict these hooks to tests with mocks or mutable setup state."*

I'd hold, and the evidence is on this same branch:

| pure-function test file | mocks/DOM | hooks | CodeRabbit findings |
|---|---|---|---|
| `utils/safeHref.test.ts` | none | none | **0** |
| `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` | none | none | 1, unrelated to hooks |
| `theme/components/zimmTextInput.test.ts` | none | none | **1, about hooks** |

Three structurally identical files, all reviewed, one flagged. And every file on this branch that *does* have `afterEach` has something to reset — `useZimmTextInputState` and `fontFace` use `vi` mocks, `useSubscribeModal` renders through testing-library. That's the line the convention actually draws.

There's also a real cost to complying: `base` is a `const` literal that's only ever spread. Initialising it in `beforeEach` means making it `let` — a mutable binding where immutable is correct — to guard against mutation that can't happen. That's a small genuine quality loss bought with a no-op hook.

So the reply makes that case, then resolves, and points the disagreement at the right venue: if the rule *is* meant to be unconditional, say so in `.claude/rules/testing.md` and apply it to all three files — a Tier 1 governance change, not footer work.

## What I need from you

Two replies to post (recipeGuards answer, zimmTextInput counter), then **resolve all four as PR author**. That's the lever — the bot leaves agreed-but-deferred threads open by design, so they won't close on their own.

One flag: resolving won't by itself flip `reviewDecision` from `CHANGES_REQUESTED` — that needs a fresh CodeRabbit review, which I'd trigger with `@coderabbitai review` afterwards. If it still won't approve with zero unresolved threads, the remaining path is a human approving review, since `coderabbit.yaml:32` sets `request_changes_workflow: true`.

Say go and I'll post both replies, resolve all four, and kick the re-review.

CodeRabbit raised one actionable item on `generateRegistry.mjs:495-523` — my fix from `13add6e`. Both of its logic claims check out.

**Bug 1 — partial unions reported as complete.** `.filter(Boolean)` silently drops members it can't resolve, and the bail-out only fires when *all* of them fail. For `A | B` where `B` lives in another file, `members` becomes `[A]`, so `members.length === 1` — and then every one of A's props satisfies "present in every member" and stays **required**. A half-known union is published as a complete, fully-required prop set.

**Bug 2 — requiredness depends on declaration order.** I counted *presence*, not optionality, and kept the first occurrence's text verbatim. Proved it by mutation — reversing the two union members in `zimmButton/index.tsx`:

```
before:  variant?: 'primary' | 'secondary'
after:   variant: 'icon'          ← same type, now claimed required
```

That is the *same class of defect I set out to fix* — a false requiredness claim — just relocated. Worth saying plainly rather than dressing up.

**Third ask — regression tests.** `scripts/` has no test file at all today. This would be the first, i.e. new harness for an unlinted dev script.

**Recommended: fix the two logic bugs, decline the tests, and pre-commit to a stopping rule.**

- Bug 1: bail to the union expression unless *every* member resolves. One condition change.
- Bug 2: track optionality per member — required only if every member declares it without `?`. A few lines.
- Tests: decline. `.claude/rules/testing.md` scopes tests to failures that are non-obvious or costly; a wrong cell in generated dev documentation is neither, and standing up the first `scripts/` test harness for it is disproportionate.
- **Stopping rule:** if a third finding lands on these same ~30 lines, I revert `13add6e` outright rather than keep going.

**The alternative, if you'd rather just end it: revert `13add6e` now.** The original finding was 🟡 Minor dev tooling whose entire visible benefit was one `?` character in a markdown table no shipped code reads. Two rounds and two order-dependent bugs is already a poor trade. I lean toward fixing rather than reverting only because the two fixes are genuinely small and I now know both failure modes concretely — reverting means parking a known-wrong row *and* still arguing a thread. - **Mac app** → `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude-code-sessions/cb50a622-…/990c5a80-…/`

## The bridge is Remote Control — already set up here

`remote-settings-consent.json` has session `990c5a80-…` consented under your account `cb50a622-…`, so this machine is already wired for it. Resume with it enabled:

```bash
cd /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa
claude --resume 652997c6-662c-4608-bb47-e37b77ba106b --remote-control
```

**The catch:** Remote Control gives you a remote head on a session that still *runs* in that terminal on this Mac. It's not a copy living inside the app — close the terminal and the session goes with it.

CONTEXT: Tim Lavelle made 13 commits (range `ec9d161..542ac65`). The reader is the project's Frontend Development Lead and knows this area deeply — they personally discovered and documented two traps in this codebase:

(a) The Zimmermann spacing scale is registered ONLY as `theme.space`. A bare token key like `spacing="m"` works, but the same bare key on a SIZING prop (`width`, `height`, `boxSize`, `minWidth`, `maxHeight`) falls through to Chakra's own `sizes` scale and silently misresolves — measured 8x to 112x wrong, and keys `s`/`m`/`l` are absent entirely so those declarations are dropped.

There is a known live instance at `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302`.

The reader also documented a rule that `var(--zimm-*)` CSS variables belong in theme recipes, never in component JSX. Tim's commits appear to have formalised policy in exactly this area, so determine whether Tim's changes SOLVE these traps, ENCODE them as policy, or WORK AROUND them.

- `9d5f89c` refactor(theme): require var(--zimm-*) over bare Chakra token keys in overrides
- `466e62b` feat(theme): build scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs, close the missing-audit gap

Note `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` is Tier 1 (frozen, UI-designer-owned); `overrides/app/theme/components/` and `globalStyles.ts` are Tier 2.

return <ExperiencePage slug={slug} isPreview={isPreview} isEditorCanvas={isEditorCanvas} />;

# The Contentful footer integration after Tim's 13 commits

## 1. The content model — five types, one join entity

All five live in `scripts/contentful/content-types/`, one file per type. Nothing is a nested/embedded object; every relationship is a Contentful reference array.

**`region`** (`region.js:1-40`) is the new keystone. One entry per SFCC storefront, with `siteId` (`Symbol`, required, `validations: [{unique: true}]`), `label` (editor-facing, e.g. "Australia"), and `locale` (explicitly *informational only* — `region.js:36-37`). Its comment states the contract plainly: `siteId` "matches an SFCC site ID from `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.generated.ts`'s `SITE_LOCALES` keys." This is the canonical, referenceable region entity, so nothing else has to carry a hardcoded site-ID list.

**`link`** (`link.js`) is `label` (localised) + `href` (not localised) + optional `regions` array referencing `region`. Deliberately generic — its description says it's "designed to be referenced from other content types later (e.g. header nav, mega-menu) without change."

**`footerNavGroup`** (`footerNavGroup.js`) is one column: `heading` (localised), a required `links` array of `link` references, and a `showContactChannels` boolean. That boolean is worth noting as a genuinely good modelling call, and the comment says why (`footerNavGroup.js:9-10`): it's "A flag, not a heading match — heading is localised, so matching its text breaks per storefront." Matching `heading === 'Contact'` would have silently died the moment an editor typed "Kontakt".

**`footerConfig`** (`footerConfig.js`) is the root: `internalTitle` (required, the `displayField`), `subscribeHeading`/`subscribeBody` (localised), required `navGroups` array, optional `legalLinks` array, `copyrightOwner`, the three contact channels `phoneHref`/`whatsAppHref`/`emailHref`, and its own optional `regions` array.

**`uiCopy`** (`uiCopy.js`) is unrelated to the footer structurally but arrived in the same work: one entry per UI string, with `title` (editor-facing, added in `c735478`), `key` (unique, not localised — "Must be identical across locales to work as a map key"), `value` (localised), and `description` (translator context).

**What an editor actually sees.** Building an AU footer means creating `link` entries, grouping them into `footerNavGroup` entries, then referencing those from a `footerConfig` — three levels of reference-picking. There is no composite editing surface; it's the standard Contentful reference-field UI at each level. The `internalTitle`/`title` fields exist purely so the entry list is scannable rather than showing raw dot-paths or blank rows.

**Localisation is declared per-field, and this is where the model and the runtime diverge — see §2.**

## 2. "Region-aware" concretely: SFCC site ID, two-stage resolution — and locale is *not* wired

Region-awareness is entirely keyed on **SFCC site ID**, resolved client-side, in two distinct stages.

The mechanism lives in `overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.ts`, which is deliberately not footer-specific — it accepts any entry shaped `{fields: {regions?: [{fields: {siteId}}]}}`. Two rules:

- **Eligibility** (`resolveByRegion.ts:22-26`): an entry with omitted or empty `regions` matches every site. Otherwise it matches only if some region's `siteId` equals the current site.
- **Specificity** (`resolveByRegion.ts:29-30`): `regions.length` where non-empty, else `Infinity`. Fewer regions = more specific; global sorts last.

Two exported functions apply those rules differently, and the split is the important part:

- `pickMostSpecificByRegion` (`:52`) — **single winner**, for the root entry. Used to choose *which* `footerConfig` renders.
- `filterByRegion` (`:37`) — **inclusive**, keeps every eligible entry. Used for arrays where multiple regional entries legitimately coexist, e.g. links inside a shared nav group.

Ties between two equally-scoped non-global entries resolve by most-recently-updated with a `console.warn` (`:71-79`). The comment is honest about why (`:46-50`): nothing in the additive-only pipeline prevents two entries both scoping to exactly `['ZimmermannUS']`, so it's resolved deterministically rather than silently normalised.

The site ID comes from `useMultiSite()` in `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:170-173`, and the two stages are applied at `:190-191`:

```ts
const resolved = pickMostSpecificByRegion<FooterConfigEntry>(configs, site.id);
setFooterData(resolved ? scopeToRegion(resolved, site.id) : null);
```

`scopeToRegion` (`:132-144`) is the second stage — it maps over `navGroups` running `filterByRegion` on each group's `links`, and over `legalLinks`. Its docstring explains why it's needed: Contentful's `include`-resolved response "nests navGroups/links/regions but applies no region scoping of its own."

Unit coverage is genuinely good here: `overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.test.ts` has 12 tests including tie-break order-independence, and `overrides/app/components/footer/index.test.tsx:64-110` covers `scopeToRegion` as pure logic.

**Now the important caveat.** The model declares `subscribeHeading`, `subscribeBody`, `heading`, `label`, and `value` as `localized: true`, but **no locale is ever passed at runtime**. The client is built without one (`overrides/app/hooks/useContentfulClient.ts:46`):

```ts
return createClient({ space: spaceId, environment, accessToken: token, host });
```

and the query passes none either (`footer/index.tsx:183`):

```ts
.getEntries({ content_type: 'footerConfig', include: 3 })
```

Same for uiCopy — `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts:110` builds a URL with `content_type`, `access_token`, `include=2`, and no `locale`. So **every one of the storefronts currently receives the Contentful space's default locale (`en`) for all localised footer and uiCopy fields.** `CONTENTFUL_FALLBACK_LOCALE` exists in `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts:24` and *is* used — but only by `pages/experience/index.tsx:95` and `pages/contentfulPreview/index.tsx:136`, never on the footer path.

This means region-awareness (site ID) is implemented and tested; localisation (locale) is modelled but not yet exercised. `uiCopy.js:8`'s description even claims entries are "fetched in bulk — all entries of this type, **one CDA call per locale**" — the implementation makes exactly one call, no locale. Worth knowing that's aspirational, not descriptive.

For calibration against your framing: `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.generated.ts` lists **11 site IDs** in `SITE_LOCALES` and **10 locales** in `SUPPORTED_LOCALES`, last synced 2026-08-07.

## 3. End-to-end data flow

```
Contentful CDA (cdn.contentful.com)
  ↓  contentful SDK client, memoised
overrides/app/hooks/useContentfulClient.ts:44-47      createClient({space, environment, accessToken, host})
  ↓
overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:178-200     useEffect → client.getEntries({content_type:'footerConfig', include:3})
  ↓  response.items as unknown as FooterConfigEntry[]   (:189)
overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.ts:52             pickMostSpecificByRegion(configs, site.id)
  ↓
overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:132-144     scopeToRegion → filterByRegion over navGroups[].links + legalLinks
  ↓  setFooterData(...)   (:191)
overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:204         <Footer data={footerData} .../>
  ↓  destructured at :64-73
  ├─ ZimmSubscribeSection   (:83)   heading/body from subscribeHeading/subscribeBody
  ├─ FooterNavColumn        (:94)   one per navGroup, + the three contact hrefs
  │    └─ footerNavColumn/index.tsx:57  links.map → ZimmNavItem
  │    └─ footerNavColumn/index.tsx:89  showContactChannels && <ZimmContactIconRow>
  └─ BottomBar              (:118)  copyrightYear/copyrightOwner + legalItems
```

**Where the fetch happens: a `useEffect` inside a component under `overrides/app/components/`.** `FooterContainer` (`footer/index.tsx:160-205`) is the default export; the presentational `Footer` (`:56`) is a named export that takes `data` as a required prop and fetches nothing.

**Does it respect the container/presentational rule?** Partially, and the code says so itself. The split is real — `Footer`, `FooterNavColumn`, `BottomBar`, `ZimmSubscribeSection` are all pure prop-consumers. But the fetch does sit under `components/`, and the JSDoc at `:156-158` flags it explicitly:

> "Note this puts a fetch inside `components/`, which components.md reserves for containers; if that matters, this should move into an `_app` override instead (Tier 2 shared shell — coordinate first)."

The justification at `:147-150` is legitimate: base `_app/index.jsx` renders `<Footer />` with no props, so there is no upstream container to own the data. Note that `542ac65`'s addition to `.claude/rules/components.md` does **not** cover this — it carves out an exception for Context-backed static-copy hooks (`useUiCopy`), not for a component-level data fetch. So this remains a knowingly-accepted deviation, not a legitimised one.

**Is it SSR-safe?** Safe, but **not server-rendered**. `useEffect` never runs during `renderToString`, so on the server `footerData` is `null` and `FooterContainer` returns `null` (`:202`). The footer is **absent from the SSR HTML entirely** and appears only after hydration + a client round-trip to `cdn.contentful.com`. Your pre-Tim fixture footer *was* in the SSR HTML. Two consequences worth weighing: every footer link (including the legal set) is now JS-dependent for crawlers, and there's a post-hydration insertion of a full-height footer with no skeleton reserving space. The project is aware of the SSR-prefetch mechanism — `pages/experience/index.tsx:54` notes "A real 404 needs SSR prefetch (getProps) — tracked separately" — so `getProps` was available and not used here.

**Two different fetch mechanisms now coexist.** The footer uses the official `contentful` SDK via `useContentfulClient`. `UiCopyProvider` (`overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:19`) uses the older hand-rolled `useContentfulEntries` from `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`, which builds a raw URL with the token in the **query string** (`useContentful.ts:110`) and calls `console.error` on failure (`:116`, `:145`). The CDA token is public/read-only by design (`config/contentful.ts:6-8`), so this isn't a credential leak in the payment-credential sense — but it does put a token into MRT access logs and Referer headers, and `UiCopyProvider` is mounted app-wide in `_app-config/index.tsx:161`, so that call now fires on **every page of every storefront**, uncached (plain `useState`/`useEffect`, no React Query).
