## 5. Failure behaviour — two deliberately opposite policies

**The footer fails closed to nothing.** `footer/index.tsx:202` is the whole story:

```ts
if (!footerData) return null;
```

That single branch covers four states, and all four are explicitly tested in `footer/index.test.tsx:145-220`: fetch pending, fetch rejected (`:167`), no entry matches the current site (`:175`), and no Contentful client configured at all (`:213`).

The rationale is at `footer/index.tsx:154-156`: "no fallback to placeholder content once wired to live data, so a Contentful outage doesn't silently ship stale placeholder copy to real shoppers."

**Does it degrade gracefully per the project rule?** It satisfies the letter — Contentful failing does not break the rest of the page, the error is caught (`:193-195`), and the failure is isolated to the footer. But the outcome is that the *entire* footer disappears, including Privacy Policy, Terms, Accessibility, Modern Slavery, and Cookie Settings. That's a compliance-adjacent surface vanishing on a CDN blip, and it's worth deciding consciously whether "no footer" is genuinely preferable to "footer with a minimal hardcoded legal set." The choice is defensible and documented; I'd just flag that it was made in the commit, not in a PRD.

Also note the `.catch(() => {...})` at `:193` swallows the error with **no logging, no Sentry, no telemetry** — a Contentful outage that blanks the footer on every page of every storefront produces zero signal. There's no project logger yet (`conventions.md` says "Use the project's logger when one is introduced"), so this is partly a missing-primitive problem, but the net effect today is a silent, invisible failure mode.

**uiCopy fails open, deliberately.** `uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:29-33` is the counterpoint, and the comment states the distinction well:

> "Fallback-on-failure by design, not just a loading placeholder: unlike structural content (e.g. FooterContainer's footerConfig, which renders nothing rather than substitute placeholder content), losing a button label or a status message to a Contentful outage should never blank a control."

`useUiCopy()` also degrades to fallback-only text with no Provider mounted (`hooks/useUiCopy.ts:19-22`, `:38`) rather than throwing — which is what makes Storybook and unit tests work with zero setup. Five keys are in use today: `footer.copyright.label` (`bottomBar/index.tsx:36`) and `footer.subscribe.{emailLabel,buttonLabel,successMessage,unavailableMessage}` (`zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:53-56`), each with an English literal fallback.

## 6. Environment Templates — what changed operationally

The old pipeline (`scripts/contentful/sync.js`, `setup/runMigrations.mjs`, `setup/detectDrift.mjs`, `migrations/001-initial-content-types.mjs`) was **deleted** and replaced by an **organization-scoped Contentful Environment Template**.

An Environment Template is an org-level, versioned bundle of content-type definitions, decoupled from any space or environment — a definition you author once and then *install* into each environment. This is Contentful's current recommended approach over independently-synced per-space content types.

The new three-step flow, and what a developer types:

| Step | Command | Script |
|---|---|---|
| Author/update the template | `npm run sync:contentful` | `scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js` |
| Install into one environment | `npm run install:contentful -- --target dev` | `setup/installTemplate.mjs` |
| Seed the `region` entries | `npm run seed:contentful-regions -- --target dev` | `setup/seedRegions.mjs` |

`npm run sync:contentful` **still exists** — it was re-pointed, not removed, so muscle memory keeps working but now does something different (builds/updates the org template rather than pushing content types to a space). `migrate:contentful` and `detect:drift` are gone; Contentful now tracks install status natively, so the `_migrationHistory` content type and drift detection are obsolete.

**One new env var**, added to `.env.sample`: `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID` tagged `# scope:shared` / `# mrt:false`, pre-populated because an org ID is a public identifier, not a credential. `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` stays `scope:personal`. The operationally meaningful part: template authoring and installation are now **org-scoped operations**, so they need org-level API reach, not just space-level.

**On the Tier 2 additive-only constraint — the safety floor holds, but the shape changed.** I verified the install call directly (`setup/installTemplate.mjs:137-139`):

```js
await client.environmentTemplate.install(
  { spaceId, environmentId: TARGET, environmentTemplateId: template.sys.id },
  { version: template.sys.version, deleteDeletedFields: DELETE_DELETED_FIELDS, takeover },
);
```

with `const DELETE_DELETED_FIELDS = args.includes('--delete-deleted-fields');` at `:36` — **defaults to `false`**. So the default path is additive-only, same as `sync.js`. But the distinction matters: `sync.js` had *no delete path in the code at all*; the new pipeline has one, reachable by anyone who passes a flag. A second guard refuses to install when validation finds unmanaged conflicting content types unless `--force` or `--takeover <ids>` is passed (`:115`, `:128`).

`protectedFiles.md` was updated in the same commit to describe this accurately — the old text said the script "is idempotent but **additive-only** — it cannot delete fields," and the new text says field deletion "is opt-in (`--delete-deleted-fields`), off by default." That's a truthful restatement, not a weakening, and CODEOWNERS ownership for these paths is unchanged (tier-2 + tier-1 approvers, just re-mapped to the two new entry points).

`seedRegions.mjs` is idempotent via deterministic entry IDs (`region-<siteId>`) and creates all 11 regions (`:40-50`). Its region list is a **static array copied** from `contentfulMapping.generated.ts` as of 2026-08-23, with a comment acknowledging it can drift — a second source of truth for the site list, which is a small but real maintenance seam.

The `shoppableImage`/hotspot Experiences components deleted in `5b2be3f` leave no dangling imports — the only surviving mention of `shoppableImage` anywhere is a usage example in a comment at `installTemplate.mjs:20`. No build risk.

## 7. The Experience Builder fix — Studio-only

`ad4fbc6` touched one file, `overrides/app/pages/experience/index.tsx`, and fixed two independent bugs that both blanked the authoring canvas.

**Bug 1 — the 404 guard killed `ExperienceRoot` in canvas mode.** `useFetchBySlug` never returns an `experience` object when running inside Studio's canvas iframe; in that mode data arrives by `postMessage`, not by API fetch. The old `if (error || !experience)` branch therefore always matched, rendered "Page not found," and returned before `ExperienceRoot` mounted — empty canvas, empty component picker. Fixed by destructuring `mode` and gating the guard (`:41`, `:51`):

```ts
const isSupervisedMode = mode === StudioCanvasMode.EDITOR || mode === StudioCanvasMode.READ_ONLY;
...
if (!isSupervisedMode && (error || !experience)) {
```

**Bug 2 — hydration mismatch.** `useFetchBySlug` initialises canvas state on `typeof window !== 'undefined'`, which differs between the SSR pass and the client's first hydration pass, producing React #418/#423 and discarding the tree. Fixed by deferring the mount until after hydration and rendering a `Spinner` identically on both server and first client paint (`:120-125`, `:159-165`), so `useFetchBySlug` only ever runs in a purely client-side pass.

**Blast radius: authoring view only.** Both changes are behind guards a real shopper cannot satisfy. `isEditorCanvas` is `params.has('expEditorMode')` (`:173-179`) — a proprietary query param Studio appends to its own iframe URL, read via React Router's `useLocation().search` so it's SSR-safe. `isSupervisedMode` depends on an SDK `mode` value only set via Studio `postMessage`. For any normal request both are `false`, the mount-guard block is skipped entirely, `ExperienceFetch` renders on the SSR pass exactly as before, and the `!experience` → 404 path still fires for genuinely missing slugs.

The page serves the catch-all `path: '/:slug'` route (`overrides/app/routes.tsx:43-48`), so it is reachable in production but only where an author has published an experience. The documented preview gate is honoured — `previewUnavailable` produces `res.status(404)` plus `<Seo noIndex />` (`:129-141`), never a fall-back to delivery. Package is `@contentful/experiences-sdk-react` `^3.8.8`; the `StudioCanvasMode` constant is imported from `@contentful/experiences-core/constants`, which is only a **transitive** dependency — an undeclared peer that could break silently on a future SDK bump.

## 8. Surprising, risky, or contradicting an earlier decision

**The `en-CA` locale is never created in Contentful.** This is the most concrete gap I found. `bootstrapSpace.mjs:40-49` creates 9 locales: `en`, `en-US`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`, `en-CH`, `en-HK`, `en-AE`. `SUPPORTED_LOCALES` (`contentfulMapping.generated.ts:8-19`) has 10 — the missing one is **`en-CA`**, the ZimmermannUSIntl locale. Meanwhile `seedRegions.mjs:42` happily creates `region-ZimmermannUSIntl` with `locale: 'en-CA'`, and a repo-wide grep confirms `en-CA` appears nowhere else in `scripts/contentful/`. So the US-International region entity exists in Contentful while its locale does not. It's currently invisible because nothing passes a locale at fetch time and non-default locales fall back to `en` anyway — but it will bite the moment locale-aware fetching lands.

**The footer never fetches in preview mode.** `footer/index.tsx:175` calls `useContentfulClient()` with no arguments, so it is always Delivery. Editors cannot preview draft footer changes in Studio or via the `?preview` flow — the footer will always show published content. Not a bug, but likely a surprise to whoever authors the first real `footerConfig`.

**`site.id` dropped the optional chaining its own cited precedent uses.** `footer/index.tsx:170-173` casts `useMultiSite()` to `{site: {id: string}}` — non-optional — then reads `site.id` at `:190`, `:191`, and in the dependency array at `:200`. The comment at `:167-169` cites `useCountryConfig.ts` as "the existing precedent for this exact lookup," but that file actually writes `site?.id` (`useCountryConfig.ts:20`), and the base SFCC hook itself defensively optional-chains (`site?.alias || site?.id`). If `site` is ever undefined, `site.id` in the dep array throws and takes the footer down at render. Low likelihood inside a real `MultiSiteProvider`, but the assertion silences exactly the check the precedent relies on.

**`console.warn` in a production path.** `resolveByRegion.ts:74-76` warns on a region tie. `conventions.md` bars `console.log`/`console.error` outside error boundaries and tooling; `console.warn` isn't named but is plainly the same spirit. Minor, and arguably the right call given there's no logger — but it will fire in shoppers' browsers.

**Tier 1 governance files were edited in this branch.** `542ac65` modified `.claude/rules/components.md`, `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md`, `.claude/rules/testing.md`, `CODEOWNERS`, and the mirrored `.cursor`/`.vscode`/copilot configs — all Tier 1 Governance per `frozenFiles.md`. The commit message asserts it was "Edited under verified tier-1-approvers identity (`gh api user` + team membership check) per AGENTS.md's Tier 1 Approval process." That's the documented exception, but it's self-asserted in a commit message — worth confirming independently given it's the one thing in this branch that changes the rules rather than the code.

**The rule change and the code's own admission point in opposite directions.** The `components.md` addition carves out a narrow, well-reasoned exception for Context-backed app-wide static-copy hooks (`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) being callable from presentational leaves. I think that exception is correct and the reasoning holds. But note what it does *not* cover: the `FooterContainer` fetch under `components/`. That deviation is still live and still flagged in its own JSDoc as something that "should move into an `_app` override instead." So the branch legitimised one pattern and left the other as acknowledged debt — easy to conflate on a skim.

**`uiCopyProvider/` was correctly added to Tier 2 + CODEOWNERS**, which is a genuine gap-closure: it's mounted at the app root in `_app-config/index.tsx:161` with the same blast radius as `_app-config` itself, and had no review routing at all. Note that `_app-config/` is itself Tier 2 Global Shell ("Owner: Both Squads — coordinate before touching") and was modified here.

**The SSR/SEO change is the item I'd surface first to the wider team.** It isn't called out in any commit message: the footer moved from server-rendered (fixture) to client-only (`useEffect`), so every footer link left the initial HTML. On a storefront whose brief explicitly says "must be SEO-friendly," losing the entire footer internal-link graph from SSR output — plus a post-hydration insertion with no reserved space — is a bigger behavioural change than "wire footer to Contentful" implies. `getProps` was the available alternative and the codebase already knows about it.</result>

# The Contentful footer integration after Tim's 13 commits

## 1. The content model — five types, one join entity

All five live in `scripts/contentful/content-types/`, one file per type. Nothing is a nested/embedded object; every relationship is a Contentful reference array.

**`region`** (`region.js:1-40`) is the new keystone. One entry per SFCC storefront, with `siteId` (`Symbol`, required, `validations: [{unique: true}]`), `label` (editor-facing, e.g. "Australia"), and `locale` (explicitly *informational only* — `region.js:36-37`). Its comment states the contract plainly: `siteId` "matches an SFCC site ID from `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.generated.ts`'s `SITE_LOCALES` keys." This is the canonical, referenceable region entity, so nothing else has to carry a hardcoded site-ID list.

**`link`** (`link.js`) is `label` (localised) + `href` (not localised) + optional `regions` array referencing `region`. Deliberately generic — its description says it's "designed to be referenced from other content types later (e.g. header nav, mega-menu) without change."

**`footerNavGroup`** (`footerNavGroup.js`) is one column: `heading` (localised), a required `links` array of `link` references, and a `showContactChannels` boolean. That boolean is worth noting as a genuinely good modelling call, and the comment says why (`footerNavGroup.js:9-10`): it's "A flag, not a heading match — heading is localised, so matching its text breaks per storefront." Matching `heading === 'Contact'` would have silently died the moment an editor typed "Kontakt".

**`footerConfig`** (`footerConfig.js`) is the root: `internalTitle` (required, the `displayField`), `subscribeHeading`/`subscribeBody` (localised), required `navGroups` array, optional `legalLinks` array, `copyrightOwner`, the three contact channels `phoneHref`/`whatsAppHref`/`emailHref`, and its own optional `regions` array.

**`uiCopy`** (`uiCopy.js`) is unrelated to the footer structurally but arrived in the same work: one entry per UI string, with `title` (editor-facing, added in `c735478`), `key` (unique, not localised — "Must be identical across locales to work as a map key"), `value` (localised), and `description` (translator context).

**What an editor actually sees.** Building an AU footer means creating `link` entries, grouping them into `footerNavGroup` entries, then referencing those from a `footerConfig` — three levels of reference-picking. There is no composite editing surface; it's the standard Contentful reference-field UI at each level. The `internalTitle`/`title` fields exist purely so the entry list is scannable rather than showing raw dot-paths or blank rows.

**Localisation is declared per-field, and this is where the model and the runtime diverge — see §2.**

## 2. "Region-aware" concretely: SFCC site ID, two-stage resolution — and locale is *not* wired

Region-awareness is entirely keyed on **SFCC site ID**, resolved client-side, in two distinct stages.

The mechanism lives in `overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.ts`, which is deliberately not footer-specific — it accepts any entry shaped `{fields: {regions?: [{fields: {siteId}}]}}`. Two rules:

- **Eligibility** (`resolveByRegion.ts:22-26`): an entry with omitted or empty `regions` matches every site. Otherwise it matches only if some region's `siteId` equals the current site.
- **Specificity** (`resolveByRegion.ts:29-30`): `regions.length` where non-empty, else `Infinity`. Fewer regions = more specific; global sorts last.

Two exported functions apply those rules differently, and the split is the important part:

- `pickMostSpecificByRegion` (`:52`) — **single winner**, for the root entry. Used to choose *which* `footerConfig` renders.
- `filterByRegion` (`:37`) — **inclusive**, keeps every eligible entry. Used for arrays where multiple regional entries legitimately coexist, e.g. links inside a shared nav group.

Ties between two equally-scoped non-global entries resolve by most-recently-updated with a `console.warn` (`:71-79`). The comment is honest about why (`:46-50`): nothing in the additive-only pipeline prevents two entries both scoping to exactly `['ZimmermannUS']`, so it's resolved deterministically rather than silently normalised.

The site ID comes from `useMultiSite()` in `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:170-173`, and the two stages are applied at `:190-191`:

```ts
const resolved = pickMostSpecificByRegion<FooterConfigEntry>(configs, site.id);
setFooterData(resolved ? scopeToRegion(resolved, site.id) : null);
```

`scopeToRegion` (`:132-144`) is the second stage — it maps over `navGroups` running `filterByRegion` on each group's `links`, and over `legalLinks`. Its docstring explains why it's needed: Contentful's `include`-resolved response "nests navGroups/links/regions but applies no region scoping of its own."

Unit coverage is genuinely good here: `overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.test.ts` has 12 tests including tie-break order-independence, and `overrides/app/components/footer/index.test.tsx:64-110` covers `scopeToRegion` as pure logic.

**Now the important caveat.** The model declares `subscribeHeading`, `subscribeBody`, `heading`, `label`, and `value` as `localized: true`, but **no locale is ever passed at runtime**. The client is built without one (`overrides/app/hooks/useContentfulClient.ts:46`):

```ts
return createClient({ space: spaceId, environment, accessToken: token, host });
```

and the query passes none either (`footer/index.tsx:183`):

```ts
.getEntries({ content_type: 'footerConfig', include: 3 })
```

Same for uiCopy — `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts:110` builds a URL with `content_type`, `access_token`, `include=2`, and no `locale`. So **every one of the storefronts currently receives the Contentful space's default locale (`en`) for all localised footer and uiCopy fields.** `CONTENTFUL_FALLBACK_LOCALE` exists in `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts:24` and *is* used — but only by `pages/experience/index.tsx:95` and `pages/contentfulPreview/index.tsx:136`, never on the footer path.

This means region-awareness (site ID) is implemented and tested; localisation (locale) is modelled but not yet exercised. `uiCopy.js:8`'s description even claims entries are "fetched in bulk — all entries of this type, **one CDA call per locale**" — the implementation makes exactly one call, no locale. Worth knowing that's aspirational, not descriptive.

For calibration against your framing: `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.generated.ts` lists **11 site IDs** in `SITE_LOCALES` and **10 locales** in `SUPPORTED_LOCALES`, last synced 2026-08-07.

## 3. End-to-end data flow

```
Contentful CDA (cdn.contentful.com)
  ↓  contentful SDK client, memoised
overrides/app/hooks/useContentfulClient.ts:44-47      createClient({space, environment, accessToken, host})
  ↓
overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:178-200     useEffect → client.getEntries({content_type:'footerConfig', include:3})
  ↓  response.items as unknown as FooterConfigEntry[]   (:189)
overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.ts:52             pickMostSpecificByRegion(configs, site.id)
  ↓
overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:132-144     scopeToRegion → filterByRegion over navGroups[].links + legalLinks
  ↓  setFooterData(...)   (:191)
overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:204         <Footer data={footerData} .../>
  ↓  destructured at :64-73
  ├─ ZimmSubscribeSection   (:83)   heading/body from subscribeHeading/subscribeBody
  ├─ FooterNavColumn        (:94)   one per navGroup, + the three contact hrefs
  │    └─ footerNavColumn/index.tsx:57  links.map → ZimmNavItem
  │    └─ footerNavColumn/index.tsx:89  showContactChannels && <ZimmContactIconRow>
  └─ BottomBar              (:118)  copyrightYear/copyrightOwner + legalItems
```

**Where the fetch happens: a `useEffect` inside a component under `overrides/app/components/`.** `FooterContainer` (`footer/index.tsx:160-205`) is the default export; the presentational `Footer` (`:56`) is a named export that takes `data` as a required prop and fetches nothing.

**Does it respect the container/presentational rule?** Partially, and the code says so itself. The split is real — `Footer`, `FooterNavColumn`, `BottomBar`, `ZimmSubscribeSection` are all pure prop-consumers. But the fetch does sit under `components/`, and the JSDoc at `:156-158` flags it explicitly:

> "Note this puts a fetch inside `components/`, which components.md reserves for containers; if that matters, this should move into an `_app` override instead (Tier 2 shared shell — coordinate first)."

The justification at `:147-150` is legitimate: base `_app/index.jsx` renders `<Footer />` with no props, so there is no upstream container to own the data. Note that `542ac65`'s addition to `.claude/rules/components.md` does **not** cover this — it carves out an exception for Context-backed static-copy hooks (`useUiCopy`), not for a component-level data fetch. So this remains a knowingly-accepted deviation, not a legitimised one.

**Is it SSR-safe?** Safe, but **not server-rendered**. `useEffect` never runs during `renderToString`, so on the server `footerData` is `null` and `FooterContainer` returns `null` (`:202`). The footer is **absent from the SSR HTML entirely** and appears only after hydration + a client round-trip to `cdn.contentful.com`. Your pre-Tim fixture footer *was* in the SSR HTML. Two consequences worth weighing: every footer link (including the legal set) is now JS-dependent for crawlers, and there's a post-hydration insertion of a full-height footer with no skeleton reserving space. The project is aware of the SSR-prefetch mechanism — `pages/experience/index.tsx:54` notes "A real 404 needs SSR prefetch (getProps) — tracked separately" — so `getProps` was available and not used here.

**Two different fetch mechanisms now coexist.** The footer uses the official `contentful` SDK via `useContentfulClient`. `UiCopyProvider` (`overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:19`) uses the older hand-rolled `useContentfulEntries` from `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`, which builds a raw URL with the token in the **query string** (`useContentful.ts:110`) and calls `console.error` on failure (`:116`, `:145`). The CDA token is public/read-only by design (`config/contentful.ts:6-8`), so this isn't a credential leak in the payment-credential sense — but it does put a token into MRT access logs and Referer headers, and `UiCopyProvider` is mounted app-wide in `_app-config/index.tsx:161`, so that call now fires on **every page of every storefront**, uncached (plain `useState`/`useEffect`, no React Query).

## 4. `contentfulFixture.ts` — renamed, and the exposure is gone

The file was **renamed, not deleted**: `5640c25` moved `overrides/app/components/footer/contentfulFixture.ts` → `overrides/app/components/footer/index.stories.content.ts`. The commit message gives the reason: "it now only ever feeds `index.stories.tsx` (Storybook), not the live container."

I verified the reference graph at HEAD. `FOOTER_FIXTURE` is imported in exactly one place: `overrides/app/components/footer/index.stories.tsx:5` (used at `:14`, `:171`, `:173`). It is **not** imported by `footer/index.tsx`, and **not** by `footer/index.test.tsx` — the test file builds its own minimal fixtures instead (`index.test.tsx:36-58`). The only other mentions are prose in comments (`types/contentful.ts:130-131`, `footer/index.tsx:21`).

**So yes — your placeholder-contact exposure is gone from production.** The values still exist in the repo at `index.stories.content.ts:33-35`:

```ts
phoneHref: 'tel:+61280808080',
whatsAppHref: 'https://wa.me/61280808080',
emailHref: 'mailto:care@zimmermann.com',
```

but nothing in the production import graph reaches that module, so it isn't bundled and those `tel:`/`wa.me:`/`mailto:` values no longer ship on any page. Production values now come from `footerConfig`'s `phoneHref`/`whatsAppHref`/`emailHref` fields, and every one passes through `isSafeHref` before reaching an anchor (`ui-kits/molecules/zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:62`), with an inert non-interactive fallback when rejected — `footerConfig.js:31-34` documents that as a deliberate CMS-injection guard.

One related placeholder *does* still ship: `LOCALE_LABEL_PLACEHOLDER = 'Australia (AUD) / ENG'` hardcoded at `footer/bottomBar/index.tsx:15`, rendered as a non-interactive `div` (`:45-50`). The comment explains it's blocked on the locale selector, which matches the known dead end there — it isn't Contentful-sourced because `FooterConfigEntry` has no field for it.

## 5. Failure behaviour — two deliberately opposite policies

**The footer fails closed to nothing.** `footer/index.tsx:202` is the whole story:

```ts
if (!footerData) return null;
```

That single branch covers four states, and all four are explicitly tested in `footer/index.test.tsx:145-220`: fetch pending, fetch rejected (`:167`), no entry matches the current site (`:175`), and no Contentful client configured at all (`:213`).

The rationale is at `footer/index.tsx:154-156`: "no fallback to placeholder content once wired to live data, so a Contentful outage doesn't silently ship stale placeholder copy to real shoppers."

**Does it degrade gracefully per the project rule?** It satisfies the letter — Contentful failing does not break the rest of the page, the error is caught (`:193-195`), and the failure is isolated to the footer. But the outcome is that the *entire* footer disappears, including Privacy Policy, Terms, Accessibility, Modern Slavery, and Cookie Settings. That's a compliance-adjacent surface vanishing on a CDN blip, and it's worth deciding consciously whether "no footer" is genuinely preferable to "footer with a minimal hardcoded legal set." The choice is defensible and documented; I'd just flag that it was made in the commit, not in a PRD.

Also note the `.catch(() => {...})` at `:193` swallows the error with **no logging, no Sentry, no telemetry** — a Contentful outage that blanks the footer on every page of every storefront produces zero signal. There's no project logger yet (`conventions.md` says "Use the project's logger when one is introduced"), so this is partly a missing-primitive problem, but the net effect today is a silent, invisible failure mode.

**uiCopy fails open, deliberately.** `uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:29-33` is the counterpoint, and the comment states the distinction well:

> "Fallback-on-failure by design, not just a loading placeholder: unlike structural content (e.g. FooterContainer's footerConfig, which renders nothing rather than substitute placeholder content), losing a button label or a status message to a Contentful outage should never blank a control."

`useUiCopy()` also degrades to fallback-only text with no Provider mounted (`hooks/useUiCopy.ts:19-22`, `:38`) rather than throwing — which is what makes Storybook and unit tests work with zero setup. Five keys are in use today: `footer.copyright.label` (`bottomBar/index.tsx:36`) and `footer.subscribe.{emailLabel,buttonLabel,successMessage,unavailableMessage}` (`zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:53-56`), each with an English literal fallback.

## 6. Environment Templates — what changed operationally

The old pipeline (`scripts/contentful/sync.js`, `setup/runMigrations.mjs`, `setup/detectDrift.mjs`, `migrations/001-initial-content-types.mjs`) was **deleted** and replaced by an **organization-scoped Contentful Environment Template**.

An Environment Template is an org-level, versioned bundle of content-type definitions, decoupled from any space or environment — a definition you author once and then *install* into each environment. This is Contentful's current recommended approach over independently-synced per-space content types.

The new three-step flow, and what a developer types:

| Step | Command | Script |
|---|---|---|
| Author/update the template | `npm run sync:contentful` | `scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js` |
| Install into one environment | `npm run install:contentful -- --target dev` | `setup/installTemplate.mjs` |
| Seed the `region` entries | `npm run seed:contentful-regions -- --target dev` | `setup/seedRegions.mjs` |

`npm run sync:contentful` **still exists** — it was re-pointed, not removed, so muscle memory keeps working but now does something different (builds/updates the org template rather than pushing content types to a space). `migrate:contentful` and `detect:drift` are gone; Contentful now tracks install status natively, so the `_migrationHistory` content type and drift detection are obsolete.

**One new env var**, added to `.env.sample`: `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID` tagged `# scope:shared` / `# mrt:false`, pre-populated because an org ID is a public identifier, not a credential. `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` stays `scope:personal`. The operationally meaningful part: template authoring and installation are now **org-scoped operations**, so they need org-level API reach, not just space-level.

**On the Tier 2 additive-only constraint — the safety floor holds, but the shape changed.** I verified the install call directly (`setup/installTemplate.mjs:137-139`):

```js
await client.environmentTemplate.install(
  { spaceId, environmentId: TARGET, environmentTemplateId: template.sys.id },
  { version: template.sys.version, deleteDeletedFields: DELETE_DELETED_FIELDS, takeover },
);
```

with `const DELETE_DELETED_FIELDS = args.includes('--delete-deleted-fields');` at `:36` — **defaults to `false`**. So the default path is additive-only, same as `sync.js`. But the distinction matters: `sync.js` had *no delete path in the code at all*; the new pipeline has one, reachable by anyone who passes a flag. A second guard refuses to install when validation finds unmanaged conflicting content types unless `--force` or `--takeover <ids>` is passed (`:115`, `:128`).

`protectedFiles.md` was updated in the same commit to describe this accurately — the old text said the script "is idempotent but **additive-only** — it cannot delete fields," and the new text says field deletion "is opt-in (`--delete-deleted-fields`), off by default." That's a truthful restatement, not a weakening, and CODEOWNERS ownership for these paths is unchanged (tier-2 + tier-1 approvers, just re-mapped to the two new entry points).

`seedRegions.mjs` is idempotent via deterministic entry IDs (`region-<siteId>`) and creates all 11 regions (`:40-50`). Its region list is a **static array copied** from `contentfulMapping.generated.ts` as of 2026-08-23, with a comment acknowledging it can drift — a second source of truth for the site list, which is a small but real maintenance seam.

The `shoppableImage`/hotspot Experiences components deleted in `5b2be3f` leave no dangling imports — the only surviving mention of `shoppableImage` anywhere is a usage example in a comment at `installTemplate.mjs:20`. No build risk.

## 7. The Experience Builder fix — Studio-only

`ad4fbc6` touched one file, `overrides/app/pages/experience/index.tsx`, and fixed two independent bugs that both blanked the authoring canvas.

**Bug 1 — the 404 guard killed `ExperienceRoot` in canvas mode.** `useFetchBySlug` never returns an `experience` object when running inside Studio's canvas iframe; in that mode data arrives by `postMessage`, not by API fetch. The old `if (error || !experience)` branch therefore always matched, rendered "Page not found," and returned before `ExperienceRoot` mounted — empty canvas, empty component picker. Fixed by destructuring `mode` and gating the guard (`:41`, `:51`):

```ts
const isSupervisedMode = mode === StudioCanvasMode.EDITOR || mode === StudioCanvasMode.READ_ONLY;
...
if (!isSupervisedMode && (error || !experience)) {
```

**Bug 2 — hydration mismatch.** `useFetchBySlug` initialises canvas state on `typeof window !== 'undefined'`, which differs between the SSR pass and the client's first hydration pass, producing React #418/#423 and discarding the tree. Fixed by deferring the mount until after hydration and rendering a `Spinner` identically on both server and first client paint (`:120-125`, `:159-165`), so `useFetchBySlug` only ever runs in a purely client-side pass.

For any normal request both are `false`, the mount-guard block is skipped entirely, `ExperienceFetch` renders on the SSR pass exactly as before, and the `!experience` → 404 path still fires for genuinely missing slugs.

The page serves the catch-all `path: '/:slug'` route (`overrides/app/routes.tsx:43-48`), so it is reachable in production but only where an author has published an experience. The documented preview gate is honoured — `previewUnavailable` produces `res.status(404)` plus `<Seo noIndex />` (`:129-141`), never a fall-back to delivery. Package is `@contentful/experiences-sdk-react` `^3.8.8`; the `StudioCanvasMode` constant is imported from `@contentful/experiences-core/constants`, which is only a **transitive** dependency — an undeclared peer that could break silently on a future SDK bump.

## 8. Surprising, risky, or contradicting an earlier decision

**The `en-CA` locale is never created in Contentful.** This is the most concrete gap I found. `bootstrapSpace.mjs:40-49` creates 9 locales: `en`, `en-US`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`, `en-CH`, `en-HK`, `en-AE`. `SUPPORTED_LOCALES` (`contentfulMapping.generated.ts:8-19`) has 10 — the missing one is **`en-CA`**, the ZimmermannUSIntl locale. ### 1. The API as it stands

`overrides/app/hooks/useUiCopy.ts` is now 38 lines and contains no fetching at all. The whole hook is one line:

```ts
export const useUiCopy = (): UiCopyContextValue => useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY;
```
— `overrides/app/hooks/useUiCopy.ts:38`

The contract (`useUiCopy.ts:3-10`) is `{ t: (key: string, fallback: string) => string; isLoading: boolean }`. Both `t` parameters are required — TypeScript will not let you call `t('some.key')` without a fallback. That single design decision is what makes every failure mode collapse to one behaviour.

Real call sites, both leaf components:

```tsx
const { t } = useUiCopy();
const copyrightLabel = t('footer.copyright.label', 'Copyright');
```
— `overrides/app/components/footer/bottomBar/index.tsx:35-36`

```tsx
const { t } = useUiCopy();
const emailLabel = t('footer.subscribe.emailLabel', 'Email');
const subscribeButtonLabel = t('footer.subscribe.buttonLabel', 'Subscribe');
const successMessage = t('footer.subscribe.successMessage', SUBSCRIBE_SUCCESS_MESSAGE);
const unavailableMessage = t('footer.subscribe.unavailableMessage', SUBSCRIBE_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE);
```
— `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:52-56`

Those are the only two consumers in the codebase. `isLoading` is exposed but read by nobody outside the tests.

**`0b8db3e` built a fetching hook plus a prop-drilling convention.** The hook (40 lines) did the fetch itself: `useContentfulEntries<UiCopyEntry>('uiCopy')`, reduce to a `Map`, return a memoised `t`. The *consumption* pattern was container-fetch-and-thread: `FooterContainer` called `useUiCopy()` once and passed five resolved strings into `<Footer>`, which threaded one down to `BottomBar` and four down to `ZimmSubscribeSection`. That cost ten new optional props across three prop types (5 on `FooterProps`, 1 on `BottomBarProps`, 4 on `ZimmSubscribeSectionProps`), each defaulting to the English literal it replaced.

**The limitation was not aesthetic prop-drilling distaste — it was that duplicate calls were literally duplicate network requests.** The hook underneath is not React Query. `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts:88-156` is a hand-rolled `useState` + `useEffect` + `fetch`:

```ts
const url = `${baseUrl}/spaces/${spaceId}/environments/${environment}/entries?content_type=${contentType}&access_token=${token}&include=2`;
```
— `useContentful.ts:110`

There is no cache, no dedup, no query key. Two components calling `useUiCopy()` in v1 meant two identical CDA round-trips; ten meant ten. Tim's own commit message names this: *"neither double-fetches since only the container calls the hook."* So the prop-drill wasn't a stylistic choice, it was the mitigation — and a mitigation that only works while there is exactly one consumer. Any second consumer anywhere in the app (header, PDP, checkout) would have had to either open its own container-level fetch or grow its own prop chain.

v1 also carried second-order costs. The leaves acquired fake configurability — microcopy-as-props that nothing but the footer would ever pass. `Footer`'s prop surface gained five pass-throughs unrelated to its actual job. All ten props were deleted, the two constants went back to module-private (`zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:12-13`), and `footer/index.tsx` reverted to being purely about `footerConfig` — the diff on that file is a clean revert of the v1 hunks.

Explicitly *not* the reasons: no SSR mismatch was being fixed (both versions are client-only), and no React Query cache-miss problem existed, because React Query was never in this path.

```tsx
<UiCopyProvider>{children}</UiCopyProvider>
```
— `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx:161`

Full nesting is `CommerceApiProvider > MultiSiteProvider > StoreLocatorProvider > ContentfulLivePreviewProvider > ChakraProvider > UiCopyProvider > {children}`. Because `_app-config` wraps the entire app *including* the base template's `_app` (which owns `IntlProvider`), `UiCopyProvider` sits **above** `IntlProvider` — so `useUiCopy` is genuinely available everywhere, `_app` included.

It provides `{t, isLoading}` through a three-level memo chain: `copyMap` on `[data]` (lines 21-27), `t` on `[copyMap]` (line 33), `value` on `[t, isLoading]` (line 35). `t` is therefore referentially stable, and there's a test asserting exactly that (`uiCopyProvider/index.test.tsx:74-83`). Note the provider re-rendering on its own `setState` does not re-render the app: `children` arrives as a stable element reference, so React bails out of that subtree and only context consumers re-render.

Data comes from `useContentfulEntries<UiCopyEntry>('uiCopy')` — one CDA call for every `uiCopy` entry, client-side only, inside a `useEffect`.

```ts
const FALLBACK_ONLY: UiCopyContextValue = {
  t: (_key: string, fallback: string) => fallback,

};
```
— `useUiCopy.ts:19-22`

That is the load-bearing decision of the whole refactor. It's what lets a leaf call the hook with zero Storybook decorators and zero Vitest setup — `footer/index.test.tsx:24-27` documents deliberately *removing* a mock because of it, and `useUiCopy.test.tsx:7-12` tests it directly.

Free-form dot-path strings. **No typed key union, no generated key type, no enum.** Five keys are in use: `footer.copyright.label`, `footer.subscribe.emailLabel`, `footer.subscribe.buttonLabel`, `footer.subscribe.successMessage`, `footer.subscribe.unavailableMessage`. The convention is implicit — `<area>.<component>.<thing>`, lowerCamel segments — and written down nowhere.

On a missing key: **return the fallback, silently.** No throw, no empty string, no log. Crucially, the *same* thing happens on all four failure modes — still loading, network error, Contentful config absent, key genuinely doesn't exist — and they are indistinguishable both at the call site and in the DOM. `uiCopyProvider/index.test.tsx:33-72` has a separate test for each, and all four assert the identical outcome. Nothing verifies that a key referenced in code exists in Contentful, or that a Contentful entry is referenced by any code. There's no `--check` guard analogous to the `generate:contentful:check` script that exists for the type definitions.

They are **parallel, non-overlapping mechanisms**. `useUiCopy` neither complements nor duplicates react-intl in a controlled way; it bypasses it.

In practice that's where the base template's ~80 KB-per-locale of strings live. Zimmermann's own override code barely touches it — only **two** files actually import it: `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:5` and `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx:8`. Every other `useIntl` mention under `overrides/` is a comment referencing the pattern.

Tim's justification leans hard on that analogy — *"the same pattern this app already uses for translations (`useIntl`)"* (`useUiCopy.ts:26-28`). It's right about provider shape and wrong about capability, in three ways a developer must know:

**(a) Locale.** react-intl resolves per-storefront locale. `useUiCopy` does not. The CDA request at `useContentful.ts:110` sends **no `locale` parameter**, so Contentful returns default-locale values only — even though `value` is declared `localized: true` (`uiCopy.js:36`) and the content type's own description claims "one CDA call per locale" (`uiCopy.js:8`). `CONTENTFUL_FALLBACK_LOCALE = 'en-US'` sits unused in `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts:24`. On an 8-storefront, 11-locale project, uiCopy is currently English-only in effect. In fairness this is project-wide, not introduced here: `useContentfulClient.ts:46` builds `createClient` with no `locale`, and the footerConfig query at `footer/index.tsx:183` doesn't pass one either.

**(b) SSR.** react-intl's messages arrive via React Query, which participates in PWA Kit's SSR prepass — translated text is in the server-rendered HTML. `useUiCopy` resolves in a `useEffect`, so the server always emits the English fallback and the text swaps after hydration. There's no hydration mismatch (the client's first render also has `data: null`), but crawlers and SEO see the fallback, and there is a visible copy swap on first paint.

**(c) Pipeline and governance.** react-intl strings go through extract/compile and the `translations/` JSON files — Tier 2, Integration/SI-owned, requiring a PR. uiCopy strings need no code change and no review at all: a Contentful editor can change any of them straight into production. That's the feature, but it's a materially different risk profile than the one the Tier 2 translations rule was written for. The `description` field (`uiCopy.js:39-47`) exists specifically as translator context for Transperfect working key-by-key.

**Decision rule, as the code actually behaves:** if the string must be editable by a content editor without a deploy → uiCopy. If it must be correct in the SSR HTML, or must vary by locale *today*, or already exists in the base catalogue, or needs variable interpolation → react-intl. Nothing prevents the same label existing in both systems, and nothing detects it.

### 6. The `uiCopy` content type and the `title` field

The model (`scripts/contentful/content-types/uiCopy.js`) is four fields: `title` (Symbol, required, non-localized, and now the `displayField`), `key` (Symbol, required, non-localized, unique — *"Must be identical across locales to work as a map key, hence not localized"*), `value` (Symbol, required, **localized**), `description` (Text, optional, non-localized). Mirrored in TypeScript at `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts:163-164`. The content type itself arrived in `5b2be3f`; `title` in `c735478`.

`title` exists purely for the editor. `displayField` was `key`, so Studio's entry list rendered raw dot-paths — unscannable past a handful of entries. `title` is a human label ("Footer — Subscribe Button Label"), never read by the app; the runtime only touches `key` and `value`. It mirrors `footerConfig`'s existing `internalTitle`.

Two things worth knowing about the model. First, `value` is a **`Symbol`, not `Text`** — Contentful caps Symbol at 256 characters. The success-message fallback is already 96 characters; anything paragraph-length would be rejected by the CMS. Symbol also means no rich text, and `t()` returns a raw string with no ICU interpolation, so a string needing a variable can't live here at all.

Second, `c735478` added a **required** field to an already-published content type with live entries — exactly the case protectedFiles.md's "Contentful Schema Definitions" note warns about (additive-only sync, hard to undo). Tim handled it correctly by backfilling `title` on the 5 existing dev entries in the same operation, but nothing in the repo automates that, so promoting this to another environment requires repeating the backfill by hand.

**Rules of hooks: clean.** `useUiCopy()` is called unconditionally at the top of both consumers (`bottomBar:35`, `zimmSubscribeSection:52`); the `t()` calls that follow are ordinary function calls, not hooks, so the four consecutive `t()` lines are fine. > **Exception — Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks** (`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) may be called from any component, including presentational leaves. […] This exception is narrow: it covers content that is identical for every consumer regardless of route/context, not anything that varies per page.

It names `useUiCopy` as the reference example and `BottomBar`/`ZimmSubscribeSection` as the reference call sites, and the same carve-out was mirrored into `.claude/skills/new-component/SKILL.md:34`.

The technicality that makes the exception honest: `useUiCopy` doesn't fetch. It's `useContext`. The rule's stated rationale — *"a component that owns its own data-fetching can't be reused somewhere the data arrives differently"* — genuinely doesn't bite, because the leaves render fully with no provider, no mock, and no network.

Defensible for a component that renders no UI, but it's an unstated exemption, and the doc pass that added two other carve-outs didn't add this one.

**The 100-entry cliff.** This is the most likely production surprise in the whole mechanism. The bulk fetch passes no `limit` (`useContentful.ts:110`), and Contentful's CDA defaults to `limit=100` (max 1000). At the 101st `uiCopy` entry, entries start silently dropping out of the response and every key in the dropped tail silently renders its English fallback — no error, no warning, and a green test suite, because the tests mock `useContentfulEntries` and structurally cannot catch it. It will present to whoever hits it as "my CMS change didn't take effect." Worth an explicit `limit` (and pagination) before entry count grows.

So uiCopy is invisible to the Preview / Live Preview flow that `ContentfulLivePreviewProvider` (`_app-config:157`) sets up — an editor previewing a draft copy change will not see it. Worth confirming with Tim whether that's intended or just not reached yet.

**A registry drift that will not self-heal.** `.claude/registry/components.md:82` reports `UiCopyProvider` as `4 — Feature-local`, contradicting protectedFiles.md's Tier 2. The registry is auto-generated, so this looks like harmless staleness — but its tier column comes from a **hardcoded** mirror list at `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs:140-166` (`TIER2_PATHS`), which `542ac65` did not update. Regenerating will reproduce the wrong tier. It needs `'app/components/uiCopyProvider/'` added to that array.

**No `.docs/` requirement exists for any of this.** `grep -rl uiCopy .docs/` returns nothing. Per AGENTS.md, `.docs/` is the source of truth for requirements — yet the microcopy mechanism, its key convention, and the uiCopy-vs-react-intl decision rule live only in commit messages, code comments, and `.claude/rules/`. That's the gap most likely to make the next developer reinvent or misapply this.

Finally, a small v1 fragility now moot but illustrative: `<Footer copyrightLabel={t(...)} {...props} />` spread `props` *after* the explicit values, and `FooterContainer`'s `Omit<FooterProps, 'data'>` permitted `copyrightLabel` — so a caller-passed value would have silently beaten the CMS value. Gone with the props, but it's the sort of thing that made the prop-threading contract brittle in the first place.</result>

Symbol also means no rich text, and `t()` returns a raw string with no ICU interpolation, so a string needing a variable can't live here at all.

Second, `c735478` added a **required** field to an already-published content type with live entries — exactly the case protectedFiles.md's "Contentful Schema Definitions" note warns about (additive-only sync, hard to undo). Tim handled it correctly by backfilling `title` on the 5 existing dev entries in the same operation, but nothing in the repo automates that, so promoting this to another environment requires repeating the backfill by hand.

### 7. Rules-of-hooks and container/presentational compliance

**Rules of hooks: clean.** `useUiCopy()` is called unconditionally at the top of both consumers (`bottomBar:35`, `zimmSubscribeSection:52`); the `t()` calls that follow are ordinary function calls, not hooks, so the four consecutive `t()` lines are fine. The Provider's `useMemo`/`useCallback` are unconditional. `useUiCopy.ts` correctly stays `.ts` per components.md's "no JSX in a hook file" — `createContext` needs none, and the JSX is confined to `uiCopyProvider/index.tsx`. (The *test* had to be renamed `.ts` → `.tsx`, since the wrapper needs JSX.)

**Container/presentational: v2 deliberately breaks the letter of the rule, and Tim documented it rather than hiding it.** `542ac65` added an explicit carve-out at `.claude/rules/components.md:72-83`:

> **Exception — Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks** (`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) may be called from any component, including presentational leaves. […] This exception is narrow: it covers content that is identical for every consumer regardless of route/context, not anything that varies per page.

It names `useUiCopy` as the reference example and `BottomBar`/`ZimmSubscribeSection` as the reference call sites, and the same carve-out was mirrored into `.claude/skills/new-component/SKILL.md:34`.

The technicality that makes the exception honest: `useUiCopy` doesn't fetch. It's `useContext`. The rule's stated rationale — *"a component that owns its own data-fetching can't be reused somewhere the data arrives differently"* — genuinely doesn't bite, because the leaves render fully with no provider, no mock, and no network.

Governance follow-through was also done: `542ac65` added `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/` to Tier 2 Global Shell (`protectedFiles.md:19`, rationale at `:23`) and to CODEOWNERS alongside `_app-config`. That's the right classification — the provider has `_app-config`'s blast radius.

One genuine gap: `uiCopyProvider/` has **no `.stories.tsx`**, and components.md > Storybook says a story is *required* for anything exported from a folder under `overrides/app/components/`. Defensible for a component that renders no UI, but it's an unstated exemption, and the doc pass that added two other carve-outs didn't add this one.

### 8. Surprises, and what a developer would get wrong first

**The 100-entry cliff.** This is the most likely production surprise in the whole mechanism. The bulk fetch passes no `limit` (`useContentful.ts:110`), and Contentful's CDA defaults to `limit=100` (max 1000). At the 101st `uiCopy` entry, entries start silently dropping out of the response and every key in the dropped tail silently renders its English fallback — no error, no warning, and a green test suite, because the tests mock `useContentfulEntries` and structurally cannot catch it. It will present to whoever hits it as "my CMS change didn't take effect." Worth an explicit `limit` (and pagination) before entry count grows.

**Unbounded, unfiltered payload on every page.** The design fetches *all* uiCopy entries app-wide on every page load, plus a pointless `include=2` (uiCopy has no link fields). Fine at 5 entries; there's no story for 500. Combined with the client-side-only fetch, this adds a CDA round-trip to every page on a project whose stated top priority is LCP ≤ 2s at p75 mobile.

**English-first paint.** Per §5(b): SSR HTML and first paint always show fallbacks, then swap post-hydration. A length-sensitive control (the subscribe button, the copyright line) will visibly reflow.

**`isLoading` is a trap.** It's exposed, memoised, tested — and used by no consumer. It also can't be used the obvious way: gating render on it would blank a control during a Contentful outage, which is precisely what the fail-open design exists to prevent. Treat it as informational only.

**Silent degradation with no dev signal.** `useContext(...) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY` means "no provider," "key missing," and "network down" are indistinguishable. A misplaced consumer will render English forever with nothing in the console. A dev-only `console.warn` on a missing key would be cheap and is absent.

**Every string ships twice and nothing reconciles them.** The code literal and the Contentful entry are both authoritative-looking, and nothing checks that they agree. A CMS typo silently overrides correct code. In v2 the two long sentences went back to module-private in `zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:12-13` — right for the leaf, but it means the duplication is now visible only inside that one file.

**Two different Contentful access paths in the same component tree.** `footerConfig` goes through the official `contentful` SDK client (`useContentfulClient` — memoised, preview-token-gated, with an explicit "never fall back to delivery" contract). `uiCopy` goes through the hand-rolled raw-`fetch` hook, which has **no preview support at all**. So uiCopy is invisible to the Preview / Live Preview flow that `ContentfulLivePreviewProvider` (`_app-config:157`) sets up — an editor previewing a draft copy change will not see it. Worth confirming with Tim whether that's intended or just not reached yet.

**A registry drift that will not self-heal.** `.claude/registry/components.md:82` reports `UiCopyProvider` as `4 — Feature-local`, contradicting protectedFiles.md's Tier 2. The registry is auto-generated, so this looks like harmless staleness — but its tier column comes from a **hardcoded** mirror list at `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs:140-166` (`TIER2_PATHS`), which `542ac65` did not update. Regenerating will reproduce the wrong tier. It needs `'app/components/uiCopyProvider/'` added to that array.

**No `.docs/` requirement exists for any of this.** `grep -rl uiCopy .docs/` returns nothing. Per AGENTS.md, `.docs/` is the source of truth for requirements — yet the microcopy mechanism, its key convention, and the uiCopy-vs-react-intl decision rule live only in commit messages, code comments, and `.claude/rules/`. That's the gap most likely to make the next developer reinvent or misapply this.

Finally, a small v1 fragility now moot but illustrative: `<Footer copyrightLabel={t(...)} {...props} />` spread `props` *after* the explicit values, and `FooterContainer`'s `Omit<FooterProps, 'data'>` permitted `copyrightLabel` — so a caller-passed value would have silently beaten the CMS value. Gone with the props, but it's the sort of thing that made the prop-threading contract brittle in the first place.</result>

Two of six landed. I verified their load-bearing claims myself before passing them on — `useEffect` fetch, `if (!footerData) return null` at `footer/index.tsx:202`, no `getProps` anywhere in the footer path, no `locale` passed to Contentful. All three confirmed.

# Interim: Contentful wiring + the copy system

## The headline nobody wrote in a commit message

**The footer is no longer server-rendered.** Pre-Tim it was a static fixture, so it was in the SSR HTML. Now it's a `useEffect` fetch with `if (!footerData) return null` — so on the server `footerData` is `null` and the footer is **absent from the initial HTML entirely**, appearing only after hydration plus a client round-trip to `cdn.contentful.com`.

Two consequences on a storefront whose brief says "must be SEO-friendly": every footer link — including the whole legal set — is now JS-dependent for crawlers, and a full-height footer inserts post-hydration with no skeleton reserving space. `getProps` was available and isn't used; the codebase even references it elsewhere for exactly this reason.

## How the footer gets its content now

```
Contentful CDA
  → useContentfulClient (memoised `contentful` SDK client)
  → footer/index.tsx:183   getEntries({content_type:'footerConfig', include:3})
  → resolveByRegion.ts:52  pickMostSpecificByRegion(configs, site.id)   ← picks ONE config
  → footer/index.tsx:132   scopeToRegion → filterByRegion over navGroups[].links  ← keeps MANY
  → <Footer data={footerData}>
```

**Region-awareness is the genuinely well-built part.** Five content types now exist: a new `region` keystone (one per storefront, `siteId` unique, referenceable so nothing hardcodes a site list), plus `link`, `footerNavGroup`, `footerConfig`, `uiCopy`. Resolution is keyed on SFCC `site.id` from `useMultiSite()`, in two deliberately different stages — *most specific wins* for the root config, *inclusive filter* for links inside a shared group. Empty/absent `regions` means "all sites." Ties break on most-recently-updated with a warn. 12 unit tests including order-independence.

One modelling call worth stealing: `footerNavGroup.showContactChannels` is a **boolean, not a heading match** — because `heading` is localised, so `heading === 'Contact'` would die the moment an editor types "Kontakt."

## Four things that will bite you

**Localisation is modelled but not wired.** `subscribeHeading`, `heading`, `label`, `value` are all `localized: true`, but **no locale is ever passed** — not by the client, not by the query. So all 11 storefronts currently receive the space's default `en` for every localised field. The `uiCopy` content type's own description claims "one CDA call per locale"; the implementation makes one call with no locale. Aspirational, not descriptive.

**A Contentful blip blanks the entire footer** — Privacy Policy, Terms, Accessibility, Modern Slavery, Cookie Settings, all of it. That's a deliberate, documented choice ("so a Contentful outage doesn't silently ship stale placeholder copy"), and it satisfies the letter of graceful degradation. But the `.catch` swallows the error with **no logging and no telemetry**, so it fails silently across every page of every storefront. Made in a commit, not in a PRD — worth ratifying or reversing consciously.

**`en-CA` doesn't exist in Contentful.** Bootstrap creates 9 locales; `SUPPORTED_LOCALES` has 10. The missing one is `en-CA` — the ZimmermannUSIntl locale — while `seedRegions.mjs` cheerfully creates `region-ZimmermannUSIntl` with `locale: 'en-CA'`. Invisible today only because nothing passes a locale. It bites the moment locale-aware fetching lands.

**Your placeholder-contact problem is gone.** `contentfulFixture.ts` was *renamed* to `index.stories.content.ts` and is now imported by exactly one file — the story. The `tel:+61280808080` / `wa.me` values still exist in the repo but are no longer in the production import graph, so they don't ship. Live values come from `footerConfig` and pass through `isSafeHref` with an inert fallback.

## The copy system, and why it was built twice in one day

That's the most instructive seam in the branch.

**`useUiCopy` is now one line:** `useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY`. Provider mounted at `_app-config/index.tsx:161`, innermost — which puts it *above* the base template's `IntlProvider`, so it's available app-wide.

**Why v1 didn't hold:** the underlying fetch hook is a hand-rolled `useState`/`useEffect`/`fetch` with no cache, no dedup, no query key. Two components calling it meant **two identical network requests**. So v1's prop-drilling wasn't stylistic — threading ten props through three components was the *mitigation*, and one that only worked while exactly one caller existed. v2 shares a single fetch, which is what makes direct calls from anywhere safe. All ten props deleted.

**The load-bearing design decision:** no Provider → returns a fallback rather than throwing. Both `t` parameters are required, so `t('footer.copyright.label', 'Copyright')` always has an answer. That's why the leaves render in Storybook and Vitest with zero setup — a test was deliberately *un*-mocked because of it.

**Where it will surprise you:**

- **The 100-entry cliff.** No `limit` is passed and Contentful's CDA defaults to 100. At entry 101, keys start silently rendering English fallbacks — no error, green tests (they mock the hook, so they structurally cannot catch it). It'll present as "my CMS change didn't take effect."
- **Missing key, still loading, network down, and no provider are all indistinguishable** — same silent fallback, nothing in the console.
- **It bypasses react-intl rather than complementing it.** No locale, not in SSR (English fallback in the HTML, swaps post-hydration), and no review gate — an editor changes production copy with no PR, versus `translations/` which is Tier 2 and Integration-owned. Different risk profile entirely. Decision rule as the code actually behaves: needs editor control without a deploy → uiCopy; needs to be right in SSR HTML, vary by locale today, or interpolate a variable → react-intl.
- Keys are free-form dot-paths with **no typed union** and no check that a key in code exists in the CMS, or vice versa.

**Governance was followed through, mostly.** `components.md` gained an explicit carve-out letting Context-backed app-wide static-copy hooks be called from presentational leaves, naming `useUiCopy` as the reference. That exception is honest — the hook doesn't fetch, it's `useContext`. `uiCopyProvider/` was added to Tier 2 and CODEOWNERS. But note the carve-out does **not** cover `FooterContainer`'s own fetch sitting under `components/` — that remains acknowledged debt, flagged in its own JSDoc as something that should move to an `_app` override. Easy to conflate on a skim.

One small thing that lands on the file I just touched: `generateRegistry.mjs`'s `TIER2_PATHS` is a hardcoded mirror list that wasn't updated, so the registry reports `UiCopyProvider` as feature-local and will keep reproducing that on regeneration.

Four agents still running — architecture/decomposition, theme and token policy, governance/rules, and tests/config/dependencies. I'll synthesise across all six once they're in, including a cross-cutting pass to catch contradictions between domains rather than just stacking six reports.

**The rule actually being applied** is a two-axis decision, and only the second axis is the atomic-design one:

**Axis 1 — `footer/` or `ui-kits/`?** Does anything about the component know it's in a footer? `BottomBar` and `FooterNavColumn` stayed footer-local (`FooterNavColumn` takes a `FooterNavGroupEntry`; `BottomBar` renders the locale placeholder and copyright). `ZimmContactIconRow`, `ZimmSubscribeSection`, `ZimmSubscribeModal`, `ZimmModal` all moved to `ui-kits/` with a JSDoc line stating the reuse claim explicitly — e.g. `zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:43-45` ("Extracted from the footer so it can be reused anywhere a storefront needs the same channels — nothing here is footer-specific"), `zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:31` ("so it can be placed on any page, not just the global footer").

- **atom** = composes no other ui-kits component. `ZimmModal` renders `createPortal` + two `chakra.div`s and nothing else (`zimmModal/index.tsx:50-61`).

**Does it match `.claude/rules/components.md`?** No — and this is the biggest gap in the whole domain. Nothing in `.claude/rules/` states the `ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/` convention as a rule. `conventions.md:81-90` still documents the flat layout only:


Every mention of `ui-kits` in `.claude/rules/` is incidental — `overrideStyling.md:174` and `:213` use it as an example path for co-located styles, `testing.md:16` and `:81` cite specific files. The tier taxonomy itself is convention-by-example, enforced by nothing. Two knock-on effects:

- `conventions.md`'s file-list doesn't mention `<name>.css.ts` at all, and `zimmTextInput.css.test.ts` is a naming shape (`<name>.css.test.ts`) that appears nowhere in any rule.
- Storybook titles were **not** re-tiered. `zimmModal` and `zimmContactIconRow` are both `'Elements/…'`; the two organisms are `'Forms/…'`; the footer stays `'Layout/Footer'`. The atoms/molecules/organisms split is a filesystem fact only and is invisible in the sidebar. CODEOWNERS is the only place the layer gets a name: `CODEOWNERS` now has a `# ── TIER 3: Shared UI kit (Owner: Both Squads)` block assigning `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` to squad-a + squad-b. Note the auto-generated `.claude/registry/components.md` still records every ui-kits component as `4 — Feature-local` (lines 86-95), because it derives tier from the `protectedFiles.md`/`frozenFiles.md` path lists and `ui-kits/` is in neither.

---

# Interim: the architecture reshape

## What Tim did, in one sentence

Your 561-line `footer/index.tsx` (five components) and your 506-line `theme/components/footer.ts` (one 35-part recipe) were **split along the same seams simultaneously** — each component got its own folder, and its recipe moved to sit *beside* it as `<name>.css.ts` instead of in `theme/`.

## The decision rule he applied

Two axes, and only the second is the atomic-design one:

**Axis 1 — does it know it's a footer?** `BottomBar` and the new `FooterNavColumn` stayed in `footer/` (they touch `FooterNavGroupEntry`, copyright, locale placeholder). `ZimmContactIconRow`, `ZimmSubscribeSection`, `ZimmSubscribeModal`, `ZimmModal` moved to `ui-kits/` — each with a JSDoc line stating the reuse claim explicitly.

**Axis 2 — composition depth.** Atom composes no other ui-kit (`ZimmModal` = portal + two divs). Molecule composes atoms only (`ZimmContactIconRow` → `ZimmIcon`). Organism composes molecules and owns state (`ZimmSubscribeSection` → `ZimmInputAction` + `useSubscribeSection`).

Two components are genuinely new: **`ZimmModal`** (the portal/backdrop/dialog chrome, split out of your `SubscribeModal`) and **`FooterNavColumn`** (extracted from inline JSX in `Footer`'s `navGroups.map`). Your subscribe state machine became `useSubscribeSection`, and `useSubscribeModal` was renamed **`useZimmModal`** with `formRef` → `trapRef: RefObject<HTMLElement>`.

## Nothing broke

I'd braced for API drift and there is none: **no prop shape changed** on any extracted component, **no default↔named export flips**, and **every recipe key is unchanged** (`Button`, `ZimmNavItem`, `ZimmTextInput`). SFCC's base `_app` still imports `app/components/footer` and still gets `FooterContainer` as the default with no props. The 35→36 part count is one genuinely new part — a dedicated `error` style in coral with `role="alert"`, so failure no longer renders as success styling. That's a real improvement on my version.

## He also fixed the bug I deferred

`useZimmModal.ts:100`:

```ts
if (!(active instanceof Node) || !trapRef.current.contains(active)) {
  (e.shiftKey ? last : first).focus();
```

That's precisely the containment branch CodeRabbit raised and I deferred to HPC-035 — focus arriving from outside the focusable set no longer escapes the dialog. Tim implemented it independently. **That HPC-035 item can be closed.**

## Three things that will trip you up

**1. The app-wide `Button` recipe is now squad-owned, not designer-owned — and the rule that says otherwise is in the same branch.** Verified all four parts:

- `zimmButton.css.ts:243` — `export const Button`, the key that styles **every Chakra `<Button>` in the app**, base SFCC components included
- `:205-207` — `BTN_HEIGHT_LG = '50px'`, `BTN_HEIGHT_SM = '41px'`, `BTN_PADDING_Y = '5px'`, the provisional values pending UI-designer sign-off
- `CODEOWNERS:186` — `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts → @pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b`, placed **last** so last-match-wins overrides the Tier 2 directory rules. No designer.
- `overrideStyling.md:184-189`, still at HEAD, written 24 minutes before the move: *"Authoring an actual new token still means editing `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1) or a `theme/components/` recipe that's still designer-owned (e.g. `button.ts`'s provisional height constants, pending sign-off) — both stay behind the full gate."*

The rule's own cited example walked out from behind its own gate in the next commit. Also worth noting the oddity independent of governance: app-wide button styling now lives filed under a single atom's folder.

**2. `var(--zimm-*)` in component JSX is now mandated.** `footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44` and `:62` carry `paddingLeft: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xs)'` in an inline `__css` merge, and `9d5f89c` added a guard *requiring* it over bare Chakra keys. If your model is "CSS vars live in theme recipes, never component JSX" — that's been deliberately reversed, and the reasoning is sound: bare keys misresolve on the unregistered scales. The theme/tokens agent is still digging into whether this fixes the underlying trap or routes around it.

**3. The layering inverted.** `theme/components/index.ts` is still the single registration barrel, but it now imports *from* `app/components/**` — the theme tree depends on the components tree. No cycle today (every `.css.ts` imports only Chakra types or `footerShared`), but one component import inside a future `.css.ts` creates a real one and drags React into the theme bundle. Separately, `theme/index.ts:5-6` still instructs you to "add a new component override by creating a file in `components/`" — Tier 1, untouched, now stale.

## The convention itself is written down nowhere

`ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/` is enforced by nothing. `conventions.md:81-90` still documents only the flat `components/productTile/` layout, doesn't mention `<name>.css.ts` at all, and `zimmTextInput.css.test.ts` is a naming shape that appears in no rule. Storybook titles weren't re-tiered either — both new molecules/atoms sit under `Elements/`, organisms under `Forms/` — so the tier split is a filesystem fact invisible in the sidebar. **After** — `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:16`:
> 2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`, `bg="var(--zimm-color-bg-02)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never** a bare Chakra/theme token string (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) — even though `theme.colors`/`theme.space` ARE registered from the same Zimmermann foundations [...] and a bare key resolves to the identical value. This is a house-style requirement, not a correctness one [...]

Mirrored in `.claude/rules/css.md:17-26`, where the example block went from:

to:

**Before** — `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`:

**After** — `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md:44`:

> A co-located `<name>.css.ts` is **not** governed by this section's Tier 2 UI-designer gate — CODEOWNERS' `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` rule routes it to the owning squad(s) only.

## 4. What a developer must do differently on Monday

1. **Stop writing `color="text.default"` / `gap="m"` / `padding="m"`.** Use `var(--zimm-color-*)` and `var(--zimm-scale-*)` instead, in both recipes and JSX/`sx` props. `npm run test` will fail you inside a registered recipe; in JSX nothing catches it, so it's on you and your reviewer.
2. **`textStyle` is the one exception** — keep using `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
3. **New component styling goes in a co-located `<name>.css.ts`**, not `theme/components/`. Register it in `theme/components/index.ts` regardless of where the file lives.
4. **Cross-file shared style values go in a shared module that stays in `theme/components/`** (the `footerShared.ts` precedent) — do not copy a literal into two co-located files.
5. **Run `npm run audit:tokens` before opening any PR touching `overrides/app/components/**` or `overrides/app/theme/components/**`.** It is not in CI. If a raw value is genuinely unavoidable, put `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or `audit-allow: <reason>` in the surrounding comment block — that's the documented downgrade vocabulary.
6. **Every logic-heavy component needs its own `index.test.ts(x)` in its own folder.** A `play` function — yours or a parent's — no longer satisfies the check. Mock the hook/child whose internals are already proven, and assert only your own render-branch/event-wiring contract.
7. **Mock `ZimmIcon` in any test that renders an icon-consuming component**, using the `vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', …)` form. Do not try to fix it in `vitest.config.ts` — that's Tier 1.
8. **You may call `useUiCopy()` / `useIntl()` from a leaf component.** Any other data-fetching hook still belongs in a page or container.
9. **Contentful schema changes are now two commands**: `npm run sync:contentful` then `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` for each environment in the chain. You now also need `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID` locally (`npm run env -- init`).
10. **Touching `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/` is now a Tier 2 change** requiring a second reviewer.

## 7. Surprising, and what it means for trusting the local suite

**`npm run lint` and `npx tsc --noEmit` are gated absolutely nowhere.** `qa.yml`'s only jobs are `detect-changes`, `unit-tests`, `storybook-test`, `e2e-localhost`, `e2e-browserstack`. Grepping all workflows for `run lint` / `eslint` / `tsc --noEmit` / `prettier` returns exactly one hit, and it's prose inside `upstream-release-watch.yml`'s issue template. So lint being red — 15 errors before this branch, 19 now — has never blocked a merge and won't. If you want the 4 new ones fixed, that has to happen by review, not by CI.

**Vitest has no SVG handling, and this branch is the first thing to hit it.** `vitest.config.ts` sets up only `jsdom` + the `app`/`~` aliases. `.storybook/main.js:47-65` explicitly strips Storybook's default SVG rule and installs `ignore-loader` for SFCC SVGs plus `asset/resource` for project SVGs. Vitest has neither, so an SVG import resolves to a string, and `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons/index.jsx:79` — `AmexSymbol.viewBox = AmexSymbol.viewBox || '0 0 38 22'` — throws on assignment to a string primitive under ESM strict mode. Tim's diagnosis is exactly right. Consequence: **every future Vitest test that renders anything transitively importing `ZimmIcon` now needs a `vi.mock`**, and there are already three such mocks. The proper fix is one alias or stub plugin in `vitest.config.ts`, which is Tier 1 — you're a tier-1-approver, so this is a cheap, high-leverage unblock that removes a growing boilerplate tax. Worth noting the mock target `'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon'` correctly intercepts importers that use relative specifiers (`'../zimmIcon'` in `zimmButton`/`zimmTextInput`), because Vitest keys mocks on resolved module ID.
