1	# Styling an Override Component
2	
3	How to style a component under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/theme/`.
4	Cross-references [overrides.md](./overrides.md) (module-replacement correctness — a
5	different concern: that file is about not breaking SFCC's own imports, this one is
6	about what values to reach for once the component compiles). Day-to-day CSS/token
7	rules live in [css.md](./css.md); this file is the practical "what do I actually type"
8	companion.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## The hierarchy — reach for these in order
13	
14	1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
15	   All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
16	2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`,
17	   `bg="var(--zimm-color-bg-02)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never** a bare Chakra/theme
18	   token string (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) — even though `theme.colors`/`theme.space`
19	   ARE registered from the same Zimmermann foundations (see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment on
20	   which scales are and aren't registered) and a bare key resolves to the identical value. This
21	   is a house-style requirement, not a correctness one: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is
22	   unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check
23	   `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. Mechanically
24	   enforced across every recipe file by `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s "no
25	   override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale" test — it walks the
26	   registered recipe map only, so it cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop (see
27	   that test's SCOPE note); apply the same discipline there by hand.
28	3. **A component's own theme config** — either centralized (`theme/components/<name>.ts`)
29	   or, per the co-location pattern below, beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — for
30	   anything that needs to vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop — see
31	   "Component-local tokens" and "Co-locating a component's theme file" below. For an
32	   interactive component with existing Chakra support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme
33	   config is the single source of truth — see "One canonical styling surface per component
34	   type" below.
35	4. **`sx` prop** for a one-off Chakra-prop-system gap, per [css.md](./css.md).
36	5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors,
37	   keyframes) — same file, same rules as [css.md](./css.md) already documents.
38	
39	**Never**: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token
40	instead. The one standing exception is `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional height/padding
41	constants (`BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`), pending UI-designer
42	sign-off — see Units below. Run `npm run audit:tokens` (`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`)
43	before opening a PR that touches `overrides/app/components/**` or
44	`overrides/app/theme/components/**` — it greps for exactly this, scoped to those two paths
45	(`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.scss`, excluding `*.test.ts(x)` and `*.stories.tsx`). A match is downgraded
46	from a failure to an acknowledged exception when the surrounding comment block already
47	contains `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or an explicit `audit-allow: <reason>` —
48	the exact vocabulary this codebase already uses for its documented raw-value exceptions, so
49	existing well-commented code doesn't need a second, separately-maintained allow-list. Built
50	2026-08-23 — it is not wired into CI yet, deliberately: someone still needs to own triaging a
51	full run's worth of pre-existing findings first (a first run against this repo surfaced 14
52	genuine pre-existing violations, none touched by that session, all outside its scope to fix).
53	Note this is a *different, broader* check than `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token-key guard
54	mentioned above: that one exists and runs today (`npm run test`), but only catches a bare
55	Chakra key standing in for a zimm var — it says nothing about a raw hex/px/rem/em literal,
56	which is what `audit:tokens` is for.
57	
58	## Units
59	
60	- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with the user's root font-size / browser zoom
61	  (WCAG 1.4.4): type (`fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`) and spacing
62	  (`spacing.ts`'s named scale). Letter-spacing values that were specified as sub-pixel px
63	  in the source don't round to clean rem numbers, so those keep a trailing `// -0.12px`
64	  comment for traceability.
65	- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should _not_ scale: border widths, focus-ring
66	  offsets, and (for now) the provisional button-height constants in `zimmButton.css.ts` that are
67	  still pending UI-designer sign-off against Handover.
68	- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts` — deliberate, so `.zimm-grid`'s media
69	  queries shift with zoom the same way Chakra's responsive props do) and other
70	  genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.
71	
72	## The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy
73	
74	`theme/foundation/colour.ts`'s primitive tier (`grey`, `ivory`, ...) is defined first as
75	plain `const`s, and the semantic/alias tier below it (`text`, `background`, `border`,
76	...) reads from those consts (`text.default: grey[900]`) instead of retyping the hex
77	value. Do the same for any new primitive/alias pair you add — two values can't disagree
78	if only one of them is ever typed.
79	
80	`zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry for `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*`
81	classes) is fully derived the same way — it imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/
82	`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid`
83	from their owning files rather than retyping values. The only literals left are the 7
84	numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with no named-scale equivalent (`025`, `700`, `1100`,
85	`1200`, `1300`, `3500`, `4500`) — not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to
86	derive them from. `theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision-guard tests still exist as a
87	regression net; treat a failure there as a real drift signal, not test noise.
88	
89	## One canonical styling surface per component type
90	
91	Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its
92	`theme/components/<name>.ts` config, consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
93	`<Link>` variant, etc.). Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in
94	`globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
95	`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class "mirror" is
96	structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing
97	with the real theme config over time. `zimmButton.css.ts` (co-located at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/`) is the single source of truth for
98	button styling; `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*` classes — use Chakra's `<Button>`
99	for any button, not a class.
100	
101	`.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool for genuinely static, non-interactive,
102	massively-reused treatments (typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout) where
103	there's no interactive state to lose.
104	
105	## Importing an already-overridden component from a new component
106	
107	If component A (e.g. `productDetailOptions`) uses component B, and B already has an
108	override (e.g. `swatch-group`), **import B via a relative path

Both fixes are in; build and unit tests running. While they go, here's what changed and one correction I owe you.

## Fix 1 — `overrideStyling.md`

Tier 1 file, named explicitly: `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`. `gh api user` → `marcelannavarro`, confirmed in `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` alongside `hanl` and `TimLavelleACC`, so I proceeded under the documented exception.

The "Component-local tokens" section now teaches `marginBottom: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)'`, says plainly that the bare-key form it used to recommend is now forbidden and **fails `npm run test`** via the bare-token guard, and cites two files that actually exist (`footer.css.ts`, `bottomBar.css.ts`) instead of `imageGallery.ts`/`swatchGroup.ts`, which don't.

I also found the responsive advice was stale in a way I hadn't reported: it recommended Chakra's array shorthand `['2xs', '2xs', 'xs', 'xs']`, which is *also* bare keys at every step. Live recipes use explicit media queries keyed off `BP` in `footerShared.ts`. That's now documented.

**Scope note:** the file had **six** references to `button.ts`, which no longer exists. I corrected five as mechanical path fixes to `zimmButton.css.ts`. I deliberately left **line 199** alone — it claims `button.ts`'s constants "stay behind the full gate," which is no longer true, and rewriting it means making a governance statement rather than fixing a path. That's the gate-sequencing question, and it's yours to decide.

## Fix 2 — the story tests, and I had the cause wrong

I told you the modal failure was a portal-vs-`canvasElement` conflict that made `testing.md`'s rule unfollowable. **That was wrong.** The play function already queries `within(document.body)` — the scope was never the problem. The real cause: `useZimmModal` starts `mounted: false` (`:38`), `ZimmModal` returns null until it flips (`:48`), so the portal contents don't exist on the first synchronous pass. `getByRole` threw before the effect ran. Changed to `await findByRole`, which retries.

So there's no rule conflict to resolve, and the decision I asked you for isn't needed. Good news, but I should have read the play function before diagnosing it.

The contrast fix: added a decorator wrapping the story in `var(--zimm-color-bg-05)` — the background the organism actually renders on in the footer. The `backgrounds` parameter only paints the preview canvas, so axe was walking up to the default white. Now it measures the real context, where `#969696` is 5.94:1 and passes. This makes the story truthful rather than suppressing the check.

Nothing committed. I'll report the full suite — `tsc`, vitest, `build-storybook`, and `test-storybook` against a verified server — before we go anywhere near a commit.

## One canonical styling surface per component type

Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its
`theme/components/<name>.ts` config, consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
`<Link>` variant, etc.). Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in
`globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class "mirror" is
structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing
with the real theme config over time. `zimmButton.css.ts` (co-located at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/`) is the single source of truth for
button styling; `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*` classes — use Chakra's `<Button>`
for any button, not a class.

# Verdict: Fix 1 = **OK** · Fix 2 = **RISKY**

Both fixes work and neither masks a defect. Fix 2's *mechanism* is sound and load-bearing, but three factual claims in its comment are wrong and it leaves a dead parameter in place.

## Best attempt to break Fix 1 (modal) — failed, fix survives

**M1 (control).** In my own built bundle I reverted *only* `findByRole("dialog"` → `getByRole("dialog"`. It reproduced the reported error verbatim, and the accessible-roles dump listed **only the three Chakra toast `region`s** — the entire portal subtree absent, exactly as `return null` predicts. Not a partially-rendered dialog, not an `isOpen` wiring bug (`isOpen` starts `true`).

**Diagnosis verified at source, not guessed.** `useZimmModal.ts:38-45` has `useState(false)` + `useEffect(() => setMounted(true), [])`; `zimmModal/index.tsx:48` has `if (!mounted || !isOpen) return null`. The missing link the author didn't state: `node_modules/@storybook/react-dom-shim/dist/react-18.js` resolves its render promise from a **`useLayoutEffect`** (`WithCallback`), which runs *before* React's passive effects — so `play` begins before `setMounted(true)` flushes. `getByRole` never had a chance.

**Not a masked defect.** The `mounted` gate is deliberate SSR protection (`createPortal(…, document.body)` would throw server-side), documented in `ZimmModalProps`, and independently covered by `overrides/app/hooks/useZimmModal.test.tsx` (focus entry, Tab-trap wrap past disabled controls, scroll-lock restore). One extra render for a portal is the standard pattern.

**Not waiting out a slow defect.** Passing `play-test` = **97 ms**; a real `findBy*` timeout = **1064 ms**. It resolves on the next tick.

**Not vacuous** (attack 2). M2 `findByRole('tablist')` → FAIL at 1064 ms. M3 heading name `/definitely not here/i` → FAIL at 1073 ms. `findBy*` rejects on absence; `toBeInTheDocument()` never receives a falsy value.

**Coverage identical** — same 3 assertions, same roles/names. `within(document.body)` predates the change (required for the portal).

## Best attempt to break Fix 2 (section) — mechanism survives, comment does not

**Contrast verified independently**, then cross-checked against axe. From `overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts`: `background['05'] = grey[900] = #191919`, `text.inverseGrey = grey[300] = #969696`. → **2.9578** on white (axe floors to **2.95** ✓) and **5.9441** on `#191919` (**5.94** ✓). Both quoted figures are correct; 12px/500 isn't WCAG "large text", so 4.5:1 applies.

**It measures the true context, not just satisfying the check.** M4 (`var(--zimm-color-bg-05)` → `transparent`) reproduced the exact violation on all 3 stories. M5 (→ `#7a7a7a`, a background that *exists* but is wrong) returned **1.45** for the heading and **4.29** for the white body text — both matching my hand-computed values. Axe genuinely recomputes from the rendered colour.

**Premise holds** (attack 4). `footer.css.ts:25` sets `backgroundColor: 'var(--zimm-color-bg-05)'` on the **`container`** part — the only background in the chain `container > main > contentRow > subscribe > ZimmSubscribeSection` (`footer/index.tsx:79-83`). The real footer assembly story passes a11y. `ZimmSubscribeSection` has exactly one consumer, and its recipe hard-codes inverse colours with no light variant — so suppressing the isolated-mount white reading is legitimate.

### What the author didn't state

1. **Wrong element.** The comment blames "the body copy (`--zimm-color-text-inverse-grey`, #969696)". Axe's node dump is `<p class="css-91dibt">Keep in touch</p>` — the **`heading`** part. The **body** is `--zimm-color-text-inverse` = **#ffffff** (`zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts:21`); in-browser computed: heading `rgb(150,150,150)`, body `rgb(255,255,255)`.
2. **Wrong part.** "Mirrors footer.css.ts's `main` part" — `main` sets only `display:flex; flexDirection:column`, no background. It's `container`.
3. **`parameters: {backgrounds: {default: 'dark'}}` is a dead no-op in Storybook 10.** `withBackgroundAndGrid` reads the selection from **`globals.backgrounds.value`** only (`initialGlobals = {backgrounds:{value: undefined}}`); no shim reads `parameters…default`. Confirmed in-browser: `.sb-show-main` = `rgb(255,255,255)`, `#addon-backgrounds-color` **absent**. So the comment's first clause is wrong (it paints *nothing*) — the fix is more necessary than stated. That line should become `globals: {backgrounds: {value: 'dark'}}` or be deleted.
4. **Fix 2 silently fixed a bug nobody logged.** Pre-fix, the white body copy and white input were **invisible** (white on white, 1:1) — and axe did *not* flag them (M4 reported only the 3 heading violations). The a11y gate was under-reporting.
5. **Visual (attack 5).** With `layout:'centered'` plus the dead `backgrounds` param, the story is a shrink-wrapped dark box on a **white** canvas, width varying per story (**264 px** Default vs **479 px** Subscribed). The footer renders a full-bleed dark band with the column capped at 320 px. Padding `--zimm-scale-2xl` (32 px) is token-based and matches the footer's *horizontal* `contentRow` padding, not its vertical (48 px mobile). Defensible, not arbitrary — but "mirrors" oversells it. Colours are faithful, so a designer isn't misled about the component itself.

**Coverage not reduced** (attack 6) — nothing removed in either file; M4/M5 prove the a11y gate still has teeth.

| `npx tsc --noEmit` | **exit 0**, 0 errors |
| `npx vitest run` | **exit 0**, 16 files / **252 tests** passed |
| `npm run build-storybook` | **exit 0** (pre-existing webpack warning: `main` 1.28 MiB > 244 KiB) |
| `test-storybook` (full, canonical) | **exit 0**, 16 suites / **83 tests** passed |
| Both files under review | **PASS in every one of 6 runs** |

Provenance: built to `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/adv-verify/sb-static`, served on **7412** (self-picked, verified free). `iframe.html` md5 `7f65ea88…` matched served output every run, and is **distinct** from the repo's stale `storybook-static/` (`8826062c…`) and from the other session's `storybook dev` on 6006 (PID 21958, untouched). All mutations were applied to my own built chunks and md5-restored to pristine; repo working tree is byte-identical to session start.

## One unrelated pre-existing issue found

`overrides/app/components/footer/index.stories.tsx` → `SubscribePlaceholder` is **not flaky, it's webfont-timing-sensitive**. Its no-layout-shift assertion (`index.stories.tsx:260`) fails `expected 490 to be 491` — **5/5 with HTTP caching off, 0/3 with caching on**. Cold-fetching Futura Round per navigation shifts the footer 1 px; the story's 1-dp rounding only absorbs sub-pixel jitter, not a whole pixel. Unmodified at HEAD and provably independent of both fixes (a footer-only run never loads either reviewed chunk). Worth a ticket — CI's pass/fail here depends on the test-runner's static-server cache headers.

### Recommended before merge (all cosmetic, none blocking)
- Fix the comment: `heading`, not "body copy"; `container`, not `main`.
- Replace or drop the dead `parameters: {backgrounds: {default: 'dark'}}`.</result>

content.text:
Suite running. Where the loop stands:

## Both verifiers reported — neither was a clean green light

**Fix 1 (modal) — OK, and it survived a real attack.** Verifier B reverted only `findByRole`→`getByRole` in its own bundle and reproduced the error verbatim, with the accessible-roles dump showing the entire portal subtree absent. It also found the mechanism I'd missed: `@storybook/react-dom-shim` resolves its render promise from a `useLayoutEffect`, which runs *before* React's passive effects — so `play` starts before `setMounted(true)` flushes. Not vacuous either: absent roles fail at ~1064ms against a 97ms pass.

**Fix 2 (contrast) — mechanism sound, my comment wrong on three counts.** All three now corrected:

- I blamed **body copy**; axe was flagging the **heading**. The body is `--zimm-color-text-inverse` = `#ffffff`.
- I said it mirrors footer's **`main`** part; `main` has no background at all — it's **`container`** (`footer.css.ts:25`).
- I said the `backgrounds` parameter "paints the preview canvas." **It paints nothing** — Storybook 10 reads `globals.backgrounds.value`, and nothing reads `parameters…default`. So it was a silent no-op, and the fix was *more* necessary than I described. Replaced with the working `globals` form.

It also caught something the fix did that I hadn't noticed: pre-fix, the white body copy and white input were **invisible** — white on white at 1:1 — and **axe didn't flag them at all.** So the a11y gate was under-reporting, not just misreporting.

## One unrelated find worth a ticket

`footer/index.stories.tsx`'s `SubscribePlaceholder` isn't flaky — it's **webfont-timing-sensitive**. Its no-layout-shift assertion fails `expected 490 to be 491` five out of five times with HTTP caching off, and passes with caching on: cold-fetching Futura Round per navigation shifts the footer by a whole pixel, which the 1-dp rounding doesn't absorb. Unmodified at HEAD, provably independent of both fixes — but it means CI's result on that story depends on the test-runner's static-server cache headers. That's a latent flake in a required check.

## Still owed before I commit

Verifier A ran *before* my five doc corrections, so those are unverified — and A's whole value was catching claims I'd made without checking. I'll send it back over just the changed passages once this suite lands. Then commit, push, and watch the run.

YOUR FOUR FINDINGS:
- **#1** id `3841007218` — `.env.sample:139` — "Place the scope marker directly above the variable."
- **#12** id `3841007282` (**Major**) — `scripts/contentful/setup/bootstrapSpace.mjs:129` — "Reconcile existing locales before skipping them."
- **#13** id `3841007291` (**Major**) — `scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs:129` — "Keep the validation gate closed for unresolved findings."
- **#14** id `3841007294` — `scripts/contentful/setup/seedRegions.mjs:42` — "Provision `en-CA` or normalise `ZimmermannUSIntl` to a provisioned locale."

CONSTRAINTS:
- **READ-ONLY, and this is important here.** These scripts talk to a live Contentful space via the Management API. Do **NOT** run any of them — not `sync:contentful`, `install:contentful`, `seed:contentful-regions`, or `bootstrapSpace.mjs`, and not with any `--dry-run` flag either. Read the source only. Do not edit, stage, commit, stash, or checkout anything; two other agent sessions are writing to this tree.
- You may read `.env.sample` but do NOT read or print the contents of `.env`, `.env.shared`, or any `.env.<tier>` file — they hold real credentials.

KEY CONTEXT:

**#14 is very likely correct and I want it confirmed rigorously.** The claim is that `seedRegions.mjs` creates a `region` entry for `ZimmermannUSIntl` carrying `locale: 'en-CA'`, while `bootstrapSpace.mjs` never provisions an `en-CA` locale in the Contentful space. Verify both halves independently: list exactly which locales `bootstrapSpace.mjs` creates, and exactly which locale values `seedRegions.mjs` writes. Then cross-check against `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.generated.ts`'s `SUPPORTED_LOCALES` and `SITE_LOCALES`. Report the precise mismatch. Also determine the actual runtime impact: does anything currently pass a locale to Contentful at fetch time? (Check `overrides/app/hooks/useContentfulClient.ts` and `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx`.) That decides whether this is live breakage or latent.

**#13 is about a safety gate.** `installTemplate.mjs` validates before installing and has `--force` / `--takeover` escape hatches, plus a `--delete-deleted-fields` flag. Read the validation logic carefully and determine whether unresolved validation findings can currently slip through and reach an install. `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` documents this pipeline as additive-only-by-default — check whether the code matches that documentation.

**#12** — `bootstrapSpace.mjs` skips locales that already exist. Determine what "reconcile" would mean concretely and whether skipping can leave a space in a wrong state (e.g. a locale present but with wrong fallback, or not enabled for CDA).

**#1** — `.env.sample` scope-marker placement. `AGENTS.md` documents the exact convention: the `# scope:...` tag goes "on its own comment line above the key". Check what line 139 actually looks like and whether it violates that. Note AGENTS.md also warns a blank placeholder value can read as non-empty to the pre-commit secret guard — check `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` for how it parses, since that determines whether this is cosmetic or functional.

FOR EACH FINDING REPORT:
- **CLAIM TRUE / FALSE / PARTLY** — with evidence from the source
- **FIX / DECLINE / DEFER** — recommendation
- **If FIX**: the exact change, and critically — is it safe to apply without running against a live Contentful space, or does it need coordinated CMS work?
- **If DECLINE**: the quotable rule/doc/code justification
- **Blast radius**: would getting this wrong affect the live dev Contentful space or only local tooling?

Be terse and concrete. Lead with #14 and #13.

# #10 — `resolveByRegion.ts:70-78` — **CLAIM TRUE** → **FIX**

The only finding that's fully correct. Empirically confirmed all three sub-claims (`npx vitest run` on a copy in `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/tie.test.ts`, 4/4 pass):

| Input | Result | Warning |
|---|---|---|
| `[a, b]` equal `updatedAt` | `a` | **0** |
| `[b, a]` equal `updatedAt` | `b` ← **order-dependent** | **0** |
| `[a, b]` / `[b, a]` absent `updatedAt` | `a` / `b` ← **order-dependent** | **0** |
| `[newer, older]` distinct | `newer` (correct) | **0** ← asymmetric |
| `[older, newer]` distinct | `newer` (correct) | 1 |

Cause: the warn + reassign both sit inside `if (candidateUpdatedAt > bestUpdatedAt)`, so a strict-greater-than can never fire when the values are equal, and never fires when the array already arrives newest-first.

**The existing order-independence test is not vacuous, but it is misnamed and mis-scoped.** `resolveByRegion.test.ts:84` ("order of the tied candidates in the input does not change the outcome") only uses *distinct* timestamps — the one case that genuinely is order-independent. It never covers equal/absent. And it deliberately omits the `console.warn` assertion its sibling at :77 makes, which is exactly what hides the asymmetry.

Also worth noting: the source's own JSDoc at :46-50 is falsified — "a console.warn surfaces it so the duplicate entry can be cleaned up" is untrue in half the orderings, which defeats the stated purpose (surfacing an editorial mistake for cleanup).

**Fix** — hoist the warn out of the comparison, add `sys.id` as a stable secondary key:
```ts
if (candidateSpecificity === bestSpecificity) {
  console.warn(`resolveByRegion: tie between two equally-scoped entries for region "${siteId}" — resolving by most-recently-updated.`);
  const bestUpdatedAt = best.sys?.updatedAt ?? '';
  const candidateUpdatedAt = candidate.sys?.updatedAt ?? '';
  const bestId = String(best.sys?.id ?? '');
  const candidateId = String(candidate.sys?.id ?? '');
  if (candidateUpdatedAt > bestUpdatedAt || (candidateUpdatedAt === bestUpdatedAt && candidateId < bestId)) {
    best = candidate;
  }
}
```
Caveat: `sys.id` is `unknown` under the `[key: string]: unknown` index signature at `resolveByRegion.ts:18`, so it needs `String(...)` or a narrow guard — not a bare `<`.

**Safe?** Yes — behaviour for distinct timestamps is unchanged, so existing tests at :77 and :84 still pass. **Effort:** ~6 lines in source, ~3 new tests, plus rename/scope the :84 test. Re-test required (`npx vitest run overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.test.ts`).

**Real-world severity is genuinely Minor** — real CDA entries always carry `updatedAt`, so the equal case needs a same-millisecond bulk publish. The doc-falsification is the stronger reason to fix.

---

# #9 — `theme/fontFace.tsx` — **CLAIM FALSE** → **DECLINE**

CodeRabbit cites a rule that **does not exist in this repo**. `grep -rni "kebab" coderabbit.yaml .coderabbit/ .claude/` returns only the two entries below and an unrelated Contentful skill line. The repo's actual rule, `.claude/rules/conventions.md` § File naming and folder structure:

> - **Zimmermann-authored files and folders:** `camelCase` (e.g. `productTile.tsx`, `useWishlist.ts`, `formatPrice.ts`).
> - **Override files (mirroring a base Salesforce file):** keep the original kebab-case filename and folder name exactly (e.g. `product-tile.tsx`).

`fontFace.tsx` is squarely in the first category:
- **No base SFCC equivalent exists.** `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/theme/` contains only `components/`, `foundations/`, `index.js`. `grep -rl "font-face\|@font-face\|fontFace" node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` → **zero hits**.
- Sibling precedent is unanimous camelCase for Zimmermann-authored theme files: `zimmTokensGlobal.tsx`, `globalStyles.ts`, and every file in `foundation/` (`colour.ts`, `gridSystem.ts`, `spacing.ts`, `zimmTokens.ts`) — note the folder is `foundation/` (singular), deliberately *not* mirroring base SFCC's `foundations/`.

**Additional decline reason: the rename would force a Tier 1 edit.** `.storybook/preview.tsx:7` imports `'../overrides/app/theme/fontFace'`. `.storybook/` is Tier 1 (`frozenFiles.md` § Test & Tooling Config; AGENTS.md Hard Rule #8: *"Never modify test configuration files (`vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, `.storybook/`...)"*). So satisfying a non-existent rule would require breaching a real one.

**Effort if declined:** 0. Reply on-thread citing conventions.md § File naming + the absence of a base SFCC `font-face` module — this is exactly the "conflicts with this repo's own rules" case AGENTS.md says to explain in-thread so CodeRabbit's learning stops re-flagging camelCase in `overrides/`.

# #6 — `zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts:22,35` — **CLAIM FALSE** → **DECLINE**

Both literals are **already covered by the documented exception vocabulary**, and the tooling confirms it. `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` output:

```
✓ 16 raw value(s) with an acknowledged exception (not failing):
  ...zimmSubscribeSection/zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts:22  '12.5rem'
  ...zimmSubscribeSection/zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts:35  '2.8125rem'
```

They land in the acknowledged bucket, not the 14 failures. `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`:

> A match is downgraded from a failure to an acknowledged exception when the surrounding comment block already contains `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or an explicit `audit-allow: <reason>` — the exact vocabulary this codebase already uses for its documented raw-value exceptions

Line 22's comment reads `provisional, pending a foundation/sizes.ts entry`; line 35's block reads `PROVISIONAL: ... Pending Kiera.` (matched case-insensitively by `EXCEPTION_MARKER_RE`).

Extracting them to named constants would also be a **net loss of traceability** — the current inline comments carry the Figma node IDs (`4019:46044`), the pixel derivation (36+4+4+1=45px), the token conflict (`actionSizes.height` offers only 52/40), and the named owner. A `const SUBSCRIBE_BODY_MAX_WIDTH` at the top of the file separates the value from that provenance. The script's own header (`auditTokenUsage.mjs:19-26`) explicitly cites this file as a calibration case for reading the explanatory comment *as* the allow-list entry.

# #7 — `uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:19` — **CLAIM PARTLY TRUE** → **FIX, but not CodeRabbit's fix**

The magic-string claim holds against `.claude/rules/conventions.md`: *"No magic numbers or strings. Any literal value with semantic meaning ... must be a named constant ... or live in a config/enum module."*

But **CodeRabbit missed that the canonical constant already exists**. `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts:53-59`:
```ts
export const CONTENT_TYPE_IDS = {
  region: 'region',
  link: 'link',
  footerNavGroup: 'footerNavGroup',
  footerConfig: 'footerConfig',
  uiCopy: 'uiCopy',
} as const;
```
`grep -rn "CONTENT_TYPE_IDS"` shows **zero consumers** — it's a config module with no first caller. Adding a *second*, file-local `UI_COPY_CONTENT_TYPE` const would create exactly the two-sources-of-truth drift the rule exists to prevent (and that `overrideStyling.md` § "The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy" warns about).

**Fix instead:**
```ts
import { CONTENT_TYPE_IDS } from 'app/config/contentfulMapping';
...
const { data, isLoading } = useContentfulEntries<UiCopyEntry>(CONTENT_TYPE_IDS.uiCopy);
```

**Safe?** Mostly — one caveat: `contentfulMapping.ts:15` imports `./contentfulMapping.generated`, pulling `SUPPORTED_LOCALES`/`SITE_LOCALES` into whatever bundle `_app-config` lands in. Small, but confirm it doesn't move the `main.js` ≤ 180 kB budget. `contentfulMapping.ts` is **not** Tier 1 (only `config/countries.ts` and `config/contentful.ts` are, per `frozenFiles.md:81-82` and `CODEOWNERS:47-48`), so the import is unrestricted. `uiCopyProvider/` is Tier 2 (Global Shell) — already under PR review.

**Adjacent, out of scope:** `pages/home/index.tsx:148` has the same magic string (`'homepage'`), and `'homepage'` isn't even in `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS`. Don't fix in this PR (Hard Rule #5, no refactoring upward).

**Effort:** 2 lines. Re-test: `npx vitest run overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/` (the test at `index.test.tsx:19` mocks `useContentfulEntries` and doesn't assert the argument, so it should be unaffected).

# #3 — `zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:51-53` — **CLAIM PARTLY TRUE** → **DEFER**

**The architectural half is fine — `.claude/rules/components.md` explicitly permits it:**
> **Exception — Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks** (`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) may be called from any component, **including presentational leaves**. ... `BottomBar` and `ZimmSubscribeSection` both call it directly for microcopy while still receiving their actual business data as props.

So there's no rule objection to calling `useUiCopy` from this molecule.

**But CodeRabbit's stated rationale is empirically false.** The claim is: *"This footer ships to eight storefronts, so screen reader users on a non-English storefront hear English channel names."* Routing through `useUiCopy` **does not fix that today**. `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts:110`:

```
`${baseUrl}/spaces/${spaceId}/environments/${environment}/entries?content_type=${contentType}&access_token=${token}&include=2`
```

No `&locale=` — `grep -n "locale" overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` → **zero hits**. The CDA returns the space default locale (`en`) for every storefront. The `uiCopy` content type *models* localisation correctly (`scripts/contentful/content-types/uiCopy.js`: `value` is `localized: true`), but the fetch never asks for a locale. So the change would relocate the English hardcoding into Contentful and still serve `en` to all 8 sites — same a11y outcome, more indirection.

Secondary corrections: these are **screen-reader-only `aria-label`s**, not visible copy (the anchor's only child is `<ZimmIcon aria-hidden>`), so the user-visible blast radius is nil. And `useUiCopy` has no key for any of them — existing keys are `footer.copyright.label`, `footer.subscribe.{emailLabel,buttonLabel,successMessage,unavailableMessage}` — so three new Contentful entries would need seeding.

CodeRabbit's note that `NEW_TAB_SUFFIX:40` needs the same treatment is correct and inherits the same defect.

**Recommendation: DEFER**, and reply on-thread that the prerequisite is a `locale` param on `useContentfulEntries` — otherwise this is motion without localisation. Same latent gap already applies to `BottomBar` and `ZimmSubscribeSection`, so it's a systemic follow-up, not a this-component fix.

If the team wants it anyway for consistency: ~5 lines, safe. `useUiCopy` degrades to the fallback literal with no Provider, so `footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx:78,80,86,87` (asserting `'Call us'` / `'Email us'`) and both `play` functions asserting `/opens in a new tab/i` keep passing untouched.

# #11 — `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs:94` — **CLAIM FALSE** → **DECLINE**

CodeRabbit's exact stated scenario does not reproduce. Ran its example through the real `stripComments`:

```
"  <a href=\"https://example.test\" padding=\"16px\" />"
  -> stripped: "  <a href=\"https://example.test\" padding=\"16px\" />"
  -> units found: ["16px"]     ← NOT truncated; 16px IS reported
```

The reasoning error: for the *second* slash in `https://` to be read as a comment start, the guard needs `line[i] === '/' && line[i+1] === '/'`. At the second slash, `line[i+1]` is `e` (the first host character), so the `//` test fails and the character is simply appended. The guard only has to survive one slash, and it does.

**CodeRabbit's proposed fix is a no-op for its own example** — its `isUrlSlash` only changes behaviour when three consecutive slashes follow a colon (`https:///`), a case that doesn't occur.

Genuine comment-stripping behaviour is intact:
```
"  const x = 'https://wa.me/61400000000'; // padding 16px in a comment"
  -> stripped: "  const x = 'https://wa.me/61400000000'; "   ← URL kept, comment dropped
"  margin: '8px', // https://figma.com/file 12px"
  -> units found: ["8px"]                                     ← 12px correctly ignored
```

**One real but different defect I did find** (CodeRabbit did not identify it): a **protocol-relative** URL truncates the line — `href="//example.test" padding="16px"` strips to `  <a href="` and loses the `16px`. Low value to fix: it's a false *negative* in a non-CI advisory script, and `isSafeHref` (`zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:62`) explicitly rejects protocol-relative hrefs, so such a literal shouldn't exist in a scanned file. Not worth a change in this PR.

**Effort if declined:** 0. Reply on-thread with the trace above — the claim is a reasoning error about `line[i+1]`, not a repo-convention disagreement, so the correction is worth stating precisely.

# #10 — `resolveByRegion.ts:70-78` — **CLAIM TRUE** → **FIX**

The only finding that's fully correct. Empirically confirmed all three sub-claims (`npx vitest run` on a copy in `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/tie.test.ts`, 4/4 pass):

| Input | Result | Warning |
|---|---|---|
| `[a, b]` equal `updatedAt` | `a` | **0** |
| `[b, a]` equal `updatedAt` | `b` ← **order-dependent** | **0** |
| `[a, b]` / `[b, a]` absent `updatedAt` | `a` / `b` ← **order-dependent** | **0** |
| `[newer, older]` distinct | `newer` (correct) | **0** ← asymmetric |
| `[older, newer]` distinct | `newer` (correct) | 1 |

Cause: the warn + reassign both sit inside `if (candidateUpdatedAt > bestUpdatedAt)`, so a strict-greater-than can never fire when the values are equal, and never fires when the array already arrives newest-first.

**The existing order-independence test is not vacuous, but it is misnamed and mis-scoped.** `resolveByRegion.test.ts:84` ("order of the tied candidates in the input does not change the outcome") only uses *distinct* timestamps — the one case that genuinely is order-independent. It never covers equal/absent. And it deliberately omits the `console.warn` assertion its sibling at :77 makes, which is exactly what hides the asymmetry.

Also worth noting: the source's own JSDoc at :46-50 is falsified — "a console.warn surfaces it so the duplicate entry can be cleaned up" is untrue in half the orderings, which defeats the stated purpose (surfacing an editorial mistake for cleanup).

**Fix** — hoist the warn out of the comparison, add `sys.id` as a stable secondary key:
```ts
if (candidateSpecificity === bestSpecificity) {
  console.warn(`resolveByRegion: tie between two equally-scoped entries for region "${siteId}" — resolving by most-recently-updated.`);
  const bestUpdatedAt = best.sys?.updatedAt ?? '';
  const candidateUpdatedAt = candidate.sys?.updatedAt ?? '';
  const bestId = String(best.sys?.id ?? '');
  const candidateId = String(candidate.sys?.id ?? '');
  if (candidateUpdatedAt > bestUpdatedAt || (candidateUpdatedAt === bestUpdatedAt && candidateId < bestId)) {
    best = candidate;
  }
}
```
Caveat: `sys.id` is `unknown` under the `[key: string]: unknown` index signature at `resolveByRegion.ts:18`, so it needs `String(...)` or a narrow guard — not a bare `<`.

**Safe?** Yes — behaviour for distinct timestamps is unchanged, so existing tests at :77 and :84 still pass. **Effort:** ~6 lines in source, ~3 new tests, plus rename/scope the :84 test. Re-test required (`npx vitest run overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.test.ts`).

**Real-world severity is genuinely Minor** — real CDA entries always carry `updatedAt`, so the equal case needs a same-millisecond bulk publish. The doc-falsification is the stronger reason to fix.

The reasoning error: for the *second* slash in `https://` to be read as a comment start, the guard needs `line[i] === '/' && line[i+1] === '/'`. At the second slash, `line[i+1]` is `e` (the first host character), so the `//` test fails and the character is simply appended. The guard only has to survive one slash, and it does.

```
  -> stripped: "  const x = 'https://wa.me/61400000000'; "   ← URL kept, comment dropped
"  margin: '8px', // https://figma.com/file 12px"
  -> units found: ["8px"]                                     ← 12px correctly ignored
```

# #14 — `seedRegions.mjs:42` en-CA — **CLAIM TRUE (mechanism confirmed; blame is inverted)**

## Evidence — the two halves, verified independently

**Locales `bootstrapSpace.mjs` provisions** (`scripts/contentful/setup/bootstrapSpace.mjs:40-50`, 9 total):
`en`(default) · `en-US` · `en-GB` · `fr` · `it` · `es` · `en-CH` · `en-HK` · `en-AE`

**Locale values `seedRegions.mjs` writes** (`scripts/contentful/setup/seedRegions.mjs:39-51`, 10 distinct):
`en` · `en-US` · **`en-CA`** · `en-GB` · `fr` · `it` · `es` · `en-CH` · `en-HK` · `en-AE`

**Set difference is exactly `{en-CA}`.**

## Cross-check against the generated config — CodeRabbit's proposed direction is wrong

`overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.generated.ts`:
- `SUPPORTED_LOCALES` (lines 8-19) = **10 codes, including `'en-CA'` at line 11**
- `SITE_LOCALES.ZimmermannUSIntl = ['en-CA']` (line 23)

So `seedRegions.mjs` is **correct** against its declared source of truth (its own header comment names `SITE_LOCALES` and it matches exactly). `bootstrapSpace.mjs`'s `LOCALES` array is the **stale** one — its comment claims "codes match SFCC sites.js locale IDs exactly" and it doesn't. It predates the US-Intl storefront. Confirmed live in SFCC config: `config/sites.overlay.js:35` → `{id: 'ZimmermannUSIntl', locales: [{id: 'en-CA', alias: 'en-ca'}]}`, `config/sites.generated.js:52` → `id: 'en-CA'`.

**CodeRabbit's title offers "or normalise `ZimmermannUSIntl` to a provisioned locale" — reject that half.** Normalising the seed would put a knowingly-wrong value in the entry and hide the real gap. The fix is to add `en-CA` to `bootstrapSpace.mjs`.

## Runtime impact — **live breakage, not latent** (but not via the field you'd expect)

Two separate things, don't conflate them:

**1. The `region.locale` field itself is inert.** `scripts/contentful/content-types/region.js:30-38` defines it as `Symbol`, `required: false`, `localized: false`, **no `in` validation** — commented "Informational only… helps an editor sanity-check". `seedRegions.mjs:54-56` writes it as a *field value* under the `en` key (`{locale: {en: 'en-CA'}}`), not as a locale selector. Grep confirms **zero consumers** of `fields.locale` anywhere in `overrides/`. So the seed itself won't fail and nothing reads it. On its own this would be cosmetic.

**2. But an unrelated path passes `en-CA` to the CDA at fetch time — and it will 400.** Traced end to end:

- `overrides/app/pages/experience/index.tsx:94-95` → `const {locale: siteLocale} = useMultiSite(); const locale = siteLocale?.id || CONTENTFUL_FALLBACK_LOCALE` — on `/en-ca/` this is `'en-CA'`
- → `:167` passes it as `localeCode` to `useFetchBySlug`
- → `node_modules/@contentful/experiences-core/dist/esm/index.js:5090` `fetchBySlug` → `:4540` `fetchExperienceEntry` → `:4551` `client.getEntries({content_type, locale, include: 3, ...filter})`
- → CDA request with `locale=en-CA` against a space with no such locale → **HTTP 400 unknown locale**

Blast surface is wide: `overrides/app/routes.tsx:45-48` registers `/:slug` as a **catch-all** for Experience pages. Failure mode degrades to `experience/index.tsx:51-62`'s "Page not found." + `<Seo noIndex />` — no crash, but a total Contentful-content outage on the US-Intl storefront rather than a visible error. `overrides/app/pages/contentfulPreview/index.tsx:136` has the identical construction.

**Unaffected:** the footer (`overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:183` — `getEntries({content_type: 'footerConfig', include: 3})`, no `locale`) and uiCopy (`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts:110` builds the URL by hand, no `locale` param). Both resolve in the space default `en`. So SFCC-55's own work is clean; this is a pre-existing hole the PR's `seedRegions.mjs` merely makes visible.

## Recommendation: **FIX** — but the one-line code change is *not* sufficient

Code change (safe, no CMS access needed):
```js
// scripts/contentful/setup/bootstrapSpace.mjs — insert after the en-US entry
{ code: 'en-CA', name: 'English (US International)', default: false, fallbackCode: 'en' },
```

**This will not repair any existing environment, and that's the important part.** `bootstrapSpace.mjs` hardcodes `'master'` in both the read (`:107`) and the write (`:134`). It relies on "cloned environments inherit them" (`:104`) — but `main()` creates environments (§1, `:75-102`) **before** creating locales (§2, `:104-141`), and Contentful environments are independent after cloning. There is no other locale-writing code anywhere (`grep locale.create` → one hit). So re-running only adds `en-CA` to `master`; `dev`/`test`/`sit`/`staging`/`uat` stay broken.

→ **Needs coordinated CMS work.** Either add `en-CA` (fallback `en`) manually per environment in the Contentful UI, or change §2 to loop `['master', ...TARGET_ENVIRONMENTS]`.

**Caveat I could not close:** I was read-only, so I can't tell whether someone already hand-added `en-CA` to the live space. Checking Settings → Locales in the dev environment is a 10-second confirmation and decides whether this is currently-broken or about-to-break.

**Blast radius:** the code edit is repo-only and zero-risk. The environment change touches the **live dev Contentful space** — adding a locale is additive and non-destructive (no existing entry is modified), but it is a real CMS mutation and should go through whoever owns that space.

# #13 — `installTemplate.mjs:127-130` validation gate — **CLAIM TRUE**

## The gate

```js
if (validation.items?.length && !FORCE && !(conflictingIds.length && TAKEOVER_IDS.length)) {
  log.error(`Refusing to install into '${TARGET}' — unresolved validation findings. Pass --force to override.`);
  process.exit(1);
}
```

`conflictingIds` (`:102-105`) is filtered to `f.message === 'conflictingContentTypes'` only.

The third clause is **unscoped**: any non-empty `--takeover` combined with any conflict existing disables the gate for **every** finding. Three ways findings reach a live install unresolved:

| Scenario | Gate fires? | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 `conflictingContentTypes` + 1 finding of any other class, `--takeover a` | **No** | installs with the other finding silently ignored |
| conflicts `a,b,c`, `--takeover a` | **No** | installs with `b`,`c` unresolved |
| conflict `a`, `--takeover typo` | **No** | gate opens on an ID that resolves nothing |

The "other finding class" case is not hypothetical: `node_modules/contentful-management/dist/types/entities/environment-template-installation.d.ts:41` types it as `{message: string; details: Record<string, unknown>}` — `message` is an open `string`, not a union. Nothing constrains findings to the one class this code handles.

Behaves correctly in the two safe cases: findings with no conflicts and no takeover → gate fires; non-conflict findings + a takeover flag → `0 && n` is falsy → gate fires.

Secondary: nothing validates `TAKEOVER_IDS ⊆ conflictingIds`, so a typo'd ID is never reported.

## Against the documentation

`.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md`'s additive-only claim is about field deletion specifically — *"Field deletion during an install is opt-in (`--delete-deleted-fields`), off by default"*. **That part the code honours exactly**: `:36` `const DELETE_DELETED_FIELDS = args.includes('--delete-deleted-fields')` → default `false` → `:139` `deleteDeletedFields: DELETE_DELETED_FIELDS`. No finding there.

The gap is the adjacent one: `--force` bypasses *all* validation, and `--force --delete-deleted-fields` together are unguarded — the exact combination the doc warns is *"difficult to undo and may break running components"*. Also note `--target` has no allowlist, so `--target master` is accepted.

It predates the US-Intl storefront. Confirmed live in SFCC config: `config/sites.overlay.js:35` → `{id: 'ZimmermannUSIntl', locales: [{id: 'en-CA', alias: 'en-ca'}]}`, `config/sites.generated.js:52` → `id: 'en-CA'`.

The `region.locale` field itself is inert.** `scripts/contentful/content-types/region.js:30-38` defines it as `Symbol`, `required: false`, `localized: false`, **no `in` validation** — commented "Informational only… helps an editor sanity-check". `seedRegions.mjs:54-56` writes it as a *field value* under the `en` key (`{locale: {en: 'en-CA'}}`), not as a locale selector. - → `node_modules/@contentful/experiences-core/dist/esm/index.js:5090` `fetchBySlug` → `:4540` `fetchExperienceEntry` → `:4551` `client.getEntries({content_type, locale, include: 3, ...filter})`
- → CDA request with `locale=en-CA` against a space with no such locale → **HTTP 400 unknown locale**

Blast surface is wide: `overrides/app/routes.tsx:45-48` registers `/:slug` as a **catch-all** for Experience pages. Failure mode degrades to `experience/index.tsx:51-62`'s "Page not found." + `<Seo noIndex />` — no crash, but a total Contentful-content outage on the US-Intl storefront rather than a visible error. `overrides/app/pages/contentfulPreview/index.tsx:136` has the identical construction.

**Unaffected:** the footer (`overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:183` — `getEntries({content_type: 'footerConfig', include: 3})`, no `locale`) and uiCopy (`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts:110` builds the URL by hand, no `locale` param). Both resolve in the space default `en`. So SFCC-55's own work is clean; this is a pre-existing hole the PR's `seedRegions.mjs` merely makes visible.

## Recommendation: **FIX** — but the one-line code change is *not* sufficient

Code change (safe, no CMS access needed):
```js
// scripts/contentful/setup/bootstrapSpace.mjs — insert after the en-US entry
{ code: 'en-CA', name: 'English (US International)', default: false, fallbackCode: 'en' },
```

**This will not repair any existing environment, and that's the important part.** `bootstrapSpace.mjs` hardcodes `'master'` in both the read (`:107`) and the write (`:134`). **Caveat I could not close:** I was read-only, so I can't tell whether someone already hand-added `en-CA` to the live space. Checking Settings → Locales in the dev environment is a 10-second confirmation and decides whether this is currently-broken or about-to-break.

```
import { afterEach, describe, test, expect, vi } from 'vitest';
...
```

# Scoreboard: 6 fix · 7 decline · 1 defer

| # | What it said | Verdict | |
|---|---|---|---|
| **14** | `en-CA` locale missing | **TRUE — live breakage** | FIX |
| **13** | Validation gate can be bypassed | **TRUE** | FIX |
| **10** | Region tie-break depends on response order | **TRUE** | FIX |
| **12** | Locales skipped without reconciling | **PARTLY** | FIX ordering, defer the rest |
| **7** | Magic string for content type ID | **PARTLY** | FIX — better than its suggestion |
| **8** | Clear Vitest mocks | **PARTLY** | FIX — for consistency, not the stated reason |
| **3** | Route icon labels through `useUiCopy` | **PARTLY** | DEFER |
| **1** | Move the `.env.sample` scope marker | **FALSE** | DECLINE |
| **2** | Remove document-level query (zimmModal) | **FALSE** | DECLINE |
| **4** | Scope play to `canvasElement` | **FALSE** | DECLINE |
| **5** | Add play coverage to subscribe section | **FALSE** | DECLINE |
| **6** | Replace provisional literals with constants | **FALSE** | DECLINE |
| **9** | Rename `fontFace.tsx` to kebab-case | **FALSE** | DECLINE |
| **11** | URL slash mangled by comment stripper | **FALSE** | DECLINE |

---

## The one that actually matters: #14

**In plain terms:** we tell Contentful "give me content in Canadian English" for the US-International storefront, but nobody ever created Canadian English in Contentful. Contentful rejects the request.

I verified both halves myself. `bootstrapSpace.mjs` creates **9 locales — no `en-CA`**. `seedRegions.mjs:42` writes `locale: 'en-CA'`. And `experience/index.tsx:94` reads the site's locale and hands it to the CDA at `:32`.

**This is current, not hypothetical.** US-Intl is already live on dev, test and sit. Every Experience page on `/en-ca/` gets a 400 and degrades to "Page not found" — silently, because the failure looks like missing content rather than a broken request. `/:slug` is the catch-all Experience route, so that's the whole CMS surface on that storefront.

**CodeRabbit offered two options and one is a trap.** It said "provision `en-CA` **or** normalise `ZimmermannUSIntl` to a provisioned locale." The second would put a knowingly-wrong locale in the entry and hide the bug. `seedRegions.mjs` is *correct* — it matches `SITE_LOCALES` and SFCC's `sites.overlay.js`. `bootstrapSpace.mjs` is the stale one; it predates the storefront.

**And the code fix alone won't repair anything.** `bootstrapSpace.mjs` hardcodes `'master'` for both reading and writing locales, and it creates environments *before* creating locales — so cloned environments never inherit them. Adding one line fixes `master` only; dev/test/sit/uat stay broken. This needs someone with Contentful access to add `en-CA` per environment, or the script reordered to loop the targets.

## The two that would undo what we shipped an hour ago: #2 and #4

Both say "query through `canvasElement`, not `document.body`." I asked for a measurement rather than an argument, and the agent built a probe rendering the real components:

```
canvasElement                    = DIV#storybook-root
canvasElement.contains(dialog)   = false
dialogs inside canvas / document = 0 / 1
canvasElement.innerHTML          = 41 chars  ← the canvas is empty
```

**In plain terms:** the modal teleports itself out of the story's box and attaches to the page body. `canvasElement` *is* that box. You cannot find something inside a box it left.

Running CodeRabbit's suggestion verbatim: **fails after a 1002ms timeout on all three queries.** The shipped form passes in 1–2ms. So #4 wouldn't just be wrong — it would re-break `5883499`, the commit that fixed those exact tests this morning, and add ~3 seconds to the run.

Its escape hatch ("provide a story-local portal target") does work — but only by **adding a portal-container prop to a shared atom purely to satisfy a test-style rule.** That's production API surface bought with no product value.

## Why these keep coming back — and the real fix

This is the third time this objection has been raised on this PR. The cause is on our side:

`testing.md:128` says, unconditionally, *"Always query through `within(canvasElement)` — never reach into `document` directly."* There is **no portal exception written anywhere.** Meanwhile `footer/index.stories.tsx:123` cites *"testing.md §Layer-2 exception"* — **a section that does not exist.**

So our own rule says the code is wrong, and the only record of the carve-out is inline comments. CodeRabbit is reading the rule correctly and we're the ones out of step. Until that exception is written down, it will re-raise on every push. `.claude/rules/` is Tier 1, so that's an ~8-line amendment behind the governance gate — and it's the durable fix, not another reply.

## Quick wins — #7 and #8

**#7:** CodeRabbit said "extract the content type ID to a named constant." Correct instinct, but it missed that **`CONTENT_TYPE_IDS` already exists** at `contentfulMapping.ts:53` — with a `ContentTypeId` type and **zero consumers**. I verified both. Its suggestion would have created a *second* source of truth for the same string. Two lines to import the existing one instead.

**#8:** graded Major, actually cosmetic — the file's only mock is created inside one test body, so `clearAllMocks` provably clears nothing. Running both variants gave identical 4/4 results. **But comply anyway**: I set the precedent on this very PR in `a207b9a` by complying with the identical finding on `zimmTextInput.test.ts`. Declining here after complying there is an inconsistency a reviewer would rightly call out. Five lines.

## Declines worth knowing about

**#9 cites a rule that doesn't exist here.** `conventions.md` says Zimmermann-authored files use **camelCase**; only files mirroring a base Salesforce file keep kebab-case. There is no base SFCC font-face module — zero hits in the package. And the rename would break `.storybook/preview.tsx`'s import, forcing a **Tier 1 edit to satisfy a non-existent rule.**

**#6's literals are already sanctioned.** Both sit in `audit:tokens`' acknowledged-exception list, matching the documented `provisional`/`pending` vocabulary. Extracting them to constants would strip the Figma node IDs and pixel derivations from the point of use — a net loss.

**#11 is a reasoning error.** For `https://` to be read as a comment start you'd need `//` — but at the second slash the next character is the first letter of the host, so the test fails and the character passes through. Its proposed fix is a no-op against its own example. The agent did find a *real* adjacent bug — protocol-relative `//host` URLs do truncate — which CodeRabbit didn't spot.

**#3's architecture is fine but its rationale is false.** `components.md` explicitly permits `useUiCopy` in a leaf. But the claim is that it fixes screen readers hearing English on non-English storefronts — and `useContentful.ts:110` sends **no locale**, so routing through the CMS still returns `en` for all 8 sites. It relocates the hardcoding without fixing the problem. Defer until the locale gap is closed.

---

## What I'd do

**Now, no CMS access needed:** #13 (tighten the gate — strictly safer), #10 (tie-break + fix the misnamed test), #7 (two lines), #8 (five lines).

**Needs a decision:** #14's CMS work, and the `testing.md` portal amendment — both need someone other than me.

**Nothing.** #1, #2, #4, #5, #6, #9, #11 — with in-thread replies, since per AGENTS.md silence teaches CodeRabbit nothing and #2/#4 will otherwise return.

Want me to start on the four code fixes?

Queued. Same two-stage shape as findings 1–12: fresh V&V first, then a precedent audit against what Tim's 14 commits establish, with the same split — **his pattern is authoritative on convention, architecture and priority; it can't overturn a measurement.**

One tension I want to flag now rather than let it resolve quietly in my favour.

**Tim's precedent may appear to exonerate my own Tier 1 edit, and I don't think I should accept that.** Commit `542ac65` edited six Tier 1 `.claude/rules/` files and `CODEOWNERS`, with a self-asserted *"Edited under verified tier-1-approvers identity"* line in the message. My `ac224a6` did the same thing on two `foundation/` files with the same justification. So a precedent audit will likely conclude "consistent with the lead's established practice."

Both overturns confirmed at source. Two corrections I owe you.

## #8 — I cited my own commit as precedent

I argued we should comply because *"the identical finding was complied with in `a207b9a`."* That commit is **mine**, and its own message says the hooks *"reset no observable state."* So I used my own decorative change to justify another decorative change — circular, and I presented it as external precedent.

Tim's actual practice is the opposite, and the decisive case is his own file: `footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx` has **1 real `vi.mock`** and **0 lifecycle hooks**. He adds them only where they reset something real — `useZimmModal.test.tsx` restores `document.body.style.overflow`, `resolveByRegion.test.ts` scopes a `console.warn` spy. **Re-verdict: DECLINE.**

The durable fix is qualifying `testing.md:67`, which still states the rule unconditionally. Tim edited that file in `542ac65` and left the line alone — so it needs him, not a no-op from us.

## #7 — my "better fix" imposed a convention its author declined

I was pleased with catching that `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS` already existed. But **Tim populated it himself in `5b2be3f`** and then used bare literals at both call sites he wrote afterwards — `footer/index.tsx:183` one commit later, `uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:19` three commits later. The registry has **zero consumers** and omits two IDs that *are* in use (`'homepage'`, `'collectionPageExp'`). Adopting it in one place would leave 3 of 4 sites inconsistent. **Re-verdict: DECLINE.**

## And the `en-CA` gap is ours, not Tim's

This is the reframe that matters most. I presented #14 as a hole in Tim's tooling. `git blame` says otherwise:

- `experience/index.tsx:32` and `:94-95` — the code that sends the locale to the CDA — are **Marcel's `7ed19fa3`** (31 Jul)
- the `en-CA` locale itself arrived in **Marcel's `e4c342e`** (7 Aug)
- Tim's `bootstrapSpace.mjs` locale list was **complete when written** (12 Jul); `en-CA` didn't exist for another 26 days

So `e4c342e` added the locale to `contentfulMapping.generated.ts` and didn't update `bootstrapSpace.mjs`. That's our drift. Also stale for the same reason: `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md:111` says *"Eleven active locales"* then lists ten, omitting `en-CA`.

## Sequencing that changes the plan

**#12 must land with or before #14, or #14 fixes nothing outside master.** `locale.create` is hardcoded to `'master'` and environment creation is skipped on re-run, so adding `en-CA` alone leaves `/en-ca/` still 400ing on dev, test, sit, staging and uat. They're one change, not two.

| | Verdict | |
|---|---|---|
| **#10** | UPHELD — strongest of all | Contradicts Tim's own JSDoc *and* his own test name; proven by probe |
| **#14 + #12** | UPHELD, must ship together | Our drift, not his |
| **#13** | UPHELD, claim overstated | Needs ≥1 conflict co-present; `--force` is the intended hatch. Tier 2 — notify Integration/SI |
| **#7, #8** | **OVERTURNED → DECLINE** | Both stylistic; both contradicted by Tim's own practice |

The pattern is clean: **all four behavioural findings survived the precedent audit; both stylistic ones did not.**

```

                 const SIZE_SUBSCRIBE_SLOT = '2.8125rem'
now:             maxWidth: '12.5rem'      minHeight: '2.8125rem'
```

Tim's decomposition carried **7 of 9** constants across as named constants and inlined exactly **2** — both into this one file. His own audit script says *"name it as a constant"*. His own commit message says the value *"had genuinely lost its 'provisional' framing when it was inlined"*. And `zimmTextInput.css.ts:28` still refers to `SIZE_SUBSCRIBE_SLOT` — a constant that **exists nowhere**. **FIX (9):** #3, #6, #10, #12, #13, #14 · C3, C4, C5
**DECLINE (8):** #1, #2, #4, #5, #7, #8, #9, #11 · **DEFER (2):** C1-adjacent governance ticket, C2

Two agents still out on findings A1–A6 and B1–B5. Then I'll run the precedent audit across those verdicts as you asked, and give you the consolidated ELI5 across all 28.

Audit a set of code-review verdicts against the conventions Tim Lavelle established on this branch, and resolve one direct contradiction between two prior reviewers. NO prior context — build your own view from the code and git history.

REPO: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa`, branch `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui`, HEAD `ac224a6`.

**THE GOVERNING DISTINCTION:**
- **Convention / architecture / priority** → Tim's established pattern is authoritative. A verdict that contradicts it should be overturned.
- **Empirical fact / measurement** → stands regardless of authorship. But check whether Tim's commits show he knowingly accepted the behaviour; if so the recommendation becomes "raise with him", not "ignore".

## PART 1 — RESOLVE THIS CONTRADICTION FIRST (highest value)

All 28 verified. Precedent audit running on the code-changing verdicts. Here's the picture.

# All 28 findings — ELI5

## Real problems worth fixing (7)

**The modal clips content you can't scroll to.** `zimmModal.css.ts`'s panel has no `maxHeight` and no `overflow`, the overlay is `position:fixed` with `align-items:center`, and the hook sets `body.overflow:'hidden'`. So tall content overflows *both* directions and centring puts half of it **above** the viewport — unreachable by scrolling, tabbing, or anything else. Measured at 320×256 (the WCAG reflow target): 138px clipped above, title and Continue button both unreachable. **Two lines fix it.** Only invisible today because the modal ships disabled — but it's the shared shell every future dialog inherits.

**`/en-ca/` is broken on three live tiers.** We ask Contentful for Canadian English; nobody ever created it there. Every Experience page on US-International 400s and shows "Page not found." **And it's our drift, not Tim's** — his locale list was complete when written; `en-CA` arrived 26 days later in Marcel's `e4c342e`, which updated the config but not the bootstrap. **Must ship with the ordering fix** or it only reaches `master` and dev/test/sit stay broken.

**Region tie-breaks silently depend on Contentful's response order.** The `console.warn` and the reassignment both sit inside a strict `>`, so equal timestamps fire neither — whichever entry arrived first wins, silently. This contradicts **Tim's own JSDoc** ("a console.warn surfaces it") **and his own test name** ("order of the tied candidates does not change the outcome") — that test only uses *distinct* timestamps, so it passes while testing around the bug.

**The install safety gate can be walked through.** Pass `--takeover` with one conflict present and *every other* validation finding is silently ignored.

**Two real lint errors** — `useState` inside `render:` in two story files. Verified the extraction fixes it and changes no behaviour.

**A factual error in Tim's own governance text.** `components.md` says both `useIntl` and `useUiCopy` "degrade gracefully… not a throw." **`useIntl` throws** — that's why `.storybook/preview.tsx` has to wrap every story in an `IntlProvider`. And `IntlProvider` lives in base SFCC `_app`, not `_app-config`.

**`projectState.md` is stale** — and worse than flagged: the entire footer/ui-kits/uiCopy body of work is absent from a file `AGENTS.md` requires reading at every session start.

## Where CodeRabbit was wrong (11)

The pattern is consistent — **it's reliable on behaviour, unreliable on convention.**

- **Three times** it asked us to scope Storybook queries to `canvasElement`. Measured: the modal portals to `document.body`, `canvasElement.contains(dialog) === false`, 0 dialogs in the canvas vs 1 in the document. Its own remedy would need a portal-container prop added to a shared component purely to satisfy a test rule.
- **Twice** it asked for kebab-case filenames. `conventions.md` says camelCase for Zimmermann-authored files; none of these has a base Salesforce equivalent. It withdrew this same finding on PR #47.
- The `https://` URL bug **doesn't reproduce** — its proposed fix is a no-op against its own example.
- `.env.sample` is conformant 60/60.
- The `floated` gap **doesn't exist** — it's derived from `focused || filled`, both already enumerated. Proved by reintroducing the original bug: the guard catches it.

## Three things I got wrong

**I cited my own commit as precedent.** On clear-mocks I argued *"the identical finding was complied with in `a207b9a`"* — that's mine, and its message concedes the hooks reset nothing. Tim's actual practice is the opposite: his `footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx` has a real `vi.mock` and **no hooks**.

**My "better fix" imposed a convention its author declined.** I was pleased to spot that `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS` already existed — but Tim populated it himself, then used bare literals at both call sites he wrote afterwards. Zero consumers, and it omits two IDs in active use.

**My defence of the inlined literals was the wrong test.** I said `audit:tokens` already treats them as acknowledged. But both **were** named constants until Tim's decomposition inlined them — he carried 7 of 9 across and inlined exactly 2, both into that one file. His own script says *"name it as a constant."* His own commit message says the value *"had genuinely lost its provisional framing when it was inlined."* And `zimmTextInput.css.ts:28` still refers to `SIZE_SUBSCRIBE_SLOT` — **a constant that exists nowhere.** Suppressing an exit code isn't conforming.

## The structural finding underneath all this

**Three of these keep recurring because our docs are wrong, not because CodeRabbit is stubborn.**

- `testing.md:128` states the `canvasElement` rule absolutely with no portal exception — and `footer/index.stories.tsx` cites *"testing.md §Layer-2 exception"*, **a section that does not exist**. That citation is mine.
- `testing.md:67` states the clear-mocks rule unconditionally, and Tim ignores it in practice.
- `.cursor/rules/development-guidelines.mdc:96` says *"use kebab-case for file names"* — stale boilerplate, not emitted by the sync script, contradicting the correct generated rule. CodeRabbit ingests both, so **that one regenerates on every PR** until reconciled.

Fixing three doc lines stops more findings than fixing any code.

## Also worth your attention

**An unrelated Contentful Studio fix is riding this footer PR** — Tim's `ad4fbc6`, `+47/-6` in `pages/experience/index.tsx`, reimplementing an *unexported* SDK internal with zero test coverage. That's a scope question for the team, not a code one.

**The mobile header has no Account control**, and HPC-018 confirms Search/Account/Bag. But it's reachable via the base drawer menu, HPC-025 says mobile chrome deliberately differs, and this PR only added comments to that file — so out of scope. One comment we added does need correcting though: it claims *"Account ships as text, so nothing is missing,"* which is true at `lg`+ and **false below it**.

I'll fold the precedent audit's rulings in when it lands, then we can pick what to actually change.

# PART 1 — RULING: **ADOPT NOWHERE.** Reviewer Y's conclusion upheld; Reviewer X overturned. Registry deletion *proposed to Tim*, not actioned.

**Authorship.** `contentfulMapping.ts` — registry container `f81f6bc` (TimLavelle, 2026-07-12); all 5 current entries `5b2be3f` (TimLavelle, 2026-08-23). `footer/index.tsx:183` — `5640c25` (TimLavelle). `uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:19` — `90069b2` (TimLavelle). `pages/home/index.tsx:148` — **Hardi, 2026-06-12** (pre-branch). `pages/experience/index.tsx:17` — **Marcel, 2026-07-31**.

### Reviewer Y verified — mostly right, with two corrections

✅ **Zero consumers — and stronger than claimed.** The only two matches repo-wide are the declaration itself and its derived type:
```
overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts:53:export const CONTENT_TYPE_IDS = {
overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts:61:export type ContentTypeId = ...
```
`git log -S"CONTENT_TYPE_IDS" --all` returns exactly one commit (`f81f6bc`, its creation). It has **never** had a consumer in 6 weeks of history.

✅ **Tim used bare literals at 2 of 2 call sites he wrote after populating it.** Both confirmed by blame.

❌ **Correction 1 — "one commit later / three commits later" is wrong.** `5640c25` is 4 commits after `5b2be3f`; `90069b2` is 9 after. Substance holds, ordering doesn't.

❌ **Correction 2 — "omits two in-use IDs" misreads the registry's semantic.** This is the decisive finding, and neither reviewer had it:

```
$ ls scripts/contentful/content-types/
footerConfig.js  footerNavGroup.js  link.js  region.js  uiCopy.js
```

Those are **exactly** the 5 registry entries. And before `5b2be3f` the registry held exactly one entry — `shoppableImage: 'shoppableImage'` — when `shoppableImage.js` was the sole def file. `5b2be3f` decommissioned it and swapped in the 5 new ones in the same diff. **`CONTENT_TYPE_IDS` has always been a 1:1 mirror of `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` — the repo-authored content model — not an inventory of strings passed to `content_type`.** `'homepage'` (Hardi) and `'collectionPageExp'` (Marcel) have no def file and were never in scope. The omission is coherent, not incomplete.

Also: only **3** `content_type` literals exist repo-wide, not 4. And `'collectionPageExp'` is already a named constant (`const EXPERIENCE_TYPE_ID = 'collectionPageExp'`) passed as `experienceTypeId` to `useFetchBySlug` — a different API surface from `content_type`. Counting it inflated the inconsistency.

### Why "adopt nowhere" rather than "adopt everywhere"

Tim's demonstrated pattern is unambiguous (2 for 2 bare literals after populating it), and the registry is *structurally* a hand-maintained second copy that cannot be derived: `content-types/*.js` are CommonJS (`module.exports`, `require()`d by `buildTemplate.js`), the registry is ESM TS in the browser bundle. Neither can import the other. Adopting it at 2 of 3 sites would add a second source of truth for ids already authoritatively declared in the defs — the exact failure mode Tim's own `overrideStyling.md` names: *"two values can't disagree if only one of them is ever typed."*

**Deletion: proposed, not ruled.** It is genuinely dead and silently driftable, but `ContentTypeId` is an exported type surface and the JSDoc reads as a deliberate content-model inventory. Tim populated it 1 day before writing the first call site and then declined it twice — that's more likely "documentation" than "forgot." Per AGENTS.md Hard Rule #9, propose and let a human confirm. **→ RAISE WITH TIM as one question: adopt it or drop it, but it shouldn't stay at zero consumers.**

### Sub-ruling: `include: 3` — **UPHELD, narrowed**

The naming half survives. The framing does not.

- **The value 3 is correct and load-bearing, not a bug.** Model depth is exactly 3: `footerConfig.navGroups[]` → `footerNavGroup.links[]` → `link.regions[]`, and `filterByRegion` reads `entry.fields.regions[].fields.siteId` (`resolveByRegion.ts:25`). Depth 3 is the minimum that populates it.
- **"Differs from `useContentful.ts:110`'s `include=2`" is a false conflict.** That line is **Hardi's, 2026-06-26** — pre-branch, not a Tim choice — and serves flat content types (`uiCopy` has zero link fields). The depths differ because the models differ.
- **"Reason undocumented" is half-wrong.** `footer/index.tsx:128-130` already enumerates the three levels: *"Contentful's `include`-resolved response nests navGroups/links/regions"*.
- **But naming it matches Tim's own practice**, which is emphatic — he names bare numbers: `OPACITY_DISABLED = 0.4`, `OPACITY_ICON_HOVER = 0.6`, plus `MODAL_MAX_WIDTH`, `NEW_TAB_SUFFIX`, `DEFAULT_INPUT_NAME`, `ZIMM_MODAL_RECIPE`, `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT`.

Reduced scope: a named constant with a one-line "why 3" at the declaration. **Not** harmonising the two depths — that would be a regression.

# PART 2 — VERDICTS

### F1 — modal overflow → **RAISE WITH TIM** (real; not knowingly accepted; adopt `maxHeight: '100%'`)
*Authorship: `zimmModal.css.ts`, `zimmModal/index.tsx`, `useZimmModal.ts`, `zimmSubscribeModal.css.ts` — all TimLavelle `5ecd515`.*

Mechanism independently confirmed. `panel` sets only `backgroundColor` / `width: '100%'` / `padding` — grep for `maxHeight|overflow|dvh|vh` across **both** the chrome recipe and the consuming `zimmSubscribeModal.css.ts` returns nothing. Overlay is `position: 'fixed', inset: 0, alignItems: 'center'`. `useZimmModal.ts:69`: `document.body.style.overflow = 'hidden'`. No scroll path anywhere.

**Did he consider it?** He considered *width* and said so explicitly: *"maxWidth is deliberately NOT set here — ZimmModal takes it as a required prop, since each dialog type has its own Figma-specified size."* There is **no comment anywhere about height or overflow**, and `MODAL_MAX_WIDTH`'s docblock is purely about width tokens. So: he consciously delegated width and never addressed height. Not a knowing tradeoff → real gap, but flag it rather than silently patching a lead's brand-new atom.

**Prefer `maxHeight: '100%'` over CodeRabbit's `calc(100dvh - …)`.** The overlay is `position: fixed; inset: 0` with `padding: var(--zimm-scale-l)`, so a flex child's `100%` already resolves to viewport-minus-padding. The `calc` form restates the padding token in a second place — the drift risk Tim's own doc warns against ("*The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy*"). `100%` is also outside `audit:tokens`' scope (it flags hex/px/rem/em only), so it introduces no new exception.

**One caveat on the measurement:** I confirmed the *mechanism* and that ~500-600px of content at 320px width against a 216px usable height (256px − 2×20px overlay padding) centred by `alignItems: center` clips roughly half above. I did **not** reproduce the specific "138px" figure — no browser run. Right order of magnitude; treat the number as unverified by me.

### F2 — hooks in `render:` → **UPHELD, but deprioritise**
*Authorship: both files TimLavelle `5ecd515`. `zimmSubscribeModal/index.stories.tsx` also touched by Marcel `5883499`.*

Real and reproduced, exactly as claimed:
```
zimmModal/index.stories.tsx  22:33  error  React Hook "useState" is called in function "render" ...
zimmSubscribeModal/index.stories.tsx  22:33  error  (same)   react-hooks/rules-of-hooks
```
These are the **only** hook-in-story instances in the repo — no other `.stories.tsx` calls a React hook at all, so there is no named-component precedent either for or against.

**But the context materially deflates the priority.** Full `npx eslint 'overrides/**/*.{ts,tsx}'` at HEAD = **19 errors, 4 warnings**; only 2 of the 19 are these. The other 17 are `prettier/prettier`: `definitions.ts` (13), `routes.tsx` (2, untouched by this branch — pre-existing), `recipeGuards.test.ts` (2, introduced by Tim in `9d5f89c` *on this branch*). And:

```
$ grep -rn "run lint|eslint|tsc --noEmit" .github/workflows/
(only inside a prompt string in upstream-release-watch.yml — no actual step)
```

**Lint and `tsc` are gated nowhere in CI.** `qa.yml` gates Vitest, Storybook interaction/a11y, and Playwright only. So the repo demonstrably tolerates lint errors, and Tim shipped ≥4 of the current 19 on this branch. Verdict stands (they're this PR's own errors, trivially fixable, and `--fix` won't do it), but it's a should-fix, not a blocker — and worth pairing with the observation that the missing lint gate is the actual root cause.

### F3 — `clearAllMocks` → `afterEach` → **OVERTURNED**
*Authorship: all three flagged files TimLavelle (`c5a8422`; `uiCopyProvider` via `0b8db3e`→`90069b2`).*

Four independent reasons, any one sufficient:

**1. The rule is not Tim's — and its own author contradicts the literal reading.** `testing.md:67` verbatim:
> `- Use `beforeEach` for setup; clear mocks with `vi.clearAllMocks()` after each test.`

`git blame`: `^cd60b7a (Hardi 2026-06-12 67)` — the **root commit**, "Initial commit during Detailed Design phase," never edited. Six days later the same author wrote `useCountryConfig.test.ts:18-20`:
```ts

  vi.clearAllMocks();

```
The rule's author read his own "after each test" as *between tests*, not *in an `afterEach` hook*.

**2. The claimed precedent doesn't exist.** `a207b9a` was **not** a `beforeEach`→`afterEach` move. It *added both hooks to a file that had neither*, and cites no reviewer finding. Marcel's own commit message:
> *"This file's resolvers are pure and it mocks nothing, so the hooks reset no observable state — added for consistency with the rule as written rather than for isolation"*

It's also **not on this branch** — `a207b9a` predates `ec9d161`. A self-initiated decorative addition to a mock-free file is not precedent for restructuring three load-bearing blocks.

**3. Tim's practice is a coherent pattern, and the discriminator is exactly "real state to reset."** He uses `afterEach` + `restoreAllMocks` precisely where there is a spy to restore — `resolveByRegion.test.ts:69-75` (`5b2be3f`), the repo's **only** `vi.spyOn`.
