# Contentful: schema promotion vs content promotion

**Bottom line:** they are two entirely separate mechanisms, and the Environment Template mechanism carries **content types only — never entries**. This is provable from the SDK's own type definitions, not just from comments.

---

## 1. `scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js` — what it assembles and pushes

**File:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js`

It reads every `.js` file in `scripts/contentful/content-types/`, maps each through `buildContentTypeTemplate()`, and pushes the result as one organization-scoped `EnvironmentTemplate` named `'Zimmermann Content Model'` (`buildTemplate.js:53`), get-or-created by name.

The payload is **content-type definitions only**. The `entities` object literally has two keys, one of which is hardcoded empty:

```js
// buildTemplate.js:139-148 (create path)
await client.environmentTemplate.create(
  { organizationId },
  {
    name: TEMPLATE_NAME,
    description: '...',
    versionName,
    versionDescription,
    entities: { contentTypeTemplates, editorInterfaceTemplates: [] },
  },
);
```

```js
// buildTemplate.js:154 (update path)
found.entities = { contentTypeTemplates, editorInterfaceTemplates: found.entities.editorInterfaceTemplates ?? [] };
```

And `contentTypeTemplates` is built from schema only — id/name/displayField/description/fields (`buildTemplate.js:93-101`), where each field is id/name/type/required/localized/validations/linkType/items/defaultValue (`buildTemplate.js:76-90`). `defaultValue` is a *field-level schema default*, not an entry.

**Proof this is a hard limit, not a choice:** the SDK type for the whole entity has no entry slot at all —

```ts
// node_modules/contentful-management/dist/types/entities/environment-template.d.ts:30-33
entities: {
    contentTypeTemplates: Array<ContentTypeTemplateProps>;
    editorInterfaceTemplates: Array<EditorInterfaceTemplateProps>;
};
```

There is no `entryTemplates`, no `entries`, no assets. **A Contentful Environment Template cannot carry entries.**

The 5 content types currently in the template: `footerConfig`, `footerNavGroup`, `link`, `region`, `uiCopy` (`scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js`).

---

## 2. `scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs` — what `install()` transfers

**File:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs`

```js

await client.environmentTemplate.install(
  { spaceId, environmentId: TARGET, environmentTemplateId: template.sys.id },
  { version: template.sys.version, deleteDeletedFields: DELETE_DELETED_FIELDS, takeover },
);
```

The payload type is fully enumerated by the SDK and contains no content:

```ts
// node_modules/contentful-management/dist/types/entities/environment-template-installation.d.ts:32-39
export type CreateEnvironmentTemplateInstallationProps = {
    version: number;
    takeover?: { items: Link<'ContentType'>[] };   // ← ContentType links only
    changeSet?: Link<'ChangeSet'>;
    deleteDeletedFields?: boolean;
};
```

So `install()` transfers: **the named template version's content types** (plus editor interfaces, empty here). `takeover` is a list of `Link<'ContentType'>` — adopting pre-existing *content types* into template management. `deleteDeletedFields` operates on *fields*. Nothing in the payload or the template can reference an entry.

Surrounding behaviour: `validate()` first (`:97`), refuse on unresolved findings unless `--force` (`:156-164`), then poll `environmentTemplateInstallation.getForEnvironment` to a terminal status (`:55-74`).

## 3. `scripts/contentful/setup/seedRegions.mjs` — the only entry-creating code

**File:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/scripts/contentful/setup/seedRegions.mjs`

Its own header states the split explicitly (`:5-10`):

> `Environment Templates (buildTemplate.js / installTemplate.mjs) cover content-TYPE schema only — entries are a separate concern and have to be seeded per environment after that environment's `region` content type exists`

- **What it creates:** exactly 11 `region` entries, one per SFCC storefront (`REGION_SEEDS`, `:39-51`), with deterministic IDs `region-<siteId>` (`:84`). Fields `siteId` / `label` / `locale`, all written under the single default locale `'en'` (`:33`, `:54-56`). This matches the `region` content type, whose three fields are all `localized: false` (`scripts/contentful/content-types/region.js`).
- **Entries only, no content types.** It never calls `contentType.*` — it assumes the type already exists and will fail otherwise.
- **Idempotent — yes, verifiably.** `:58-69` does a `client.entry.get` probe and returns early on hit:

```js
let exists = true;
try {
  await client.entry.get({ environmentId, entryId });
} catch (err) {
  if (err.name !== 'NotFound') throw err;
  exists = false;

```

The `err.name !== 'NotFound'` check is **correct**, not a guess: `node_modules/contentful-sdk-core/dist/error-handler.js:55-59` sets `error.name = data.sys?.id`, which is `'NotFound'` for a Contentful 404. Non-404s rethrow rather than being swallowed.

- **What it does if an entry already exists:** logs `⏭️ region-<siteId> already exists` and skips. It does **not** update or re-publish. Note the function is *named* `upsertEntry` (`:53`) but is create-or-skip, not upsert — a drifted/hand-edited region entry will never be corrected by re-running this.
- **Publishing:** `:71-72` — `entry.createWithId` then `entry.publish`. New entries land published, so they're visible on the CDA immediately.

| file:line | call | notes |
|---|---|---|

| `scripts/contentful/setup/seedRegions.mjs:72` | `client.entry.publish(...)` | **the only `.publish()` in the repo** — confirmed |

### Two real bugs found in passing (both outside your question, both worth logging)

**a) `promoteAlias.mjs:70` will throw at runtime.** The plain client has no `environmentAlias.createOrUpdate`:

```js
// node_modules/contentful-management/dist/cjs/index.cjs:14030-14036
environmentAlias: {
    get: ..., getMany: ..., createWithId: ..., update: ..., delete: ...,
},
```

`bootstrapSpace.mjs:238-240` documents this exact fact — *"The plain client has no createOrUpdate for environmentAlias"* — and uses the correct get→update / createWithId split. `promoteAlias.mjs` did not get that fix. It is only reachable on the non-dry-run path when an alias actually needs flipping, which is why it has likely never surfaced. This is the **production content-release mechanism**, so it matters.

```ts
createWithId: { params: GetSpaceEnvironmentParams & { sourceEnvironmentId?: string }; payload: ...; headers?: ... }
```

So `'master'` lands in the `headers` slot, `params.sourceEnvironmentId` is `undefined`, and no `X-Contentful-Source-Environment` header is sent (`index.cjs:1976-1988`). ## 5. `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` — what it documents, and where it's wrong

**File:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` (137 lines)

The doc is overwhelmingly about **runtime read paths** (CDA/CPA/Images API, live preview, publish webhooks, caching, failure modes). It contains essentially **no promotion process**. The only schema-management section is §2, in full:

> **`.docs/integration/02-contentful.md:36-42`**

> Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:
> - Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
> - A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
> - Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.

It also scopes entry seeding **out** at `:18`: *"Out of scope of this document: Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)"* — and never mentions entry seeding anywhere at all.

### Contradictions with the actual scripts

1. **"A sync script... idempotently upserts content types into the target environment"** (`:41`) describes the *old, deleted* per-environment `sync.js` pipeline. The current mechanism is two-stage — build an org-level template (`sync:contentful`), then install it per environment (`install:contentful --target`). The doc mentions neither Environment Templates nor the org scope. `scripts/contentful/README.md:9` and `.docs/architecture.md:160-166` both describe the new mechanism correctly; **02-contentful.md is stale**.
2. **"never deletes a field from a live content type"** (`:41`) is no longer unconditionally true. `installTemplate.mjs:36` + `:177` expose `--delete-deleted-fields`. The `regions` field is built and shipping — `link.js` and `footerConfig.js` both carry a `regions` field, and `region.js` exists as the canonical referenceable type with 11 seeded entries.
4. **§7 locale list** (`:111`) reads *"en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE"* — 10 locales, described as "Eleven active locales", and using `en-AU` where the space actually uses `en` as the default (`bootstrapSpace.mjs:41`, `seedRegions.mjs:33`). `en-CA` (ZimmermannUSIntl) is missing entirely.

## 6. Other Contentful documentation in `.docs/`

`grep -ril contentful .docs/` returns 20 files; only these say anything about promotion, seeding, or migration:

| File | What it says |
|---|---|
| `.docs/architecture.md:160-196` | **The most accurate doc.** Correctly describes the Environment Template mechanism, names `buildTemplate.js` / `installTemplate.mjs` / `content-types/`, gives the register-a-new-type steps, and states *"Both scripts are idempotent"* and *"Field deletion during an install is opt-in (`--delete-deleted-fields`)"*. **Gap: it never mentions entries or `seedRegions.mjs` at all.** A reader following only this doc would install the template and wonder why the storefront has no region data. |
| `.docs/temp/tsd-architecture.md:293-302` (§7.3) | Same content as architecture.md, condensed. Also content-types only; no mention of entries or seeding. `:259` records the CMA token as CI-host-only. |

| `.docs/planning/regionalConfigSyncPlan.md:64` | Uses `installTemplate.mjs` only as a *shape precedent* for the SFCC regional-config sync job (a manual/cron script, not runtime). Nothing about Contentful entries. |
| `.docs/temp/openItems.md:52` | Duplicate of 02-contentful.md §10.1 (the stale `regions`-field open item). |
| `README.md:118-128` | The best operational summary — a table of all 7 Contentful commands with owners. It is the **only doc that lists `seed:contentful-regions`** alongside the schema commands (`:126`), correctly noting it must run *"after that environment has the `region` content type installed"*. Minor inaccuracy at `:127`: it describes `generate:contentful` as *"Generate / verify local TypeScript types from Contentful content models"* — it actually generates the **Studio Experiences component registry** from `@cf` JSDoc tags (`scripts/contentful/generateDefinitions.mjs:1-22`), unrelated to content models. |

---

## 7. Definitive answer: install into an empty environment

**(a) — content types but zero entries.** Specifically: 5 content types (`footerConfig`, `footerNavGroup`, `link`, `region`, `uiCopy`), their editor interfaces (empty in this template), and **no entries and no assets whatsoever.**

Evidence, in descending order of strength:

1. **The SDK type makes entries structurally impossible.** `EnvironmentTemplateProps.entities` has exactly two keys — `contentTypeTemplates` and `editorInterfaceTemplates` (`environment-template.d.ts:30-33`). There is no field an entry could occupy.
2. **The install payload type is fully enumerated and entry-free:** `{version, takeover?: {items: Link<'ContentType'>[]}, changeSet?, deleteDeletedFields?}` (`environment-template-installation.d.ts:32-39`).
3. **`buildTemplate.js` only ever reads `content-types/*.js`** (`:115-130`) and hardcodes `editorInterfaceTemplates: []` (`:146`). No code path reads entry data.
4. **The repo's own tooling agrees:** `seedRegions.mjs` exists solely because the template can't carry entries, and says so in its header (`:5-8`).
5. **The negative check holds:** the only `entry.create*` / `.publish()` calls in the entire repo are `seedRegions.mjs:71-72`.

### The important caveat: environments are never actually empty in this pipeline

The literal question is (a), but the real-world flow adds a second, distinct entry-transfer mechanism you should know about:

**`bootstrapSpace.mjs:166` creates each environment as a clone of `master`** — `client.environment.createWithId(...)`. A Contentful environment clone copies the source environment's full state at clone time: content types, **entries**, assets, and locales. The repo confirms the clone-copies-state semantics for locales in its own comments (`bootstrapSpace.mjs:69-70`, `:123-124`: *"a clone inherits master's locales as they stood at clone time, and nothing back-fills afterwards"*), and the release workflow at `promoteAlias.mjs:13-17` — *"Create a release environment (clone master...)"* → install template → test → flip alias — only functions as a release mechanism because the clone carries content forward.

So there are exactly **three** ways an entry can appear in an environment here:

| Mechanism | Carries | When |
|---|---|---|
| Environment clone (`bootstrapSpace.mjs:166`) | Whatever the source (`master`) had, one-time snapshot | Environment creation only |
| `seedRegions.mjs` | 11 `region` entries, that's all | Manually, per `--target` |
| Editors in the Contentful web app | Everything else — `footerConfig`, `footerNavGroup`, `link`, `uiCopy` | Continuously |

### The genuine gap this exposes

**There is no forward content promotion in this repo, at all.** A `footerConfig` entry authored in `dev` has no automated path to `test`, `sit`, `staging`, `uat`, or `master`. `installTemplate.mjs`'s promotion chain (`dev → test → sit → staging → uat → master`, `:22`) moves **schema only**. Entries move either backwards (master → new clone) or not at all.

If someone tells you "we promote content dev → prod," that is not what this code does. Content release here is the **alias-flip model** (`promoteAlias.mjs`): author content directly in a release environment cloned from master, install the schema template into it, test it by direct environment ID, then flip the `production` and `master` aliases to it. Under that model the alias flip *is* the content promotion — which makes the `createOrUpdate` bug at `promoteAlias.mjs:70` the single highest-consequence defect I found.</result>

**(a) — content types but zero entries.** Specifically: 5 content types (`footerConfig`, `footerNavGroup`, `link`, `region`, `uiCopy`), their editor interfaces (empty in this template), and **no entries and no assets whatsoever.**

Evidence, in descending order of strength:

1. **The SDK type makes entries structurally impossible.** `EnvironmentTemplateProps.entities` has exactly two keys — `contentTypeTemplates` and `editorInterfaceTemplates` (`environment-template.d.ts:30-33`). There is no field an entry could occupy.
2. **The install payload type is fully enumerated and entry-free:** `{version, takeover?: {items: Link<'ContentType'>[]}, changeSet?, deleteDeletedFields?}` (`environment-template-installation.d.ts:32-39`).
3. **`buildTemplate.js` only ever reads `content-types/*.js`** (`:115-130`) and hardcodes `editorInterfaceTemplates: []` (`:146`). No code path reads entry data.
4. **The repo's own tooling agrees:** `seedRegions.mjs` exists solely because the template can't carry entries, and says so in its header (`:5-8`).
5. **The negative check holds:** the only `entry.create*` / `.publish()` calls in the entire repo are `seedRegions.mjs:71-72`.

### The important caveat: environments are never actually empty in this pipeline

The literal question is (a), but the real-world flow adds a second, distinct entry-transfer mechanism you should know about:

**`bootstrapSpace.mjs:166` creates each environment as a clone of `master`** — `client.environment.createWithId(...)`. A Contentful environment clone copies the source environment's full state at clone time: content types, **entries**, assets, and locales. The repo confirms the clone-copies-state semantics for locales in its own comments (`bootstrapSpace.mjs:69-70`, `:123-124`: *"a clone inherits master's locales as they stood at clone time, and nothing back-fills afterwards"*), and the release workflow at `promoteAlias.mjs:13-17` — *"Create a release environment (clone master...)"* → install template → test → flip alias — only functions as a release mechanism because the clone carries content forward.

So there are exactly **three** ways an entry can appear in an environment here:

| Mechanism | Carries | When |
|---|---|---|
| Environment clone (`bootstrapSpace.mjs:166`) | Whatever the source (`master`) had, one-time snapshot | Environment creation only |
| `seedRegions.mjs` | 11 `region` entries, that's all | Manually, per `--target` |
| Editors in the Contentful web app | Everything else — `footerConfig`, `footerNavGroup`, `link`, `uiCopy` | Continuously |

### The genuine gap this exposes

**There is no forward content promotion in this repo, at all.** A `footerConfig` entry authored in `dev` has no automated path to `test`, `sit`, `staging`, `uat`, or `master`. `installTemplate.mjs`'s promotion chain (`dev → test → sit → staging → uat → master`, `:22`) moves **schema only**. Entries move either backwards (master → new clone) or not at all.

If someone tells you "we promote content dev → prod," that is not what this code does. Content release here is the **alias-flip model** (`promoteAlias.mjs`): author content directly in a release environment cloned from master, install the schema template into it, test it by direct environment ID, then flip the `production` and `master` aliases to it. Under that model the alias flip *is* the content promotion — which makes the `createOrUpdate` bug at `promoteAlias.mjs:70` the single highest-consequence defect I found.</result>

# Contentful CLI Tooling — Local Capability & Danger Audit

## 1. Installed versions

| Package | Version | Provenance | Binary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `contentful-cli` | **4.0.4** | direct dep (`package.json`) | `contentful` |
| `contentful-export` | **8.1.0** | transitive via contentful-cli (`^8.0.0`) | `contentful-export` — **BROKEN, see §6** |
| `contentful-import` | **10.0.0** | transitive via contentful-cli (pinned `10.0.0`) | `contentful-import` |
| `contentful-migration` | **5.1.0** | transitive via contentful-cli (`^5.0.0`) | `contentful-migration` |
| `contentful-management` | 12.3.2 | direct dep (SDK, not CLI) | — |

Only `contentful-cli` and `contentful-management` are direct dependencies. **Nothing in `scripts/`, `package.json`, or `.github/` shells out to any of these CLIs** — the repo's own Contentful tooling uses the `contentful-management` SDK directly. These CLIs are available but currently unused by project automation.

## 2. Command surface

`contentful space`:
```
  space accesstoken         Manage and list your delivery access tokens
  space environment-alias   Manage and list environment aliases
  space create / delete / export / import / list / use
  space environment         Manage and list environments
  space generate            Generate code for different tasks
  space migration           Parses and runs a migration script on a Contentful space
  space seed                Seed a content model and content based on given templates
```

`contentful space environment`: `create`, `delete`, `list`, `use`.

Also relevant to promotion: `contentful merge export|show` (diff two environments, emit a migration script) and `contentful space environment-alias create|list|update`.

> **Help is unreliable past depth 2.** `contentful space environment create --help` prints the *root* help instead — a `.demandCommand(4)` quirk in `dist/lib/cli.js`. Flags for those commands were read from source, not help output.

## 3. Authentication — the documented env var is NOT honoured

`contentful-cli` reads exactly **two** environment variables anywhere in `dist/` (verified by exhaustive grep): `CONTENTFUL_CONFIG_FILE` and `NODE_ENV`. Auth resolution (`dist/lib/context.js`) is:

1. `--management-token` / `--mt` flag, else
2. `managementToken` in a `.contentfulrc.json`, located by:
   ```js
   const pathOverride = process.env.CONTENTFUL_CONFIG_FILE;
   if (pathOverride) { return pathOverride; }
   const defaultPath = resolve(homedir(), contentfulrc);
   const nestedConfigPath = yield findUp(contentfulrc);
   configPath = nestedConfigPath || defaultPath;
   ```

| Tool | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` (repo's var) | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_ACCESS_TOKEN` | `.contentfulrc.json` | Flag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `contentful-cli` | ❌ no | ❌ no | ✅ | `--management-token`/`--mt` |
| `contentful-export` | ❌ (reads **zero** env vars) | ❌ | ❌ | `--management-token` |
| `contentful-import` | ❌ (reads **zero** env vars) | ❌ | ❌ | `--management-token` |
| `contentful-migration` | ❌ no | ✅ **yes** | ✅ (`managementToken` or `cmaToken`) | `--access-token`/`-a` |

**This is a live footgun.** `.env.sample:161` defines `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`, and every repo script consumes it. No CLI here honours that name. `contentful-migration` honours the similar-but-different `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_ACCESS_TOKEN` (`built/bin/lib/config.js:63`). A `--env-file=.env` invocation that "works" for repo scripts will leave the CLI unauthenticated.

**Secondary risk:** `findUp('.contentfulrc.json')` walks up from cwd, so a repo-local file wins over `~/`. `contentful login` / `contentful space use` **writes the plaintext CMA token** to that path (`storeRuntimeConfig`). `.contentfulrc.json` is **not in `.gitignore`** — verified. Today no such file exists anywhere in the tree or in `$HOME`, so this is latent, not active.

## 4. Danger surface

### 4.1 `--environment-id` silently defaults to `master` — and the help text hides it

This is the single highest-risk finding. There are **three** independent `master` defaults:

**(a) Standalone `contentful-import` — documented:**
```
      --environment-id           ID the environment in the destination space
                                                    [string] [default: "master"]
```

**(b) `contentful space export` / `space import` — UNDOCUMENTED.** Help shows *no* default:
```
  --environment-id           ID the environment in the destination space[string]
```
But `dist/lib/utils/middlewares.js` hard-codes it:
```js
const environment = environmentId || activeEnvironmentId;
if (environment) { context.activeEnvironmentId = environment; }
if (!context.activeEnvironmentId) {
    context.activeEnvironmentId = 'master';
}
```
Both commands then pass `environmentId: activeEnvironmentId` straight into the library. **Omitting `--environment-id` on `contentful space import` writes to `master`, and the help text gives no warning.**

**(c) Library-level fallback** in `contentful-import/dist/index.js:1231` (`parseOptions` `defaultOptions`), plus `contentful-migration`'s `[default: "master"]`.

`--space-id` is *asserted* (`assertSpaceIdProvided` throws a helpful error). `--environment-id` has **no equivalent assertion** — it just becomes `master`.

**Note the sticky-state variant:** `contentful space environment use` persists `activeEnvironmentId` to `.contentfulrc.json`. A later `contentful space import` with no flags targets whatever was last "used" — invisible, machine-local state deciding which environment gets written.

### 4.2 `space environment delete` has NO confirmation prompt

`space delete` gates on a prompt:
```js
if (!yes) {
    log(`You are about to delete your ${space.name} ... This cannot be undone.`);
    const confirm = yield confirmation('Do you want to confirm the deletion?');
    if (!confirm) { ... return; }
}
```
`space environment delete` (`environment_cmds/delete.js`) has **no `confirmation()` call and no `--yes` flag** — it goes straight to `yield environment.delete()`. `--environment-id` is `demandOption: true`, so it can't hit an implicit default, but there is zero interactive safety net.

### 4.3 Import overwrites by default

`contentful-import` matches destination entities **by `sys.id`** and updates in place:
```js
function getDestinationEntityForSourceEntity(destinationEntitiesById, sourceEntity) {
  return destinationEntitiesById.get(get(sourceEntity, "sys.id")) || null;
}
const operation = destinationEntity ? updateOperation : "create";
```
`updateDestinationWithSourceData` does `assign(destinationEntity, plainData)` then `.update()` — a clobber of existing content at that ID. Opt out with `--skip-content-updates` / `--skip-asset-updates` (both `default: false`).

### 4.4 Silent field data-loss when `--skip-content-model` is set
```js
if (skipContentModel && err.name === "UnknownField") {
    const errors = get(JSON.parse(err.message), "details.errors");
    entry.transformed.fields = cleanupUnknownFields(entry.transformed.fields, errors);
```
With `--skip-content-model`, fields the destination model doesn't recognise are **stripped and the entry is retried** — the entry lands, quietly missing data. Without that flag, the same case surfaces as an error.

### 4.5 Other
- `--host` defaults to `api.contentful.com`; a wrong value silently retargets a region.
- `--config <file>` can supply *every* option including `spaceId`/`environmentId`, overriding what the command line appears to say.
- Webhooks are master-only: `skip: () => contentModelOnly || environmentId !== "master" && "Webhooks can only be imported in master environment"`.

## 5. ID preservation, publish state, model mismatch

**Entry IDs: preserved.**
```js
return id ? space.createEntryWithId(contentTypeId, id, plainData) : space.createEntry(contentTypeId, plainData);
```
Same `create<Type>WithId` pattern for assets/content types/locales/tags. IDs are stable across environments — which is exactly why §4.3's overwrite-by-ID is dangerous.

**Publish state: preserved, per-entity.**
```js
function publishEntities2({ entities, sourceEntities, requestQueue }) {
  const entityIdsToPublish = sourceEntities.filter(({ original }) => original.sys.publishedVersion).map(({ original }) => original.sys.id);
  const entitiesToPublish = entities.filter((entity) => entityIdsToPublish.indexOf(entity.sys.id) !== -1);
  return publishEntities({ entities: entitiesToPublish, requestQueue });
}
```

`contentful-import` matches destination entities **by `sys.id`** and updates in place:

```js
  return destinationEntitiesById.get(get(sourceEntity, "sys.id")) || null;
```

```js
    entry.transformed.fields = cleanupUnknownFields(entry.transformed.fields, errors);
```
With `--skip-content-model`, fields the destination model doesn't recognise are **stripped and the entry is retried** — the entry lands, quietly missing data. Without that flag, the same case surfaces as an error.

### 4.5 Other
- `--host` defaults to `api.contentful.com`; a wrong value silently retargets a region.
- `--config <file>` can supply *every* option including `spaceId`/`environmentId`, overriding what the command line appears to say.
- Webhooks are master-only: `skip: () => contentModelOnly || environmentId !== "master" && "Webhooks can only be imported in master environment"`.

**Entry IDs: preserved.**
```js

```
Same `create<Type>WithId` pattern for assets/content types/locales/tags. IDs are stable across environments — which is exactly why §4.3's overwrite-by-ID is dangerous.

**Publish state: preserved, per-entity.**
```js
function publishEntities2({ entities, sourceEntities, requestQueue }) {
  const entityIdsToPublish = sourceEntities.filter(({ original }) => original.sys.publishedVersion).map(({ original }) => original.sys.id);
  const entitiesToPublish = entities.filter((entity) => entityIdsToPublish.indexOf(entity.sys.id) !== -1);

}
```

Caveat: `contentful-export` has `--include-drafts` (`default: false`) and `--include-archived` (`default: false`). **Drafts are excluded from the export by default**, so "publish state preserved" only holds for what you actually exported.

**Differing destination content model: allowed, with real caveats.**
- Import fetches only the destination content types matching source IDs (`batchedIdQuery` on `contentTypeIds`) — it does not require the models to be identical.
- Hard blocker: **default locale must match**, or it throws:
  > `Please make sure the destination space have the same default locale as the source`
- With `--skip-content-model`: unknown fields silently dropped (§4.4).
- Without it: content types are imported/updated first, converging the destination model toward the source.
- `--content-model-only` and `--skip-content-model` are mutually exclusive (throws). `--skip-locales` is only valid alongside `--content-model-only` (throws otherwise).

**Model vs. content flags:**

| Flag | Tool | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--content-model-only` (types only) | import | `false` |
| `--skip-content-model` (skips types **and locales**) | both | `false` |
| `--content-only` (entries + assets only) | export | `false` |
| `--skip-content` (skips assets + entries) | export | `false` |
| `--skip-content-publishing` | import | `false` |
| `--skip-content-updates` / `--skip-asset-updates` | import | `false` |
| `--include-drafts` / `--include-archived` | export | `false` |

```
contentful space import --space-id <ID> --environment-id <DEST> --management-token <TOKEN> --content-file <FILE>
```

content.text:
All three agents in, and I've independently verified the load-bearing claims. Here's the whole picture.

---

# What we know

## The two mechanisms are structurally separate

| | Content **types** (schema) | Content (**entries**) |
|---|---|---|
| Mechanism | Org-scoped Environment Template | *nothing automated* |
| Build | `npm run sync:contentful` | — |
| Deploy | `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` | — |
| Source of truth | `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` | the Contentful UI |

**An Environment Template cannot carry entries — this is structural, not a project choice.** The SDK type has exactly two slots:

```ts
// contentful-management/dist/types/entities/environment-template.d.ts:30-33
entities: {
    contentTypeTemplates: Array<ContentTypeTemplateProps>;
    editorInterfaceTemplates: Array<EditorInterfaceTemplateProps>;
};
```

No `entries`, no `assets`. And the install payload's only content reference is `takeover?: {items: Link<'ContentType'>[]}`. The repo knows this — `seedRegions.mjs` exists solely to work around it, and says so in its header.

## The live state

| tier | env | types | entries |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dev** | `dev` | **14** | **42** (+3 assets) |
| test / sit / uat / staging | each own | **0** | **0** |
| prod | *unset* | — | no delivery token |

## Three gaps, in order of severity

**1. The template covers 5 of dev's 14 types.** `footerConfig`, `footerNavGroup`, `link`, `region`, `uiCopy` are in code. The other 9 — `collectionPageExp`, `contentCard`, `homepageContentRow`, `homepageHeroBanner`, `image`, `pdpAccordionContent`, `plpInlineGridInsert`, `product`, `promotionalAnnouncementBanner` — exist only inside the dev environment, authored in the UI, with no code representation. `install:contentful` cannot move them.

**2. There is no forward content promotion in this repo at all.** A `footerConfig` authored in dev has no path to any other tier. The only entry-writing code in the entire repo is `seedRegions.mjs:71-72`, and it handles `region` and nothing else.

**3. The repo's actual release model isn't forward promotion — it's an alias flip.** Per `promoteAlias.mjs`: clone `master` → install the template → author and verify → repoint the `production`/`master` aliases. Content moves *backwards* (master → clone), never forwards. Worth knowing before anyone designs a "promote content to prod" process that the tooling was never built for.

## The CLI is installed, unwired, and won't read our token

`contentful-cli@4.0.4` with `space export` / `space import` — genuine entry migration. No npm script, workflow, or doc invokes it.

**It does not honour `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`.** Verified by exhaustive grep — `contentful-cli` reads only `CONTENTFUL_CONFIG_FILE` and `NODE_ENV`; `contentful-import` and `contentful-export` read **zero** env vars. Auth must come from `--management-token` or `~/.contentfulrc.json`. A `--env-file=.env` invocation that works for repo scripts leaves the CLI unauthenticated.

## Three real bugs found (I verified each)

| file:line | defect | severity |
|---|---|---|
| `promoteAlias.mjs:70` | calls `environmentAlias.createOrUpdate` — **that method appears in 0 files** in `contentful-management@12.3.2`. Throws at runtime on the non-dry-run path | **High** — this is the production cutover script. `bootstrapSpace.mjs:238-240` already documents the fix and does it correctly |
| `installTemplate.mjs:89` | error text says run `npm run build:contentful`; no such script — it's `sync:contentful` | Low |
| `bootstrapSpace.mjs:166` | clone source `'master'` passed in the `headers` slot, not `params.sourceEnvironmentId` | Benign today (Contentful defaults to master anyway); breaks silently if the source ever changes |

Also: `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` §2 still describes the retired per-environment `sync.js` pipeline. `.docs/architecture.md:160-196` is correct on schema but never mentions entries or `seedRegions.mjs`.

---

# What we need

1. **A working CMA token** — still the hard blocker. Nothing below runs without it.
2. **`CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID`** in `.env.shared` — `installTemplate.mjs:77` requires it.
3. **One decision from Integration:** are the 9 UI-only content types *meant* to be code-managed? That determines whether this is a one-off unblock or a backfill of `content-types/`.

---

# What we do

**Immediate — unblock the tester.** All four types the footer needs are in the template, so the governed path works for schema. Entries come across by import, because the template structurally cannot carry them.

**Then — the real question.** test is one of *four* empty tiers, and 9 content types have no code representation. That's an Integration conversation, not a footer fix.

---

# How we do it

Every command below needs the CMA token working first. **Nothing here is safe to run against a token you haven't verified.**

### Step 1 — schema into test

```bash
npm run install:contentful -- --target test --dry-run   # preview: the gate runs in dry-run
npm run install:contentful -- --target test
```

### Step 2 — region entries

```bash
npm run seed:contentful-regions -- --target test
```

⚠️ **No `--dry-run` on this one.** It's the only writing script with no preview mode — it creates *and publishes* 11 live entries immediately. It is idempotent (skips existing IDs), so a re-run is safe; a first run is not previewable.

### Step 3 — the 22 footer entries

`footerConfig` (1) + `footerNavGroup` (3) + `link` (18). Either hand-author them in the test UI, or migrate:

```bash
CMA=$(grep '^CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN=' .env | cut -d= -f2-)

npx contentful space export \
  --space-id u9kb6gp6slxu --environment-id dev \
  --management-token "$CMA" \
  --content-only --content-file footer-entries.json \
  --query-entries "content_type=footerConfig" # repeat per type, or export all and trim

npx contentful space import \
  --space-id u9kb6gp6slxu --environment-id test \
  --management-token "$CMA" \
  --content-file footer-entries.json
```

**Pass `--environment-id` and `--management-token` explicitly, every time.** Reasons, all verified:

- **`--environment-id` silently defaults to `master`** — which is production. On `contentful space import` this default is *undocumented*: the help text shows no default, but `dist/lib/utils/middlewares.js` hard-codes `context.activeEnvironmentId = 'master'`. `--space-id` throws when missing; `--environment-id` just becomes master.
- `contentful space environment use` persists an active environment to `.contentfulrc.json`, so a flagless import targets whatever was last "used" — invisible machine-local state deciding what gets written.
- Import matches by `sys.id` and **updates in place**. Harmless into an empty test; destructive if pointed anywhere populated.
- Export **excludes drafts by default** (`--include-drafts` is `false`), so only published entries move — which is what you want here.
- Entry IDs and publish state are preserved, so test ends up genuinely mirroring dev.

Two caveats: `contentful space import` requires the **default locale to match** between source and destination, or it throws — both were cloned from master, so it should hold, but that's the one thing to watch. And **the standalone `node_modules/.bin/contentful-export` bin is broken** in this install (`yargs@18` is ESM-only; it crashes before parsing arguments). Use `npx contentful space export` as above — the CLI subcommand bundles its own yargs and works.

### Step 4 — verify without deploying

```bash
curl -s "https://cdn.contentful.com/spaces/u9kb6gp6slxu/environments/test/entries?content_type=footerConfig&limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(grep '^CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN=' .env.test | cut -d= -f2-)"
```

`total: 1` means the footer will render. Same command with `sit`/`uat`/`staging` once you repeat steps 1–3 for those.

---

## What I'd flag to Integration before running any of it

`scripts/contentful/` is Tier 2, Integration/SI-owned, and steps 1–3 write to a shared tier. Three things worth their sign-off: whether the four empty tiers are empty *deliberately*; whether the 9 UI-only content types should be backfilled into `content-types/`; and the `promoteAlias.mjs:70` bug, since it means the production cutover path has almost certainly never been executed successfully.

I've changed nothing. Every call I made this session was a GET.

══ memory files: 38 ══

───────── feedback_authorisation_and_scope.md ─────────

**Three levels of authorisation, and they are separate.** During SFCC-55 two commits went in
unasked; the diagnosis was *"'Run it' and the visual check were investigation requests, not commit
approvals."* Marcel's response became a standing rule: *"avoid commiting without my go signal"*,
later escalated mid-turn to *"do not commit and push until my approval."*

Correct shape: **change → verify → stop and show the diff → wait.** This sharpens AGENTS.md Hard
Rule #15 with the distinction the rule leaves implicit — investigate ≠ fix ≠ commit.

**The audit-loop failure mode.** The build became a self-sustaining audit-and-fix cycle; Marcel
called it: *"the work that we've been doing has been a nonstop audit and fix loop ... are we
overengineering and doing work that's outside of the scope."* Measured: 55 commits, a 3.0:1 rework
ratio, `footer/index.tsx` touched **32 times in 5 days**. The verdict was not that the work was
wasted but that it was mis-ordered — *"you are building in the wrong order."*

The diagnostic that separates real work from generated work: *"The six applicable ones fix things
that were actually broken. The seven others came from **reading code we'd just written**."* If a
finding's origin is your own fresh output rather than a spec, a failure, or a review, it is
probably not the next thing to do.

Two concrete correctives:
- **Read the review queue before starting a self-directed pass.** A six-hour-old Major CodeRabbit
  finding named a live security bypass while the loop was polishing comment placement.
- **Ban "it's good practice" as a justification.** A fix needs a named requirement, a reproduced
  failure, or a review comment behind it.

**Present verdicts, don't auto-fix.** Marcel repeatedly asked for findings organised for his call —
*"do not decide for me, i'll make the calls based on the findings"* — and for the ELI5-but-I'm-the-
FED-Lead register. Options with a recommendation, not a completed change.

**Why:** the expensive failures on this project were not bad code, they were unrequested work and
unrequested commits.

**How to apply:** when a task produces a list of possible improvements, separate the ones traceable
to a spec/failure/review from the ones traceable to your own just-written code, and offer the
second group rather than doing them. Related: [[feedback-prove-dont-assert]],
[[feedback-local-only-docs]].

───────── feedback_local_only_docs.md ─────────

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Desktop/fedLead-playbook.md` and
`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Desktop/fedBuild-manual.md` are **local-only files on Marcel's
machine**. They are a legitimate input to the work, but must never be referenced in anything
another person can read: PR review replies, commit messages, or code comments.

Caught in the SFCC-55 session (652997c6) when a CodeRabbit reply cited the playbook as
justification. Marcel: *"it's wrong to mention the fed lead playbook here, because that file is
only local to me, what should we do about this?"* The reply was rewritten to rest on
`AGENTS.md` Hard Rule #4 instead, which reaches the same conclusion from a source the reviewer
can actually open.

Also standing from the same session: **no `Co-Authored-By` line on any commit** — stated as
*"no authored by claude in the commit messages"*. This overrides the default commit trailer.

**Why:** a citation nobody else can verify reads as an appeal to a private authority; it can't be
checked, and for CodeRabbit specifically it teaches the bot nothing (see the in-thread reply rule
in AGENTS.md).

**How to apply:** when a local doc is the real reason for a decision, find the public equivalent
in `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/rules/`, or `.docs/` and cite that. If no public equivalent exists,
argue the merits directly rather than naming the local file. Related: [[feedback-pr-body-standard]].

───────── feedback_message_drafting_audience.md ─────────

**Rule:** when drafting a message for the user to send to a colleague, only include what that
colleague's own role/discipline needs to act — strip anything that's really "how the sausage
got made" on the research/delivery side, even if it's accurate and was hard-won.

**Why:** corrected twice in the same drafting task (2026-08-11, the Booxi/Book-a-Fitting
calendar question from a designer, Kiera Rikard-Bell, to the user). First pass used a "good
news / bad news" framing — rejected as unnecessary editorializing. Second pass still named
Tim Lavelle, a specific PM/BA Teams thread, and "we still need a session with Booxi on
implementation approach" — rejected as oversharing, because Kiera is a designer, not a FED
(front-end developer), and none of that internal delivery-process detail is something she
needs in order to answer her own question. The user's framing: keep the reply "mainly
concerned with the design" for a design audience — i.e. filter by *what changes for the
recipient's own work*, not by what's true or interesting.

**How to apply:** before sending a drafted reply, ask "does the recipient's role change what
they'd do with this fact?" A designer needs to know a vendor's widget would constrain her
visual freedom — she doesn't need to know which internal Teams channel confirmed scope, who
said it, or that a follow-up session hasn't happened yet. Reserve those specifics for messages
to people in the same discipline as the underlying research (PM/delivery/dev), or for the
user's own reference — not for cross-discipline replies. When in doubt, cut toward the
shorter, role-scoped version and let the user ask for more detail if they want it restored.

Related: [[project_calendar_component_gap]].

───────── feedback_pr_body_standard.md ─────────

When opening a PR, match the **actual accepted PRs #46 and #47** as the house-style basis — NOT a freehand body and NOT the literal `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` (the template's `type(scope): SFCC-### desc` title rule is aspirational; the real PRs don't follow it).

**The real convention (from #46/#47):**
- **Title:** plain Conventional Commits — `feat(ci): <short desc>`, **no SFCC key in the title**.
- **Body sections, in order:** `# Description` → `# Linked` → `# Squad ownership` → `# Types of Changes` → `# Changes` → `# How to test-drive this PR` → `# Protection-tier check` → `# Testing`. **Omit** Accessibility / Localisation / Third-party-integrations entirely when they don't apply (don't pad them as "n/a"). No tier *table*, no separate "CodeRabbit pre-merge gates" block.
- **Linked:** `- Ticket: <workstream> under epic **SFCC-1** (Platform Setup & Environments); design in Confluence *Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)* (335216656)` and `- Sprint: SFCC Sprint 2`. (The env/CI/tag-based-promotion work is tracked under **epic SFCC-1** + Confluence 335216656 — NOT SFCC-254 in the PR body, and NOT in the title.)
- **Changes:** plain bullet list.
- **Types of Changes:** tick **New feature** for a `feat(...)`, even CI ones.
- **Protection-tier check:** a `> ⚠️ **Tier 1 change** — <file> ... Authenticated as marcelannavarro, member of @ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers; CODEOWNERS auto-requests review` blockquote, then affirmative `- [x] Tier 1 file(s) modified — owner review required (...)`.
- **Testing:** `[x] ... — N/A` lines + a final `N/A: Storybook / Vitest / Playwright (...)`.

**Why:** 2026-08-06, PR #48. First I opened it with a freehand body (bypassed the standard); the user flagged "not abiding by standards, particularly the body — this was bypassed from me." Then I over-corrected to the literal template (added SFCC-254 to the title, tier table, padded a11y/l10n sections). User: "still off — look into PR 46 and 47 as basis." Fixed by matching #46/#47 exactly.

**How to apply:** Before `gh pr create`, pull the bodies of #46/#47 (`gh pr view 46 --json body`) and mirror their structure/wording. Keep the honesty rule ([[project-pr42-env-security-gotcha]] style): don't tick a box for a step not actually done — mark it N/A explicitly.

───────── feedback_prove_dont_assert.md ─────────

Across the four-day SFCC-55 session (652997c6) the single recurring failure mode was
**verification theatre**: a check built from the same assumption as the thing it was checking,
which therefore passed vacuously. The session's own root-cause line was *"the verification
instrument was built from the same belief as the thing verified, and never made to fail on
purpose."*

Concrete instances, all self-caught after reporting a false all-clear:

- `safeHref` reported "well covered, 3 layers" — 13 test cases contained **zero backslashes**,
  the exact vector CodeRabbit had already named.
- A `fontFace` test had two tests iterating an empty array (`forEach` over `[]`) and missed the
  original bug entirely, because jsdom always provides `window` so every case took the browser branch.
- A mutation test "passed" because `perl -pi` works line-at-a-time and can't match `\n`.
- A recipe parity check false-alarmed three times on recipes whose `baseStyle` is a **function**
  (naive `Object.keys` reports every part missing).
- A literal-count sweep inflated 19→41 by matching `.rem` inside `removeEventListener`.

**Why:** Marcel repeatedly asked for "in-depth, intensive, exhaustive, recursive" V&V with
*"actual value and feasibility tests ran"* rather than face-value acceptance — and the pattern
above is precisely what defeats that. A green check that was never proven capable of going red
carries no information.

**How to apply:** before reporting any check as passing, mutate the thing under test so the check
*must* fail, and confirm it does. State plainly when something is asserted rather than proven —
e.g. a React ref clear is not DOM-observable, so say so instead of implying it was measured.
Related: [[project-test-harness-gaps]].

───────── user_role.md ─────────

Frontend development lead spanning both Squad A and Squad B. First time on this project — completed full onboarding 2026-07-10.

- Covers both squads, so cross-squad coordination questions route to him rather than needing escalation
- New to the codebase; starting with exploration and learning before picking up tickets
- Email: marcel.a.n.navarro@accenture.com
- GitHub login: `marcelannavarro` — confirmed member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` (verified via `gh api orgs/ZimmermannAU/teams/tier-1-approvers/members` on 2026-07-28). Relevant to AGENTS.md's Tier 1 Approval flow — `gh api user --jq .login` should match this. Re-verify if `gh auth status` shows a different account.
- Acts as a PR reviewer on this repo (not just author) — e.g. left a CHANGES_REQUESTED review on PR #42. Other tier-1-approvers seen in the org: `mani060689`, `TimLavelleACC` — likely squad colleagues, not the user.

───────── project_component_structure_decided.md ─────────

Supersedes an earlier note of mine that called this unsettled and said "build flat, don't create
`atoms/`". **That was wrong** — it came from a 19 Aug analysis that was superseded later in the
same session once the decision landed.

**Placement — decided.** Zimmermann design-system components live at:
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/index.tsx`
(today: `zimmButton`, `zimmIcon`, `zimmLogo`, `zimmNavItem`, `zimmTextInput` as atoms;
`zimmInputAction` as the one molecule; no organisms yet).

**Casing — three families, each correct in its own, don't generalise between them:**

| Family | Casing |
|---|---|
| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab — must match upstream's import path |
| **ui-kit component** | **`zimmButton/` camelCase — Zimmermann-authored, the default rule** |
| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase — mirrors upstream exactly |

Kebab-case applies *only* to files mirroring a base Salesforce file. Note also the theme key is
PascalCase (`ZimmTextInput`) while its recipe file is camelCase (`zimmTextInput.ts`).

**Tier — by what the component's own template renders**, not visual size. Atom = renders no other
component; Molecule = only atoms; Organism = ≥1 molecule. An icon passed as a prop doesn't count
(`icon="close"` keeps a Button an atom), and slotted children don't count. When porting from the
F2R library the tier is already recorded as `composes: [...]` — use it rather than re-deriving,
and add `@see f2r/02-design/library/elements/<name>` in the JSDoc.

**Styling surface — decided: a theme recipe, always.** Not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` class,
not co-located CSS. For a bespoke component wrapping a native element, the `chakra()` factory is
the bridge — native semantics plus recipe styling, read via `useMultiStyleConfig`. **Register the
recipe in `theme/components/index.ts` or destructuring throws at runtime.** F2R `.styles.ts` files
using `.zimm-*` classes are a faithful Figma→CSS transcription and good raw material — *convert
them to a recipe, don't copy the pattern*; never reintroduce `.zimm-btn-*`.

The reasoning against co-located CSS is worth keeping: a stylesheet can only see `var(--zimm-*)`,
which is **derived output at the bottom of the token pipeline**. Author there and you lose
`textStyle`, the named `theme.space` scale, semantic colour tokens, responsive arrays, and the
theme drift-guard tests. Not bad CSS — the wrong end of the pipeline.

**Planning fact:** `overrides/app/components/` contains only **seven** directories
(`_app-config`, `button`, `contentful`, `foundation`, `header`, `icons`, `pageContainer`).
`product-tile`, `display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `footer`, `list-menu`,
`drawer-menu`, `seo` are all still `Origin = Base` despite being referenced throughout
`.claude/rules/`. **Assume most stories pay copy-first**, and expect a rules file's worked example
not to exist yet.

**Why:** getting this wrong adds a fifth competing structure, and my own stale version of it would
have sent a future build in the opposite direction from the agreed one.

**How to apply:** source is Marcel's `~/Desktop/fedBuild-manual.md` §2–§3 — **local-only, never
cite it in a PR, commit or code comment** ([[feedback-local-only-docs]]). Cite `conventions.md` /
`components.md` / `overrideStyling.md` instead. Related: [[project-styling-layer-boundary]].

───────── project_styling_layer_boundary.md ─────────

PR #56 set the token architecture: `foundation/*.ts` (source, Tier 1) → `zimmTokens.ts`
(**derived — never hand-edit**) → `theme/components/<name>.ts` recipes consuming
`var(--zimm-*)` → component JSX using only rungs 1–2 (`textStyle="body2"`,
`color="text.default"`).

**`var(--zimm-*)` in component JSX is the violation** — and two separate PRs made it, which is
why it's worth remembering rather than assuming it's obvious. #56's *demonstration* converted
three theme files to `var()`, so a developer skimming the diff concludes "the new convention is
`var()`" without noticing all three were theme files. Results: PR #52 hand-rebuilt in `sx` what
`textStyle="heading3"` already gave, five times over; PR #55 built `cssVars.ts` — 241 lines
mirroring `zimmTokens.ts`'s keys as `var()` strings plus a reimplementation of seven registered
text styles, **recreating one layer up the exact duplication #56 had just deleted**. It was
removed (245 lines, 53 refs across 8 files).

Scale of what #56 fixed: 237 hand-typed literals in `foundation/` → 64, of which **173 were
duplicates** (the same `24px` in `typography.ts` and again in `zimmTokens.ts`).

**The one real exception:** sizing props must use the CSS var, because the scale is registered
as `theme.space` only — see [[project-chakra-scale-registration]].

**Why:** the duplication is invisible until two copies disagree, and both misreads passed
CodeRabbit — it confirmed every correctness finding and raised *zero* architecture findings.

**How to apply:** when a component needs a brand value, reach for `textStyle` or a semantic
token first; if it needs something a Chakra prop can't express, put it in the component's
recipe, not in JSX. When two recipes need the same unresolved value, extract a named constant
(the `navConstants.ts` pattern) rather than typing it twice.

───────── project_chakra_scale_registration.md ─────────

`overrides/app/theme/index.ts` registers the Zimmermann scale as **`space` only**
(`space: spacing`, line 56). `sizes`, `fontSizes`, `lineHeights` and `letterSpacings` are
deliberately **not** registered. Consequences, both measured during SFCC-55 (session 652997c6):

- **Sizing props** (`width`/`height`/`boxSize`/`min|maxWidth|Height`) resolve through
  `theme.sizes`, so a bare key falls through to Chakra's defaults — measured blow-up range
  **8×–112×** (`width: 'xl'` rendered footer contact icons at **576px**). Worse, `s`/`m`/`l` are
  **absent** from Chakra's `sizes`, so those declarations are dropped entirely and silently.
- **Typography props** have the same twin: `fontSize: '2xs'` emits 0.625rem where 0.875rem was
  intended, and `'4xs'` emits nothing at all.

**Always use the CSS var on those props** — `width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'`, never `width: 'xl'`.
Spacing props (`margin`/`padding`/`gap`) are fine with bare keys.

Two related traps from the same work: Chakra resolves a token only as the **entire** value, so
`padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim and dropped by the browser (use axis props); and a
shorthand declared *after* a longhand resets it (`padding: 0` after `paddingBlock` — use
`paddingInline`).

**Live unfixed instance:** `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302` has
`fontSize="l"`, which emits nothing. Pre-existing, outside the footer scope, still there as of
2026-08-22.

**Why:** these fail silently — no error, no warning, just wrong or absent CSS. The 576px icon
bug destroyed the entire footer layout before the cause was found.

**How to apply:** `recipeGuards.test.ts` guards the first two cases (bare key on a sizing prop,
bare key in a compound shorthand) and is mutation-verified — run it after touching any recipe.
`theme/index.ts`'s own header comment lists what is and isn't registered.

───────── project_shared_ui_barrel_trap.md ─────────

The tempting high-leverage play in a slim-overrides project: override
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui/<Name>` so branded styling propagates
into every base SFCC component for free — base cart, checkout and account all inherit
Zimmermann buttons, no import churn, no forked components.

**It does not work.** `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` does `export {Button} from './Button'` — a
**relative** export, which the ccExtensibility resolver does not rewrite. And the consumption
pattern is the wrong way round: **208 base files import the barrel; 0 import
`shared/ui/Button`.** So the override intercepts nothing.

This was asserted confidently once and was wrong; Tim's framing (raw components for Contentful)
turned out to be the correct one. An exception note was added to both Desktop docs.

**Why:** it's an architecturally attractive idea that reads as obviously correct, and the
failure is invisible — the override compiles, resolves, and simply never gets imported.

**How to apply:** before scoping a story around "override X and it propagates", grep the base
package for who actually imports the path you're overriding
(`grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`).
Distinct from, but same family as, the resolver trap already documented in
`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` — Storybook and Vitest don't load the resolver at all, so a
base-path import silently renders the unstyled base component there.

───────── project_figma_metrics_rule.md ─────────

**The discriminator is node type, not a fudge factor.** An earlier version of this memory said
simply "Figma reports the glyph box, CSS reports the line box." That's only true of **text nodes**,
and the missing half is what makes the rule usable:

- **Text nodes** report a **cap-height box** (`text-box-trim: trim-both`, `text-box-edge:
  cap_alphabetic`). **Not comparable** to a CSS line box. Measured artifacts: "KEEP IN TOUCH" 8 vs
  18, body copy 26 vs 36, `errorText` 9 vs 18.
- **Frames and instances** report a **real box**. **Directly comparable** — so a delta here is a
  genuine defect. The `Textfield` *instance* at 44/59 against our 45/68 was a real gap, and the
  naive "it's just cap height" rule would have wrongly dismissed it.

**Supporting heuristic:** a *uniform* residual across siblings is measurement; a *varying* one is a
defect. Three contact items all sitting at +7 after every real cause was removed = the heading's
cap box.

**Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** In shipped `zimmNavItem.ts`, deriving from `lineHeight` +
4.5px padding produced 24/24/24/24/38 = 134 — exactly Figma's `Links` frame.

**There are TWO Figma files and comparisons must be like-for-like from one:**
`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` (design system) and `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (composed page states).
Comparing an initial state from the design-system symbol against an error state from the page file
produced two wrong conclusions in a row — first "the slot is 59px in both states" (actually
`Subscribed=False` 320×44 vs `Subscribed=True` 308×59, with a compensating gap change 40→24: the
design **repositions**, it doesn't reserve), then a "reserve the slot" fix that suppressed intended
growth when the 68px padded box was already design-correct.

**Frames are not breakpoints.** Frames exist at 402/1023/1440; breakpoint tokens are 768/860/1024.
The unframed **768–1022 band was genuinely broken** (18px horizontal scroll, 7 wrapped labels) and
covers three iPad models in portrait. `flexWrap: nowrap` prevents *breaking*, not *shrinking* — the
row refused to break so the words broke instead.

**No automated gate in this stack catches a layout defect.** `width: 'xl'` resolving through
`theme.sizes` (36rem) blew contact icons to 576px and destroyed the footer on every page while
passing tsc, eslint, vitest, local *and* remote CodeRabbit, and Storybook a11y. Only rendering
beside Figma found it.

**Method notes:** measure `y` relative to the component root (Figma reports frame-relative
coordinates); use `domcontentloaded`, never `networkidle`, on a dev server; dismiss the consent
banner first; `Range.getClientRects()` gives per-line widths to *prove* a wrap point;
`document.fonts.check()` returns `true` for unavailable families and is useless — compare widths
instead; and **mutation-test layout fixes at mobile**, since two fixes read as Δ0 at 1440 only
because a taller sibling column masked them.

**How to apply:** before calling any Figma-vs-code delta an artifact, check the node type. Text →
likely artifact, verify uniformity. Frame or instance → treat as real. See
[[feedback-prove-dont-assert]] and [[project-chakra-scale-registration]].

───────── project_test_harness_gaps.md ─────────

All verified live against the installed toolchain on 2026-08-22, not taken from the transcript.

**a11y IS gated — corrects both the SFCC-55 session and an earlier version of this memory.**
The session concluded four separate times that "a11y is not gated, there's no
`.storybook/test-runner.js`". That was **Storybook 8 knowledge and is wrong for what's installed.**
`@storybook/test-runner@0.24.4`'s `dist/setup-page-script.js:390-402` reads
`parameters.a11y.test` and rejects when it `=== "error"`; `.storybook/preview.tsx` sets exactly
that; `addon-a11y@10.4.6` runs `axe.run` with `initialGlobals.manual: false`; `axe-core@4.11.4` is
present. **No `test-runner.js` is needed — do not remove that `preview.tsx` a11y block.**
Honest caveat: the gate has never been made to fail on purpose, so by the project's own standard
it is unproven, just not absent.

**A skipped required check counts as passing.** Live on PR #59: `gh pr checks 59` shows all four
suites `skipping` — including both *required* checks — while `mergeable: true`. Cause:
`detect-changes` uses `since_last_remote_commit: true`, and a final push touching only
`.claude/registry/components.md` + `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` fell outside every allow-list.
A 64-commit, ~5,000-line PR became merge-eligible with **zero test evidence on its head SHA**.
Always read `gh pr checks` for `skipping`, not just for green.

**Gated nowhere at all** (grepped all 15 workflows): `eslint`, `prettier`, `tsc --noEmit`, any CSS
bundle budget. `npm run lint` currently fails repo-wide on 19 pre-existing prettier errors and CI
never notices. `bundlesize` never runs on a PR to `develop`.

**A named gate that cannot fail:** `digital-sit.yml`'s "MuleSoft contract tests" runs
`npm run test:contracts`, which is `echo 'TODO…' && exit 0` — and it's a hard `needs` of
`sit-gate`.

**A Tier 1 rule that breaks if followed verbatim:** `.claude/rules/testing.md:87` prescribes
`@storybook/test`, which is **not installed** — Storybook 10 moved it to `storybook/test`, which is
what the live footer story imports. Line 100's "never reach into `document`" also lacks the portal
carve-out that portalled dialogs need.

**Still-true harness traps:** `test-storybook` needs a **built** Storybook (dev-server runs made
four mutation results uninterpretable); **Vitest does not run `play`**; **`extendTheme` does not
populate `theme.__cssMap`** — only `ChakraProvider` does via `toCSSVar`, so a direct `css()(theme)`
assertion passes vacuously; **jsdom always provides `window`**, so an SSR branch needs
`// @vitest-environment node`; every jsdom rect is 0, so layout assertions there are meaningless.

**E2E reality:** the only spec in the repo is `SMOKE-homepage-load.spec.js`, so `@SFCC-55`-scoped
BrowserStack runs matched zero tests — a silent no-op, not a pass.

**Why:** each of these makes a green or absent signal look like evidence. The a11y one is the most
dangerous in reverse — believing it's ungated invites deleting the thing that gates it.

**How to apply:** verify a gate against the installed package version before claiming it does or
doesn't run. See [[feedback-prove-dont-assert]].

The unframed **768–1022 band was genuinely broken** (18px horizontal scroll, 7 wrapped labels) and
covers three iPad models in portrait. `flexWrap: nowrap` prevents *breaking*, not *shrinking* — the
row refused to break so the words broke instead.

**No automated gate in this stack catches a layout defect.** `width: 'xl'` resolving through
`theme.sizes` (36rem) blew contact icons to 576px and destroyed the footer on every page while
passing tsc, eslint, vitest, local *and* remote CodeRabbit, and Storybook a11y. Only rendering
beside Figma found it.

**Method notes:** measure `y` relative to the component root (Figma reports frame-relative
coordinates); use `domcontentloaded`, never `networkidle`, on a dev server; dismiss the consent
banner first; `Range.getClientRects()` gives per-line widths to *prove* a wrap point;
`document.fonts.check()` returns `true` for unavailable families and is useless — compare widths
instead; and **mutation-test layout fixes at mobile**, since two fixes read as Δ0 at 1440 only
because a taller sibling column masked them.

**How to apply:** before calling any Figma-vs-code delta an artifact, check the node type. Text →
likely artifact, verify uniformity. Frame or instance → treat as real. See
[[feedback-prove-dont-assert]] and [[project-chakra-scale-registration]].

───────── project_test_harness_gaps.md ─────────

All verified live against the installed toolchain on 2026-08-22, not taken from the transcript.

**a11y IS gated — corrects both the SFCC-55 session and an earlier version of this memory.**
The session concluded four separate times that "a11y is not gated, there's no
`.storybook/test-runner.js`". That was **Storybook 8 knowledge and is wrong for what's installed.**
`@storybook/test-runner@0.24.4`'s `dist/setup-page-script.js:390-402` reads
`parameters.a11y.test` and rejects when it `=== "error"`; `.storybook/preview.tsx` sets exactly
that; `addon-a11y@10.4.6` runs `axe.run` with `initialGlobals.manual: false`; `axe-core@4.11.4` is
present. **No `test-runner.js` is needed — do not remove that `preview.tsx` a11y block.**
Honest caveat: the gate has never been made to fail on purpose, so by the project's own standard
it is unproven, just not absent.

**A skipped required check counts as passing.** Live on PR #59: `gh pr checks 59` shows all four
suites `skipping` — including both *required* checks — while `mergeable: true`. Cause:
`detect-changes` uses `since_last_remote_commit: true`, and a final push touching only
`.claude/registry/components.md` + `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` fell outside every allow-list.
A 64-commit, ~5,000-line PR became merge-eligible with **zero test evidence on its head SHA**.

bundle budget. `npm run lint` currently fails repo-wide on 19 pre-existing prettier errors and CI

every page, and mobile LCP (≤ 2s p75) is a top project priority. That growth is currently
ungated in both directions — nothing fails if CSS doubles.

enforcing, it's a new `bundlesize` entry (Tier 1 — `package.json` root), not a config that
already exists. Fix the stale `projectState.md` line at the same time.

───────── project_coverage_threshold ─────────

**There is no unit-test coverage percentage for the PWA frontend repo (this repo).** Testing is deliberately risk-based, not percentage-based. Re-verified 2026-08-06 by an exhaustive triangulated scan (codebase+config, Confluence 14 CQL / full 185-page tree, Jira 22 JQL / all 4 projects) — all three surfaces agree.

- This PWA repo: `test` = `vitest run` (no `--coverage`), no `test:coverage` script, no `@vitest/coverage-*` installed, `vitest.config.ts` has no `coverage` thresholds (+ `passWithNoTests: true`), no codecov/sonar/.nycrc, and `qa.yml`'s `unit-tests` job just runs `npm test` (pass/fail, no coverage gate). - **Actual inventory as of 2026-08-06:** only **2** unit-test files exist repo-wide, both hooks — `useCountryConfig.test.ts` (10 tests) + `useContentfulClient.test.ts` (5 tests) = **15 tests**. Untested logic-and-risk hotspots: the Tier 1 `overrides/app/ssr/` helpers (CSP, SLAS auth, payment metadata) and the pages/.

No dedicated Testing/QA epic exists; unit tests appear only as an unquantified pipeline step in SFCC-1.

**Why:** Both repos live in the same SFCC Confluence space, so the backend's 90% Jest threshold is easy to misread as a frontend requirement.
**How to apply:** If asked for the PWA's coverage target, answer "none — risk-based selective testing." Don't wire a coverage threshold into `vitest.config.ts`/`qa.yml` on the strength of the 90% Confluence figure. Related: [[reference-confluence-sfcc]].

───────── project_story_decomposition_pattern ─────────

The team decomposes UI work as **component-based user stories**. As of 2026-08-11 this is
formally documented, not just informal precedent — see Confluence **"04.71 Writing User
Stories for Components"** (page 400195600, v2, brand new, zero comments; child of **"04.7
Component Inventory"**, page 400195591, v13, mapped 1:1 to Figma "Zimmermann_Design_System_2026").
Formal rule set:

- **Level 1 — Component epics** (the "build" story): PWA-Kit-only components (Button,
  Textfield, Dropdown, Cart Item) get **one** story in the PWA Kit epic. Contentful+PWA-Kit
  components (Banner, Editorial Cards, Footer, Navigation) get **two** stories — one in the
  Contentful epic (content model/authoring/validation), one in PWA Kit (rendering) — "a
  Contentful component always needs a PWA Kit story too; a PWA-Kit-only component does not
  need a Contentful story."
- **Level 2 — Page epics** (the "experience" story, e.g. PDP/PLP/Checkout): shopper-perspective,
  how components work together on that page; must NOT repeat Level-1 build detail.
- Doesn't explicitly address SFCC-commerce-data-sourced components (vs. Contentful) — per
  components.md's container/presentational rule these should default to "PWA Kit only" since
  SFCC is an API contract, not editorially authored content — but confirm this reading rather
  than assuming it.

**Epic structure corrected:** the components epic is **SFCC-2 "PWA Kit Components"** (status
To Do; "the shared UI component library... consumed across all frontend epics," page-level
build carved into separate epics) — NOT SFCC-1, which is "Platform Setup & Environments" and
unrelated. Page epics: SFCC-5 PDP, SFCC-6 PLP, SFCC-7 Search & Recommendations, SFCC-11 Cart,
SFCC-19 Regional Storefronts.

**The pattern is already the dominant real-world shape, not aspirational** — confirmed across
Cart (SFCC-11, 20 stories), PLP (SFCC-6, 17), PDP (SFCC-5, 18), Search (SFCC-7, 19): nearly
every story is a single component/feature slice. Live examples: filters = SFCC-104 (BM config,
shared) → SFCC-108 (Search filter UI component) → SFCC-199 (PLP integration, Ready For Review);
Recently Viewed = SFCC-83 (shared component, Tech design, 3 SP) with consent peeled out into
SFCC-106; SFCC-195 (PDP "Details & Care" slide-out tab, Ready For Review) slices only one tab —
siblings SFCC-102/267/266/101 cover the other tabs separately.

**Surviving old-style broad stories** (good "before" examples to raise at the meeting):
SFCC-90 "Homepage Layout & Content Modules UI" (5 SP, In Refinement) bundles 6 distinct content
modules into one ticket with no sub-split. SFCC-52 "Global Header UI" / SFCC-55 "Global Footer
UI" (3 SP each, Ready for Development) are partially decomposed — self-limited to "shell and
layout only" with icon destinations/link wiring/Omneo integration carved out — but still bundle
multiple components per ticket.

**Live worked examples, seeded the morning of 2026-08-11** (hours before a "components ways of
working" meeting) by Isabel "Izzy" Chaloner (Delivery Lead), all parented under SFCC-2:
SFCC-691/692/694 (Title and Link Component × PWA Kit / Contentful / PDP) and SFCC-698/699/700
(Editorial Cards Module × Contentful / PWA Kit / PLP). Both source components are deliberately
from the design-system inventory's "Not Confirmed" rows — teaching examples, not committed work.
Note: the "— PDP"/"— PLP" (Level-2-shaped) variants are reportedly ALSO parented under SFCC-2
rather than SFCC-5/SFCC-6 — worth confirming whether that's intentional or simplified for
illustration only.

An earlier, rougher precursor predates the formal doc: SFCC-648 "pdp/size-selector" and SFCC-650
"pdp/add-to-bag" (created 2026-08-07 by Jasmijn Tsang, Lead BA, under SFCC-2), lowercase
code-path-style titles, splitting the bundled SFCC-92 "PDP — Size Selection & Add to Bag"
(Blocked, 5 SP) into atomic pieces.

My reusable heuristic for cutting a UI story (worked example: SFCC-195 PDP accordion,
2026-08-07) — still holds, now reinforced by 04.71:
1. **Slice by data source, not by UI surface** (one story per tab is the wrong cut). Group
   tabs/sections that share a data path (SFCC attr / Contentful / AP21).
2. **Split again where risk/readiness differs** — unconfirmed attribute, unauthored content,
   unbuilt integration.
3. **Every story a vertical slice** — give a "shell"/enabler story a real first slice so it's
   demoable, never a horizontal orphan.
4. **Quarantine later-sprint / other-squad work** (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #14) — carve it out as a
   deferred dependency and design the current build to **degrade gracefully** ("renders now,
   wired later"). Example: PDP Assistance tab's "Start a Chat" → Inside Chat is Squad B /
   Sprint 7, consent-gated (Didomi) — keep Assistance bundled with Shipping & Returns and defer
   only the chat trigger.
5. **Offer sub-tasks, not more stories,** when a BA wants finer granularity.
6. **Check the ticket against source-of-truth docs** — flag anything it assumes that the PRD
   still lists as open (e.g. `.docs/temp/openItems.md` #2: SFCC-vs-Contentful ownership on
   composed PDP/PLP pages is still unconfirmed — this directly blocks cleanly deciding some
   Level-1 "which epic(s) does this need a story in" calls for composed-page components).

Full write-up previously referenced as `learning/2026-08-07-user-story-breakdown.md` **no
longer exists on disk** (checked 2026-08-11, both `./learning/` and `./.docs/learning/` are
empty) — don't cite it as available; this memory file is the source of truth instead.

Component Inventory"**, page 400195591, v13, mapped 1:1 to Figma "Zimmermann_Design_System_2026").
Formal rule set:

- **Level 1 — Component epics** (the "build" story): PWA-Kit-only components (Button,
  Textfield, Dropdown, Cart Item) get **one** story in the PWA Kit epic. Contentful+PWA-Kit
  components (Banner, Editorial Cards, Footer, Navigation) get **two** stories — one in the
  Contentful epic (content model/authoring/validation), one in PWA Kit (rendering) — "a

  need a Contentful story."
- **Level 2 — Page epics** (the "experience" story, e.g. PDP/PLP/Checkout): shopper-perspective,

  SFCC is an API contract, not editorially authored content — but confirm this reading rather

**Epic structure corrected:** the components epic is **SFCC-2 "PWA Kit Components"** (status
To Do; "the shared UI component library... consumed across all frontend epics," page-level
build carved into separate epics) — NOT SFCC-1, which is "Platform Setup & Environments" and
unrelated. Page epics: SFCC-5 PDP, SFCC-6 PLP, SFCC-7 Search & Recommendations, SFCC-11 Cart,
SFCC-19 Regional Storefronts.

**The pattern is already the dominant real-world shape, not aspirational** — confirmed across
Cart (SFCC-11, 20 stories), PLP (SFCC-6, 17), PDP (SFCC-5, 18), Search (SFCC-7, 19): nearly
every story is a single component/feature slice. Live examples: filters = SFCC-104 (BM config,
shared) → SFCC-108 (Search filter UI component) → SFCC-199 (PLP integration, Ready For Review);
Recently Viewed = SFCC-83 (shared component, Tech design, 3 SP) with consent peeled out into
SFCC-106; SFCC-195 (PDP "Details & Care" slide-out tab, Ready For Review) slices only one tab —
siblings SFCC-102/267/266/101 cover the other tabs separately.

**Surviving old-style broad stories** (good "before" examples to raise at the meeting):
SFCC-90 "Homepage Layout & Content Modules UI" (5 SP, In Refinement) bundles 6 distinct content
modules into one ticket with no sub-split. SFCC-52 "Global Header UI" / SFCC-55 "Global Footer
UI" (3 SP each, Ready for Development) are partially decomposed — self-limited to "shell and
layout only" with icon destinations/link wiring/Omneo integration carved out — but still bundle
multiple components per ticket.

**Live worked examples, seeded the morning of 2026-08-11** (hours before a "components ways of
working" meeting) by Isabel "Izzy" Chaloner (Delivery Lead), all parented under SFCC-2:
SFCC-691/692/694 (Title and Link Component × PWA Kit / Contentful / PDP) and SFCC-698/699/700
(Editorial Cards Module × Contentful / PWA Kit / PLP). Both source components are deliberately
from the design-system inventory's "Not Confirmed" rows — teaching examples, not committed work.
Note: the "— PDP"/"— PLP" (Level-2-shaped) variants are reportedly ALSO parented under SFCC-2

An earlier, rougher precursor predates the formal doc: SFCC-648 "pdp/size-selector" and SFCC-650
"pdp/add-to-bag" (created 2026-08-07 by Jasmijn Tsang, Lead BA, under SFCC-2), lowercase

My reusable heuristic for cutting a UI story (worked example: SFCC-195 PDP accordion,
2026-08-07) — still holds, now reinforced by 04.71:
1. **Slice by data source, not by UI surface** (one story per tab is the wrong cut). Group
   tabs/sections that share a data path (SFCC attr / Contentful / AP21).
2. **Split again where risk/readiness differs** — unconfirmed attribute, unauthored content,

3. **Every story a vertical slice** — give a "shell"/enabler story a real first slice so it's

4. **Quarantine later-sprint / other-squad work** (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #14) — carve it out as a
