## 3. Rule-by-rule: what each catches, and what it misses

### ast-grep — all three are `severity: warning`, so all three are review comments, not failures

**`img-missing-alt`** (`.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/img-missing-alt.yml:6-14`) — any JSX element whose name matches `^img$` with no attribute matching `^alt\b`.
> **Blind spot:** the regex is anchored lowercase-only. This is a **Chakra UI v2** codebase, where the idiomatic element is `<Image>`, not `<img>` — and `<Image>`, `<AspectRatio><Image/></AspectRatio>`, and any `<ZimmImage>` wrapper are all invisible to this rule. Also `alt={undefined}` and `alt={maybeUndefinedVar}` satisfy the check textually while producing no accessible name at runtime; conversely `{...imgProps}` carrying a real `alt` is flagged as a false positive.

**`icon-button-missing-aria-label`** (`.../icon-button-missing-aria-label.yml:6-14`) — name matching `^IconButton` (prefix, so `IconButtonWithRegistration` is correctly caught) without `^aria-label\b`.
> **Blind spot, and it's a nasty one:** `\b` after `label` requires a non-word character next. In `aria-labelledby` the next character is `l`, so **`aria-labelledby` does not satisfy the rule** — a correct, spec-compliant a11y pattern gets flagged as a violation. In the other direction, an aliased import (`import {IconButton as IB}` → `<IB>`), a differently-named wrapper (`ZimmIconButton`), or an icon-only `<Button><SearchIcon/></Button>` all evade entirely.

**`clickable-non-interactive-element`** (`.../clickable-non-interactive-element.yml:6-18`) — a fixed list (`div|span|Box|Flex|Stack|VStack|HStack|Grid|Text|PopoverFooter|PopoverHeader`) with an `onClick` attribute and no `role`.
> **Blind spots, three of them.** (a) The element list is closed; `Center`, `SimpleGrid`, `GridItem`, `Container`, `Card`, `Wrap`, `li`, `td`, `section`, `Heading`, `Badge`, `Tag` all evade. (b) It checks only for the *presence* of `role` — `role="presentation"` and `role="none"`, which are the exact opposite of correct, satisfy it. (c) `.claude/rules/components.md` requires `role` **plus `tabIndex={0}` plus `onKeyDown`**; the rule checks none of the latter two, so `<div role="button" onClick={...}>` with zero keyboard support passes the machine check and still fails WCAG. Also `onMouseDown`/`onPointerDown` evade.

`utils/jsx-element.yml:4-7` defines the shared `jsxElement` util as `jsx_opening_element` OR `jsx_self_closing_element` — correct, covers both forms.

Note `essential_rules: true` (`coderabbit.yaml:368`) means CodeRabbit *also* runs its own built-in ast-grep packs on top of these three.

### semgrep — both `severity: ERROR`, both `languages: [typescript]`

**`payment-credential-logged`** (`semgrep.yml:5-26`) — taint mode. Sources: a function parameter (`:15-18`) or a `const` declaration (`:20-23`) whose name matches `(?i)(cardNumber|cvv|pin|cardNum|pan)`. Sinks: `console.$METHOD(...)` and `Sentry.$METHOD(...)` (`:25-26`).
> **Blind spots — the sink list is the big one.** `.claude/rules/conventions.md` bans these values from *"any `console.*` call, Sentry breadcrumb/event, GTM dataLayer push, analytics event, MRT access log, or response body"* and from `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`/IndexedDB/cookies and query strings. **Only two of those are sinks.** `dataLayer.push({cvv})`, `localStorage.setItem('pin', pin)`, `logger.info(cvv)`, a `fetch()` query string, and a returned response body all pass clean.
> **Source blind spots:** `let`/`var` are not sources (only `const`). Property access — `formData.cvv`, `card.cardNumber` — is not a source. Destructuring (`const {cvv} = form`) does not bind `$VAR` to an identifier. And the name list misses **`cvc`**, the Visa/Mastercard spelling, plus `securityCode`. Aliasing the sink (`const log = console.log; log(cvv)`) evades.
> **False-positive risk:** the regex is unanchored substring, so `spinner`, `pinned`, `pinnedItems` all match `pin`.

**`dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized`** (`semgrep.yml:28-35`) — matches the JSX attribute form and excludes anything of shape `$SANITIZER.sanitize(...)`.
> **Blind spot, evasion side:** any object property spread evades — `<div {...{dangerouslySetInnerHTML:{__html: dirty}}} />`, `const props = {...}; <div {...props} />`, or `React.createElement('div', {dangerouslySetInnerHTML:{__html: dirty}})`. And the exclusion matches *any* receiver with a `.sanitize()` method, so a no-op `noop.sanitize(dirty)` passes.
> **Blind spot, false-positive side — this one will bite daily:** the exclusion requires the sanitizer call to be **inline in the JSX**. The normal, correct pattern —
> ```tsx
> const clean = DOMPurify.sanitize(dirty)
> return <div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html: clean}} />
> ```
> — does not match `pattern-not`, so **properly sanitized code gets flagged as an XSS ERROR.** So does `sanitizeHtml(dirty)` (the `sanitize-html` package's bare-function default export, no `.sanitize` receiver).
> `overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx:6` documents that it deliberately avoids `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` entirely, so the repo has no live instance to calibrate against yet.

Both rules declare `languages: [typescript]`. Whether semgrep's `typescript` target reliably parses `.tsx` in the version CodeRabbit runs is **something I could not determine from this repo** — the ast-grep rules alongside them explicitly declare `language: tsx`, which suggests the distinction was considered there and not here. Worth an empirical check before relying on either rule to cover component files.

## 4. Git hooks — prevention vs. best-effort

Managed by Husky v9 via `"prepare": "husky"` (`package.json:52`). The `.husky/*` files are one-line delegators: `.husky/pre-commit:1` → `bash scripts/hooks/pre-commit`, `.husky/commit-msg:1` → `bash scripts/hooks/commit-msg "$1"`, `.husky/pre-push:1` → `bash scripts/hooks/pre-push`.

**`pre-commit`** (`scripts/hooks/pre-commit`, 324 lines) does five things:
1. Resolves `node` through nvm/fnm/volta, hard-fails if absent (`:22-42`).
2. Regenerates `.claude/registry/` and auto-stages it when `overrides/app/{components,hooks,utils,pages}` or `routes.tsx` is staged (`:49-62`).
3. Regenerates derived AI-config files via `syncCursorRules.mjs --fix` and auto-stages them when a `.claude/rules/*.md` or `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` is staged; **blocks** on failure (`:71-87`). Warns (does not block) when a SKILL.md changes without `.claude/skills/README.md` also staged, plus a Confluence reminder (`:97-118`).
4. Regenerates Contentful `definitions.ts` from staged `experiences/*.tsx` and **blocks** on codegen failure (`:126-160`).
5. **Blocks** direct edits to derived config (`.cursor/rules/`, `.vscode/instructions/`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`) when the `.claude/` source isn't co-staged (`:171-250`), and **blocks** `.env.sample` commits where a secret-class key has a non-empty value or the value looks like a JWT / 32+ hex / 40+ base64 / a known provider prefix (`:264-322`).

> **What `pre-commit` does NOT do: it runs no lint, no `tsc`, and no tests.** Nothing local checks that your code compiles before it becomes a commit.

**`commit-msg`** (`scripts/hooks/commit-msg`) — blocks anything not matching `^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|upstream-sync)(\([a-z0-9/._-]+\))?: .{1,100}$` (`:17`), with a pass-through for `Merge|Revert|fixup!|squash!|WIP` (`:10-12`). Scope must be lowercase — `feat(ProductTile):` is rejected. Subject capped at 100 chars.

**`pre-push`** (`scripts/hooks/pre-push`) — rejects malformed `v*` tags, allowing only `vX.Y.Z-rc.N`, `vX.Y.Z`, `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N` (`:20-21`). Keys on the **remote** ref, so `git push origin branch:refs/tags/vX` is also caught (`:16-17`); skips deletions (`:28`). Its own header (`:4-7`) is candid: on the Team plan ruleset `tag_name_pattern` is Enterprise-only, so **this hook is the primary prevention** and `tag-validate.yml` is post-hoc detection only. Non-`v*` tags and all branch pushes pass untouched — **`pre-push` runs no tests, lint, or type-check.**

**Bypass:** every one of these is defeated by `git commit --no-verify` / `git push --no-verify`, by `npm install --ignore-scripts` (Husky never installs), or by a fresh clone where `prepare` didn't run. `scripts/hooks/README.md:19-21` states hooks should not be bypassed and points at AGENTS.md hard rule 13. **All three are best-effort, none are prevention.** The only hook whose bypass has no server-side backstop is `pre-push` — CodeRabbit checks commit format at PR time (`coderabbit.yaml:129-135`), and CI can't un-push a bad tag.

**Separate layer — Claude Code's own hooks** (`.claude/settings.json`): a `PreToolUse` hook blocks Write/Edit on `develop`/`main` (`:9`), `tier2Warn.sh` warns non-blockingly (`:13`), a `PostToolUse` Prettier format-on-Write (`:24`), plus `contentfulDriftWarn.sh`, `registryUpdate.sh`, `testFileRemind.sh`. All four helper scripts exist in `.claude/hooks/`. These govern only what Claude does — they are invisible to a human editing in an IDE.

## 5. `protected-file-guard.yml` and the tier system

Trigger: `pull_request` to `develop`, `main`, `release/**`; types `opened, synchronize, reopened` (`:8-13`).

- **`tier1-guard` — "🔴 Tier 1 — Frozen Files Check"** (`:39`). Prints a loud banner and an owner-contact map when a Tier 1 path changes (`:97-139`). **Explicitly NOT a required check** — the 20-line comment at `:24-37` documents why: GitHub's Feb-2025 lockdown of cross-run check-run updates made a "fail-until-approved, flip-on-review" required check impossible to build. **The real gate is CODEOWNERS + `require_code_owner_reviews`**, which I verified is `true` on all three branches.
- **`branch-target-guard` — "🔴 Branch Target Check"** (`:150`) — **the only required check that always runs.** It asserts exactly one thing (`:165`): `base == main && head == feature/*` → fail. Nothing else.
- **`tier2-warning` — "🟡 Tier 2 — Protected Files Warning"** (`:187`) — posts/updates a PR comment with a checklist (`:251-268`). Non-blocking by design (`:184-185`).
- **`cross-squad-guard` — "🟡 Cross-Squad Boundary Check"** (`:307`) — comments when a PR touches both Squad A (`:324-336`) and Squad B (`:343-355`) paths. Non-blocking.

### Path-coverage drift I verified (this is the actionable part)

`CODEOWNERS` has **no catch-all `*` rule** (verified — 190 lines, no default owner). So a path absent from CODEOWNERS requires **no** code-owner review, regardless of what `frozenFiles.md` says.

| Path | frozenFiles/protectedFiles tier | In CODEOWNERS? | In guard's tier1/tier2 list? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `babel.config.js` | **Tier 1** (Build Pipeline) | **NO** | **NO** |
| `tsconfig.json` | **Tier 1** (Build Pipeline) | **NO** | **NO** |
| `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts` | **Tier 2** | **NO** | **NO** |
| `overrides/app/ssr/**` (CSP, SLAS tokens) | Tier 1 | yes (`CODEOWNERS:46`) | **NO** |
| `vitest.setup.ts` | Tier 1 | yes (`:57`) | **NO** |
| `.browserstack.yml` | Tier 1 | yes (`:60`) | **NO** |
| `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` / `contentful.ts` | Tier 1 | yes (`:47-48`) | **NO** |
| `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/` | Tier 2 | yes (`:93`) | **NO** |
| `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`, `scripts/contentful/*` | Tier 2 | yes (`:139`, `:146-148`) | **NO** |

Two of these are real holes rather than cosmetic warning gaps: **`babel.config.js` and `tsconfig.json` are declared Tier 1 in `frozenFiles.md` but have zero enforcement anywhere** — no code owner, no warning. `tsconfig.json` is what enforces strict mode and the path aliases; `babel.config.js` is the other half of the alias config. **`overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`** is Tier 2 per `protectedFiles.md`, emits CSS on every page, and is likewise ungated — `CODEOWNERS:117` covers `theme/components/` only, and `globalStyles.ts` sits one level up.

`overrides/app/ssr/**` is the interesting middle case: the **real** gate (CODEOWNERS) works, but `protected-file-guard.yml:73` uses the glob `overrides/app/ssr.*`, which matches `ssr.js` but not `ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts`. So a CSP change gets a silent PR with no Tier 1 banner — the reviewer's most visible signal is missing on one of the highest-blast-radius files in the repo.

Finally, `CODEOWNERS:186` — `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only. CODEOWNERS is **last-match-wins**, so this deliberately *downgrades* a co-located style file inside `header/` or `footer/` out of Tier 2 (documented at `:178-186`, and flagged as an open governance question in `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`).

## 7. What bites you — ten traps

**1. A docs-only final commit turns both required checks green. This already happened.**
`qa.yml:72` diffs against the previous push, not the merge base. On PR #59 the last commit was `604ece54 docs: reconcile the bootstrap docs...`, and `gh pr checks 59` shows the final state: `Unit tests (Vitest) — skipping`, `Storybook interaction & a11y tests — skipping`, `Playwright E2E (localhost) — skipping`, `Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack) — skipping`. A PR that rewrote the entire footer merged with **both required test gates reporting skipped-as-passing** on the merged SHA. The `qa.yml:66-71` comment argues this is safe because "nothing relevant changed since the last time those suites ran" — but that reasoning silently assumes the earlier run *passed*. **If a push fails unit tests and you then push a docs-only commit, the required check flips to green.** As a lead: read the *history* of check runs on a PR, not the current state, and treat "skipping" on the head SHA as "unverified," not "passed."

**2. `detect-changes` failing green-lights the PR.**
Both required test jobs carry `needs: detect-changes` plus a plain `if:` (`qa.yml:210-211`, `:239-240`), so GitHub's implicit `success()` over `needs` applies. If `detect-changes` fails — a `tj-actions/changed-files` hiccup, a filename with shell metacharacters, a `git fetch` failure at `qa.yml:190-194` — both jobs skip, and skipped required checks pass (`qa.yml:22`). The single most load-bearing job in the pipeline is not itself a required check.

**3. A header-only change gets the *narrowest* E2E scope despite the *widest* blast radius.**
`e2e_homepage` (`qa.yml:97-102`) includes `overrides/app/components/header/**`. The subset check at `qa.yml:139-146` narrows to `--grep "@homepage"` when every changed file is in that list. So a PR touching only the global header — Tier 2, renders on every page — runs *only* homepage E2E. Checkout, PDP, and account journeys never execute. (And E2E isn't a required check anyway, so it's a warning-of-a-warning.)

**4. `main` has no test gate, and `Branch Target Check` barely checks anything.**
`main` requires exactly one status: `🔴 Branch Target Check`, whose entire assertion is `base == main && head == feature/*` (`protected-file-guard.yml:165`). A `fix/*` branch targeting `main` directly passes it. A `release/*` or `hotfix/*` → `main` passes trivially. Combined with `dismissesStaleReviews: false` and `requireLastPushApproval: false` on `main`, you can secure an approval and then push anything before merging.

**5. `babel.config.js`, `tsconfig.json`, and `globalStyles.ts` are declared protected and are enforced nowhere.**
`frozenFiles.md` calls the first two Tier 1 Build Pipeline; `protectedFiles.md` calls the third Tier 2. None appear in CODEOWNERS, and CODEOWNERS has no catch-all. **`.claude/rules/` is documentation, not configuration** — the tier a file *is* equals the tier CODEOWNERS says it is. When onboarding, teach people to check `CODEOWNERS`, not `frozenFiles.md`, if they want to know what will actually block.

`coderabbit.yaml:391-393` sets `ignore_title_keywords: ["chore(deps)", "dependabot"]`. Title-matched, not author-matched — so a human PR titled `chore(deps): bump the thing` gets **no CodeRabbit review at all**, including no semgrep, no ast-grep, no gitleaks. Combined with `drafts: false` (`:389`), a PR that stays in draft is also never reviewed. Neither state is visible as a failing check; it just looks quiet.

**7. The semgrep XSS rule flags the *correct* pattern and misses the dangerous one.**
`semgrep.yml:35` only excludes an **inline** `$SANITIZER.sanitize(...)`. The idiomatic `const clean = DOMPurify.sanitize(dirty)` followed by `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html: clean}}` is reported as an ERROR. Meanwhile a spread-props form evades the rule completely, and any object with a no-op `.sanitize()` method satisfies the exclusion. Expect your team to learn to ignore this rule — which is precisely how a real finding gets waved through. Per AGENTS.md's CodeRabbit-reply rule, when you dismiss one of these, **reply in-thread explaining why**, or CodeRabbit re-raises it forever.

**8. The `aria-labelledby` false positive.**
`icon-button-missing-aria-label.yml:14`'s `^aria-label\b` does not match `aria-labelledby` (word boundary fails on the following `l`). A correctly-labelled IconButton using `aria-labelledby` is reported as an accessibility violation. Same family of problem as #7 — the rule punishes the more sophisticated correct answer.

**9. The only a11y gate is a Storybook job that skips on a util change.**
`storybook-test` (`qa.yml:236`) is the sole automated WCAG check on a PR, and its trigger path list (`qa.yml:80-88`) omits `overrides/app/utils/**` and `overrides/app/config/**`. Combined with trap #1, a11y coverage is conditional on your last commit's file paths. And per `.claude/rules/testing.md`, `ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest, so icon-consuming components must be mocked in unit tests too — meaning neither layer reliably exercises them.

**10. `e2e-browserstack` burns paid sessions on cancelled runs, and its comment says otherwise.**
`qa.yml:433` uses `always()`; `qa.yml:314` uses `!cancelled()`. The comment at `qa.yml:431` claims they're the same. `e2e-localhost`'s comment (`:309-312`) explains that `!cancelled()` was chosen deliberately so a superseded push doesn't burn a runner slot. BrowserStack — the one that costs real money per session — didn't get the fix. Worth a one-line PR, though note `.github/workflows/` is Tier 1 and needs a code-owner review.

## 3. Consent-gated behind Didomi, and the fail-closed rule

**The rule** (`index.md:61`, `12-didomi.md:100`): if Didomi cannot determine consent state, **no third-party tracking or marketing script loads**. `12-didomi.md:100` is specific about the mechanism — the Didomi Web SDK does *not* self-default to denied; **the storefront implements a 5-second timeout** (explicitly "a project decision, not a Didomi-recommended value"), and on timeout Consent Mode signals stay denied and no gated script loads.

Per `12-didomi.md:75-79`:

| Bucket | Gated scripts |
|---|---|
| **Required — NOT gated** | Didomi itself, SFCC SCAPI, Contentful Delivery API, PWA→MRT proxy reads, **Adyen Drop-in** |
| **Analytics** | GTM analytics tags (GA4 etc.), **Crazy Egg** (all storefronts), **Optimizely Web** (US only) — categories still TBC |
| **Marketing** | Meta Pixel, GTM marketing tags, Enhanced Conversions |
| **Performance** | **Narvar Promise EDD** (TBC), **Google Maps autocomplete**, **Inside Chat** (TBC), Omneo widget (vendor disclosure only) |
| **Region-conditional** | **reCAPTCHA** — gated in **EU & UK only** (`10-recaptcha.md:54-55,64-73`); a visitor who declines gets **no bot protection** there |
| **Undecided** | **Measmerize** (`17-measmerize.md:123`) and **Vimeo** (`18-vimeo.md:60-69`) both carry an unresolved *blocking* choice between SDK-level tracking disable / `dnt=1` versus a full script gate |

**Important carve-out to the LCP budget:** `12-didomi.md:87` grants **Optimizely on the US storefront** a deliberate exception — it head-loads before render so its anti-flicker snippet works, and this is allowed to take priority over LCP. Crazy Egg has no such carve-out.

Every file follows one fixed 11-section template (`index.md:67-83`) and answers "what will **our** storefront do": scope boundary, browser architecture, credential placement, consent posture, per-region matrix, failure modes, and **numbered open items with named owners**. ## 3. Consent-gated behind Didomi, and the fail-closed rule

**The rule** (`index.md:61`, `12-didomi.md:100`): if Didomi cannot determine consent state, **no third-party tracking or marketing script loads**. `12-didomi.md:100` is specific about the mechanism — the Didomi Web SDK does *not* self-default to denied; **the storefront implements a 5-second timeout** (explicitly "a project decision, not a Didomi-recommended value"), and on timeout Consent Mode signals stay denied and no gated script loads.

Per `12-didomi.md:75-79`:

| Bucket | Gated scripts |
|---|---|
| **Required — NOT gated** | Didomi itself, SFCC SCAPI, Contentful Delivery API, PWA→MRT proxy reads, **Adyen Drop-in** |
| **Analytics** | GTM analytics tags (GA4 etc.), **Crazy Egg** (all storefronts), **Optimizely Web** (US only) — categories still TBC |
| **Marketing** | Meta Pixel, GTM marketing tags, Enhanced Conversions |
| **Performance** | **Narvar Promise EDD** (TBC), **Google Maps autocomplete**, **Inside Chat** (TBC), Omneo widget (vendor disclosure only) |
| **Region-conditional** | **reCAPTCHA** — gated in **EU & UK only** (`10-recaptcha.md:54-55,64-73`); a visitor who declines gets **no bot protection** there |
| **Undecided** | **Measmerize** (`17-measmerize.md:123`) and **Vimeo** (`18-vimeo.md:60-69`) both carry an unresolved *blocking* choice between SDK-level tracking disable / `dnt=1` versus a full script gate |

**Important carve-out to the LCP budget:** `12-didomi.md:87` grants **Optimizely on the US storefront** a deliberate exception — it head-loads before render so its anti-flicker snippet works, and this is allowed to take priority over LCP. Crazy Egg has no such carve-out.

## 4. Integrations touching checkout / payment — the "never silently substitute" rule

Per `AGENTS.md` > Graceful Degradation: *never silently substitute a different checkout, payment, or commerce flow when an integration is down — surface an explicit error instead.*

| System | Checkout/payment surface | Where the doc encodes the rule |
|---|---|---|
| **Adyen** (`07`) | Drop-in at payment step; 3DS2; wallets; saved-card CVV; webhook relay | `07-adyen.md:116` — Drop-in load failure **blocks order placement** with a Reload CTA; `:121` — new-session failure is a P1 |
| **Global-e** (`08`) | Owns the entire international checkout iframe | `08-global-e.md:171` — **the sharpest statement of the rule**: on a stale/missing price book, "Do not silently fall back to an SFCC checkout for an international destination — that would route the order through the wrong checkout flow and carries tax / regulatory risk"; `:174` — cart-total mismatch → reject, "Never silently adjust totals" |
| **SFCC / SCAPI** (`01`) | Basket, order placement, saved-payment token refs | `01-sfcc.md:87` — order-placement 5xx **after** Adyen authorisation is a hard error, "the order cannot fail silently" |
| **GiveX** (`05`) | Gift card / credit note as a payment instrument; checkout "Check Balance" | `05-givex.md:100-106` — card number + PIN are payment credentials: POST body only, no storage, no logging, redaction in logger + Sentry `beforeSend` |
| **MuleSoft** (`03`) | Cart → checkout entry stock check (CAI-034) | `03-mulesoft.md:111` — **block checkout entry** on 5xx: "Do not silently progress; a stale stock decision risks an oversell" |
| **Google Maps** (`09`) | Address step (delivery + billing) | Degrades *to manual entry* — this is an explicitly sanctioned fallback (`09-google-maps.md:117-119`), not a substituted flow |
| **Narvar** (`11`) | Delivery-method step EDD | Explicitly **must never block checkout** (`11-narvar.md:101`) — suppress the EDD line only |
| **reCAPTCHA** (`10`) | Login/register gate ahead of checkout | Failure **blocks submit** (`10-recaptcha.md:78-79`) |

Note the tension: `05-givex.md:110-125` (gift card purchase/redemption) is domestic-only at launch and **not** available at Global-e international checkout (GC-050); `07-adyen.md:139` adds that cards saved via Global-e never sync back to SFCC/Adyen (CRM-173). Anyone building a saved-payment or gift-card UI needs both facts in hand.

## 7. "What bites you" — traps for a frontend lead

## Branch model
`AGENTS.md` Branch Rules + `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`. Verified live via GraphQL `branchProtectionRules`:

| Branch | Required checks | Approvals | Code-owner | Admin-enforced | Stale reviews dismissed | Conversation resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| `main` | `🔴 Branch Target Check` **only** | 1 | yes | yes | **no** | **no** |
| `release/**` | `🔴 Branch Target Check`, `SIT Gate` | 1 | yes | yes | **no** | **no** |

`main` has **no test gate at all**, and `🔴 Branch Target Check` asserts exactly one thing (`protected-file-guard.yml:165`): `base == main && head == feature/*` → fail. Code fixes on a release go via `fix/release-{version}-{desc}` targeting the release branch (`releaseBranchesRules.md:34-46`); the forward-merge to `develop` happens through the release back-merge, never a separate PR (`:12,:36`).

| Pattern | Who | Verified enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` | any developer | ruleset `tag-rc` (20487306), `bypass_actors: []` — `update`+`deletion` restricted **for everyone** |
| `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N` | tier-1-approvers only | ruleset `tag-release` (20487243), `creation` restricted, bypass = team id `18338648` = **`tier-1-approvers`** (confirmed) |

## Version guard behaviour (`scripts/versionGuard.mjs`)

`VERSION_TAG = /^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$/` (`:31`). Pages 20×100 deployments newest-first (`:62-77`) so branch deploys can't bury the last tag. Fails closed on lookup error (`:92`), on invalid stored ref (`:74`), and on non-semver input (`:85`). `record` fails the run if it can't write the baseline (`:117`).

**The hole is the skip path.** `check` *passes* on any non-version-tag ref (`:84`) and `record` *skips* it (`:103`). Since `deploy-uat.yml:9` defaults to `develop`, `deploy-stg.yml:9` defaults to `main`, and `deploy-prod.yml:7` explicitly advertises "Tag or branch", **a branch deploy to any tier bypasses the guard entirely and leaves no baseline** — so the guard's notion of what's live silently diverges from reality.

`rollback=true` skips `check` but still runs `record` (`if: success()`, no rollback condition), so the rolled-back tag becomes the new baseline — doc is accurate here. Its only gate is environment required reviewers, which **do not exist**.

## Tag naming enforcement, three layers
1. `scripts/hooks/pre-push:20-21` — prevention, bypassable via `--no-verify` or a clone where `prepare` never ran.
2. `tag-validate.yml:19-20` — post-hoc detection only, not a block.
3. Rulesets — immutability + tier-1-only final tags (real); naming inert on Team plan.

## Doc-vs-workflow disagreements
- `tagging.md` calls test/uat/staging/prod "tag-promoted / deliberate". **Three of the four default to a branch ref.**
- `tagging.md`'s environment table omits `deploy-preview.yml` entirely.
- `deploy-dev.yml:92-119`'s `tag-sprint` job diffs `scripts/sprint.txt` — **that file does not exist and never has**. The job is permanently dead.
- `test:contracts` is `echo 'TODO…' && exit 0` (`package.json:85`). The "MuleSoft contract tests" job in both `deploy-dev.yml:32` and `digital-sit.yml:116` always passes vacuously, and `sit-gate:144-147` counts that as a real signal.
- `package.json:57` runs `lhci autorun --config=tests/lighthouserc.js`; `tests/` doesn't exist. The real file is `./lighthouserc.js`. `AGENTS.md:37` and `protected-file-guard.yml:82` both name the stale path; `CODEOWNERS:61` covers the real one.
- `.docs/architecture.md:91,108` still lists a 5-tier topology with no Test and MRT target `stage`. Stale.

## What bites you — release
1. **A branch ref silently disarms the downgrade guard on prod.** One click on `deploy-prod.yml` with `develop` and the guard logs a green "not a version tag — skipping."
2. **After any branch deploy, the guard's baseline is a lie.** It will later block a genuinely-newer tag against a stale recorded tag while the environment actually runs something else. Re-run `node scripts/versionGuard.mjs record prod <tag>` after any out-of-band deploy.
3. **`rollback=true` is a real, ungated bypass right now.** Setting required reviewers on `prod`/`staging`/`uat` is the single highest-value fix in this whole report.
4. **`main` is the least-protected branch in the repo.** No tests, no stale-review dismissal.
5. **The SIT gate cannot pass** — no LHCI secrets, no `*.p0.spec`. Discover this the week you cut `release/v0.1.0` and you're blocked on secrets provisioning, not code.
6. **Three-way name divergence:** GitHub Environment (`staging`/`prod`) ≠ workflow file (`stg`/`prod`) ≠ MRT target (`staging`/`production`). Tooling must key off the GitHub Environment name; `versionGuard.mjs` does.
7. **An unrelated Pages-publish failure blocks the SIT deploy.** `deploy-sit.yml:18` keys off `workflow_run.conclusion`, which is the *whole workflow's* result — including `deploy-playwright-report` (`digital-sit.yml:55-66`, `if: always()`).

# 3. PR and review workflow

## Mechanically enforced at PR time
- Three required checks on `develop` (above). **`Playwright E2E (localhost)` and `Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)` are required nowhere** — they can be red and the PR merges. `teardown-preview.yml` reported `fail` on PR #59 and it merged.
- `qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` gates everything via `since_last_remote_commit: true` (`:72`) — diffed against the previous push, not the merge base. The file's own comment at `:22-23` acknowledges *"GitHub treats a skipped required check as passing."*
- `detect-changes` is itself **not** a required check. If it fails, both required jobs skip → both pass.
- `storybook-test` is the **only** automated a11y gate, and its path list (`qa.yml:80-88`) omits `overrides/app/utils/**` and `overrides/app/config/**`.
- E2E scope narrowing has exactly **one** area allow-list, `e2e_homepage` (`qa.yml:97-102`), despite `testing.md` listing seven.

## CodeRabbit — advisory as a check, blocking as a reviewer
`request_changes_workflow: true` (`coderabbit.yaml:32`) + `requiredApprovingReviewCount: 1` means a *Changes requested* review blocks the merge button. But the `CodeRabbit` status check is in no required-context list, so its `mode: error` pre-merge checks (`:399-430`) don't block that way. On `develop`, only `HardiAcn` can dismiss reviews.

Two switches that turn it off invisibly: `ignore_title_keywords: ["chore(deps)", "dependabot"]` (`:391-393`) is **title-matched, not author-matched**, and `drafts: false` (`:389`). Neither shows as a failing check — it just goes quiet.

`code_guidelines.filePatterns` (`:462-465`) loads literal file content and **does not follow AGENTS.md's markdown links** — `overrideStyling.md` and `tagging.md` are not in the list and are therefore invisible to review.

## Rule blind spots worth knowing
All three ast-grep rules are `severity: warning`. Both semgrep rules are `ERROR`.
- `img-missing-alt` matches `^img$` only — **`<Image>`, the idiomatic Chakra element, is invisible.**
- `icon-button-missing-aria-label`'s `^aria-label\b` **does not match `aria-labelledby`** (word boundary fails on the following `l`) — the more correct answer gets flagged.
- `clickable-non-interactive-element` accepts `role="presentation"`/`role="none"`, and checks neither `tabIndex` nor `onKeyDown` despite `components.md` requiring both.
- `payment-credential-logged` sinks are only `console.*` and `Sentry.*` — `dataLayer.push`, `localStorage.setItem`, a logger, a query string and a response body all pass. Sources exclude `let`/`var`, property access and destructuring; the name list misses **`cvc`**.
- `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` only excludes an *inline* `.sanitize()`. The idiomatic `const clean = DOMPurify.sanitize(dirty)` then `{{__html: clean}}` is **reported as an ERROR**, while a spread-props form evades entirely.

## Git hooks — all best-effort
`pre-commit` (324 lines) regenerates the registry, syncs derived AI configs, regenerates Contentful definitions, **blocks** direct edits to derived config, and **blocks** `.env.sample` commits with secret-shaped values. **It runs no lint, no `tsc`, no tests.** `commit-msg` enforces conventional commits with a lowercase scope. `pre-push` validates `v*` tag names. All defeated by `--no-verify` or `npm install --ignore-scripts`.

## No CI gate at all
`npm run lint` · `npx tsc --noEmit` · `npm run audit:tokens` (14 untriaged pre-existing violations) · `npm run format` (globs `**/*.{js,jsx}`, so it never touches `overrides/`'s TypeScript) · `sync:ai-rules:check` · **test coverage** (`vitest.config.ts` has no coverage block). Bundle size and Lighthouse exist but only post-merge or at release tier.

## Human-only
Running `cr review --light --base develop` before every non-trivial commit (AGENTS.md calls it "required, not optional" — nothing verifies it). Replying in-thread to every CodeRabbit finding — **`requiresConversationResolution: false` on all three branches**, so nothing blocks a merge with every thread unanswered. Pasting the Jira URL into the PR body. The copy-first override protocol.

## What bites you — PR
1. **A docs-only final commit turns both required gates green.** Read the *history* of check runs on a PR, not the head SHA's current state. "skipping" means unverified, not passed — and if an earlier push failed unit tests, a docs commit flips the required check to green.
2. **`detect-changes` failing green-lights the PR.** The most load-bearing job in the pipeline is not itself required.
3. **A header-only change gets the narrowest E2E scope despite the widest blast radius** — `e2e_homepage` includes `components/header/**`.
4. **`chore(deps):` in a human PR title disables CodeRabbit entirely** — no semgrep, no ast-grep, no gitleaks.
5. **The semgrep XSS rule flags the correct pattern and misses the dangerous one.** Your team will learn to ignore it. When you dismiss one, reply in-thread with the reason or CodeRabbit re-raises it forever.
6. **Renaming a `qa.yml` job breaks merging repo-wide** — required contexts match by display name; the check would sit "Expected" forever. And `.github/workflows/` is Tier 1.
7. **`e2e-browserstack` uses `always()` (`qa.yml:433`) while the comment above it claims parity with `e2e-localhost`'s `!cancelled()` (`:314`)** — superseded pushes burn paid BrowserStack sessions.
8. **`CODERABBIT_API_KEY` is a live 61-char credential stored as a plaintext GitHub Actions *variable*** in the `shared` and `dev` environments — readable via the API by anyone with repo read, and unmasked in logs. It should be a secret.

- `storybook-test` is the **only** automated a11y gate, and its path list (`qa.yml:80-88`) omits `overrides/app/utils/**` and `overrides/app/config/**`.
- E2E scope narrowing has exactly **one** area allow-list, `e2e_homepage` (`qa.yml:97-102`), despite `testing.md` listing seven.

## CodeRabbit — advisory as a check, blocking as a reviewer
`request_changes_workflow: true` (`coderabbit.yaml:32`) + `requiredApprovingReviewCount: 1` means a *Changes requested* review blocks the merge button. But the `CodeRabbit` status check is in no required-context list, so its `mode: error` pre-merge checks (`:399-430`) don't block that way. On `develop`, only `HardiAcn` can dismiss reviews.

Two switches that turn it off invisibly: `ignore_title_keywords: ["chore(deps)", "dependabot"]` (`:391-393`) is **title-matched, not author-matched**, and `drafts: false` (`:389`). Neither shows as a failing check — it just goes quiet.

`code_guidelines.filePatterns` (`:462-465`) loads literal file content and **does not follow AGENTS.md's markdown links** — `overrideStyling.md` and `tagging.md` are not in the list and are therefore invisible to review.

## Rule blind spots worth knowing
All three ast-grep rules are `severity: warning`. Both semgrep rules are `ERROR`.
- `img-missing-alt` matches `^img$` only — **`<Image>`, the idiomatic Chakra element, is invisible.**
- `icon-button-missing-aria-label`'s `^aria-label\b` **does not match `aria-labelledby`** (word boundary fails on the following `l`) — the more correct answer gets flagged.
- `clickable-non-interactive-element` accepts `role="presentation"`/`role="none"`, and checks neither `tabIndex` nor `onKeyDown` despite `components.md` requiring both.
- `payment-credential-logged` sinks are only `console.*` and `Sentry.*` — `dataLayer.push`, `localStorage.setItem`, a logger, a query string and a response body all pass. Sources exclude `let`/`var`, property access and destructuring; the name list misses **`cvc`**.
- `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` only excludes an *inline* `.sanitize()`. The idiomatic `const clean = DOMPurify.sanitize(dirty)` then `{{__html: clean}}` is **reported as an ERROR**, while a spread-props form evades entirely.

## Git hooks — all best-effort
`pre-commit` (324 lines) regenerates the registry, syncs derived AI configs, regenerates Contentful definitions, **blocks** direct edits to derived config, and **blocks** `.env.sample` commits with secret-shaped values. **It runs no lint, no `tsc`, no tests.** `commit-msg` enforces conventional commits with a lowercase scope. `pre-push` validates `v*` tag names. All defeated by `--no-verify` or `npm install --ignore-scripts`.

## Two findings worth acting on independently of this doc work

**1. `CODERABBIT_API_KEY` is a plaintext GitHub Actions *variable* — 61 characters, retrievable via the API by any repo collaborator.** Also stored as variables in `dev`: `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` (gates unpublished draft content) and `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN`.

In fairness, `.env.sample`'s header records the plaintext-variable mechanism as a *conscious, confirmed tradeoff* for centralisation. But that reasoning was written for non-secret public identifiers — site IDs, short codes, container IDs. A live API key and a draft-content token aren't that. Worth revisiting as secrets rather than variables.

**2. PDP ownership is inverted on your current branch.** `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info`:

| source | says |
|---|---|
| `CODEOWNERS:162` — **enforcing** | `@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b` |
| `squadA.md:4,34` | Squad A |
| `squadB.md:41` | "Squad A territory" |

## 1. How a value resolves

### The pipeline is one-way

```
theme/foundation/*.ts   ← source of truth (Tier 1)
        ↓
zimmTokens.ts           ← DERIVED. Never hand-edit.
        ↓
--zimm-* CSS custom properties
        ↓
recipes: <name>.css.ts / theme/components/*.ts
        ↓
component JSX
```

`zimmTokens.ts` imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/
`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid` from their owning files rather than
retyping values. The only literals left in it are 7 numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with
no named-scale equivalent.

**A Tier 1 comment is wrong about those 7.** `theme/index.ts:47` says the 15 numeric aliases
*"are duplicates of the named scale."* `overrideStyling.md:83-85` says 7 of them are not, and
`overrideStyling.md` is right: `025` (1px), `700` (28px), `1100` (44px), `1200` (48px),
`1300` (52px), `3500` (140px), `4500` (180px) are hardcoded in `zimmTokens.ts`; the other 8
derive from `spacing`.

### The registration reality — this is the one that breaks layouts

`theme/index.ts` registers the Zimmermann scale as **`space` only** (line 56). `sizes`,
`fontSizes`, `lineHeights` and `letterSpacings` are deliberately **not** registered, because
registering them would restyle the base retail-react-app at ~199 call sites.

| Prop family | Reads | Bare key like `'xl'` |
|---|---|---|
| `margin` `padding` `gap` | `theme.space` ✅ registered | correct |
| `width` `height` `boxSize` `min/maxWidth/Height` | `theme.sizes` ❌ not registered | **falls through to Chakra's defaults** |
| `fontSize` `lineHeight` `letterSpacing` | ❌ not registered | wrong value, or nothing |

Measured blow-up range: **8×–112×**. `width: 'xl'` resolves through `theme.sizes.xl` = 36rem
= **576px** — that shipped, blew the footer contact icons to 576px, and destroyed the layout
on every page. Worse: `s`, `m`, `l` are **absent** from Chakra's `sizes`, so those
declarations are dropped entirely and silently.

Typography has the same twin. `fontSize: '2xs'` emits 0.625rem where 0.875rem was intended;
`fontSize: '4xs'` emits nothing at all.

**Live unfixed instance:** `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302` has `fontSize="l"`,
which emits nothing. Pre-existing, out of scope for every PR that has touched that file since.
`recipeGuards.test.ts` cannot reach it — it walks the registered recipe map only, and this is
a JSX prop. Its own `SCOPE:` note says so.

**The rule:** on a sizing or typography prop, always the CSS var —
`width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'`, never `width: 'xl'`. Spacing props are fine with bare keys as
far as *correctness* goes; house style is a separate question, below.

### [CORRECTED] `var(--zimm-*)` in component JSX is now required, not a smell

An earlier revision of this document said component JSX should use `textStyle` plus semantic
token strings (`color="text.default"`, `padding="m"`), and that seeing `var()` in a `.tsx` was
a signal to look closer. **That is inverted from the current rule and following it now fails
review.**

`overrideStyling.md` hierarchy point 2 and `css.md` both state it plainly:

```tsx
// ❌ a bare Chakra/theme token string
<Box color="text.default" padding="m" />

// ✅ the raw var(--zimm-*) reference
<Box color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" padding="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />
```

The stated reason is **house style, not correctness**: a bare key resolves to the identical
value on a registered scale, but it forces a reviewer to check `theme/index.ts`'s
registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. A `var()` reference is
unambiguous at every call site.

`textStyle` is the one legitimate bare key — there is no `var()` for the composite expansion,
only for its individual pieces.

**What survives from the old advice, and is still the main point:** brand values mostly should
not be in JSX at all. Measured on `develop` 2026-08-25 — `var(--zimm-*)` appears in **18
recipe files** (14 co-located `<name>.css.ts` + 4 `theme/components/*.ts`) and in exactly
**one** component `.tsx`: `footer/footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44,62`, a conditional
`paddingLeft` that no Chakra prop expresses. So the practice is: type via `textStyle`,
colour and spacing into the recipe, `var()` in JSX only for a genuine prop-system gap.

**Live violations right now:** `ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductName/index.tsx:20` and
`zimmProductModelInfo/index.tsx:23` both use `color="text.default"`.

### The real invariant is single-sourcing, not `var()` syntax

Ask of any value: *is this typed more than once?* Not: *is this a `var()`?* An audit built on
syntax generates mostly noise.

PR #56 reduced `foundation/`'s hand-typed literals from 237 to 64 — **173 were duplicates**,
the same `24px` appearing in `typography.ts` and again in `zimmTokens.ts`. Two later PRs
recreated that duplication one layer up without noticing: PR #52 hand-rebuilt in `sx` what
`textStyle="heading3"` already gave, five times; PR #55 added `cssVars.ts`, 241 lines mirroring
`zimmTokens.ts`'s keys as `var()` strings plus a reimplementation of seven registered text
styles. It was removed — 245 lines, 53 references across 8 files.

Both misreads passed CodeRabbit. It confirmed every correctness finding and raised **zero**
architecture findings.

### Units

- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with root font-size or browser zoom (WCAG 1.4.4) —
  type and spacing. Sub-pixel letter-spacing values keep a trailing `// -0.12px` comment for
  traceability, since they don't round to clean rem.
- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should *not* scale — border widths, focus-ring offsets.
- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts`, deliberate so media queries shift with zoom)
  and other genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.

## 2. Chakra behaviours that fail silently

Seven mechanisms. None produces an error, a warning, or a failing type-check.

**1. `extendTheme` deep-merges — it does not replace.** A recipe named `Footer` merges into
base SFCC's `Footer` rather than replacing it, inheriting parts you never wrote. Namespace
everything: `ZimmFooter`, not `Footer`. `recipeGuards.test.ts` enforces this with
`INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` — those three are deliberate; anything
else must be namespaced.

**2. A recipe unit test cannot catch the merge.** `extendTheme` does **not** populate
`theme.__cssMap` — only `ChakraProvider` does, via `toCSSVar`. So a direct `css()(theme)`
assertion in Vitest passes vacuously against an unmerged object.

**3. Compound values never tokenise.** Chakra resolves a token only as the **entire** value.
`padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim and dropped by the browser. Use axis props
(`paddingInline`, `paddingBlock`).

**4. A shorthand declared after a longhand resets it.** `padding: 0` after `paddingBlock`
wipes it. Order matters; prefer the axis props throughout.

**5. `IconButton` hard-sets `padding: "0"`.** Any padding you pass is overwritten.

**6. Register the recipe or destructuring throws at runtime.** Chakra resolves a recipe by the
string key passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path — so co-location is free, but the
key must be in `theme/components/index.ts`.

**7. Breakpoint tokens conflict with Chakra's.** `BP.desktop` is 64em; Chakra's `lg` is 62em
and `xl` is 80em. A responsive array silently steps at the wrong width. Write explicit media
queries:

```ts
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
```

The array shorthand also puts a bare token key at every step, and the guard flags all four.

## 3. Component structure

### Placement — settled

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/index.tsx
```

Being under `components/` is load-bearing for the registry generator, which scans that path.

**Three casing families, each correct in its own context. Do not generalise between them:**

| Family | Casing | Why |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | must match upstream's import path |
| ui-kit component | `zimmButton/` camelCase | Zimmermann-authored — the default rule |
| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | mirrors upstream exactly |

Kebab-case applies *only* to files mirroring a base Salesforce file. Note the theme key is
PascalCase (`ZimmTextInput`) while its recipe file is camelCase.

### Tier is by composition, not visual size

Read it off the imports, not the DOM:

- **atom** — imports no other ui-kit. `zimmModal` is an atom despite being portal + backdrop +
  `role="dialog"` chrome, because it owns no content (`maxWidth`, `labelledBy`, children all
  come from the caller).
- **molecule** — composes atoms with light local logic. `zimmInputAction` = TextInput + Button
  + local validation state.
- **organism** — composes molecules/atoms **and owns domain state**. `zimmSubscribeSection`
  owns the subscribe state machine.

An icon passed as a prop doesn't count (`icon="close"` keeps a Button an atom). Slotted
children don't count.

**Storybook `title` is a different axis from the folder.** Folder = composition depth;
`title` = domain. `zimmModal` (atom) → `Elements/`; `zimmSubscribeSection` (organism) →
`Forms/`; `Footer` → `Layout/`. Don't conflate them.

### Styling surface — a registered recipe, always

Not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` class, not a plain stylesheet. The recipe may live beside
the component as `<name>.css.ts` or centrally in `theme/components/` — Chakra resolves by
string key, so this is purely organisational.

The argument against authoring in a stylesheet is worth keeping: a stylesheet can only see
`var(--zimm-*)`, which is **derived output at the bottom of the pipeline**. Author there and
you lose `textStyle`, the named `theme.space` scale, semantic colour tokens, and the theme
drift-guard tests. Not bad CSS — the wrong end of the pipeline.

For a bespoke component wrapping a native element, the `chakra()` factory is the bridge:
native semantics plus recipe styling, read via `useMultiStyleConfig`.

**Co-location changes who reviews it.** `CODEOWNERS:186`
(`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only) is placed **last** among the
`components/` rules, and CODEOWNERS is last-match-wins, not most-specific-wins. So a `.css.ts`
inside `footer/` drops the Tier 2 approver requirement the surrounding directory carries,
while `footer/index.tsx` keeps it. The stated rationale: a co-located recipe *composes
established tokens*; authoring a new token still means `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1).

`overrideStyling.md` flags its own inconsistency here rather than papering over it —
`zimmButton.css.ts` keys the app-wide `Button` recipe and is no longer designer-gated.

### No data-fetching in `components/`

Anything under `overrides/app/components/` receives data as props. Data-fetching belongs in
`overrides/app/pages/` or a container.

**One documented exception:** Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks (`useIntl`,
`useUiCopy`) may be called from any component including presentational leaves, because they
read from a Provider mounted above the route tree. Narrow by design — content identical for
every consumer regardless of route, not anything that varies per page.

**Their no-Provider behaviour differs, and it matters for tests.** `useUiCopy` degrades:
`useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY`, one line, renders with zero setup. **`useIntl`
throws** (`invariantIntlContext`), and its `IntlProvider` is mounted by the base SFCC `_app`,
not `_app-config` — a strictly narrower subtree. Any Vitest test rendering a `useIntl` consumer
must wrap it.

### Two API patterns worth copying

- **Encode the a11y contract in a discriminated union** so an inaccessible combination doesn't
  type-check.
- **Make an absent affordance opt-in**, not a silent default.

### Do not trust the registry's tier column

`generateRegistry.mjs:122` hardcodes tier arrays, lists no `ui-kits` path, and defaults
everything else to Tier 4. The registry is auto-generated and its *paths* are reliable; its
*tier* column is not.

An earlier revision said **seven** directories. It is now **eleven**:

```
_app-config  button  contentful  footer  foundation  header
icons  pageContainer  product-view  ui-kits  uiCopyProvider
```

`footer/` is a full override with three co-located recipes. Two organisms exist
(`zimmSubscribeModal`, `zimmSubscribeSection`) where an earlier note said none did.
`theme/components/button.ts` no longer exists — it is
`ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts`. `theme/components/` now holds only

## 4. What an override actually intercepts

Three silent failure modes. In each, the override compiles, resolves, and never runs.

**1. The resolver is webpack-only.** `ccExtensibility` in `package.json` redirects
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` in the **real app build only**.
`.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to `node_modules`, and `vitest.config.ts`
doesn't touch it. So a base-path import of an already-overridden component builds correctly in
the shipped app and silently renders the **unstyled base version** in Storybook and Vitest —
the story looks like it's exercising your override and isn't.

When importing a component that already has an override, use a **relative path**
(`'../swatch-group'`), not the base path.

**2. A relative barrel re-export is not rewritten.** The attractive play — override
`shared/ui/<Name>` so branded styling propagates into base cart, checkout and account for free
— **does not work.** `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` does `export {Button} from './Button'`, a
relative export the resolver does not rewrite. And the consumption pattern is the wrong way
round: **208 base files import the barrel; 0 import `shared/ui/Button`.** The override
intercepts nothing.

**3. A conditional render of an alternate module.** Overriding a component doesn't help if the
parent renders something else on that route. `footer` never reaches `/checkout`.

**The generalised check**, before scoping any story around "override X and it propagates":

```bash
grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" \
  node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/
```

### The SFCC bridge pattern

If a component is used internally by SFCC's own base components, its **default export must
stay a faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour.
Put Zimmermann-only styling behind a **named export** that wraps it. `product-tile`'s
`CardBaseline` + default is the reference.

Where token-driven theming suffices, a theme recipe is preferable to a second export — the
prop-narrowing that motivated `CardBaseline` isn't needed for styling alone.

## 5. Figma to code

### The discriminator is node type, not a fudge factor

- **Text nodes** report a **cap-height box** (`text-box-trim: trim-both`,
  `text-box-edge: cap_alphabetic`). **Not comparable** to a CSS line box. Measured artifacts:
  "KEEP IN TOUCH" 8 vs 18, body copy 26 vs 36, `errorText` 9 vs 18.
- **Frames and instances** report a **real box**. **Directly comparable** — a delta here is a
  genuine defect. The `Textfield` *instance* at 44/59 against 45/68 was a real gap, and a naive
  "it's just cap height" rule would have wrongly dismissed it.

**Supporting heuristic:** a *uniform* residual across siblings is measurement; a *varying* one
is a defect. Three contact items all sitting at +7 after every real cause was removed = the
heading's cap box.

**Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** In shipped `zimmNavItem.css.ts`, deriving from
`lineHeight` + 4.5px padding produced 24/24/24/24/38 = 134 — exactly Figma's `Links` frame.

### There are two Figma files and comparisons must be like-for-like

`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` (design system) and `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (composed page states).
Comparing an initial state from the design-system symbol against an error state from the page
file produced two wrong conclusions in a row — first "the slot is 59px in both states"
(actually `Subscribed=False` 320×44 vs `Subscribed=True` 308×59, with a compensating gap
change 40→24: the design **repositions**, it doesn't reserve), then a "reserve the slot" fix
that suppressed intended growth when the 68px padded box was already correct.

### Frames are not breakpoints

Frames exist at 402/1023/1440; breakpoint tokens are 768/860/1024. The unframed **768–1022
band was genuinely broken** — 18px horizontal scroll, 7 wrapped labels — and covers three iPad
models in portrait. `flexWrap: nowrap` prevents *breaking*, not *shrinking*: the row refused to
break, so the words broke instead.

### Type metrics

The fallback stack renders roughly **13% wider** than Futura Round, which is why serving the
real faces matters for parity review. `document.fonts.check()` returns `true` for unavailable
families and is useless — compare widths instead.

### Measurement method

Measure `y` relative to the component root (Figma reports frame-relative coordinates). Use
`domcontentloaded`, never `networkidle`, on a dev server. Dismiss the consent banner first.
`Range.getClientRects()` gives per-line widths to *prove* a wrap point. **Mutation-test layout
fixes at mobile** — two fixes read as Δ0 at 1440 only because a taller sibling column masked
them.

**A design nudge is still spec.** A deliberate deviation gets documented at the point of use,
not silently followed or silently ignored.

### No automated gate in this stack catches a layout defect

`width: 'xl'` resolving to 576px destroyed the footer on every page while passing `tsc`,
`eslint`, `vitest`, local *and* remote CodeRabbit, and the Storybook a11y run. Only rendering
beside Figma found it.

## 6. Layout mechanics

Six mechanisms, each with its fix.

1. **Wrapped-element width** — a wrapper shrinks to content unless told otherwise.
2. **`minHeight` + centring** — reserves space without collapsing when empty.
3. **Inline descender leak** — an inline element's line box includes descender space; use
   `display: block` or set `lineHeight` explicitly.
4. **Gap ownership** — the parent owns the gap, never the child's margin. Two owners drift.
5. **`flexWrap: nowrap` prevents breaking, not shrinking** — the words break instead.
6. **NBSP as ` `** — a literal non-breaking space in source is invisible to review and
   survives reformatting unpredictably.

## 7. Building against absent data

### Three patterns, only the first correct

**Guard, then render inert but perceivable.** Never render nothing where a control was
promised; never render a control that can't act.

- **An empty-string fallback is a layout bug** — the box collapses and everything shifts.
- **A silent element swap actively lies** — it promises an affordance that isn't there.
- **Fix at the atom**, not at each call site.

### The three-tier policy — the most reusable decision in the footer build

Behaviour differs by what the content *is*:

| Content class | Behaviour | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Structural** (`footerConfig`) | render **nothing** — `if (!footerData) return null` | no fallback to placeholder once wired to live data, so an outage doesn't ship stale placeholder copy to real shoppers |
| **Microcopy** (`uiCopy`) | fall back to the **English literal** | losing a button label to an outage should never blank a control |
| **Per-item destination** (a contact href) | degrade **that item only** to a labelled non-interactive `<span>` | perceivable, but no false affordance |

The per-item case is the carefully argued one: no `href`, no `tabIndex`, so nothing promises an
action that cannot be performed (WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4) — but **labelled, not `aria-hidden`**, so
a screen-reader user learns the channel exists instead of getting silence (avoiding the 1.1.1
information loss an earlier `aria-hidden` caused).

The same treatment is reused three times for "control with no action": the contact fallback,
`ZimmNavItem`'s no-href branch (renders a `<button>` that doesn't navigate), and `BottomBar`'s
locale placeholder (a `<div>`, deliberately not a `<button>`).

### Never branch on localised CMS text

`footerNavGroup` carries `showContactChannels: boolean` rather than matching
`heading === 'Contact'` — because `heading` is localised and silently stops matching the moment
an editor writes "Kontakt" or "Contacto". This footer ships to eight storefronts.

### Guarding hrefs

Every CMS-sourced href passes `isSafeHref` before reaching an anchor. The subtlety: WHATWG URL
parsing strips C0 control characters, tab, LF and CR *before* scheme detection, so a naive
`^javascript:` regex is bypassed by `java\tscript:`. **Normalise, then test.**

## 8. CMS data and the tier reality

New section. The footer rendered correctly in dev and was blank on the test tier, and nothing
in the component was wrong.

### Content types and entries promote by different mechanisms

| | Content **types** (schema) | Content (**entries**) |
|---|---|---|
| Mechanism | org-scoped Environment Template | *nothing automated* |
| Build | `npm run sync:contentful` | — |
| Deploy | `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` | — |

**A template cannot carry entries — this is structural.** The SDK type has exactly two slots:

```ts
// contentful-management/dist/types/entities/environment-template.d.ts:30-33
entities: {
    contentTypeTemplates: Array<ContentTypeTemplateProps>;
    editorInterfaceTemplates: Array<EditorInterfaceTemplateProps>;
};
```

No `entries`, no `assets`. The only entry-writing code in the repo is `seedRegions.mjs:71-72`,
which handles the 11 `region` entries and nothing else.

### Verified tier state, 2026-08-25

| tier | content types | published entries |
|---|---|---|
| **dev** | **14** | **42** (+3 assets) |
| test / sit / uat / staging | **0** | **0** |
| prod | no environment id configured | — |

The environments exist — the CDA returned `total: 0`, not `NotFound`. Nothing has ever been
promoted out of dev.

**The template covers 5 of dev's 14 types** — `footerConfig`, `footerNavGroup`, `link`,
`region`, `uiCopy`. The other 9 exist only inside the dev environment, UI-authored, with no
code representation, and `install:contentful` cannot move them.

**There is no forward content promotion in this repo at all.** The actual release model is the
alias flip in `promoteAlias.mjs`: clone master → install template → author and verify →
repoint `production`/`master`. Content moves *backwards* (master → clone), never forwards.

### Fetch-depth is load-bearing

`include: 3` is not arbitrary. At depth 2 the `regions` array arrives as unresolved stubs,
`region.fields.siteId` throws, the `.catch` swallows it, and the **entire footer renders
nothing**. A resolution-depth mistake looks identical to a network failure from the page.

### Locale is not passed on any Contentful fetch

`useContentful.ts:110` builds a URL with `content_type`, `access_token` and `include` only.
All eight storefronts get the space default. Four call sites, three paths. Blocked on a shared-
hook signature change, which is a team RFC.

### The check to run before promising a component works on a tier

```bash
curl -s "https://cdn.contentful.com/spaces/<space>/environments/<env>/entries?content_type=<type>&limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <that tier's delivery token>"
```

`total: 1` means it will render. `unknownContentType` means the model was never installed.
Note the CDA returns an unreliable `total` at `limit=0` — use `limit=1`.

## 9. Accessibility patterns

Six recurring success criteria and what each actually demanded.

- **1.1.1** — a degraded control must stay *labelled*, not `aria-hidden`. Silence is
  information loss.
- **1.4.4 / 1.4.10** — `rem` for anything that must survive zoom; a modal panel needs
  `maxHeight` + `overflowY` or tall content centres half-off-screen and is unreachable.
- **2.4.4 / 3.2.4** — no `href` and no `tabIndex` on a control that cannot act, so nothing
  promises an action that can't be performed.
- **2.5.8** — 24×24 minimum target size, which is a WCAG **2.2** addition and easy to miss if
  working from a 2.1 checklist.
- **Focus** — a programmatic `.focus()` does **not** match `:focus-visible`. A focus ring
  styled only on `:focus-visible` will not appear after a scripted focus move.
- **Portal + focus trap** — when `activeElement` is outside the trap, the trap must handle it
  rather than assume containment.

Every `IconButton` needs `aria-label`; every `<img>` needs `alt` (`alt=""` for decorative).
Note the ast-grep rule matches `^img$` only, so Chakra's `<Image>` is invisible to it, and its
`aria-label` check does not match `aria-labelledby`.

## 10. Verification: what actually proves anything

### The integrity principle

> The verification instrument was built from the same belief as the thing it verified, and was
> never made to fail on purpose.

That is the single recurring failure mode. A green check that was never proven capable of going
red carries no information.

Catalogued instances, all self-caught after reporting a false all-clear: a `safeHref` suite
reported "well covered, 3 layers" whose 13 cases contained **zero backslashes** — the exact
vector already named; a `fontFace` test iterating an empty array; a mutation test that
"passed" because `perl -pi` works line-at-a-time and cannot match `\n`; a recipe parity check
that false-alarmed three times on recipes whose `baseStyle` is a **function**; a literal-count
sweep that inflated 19→41 by matching `.rem` inside `removeEventListener`.

### Copy the non-vacuity meta-test

`recipeGuards.test.ts` includes `test('collect() actually walks the registered recipes')`
precisely because every other guard asserts `toEqual([])`, which an empty input satisfies.
Stubbing `components` to `{}` turned the whole file green — verified.

Same shape for layout assertions: a pure before/after equality is satisfied vacuously by a
collapsed container (`display:none`, `height:0`, an ancestor `display:none` — and every rect
is 0 in jsdom). **Anchor the measurement above zero first.**

And resolve a function-form `baseStyle` across **all** boolean prop combinations, not the
default one. The original bug hid down a conditional branch a single-resolution walk never
entered.

### Green tests that encode the bug

A suite can test *around* a defect. The region tie-break suite had a case named "order of the
tied candidates does not change the outcome" that used only **distinct** timestamps — the one
arrangement already order-independent. It passed while the bug was live.

Mutation testing is necessary but not sufficient: it proves the check *can* fail, not that it
fails for the right reason.

### [CORRECTED] What is and is not gated

**a11y IS gated.** An earlier belief — repeated four times in one session and again by a fresh
analysis this week — was that a11y is ungated because there is no `.storybook/test-runner.js`.
**That is Storybook 8 knowledge and is wrong for what is installed.**
`@storybook/test-runner@0.24.4`'s `dist/setup-page-script.js:390-397` reads
`story.parameters?.a11y?.test` and throws when it `=== "error"`; `.storybook/preview.tsx:44`
sets exactly that. No `test-runner.js` is needed. **Do not delete that `preview.tsx` block.**

Honest rider: the gate has never been made to fail on purpose, so by the standard above it is
**unproven, not absent**.

**Gated nowhere at all:** `eslint`, `prettier`, `tsc --noEmit`, `audit:tokens`, any CSS bundle
budget, test coverage. `npm run lint` currently fails repo-wide on pre-existing prettier errors
and CI never notices.

**A skipped required check counts as passing.** Live on PR #59: all four suites reported
`skipping` — including both *required* checks — while `mergeable: true`. `detect-changes` uses
`since_last_remote_commit`, and a final push touching only registry files fell outside every
allow-list. A 93-commit PR became merge-eligible with **zero test evidence on its head SHA**.
Read `gh pr checks` for `skipping`, not just for green.

**A named gate that cannot fail:** `npm run test:contracts` is `echo 'TODO…' && exit 0`, and
it is a hard `needs` of `sit-gate`.

### Harness traps

- **`test-storybook` needs a *built* Storybook.** Dev-server runs made four mutation results
  uninterpretable.
- **Vitest does not run `play`.**
- **jsdom always provides `window`**, so an SSR branch needs `// @vitest-environment node`.
- **Every jsdom rect is 0** — layout assertions there are meaningless.
- **`ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest.** It imports the base SFCC icons barrel, whose top-level
  `AmexSymbol.viewBox = ...` fails because SVG imports resolve to raw path strings here.
  Unfixable from a test file (`vitest.config.ts` is Tier 1). Mock at the smallest surface:
  ```ts
  vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', () => ({ ZimmIcon: () => null }))
  ```
  …or forward `aria-label`/`aria-hidden` when an assertion depends on the accessible name.
- **Portalled content is scoped to `document.body`, not `canvasElement`.** `canvasElement` is
  `#storybook-root`, a *sibling* of the portal target. Measured: `canvasElement.innerHTML` is
  41 characters, 0 dialogs inside the canvas against 1 in the document. A canvas-scoped
  `getByRole` fails immediately; `findByRole` fails after ~1002ms; the body-scoped form passes
  in 1–2ms. `testing.md:100`'s "never reach into `document`" has no portal carve-out — that is
  a documentation defect, not a code one.
- **`@storybook/test` is not installed.** `testing.md:87` prescribes it; Storybook 10 moved it
  to `storybook/test`. Following that line verbatim breaks.

### The gap no tool covers

Duplication and reuse. No tool detects "this is a second Button." Nothing catches a bare token
key used as a JSX prop. Nothing catches a layout defect. Nothing catches a component whose data
doesn't exist on the tier it ships to.

# FED Build Manual — Manual UI Build & Delivery

**Owner:** Marcel Navarro · **Started:** August 2026 · **Revised:** 25 August 2026

The developer-facing half. This is the sequenced procedure for taking a Zimmermann UI story
from session start to merged PR.

**Companions:** `uiBuild-knowledge.md` (why the machine behaves the way it does — read it when
something fails silently) · `fedLead-playbook.md` (the lead role: refinement, estimation,
review culture, escalation).

**Authority on styling:** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`. If this manual and that file
disagree, **that file wins** — and tell me, because it means this one is stale.

---

## 1. The Operating Principles

### Static-first

Props in, markup out. A component under `overrides/app/components/` receives its data and
renders it. It does not fetch.

Mock data goes in the story — never a temporary fetch you intend to remove. A component that
owns its own data-fetching cannot be reused where the data arrives differently: SSR-prefetched,
mocked in Storybook, or composed by a parent that already has it.

**The one exception**, and it is narrow: Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks
(`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) may be called from any component, including a presentational leaf.
They read from a Provider mounted above the route tree, so they don't create the
SSR/Storybook/composition problem the rule exists to prevent. This covers content identical for
every consumer regardless of route — not anything that varies per page.

⚠️ **Their no-Provider behaviour differs and it will bite you in tests.** `useUiCopy` degrades
to fallback text and renders with zero setup. **`useIntl` throws**, and its `IntlProvider` is
mounted by the base SFCC `_app`, not `_app-config` — a narrower subtree than you'd expect. Any
Vitest test rendering a `useIntl` consumer must wrap it.

### Leverage what already exists

Four rungs, in order:

1. **Use the base SFCC component as-is.**
2. **Override it** — mirror the path under `overrides/`, keep the kebab-case filename.
3. **Compose existing ui-kit atoms** into something new.
4. **Build a new component.** Rarest. Justify it.

Before rung 4, check the registry (`.claude/registry/`) and grep `ui-kits/`.

⚠️ **The `shared/ui` barrel is not the leverage play it looks like.** Overriding
`shared/ui/<Name>` to propagate branded styling into base cart/checkout/account **does not
work** — `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` re-exports relatively, which the resolver doesn't rewrite,
and 208 base files import the barrel while 0 import the individual module. See
`uiBuild-knowledge.md` §4.

### Figma stays open the whole time

Not at the end. **And check the Jira card's Figma link actually points at your frame** — a
stale link propagates: you build the wrong thing, the BA signs off against a different frame,
QA tests a third source. If it's wrong, ask the BA to fix the card rather than working it out
in a DM.

There are **two Figma files** and cross-comparing them produces confident nonsense. See
`uiBuild-knowledge.md` §5.

### Ask in the group chat

Roughly 30 minutes stuck is the trigger. One question at a time.

### The bar you're building to

The SOW allows **10 defects, no Sev3**. That's the whole project, not per sprint. Expect UI PRs
to be reviewed against the preview environment **and** Figma. Self-review the same way before
you open it (§9) — it's faster than a review round-trip.

## 2. Before you write any code

### Confirm the branch

```bash
git branch --show-current
```

If it's `develop` or `main`, stop. No changes.

### Check what already exists

Read `.claude/registry/` for the component. The `Origin` column is what matters:

| Origin | Means |
|---|---|
| `Custom` | Zimmermann-authored, already here |
| `Override` | already mirrored into `overrides/` |
| **`Base`** | **still upstream — you pay copy-first** |

⚠️ **Do not trust the registry's `Tier` column.** `generateRegistry.mjs:122` hardcodes tier
arrays, lists no `ui-kits` path, and defaults everything else to Tier 4. Paths are reliable;
tiers are not. For what actually blocks, read `CODEOWNERS`.

### The three component families

| Family | Casing | Example |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | kebab-case, matching upstream exactly | `product-tile/` |
| **ui-kit component** | **camelCase — the default for new work** | `zimmButton/` |
| `shared/ui` primitive | PascalCase, mirroring upstream | `Button/` |

Kebab-case applies *only* to files mirroring a base Salesforce file. Naming a Zimmermann-
authored file in kebab-case falsely signals Salesforce origin — which inverts the convention's
whole purpose.

### Where a new component goes

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/
  index.tsx
  index.stories.tsx
  <name>.css.ts          ← the recipe
  index.test.tsx         ← if it has branching or event wiring
```

**Tier by composition, read off the imports:**

- **atom** — imports no other ui-kit
- **molecule** — composes atoms, light local state
- **organism** — composes molecules/atoms **and owns domain state**

An icon passed as a prop doesn't count. Slotted children don't count.

### What's actually overridden today

Eleven directories:

```
_app-config  button  contentful  footer  foundation  header
icons  pageContainer  product-view  ui-kits  uiCopyProvider
```

Still base, despite being referenced throughout `.claude/rules/`: `product-tile`,
`display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `list-menu`, `drawer-menu`, `seo`.
**Assume most stories pay copy-first.**

### The copy-first rule

For any task requiring an override that doesn't exist yet, prepare **all of them at once**
before any functional change:

1. Copy each file from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path.
2. Convert to `.ts`/`.tsx`, update imports.
3. `npx tsc --noEmit`.
4. Add a temporary `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')` to each.
5. **Stop.** Let the user confirm the overrides are rendering.
6. Remove the `console.log`s, then make functional changes.

Never bundle this silently with functional work.

## 3. Design Foundations

*The longest section, and the part that moves. Read it before your first component.*

### The styling hierarchy

1. **`textStyle`** for anything textual — `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`. All 22
   Handover text styles are registered.
2. **`var(--zimm-*)`** for colour and spacing.
3. **The component's own recipe** for anything varying by variant/size/state.
4. **`sx`** for a one-off prop-system gap.
5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it. In practice: never. There is
   no `.scss` anywhere in the footer or `ui-kits`.

### ⚠️ [CORRECTED] Rung 2 inverted — bare token strings are now wrong

An earlier revision of this manual taught `color="text.default"` and `padding="m"`, and said
seeing `var()` in a `.tsx` was a smell. **That is backwards from the current rule.**

```tsx
// ❌ bare Chakra/theme token string
<Box color="text.default" padding="m" />

// ✅ raw var(--zimm-*) reference
<Box color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" padding="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />
```

The reason is **house style, not correctness** — a bare key resolves identically, but forces a
reviewer to check `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it's correct.

`textStyle` stays a bare key. It's the one exception: there's no `var()` for the composite.

**In practice this rarely arises**, because brand values mostly shouldn't be in JSX at all.
Measured on `develop`: `var(--zimm-*)` appears in **18 recipe files** and exactly **one**
component `.tsx` — a conditional `paddingLeft` no Chakra prop expresses. Type via `textStyle`,
colour and spacing into the recipe, `var()` in JSX only for a genuine gap.

### ⚠️ The trap: a spacing key on a sizing prop

**This shipped a completely broken footer, so it's worth being blunt about.**

```tsx
padding: 'xl',   // ✅ reads theme.space.xl
width: 'xl',     // ❌ reads theme.sizes.xl = 36rem = 576px
```

Only `space` is registered. `sizes`, `fontSizes`, `lineHeights`, `letterSpacings` are not.
Measured blow-up range **8×–112×**. And `s`/`m`/`l` are absent from Chakra's `sizes`, so those
declarations are **dropped silently**.

Nothing catches this. `'xl'` is a valid `SystemStyleObject` value so TypeScript is satisfied,
no lint rule exists, and no test asserts layout. It passed `tsc`, `eslint`, `vitest`,
CodeRabbit (local *and* PR) and the Storybook a11y run — only rendering the page found it.

`recipeGuards.test.ts` now guards it **inside recipes**. It cannot see a JSX prop.

### ⚠️ `extendTheme` MERGES — it does not replace

Name a recipe `Footer` and it deep-merges into base SFCC's `Footer`, inheriting parts you never
wrote. Namespace everything: `ZimmFooter`.

`INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` — those three are deliberate. Anything
else must be namespaced, and `recipeGuards.test.ts` fails the build if it isn't.

⚠️ A recipe unit test **cannot catch this**: `extendTheme` doesn't populate `theme.__cssMap`,
only `ChakraProvider` does. A direct `css()(theme)` assertion passes vacuously.

### Responsive steps are explicit media queries

```ts
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: {
  flexDirection: 'row',
  padding: `var(--zimm-scale-4xl) var(--zimm-scale-3xl) ${SPACE_SECTION}`,
},
```

Two reasons. The array shorthand (`['2xs','2xs','xs','xs']`) puts a bare token key at every
step and the guard flags all four. And `BP.desktop` (64em) **conflicts with Chakra's `lg`=62em
/ `xl`=80em**, so a responsive prop silently steps at the wrong width.

### Register the recipe or it throws

Chakra resolves a recipe by the string key passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path.
Co-location is therefore free — but the key must be in `theme/components/index.ts` or
destructuring throws at runtime.

The consumption pattern is always three lines:

```ts
const ZIMM_FOOTER_RECIPE = 'ZimmFooter';
const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_FOOTER_RECIPE, {});
```

### Interaction state belongs in CSS, not React state

`_hover`, `_active`, `_focusVisible`, `_disabled` in the recipe. Not `useState` + `onMouseEnter`.
It looks identical in a screenshot and behaves differently in five ways that all matter:
touch devices, keyboard focus, rapid pointer movement, SSR output, and re-render cost.

⚠️ A programmatic `.focus()` does **not** match `:focus-visible`. A ring styled only on
`:focus-visible` won't appear after a scripted focus move.

### You don't add tokens

A missing token is an escalation to the UI designer (§8), not a number you invent.

If you must ship a placeholder pending sign-off, make it a **named constant with a comment
containing `provisional`, `pending`, or `placeholder`** — `npm run audit:tokens` reads that
comment and downgrades the finding to an acknowledged exception rather than a violation.
`audit-allow: <reason>` works too.

Current state: **19 unacknowledged violations** repo-wide. Don't add to it.

### Compound values and shorthand order

```ts
padding: 'xs 0',        // ❌ emitted verbatim, browser drops it
paddingInline: 0,       // ✅
```

Chakra resolves a token only as the **entire** value. And a shorthand declared *after* a
longhand resets it — `padding: 0` after `paddingBlock` wipes it.

### Figma comparison

Text nodes report a **cap-height box** and are **not comparable** to a CSS line box. Frames and
instances report a **real box** and are. A uniform residual across siblings is measurement; a
varying one is a defect. Full method in `uiBuild-knowledge.md` §5.
