## 4. The build sequence

### Step 1 — does it exist?

Registry, then `ui-kits/`, then the base package.

### Step 2 — pick the rung

**Use as-is** → done.

**Override** → copy-first (§2). Keep the kebab-case filename. If the component is used
internally by SFCC's own components, the **default export must stay a faithful port** — full
prop surface, same `forwardRef` — with Zimmermann styling behind a named export. Check with:

```bash
grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" \
  node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/
```

⚠️ **When importing a component that already has an override, use a relative path**
(`'../swatch-group'`), not the base path. The resolver is webpack-only — Storybook and Vitest
don't load it, so a base-path import silently renders the **unstyled base component** in both.

**Build custom** → §2's folder layout.

### Step 3 — execute

Named export matching the folder. Props type named for the component, declared at the top of
the file. Move it to `types.ts` only when a sibling file consumes it.

**Split when:** the component function passes ~150 lines, or branching gets deep. **Extract to
a hook when:** there are ≥2 related `useState` that change together, or a `useEffect` has a
non-trivial dependency array or a cleanup function.

### Step 4 — apply design styles

Recipe first. `sx` for genuine gaps. Never a raw literal.

---

## 5. Storybook — non-negotiable, and your build surface

Every component exported from its folder needs `index.stories.tsx`. Build *in* Storybook, not
in the running app.

### Categorisation

`Foundation/` · `Elements/` · `Layout/` · `Commerce/` · `Forms/` · `Pages/` · `Contentful/`

⚠️ **Story `title` is a different axis from the folder.** Folder = composition depth;
`title` = domain. `zimmModal` is an atom that lives under `Elements/`;
`zimmSubscribeSection` is an organism under `Forms/`.

### Content

Every file has a `Default`. Add named exports for meaningful states (`Loading`, `OutOfStock`),
not every prop combination. Add `play` only where there's interactive behaviour worth
asserting.

```tsx
import {expect, userEvent, within} from 'storybook/test'
```

⚠️ **`@storybook/test` is not installed.** `.claude/rules/testing.md:87` prescribes it;
Storybook 10 moved it to `storybook/test`. Following that line verbatim breaks. The rule is
wrong, not your code.

### Two things Storybook won't show truthfully

- **`test-storybook` needs a *built* Storybook.** Running it against the dev server makes
  results uninterpretable.
- **Portalled content is not inside `canvasElement`.** `canvasElement` is `#storybook-root`, a
  *sibling* of the portal target. Measured: 0 dialogs inside the canvas against 1 in the
  document. Query `document` for a portalled dialog and use `findByRole`, not `getByRole` —
  the render promise resolves from `useLayoutEffect`, before passive effects have mounted the
  portal. `testing.md:100`'s "never reach into `document`" has no portal carve-out; that's a
  documentation gap.

### Your branch gets a live MRT URL automatically

`deploy-preview.yml` deploys every push to `feature/**`/`fix/**` to its own ephemeral MRT
environment and posts the URL. Use it for the three-surface review in §9.

## 6. Accessibility — written as AC, not added later

WCAG **2.2** AA. Fall back to 2.1 only where 2.2 is technically infeasible, and document why.

Standing AC set for every component:

- Keyboard operable, in a sensible order
- Visible focus indicator
- Accessible name on every control
- Correct semantic element (`button` for actions, `a` for navigation)
- Colour contrast 4.5:1 body / 3:1 large
- **24×24 minimum target size** (2.5.8 — a 2.2 addition, easy to miss from a 2.1 checklist)

### [CORRECTED] a11y IS gated in CI

An earlier revision of this manual, and two separate analyses since, concluded a11y is ungated
because there is no `.storybook/test-runner.js`. **That is Storybook 8 knowledge and is wrong
for what's installed.** `@storybook/test-runner@0.24.4`'s `setup-page-script.js:390-397` reads
`story.parameters?.a11y?.test` and throws when it's `"error"`; `.storybook/preview.tsx:44` sets
exactly that.

**Do not delete that `preview.tsx` block.** Honest rider: the gate has never been made to fail
on purpose, so it is *unproven*, not absent.

### What the ast-grep rules miss

All three are `severity: warning`.

- `img-missing-alt` matches `^img$` only — **Chakra's `<Image>` is invisible to it.**
- The `IconButton` rule's `^aria-label\b` **does not match `aria-labelledby`** — the more
  correct answer gets flagged.
- The clickable-non-interactive rule checks neither `tabIndex` nor `onKeyDown`, despite
  `components.md` requiring both.

Get these right at authoring time; don't rely on the tooling.

## 7. Data availability per tier

**Your component is not done until its data exists where it ships.**

This is new, and it's here because the footer passed every gate, rendered perfectly in dev and
Storybook, and was **blank on the test tier**. Nothing in the component was wrong.

### The two mechanisms are separate

| | Content **types** (schema) | Content (**entries**) |
|---|---|---|
| Deploy | `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` | *nothing automated* |

**An Environment Template cannot carry entries.** It's structural — the SDK type has slots for
`contentTypeTemplates` and `editorInterfaceTemplates` and nothing else. The only entry-writing
code in the repo seeds the 11 `region` entries.

### Verified state, 2026-08-25

| tier | types | entries |
|---|---|---|
| **dev** | 14 | 42 |
| test / sit / uat / staging | **0** | **0** |

The environments exist and are empty. Nothing has ever been promoted out of dev. **The
template covers only 5 of dev's 14 types** — the other 9 were UI-authored and have no code
representation.

### Before you say a component works on a tier

```bash
curl -s "https://cdn.contentful.com/spaces/<space>/environments/<env>/entries?content_type=<type>&limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <that tier's delivery token>"
```

`total: 1` → it will render. `unknownContentType` → the model was never installed. Use
`limit=1`; the CDA returns an unreliable `total` at `limit=0`.

### Fetch depth is load-bearing

`include: 3` is not arbitrary. At depth 2 the `regions` array arrives as unresolved stubs, a
field access throws, the `.catch` swallows it, and the **entire component renders nothing**.
A depth mistake is indistinguishable from a network failure when you're looking at the page.

**Check the Network tab before assuming the component is broken.** Eight distinct failure modes
look identical from the rendered page.

## 9. Before you open a PR

### Gate zero — does it build

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run lint
npm run test
npm run audit:tokens
npm run build
```

⚠️ **Vitest does not run `play` functions.** Storybook interaction tests are a separate
command against a *built* Storybook.

⚠️ **`lint`, `tsc` and `audit:tokens` are gated nowhere in CI.** If you don't run them, nobody
does. `npm run lint` currently fails repo-wide on pre-existing prettier errors.

### Two repo-specific failure modes

- **A `develop` merge can delete a declaration your branch depends on.** Re-run `tsc` **after**
  every merge, not just before.
- **The rule can be wrong, not your code.** Several `.claude/rules/` lines currently prescribe
  things that break — `testing.md:87`'s `@storybook/test`, `testing.md:100`'s missing portal
  carve-out. Check the rule against the installed package before contorting the code.

### Three-surface self-review

Review your own PR the way the reviewer will:

1. **The diff** — token usage, naming, dead code, test coverage.
2. **The preview environment** — the MRT URL on your branch.
3. **Figma, side by side** — at mobile *and* desktop. Layout bugs are invisible in a diff and
   invisible to every automated gate.

### Local CodeRabbit

```bash
coderabbit auth status
cr review --light --base develop
```

Required by AGENTS.md, verified by nothing. Use judgement on whether a flagged finding is worth
fixing now or leaving for the PR review — but the review must actually run.

### Self-check

- [ ] `tsc`, `lint`, `test`, `audit:tokens`, `build` all clean
- [ ] Story exists, with `play` if there's interactive behaviour
- [ ] Test exists if there's branching or event wiring
- [ ] No raw hex/px/rem/em without a `provisional`/`pending`/`audit-allow` comment
- [ ] No bare token key on a sizing or typography prop
- [ ] Recipe namespaced and registered in `theme/components/index.ts`
- [ ] Keyboard-operable, focus visible, names on all controls, 24×24 targets
- [ ] Compared against Figma at mobile and desktop
- [ ] Jira URL in the PR body (the Forge app isn't installed — nothing does this for you)
- [ ] Protection-tier block filled honestly
- [ ] No `Co-Authored-By` trailer

### ⚠️ Read the check *history*, not the head SHA

**A skipped required check counts as passing.** `detect-changes` diffs
`since_last_remote_commit`, so a final docs-only commit can flip both required checks to green
even if an earlier push failed them. This happened on PR #59 — a 93-commit PR became
merge-eligible with **zero test evidence on its head SHA**.

Read `gh pr checks` for `skipping`, not just for green.

## 10. Responding to a CodeRabbit review

**Reply in-thread to every finding — fixed or not.** CodeRabbit's learning picks up patterns
from PR conversation. Silence teaches it nothing; a fix commit with no reply doesn't count.

- **Fixed** → a short reply confirming it, referencing the commit.
- **Not fixing** → explain *which specific rule or doc* justifies it, so the same pattern gets
  recognised next time instead of re-flagged.

Nothing enforces this: `requiresConversationResolution` is `false` on all three protected
branches, so a PR merges with every thread unanswered.

These encode more project convention than the fixes did:

- **Only four files are true absolutes** — `ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`,
  `worker/main.js`. Being Tier 1 is not by itself disqualifying; being one of the four named
  absolutes is.

  over-read, and it was conceded as one.
- **An incidental Tier 1 edit that *could* be split out *should* be.** Declining on mootness is
  the weak position.
- **Fixing a bug in one component doesn't license touching its neighbours** (Hard Rule #5) —
  even a confirmed real bug, if it's pre-existing and out of scope. The systemic fix is a lint
  rule with its own story.
- **Never accept CodeRabbit's offer to open a GitHub issue.** This project tracks in Jira; a
  GitHub issue is a parallel tracker nobody watches.
- **When a repo rule is stated unconditionally, conform even for a provable no-op** — and add
  an inline comment saying so, so the next reader doesn't hunt for phantom state.
- **Cite the PRD line before you cite it.** A wrong citation in a decline poisons CodeRabbit's
  learning store and has to be retracted in-thread, not silently amended in a later commit.

### Two switches that silence it invisibly

`chore(deps)` or `dependabot` **in the PR title** disables CodeRabbit entirely — title-matched,
not author-matched. So does draft status. Neither shows as a failing check; it just goes quiet.

## 11. Hard stops

1. Never work on `develop` or `main`.
2. Never modify a Tier 1 file without it being named in the prompt and owner approval confirmed.
3. Never modify `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`.
4. Never modify `ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js` — absolute,
   no exception.
5. Never refactor upward. Fixing a component doesn't mean touching the hook it calls.
6. Never rename or move a shared hook or component.
7. Never add or remove packages without Integration approval. When approved, `npm install` —
   don't hand-edit `package.json`.
8. Never modify test configuration.
9. Never delete files without being explicitly asked.
10. Never touch more than one protection tier in a change without confirming scope.
11. Never commit, push, or open a PR without an explicit request in the current prompt.
    Resuming from a summary or a "natural next step" is not an instruction to commit.

### Shared shell needs coordination

`header/`, `footer/`, `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/`, `seo/`, `_app/`, `_app-config/`,
`uiCopyProvider/`, `routes.tsx` are Tier 2 Global Shell, owned by **both** squads. Coordinate
before touching.

⚠️ **`.claude/rules/` is documentation; `CODEOWNERS` is configuration.** When you want to know
what will actually block a merge, read `CODEOWNERS`. It has **no catch-all rule**, so a path
absent from it needs no code-owner review regardless of what any rules file says. `squadA.md`
and `squadB.md` are six weeks stale and contradict `CODEOWNERS` on PDP ownership — CODEOWNERS
says Squad B and is the one that enforces.

---

## 12. Performance

LCP ≤ **2s at p75 mobile**. Not a polish pass.

- **Images** — always lazy-load, always serve correctly sized. Never render a full-resolution
  image at thumbnail size.
- **Code splitting** — dynamic `import()` for anything heavy not needed on first render.
- **Data fetching** — request only the fields you need; parallelise. Waterfalls are not
  acceptable.
- **Third-party** — nothing loads before consent, and nothing consent-gated may block LCP. Use
  `defer`, `async`, or post-hydration injection.
- **Bundle** — `main.js` ≤ 180 kB, `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB, enforced by `bundlesize`.

⚠️ **No CSS budget exists.** `projectState.md`'s "main.css < 50 kB" was never implemented. CSS
growth is currently ungated in both directions.

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit                 # gated nowhere — run it yourself
npm run lint                     # gated nowhere
npm run test                     # Vitest — required check on develop
npm run audit:tokens             # gated nowhere; 19 violations outstanding
npm run build
cr review --light --base develop
```

`npm start` — **do not run.** Ask for a restart if needed.

**Icons:** never import from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons`. If an icon is
missing from the overrides set, ask — don't substitute a visually similar one.
(`header/index.tsx:60` currently violates this.)

### The eight things people get wrong most

1. A bare token key on a **sizing** prop — `width: 'xl'` = 576px.
2. A recipe not namespaced, silently merging into a base SFCC recipe.
3. A recipe not registered — runtime throw on destructuring.
4. A base-path import of an already-overridden component — renders the base version in
   Storybook and Vitest.
5. `padding: 'xs 0'` — compound values never tokenise.
6. A raw literal with no `provisional`/`pending` comment.
7. Assuming the component is broken when the **data doesn't exist on that tier**.
8. Reading a PR's head-SHA checks as green when they're actually `skipping`.

## 1. `fedBuild-manual.md` (1056 → 685) — highest risk, confirmed

### Rank 1 — `iconSizes` / `actionSizes` / `motion` are gone entirely. **WORTH RESTORING.**

The single sharpest loss in the whole set. Backup §3:

> ### Icon sizes, action sizes and motion are NOT theme tokens
> These collide with Chakra scales too (`theme.sizes.lg` is 32rem and backs `w`/`h`/`boxSize` everywhere), so they're **imported as constants** instead:
> ```tsx
> import { iconSizes, actionSizes, motion } from 'app/theme/foundation';
> <Icon boxSize={iconSizes.lg} />                    // 20px
> <Button height={actionSizes.height.lg} />          // 52px
> ```
> `iconSizes` — `lg` 20 · `md` 16 · `sm` 12
> `actionSizes` — `height.{lg:52, md:40}` · `paddingX.{lg:32, md:20}` · `gap:16`
> `motion` — `duration.{fast:200ms, default:300ms, slow:500ms}` · `easing.{standard, slides, fades}`
> ⚠️ **Motion values are PROVISIONAL** and pending designer sign-off.

Across all three new files, `iconSizes`/`actionSizes` appear **once**, in a list of things `zimmTokens.ts` imports (`uiBuild-knowledge.md:33`). `motion` appears nowhere as guidance. The PROVISIONAL warning is gone.

**Verified still current:** `sizes.ts` exists with exactly those values, and its own header comment says *"Import these constants directly instead — `<Icon boxSize={iconSizes.lg} />`"*. `motion.ts` still carries `PROVISIONAL: Motion design is pending formal sign-off`.

Why this costs the most: the new docs spend three separate passages warning that a bare key on `boxSize`/`width` is an 8×–112× blow-up, and that a raw px literal is an `audit:tokens` violation — **then never say what the correct answer is.** A developer sizing an icon now has both wrong answers documented and the right one deleted.

### Rank 2 — the Storybook `ignore-loader` empty-icon fact. **WORTH RESTORING.**

> Base-template SVGs are `ignore-loader`ed in `.storybook/main.js`, mirroring the browser build. Any icon sourced from `@salesforce/retail-react-app` therefore renders as an **empty box** in Storybook while rendering correctly in the app. Twelve of `ZimmIcon`'s types are currently in that state. Our own icons in `zimm.tsx` are unaffected — so an icon that appears blank in Storybook is usually a sourcing signal, not a broken glyph.

Zero hits for `ignore-loader` or `empty box` in the new set. Pure debugging-hours loss, and it pairs with the `ZimmIcon`-throws-under-Vitest note that *was* kept (`uiBuild` §10) — the two are the same root cause and only half survived.

New docs say only *"All 22 Handover text styles are registered"* (`fedBuild-manual.md:167`). The enumerated list — `heading1Strong heading1 heading2 heading3 · body1Strong body1 body2Strong body2 · mobileBody1Strong mobileBody1 mobileBody2 · label caption · linkLg linkSm · button buttonSm · productNames price · navigation · footer · serif` — is gone from all three.

**Verified:** `typography.ts` still defines exactly those 22 keys. `textStyle` is the mandatory first rung of the hierarchy in all three new docs; the list of legal values for that rung now exists nowhere in the doc set.

### Rank 4 — three `extendTheme` merge mechanics. **WORTH RESTORING.**

Three distinct facts, all gone:

**(a) The `parts` rule:**
> Always declare your own `parts` array. A recipe with no `parts` inherits the base's list, so any Zimmermann part you add is undeclared.

**(b) The reordering mechanism** (the subtle half of the merge trap):
> A key that already exists in the base keeps the *base's* position in the merged object; a key you add that the base lacks is appended **last**.

Both new docs state *that* `extendTheme` merges and *that* shorthand-after-longhand resets — but neither says the merge is what **reorders** them. `uiBuild` §2 splits these into separate numbered items (1 and 4) with no link, so the causal chain that made the footer's `subscribeHeading` gap collapse is no longer derivable.

New `fedBuild` §5 is one sentence. Gone:

Zero hits for `/session-start`, `/scope-check`, `/audit-tier`, `/code-quality`, `/pr-checklist` as guidance anywhere in the new set (one incidental mention of `/session-start` inside a staleness warning). ### The §6 rewrite is a degradation, not a compression. **WORTH RESTORING — all six.**

Backup §6 was six mechanisms with mechanisms and fixes. New §6 is headed *"Six mechanisms, each with its fix"* and four of the six state no mechanism and no fix. Four are **materially different claims**:

| # | Backup | New | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "A wrapped element takes **available width, not its longest line**. `width: min-content` resolves to the widest unbreakable run." | "a wrapper **shrinks to content** unless told otherwise" | **Opposite claim.** `min-content` gone (zero hits) |
| 2 | "`minHeight` plus `align-items: center` **loses leading when content wraps**… Derive height from `lineHeight` plus padding instead." | "reserves space without collapsing when empty" | **Bug turned into a feature.** The fix is gone |
| 3 | "a block `<li>` wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` adds roughly 1.5-2px per row… **Fix with `display: flex` on the `<li>`**" | "use **`display: block`** or set `lineHeight` explicitly" | **The new fix is the bug.** See below |
| 4 | "If the design nests a group inside a stack with no gap, do not reproduce it as a sibling in a gapped flex container… **Give the gap to the heading (`marginBottom`)** rather than the column." | "the parent owns the gap, **never the child's margin**" | **Direct inversion of the prescription** |

**#3 verified against the shipped code.** `overrides/app/components/footer/footerNavColumn/footerNavColumn.css.ts:63-69`:

> ```
> // display:flex, not the default list-item. ZimmNavItem renders an inline-flex <a> of
> // exactly 24px, but a block-level <li> wraps it in a line box whose 24px strut adds
> // descender space below the baseline — measured 25.5px against the anchor's 24px. That
> // 1.5px leaked once per row … making the links column 9px taller than Figma's 158px.
> // Making the <li> a flex container removes the line box entirely
> listItem: { listStyle: 'none', display: 'flex' },
> ```

`display: block` is precisely the state that caused the defect. The new doc prescribes it as the fix. This is the only place in the audit where the revision would actively reintroduce a shipped bug.

## 1. `fedBuild-manual.md` (1056 → 685) — highest risk, confirmed

### Rank 1 — `iconSizes` / `actionSizes` / `motion` are gone entirely. **WORTH RESTORING.**

The single sharpest loss in the whole set. Backup §3:

> ### Icon sizes, action sizes and motion are NOT theme tokens
> These collide with Chakra scales too (`theme.sizes.lg` is 32rem and backs `w`/`h`/`boxSize` everywhere), so they're **imported as constants** instead:
> ```tsx
> import { iconSizes, actionSizes, motion } from 'app/theme/foundation';
> <Icon boxSize={iconSizes.lg} />                    // 20px
> <Button height={actionSizes.height.lg} />          // 52px
> ```
> `iconSizes` — `lg` 20 · `md` 16 · `sm` 12
> `actionSizes` — `height.{lg:52, md:40}` · `paddingX.{lg:32, md:20}` · `gap:16`
> `motion` — `duration.{fast:200ms, default:300ms, slow:500ms}` · `easing.{standard, slides, fades}`
> ⚠️ **Motion values are PROVISIONAL** and pending designer sign-off.

Across all three new files, `iconSizes`/`actionSizes` appear **once**, in a list of things `zimmTokens.ts` imports (`uiBuild-knowledge.md:33`). `motion` appears nowhere as guidance. The PROVISIONAL warning is gone.

**Verified still current:** `sizes.ts` exists with exactly those values, and its own header comment says *"Import these constants directly instead — `<Icon boxSize={iconSizes.lg} />`"*. `motion.ts` still carries `PROVISIONAL: Motion design is pending formal sign-off`.

Why this costs the most: the new docs spend three separate passages warning that a bare key on `boxSize`/`width` is an 8×–112× blow-up, and that a raw px literal is an `audit:tokens` violation — **then never say what the correct answer is.** A developer sizing an icon now has both wrong answers documented and the right one deleted.

### Rank 2 — the Storybook `ignore-loader` empty-icon fact. **WORTH RESTORING.**

> Base-template SVGs are `ignore-loader`ed in `.storybook/main.js`, mirroring the browser build. Any icon sourced from `@salesforce/retail-react-app` therefore renders as an **empty box** in Storybook while rendering correctly in the app. Twelve of `ZimmIcon`'s types are currently in that state. Our own icons in `zimm.tsx` are unaffected — so an icon that appears blank in Storybook is usually a sourcing signal, not a broken glyph.

Zero hits for `ignore-loader` or `empty box` in the new set. Pure debugging-hours loss, and it pairs with the `ZimmIcon`-throws-under-Vitest note that *was* kept (`uiBuild` §10) — the two are the same root cause and only half survived.

**(b) The reordering mechanism** (the subtle half of the merge trap):
> A key that already exists in the base keeps the *base's* position in the merged object; a key you add that the base lacks is appended **last**.

Both new docs state *that* `extendTheme` merges and *that* shorthand-after-longhand resets — but neither says the merge is what **reorders** them. `uiBuild` §2 splits these into separate numbered items (1 and 4) with no link, so the causal chain that made the footer's `subscribeHeading` gap collapse is no longer derivable.

## 2. `uiBuild-knowledge.md` (456 → 690) — grew, but §6 got worse

This file gained substantially (§8 CMS tiers, §11 signposts). Its losses are concentrated and one is actively harmful.

### The §6 rewrite is a degradation, not a compression. **WORTH RESTORING — all six.**

Backup §6 was six mechanisms with mechanisms and fixes. New §6 is headed *"Six mechanisms, each with its fix"* and four of the six state no mechanism and no fix. Four are **materially different claims**:

| # | Backup | New | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "A wrapped element takes **available width, not its longest line**. `width: min-content` resolves to the widest unbreakable run." | "a wrapper **shrinks to content** unless told otherwise" | **Opposite claim.** `min-content` gone (zero hits) |
| 2 | "`minHeight` plus `align-items: center` **loses leading when content wraps**… Derive height from `lineHeight` plus padding instead." | "reserves space without collapsing when empty" | **Bug turned into a feature.** The fix is gone |
| 3 | "a block `<li>` wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` adds roughly 1.5-2px per row… **Fix with `display: flex` on the `<li>`**" | "use **`display: block`** or set `lineHeight` explicitly" | **The new fix is the bug.** See below |
| 4 | "If the design nests a group inside a stack with no gap, do not reproduce it as a sibling in a gapped flex container… **Give the gap to the heading (`marginBottom`)** rather than the column." | "the parent owns the gap, **never the child's margin**" | **Direct inversion of the prescription** |

**#3 verified against the shipped code.** `overrides/app/components/footer/footerNavColumn/footerNavColumn.css.ts:63-69`:

> ```
> // display:flex, not the default list-item. ZimmNavItem renders an inline-flex <a> of
> // exactly 24px, but a block-level <li> wraps it in a line box whose 24px strut adds
> // descender space below the baseline — measured 25.5px against the anchor's 24px. That
> // 1.5px leaked once per row … making the links column 9px taller than Figma's 158px.
> // Making the <li> a flex container removes the line box entirely
> listItem: { listStyle: 'none', display: 'flex' },
> ```

`display: block` is precisely the state that caused the defect. The new doc prescribes it as the fix. This is the only place in the audit where the revision would actively reintroduce a shipped bug.

## 2. `uiBuild-knowledge.md` (456 → 690) — grew, but §6 got worse

This file gained substantially (§8 CMS tiers, §11 signposts). Its losses are concentrated and one is actively harmful.

### The §6 rewrite is a degradation, not a compression. **WORTH RESTORING — all six.**

Backup §6 was six mechanisms with mechanisms and fixes. New §6 is headed *"Six mechanisms, each with its fix"* and four of the six state no mechanism and no fix. Four are **materially different claims**:

| # | Backup | New | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "A wrapped element takes **available width, not its longest line**. `width: min-content` resolves to the widest unbreakable run." | "a wrapper **shrinks to content** unless told otherwise" | **Opposite claim.** `min-content` gone (zero hits) |
| 2 | "`minHeight` plus `align-items: center` **loses leading when content wraps**… Derive height from `lineHeight` plus padding instead." | "reserves space without collapsing when empty" | **Bug turned into a feature.** The fix is gone |
| 3 | "a block `<li>` wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` adds roughly 1.5-2px per row… **Fix with `display: flex` on the `<li>`**" | "use **`display: block`** or set `lineHeight` explicitly" | **The new fix is the bug.** See below |
| 4 | "If the design nests a group inside a stack with no gap, do not reproduce it as a sibling in a gapped flex container… **Give the gap to the heading (`marginBottom`)** rather than the column." | "the parent owns the gap, **never the child's margin**" | **Direct inversion of the prescription** |

**#3 verified against the shipped code.** `overrides/app/components/footer/footerNavColumn/footerNavColumn.css.ts:63-69`:

> ```
> // display:flex, not the default list-item. ZimmNavItem renders an inline-flex <a> of
> // exactly 24px, but a block-level <li> wraps it in a line box whose 24px strut adds
> // descender space below the baseline — measured 25.5px against the anchor's 24px. That
> // 1.5px leaked once per row … making the links column 9px taller than Figma's 158px.
> // Making the <li> a flex container removes the line box entirely
> listItem: { listStyle: 'none', display: 'flex' },
> ```

`display: block` is precisely the state that caused the defect. The new doc prescribes it as the fix. This is the only place in the audit where the revision would actively reintroduce a shipped bug.

### `textStyle` can never emit a `var()` — and the 85% consequence. **WORTH RESTORING.**

> `zimmTokens.ts` imports *from* `typography.ts`, so the reverse would be a circular import. `textStyle` therefore always expands to resolved literals at build time. **This is correct behaviour, not a defect** — and it means roughly **85% of what an emitted-CSS audit flags as "raw literals" is `textStyle` working as designed.**

Zero hits for `circular import` or the 85% figure. This is the fact that stops the next `audit:tokens` run from being misread — and `audit:tokens` is now cited in five places across the new set with an open "triage 19 findings" action.

Done. Both verification passes ran, and the second one earned its keep — it caught a change that would have reintroduced a shipped bug.

## Final state

| file | original | after revision | after fixes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `fedLead-playbook.md` | 800 | 688 | **792** |
| `fedBuild-manual.md` | 1,056 | 685 | **807** |
| `uiBuild-knowledge.md` | 456 | 690 | **763** |
| `zimmermann_frontend_lead_playbook.md` | 474 | — | **496** (archived) |

Backups of all four originals: `~/.claude/jobs/652997c6/tmp/`.

## What the verifiers caught

**The worst one was mine.** My rewritten §6 of `uiBuild-knowledge.md` prescribed `display: block` for the inline-descender leak. The shipped code uses `display: flex`, and its own comment explains that **`display: block` is the bug** — a block `<li>` wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` measured 25.5px against the anchor's 24px, leaking 1.5px per row and making the footer's links column 9px taller than Figma. Three of the other five mechanisms in that section were also inverted or stripped of their fix. Section rewritten from the shipped code.

**Second worst:** I cited `product-tile`'s `CardBaseline` as the live reference for the SFCC bridge pattern — while the same document correctly listed `product-tile` as still base. Zero hits for `CardBaseline` in `overrides/`. I'd replaced an honest "no worked precedent exists" warning with a false pointer. Restored.

**The de-duplication cost real reference material.** The docs warned that a bare key on `boxSize` is an 8×–112× blow-up *and* that a raw px literal is an audit violation — then deleted `iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`, which is the correct answer. Both wrong answers documented, the right one gone. Also restored: the 22 `textStyle` names, the spacing scale, the `ignore-loader` empty-icon fact, the two semgrep security rules, the `extendTheme` `parts` rule and merge-reordering mechanism, and the override-first *positive* case.

**23 factual defects fixed**, including four that came from my own memory files — `208` barrel importers is really 212, `header/index.tsx:302` is 311, `testing.md:87/100` are 115/128, and the "18 recipe files" figure was measured on your working tree while attributed to `develop` (it's 14 there). Both memories corrected too.

## Two things to know

**`fedBuild-manual.md` had a real contradiction** — it marked `padding="m"` ❌ on one line and `padding: 'xl'` ✅ eleven lines later. Both are bare token keys on a spacing prop. Now stated explicitly: a bare key on a *spacing* prop is correct-but-against-house-style; on a *sizing or typography* prop it's broken. First gets a review comment, second ships a 576px icon.

**`fedLead-playbook.md` had nine orphaned `*Covers responsibilities N*` labels** pointing at a mandate table I'd compressed away — and they were scrambled against the original besides. Removed rather than faked.

The audit also flagged voice drift I haven't fully corrected: `fedBuild` lost 76% of its second-person address, and `fedLead` §3–§4 carry the retired doc's essayistic register next to a table-heavy governance section. Both are readable; neither is wrong. Worth a pass if it bothers you when you read them.

7	decisions, event wiring) gets its own `index.test.ts`/`index.test.tsx`, even when the state it
8	renders is owned by a hook that already has its own test, or a parent's assembly-level
9	Storybook `play` already exercises the rendered result. Resolve the duplication concern by
10	**scoping what that file asserts** — mock the hook/child component whose internals are proven
11	elsewhere, and test only this component's own contract (given a state, does it render the
12	right branch; given a DOM event, does it call the right handler) — not by leaving the
13	component with no test of its own. Relying on a *different* component's story to prove *this*

15	and can silently vanish if that unrelated file changes. See

17	resulting pattern (mocks `useSubscribeSection` and `ZimmSubscribeModal`, tests only its own

content.text:
I have the full picture, and the three issues you're seeing are one root cause with three symptoms. Here's the rundown.

---

# How the footer's responsiveness is wired

## 1. There are four bands, and they don't match the project's grid

The footer defines its own breakpoints in `theme/components/footerShared.ts`:

| name | value | source |
|---|---|---|
| `tablet` | 48em / **768px** | imported from `foundation/gridSystem.ts` ✅ |
| `tabletWide` | 53.75em / **860px** | **footer-only — no foundation equivalent** |
| `desktop` | 64em / **1024px** | **footer-only — and ≠ Chakra's `lg` 62em / `xl` 80em** |

Meanwhile `gridSystem.ts` says the page is **tablet from 768 all the way to 1279px**, and desktop only at 1280.

So the footer flips into its desktop layout at **1024**, while the rest of the page is still in tablet. And it inserts an extra step at **860** that exists nowhere else in the system. That's four footer bands against the grid's three, with only one boundary shared.

## 2. How the top row is built

`footer.css.ts` lays out one flex row at ≥768px with three decisions that interact badly:

```ts
contentRow: { flexDirection: 'row', justifyContent: 'space-between',
              gap: 0,                                    // ← no gap between the two columns
              padding: '4xl 3xl 3rem' }                  // ← 40px each side
subscribe:   { flex: '0 0 20rem' }                       // ← 320px, CANNOT shrink
links:       { flex: 1 }                                 // ← absorbs everything left over
```

The email field inside the subscribe column is `width: 100%`, so it's **always exactly 320px** from 768px upward.

**`gap: 0` is the key.** `justify-content: space-between` only pushes things apart when there's leftover space — and `links: flex: 1` eats all of it by definition. So there is **zero designed separation** between the email field and the nav groups. The only thing keeping them apart is `justifyContent: flex-end` inside `linksInner`, which pushes the columns right *if* they have room to spare.

## 3. The arithmetic — this is your issue #1 and #2

Space available for the nav block = **viewport − 80 (padding) − 320 (subscribe)**.

Space the three nav columns want = **3 × 160px** (their `maxWidth`) **+ 2 × the gap**, and the gap changes per band:

| viewport | gap | needed | available | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 768 | 40px | 560 | **368** | short **192px** |
| 859 | 40px | 560 | **459** | short **101px** |
| **860** | **80px** | **640** | **460** | short **180px** ← *worse than 859* |
| 1023 | 80px | 640 | **623** | short 17px |
| **1024** | 0 | 480 | **600 fixed** | ✅ 120px slack |

**The entire 768–1023 band is short, and the 860 breakpoint makes it worse rather than better.** `linksInner` doubles its gap from 40px to 80px at 860 — spending 40 more pixels it doesn't have.

Then at 1024 everything snaps right, because `links` stops being `flex: 1` and becomes a fixed 600px box with `gap: 0` and `space-between`.

**Why the text wraps (issue #2).** The nav column is:

```ts
col: { minWidth: 0, ... }                               // base
     [tablet]: { width: 'auto', maxWidth: '160px', flexShrink: 1 }
```

`linksInner` is `flexWrap: nowrap`. So when the row is short, the columns **cannot wrap to a second line** — and with `flexShrink: 1` and `minWidth: 0` they will squeeze all the way to zero. The row refuses to break, so the words break instead. "Book an Appointment", "Acknowledgement of Country", "Orders & Shipping" go first.

**Why there's no space to the email field (issue #1).** Same cause, seen from the other side. The columns squeeze right up against the 320px subscribe column because `gap: 0` gives them nothing to stop at, and `flex-end` has no slack to work with.

## 4. The bottom bar — issue #3

`bottomBar.css.ts` at ≥768px puts everything in one row with `space-between`, and **every single item is `whiteSpace: 'nowrap'`**:

- the locale control (`localeText`, `localeButton`)
- the copyright (`copyright`)
- **five** legal links (`legalGrid` switches to `flexWrap: 'nowrap'` at tablet)

Nothing can wrap. Nothing can shrink. The five links are Accessibility · Terms & Conditions · Privacy Policy · Modern Slavery · Cookie Settings, with 24px gaps at tablet and 32px at desktop.

When the total exceeds the available width, there's no relief valve — it just overflows and you get horizontal scroll. On mobile this is handled properly (a 2-column wrapping grid with `width: 140px` per link); that safety net is switched **off** at exactly the point the row gets tight.

## 5. The one root cause

**Every fixed dimension in the footer is sized for the 1440px Figma frame, and the only escape hatch — wrapping — is disabled across the whole tablet band.**

Three fixed values (320px subscribe, 160px column cap, 600px links box) plus `flexWrap: nowrap` plus `gap: 0` means the layout has no way to absorb a viewport it wasn't drawn at. Figma has frames at **402 / 1023 / 1440**. The band 768–1022 was never drawn — and it's exactly where all three of your symptoms live.

This is a known-shaped problem here: `.claude/rules/` and the footer's own comments record that the unframed tablet band caused 18px of horizontal scroll and seven wrapped labels once before.

---

## What I'd want before proposing a fix

The box arithmetic above is exact. The **text widths are estimates** — I haven't measured where each label actually breaks, and the fallback font renders ~13% wider than Futura Round, so the break points differ before and after the webfont loads.

I can get real numbers by building Storybook and measuring the footer at 768 / 800 / 860 / 900 / 1023 / 1024, which would give you the precise break point for each symptom rather than my arithmetic. Want me to do that before we talk fixes?

I haven't changed anything — this was all reading.

Exact break points, measured at 1px resolution with a falsifiable instrument.

# Real break points

## Issue #2 — nav labels wrapping

**Two broken zones with a clean island between them:**

| range | state | what wraps |
|---|---|---|
| ≤ 767 | ✅ clean | mobile 2-col layout |
| **768 – 835** | ❌ **broken** | Brand Protection, Boutique Locator, Book an Appointment, Orders & Shipping |
| 836 – 859 | ✅ clean | — |
| **860 – 915** | ❌ **broken again** | Brand Protection, Book an Appointment, Orders & Shipping |
| 916 + | ✅ clean | — |

**The `tabletWide` breakpoint at 860 actively re-breaks a layout that had just recovered.** At 859 the columns have reached their natural width (115/135/106) and nothing wraps. At 860 the `linksInner` gap jumps from 40px → 80px, the columns are squeezed back to 97/114/89, and the labels wrap again. That breakpoint spends 40px it doesn't have.

## Issue #3 — bottom bar

Not overflow — **"Terms & Conditions" wraps onto two lines**, making the bar **93px tall instead of 79px**.

| range | bar height |
|---|---|
| **768 – 908** | **93px** ← "Terms & Conditions" on 2 lines |
| 909 + | 79px |

Every item in that row is `whiteSpace: nowrap` *except* the anchors' own text, so the row can't compress — the longest link just breaks internally instead.

## Issue #1 — no space between email field and nav groups

| range | gap |
|---|---|
| **768 – 1023** | **0px** — they touch |
| 1024 | 24px |
| 1440 | 440px |

Exactly zero across the entire tablet band, because `contentRow` sets `gap: 0` and `links: flex: 1` absorbs all remaining space, leaving `space-between` nothing to distribute. It only appears at 1024 when `links` becomes a fixed 600px box.

---

## Why this reads as "certain points"

Overlay the three and the tablet band has **five** distinct states:

```
767 ────┬──── mobile: everything fine
768 ────┤ nav wraps · legal wraps · gap 0
836 ────┤ nav OK   · legal wraps · gap 0
860 ────┤ nav wraps · legal wraps · gap 0     ← tabletWide makes it worse
909 ────┤ nav wraps · legal OK    · gap 0
916 ────┤ nav OK    · legal OK    · gap 0
1024 ───┴──── desktop: fully correct
```

## The part that matters for QA

Common portrait tablet widths land almost entirely inside the broken zones:

| device (portrait) | width | state |
|---|---|---|
| iPad Mini 6th gen | 744 | ✅ mobile layout |
| iPad Mini (older) | **768** | ❌ all three issues |
| iPad 10.9" | **810** | ❌ all three |
| iPad Air | **820** | ❌ all three |
| iPad Pro 11" | **834** | ❌ **misses the clean island by 2px** |
| iPad Pro 12.9" | 1024 | ✅ correct |

Only the 12.9" Pro renders the footer as designed.

---

## Method notes

Measured against a fresh `build-storybook` of this branch, `Layout/Footer → Default`, served static — not the dev server.

Two things I verified rather than assumed:

- **Futura Round is genuinely loaded** — "BOOK AN APPOINTMENT" renders at 151.8px against 167.3px for a deliberately-bogus family, a 10.2% delta matching the documented ~13%. So these are real-font break points, not fallback ones. They will differ slightly *before* the webfont loads.
- **My first wrap detector was broken** and I discarded its output. It used `getClientRects()` on the anchor, which returns multiple rects for an `inline-flex` element regardless of line breaks — it reported every label as wrapped even at 1440. The replacement counts distinct line-tops from the *text nodes*, and I proved it both ways: it reports nothing unexpected at 1440, and it correctly reports 2 lines when an anchor is forcibly narrowed.

**"Acknowledgement of Country" wraps at every width including 1440 — that's by design**, per the code comments: Figma's own item is 118×38 (two lines), and the 160px cap exists to reproduce that. I excluded it from the counts above.

Nothing changed — measurement only. Want me to work up fixes?

Measured, not assumed. Here's what her message settles and what it doesn't.

## Her spec vs our code — she's confirmed we're right on all three

| band | Figma | our code | |
|---|---|---|---|
| mobile | 320 – 767 | `< 768` (base) | ✅ |
| tablet | 768 – 1023 | `BP.tablet = 768` | ✅ |
| desktop | 1024 + | `BP.desktop = 1024` | ✅ |
| — | **no variant** | **`BP.tabletWide = 860`** | ❌ **we invented this** |

That's the useful part of her message: it independently confirms 768 and 1024, and it exposes a fourth breakpoint that has no variant behind it.

**`BP.tabletWide` has exactly one call site** — the `linksInner` gap jumping 40px → 80px at 860. That's its entire reason to exist, and it's the thing that re-breaks the layout at 860.

## The counterfactual, measured

I injected the removal and re-swept 768–1024 at 4px steps:

| scenario | broken ranges | damage |
|---|---|---|
| **A · current** | 768–832 **and 860–912** | ~124px of the 256px band |
| **B · `tabletWide` removed** | 768–832 only | **~68px** |

Deleting one media query removes an entire broken zone and halves the damage. Cheap, and it aligns the code with a design that never had a fourth variant.

## What her message does *not* resolve

This is the part worth pushing back on, gently. She's reading the symptom as tablet styling leaking below 768 — *"when the breakpoint reaches 767px it will condense to mobile, so we shouldn't have that weird tablet behaviour."* We already do that correctly; at 767 the mobile layout takes over cleanly and nothing is broken there.

**The breakage is inside the tablet band, and it's a design gap, not a code gap.** The tablet comp is drawn at **1023px — the very top of its own range.** It also has to render at **768px**, which is 255px narrower, and nothing in the comp says what gives way. The subscribe column is a fixed 320px at every width, so at 768 the three nav groups get 368px to fit ~436px of content.

That's why 768–832 stays broken even with `tabletWide` gone. No amount of breakpoint correction fixes it — something has to be *specified* as flexible.

content.text:
# The footer's responsiveness, plainly

## The one-sentence version

The footer is built from **fixed-width pieces** that have to fit inside a **shrinking box**, and we told them they're **not allowed to move to a new line** — so when the box gets too small, the words break instead of the layout.

---

## 1. How the footer is put together

From 768px up, the top of the footer is two things side by side:

```
│←40px→│  EMAIL SIGN-UP  │  ABOUT   CONTACT   HELP  │←40px→│
        │←── 320px ──→│  │←──── whatever's left ───→│
             FIXED              FLEXIBLE
```

Three facts about this, and all three matter:

- **The email box is exactly 320px and refuses to shrink.** In CSS that's `flex: 0 0 320px` — the middle `0` literally means "never give up any width."
- **The nav block takes whatever remains.** No more, no less.
- **There is no gap between them.** We set `gap: 0`.

## 2. The maths that breaks

At a 768px tablet:

```
768   screen
 -80  padding (40 each side)
-320  email box (fixed, won't shrink)
────
 368  ← left for the three nav columns
```

But the three columns need:

```
115 + 135 + 106   = 356   (their natural widths)
     + 40 + 40    =  80   (gaps between them)
─────────────────────────
                    436   ← what they need
```

**436 needed, 368 available. Short by 68px.**

## 3. So what happens to the missing 68px?

Here's the crux. When things don't fit, a layout has three ways out:

| escape route | did we allow it? |
|---|---|
| Move to a new line | ❌ we set `flexWrap: nowrap` |
| Get narrower | ✅ allowed — `flexShrink: 1`, `minWidth: 0` |
| Overflow the screen | ❌ blocked |

We closed the only good exit and left the bad one open. So the columns squeeze — from 115/135/106 down to **93/109/86** — and the text inside has nowhere to go but a second line.

**"Book an Appointment" becomes "Book an / Appointment."** That's your issue #2.

## 4. Why all three symptoms are the same bug

**Issue #1 — no space between email and nav.** `gap: 0` plus "nav takes everything left over" means there's nothing to separate them. Measured: **0px from 768 all the way to 1023.** It only appears at 1024, where the nav block becomes a fixed 600px box and the leftover space finally lands between them.

**Issue #2 — nav text wrapping.** The squeeze above.

**Issue #3 — bottom bar.** Same shape, different row. Every item down there is set to `nowrap`. So when the row is too tight, nothing can move to a new line — and **"Terms & Conditions"** (the longest label) breaks internally instead, making the whole bar **93px tall instead of 79px**.

One cause: *fixed pieces + no permission to wrap*. Three places it shows up.

## 5. The extra mistake at 860px

We invented a fourth breakpoint that isn't in the design. At **860px**, it makes the gaps between nav columns **bigger** — 40px → 80px.

Think about what that means. At 859px, everything has just barely recovered and looks fine. At 860px we spend 40 more pixels on empty space — pixels we don't have — and it breaks again:

```
767  mobile          ✅ fine
768  ──┐
     ❌ BROKEN        columns squeezed, words wrap
832  ──┘
836  ──┐ ✅ recovered — everything fits
859  ──┘
860  ──┐  ← our invented breakpoint fires here
     ❌ BROKEN AGAIN  gaps grow, columns squeezed again
912  ──┘
916  ──┐ ✅ fine
1023 ──┘
1024 desktop         ✅ fine
```

**I tested removing it.** Broken width across the tablet band drops from ~124px to ~68px — the entire second zone disappears. It's one media query with **one call site**.

## 6. What Kiera's message actually told us

Her spec — mobile 320–767, tablet 768–1023, desktop 1024+ — **confirms all three of our real breakpoints are correct.** That's genuinely useful; it rules out a whole class of explanation.

It also exposes the 860 as having no design behind it. There is no "tablet-wide" variant. We made it up.

But her conclusion — *"when it reaches 767 it condenses to mobile, so we shouldn't have that weird tablet behaviour"* — is diagnosing the wrong thing. Tablet styling isn't leaking below 768. We handle 767 correctly.

**The breakage is inside the tablet band, and it's a gap in the design, not the code.**

Here's why, and it's the single most important point:

> **The tablet comp is drawn at 1023px — the widest tablet ever gets.** But tablet has to work all the way down to 768px. That's **255px narrower** than anything anyone drew. Nobody ever decided what gives way.

We had to guess, and we guessed "make the email box rigid and let the nav columns absorb 100% of the loss." That guess is what fails.

## 7. What actually needs to happen

**Two things, and only one of them is ours.**

**Ours — free, do it now:** delete the 860px breakpoint. It's not in the design, it has one call site, and removing it measurably fixes 56px of the broken band.

**Kiera's — needs a decision:** what should the tablet layout do at 768px? Something has to be allowed to flex, and only design can say which:

- the email box narrows below 320, **or**
- the nav groups go two-up and stack, **or**
- the gaps tighten at the narrow end

Any of those works. Picking one is a design call, not an engineering one.

## Why this matters more than it looks

Common tablet widths in portrait:

| device | width | today |
|---|---|---|
| iPad Mini | **768** | ❌ broken |
| iPad 10.9" | **810** | ❌ broken |
| iPad Air | **820** | ❌ broken |
| iPad Pro 11" | **834** | ❌ **misses the clean zone by 2px** |
| iPad Pro 12.9" | 1024 | ✅ fine |

**Every iPad in portrait except the 12.9" Pro is inside a broken range.** That's the whole reason this reads as "weird behaviour at certain points" rather than a clean pass or fail.

---

One note on trust: the first wrap-detector I wrote was wrong — it flagged every label as wrapped even at 1440px, where the design says nothing should. I threw its output away and rebuilt it, then proved the replacement works by forcing a wrap and confirming it caught it. **Every number above comes from the second one.**

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| broken ranges | 768–832 **and 860–912** | **768–834 only** |
| broken span | ~124px | **~68px** of the 256px band |
| gap at 860 | 80px | 40px |

**2. It spans two protection tiers.** `footer.css.ts` resolves to squads-only via CODEOWNERS line 186 (last-match-wins, Tier 3), while `theme/components/footerShared.ts` hits line 117 — **Tier 2, `@tier-2-approvers`**. **3. 768–834 is still broken, and it isn't fixable in code.** That's the fixed-320px email column — at 768 the nav block gets 368px for 436px of content. Which element flexes is a design decision, and it's the question in the draft reply to Kiera.

So the footer switches layout 256px before the rest of the page does. That may be intentional or may be a second gap — worth asking, but it's a Tier 1 foundation file and out of scope here.

content.text:
Measured. Here's the trade-off in one line, then the message for Kiera.

## The constraint, exactly

At 768px there are **688px** of usable width. The desktop-derived layout wants:

```
320 (email)  +  40 (separation)  +  356 (3 nav columns)  +  80 (2 gaps)  =  796px
                                                              available  =  688px
                                                              SHORT BY   =  108px
```

**At 768 you can have any two of: a 320px email field, visible separation, nav groups on one row.** Not all three. Every measured solution is a choice about which one to give up.

## What each option actually does (all measured at 768px)

| option | email | separation | nav rows | footer height | clean at 768? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **today** | 320 | 0 | 1 | 518px | ❌ from 836 |
| **F3 · shrink the field** | **240** | **44** | 1 | **504px** | ✅ |
| **F5 · wrap nav to 2 rows** | **320** | **40** | 2 | **678px** | ✅ |
| **D · tighten everything** | 280 | 0 | 1 | 504px | ✅ |
| F1 · keep all three | 320 | 40 | 1 | 532px | ❌ from 852 — *worse than today* |

One dev-side finding worth recording: **making the email column "flexible" does nothing.** I tried `flex: 1 1 320px; min-width: 240px` and it stayed at 320 — because the row itself isn't overflowing, the nav block inside it is. The email column never feels pressure, so it never shrinks. Any fix has to name an explicit narrower width or change the nav's wrapping rules; "let it flex" isn't an option that exists here.

---

## Draft for Kiera

> Hi Kiera — following up with something concrete on the tablet footer.
>
> Removing the 860px breakpoint helped, and thank you for spotting it. It fixed everything from about 836px up. What's left is the narrow end of tablet — **768 to 835px**, which covers iPad Mini, iPad 10.9" and iPad Air in portrait, plus iPad Pro 11" by 2px.
>
> The reason it's stuck is a space problem, not a bug. At 768px the footer has 688px to work with, and the tablet design needs 796px to fit as drawn — the email field (320), the space between it and the nav groups (40), and the three nav columns with their gaps (436). We're 108px short.
>
> So something has to give, and it's a design call which one. Three options that all work — I've built and measured each:
>
> **Option 1 — narrow the email field to 240px** *(our recommendation)*
> ```
> │ Email ──────── │←44px→│ ABOUT   CONTACT   HELP │
> ```
> Everything else stays as designed: one row of nav groups, proper spacing restored, footer height unchanged. The field is narrower but still comfortably fits the placeholder and a typed address.
>
> **Option 2 — let the nav groups wrap onto two rows**
> ```
> │ Email ──────────── │←40px→│ ABOUT    CONTACT │
>                             │ HELP             │
> ```
> Keeps the email field at its full 320px and keeps the spacing. Cost is height — the footer grows from ~505px to ~680px at 768px. Arguably consistent with mobile, which already stacks.
>
> **Option 3 — tighten everything a little**
> Email to 280px and the nav gaps from 40 to 24. Fits, but the email field and the nav groups end up touching with no space between them — which is the thing that looks wrong today.
>
> Any of the three fixes it; they just look different. Could you have a look and tell us which reads best? If it's easier to judge visually I can put all three on a branch and send screenshots at 768.
>
> Two smaller ones while you're in there:
> - **"Terms & Conditions"** in the bottom bar wraps to two lines below ~909px, making that bar 14px taller. Shorten the label, or let the row wrap?
> - The footer switches to its desktop layout at **1024px**, but the page grid doesn't until **1280px**. Is 1024 right for the footer specifically, or should they match?

---

The last bullet is the one I'd genuinely like an answer to — it's the `BP.desktop` vs `gridSystem.xl` mismatch I flagged earlier, and it means the footer changes shape 256px before the rest of the page does.

Want me to build the three options on a branch and capture screenshots at 768 so she's choosing from pictures rather than description?

# Ship the footer `tabletWide` breakpoint removal as a PR

## Context

The tester and Kiera both flagged the footer misbehaving on tablet. Investigation found three
symptoms — the email field crowding the nav groups, nav labels wrapping, and the bottom bar
growing taller — with one shared root cause: fixed-width pieces in a shrinking box with
`flexWrap: nowrap` closing the only escape route.

Inside that, one thing was **our own invention rather than a design constraint**:
`BP.tabletWide` (53.75em / 860px). Kiera confirmed the Figma Footer component has exactly three
size variants — Mobile 320–767, Tablet 768–1023, Desktop 1024+ — read off the comps' own
min/max widths. There is no fourth variant. The breakpoint had a single call site and was
actively harmful: the nav columns reach their natural width around 836px, but at 860px this rule
spent 40px more on gaps than the row had, squeezing them back below content width and re-wrapping
labels that had just recovered.

**Intended outcome:** delete the unbacked breakpoint. Measured across 768–1024 in 2px steps
against a built Storybook, this takes the broken span from ~124px to ~68px of the 256px tablet
band, and eliminates the 860–912 zone entirely.

The remaining 768–834 breakage is **out of scope** — it needs a design decision from Kiera about
which element flexes, and is tracked separately.

## Current state

Branch `fix/footer-tablet-wide-breakpoint`, cut from `develop` @ `04039a9`. Edits are already
made and verified; nothing is committed.

```
overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts   |  3 ---
overrides/app/theme/components/footerShared.ts  | 17 +++++++++++++----
```

- **`footer.css.ts`** — removed the `@media (min-width: ${BP.tabletWide})` block on `linksInner`
  (a `gap` step from `3xl` to `5xl`).
- **`footerShared.ts`** — removed the `tabletWide` entry from `BP` and recorded why, so it isn't
  reintroduced. The `audit-allow:` comment was re-verified as still associating after the edit.

### Evidence already gathered

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | exit 0 |
| `npm run test` | 379 passed / 25 files |
| `npm run audit:tokens` | 4 on `develop`, 4 on branch — **zero added** |
| Browser measurement | broken span ~124px → **~68px**; 856–864 now holds 115/135/106 with no wrapping |

The wrap detector used for those numbers is falsification-checked: it reports the by-design
"Acknowledgement of Country" wrap at 1440 and nothing else, and correctly reports 2 lines when an
anchor is forcibly narrowed. An earlier detector was discarded for reporting every label as
wrapped.

## Plan

### 1. Pre-commit review gates

Run in order, on the branch as it stands:

- `npm run lint` — **capture the `develop` baseline first** (`git stash`, run, `git stash pop`).
  Lint is gated nowhere in CI and is known to fail repo-wide on pre-existing prettier errors; the
  only question is whether this change *adds* any.
- `/code-quality` — read-only audit of the branch diff against `.claude/rules/`.
- `cr review --light --base develop` — CodeRabbit CLI 0.7.5 is installed and `cr` is on PATH.
  Required by AGENTS.md before a non-trivial commit. Confirm `coderabbit auth status` first.
- `node_modules/.bin/test-storybook --ci --url http://127.0.0.1:6006` against a **built**
  Storybook — this is what CI runs (`qa.yml:405-411`); there is no npm script for it.
  `storybook-static` is already built from this branch. Serve it on 6006 first.

The Storybook run matters because `index.stories.tsx` has a `play` function that measures layout
stability. It compares *before/after* heights rather than absolute values, so a breakpoint change
should not affect it — but that is an assumption to test, not state.

Fix anything these surface, then re-run the affected gate.

### 2. Commit

One commit, conventional format per `scripts/hooks/commit-msg`. **No `Co-Authored-By` trailer.**

Proposed subject:

```
fix(footer): remove the unbacked 860px tablet-wide breakpoint
```

Body should state: the breakpoint had no Figma variant (confirmed by the UI designer against the
comps' min/max widths), it had one call site, and removing it takes the broken tablet span from
~124px to ~68px measured in 2px steps against a built Storybook.

### 3. Push and open the PR

Match the house style from merged PRs #46/#47 — **not** the literal template, which is
aspirational. Plain conventional title, no SFCC key in the title.

Body sections in order: `# Description` → `# Linked` → `# Squad ownership` →
`# Types of Changes` → `# Changes` → `# How to test-drive this PR` → `# Protection-tier check` →
`# Testing`. Omit Accessibility / Localisation / Third-party sections entirely rather than
padding them with "n/a".

**Linked** (decided with the user):

```
- Follows up: SFCC-55 (Global Footer UI, merged in PR #59)
- Sprint: SFCC Sprint 5
```

No live ticket. Note the consequence honestly in the PR: with no `SFCC-\d+` key in the title,
body or branch name, `e2e-browserstack` will not run at all. That is by design in `qa.yml`, not a
failure — there is nothing to attribute results to in Zephyr.

**Protection-tier check** — this change spans two tiers and the PR must say so:

| file | CODEOWNERS rule | owner |
|---|---|---|
| `footer/footer.css.ts` | line 186 (last match wins) | `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b` — Tier 3 |
| `theme/components/footerShared.ts` | line 117 | `@tier-2-approvers` — **Tier 2** |

### 4. Notifications owed

- **Squad B** — `footer/` is Tier 2 Global Shell, owned by both squads.
- **Kiera / UI designer** — `theme/components/` is designer-owned, and this change is a direct
  result of her variant-spec message. Send the drafted reply covering the 768–834 options at the
  same time.

## Verification

After the PR is open:

```bash
gh pr checks <n>          # read for "skipping", not just green
```

Both changed files fall inside `qa.yml`'s watched paths (`overrides/app/components/**` and
`overrides/app/theme/**`), so `unit-tests` and `storybook-test` should genuinely run rather than
skip. If either reports `skipping`, that is a signal to investigate, not to merge.

End-to-end confirmation that the fix holds:

```bash
npm run build-storybook
python3 -m http.server 6099 --directory storybook-static &
# then measure Layout/Footer → Default across 768–1024
```

Expected: no unplanned label wrapping from **836px** upward, gap steady at 40px across 856–864,
columns holding 115/135/106. The only wrap at any width should be "Acknowledgement of Country",
which is by design.

## Explicitly out of scope

- **768–834 still breaks.** Needs Kiera to choose which element flexes. Three measured options
  exist (narrow the email field to 240px; let the nav wrap to two rows; tighten everything).
- **Bottom bar** — "Terms & Conditions" wraps below ~909px, making that bar 14px taller.
- **`BP.desktop` (1024) vs `gridSystem.xl` (1280)** — the footer changes layout 256px before the
  page grid does. May be intentional; `gridSystem.ts` is Tier 1, so it is a separate conversation.

## Approval gate

Do not commit, push, or open the PR without explicit approval. Run the review gates, report what
they find, show the diff and the drafted commit message and PR body, then stop.

Audit code quality for the specified scope. Do not modify any files — this is a read-only
diagnostic. Produce a prioritised report with actionable fixes.

---

## Input

The user will provide one of:
- A file path or directory to audit
- No argument — default to files changed on the current branch: `git diff --name-only main`

If no argument is given, run: `git diff --name-only main` and audit those files.
Exclude test files (`*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`), stories (`*.stories.tsx`), and any registry files.

---

## Parallel execution

For audits covering more than 5 files, split into four independent checks and run them
as parallel agents simultaneously. Each agent receives only its own checklist — do not
bundle all checks into one agent.

- **Agent A — Naming & structure**
- **Agent B — Import analysis**
- **Agent C — TypeScript coverage**
- **Agent D — Test & story coverage**

For 5 files or fewer, run all checks sequentially in a single pass.

---

## Agent A — Naming & structure

Rules are defined once, split across [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md)
(cross-cutting), [css.md](../../rules/css.md) (Chakra/styling), and
[components.md](../../rules/components.md) (components/hooks/Storybook) — read the relevant
ones first, then apply each rule to the files in scope. Do not re-list the rules here;
that's how the files drift apart.

Walk the file list and audit each file against the relevant section:

- Every file → conventions.md **General** section.
- Every file with JSX/Chakra props → css.md **Tokens** section (no hardcoded hex/px values).
- `.tsx` under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/` → components.md
  **Components** + **Composition** sections, plus conventions.md **File naming and folder
  structure**.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/hooks/` → components.md **Hooks** section.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/utils/` → conventions.md **Utilities** section.

For each violation, record `file:line` and which rule file + bullet failed — the section
anchor is enough (e.g. "components.md → Components → Props type placement").

---

## Agent B — Import analysis

For each file, read the import statements and check:

- No circular imports: if File A imports from File B, File B must not import from File A
  (check by reading the imported file's imports in turn — one level deep is sufficient).
- No imports from a higher tier without justification:
  - A component must not import directly from internal `commerce-sdk-react` source paths.
  - A page must not bypass its own hooks to call raw API functions.
- No imports from a later-sprint feature (reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` when present).
- No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels — flag for path alias review.

---

## Agent C — TypeScript coverage

Check each file against the relevant rule file:

- Every `.ts`/`.tsx` → [typescript.md](../../rules/typescript.md) in full (no `any` without
  justification, `type` vs `interface`, non-null assertions, discriminated unions, utility
  types, `import type`, `satisfies`, `readonly`, generic naming).
- Components → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Components** (props type name,
  placement, optional `?`, callback naming, JSDoc).
- Hooks → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Hooks** (typed params, explicit
  return type, JSDoc with `@returns`).

Then run `npx tsc --noEmit` **once** for the whole branch (not per file) and report any
errors. Cross-reference any new errors against the files in scope.

---

## Agent D — Test & story coverage

For each component file under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/`:
- A paired `*.stories.tsx` exists in the same directory (required by [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) > Testing).
- For logic-heavy components or hooks: the component's **own** `*.test.ts`/`*.test.tsx` exists
  in the same folder. A `play` function elsewhere (this component's own story, or — this is
  the common miss — a *different* component's assembly-level story) does not substitute for
  it, even when it happens to exercise the same rendered output; see testing.md's note under
  "What to test (and what to skip)". A component's own test file may still mock a hook or
  child component whose internals are covered elsewhere — the point is that the component's
  own render-branch/event-wiring contract has a test discoverable from its own folder.
- If a test file exists, verify:
  - At least one test covers the primary render case.
  - At least one test covers a user interaction (click, input) if the component has interactive elements.
  - No tests use `toBeTruthy()` as the sole assertion — check for meaningful assertions.
- If a paired `.stories.tsx` is missing, flag as MISSING STORY (mandatory).
- If a logic-heavy file has no test file of its own, flag as MISSING TEST — regardless of
  whether a `play` function exists somewhere else in the codebase.

For each utility file under `overrides/app/utils/`:
- **`.test.ts` required** when the utility has ≥1 conditional branch or performs ≥1

- If a test file exists, verify it covers both the happy path and at least one edge case

## Code Quality Report

**Scope:** `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts`, `overrides/app/theme/components/footerShared.ts`
**Branch:** `fix/footer-tablet-wide-breakpoint` (vs `develop` @ `04039a9`)
**Date:** 2026-08-27

### 🔴 Must fix before PR merge

None.

### 🟡 Should fix in this PR

None.

### 🔵 Backlog (log, don't block)

- **`footerShared.ts:28`** — nothing validates that a `BP` key exists. Deleting `tablet` or `desktop` would emit `@media (min-width: undefined)`, which `recipeGuards.test.ts` does **not** check (it has no media-query validation at all), `tsc` accepts, and lint ignores. This change was silent by that route too — no gate noticed a key disappearing. Adding a shape assertion for a two-key const is the kind of low-value test `testing.md` discourages, so this is an observation about the guard's blind spot rather than a request.
- **`footerShared.ts:15-27`** — the `audit-allow:` marker now sits 13 lines above `export const BP`. Verified structurally sound: lines 9–27 are one contiguous comment block with no blank line, and both values still report as acknowledged exceptions. Flagging only because a future edit that inserts a blank line into that block would silently un-acknowledge `'64em'` and add a token-audit violation.

### ✅ Checks that passed cleanly

**Naming & structure** — TypeScript-only ✅ · no `console.*` ✅ · no commented-out *code* introduced (the addition is prose rationale, matching the house style already used in `footerNavColumn.css.ts`) ✅ · Australian spelling preserved (`COLOUR_HALF_INV`) ✅ · no new magic values ✅ · file naming correct for both families — `footerShared.ts` camelCase Zimmermann-authored, `footer.css.ts` the co-located recipe pattern ✅

**Hardcoded design values** — `footer.css.ts:10-13` holds four raw literals, all **pre-existing and untouched by this diff**, each carrying a named-constant + provenance comment so `audit:tokens` reports them as acknowledged. Not a finding against this change.

**Imports** — no circular dependency (`footerShared` → `foundation/gridSystem`; `gridSystem` imports nothing back) ✅ · relative depth 1, well under the 3-level limit ✅ · no internal `node_modules/@salesforce/...` paths ✅ · no later-sprint imports ✅

**TypeScript** — no `any` · no non-null assertions · `as const` correctly preserves literal types on `BP` · `breakpoints` is a runtime value so the plain `import` (not `import type`) is right · `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0 ✅

**Test & story coverage** — neither file is a component, so no story is required. The recipe is exercised by `recipeGuards.test.ts` on every `npm run test`; `footerShared.ts` exports two branchless constants, exempt per `conventions.md` → Utilities ✅

### Summary

**0 must-fix · 0 should-fix · 2 backlog items**

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | exit 0 |
| `npm run test` (Vitest) | **379 passed** / 25 files |
| `test-storybook --ci` | **98 passed** / 23 suites |
| `npm run lint` | 19 problems — **identical to `develop`**, neither file flagged |
| `npm run audit:tokens` | 4 unacknowledged — **identical to `develop`** |
| `cr review --light --base develop` | **No findings ✔** |
| `/code-quality` | 0 must-fix, 0 should-fix |
| Browser measurement | broken span ~124px → **~68px** |

## One correction from the conventions research

**No Storybook test actually exercises the tablet band.** There's no `addon-viewport` registered and no viewport set in `preview.tsx`, so the runner uses Playwright's default **1280×720** — above `BP.desktop`. The `tabletWide` rule was never active in any Storybook run.

════════════ PR #64 (most recent template-following) ════════════
TITLE: feat(pdp): SFCC-89 static product information — name, price, description, model line, and style code


# Description

Renders the five static product fields on the PDP per SFCC-89 — product name, full
price in the active storefront's currency, description, "Model is…" copy, and style
code — as five ui-kit atoms composed by two molecules, consumed by the product detail
page. No commerce interaction, no Contentful, no gallery: swatches (SFCC-91), size and
add-to-bag (SFCC-92), the gallery (SFCC-186/187/188), accordions (SFCC-195/102), badges
(SFCC-132/225) and was/now pricing (SFCC-194) are all separate stories and none of them
is touched here.

The model line reads `c_modelFit`. Nothing scrapes `c_sizeFit`.

Seven points worth surfacing before review:

- **The copy-first port is its own commit and reviewable on its own.** `d1fb034` is the
  mechanical `.jsx` → `.tsx` port of `product-view` and `product-detail` with **zero**
  functional change — `AGENTS.md`'s copy-first rule requires that split, and it is the
  largest commit by line count. Reading it first makes the other five small.
- **`product-view/index.tsx` gains exactly one optional slot, `renderHeader`.** The
  default export stays a faithful, undecorated SFCC bridge — base components import this
  module, so its prop surface and `forwardRef` behaviour are unchanged and the slot
  defaults to the base header. No other slots were added speculatively.
- **Type sits in the recipes, not on the JSX elements.** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`
  is silent on *where* a `textStyle` should live rather than contradictory: hierarchy point 1
  happens to show it as a prop (`textStyle="body2"`), but its actual rule is "never a raw
  `fontSize`", and point 3 plus "one canonical styling surface per component type" both point
  at the component's own theme config. PR #59 settled it in practice — seven recipe files
  carry `textStyle`, zero JSX props do — and this PR follows that deliberately. A
  one-sentence clarification to point 1 is worth a separate doc PR (that file is Tier 1
  governance): until it lands, the doc still reads as prescribing the prop form, and nothing
  mechanical catches the difference — `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s `TYPOGRAPHY_PROPS` checks only
  `fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`letterSpacing`, so a `textStyle` in the wrong place is invisible to
  `tsc`, eslint, the guard and axe alike.
- **Five changed files have no CODEOWNERS rule, so GitHub auto-requests no reviewer for
  them.** There is no default (`*`) owner in CODEOWNERS. Named by hand below.
- **The loading state diverges from base deliberately.** Base renders nothing until the
  product resolves; this page wraps the static fields in a `Skeleton` with a
  `minHeight` pinned to a line-height token, so the info column does not reflow when the
  data lands. Called out because it is a visible behavioural difference from the base PDP.
- **`staticProductHeader` has a story that `components.md` says it does not need.** That
  rule exempts "purely internal sub-components that only render inside one parent", which
  this partial is. It got one anyway: it is the only place the name's heading level is
  decided, and a wrong level (`h3` where the page needs `h1`) is invisible to `tsc`, to
  eslint, and to a passing unit test — but it is an axe violation, and every story is an
  axe assertion. Categorised `Commerce/StaticProductHeader` rather than `Pages/`, since
  `Pages/` is specified for full page assemblies and explicitly not per-sub-section stories.
- **Our components' internal spacing is exact; the column they sit in is not, and that's
  SFCC-723.** A 4-viewport sweep of the rendered page confirms every internal metric against
  the DS and finds **zero** off-token paddings/margins/gaps. But Figma puts the info column at
  **218px** (`5083:70358`) with the model line and style code *inside* it, while base's PDP
  layout gives our content **660px** at 1440 and leaves the meta block full-width below the
  accordions. That is `pdp/hero` layout geometry — **SFCC-723**, out of scope here. Flagging it
  so "design fidelity" is not read as covering the column itself.
- **The product name is an `h2`; the page's only `h1` is base's screen-reader-only "Product
  Details"** (`<Heading as="h1" srOnly>`, base-verbatim). Not an axe violation — which is why
  every a11y gate passes — but for a PDP the product name as `h1` is the SEO norm. Our `h2` is
  deliberately consistent with base rather than introducing a second `h1`; changing it means
  replacing base's, which is page-structure scope beyond this story. Worth its own ticket.
- **For QA: base renders `ProductView` twice** (one per breakpoint, one `display: none`), so
  `product-name`, `product-price`, `product-description` and `product-content` each appear
  **twice** in the DOM. Playwright strict mode will fail on a bare `getByTestId` — SFCC-732/733
  specs need a visibility filter.
- **`formatPrice` is duplicated** between the page and `partials/staticProductHeader.tsx`.
  The partial carries a comment pointing at the page's copy and vice versa. Left duplicated
  rather than lifted to `utils/` — extracting it would be refactoring upward out of this
  story's scope. Worth a follow-up.
- **6 of the 8 commits carry `.claude/registry/` churn.** The `PostToolUse` hook regenerates
  it on any `components/`/`pages/` edit and the `pre-commit` hook `git add`s it. Mechanical
  — skip those hunks.

`header/index.tsx:299` spreads `{...styles.popoverContent}` off a recipe that declares no
such part, in both our override and the base template it was copied from
(`retail-react-app/app/components/header/index.jsx:265`) — `popoverContent` is a **ListMenu**
part, so it is an upstream cross-recipe name mixup. It resolves to `undefined` and
`{...undefined}` is a legal no-op, so nothing breaks and Chakra's own `Popover` recipe styles
the element anyway. Pre-existing, out of scope here, and the only instance repo-wide; it
surfaces in the changed-files view because this PR ports that file. Worth its own ticket.
