content.content:
# Protection-tier check

> **No Tier 1 file is modified by this PR.**
>
> ⚠️ **Tier 2** — `overrides/app/routes.tsx` (Global Shell, **both squads**; CODEOWNERS
> additionally routes it to tier-1 and tier-2 approvers, so their review is auto-requested)
> and `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (**UI-Designer-owned** — registration
> entries only, no design values). `overrides/app/components/product-view/` is treated as
> Tier 2 by convention; note no tier list or CODEOWNERS entry actually covers it.

**Five files match no CODEOWNERS rule, and there is no default owner — reviewers named by
hand:** `components/product-view/index.tsx` (shared SFCC bridge imported by base components;
treated as Tier 2, **Squad B** notified), `theme/index.test.tsx`, `utils/richText.tsx` +
`richText.test.tsx`, and `types/vendor.d.ts`.

# Testing

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean. Not wired into CI; this is the only place it runs
- [x] `npm run lint` — 17 errors / 15 warnings, both at `develop`'s baseline. Error count
      held as an invariant across all commits
- [x] `npm run test` (Vitest) — 379 passed / 25 files
- [x] Storybook interaction + a11y — 24 suites / 106 tests. `.storybook/preview.tsx` sets
      `a11y: {test: 'error'}`, so every story is also an axe assertion
- [x] `npm run audit:tokens` — 14 unacknowledged / 22 acknowledged, unchanged from
      `develop`. Not wired into CI either
- [x] **Box model — 4 viewports (402 / 768 / 1024 / 1440), 0 off-token paddings, margins or
      gaps.** Meta rows 28/28px, style-code label→value 4px, name→price and price→description
      20px, list indent 16px (provisional, no DS spec), markers `disc`, all margins 0 — every
      value identical at all four widths. Note 768–1279 is undesigned in the DS, so those two
      widths are measured for stability, not compared to a spec
- [x] Accessibility — 106 axe assertions across 24 Storybook suites (`preview.tsx` sets
      `a11y: {test: 'error'}`); `aria-live="polite"` + `aria-atomic="true"` confirmed on the
      price element on the live page at all four viewports
- **Not verified: the price announcement itself.** Nobody has switched a variant with a screen
      reader running. The live region is proven present and unit-tested; that a given AT
      vocalises it is untested. Also worth knowing: before consent, Didomi's dialog `aria-hidden`s
      the whole page — correct fail-closed behaviour, but a screen-reader user meets consent first
- [x] Local CodeRabbit (`cr review --light --base develop`) — no findings
- [x] `/code-quality` audit vs `develop` — run; findings triaged. Deferred with reasons rather
      than fixed late in this PR: the `any` type aliases in the two copy-first ports should import
      `ShopperProductsTypes` from `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` (which does export it — the aliases'
      stated justification is wrong); `renderHeader` has no test; the seven new components use
      `data-testid` where `testing.md` prefers role/text selectors (zero of the ten existing
      Zimmermann `ui-kits` components use one). None changes behaviour; all are follow-ups
- [x] Runtime behaviour on a live PDP — developer-verified at two checkpoints
- **N/A: Playwright.** No PDP spec exists (`e2e/tests/` holds two homepage smoke tests) and
      writing one is gated on Lead QA signing off a Gherkin `.feature` first, per the
      three-stage workflow. Not closable in this PR

# Accessibility

Minimum bar **WCAG 2.1 AA**; 2.2 AA aspirational. This PR adds no interactive elements — the
five components are a heading, a paragraph, two text blocks and a two-node row.

- [ ] There are no UI changes
- [ ] **Tested with a screen reader — NOT done.** The price carries `aria-live="polite"` +
      `aria-atomic="true"` (confirmed on the live page at four viewports) and is unit-tested,
      but nobody has switched a variant with VoiceOver or TalkBack running. **The one open
      a11y item on this PR.** Worth knowing when you do: before consent, Didomi's dialog
      `aria-hidden`s the whole page, so a screen-reader user meets consent first
- [x] Keyboard-only navigation — no interactive elements are added, so there is nothing new
      in the tab order
- [x] Colour contrast meets WCAG 2.1 AA — `text.default` (#191919) ≈ 16:1 and
      `text.secondary` (#666666) ≈ 5.7:1 on white, both above 4.5:1; also covered by axe
- [x] Changes comply with [WCAG 2.1 AA](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/quickref/?levels=aa) —
      axe reports 0 violations across all 24 Storybook suites
- [x] Common UI patterns follow [WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/)
- [x] _(Bonus)_ [WCAG 2.2 AA](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/quickref/?levels=aa) considered —
      **4.1.3 Status Messages** is precisely why the price is a live region: choosing a variant
      rewrites the URL's `pid` and repaints the price with no focus change, so without it the
      number a shopper is buying at changes silently

Known, deliberately not fixed here: the product name is an `h2` because the page's only `h1`
is base's screen-reader-only "Product Details". Not an axe violation, but off the SEO norm for
a PDP — replacing base's `h1` is page-structure scope beyond this story.

# Localisation

- [ ] No copy changes
- [x] Copy change **noted as pending translation.** One new string — the style-code label,
      `product_view.label.style_code` — goes through `intl.formatMessage` with a
      `defaultMessage`, and no `translations/` entry is added. That directory is Tier 2
      (Integration / SI Partner). Behaviour until extraction runs: each site's default locale
      is silent, because `config/sites.js` sets `defaultLocale` to its first locale and
      `@formatjs` only raises `MissingTranslationError` when `locale !== defaultLocale`;
      non-default locales route through base `_app`'s `onError`, which downgrades
      `MISSING_TRANSLATION` to a `logger.warn` and returns. No crash, no console error.

# Known gaps and follow-ups

A `/code-quality` audit against `develop` ran before this PR. Nine findings were triaged as
follow-ups rather than fixed here — none changes behaviour, and each would either edit a
copy-first port or refactor tests late in a gated PR:

- **Types.** Both ports alias `SfccProduct`/`Variant`/`Category`/`PriceData` to `any`. The
  in-file justification has been corrected: `@salesforce/retail-react-app` shipping no types is
  true but beside the point — these shapes are `commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s and it does export
  `ShopperProductsTypes`. Substituting also clears 3 of the 15 lint warnings, which moves a
  baseline this branch holds as an invariant across all 8 commits — hence not bundled here. The
  same follow-up covers `SfccVariationValue.image` (declared a Product, read as an `Image`) and
  `name: string` where upstream is `name?: string`.
- **`renderHeader` has no test.** Both call sites pass byte-identical prop objects today with
  nothing pinning that, and the default-vs-supplied branch is untested. A test needs the shared
  `renderWithProviders` helper `testing.md` calls for and that doesn't exist yet — that helper is
  the real unit of work.
- **Selectors.** The seven new components carry `data-testid`; `testing.md` wants role/text first
  and reserves test IDs for elements with no semantics. Zero of the ten existing Zimmermann
  `ui-kits` components use one, so this is a divergence worth correcting — as a test refactor with
  its own review, not late here. The two molecule wrappers legitimately qualify and would stay.
- **Assertion consistency.** Collapse behaviour is asserted three ways across six suites;
  standardise on `toBeEmptyDOMElement()`.
- **The seven registration pins catch an unregistration only** — a recipe emptied to `{}` still
  passes. Four of the seven pin no resolved value anywhere, which matters more now type lives in
  the recipes. Documented in-file; closing it means asserting a resolved value per recipe.
- **`staticProductHeader.tsx:58,60`** carries bare Chakra keys lifted verbatim from base
  `product-view`. `minWidth={64}` is the one that matters — `sizes` is not a registered scale
  here, so a bare key can misresolve rather than just read oddly.
- **`app/constants` is imported by base path in both ports** (base-verbatim). No behavioural
  impact — the override is a pure superset re-export — but a constant's *value* changing would
  split base consumers from these two files.
- **The shipped ProductView/PDP path has no coverage in this repo.** Base ships `index.test.js`
  for both (39 and 24 cases); `vitest.config.ts` scopes collection to `overrides/**`, so they
  never run here. Not a CI regression — the override now shadows the implementation those suites
  were written against. Base's suites are a ready-made porting source.

Owner-side, not ours: the cap-height/leading-trim spacing question and a named 28px spacing step
(designer — `--zimm-scale-700` is raw px for a spacing alias, against the Units rule);
`overrideStyling.md`'s `isFromExtends` rationale is wrong in a way that *understates* the rule,
and its "known instance" cites two files that exist on no branch (governance); no ESLint
`import/*` rules, so the highest-value override rule is human-review-only (Integration).

---

# Commit message

```
fix(footer): remove the 860px breakpoint so tablet nav labels stop re-wrapping

BP.tabletWide (53.75em) stepped linksInner's gap from 3xl to 5xl. It had one call
site and no design behind it: the Figma Footer component has exactly three size
variants — Mobile 320-767, Tablet 768-1023, Desktop 1024+ — confirmed by the UI
designer against the comps' own min/max widths.

It was also actively harmful. The nav columns reach their natural width around
836px, but at 860px the rule spent 40px more on gaps than the row had, squeezing
them back below content width and re-wrapping labels that had just recovered.

Measured across 768-1024 in 2px steps against a built Storybook: the broken span
drops from ~124px to ~68px of the 256px tablet band, and the 860-912 zone
disappears entirely. The remaining 768-834 breakage is a separate design-side
decision about which element flexes, not addressed here.
```

Subject is 77 chars, `fix` + lowercase scope — passes `commit-msg`'s regex. No `Co-Authored-By`.

---

# PR title

```
fix(footer): remove the 860px tablet-wide breakpoint
```

No SFCC key — following the #46/#47 precedent for work with no story. (#59 and #64 carry keys because they had one.)

---

# PR body

```markdown
# Description

Removes `BP.tabletWide` (53.75em / 860px) and its single call site. It was our own
invention, not a design constraint, and it was making the tablet footer worse.

The footer misbehaves across the tablet band in three ways — the email field crowding
the nav groups, nav labels wrapping, and the bottom bar growing 14px taller. All three
share a root cause: fixed-width pieces in a shrinking box with `flexWrap: nowrap`
closing the only escape route. **This PR fixes one specific contributor to that, not
the root cause.**

`tabletWide` stepped `linksInner`'s gap from `3xl` (40px) to `5xl` (80px) at 860px. The
nav columns reach their natural width (115/135/106) around 836px and stop wrapping — and
then at 860px this rule spent 40px more on gaps than the row had, squeezing them back
below content width and re-wrapping labels that had just recovered.

Kiera confirmed the Figma Footer component has exactly three size variants, read off the
comps' own min/max widths: **Mobile 320–767, Tablet 768–1023, Desktop 1024+**. There is
no fourth variant. Our other two breakpoints (`tablet` 768, `desktop` 1024) match hers
exactly; this one had nothing behind it.

Measured across 768–1024 in 2px steps against a built Storybook:

| | broken ranges | span |
|---|---|---|
| before | 768–832 **and 860–912** | ~124px |
| after | 768–834 | **~68px** |

> **What this does not fix, and why it isn't in scope.** 768–834 still breaks. The email
> column is a fixed 320px that never shrinks, so at 768px the nav block gets 368px to fit
> 436px of content — 68px short. Closing it means something has to flex, and which one is
> a design decision: narrow the email field to 240px, let the nav wrap to two rows, or
> tighten the gaps. All three are measured and drafted for Kiera; none belongs in a PR
> that removes an unbacked breakpoint.

# Linked

- Follows up: **SFCC-55** (Global Footer UI), merged in #59 — this is a defect in what
  that shipped. No ticket exists for footer responsive work; `gh issue list` and a sweep
  of `.docs/`/`.claude/` turned up nothing, so this is deliberately unticketed rather
  than mislinked.
- Sprint: SFCC — Sprint 5

> With no `SFCC-\d+` key in the title, body or branch name, `e2e-browserstack` will not
> run at all. That is `qa.yml`'s designed behaviour, not a failure — with nothing to
> attribute results to in Zephyr, there is nothing correct to run.

# Squad ownership

- [x] Cross-squad — both leads notified

`components/footer/` is Tier 2 Global Shell owned by both squads. `.claude/rules/squadA.md`
lists footer under Squad A but instructs notifying Squad B before any change; #59 shipped
it as Squad B.

# Types of Changes

- [x] **Bug fix** (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

# Changes

- `components/footer/footer.css.ts` — removed the `@media (min-width: ${BP.tabletWide})`
  block on `linksInner` (three lines; a `gap` step from `3xl` to `5xl`)
- `theme/components/footerShared.ts` — removed the `tabletWide` entry from `BP`, and
  recorded why at the point of use so it is not reintroduced. `tablet` and `desktop` are
  unchanged

# How to test-drive this PR

- The branch gets its own MRT preview URL automatically — open the footer and drag the
  window from 768 to 1024. Nothing should re-wrap once it settles at ~836px
- `npm run build-storybook`, serve it, open `Layout/Footer → Default` and step the
  viewport through 856 → 864. Before: columns collapse to 97/114/89 at 860 and labels
  wrap. After: they hold 115/135/106
- "Acknowledgement of Country" wraps at every width including 1440 — that is by design;
  Figma's own item is two lines and the 160px column cap reproduces it

# Protection-tier check

> **No Tier 1 file is modified by this PR.**
>
> ⚠️ **Tier 2** — `overrides/app/theme/components/footerShared.ts`
> (**UI-Designer-owned**). `protectedFiles.md:41-43` names this file explicitly as staying
> Tier 2 because it holds genuinely cross-component shared values that co-location does
> not cover. The change is one deleted constant plus a comment; no design value moves.
>
> `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts` sits inside a Tier 2 directory but is
> **not** governed by that tier's designer gate — CODEOWNERS `:186`
> (`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts`) is the last matching rule and routes it to the
> owning squads only, per `protectedFiles.md:39-41`.

This change therefore spans two ownership surfaces (Tier 2 designer-owned, Tier 3
squad-owned). Flagged per AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 rather than split, since removing the
constant without its call site — or vice versa — would leave the repo in a worse state
than either end point.

# Testing

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean. Not wired into CI; this is the only place it runs
- [x] `npm run lint` — 19 problems (4 errors / 15 warnings), **identical to `develop`**.
      Neither changed file appears in the output. The 4 errors are pre-existing
      `prettier/prettier` in `routes.tsx` and `recipeGuards.test.ts`
- [x] `npm run test` (Vitest) — 379 passed / 25 files
- [x] Storybook interaction + a11y — 98 passed / 23 suites. `preview.tsx` sets
      `a11y: {test: 'error'}`, so every story is also an axe assertion
- [x] `npm run audit:tokens` — 4 unacknowledged, **identical to `develop`**. Re-checked
      after the comment edit: `footerShared.ts`'s `audit-allow` marker still associates
      and both its values remain acknowledged
- [x] Local CodeRabbit (`cr review --light --base develop`) — **no findings**
- [x] `/code-quality` vs `develop` — 0 must-fix, 0 should-fix. Two backlog notes below
- [x] **Browser measurement** — `Layout/Footer → Default` swept 768–1024 in 2px steps
      against a built Storybook. Broken span ~124px → ~68px; 856–864 holds 115/135/106
      with no wrapping. Futura Round confirmed loaded (151.8px vs 167.3px fallback for
      "BOOK AN APPOINTMENT"), so these are real-font break points
- **Not verified by any automated test: the fix itself.** No Storybook viewport addon is
      registered and `preview.tsx` sets no viewport, so the runner uses Playwright's
      default 1280×720 — above `BP.desktop`. **The removed rule was never active in any
      Storybook run.** The 98 passing tests prove no regression; they are not evidence the
      fix works. That evidence is the developer-run measurement above and is not
      reproducible in CI
- **N/A: Playwright.** `e2e/tests/` holds one homepage smoke spec. A footer spec is gated
      on Lead QA signing off a Gherkin `.feature` first, per the three-stage workflow

# Known gaps and follow-ups

- **768–834 still breaks** — needs Kiera to choose which element flexes. Three options
  measured: email field to 240px (keeps one row and restores 44px separation, footer
  height unchanged); nav wraps to two rows (keeps the 320px field, footer grows ~175px);
  or tighten everything (fits, but the field and nav still touch)
- **Bottom bar** — "Terms & Conditions" wraps to two lines below ~909px, making that bar
  93px instead of 79px. Same root cause, separate fix
- **`BP.desktop` (1024) vs `gridSystem.xl` (1280)** — the footer switches to its desktop
  layout 256px before the page grid does. May be intentional; `gridSystem.ts` is Tier 1,
  so worth a designer answer before anyone changes either
- **Nothing validates that a `BP` key exists.** Deleting one emits
  `@media (min-width: undefined)`, which `recipeGuards.test.ts` does not check (it has no
  media-query validation), `tsc` accepts and lint ignores. This change was silent by that
  route too — a guard blind spot, noted rather than fixed
- **`footerShared.ts`'s `audit-allow` marker now sits 13 lines above its declaration.**
  Verified sound — lines 9–27 are one contiguous comment block — but a future edit that
  inserts a blank line there would silently un-acknowledge `'64em'`
```

**Cross-squad vs Squad A.** I ticked Cross-squad. `squadA.md` claims footer as Squad A territory but tells you to notify Squad B; #59 shipped as Squad B. Cross-squad is the honest reading of "Global Shell, both squads" and means neither lead is surprised — but say the word if you'd rather match #59.

A reviewer seeing 98 green Storybook tests on a layout PR will reasonably assume they cover the change, and they don't — the removed rule was never active at 1280×720. Better they learn that from the body than from a regression.

    BP.tabletWide (53.75em) stepped linksInner's gap from 3xl to 5xl. It had one call
    site and no design behind it: the Figma Footer component has exactly three size
    variants — Mobile 320-767, Tablet 768-1023, Desktop 1024+ — confirmed by the UI
    designer against the comps' own min/max widths.
    
    It was also actively harmful. The nav columns reach their natural width around
    836px, but at 860px the rule spent 40px more on gaps than the row had, squeezing
    them back below content width and re-wrapping labels that had just recovered.

    drops from ~124px to ~68px of the 256px tablet band, and the 860-912 zone
    disappears entirely. The remaining 768-834 breakage is a separate design-side
    decision about which element flexes, not addressed here.

nav groups, nav labels wrapping, and the bottom bar growing 14px taller. All three share a
root cause: fixed-width pieces in a shrinking box with `flexWrap: nowrap` closing the only
escape route. **This PR fixes one specific contributor to that, not the root cause.**

`tabletWide` stepped `linksInner`'s gap from `3xl` (40px) to `5xl` (80px) at 860px. The nav
columns reach their natural width (115/135/106) around 836px and stop wrapping — and then at
860px this rule spent 40px more on gaps than the row had, squeezing them back below content
width and re-wrapping labels that had just recovered.

Kiera confirmed the Figma Footer component has exactly three size variants, read off the
comps' own min/max widths: **Mobile 320–767, Tablet 768–1023, Desktop 1024+**. There is no
fourth variant. Our other two breakpoints (`tablet` 768, `desktop` 1024) match hers exactly;
this one had nothing behind it.

Measured across 768–1024 in 2px steps against a built Storybook:

| | broken ranges | span |
|---|---|---|
| before | 768–832 **and 860–912** | ~124px |
| after | 768–834 | **~68px** |

> **What this does not fix, and why it isn't in scope.** 768–834 still breaks. The email
> column is a fixed 320px that never shrinks, so at 768px the nav block gets 368px to fit
> 436px of content — 68px short. Closing it means something has to flex, and which one is a
> design decision: narrow the email field to 240px, let the nav wrap to two rows, or tighten
> the gaps. All three are measured and drafted for the UI designer; none belongs in a PR that
> removes an unbacked breakpoint.

message.content: what does our PR fix again?

content.text:
**One thing: it deletes a breakpoint we invented that had no design behind it — and that was actively making the tablet footer worse.**

## What was wrong

`BP.tabletWide` (860px) had a single job: at 860px it grew the gaps between the three nav columns from 40px to 80px.

The problem is *where* it fired. The nav columns finally reach their natural width around **836px** and stop wrapping. Then at 860px this rule spent 40px more on empty gap than the row actually had — squeezing the columns back below their content width and re-wrapping labels that had just recovered.

So the footer looked fine at 859px and broke again at 860px.

Kiera's variant spec confirmed there is no fourth breakpoint in the design — Mobile 320–767, Tablet 768–1023, Desktop 1024+. Our other two match hers exactly. This one was ours.

## What it fixes

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| broken ranges | 768–832 **and 860–912** | 768–834 |
| broken span | ~124px | **~68px** |

**The 860–912 zone is gone entirely.** Roughly half the damage across the tablet band, from deleting three lines.

## What it does *not* fix

- **768–834 still breaks.** That's the fixed 320px email column — at 768px the nav block gets 368px to fit 436px of content. Blocked on a design decision about which element flexes.
- **The zero gap between the email field and the nav groups** — still 0px across the whole 768–1023 band.
- **The bottom bar** — "Terms & Conditions" still wraps below ~909px, making that bar 14px taller.

So: one of the three symptoms you reported is partially fixed, and the other two are untouched. This PR was worth shipping on its own because removing the invented breakpoint is correct no matter which option Kiera picks — but it's a first step, not the fix.

content.text:
Now the difference is real and clean.

## Use **880 × 1000**

| | develop | PR #69 |
|---|---|---|
| gap between nav columns | **80px** | **40px** |
| column widths | 103 / 121 / 95 *(squeezed)* | **115 / 135 / 106** *(natural)* |
| wrapped labels | **3** — Brand Protection, Book an Appointment, Orders & Shipping | **none** |
| footer height | **518px** | **504px** |

880px sits comfortably mid-zone, so you're not on a boundary where a 1px browser difference muddies the comparison. Height 1000 frames the whole footer with room to spare — it's 518px at its tallest here.

## The 14px height drop is your clearest tell

If you want one number that proves it without squinting at labels: **518 → 504**. That's the third row of wrapped text disappearing.

## Alternative widths

| width | why |
|---|---|
| **860** | the exact pixel the rule fires. Same 3 wraps, and columns at their most squeezed (97/114/89). Most dramatic, but you're one pixel from the boundary |
| **900** | 2 wraps instead of 3 — less dramatic |
| **912** | last broken pixel. Only 2 wraps and heights match (490 both sides) — **avoid, it's the weakest comparison** |

## The knife-edge shot, if you want it

Set **859 × 1000**, then **860 × 1000**, on `develop` only:

- 859 → clean, columns at 115/135/106
- 860 → 3 labels wrap, columns collapse to 97/114/89

That's the bug in two screenshots from a single branch — one pixel of viewport, and the layout falls apart. It makes the case better than any before/after pair, because it shows the breakpoint firing rather than just that things differ.

---

Method note: my first run reported both states as identical with `gap: 80` on the removed side. The injected stylesheet was never being cleared between iterations — Emotion injects stylesheets dynamically, so `styleSheets[last]` wasn't mine and the id I set for cleanup landed on the wrong node. The numbers above come from a rewrite that loads a fresh page per state instead. Worth knowing since the first output looked plausible and was wrong.

65	  / React Query hook). Data-fetching belongs in `overrides/app/pages/` or another container
66	  component, which then passes the result down. This generalizes the existing
67	  "no commerce state hooks inside leaf components" rule to _all_ data-fetching, not just
68	  commerce SDK hooks — the reasoning is the same either way: a component that owns its own
69	  data-fetching can't be reused somewhere the data arrives differently (SSR-prefetched,
70	  mocked in Storybook, composed from a parent that already has it).
71	
72	  **Exception — Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks** (`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) may
73	  be called from any component, including presentational leaves. Both read from a Provider
74	  mounted above the route tree, not from a per-page/per-component fetch — so calling one from
75	  a leaf doesn't create the SSR/Storybook/parent-composition problem the rule above exists to
76	  prevent, and doesn't multiply fetches the way an SDK hook would. `useUiCopy`
77	  (`overrides/app/hooks/useUiCopy.ts`, Provider at `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/`)
78	  is the reference example — `BottomBar` and `ZimmSubscribeSection` both call it directly
79	  for microcopy while still receiving their actual business data as props. This exception is
80	  narrow: it covers content that is identical for every consumer regardless of route/context,
81	  not anything that varies per page.
82	
83	  **Their no-Provider behaviour differs, and it matters for tests and stories.** `useUiCopy`
84	  degrades to fallback text — `useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY` — so a leaf calling
85	  it renders with zero setup. `useIntl` **throws** (`react-intl`'s `invariantIntlContext`:
86	  _"Could not find required `intl` object"_), and its `IntlProvider` is mounted by the **base
87	  SFCC `_app`**, not by `_app-config` — a strictly narrower subtree. `.storybook/preview.tsx`
88	  supplies one for stories precisely because of this; any Vitest test rendering a `useIntl`
89	  consumer must wrap it too. An earlier revision of this paragraph claimed both hooks degrade
90	  gracefully and that both Providers sit in `_app-config`; neither is true of `useIntl`.
91	- **Extract-to-hook threshold.** Pull inline component logic out into a custom hook
92	  (`overrides/app/hooks/use<ComponentName><Feature>.ts`) when either is true:
93	
94	  - The component has ≥2 pieces of related `useState` that change together (a strong signal
95	    the state belongs in one place, whether that's a custom hook or a single reducer).
96	  - Any `useEffect` has a non-trivial dependency array or a cleanup function — non-trivial
97	    meaning more than a single obvious dependency, or the effect does anything beyond a
98	    one-line side effect.

1	# Testing Conventions
2	
3	Three layers, three purposes. **Do not duplicate coverage across layers** — pick the cheapest layer that proves the behaviour.
4	
5	**This is not license to skip a component's own test file because its behaviour happens to be
6	covered transitively elsewhere.** A component with real logic (branching, prop→JSX mapping
7	decisions, event wiring) gets its own `index.test.ts`/`index.test.tsx`, even when the state it
8	renders is owned by a hook that already has its own test, or a parent's assembly-level
9	Storybook `play` already exercises the rendered result. Resolve the duplication concern by
10	**scoping what that file asserts** — mock the hook/child component whose internals are proven
11	elsewhere, and test only this component's own contract (given a state, does it render the
12	right branch; given a DOM event, does it call the right handler) — not by leaving the
13	component with no test of its own. Relying on a *different* component's story to prove *this*
14	component's contract means the coverage isn't discoverable from the component's own folder,
15	and can silently vanish if that unrelated file changes. See
16	`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` for the
17	resulting pattern (mocks `useSubscribeSection` and `ZimmSubscribeModal`, tests only its own
18	render-branch/event-wiring contract). A component with no branching or decision logic at all
19	(pure prop interpolation, e.g. `BottomBar`) still doesn't need its own suite — the exemption
20	below for single-parent internal components still applies there.
21	
22	| Layer | Tool | What it covers | File pattern | CI gate |
23	|---|---|---|---|---|
24	| Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms, hook behaviour in isolation | `*.test.ts` co-located with the source | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
25	| Component interaction | Storybook `play` | User-facing interactions in a single component (clicks, form fills, focus management) | `*.stories.tsx` `play` function | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
26	| E2E | Playwright | Full user journeys across pages, multi-region, integration boundaries | `e2e/tests/**/*.spec.{ts,js}` | Every PR (`qa.yml`) — desktop + mobile Chromium against localhost/dev API; BrowserStack multi-browser on `release/**` only |
27	
28	> Higher-level project rules: [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Testing. Day-to-day file conventions: [conventions.md](./conventions.md). This file describes **how** to write tests at each layer.

content.text:
Implemented and verified. **Not committed** — and there's a decision for you before I do.

## Measured against the Figma frames

| viewport | layout | subscribe | site map | separation | vs design |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 768–944 | **stacked** | 320 | 523 | 80px vertical | ✅ the annotation |
| **946** | inline | 320 | 523 | **23px** | ✅ the 946 threshold |
| 1023 | inline | 320 | 523 | **100px** | ✅ Figma: 460−360 = **100** |
| 1024 | inline | 320 | **600** | 24px | ✅ |
| 1440 | inline | 320 | 600 | **440px** | ✅ Figma: 800−360 = **440** |

**Zero wrapped labels at every width.** The 768–834 band is gone — not narrowed, gone — because below 946 the site map now stacks underneath instead of competing for the row.

## What actually changed

The design uses **one** mechanism at both breakpoints that we weren't using: the Site Map is a **fixed box** (523 tablet / 600 desktop, `shrink-0`) and the column gaps are *derived* by `justify-between`, not set. Our tablet rule was `flex: 1` + an explicit 40px gap + `flex-end` — a different mechanism that happened to look right at one width. Desktop was already correct; tablet now matches it.

Gates: `tsc` 0 · **379** Vitest · **98** Storybook · lint 19 (baseline) · audit:tokens 4 (baseline) · CodeRabbit **no findings**.

## Three things you need to decide or pass on

**1. Pushing dismisses the approval.** `develop` has `dismissesStaleReviews: true`, and #69 currently reads `APPROVED`. These commits will reset it to `REVIEW_REQUIRED`. Expected, but worth knowing it isn't a mistake when it happens.

**2. I couldn't find the padding Kiera mentioned.** She said she "added some padding to the subscribe container." The Subscribe Section's layout in Figma is `flex flex-col gap-[40px] items-start max-w-[320px] w-[320px]` — **no padding**. What *is* new on the Content frame is `gap-y-[80px]`, the stack gap. I implemented what the design actually specifies rather than inventing padding to match the description. Worth confirming with her that the annotation and the gap are the whole change.

**3. Column gaps measure 84px where Figma says 80px** (and 122 vs 118.5 at desktop). Not a defect and not worth chasing: our columns render ~7px narrower in total than Figma's text boxes, and since the gap is *derived* from the fixed 523px width, that difference lands in the gap. `footerNavColumn.css.ts` already documents this — "exact column widths still will not match Figma… content-driven and follow the font."

## One consequence worth flagging to Kiera

**The footer gets substantially taller on tablet** — 490px inline, **747px stacked at 768**. That's the design's own trade, but it's a +257px jump at 946px that nobody may have pictured. If that's a surprise, the alternative is narrowing the email field instead of stacking (measured earlier: 240px keeps one row at the same height).

Want me to commit and push, or hold while you check the padding question with her?

The entire subscribe subtree has exactly one padding value and it's **vertical**: 4px top and bottom on the input, which we already render (our field is 45px = 36 content + 4 + 4 + 1 border).

So Kiera's "added some padding to the subscribe container" doesn't correspond to anything in these frames. Three possibilities, and only she can say which: the edit didn't save to this file, she's describing the new `gap-y-[80px]` on Content loosely as padding, or it's in a frame she hasn't pointed us at. **What did land is the 946px annotation and the stack gap — and I've implemented both.**

## #3 — My claim was right, but I hadn't actually verified it

I'd asserted "font metrics, not a defect." Checking properly:

| column | our box | Figma box | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| About | 115 | 118 | −3.0 |
| **Contact** | **135** | **139** | **−4.0** |
| Help | 105.6 | 106 | −0.4 |
| | | **total** | **−7.4** |

Contact's −4.0 exactly matching Figma's 4px `pl` looked like we might be missing that padding. **We're not** — it's applied in two places, mirroring the design's own structure:

- `footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44` → the heading, matching Figma's `wrapper` with `pl-[4px]`
- `footerNavColumn/index.tsx:62` → each `<li>`, matching Figma's per-`footer-item` `pl-[4px]`

Our Contact box is 135 with the 4px included (content 131); Figma's is 139 with its 4px included (content 135). Same structure, 4px of font-rendering difference in the widest label. All three deltas are the same cause.

That −7.4px total lands in the two derived gaps: **(523 − 356) ÷ 2 = 83.5 ≈ 84** against Figma's 80.

**And this is a virtue of the mechanism, not a workaround.** Because the gap is derived from the fixed 523px width rather than set, it self-corrects — if the font metrics ever shift, the columns and gaps rebalance without anyone touching a number. That's precisely what the old hardcoded 80px `tabletWide` rule couldn't do.

## The two open questions, resolved

**The padding doesn't exist.** Not in the Subscribe Section, not in Stay In Touch, not anywhere in the Textfield subtree. The only padding in that whole branch of the tree is `py-[4px]` — vertical, on the input, already implemented. There is nothing to build.

- `gap-y-[80px]` on the Content frame — the stack gap

Audit code quality for the specified scope. Do not modify any files — this is a read-only
diagnostic. Produce a prioritised report with actionable fixes.

---

## Input

The user will provide one of:
- A file path or directory to audit
- No argument — default to files changed on the current branch: `git diff --name-only main`

If no argument is given, run: `git diff --name-only main` and audit those files.
Exclude test files (`*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`), stories (`*.stories.tsx`), and any registry files.

---

## Parallel execution

For audits covering more than 5 files, split into four independent checks and run them
as parallel agents simultaneously. Each agent receives only its own checklist — do not
bundle all checks into one agent.

- **Agent A — Naming & structure**
- **Agent B — Import analysis**
- **Agent C — TypeScript coverage**
- **Agent D — Test & story coverage**

For 5 files or fewer, run all checks sequentially in a single pass.

---

## Agent A — Naming & structure

Rules are defined once, split across [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md)
(cross-cutting), [css.md](../../rules/css.md) (Chakra/styling), and
[components.md](../../rules/components.md) (components/hooks/Storybook) — read the relevant
ones first, then apply each rule to the files in scope. Do not re-list the rules here;
that's how the files drift apart.

Walk the file list and audit each file against the relevant section:

- Every file → conventions.md **General** section.
- Every file with JSX/Chakra props → css.md **Tokens** section (no hardcoded hex/px values).
- `.tsx` under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/` → components.md
  **Components** + **Composition** sections, plus conventions.md **File naming and folder
  structure**.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/hooks/` → components.md **Hooks** section.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/utils/` → conventions.md **Utilities** section.

For each violation, record `file:line` and which rule file + bullet failed — the section
anchor is enough (e.g. "components.md → Components → Props type placement").

---

## Agent B — Import analysis

For each file, read the import statements and check:

- No circular imports: if File A imports from File B, File B must not import from File A
  (check by reading the imported file's imports in turn — one level deep is sufficient).
- No imports from a higher tier without justification:
  - A component must not import directly from internal `commerce-sdk-react` source paths.
  - A page must not bypass its own hooks to call raw API functions.
- No imports from a later-sprint feature (reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` when present).
- No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels — flag for path alias review.

---

## Agent C — TypeScript coverage

Check each file against the relevant rule file:

- Every `.ts`/`.tsx` → [typescript.md](../../rules/typescript.md) in full (no `any` without
  justification, `type` vs `interface`, non-null assertions, discriminated unions, utility
  types, `import type`, `satisfies`, `readonly`, generic naming).
- Components → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Components** (props type name,
  placement, optional `?`, callback naming, JSDoc).
- Hooks → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Hooks** (typed params, explicit
  return type, JSDoc with `@returns`).

Then run `npx tsc --noEmit` **once** for the whole branch (not per file) and report any
errors. Cross-reference any new errors against the files in scope.

---

## Agent D — Test & story coverage

For each component file under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/`:
- A paired `*.stories.tsx` exists in the same directory (required by [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) > Testing).
- For logic-heavy components or hooks: the component's **own** `*.test.ts`/`*.test.tsx` exists
  in the same folder. A `play` function elsewhere (this component's own story, or — this is
  the common miss — a *different* component's assembly-level story) does not substitute for
  it, even when it happens to exercise the same rendered output; see testing.md's note under
  "What to test (and what to skip)". A component's own test file may still mock a hook or
  child component whose internals are covered elsewhere — the point is that the component's
  own render-branch/event-wiring contract has a test discoverable from its own folder.
- If a test file exists, verify:
  - At least one test covers the primary render case.
  - At least one test covers a user interaction (click, input) if the component has interactive elements.
  - No tests use `toBeTruthy()` as the sole assertion — check for meaningful assertions.
- If a paired `.stories.tsx` is missing, flag as MISSING STORY (mandatory).
- If a logic-heavy file has no test file of its own, flag as MISSING TEST — regardless of
  whether a `play` function exists somewhere else in the codebase.

For each utility file under `overrides/app/utils/`:
- **`.test.ts` required** when the utility has ≥1 conditional branch or performs ≥1
  transformation (currency, locale, mapping, parsing, etc.). Trivial re-exports and
  one-liners are exempt.
- If a test file exists, verify it covers both the happy path and at least one edge case
  (empty input, null, locale variation — whichever applies).

**Scope:** [files audited]

**Date:** [today]

### 🔴 Must fix before PR merge

[Issues that affect maintainability or violate conventions — one line per issue with file:line]

### 🔵 Backlog (log, don't block)
[Minor style issues, missing test cases for edge cases — one line per issue]

### ✅ No issues found
[List checks that passed cleanly]

### Summary
X must-fix · Y should-fix · Z backlog items
```

# Answer: no, Kiera changed nothing on the bottom bar

The Legel frame is **byte-identical** to my earlier pull — same geometry, same positions — and there is **no `data-development-annotations`** anywhere in its subtree. Her changes were confined to the Content frame (the 946 annotation and `gap-y-[80px]`).

## But pulling the spec found two real disagreements

### 1. `flex-wrap` — and this is the bottom bar bug

```
Legel:  content-start flex flex-wrap items-start justify-between
Legal:  content-start flex flex-wrap gap-[0px_24px] items-start
```

**The design wraps at both levels.** Ours sets `flexWrap: 'nowrap'` on `legalGrid` at tablet (`bottomBar.css.ts:79`).

That's the cause of the symptom you reported. When the row runs out of space, the design moves a *whole legal link* onto a second line. Ours forbids that, so the longest label breaks internally instead — **"Terms & Conditions" splitting across two lines below ~909px**, making the bar 93px instead of 79px.

We closed the escape route the design deliberately left open. Same shape as the nav-column bug, different row.

### 2. Horizontal padding is 32px, not 40px

```
Legel:  px-[var(--alias/space/800,32px)] py-[var(--alias/space/600,24px)]
```

Confirmed by geometry — Language sits at `x=32` in a 1023-wide frame, with a matching 32px right margin. Desktop is different: `x=40`.

Ours uses **40px** at tablet (`bottomBar.css.ts:26`), and the comment says why:

> *"holding this at 2xl until 1024px left the whole 768-1023px band with the bottom bar inset 8px less than the content above it"*

**That 8px inset is intentional in the design.** Content and Logo are at 40px, the bottom bar at 32px, at tablet only. We read it as a bug and corrected it away.

Our vertical padding (24px), the 24px tablet / 32px desktop legal gaps, the 4px language gap and the 8px item padding all match exactly.

## Scope call for you

Neither is caused by this PR, and neither is what Kiera asked for. Three options:

**Fix both here.** Two small changes: `flexWrap: 'wrap'` and `3xl → 2xl`. They complete the tablet story — you'd close all three symptoms in one PR. Cost: the PR grows again after an approval was already dismissed once.

**Fix the wrap only.** It's the actual defect and the same root cause the PR already addresses. Leave the 32/40 padding, since reverting a deliberate, documented decision deserves Kiera confirming she meant the 8px offset.

**Neither — separate PR.** Cleanest scope, but leaves a known bug shipping.

I'd take the second. The wrap is unambiguous — the design says wrap, we say nowrap, and the consequence is visible. The padding is a judgement someone made on purpose against what turns out to be the design's intent, and that deserves a sentence from Kiera rather than a silent revert.

Your call before I commit anything.

input.description: Measure total footer height profile

content.text:
Bottom bar fixed and measured. One thing still needs a human answer.

## What the wrap fix does

**No label breaks inside itself at any width now.** The design's escape route is open again — a whole legal link moves to the next line instead of "Terms & Conditions" splitting in half.

| viewport | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 768 | 93px, **"Terms & Conditions" broken** | 140px, clean — locale row + legal on 2 rows |
| 800–908 | 93px, **broken** | 109px, clean — locale row + legal row |
| 909+ | 79px, clean | 79px, clean |

The height increases are the wrap doing its job: the groups stack rather than a word snapping. That's `flex-wrap` + `justify-between` + `shrink-0` on both children, exactly as the Legel and Legal frames specify.

## Full footer height profile

| vw | content | logo | bar | **total** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 402 | 661 | 135 | 209 | 1005px |
| **768** | 519 | 135 | 140 | **794px** |
| 800–900 | 519 | 135 | 109 | 763px |
| 944 | 519 | 135 | 79 | 733px |
| **946** | 276 | 135 | 79 | **490px** |
| 1024+ | 276 | 135 | 79 | 490px |

Gates: `tsc` 0 · **379** Vitest · audit:tokens **4** (baseline).

There's a **304px jump at the 946 boundary** (794 → 490). That's the annotation's own arithmetic, not something I introduced — but it's the number Kiera should see, because a tablet footer that's 794px tall at 768 is a real design consequence and I doubt it was pictured when the annotation was written.

## The one thing I've left alone

**Horizontal padding is still 40px; the design says 32px.** Confirmed still rendering `padL: 40px` at every tablet width in the measurement above.

I'm not reverting it silently because it's **Tim's deliberate decision** — commit `5ecd515`, 23 Aug, the footer decomposition — with a written rationale:

> *"holding this at 2xl until 1024px left the whole 768-1023px band with the bottom bar inset 8px less than the content above it — the locale control and the legal links sat left of the subscribe column and the logo."*

He treated the 8px offset as a bug. The Figma frame says it's intent: Content and Logo at 40px, Legel at **32px**, at tablet only — desktop is 40px everywhere. So one of them is wrong and it isn't my call to pick.

Per AGENTS.md's doc-integrity rule, that's a pause-and-ask, not a silent override — the project lead's documented decision contradicts the design source of truth.

content.text:
Reproduced, and the mechanism is exact.

# The bug

`zimmTextInput.css.ts:174` renders the validation error with `marginTop: 4px` and **no reserved space**. The `control` slot above it sets `minHeight: 45px` — a *minimum*, not a fixed height — so when the error appears the slot grows **45 → 67px (+22)** and everything below it moves.

```
idle:   [ Email ________________ › ]              45px
error:  [ Email ________________ › ]              45px
        Please enter a valid email address.       + 4px margin + 18px line  =  67px
```

## Why the direction differs by breakpoint — your three symptoms

| viewport | layout | what moves |
|---|---|---|
| **402 mobile** | stacked | site map, logo, bottom bar **all push down +22** |
| **768 / 900 tablet** | stacked | same — **everything below pushes down +22** |
| **1023 / 1440 desktop** | inline | site map **doesn't move** (`linksTop` unchanged); only the logo and bar shift **+21** |

The heading never moves — `headingTop` is identical in all five rows. The subscribe column grows *downward* from a fixed top.

**Desktop reads as a "jump up" for a different reason than the other two.** When the columns are side by side, the site map stays put and only the content *below the row* moves. So the error appears to push the footer open from the middle rather than shove a column down — the subscribe column visually grows *into* the space beside the site map, and the eye reads the logo/bar as jumping. Stacked, there's no sibling to absorb it, so the whole lower footer slides down.

Same +22px in every case. Only what absorbs it changes.

## Why our existing guard didn't catch this

`index.stories.tsx`'s `SubscribePlaceholder` play asserts zero layout shift — and it passes. It exercises the **submit-unavailable** path, where the message is 2 lines / 36px and fits inside the 45px slot. I measured that path first: **0px shift at every breakpoint**.

The *validation* path was never covered. The slot was sized for one message and not the other.

## Two things before I propose a fix

**Your three Figma links are the bottom bar**, not the subscribe section — `1892:50522`, `40000407:23786` and `40000407:23933` are the desktop, tablet and mobile `Legel` frames. I need the error-state frames to know the intended treatment.

That matters because there's a known open conflict here. `zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts` says the slot is **provisional**:

> *"45px — the height ZimmInputAction currently renders… PROVISIONAL: Figma's success state keeps a Textfield instance at 320x59 (node 4019:46044), so the designed slot is 59px in both states — there is no token for it and `actionSizes.height` offers only 52/40. Pending Kiera."*

So the design may already reserve **59px**, which would absorb some of this. Whether it reserves enough for the error line is exactly what I can't answer without the right frames.

Can you send the subscribe-section error-state nodes for the three breakpoints? With those I can tell you whether the fix is "reserve the error line permanently" or "the design expects the growth and only our slot height is wrong."

content.text:
Two answers here, and the first one matters more than the nodes.

## The phenomenon

You're describing two different things that both prevent it, so worth separating:

**The problem** is **layout shift** — specifically **Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)**, one of the three Core Web Vitals. Content appearing and displacing what's already rendered.

**Your proposed behaviour** — *"uses existing space, as if floating"* — is **taking the element out of the normal document flow**. In CSS terms, `position: absolute` inside a `position: relative` ancestor. The element renders but occupies no space in the flow, so nothing below it moves.

The alternative fix for the same problem is **space reservation**: make the container always tall enough for its tallest state, so the error drops into space that was already there. **That's what this codebase already does** — the `control` slot's `minHeight: 45px` is exactly that pattern, and `uiBuild-knowledge.md` §7 records it as the house approach. It just reserved for the wrong message.

| | out-of-flow (your instinct) | space reservation (current pattern) |
|---|---|---|
| shift | none | none |
| idle height | unchanged | permanently taller |
| risk | error can **overlap** what's below | wasted whitespace in the common case |

Neither is "more correct" — it's a design call about whether the footer carries the error's height at all times.

Now the nodes.

content.text:
All four nodes 404 — deleted, not just outdated. The file now has a single page named `-----`, so there's nothing to reference there. That's fine; the answer doesn't depend on them.

# Recommendation: space reservation, not floating

## Why not out-of-flow

Your instinct is the right *goal* — no shift — but `position: absolute` is the wrong mechanism **here specifically**, because the subscribe column never has empty space below it to float into:

| viewport | what sits directly below the field |
|---|---|
| 402 mobile | the ABOUT nav column |
| 768–944 tablet | the site map (stacked) |
| 946+ desktop | the logo band |

An out-of-flow error would render **on top of** that content. And this isn't decorative text — it's `role="alert"` inside an `aria-live` region. Overlapping live-region text against a WCAG 2.2 AA bar turns a layout bug into an accessibility one. You'd trade a shift for an overlap.

Floating works when there's slack beneath — a form field in a tall page. This footer has none by construction.

## Why reservation is the right fit

**It's already the pattern.** `control` has `minHeight: SIZE_SUBSCRIBE_SLOT` doing exactly this. `uiBuild-knowledge.md` §7 records reserve-then-render as the house approach, and `SubscribePlaceholder`'s play exists specifically to assert zero shift — it passes today. The machinery is built; it was just sized wrong.

**The author already chose `minHeight` over `height` deliberately:**

> *"minHeight rather than height so copy that genuinely needs a third line on a narrow viewport still grows instead of clipping; centring only positions the content, it does not define the height."*

That's the correct instinct. Growth is a safety valve against clipped text.

## The actual root cause — and it's not the number

The reservation was derived from **one state**:

> *"45px — the height ZimmInputAction currently renders (36px content + 4px/4px padding + 1px border)"*

Measured from idle. Never checked against the tallest state. Here's the full set:

| state | height | fits in 45? |
|---|---|---|
| idle (input) | 45px | — |
| success message | 36px | ✅ |
| unavailable message | 36px | ✅ |
| **validation error** (input + 4 margin + 18 line) | **67px** | ❌ **+22** |

Three of four fit, which is why it shipped and why the shift-guard passes. **Bumping 45 → 67 fixes today's symptom and leaves the same defect in place** — the next state anyone adds repeats it.

The fix has two parts: reserve for the tallest state, and add a test that renders *every* state and asserts one height. That's the thing that would have caught this.

## What still needs Kiera

Two numbers, and they're the same conversation:

- `SIZE_SUBSCRIBE_SLOT` is already flagged provisional — *"Figma's success state keeps a Textfield instance at 320x59… the designed slot is 59px in both states — there is no token for it and `actionSizes.height` offers only 52/40. Pending Kiera."* **59 still doesn't cover 67.**
- Whether the error even belongs *below* the field. Figma's Textfield is 320×44 with its own `helper`/`error` slot — if the design shows the message **inside** the field's box rather than appended under it, the height never changes and neither fix is needed. Our implementation appends; I can't tell from the deleted nodes whether that's right.

That second one is worth asking before we build anything, because it changes the answer from "reserve 67" to "the field renders its own error and stays 44".

## What I'd do

Ask Kiera one question — *does the error message sit inside the field's box or below it?* — and reserve for the tallest state either way. It's the same slot she already owes us a number for, so it's one conversation, not two.

I haven't changed anything. The bottom-bar wrap fix and the tablet layout are still sitting uncommitted, waiting on her padding answer too — worth batching all three into one message to her.
